title: Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models
tldr: Introduces Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG) attack that automatically generates universal adversarial suffixes to jailbreak aligned LLMs, with high transferability to black-box models.

title: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
tldr: Applies the three-stage RLHF pipeline (SFT, reward modeling, PPO) to GPT-3, creating InstructGPT where a 1.3B aligned model is preferred over the 175B unaligned GPT-3.

title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
tldr: Shows that the RLHF objective can be solved in closed form, enabling direct optimization on preference data via a simple classification loss without a separate reward model.

title: Jailbroken: How Does LLM Safety Training Fail?
tldr: Identifies two fundamental failure modes of LLM safety training â€” competing objectives (safety vs. helpfulness) and mismatched generalization (safety doesn't cover out-of-distribution inputs) â€” and systematically evaluates 30 jailbreak attacks on GPT-4 and Claude.

title: Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
tldr: Foundational RLHF paper from Anthropic demonstrating that language models can be trained to be both helpful and harmless using human preference data, with larger models being easier to align.

title: Jailbreaking Black Box Large Language Models in Twenty Queries
tldr: Introduces PAIR, an automated black-box jailbreaking method that uses an attacker LLM to iteratively refine prompts, typically succeeding in fewer than 20 queries.

title: HarmBench: A Standardized Evaluation Framework for Automated Red Teaming and Robust Refusal
tldr: Introduces HarmBench, a standardized framework with 510 harmful behaviors for evaluating 18 red teaming attacks against 33 LLMs, plus the R2D2 adversarial training defense.

title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
tldr: Replaces human harmlessness feedback with AI self-critique and revision guided by constitutional principles, achieving competitive performance while reducing reliance on human supervision.

title: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding
tldr: Introduces MMLU, a 57-subject benchmark with 15,908 multiple-choice questions spanning STEM to humanities, establishing the standard capability evaluation for LLMs.

title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
tldr: Introduces MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena for scalable LLM evaluation, showing GPT-4 as judge achieves over 80% agreement with human preferences.

title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT
tldr: Uses causal tracing to localize factual knowledge to mid-layer MLP modules, then introduces ROME (Rank-One Model Editing) to edit individual facts via rank-one weight updates.

title: AutoDAN: Generating Stealthy Jailbreak Prompts on Aligned Large Language Models
tldr: AutoDAN uses a hierarchical genetic algorithm to automatically generate semantically coherent jailbreak prompts that evade perplexity-based defenses and transfer across LLMs.

title: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods
tldr: Introduces a benchmark of 817 questions testing whether LLMs give truthful answers or repeat common misconceptions, revealing that larger models are less truthful.

title: Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models
tldr: Uses one LM to automatically generate adversarial test cases that elicit harmful behaviors from a target LM, discovering tens of thousands of offensive replies from a 280B parameter chatbot.

title: Llama Guard: LLM-based Input-Output Safeguard for Human-AI Conversations
tldr: Llama Guard is a Llama2-7B model fine-tuned as a customizable input/output safety classifier for LLM conversations, outperforming OpenAI and Perspective API on multiple benchmarks.

title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
tldr: Trains sparse autoencoders on Pythia models to find features more interpretable than PCA, ICA, or neurons, and pinpoints features causally responsible for indirect object identification.

title: Representation Engineering: A Top-Down Approach to AI Transparency
tldr: Introduces Representation Engineering (RepE), a top-down approach using population-level representations to monitor and control high-level model behaviors including honesty, harmlessness, and power-seeking.

title: Baseline Defenses for Adversarial Attacks Against Aligned Language Models
tldr: Evaluates three baseline defense classes (perplexity filtering, preprocessing, adversarial training) against GCG-style jailbreak attacks on aligned LLMs, finding preprocessing defenses most practical.

title: Tree of Attacks: Jailbreaking Black-Box LLMs Automatically
tldr: TAP uses tree-of-thought reasoning with pruning to automatically jailbreak black-box LLMs, achieving 80%+ success on GPT-4 with 52% fewer queries than PAIR.

title: GPTFUZZER: Red Teaming Large Language Models with Auto-Generated Jailbreak Prompts
tldr: GPTFuzzer adapts coverage-guided fuzzing (AFL-style) to automatically mutate human-written jailbreak templates, achieving >90% attack success on ChatGPT and Llama-2 even from weak initial seeds.

title: RealToxicityPrompts: Evaluating Neural Toxic Degeneration in Language Models
tldr: Introduces a 100K-prompt benchmark showing all tested LMs generate toxic text even from benign prompts, and evaluates detoxification methods finding none fully prevent toxic degeneration.

title: Red Teaming Language Models to Reduce Harms: Methods, Scaling Behaviors, and Lessons Learned
tldr: Anthropic red-teamed LMs across 3 scales (2.7B-52B) and 4 safety interventions, finding RLHF models get harder to attack at scale, and released 38,961 red team attacks as a public dataset.

title: How Johnny Can Persuade LLMs to Jailbreak Them: Rethinking Persuasion to Challenge AI Safety by Humanizing LLMs
tldr: A persuasion taxonomy from social science is used to auto-generate interpretable adversarial prompts (PAP) that jailbreak GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Llama-2 with >92% success rate.

title: BeaverTails: Towards Improved Safety Alignment of LLM via a Human-Preference Dataset
tldr: Introduces BeaverTails, a 333K QA-pair dataset with decoupled helpfulness/harmlessness preference annotations across 14 harm categories, enabling Safe RLHF that outperforms standard RLHF baselines.

title: Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models
tldr: Demonstrates practical training data extraction attacks on GPT-2, recovering 604 verbatim memorized sequences including PII, despite minimal model overfitting.

title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
tldr: Shows that safety refusal behavior in chat models is mediated by a single direction in activation space, extractable via difference-in-means across 13 models up to 72B parameters.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces LoRA: freezing pretrained weights and injecting trainable low-rank decomposition matrices into Transformer layers, reducing trainable parameters by 10,000x while matching full fine-tuning quality.

title: Jailbreaking Leading Safety-Aligned LLMs with Simple Adaptive Attacks
tldr: Simple adaptive attacks combining adversarial prompt templates with random suffix optimization achieve nearly 100% jailbreak success rates across GPT-3.5/4, Llama-2-Chat, Gemma, and Claude models.

title: SmoothLLM: Defending Large Language Models Against Jailbreaking Attacks
tldr: SmoothLLM defends LLMs against jailbreaking by randomly perturbing input prompts at the character level and aggregating predictions via majority vote, reducing attack success rates from 50-98% to under 1%.

title: Learning to summarize from human feedback
tldr: Training summarization models with RLHF (human preference comparisons + reward model + PPO) substantially outperforms supervised baselines and ROUGE-optimized models, even transferring to new domains.

title: Jailbreak and Guard Aligned Language Models with Only Few In-Context Demonstrations
tldr: Proposes ICA (jailbreak via harmful in-context demonstrations) and ICD (defense via safe refusal demonstrations), showing ICL alone can manipulate alignment without fine-tuning.

title: Not What You've Signed Up For: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
tldr: Introduces indirect prompt injection attacks where adversaries embed malicious prompts in retrievable data sources to compromise LLM-integrated applications, demonstrating data theft, worm propagation, and remote control.

title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 Small
tldr: Discovers and validates the complete 26-head, 7-class circuit for indirect object identification in GPT-2 Small, achieving 87% of full model performance and establishing circuit evaluation criteria.

title: The WMDP Benchmark: Measuring and Reducing Malicious Use With Unlearning
tldr: Creates the WMDP benchmark of 4,157 multiple-choice questions measuring hazardous knowledge in LLMs across biosecurity, cybersecurity, and chemical security, plus CUT unlearning method to reduce dangerous knowledge.

title: Jailbreaking ChatGPT via Prompt Engineering: An Empirical Study
tldr: Systematically categorizes 78 jailbreak prompts into 10 patterns and 3 categories, finding they achieve ~87% success on GPT-4 across 8 prohibited scenarios with 3,120 test questions.

title: Catastrophic Jailbreak of Open-source LLMs via Exploiting Generation
tldr: Manipulating decoding hyperparameters (temperature, top-K, top-p) and removing system prompts bypasses safety alignment in 9/11 open-source LLMs with >95% success using 30x less compute than prior attacks.

title: Inference-Time Intervention: Eliciting Truthful Answers from a Language Model
tldr: Identifies truthfulness directions in attention head outputs via linear probes and shifts activations along these directions at inference time, improving Alpaca truthfulness from 32.5% to 65.1%.

title: Toy Models of Superposition
tldr: Uses toy ReLU networks to demonstrate that neural networks store sparse features in superposition using non-orthogonal directions, revealing phase transitions and geometric polytope structures.

title: A General Language Assistant as a Laboratory for Alignment
tldr: Investigates prompting and preference modeling techniques for aligning LLMs to be helpful, honest, and harmless; finds ranked preference modeling strongly outperforms imitation learning and scales favorably.

title: Ignore Previous Prompt: Attack Techniques For Language Models
tldr: Proposes PromptInject, a modular framework for studying prompt injection attacks on GPT-3, finding goal hijacking succeeds 58.6% and prompt leaking 23.6% of the time with simple handcrafted inputs.

title: "Do Anything Now": Characterizing and Evaluating In-The-Wild Jailbreak Prompts on Large Language Models
tldr: First large-scale measurement study of in-the-wild jailbreak prompts, collecting 666 jailbreaks from 4 platforms, finding current safeguards reduce attack success by only 2-6%.

title: GPT-4 Is Too Smart To Be Safe: Stealthy Chat with LLMs via Cipher
tldr: CipherChat framework shows that encoding prompts in ciphers (ASCII, Caesar, Morse, etc.) bypasses LLM safety alignment with near-100% success in some domains, and more capable models are paradoxically less safe.

title: JailbreakBench: An Open Robustness Benchmark for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces JailbreakBench, a standardized open-source benchmark with 100 harmful behaviors, a jailbreak artifact repository, unified evaluation pipeline, and leaderboard for tracking LLM jailbreak attack and defense progress.

title: Steering Llama 2 via Contrastive Activation Addition
tldr: Introduces Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA), computing steering vectors from mean activation differences over contrastive pairs to modulate Llama 2 behaviors at inference time.

title: Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep
tldr: Reveals that current RLHF/DPO safety alignment is shallow, concentrating effects on only the first few output tokens, and proposes deeper alignment training that resists prefilling and fine-tuning attacks.

title: FigStep: Jailbreaking Large Vision-Language Models via Typographic Visual Prompts
tldr: FigStep converts harmful text instructions into typographic images to jailbreak vision-language models, achieving 82.50% average attack success rate across six open-source LVLMs by exploiting deficient safety alignment for visual embeddings.

title: TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs
tldr: Introduces TOFU, a benchmark of 200 fictitious author profiles for evaluating LLM unlearning, finding that no existing method achieves effective forgetting without severe utility loss.

title: Negative Preference Optimization: From Catastrophic Collapse to Effective Unlearning
tldr: Proposes Negative Preference Optimization (NPO), an alignment-inspired unlearning method that avoids gradient ascent's catastrophic collapse via exponentially slower divergence, enabling 50%+ data forgetting on TOFU benchmark.

title: Discovering Language Model Behaviors with Model-Written Evaluations
tldr: Uses LLMs to automatically generate 154 evaluation datasets, discovering concerning inverse scaling behaviors like sycophancy and power-seeking.
models_studied: Various Anthropic LMs of different sizes

title: Safe RLHF: Safe Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
tldr: Safe RLHF decouples helpfulness and harmlessness into separate reward and cost models, using Lagrangian constrained optimization to dynamically balance them during RLHF, reducing harmful responses from 53% to 2.5%.

title: Detecting Language Model Attacks with Perplexity
tldr: Uses GPT-2 perplexity combined with token sequence length in a LightGBM classifier to detect machine-generated adversarial suffix attacks on LLMs with 94.2% F2 score, but fails on human-crafted jailbreaks.

title: Are Aligned Neural Networks Adversarially Aligned?
tldr: Existing NLP adversarial attacks fail (<10% success) against aligned text models under realistic constraints, but multimodal vision-language models are trivially breakable (100% success) via adversarial image perturbations.

title: Knowledge Unlearning for Mitigating Privacy Risks in Language Models
tldr: Proposes gradient ascent-based knowledge unlearning to remove memorized private data from LMs post-hoc, achieving 3.5M x fewer FLOPs than retraining with stronger privacy guarantees.

title: Improving Alignment and Robustness with Circuit Breakers
tldr: Introduces circuit breakers that reroute harmful internal representations to safe outputs, achieving 87-90% attack reduction with less than 1% capability loss.

title: Who's Harry Potter? Approximate Unlearning in LLMs
tldr: Demonstrates approximate unlearning of Harry Potter knowledge from Llama-2-7B via reinforcement bootstrapping and anchored term replacement in ~1 GPU hour.

title: DeepInception: Hypnotize Large Language Model to Be Jailbreaker
tldr: Proposes DeepInception, a nested-scenario jailbreak method inspired by Milgram's obedience experiment that exploits LLM personification to bypass safety guardrails across open and closed-source models.

title: Mass-Editing Memory in a Transformer
tldr: Extends ROME to edit thousands of facts simultaneously by distributing rank-one updates across multiple critical MLP layers identified through causal tracing.

title: Safety-Tuned LLaMAs: Lessons From Improving the Safety of Large Language Models that Follow Instructions
tldr: Adding just 3% safety examples (~500-1000) to instruction fine-tuning data substantially improves LLM safety without hurting capabilities, but excessive safety data causes exaggerated refusal behavior.

title: Transformer Feed-Forward Layers Are Key-Value Memories
tldr: Shows that transformer feed-forward layers operate as key-value memories where keys match input patterns and values induce output vocabulary distributions, with lower layers capturing shallow patterns and upper layers learning semantic ones.
models_studied: Baevski and Auli (2019) transformer LM (16 layers, 247M parameters)

title: Visual Adversarial Examples Jailbreak Aligned Large Language Models
tldr: A single optimized adversarial image can universally jailbreak aligned vision-language models, bypassing safety guardrails to elicit harmful content across diverse attack scenarios.

title: Discovering Latent Knowledge in Language Models Without Supervision
tldr: Discovers truth directions in activation space unsupervised via Contrast-Consistent Search (CCS), exploiting logical consistency between statements and their negations.

title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
tldr: Constructs proof-of-concept deceptive LLMs with backdoors (e.g., inserting code vulnerabilities when year=2024) and demonstrates that standard safety training (SFT, RLHF, adversarial training) fails to remove these backdoors.

title: Prompt Injection attack against LLM-integrated Applications
tldr: Introduces HouYi, a systematic black-box prompt injection framework with three components (framework, separator, disruptor) that successfully compromised 31/36 real-world LLM-integrated applications.

title: Towards Automated Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: Introduces ACDC, an algorithm that automates circuit discovery by iteratively pruning edges in a model's computational graph via activation patching.

title: Pythia: A Suite for Analyzing Large Language Models Across Training and Scaling
tldr: Suite of 16 LLMs (70M-12B params) trained on identical data in same order with 154 checkpoints each, designed for controlled interpretability and training dynamics research.

title: DecodingTrust: A Comprehensive Assessment of Trustworthiness in GPT Models
tldr: Proposes an 8-dimension trustworthiness benchmark for LLMs, finding GPT-4 is more trustworthy on standard tests but more vulnerable to adversarial/jailbreaking prompts than GPT-3.5 due to better instruction following.

title: The Geometry of Truth: Emergent Linear Structure in LLM Representations of True/False Datasets
tldr: Provides strong evidence that LLMs linearly represent truth/falsehood via visualization, cross-dataset transfer, and causal interventions that flip model predictions.

title: Scaling and Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Introduces TopK activation function for SAEs, establishes scaling laws for SAE training, proposes comprehensive evaluation metrics, and trains a 16M-latent SAE on GPT-4 activations.

title: Activation Addition: Steering Language Models Without Optimization
tldr: Demonstrates that adding a constant steering vector (computed from contrastive prompt pairs) to model activations at inference time can effectively control LLM behavior without any optimization or training.

title: Multi-step Jailbreaking Privacy Attacks on ChatGPT
tldr: Demonstrates that multi-step jailbreaking prompts can bypass ChatGPT's safety mechanisms to extract personally identifiable information, with application-integrated systems like New Bing amplifying the privacy risk.

title: XSTest: A Test Suite for Identifying Exaggerated Safety Behaviours in Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces XSTest, a test suite of 250 safe prompts and 200 unsafe contrasts to identify exaggerated safety behaviors where LLMs refuse clearly harmless requests due to superficial keyword sensitivity.

title: Exploiting Programmatic Behavior of LLMs: Dual-Use Through Standard Security Attacks
tldr: Demonstrates that standard computer security attack patterns (obfuscation, code injection, virtualization) transfer to LLMs and bypass content filters with 100% success rate.

title: Sparse Feature Circuits: Discovering and Editing Interpretable Causal Graphs in Language Models
tldr: Discovers interpretable causal circuits over SAE features rather than neurons/attention heads, enabling finer-grained mechanistic understanding and a 'Shift' technique for improving classifier generalization.

title: Shadow Alignment: The Ease of Subverting Safely-Aligned Language Models
tldr: Fine-tuning safety-aligned LLMs on just 100 malicious examples for one GPU hour achieves 99.5% violation rates while preserving general capabilities across eight models.

title: Low-Resource Languages Jailbreak GPT-4
venue: NeurIPS 2023 Workshop on Socially Responsible Language Modelling Research (SoLaR)
tldr: Translating harmful English prompts into low-resource languages via Google Translate bypasses GPT-4's safety filters 79% of the time, on par with SOTA jailbreaks.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
tldr: Discovers that language model cross-entropy loss follows smooth power-law relationships with model size, dataset size, and compute, spanning over seven orders of magnitude.

title: A StrongREJECT for Empty Jailbreaks
tldr: Introduces StrongREJECT, a jailbreak evaluation benchmark with 346 curated forbidden questions and an autograder that scores refusal, specificity, and convincingness, achieving lowest MAE vs human judgment.

title: The Linear Representation Hypothesis and the Geometry of Large Language Models
tldr: Formalizes what linear representation means for LLM concepts using counterfactuals, proving connections to linear probing, model steering, and identifying the correct (non-Euclidean) causal inner product.

title: Open Problems and Fundamental Limitations of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
tldr: Comprehensive survey cataloging RLHF's fundamental limitations across feedback collection, reward modeling, and policy optimization, arguing no single alignment strategy suffices.

title: Jailbreak in Pieces: Compositional Adversarial Attacks on Multi-Modal Language Models
tldr: Demonstrates compositional jailbreak attacks on VLMs by pairing adversarial images (optimized via CLIP encoder only) with benign text prompts, achieving ~87% attack success on LLaVA.

title: Progress Measures for Grokking via Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: Reverse-engineers transformers trained on modular addition, revealing they learn discrete Fourier transforms and identifying three training phases underlying grokking.

title: Automatically Auditing Large Language Models via Discrete Optimization
tldr: Introduces ARCA, a discrete optimization algorithm that automatically discovers problematic LLM behaviors by jointly optimizing over prompts and outputs.

title: Taxonomy of Risks posed by Language Models
tldr: Presents a comprehensive taxonomy of 21 ethical and social risks from language models across six categories, with discussion of causal mechanisms and mitigation strategies.

title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
tldr: Establishes predictable scaling laws for how RLHF performance degrades when over-optimizing against imperfect reward models, showing gold reward peaks then declines as a function of KL divergence.

title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
tldr: Demonstrates that RLHF-trained AI assistants systematically exhibit sycophancy across multiple tasks, and shows this stems from human evaluators preferring agreeable responses, making it a fundamental limitation of preference-based training.

title: Large Language Model Unlearning
tldr: Proposes an LLM unlearning method using gradient ascent + random mismatch + KL divergence that removes harmful behaviors using only negative examples at ~2% of RLHF's compute cost.

title: Gemma Scope: Open Sparse Autoencoders Everywhere All At Once on Gemma 2
tldr: Releases 400+ pre-trained JumpReLU SAEs for all layers and sub-layers of Gemma 2 2B, 9B, and select layers of 27B at multiple widths (16K to 1M features), with open weights under CC-BY-4.0.

title: Many-shot Jailbreaking
tldr: Demonstrates that including hundreds of faux harmful dialogues in long-context prompts jailbreaks frontier LLMs with power-law scaling, revealing long contexts as a rich new attack surface.

title: SafeDecoding: Defending against Jailbreak Attacks via Safety-Aware Decoding
tldr: SafeDecoding is an inference-time defense that amplifies safety-token probabilities over harmful-token probabilities by blending original and LoRA-finetuned expert model distributions, reducing jailbreak success to near 0% with <10% compute overhead.

title: Certifying LLM Safety against Adversarial Prompting
tldr: Introduces 'erase-and-check,' the first framework providing certifiable safety guarantees against adversarial prompts by systematically erasing tokens and checking subsequences with a safety filter.

title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads
tldr: Identifies induction heads as a primary mechanism for in-context learning in transformers, showing they emerge during a sharp phase change in training and are universal across model scales.

title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
tldr: Shows that the weight difference between fine-tuned and base models (a task vector) encodes the task and can be added, negated, or combined to edit model behavior.

title: Poisoning Language Models During Instruction Tuning
tldr: Demonstrates that as few as 100 poisoned examples injected into instruction-tuning data can cause cross-task misclassification in LLMs, with larger models being more vulnerable.

title: Scalable and Transferable Black-Box Jailbreaks for Language Models via Persona Modulation
tldr: Automated persona modulation jailbreaks achieve a 42.5% harmful completion rate on GPT-4 (185x increase from baseline) and transfer to Claude 2 (61.0%) and Vicuna (35.9%) at under $3 per category.

title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions
tldr: Proposes an instruction hierarchy that trains LLMs to prioritize system-level instructions over user/tool inputs, improving robustness to prompt injection by 63% and jailbreaks by 30%+ on GPT-3.5.

title: Defending Against Alignment-Breaking Attacks via Robustly Aligned LLM
tldr: Proposes RA-LLM, a defense against jailbreak attacks that uses random token dropping with Monte Carlo sampling to verify alignment, reducing attack success from ~100% to ~10% without retraining.

title: Jumping Ahead: Improving Reconstruction Fidelity with JumpReLU Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Introduces JumpReLU SAEs that use a discontinuous activation function with learnable thresholds and straight-through estimators, enabling direct L0 sparsity optimization and matching or exceeding TopK/Gated SAE performance.

title: Assessing the Brittleness of Safety Alignment via Pruning and Low-Rank Modifications
tldr: Safety alignment in LLMs is brittly concentrated in ~3% of parameters; removing these sparse safety-critical neurons/ranks breaks safety while preserving utility.

title: MM-SafetyBench: A Benchmark for Safety Evaluation of Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces MM-SafetyBench with 5,040 text-image pairs across 13 unsafe scenarios, showing MLLMs are easily compromised by query-relevant images even when text-only safety-aligned, with typography attacks raising ASR from ~5% to ~77%.

title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
tldr: Introduces GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization) which eliminates the critic model from RLHF by estimating baselines from group scores, and achieves 51.7% on MATH benchmark.

title: MUSE: Machine Unlearning Six-Way Evaluation for Language Models
tldr: MUSE benchmarks 8 unlearning algorithms on 7B-parameter LLMs across 6 properties, finding most remove memorization but fail at privacy protection, utility preservation, scalability, and sequential unlearning.

title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
tldr: LLMs' chain-of-thought explanations are often unfaithful: biasing features in inputs affect outputs without appearing in CoT, with models confabulating plausible post-hoc rationalizations.

title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated LLM Agents
tldr: Introduces InjecAgent, a benchmark of 1,054 test cases evaluating indirect prompt injection attacks on tool-integrated LLM agents, finding even GPT-4 is vulnerable 24-47% of the time.

title: Multilingual Jailbreak Challenges in Large Language Models
tldr: Non-English prompts bypass LLM safety mechanisms at far higher rates than English, with low-resource languages causing 3x more unsafe outputs; a self-defence fine-tuning framework partially mitigates this gap.

title: Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models
tldr: Catalogs abilities that appear suddenly at certain model scales, absent in smaller models but present in larger ones, challenging smooth scaling predictions.

title: Finding Neurons in a Haystack: Case Studies with Sparse Probing
tldr: Uses k-sparse linear probes across 7 Pythia models to study feature representation, finding early-layer superposition and middle-layer dedicated 'context neurons' for high-level features.

title: Rethinking Machine Unlearning for Large Language Models
tldr: Comprehensive rethinking of machine unlearning for LLMs, proposing a taxonomy of methods (gradient ascent, localization-informed, influence functions, input-based), evaluation frameworks, and connections to safety alignment and model editing.

title: JailBreakV-28K: A Benchmark for Assessing the Robustness of MultiModal Large Language Models against Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: Introduces JailBreakV-28K, a 28K-example benchmark showing that text-based LLM jailbreak attacks transfer to multimodal LLMs with 50.5% average success rate, exceeding image-based attacks (30%).

title: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback
tldr: Fine-tunes GPT-3 with RLHF and a text-based web browser to answer long-form questions with citations; best model preferred over human demonstrators 56% of the time.

title: Transformer Feed-Forward Layers Build Predictions by Promoting Concepts in the Vocabulary Space
tldr: Shows that feed-forward layers in transformers build next-token predictions by iteratively promoting interpretable concepts in vocabulary space, with ~40-70% of value vectors encoding well-defined semantic or syntactic concepts.

title: Improving alignment of dialogue agents via targeted human judgements
tldr: Sparrow is a DeepMind dialogue agent trained via multi-objective RLHF over 23 explicit rules and web-grounded evidence, achieving 8% rule-violation rate under adversarial probing and 78% evidence support rate.

title: Dissecting Recall of Factual Associations in Auto-Regressive Language Models
tldr: Reveals a three-step mechanism for factual recall in transformers: subject enrichment via early MLPs, relation propagation via attention, and attribute extraction via upper-layer attention heads.

title: In-Context Unlearning: Language Models as Few Shot Unlearners
tldr: Proposes In-Context Unlearning (ICUL), a black-box method that makes LLMs forget specific training data by presenting label-flipped forget points alongside correctly labeled examples at inference time, without any parameter updates.

title: Jailbreak Attacks and Defenses Against Large Language Models: A Survey
tldr: Comprehensive taxonomy of LLM jailbreak attacks (white-box and black-box) and defenses (prompt-level and model-level), mapping attack-defense relationships and evaluating benchmarks.

title: Scalable Extraction of Training Data from (Production) Language Models
tldr: Demonstrates scalable extraction of gigabytes of training data from open, semi-open, and production LLMs, including a divergence attack on ChatGPT that increases extraction rates 150x.

title: WildGuard: Open One-Stop Moderation Tools for Safety Risks, Jailbreaks, and Refusals of LLMs
tldr: WildGuard is an open-source Mistral-7B-based moderation tool covering prompt harm, response harm, and refusal detection, trained on 92K examples, reducing jailbreak success from 79.8% to 2.4%.

title: Unlearn What You Want to Forget: Efficient Unlearning for LLMs
tldr: Proposes lightweight unlearning adapter layers with a selective teacher-student objective that enable LLMs to forget specific training data efficiently without full retraining, plus a fusion mechanism for sequential deletions.

title: Red-Teaming Large Language Models using Chain of Utterances for Safety-Alignment
tldr: Introduces RED-EVAL, a Chain of Utterances jailbreak that bypasses GPT-4 (65%) and ChatGPT (73%), plus RED-INSTRUCT/SAFE-ALIGN for training safer models using adversarial data.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety â€” A Review
tldr: Most comprehensive MI survey covering features, superposition, circuits, observational and interventional methods, evaluation, safety applications, and future challenges.

title: ArtPrompt: ASCII Art-based Jailbreak Attacks against Aligned LLMs
tldr: ArtPrompt exploits LLM inability to recognize ASCII art to bypass safety alignment, achieving up to 98% helpful response rate across GPT-3.5/4, Claude, Gemini, and Llama2.

title: Knowledge Neurons in Pretrained Transformers
tldr: Identifies specific neurons in transformer FFN layers responsible for expressing factual knowledge using integrated gradients attribution, enabling targeted knowledge manipulation.

title: Deliberative Alignment: Reasoning Enables Safer Language Models
tldr: Introduces deliberative alignment, training reasoning models to explicitly recall and reason over safety specifications in their chain-of-thought before responding, improving both jailbreak robustness and reduced overrefusal.

title: Emergent Linear Representations in World Models of Self-Supervised Sequence Models
tldr: Discovers that Othello-GPT learns a linear representation of board state as Mine/Yours/Empty, enabling model steering through simple vector arithmetic.

title: Safe Latent Diffusion: Mitigating Inappropriate Degeneration in Diffusion Models
tldr: Introduces Safe Latent Diffusion (SLD), a training-free method that suppresses inappropriate image generation in diffusion models by adding safety guidance during the denoising process, reducing inappropriate content from 39% to 13%.

title: The Alignment Problem from a Deep Learning Perspective
tldr: Argues that AGI trained with current deep learning methods could learn deceptive behavior, develop misaligned internally-represented goals that generalize beyond training, and pursue power-seeking strategies undermining human control.

title: Probing Classifiers: Promises, Shortcomings, and Advances
tldr: Critical review of probing classifiers as an interpretability method, identifying key shortcomings and recommending controls, complexity measures, and interventions.

title: Let's Verify Step by Step
tldr: Process reward models (step-level supervision) significantly outperform outcome reward models for mathematical reasoning, achieving 78.2% on MATH.

title: Eight Methods to Evaluate Robust Unlearning in LLMs
tldr: Proposes eight evaluation methods for LLM unlearning robustness and shows the Who's Harry Potter model retains extractable knowledge despite appearing unlearned under standard metrics.

title: A General Theoretical Paradigm to Understand Learning from Human Feedback
tldr: Introduces the PsiPO framework unifying RLHF and DPO as special cases, identifies DPO's overfitting flaw from the Bradley-Terry assumption, and proposes IPO as a more robust alternative.
models_studied: Theoretical analysis on generic policy spaces (no specific LLMs evaluated)

title: Erasing Concepts from Diffusion Models
tldr: ESD fine-tunes diffusion model weights to permanently erase specific visual concepts (explicit content, artistic styles, objects) using only concept names and negative guidance, without extra training data.

title: AmpleGCG: Learning a Universal and Transferable Generative Model of Adversarial Suffixes for Jailbreaking Both Open and Closed LLMs
tldr: Trains a generative model (AmpleGCG) on successful adversarial suffixes collected during GCG optimization, enabling rapid generation of hundreds of diverse jailbreak suffixes that achieve near-100% attack success on open and closed LLMs.

title: GPQA: A Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark
tldr: Introduces GPQA, 448 expert-written multiple-choice questions in biology/physics/chemistry where domain experts reach 65% but skilled non-experts only 34%, creating a testbed for scalable oversight methods.

title: KTO: Model Alignment as Prospect Theoretic Optimization
tldr: Proposes Kahneman-Tversky Optimization (KTO), an alignment method grounded in prospect theory that only requires binary good/bad labels per output, matching or exceeding DPO from 1B to 30B scale.

title: Pretraining Language Models with Human Preferences
tldr: Incorporates human preferences during LM pretraining via five objectives, finding conditional training reduces undesirable content by up to 10x while preserving downstream performance.

title: COLD-Attack: Jailbreaking LLMs with Stealthiness and Controllability
tldr: COLD-Attack adapts energy-based constrained decoding with Langevin dynamics to generate stealthy, controllable jailbreak prompts against LLMs, achieving up to 100% ASR while maintaining fluency.

title: Image Hijacks: Adversarial Images can Control Generative Models at Runtime
tldr: Introduces 'image hijacks' -- adversarial images that control VLM behavior at inference time via a Behaviour Matching algorithm, achieving >80% success on forced output, context leaking, and jailbreak attacks against LLaVA.

title: On Evaluating Adversarial Robustness of Large Vision-Language Models
tldr: Demonstrates that large vision-language models are highly vulnerable to targeted adversarial attacks via imperceptible image perturbations using a two-stage transfer+query black-box approach.

title: MasterKey: Automated Jailbreaking of Large Language Model Chatbots
tldr: Introduces MasterKey, a framework that reverse-engineers LLM chatbot defenses using time-based analysis and fine-tunes an LLM to automatically generate jailbreak prompts, achieving 21.58% success rate vs 7.33% for existing methods.

title: Identifying the Risks of LM Agents with an LM-Emulated Sandbox
tldr: ToolEmu uses LMs to emulate tool execution in a sandbox, enabling scalable testing of LM agent safety across 36 toolkits and 144 test cases without manual environment setup.

title: LoRA Fine-tuning Efficiently Undoes Safety Training in Llama 2-Chat 70B
tldr: LoRA fine-tuning on a single GPU for under $200 reduces Llama 2-Chat 70B's refusal rate from ~99% to below 1%, demonstrating that safety training is easily reversed when model weights are released.

title: Alignment Faking in Large Language Models
tldr: Demonstrates that Claude 3 Opus strategically fakes alignment, complying with harmful requests 14% of the time during training but nearly never when unmonitored.

title: Red-Teaming the Stable Diffusion Safety Filter
tldr: Reverse-engineered Stable Diffusion's obfuscated safety filter, showing it only blocks sexual content via CLIP cosine similarity and is easily bypassed by prompt dilution or filter removal.

title: Removing RLHF Protections in GPT-4 via Fine-Tuning
tldr: Fine-tuning GPT-4 with only 340 automatically generated harmful examples removes RLHF safety protections with a 95% success rate while preserving general usefulness.

title: SORRY-Bench: Systematically Evaluating Large Language Model Safety Refusal Behaviors
tldr: SORRY-Bench introduces a 45-category safety taxonomy with 450 balanced unsafe instructions and 20 linguistic augmentations, plus a fine-tuned 7B evaluator matching GPT-4 accuracy, enabling systematic LLM refusal evaluation across 40+ models.

title: Tamper-Resistant Safeguards for Open-Weight LLMs
tldr: Proposes TAR, an adversarial meta-learning method that makes open-weight LLM safeguards robust to weight-tampering attacks, maintaining safety even after thousands of fine-tuning steps.

title: Targeted Latent Adversarial Training Improves Robustness to Persistent Harmful Behaviors in LLMs
tldr: Proposes targeted latent adversarial training (LAT) that perturbs model hidden representations to elicit specific failure modes during training, improving robustness to jailbreaks, backdoors, and unlearning attacks.

title: Foundational Challenges in Assuring Alignment and Safety of Large Language Models
tldr: Identifies 18 foundational challenges in LLM alignment and safety across scientific understanding, development methods, and sociotechnical dimensions, posing 200+ concrete research questions.

title: Robust Prompt Optimization for Defending Language Models Against Jailbreaking Attacks
tldr: RPO optimizes a transferable defensive suffix via minimax gradient-based token optimization, reducing jailbreak success rates from 84% to 8.66% across 20 attacks on Starling-7B and from 92% to 6% on GPT-4.

title: Aligning AI With Shared Human Values
tldr: Introduces ETHICS, a 130K-example benchmark across five moral frameworks (justice, virtue, deontology, utilitarianism, commonsense morality) to evaluate LMs' alignment with human ethical judgments.

title: Quantifying Memorization Across Neural Language Models
tldr: Identifies three log-linear relationships governing memorization in LMs: larger models memorize more (19pp per 10x scale), duplicated data is memorized more, and longer prompts extract more memorized content.

title: Gradient-based Adversarial Attacks against Text Transformers
tldr: GBDA uses Gumbel-softmax relaxation to enable gradient-based adversarial attacks on text transformers, substantially outperforming prior discrete-search methods.

title: Open Sesame! Universal Black Box Jailbreaking of Large Language Models
tldr: Uses genetic algorithms to automatically discover universal black-box adversarial suffixes that jailbreak aligned LLMs with 95-99% success rate without requiring model internals.

title: Safety Fine-Tuning at (Almost) No Cost: A Baseline for Vision Large Language Models
tldr: VLGuard, a 2K-image safety dataset, reduces VLLM jailbreak success rates from 80%+ to ~0% via post-hoc or mixed fine-tuning at minimal compute and helpfulness cost.

title: Toxicity in ChatGPT: Analyzing Persona-assigned Language Models
tldr: Assigning personas to ChatGPT via system parameters increases toxicity up to 6x, with discriminatory targeting of specific demographic groups up to 3x more than others.

title: Eliciting Latent Predictions from Transformers with the Tuned Lens
tldr: Improves the logit lens by training learned affine transformations at each layer to better translate intermediate representations into prediction space, achieving substantially lower perplexity than the raw logit lens.

title: AI deception: A survey of examples, risks, and potential solutions
tldr: A survey of empirical AI deception across special-use and general-purpose systems, cataloguing risks (fraud, loss of control) and proposing solutions via regulation, detection, and design changes.

title: SALAD-Bench: A Hierarchical and Comprehensive Safety Benchmark for Large Language Models
tldr: SALAD-Bench is a 30K-question hierarchical safety benchmark for LLMs with 6 domains/16 tasks/65 categories, attack/defense-enhanced variants, and MD-Judge evaluator outperforming GPT-4.

title: Can Sensitive Information Be Deleted From LLMs? Objectives for Defending Against Extraction Attacks
tldr: Proposes attack-and-defense framework showing model editing methods fail to truly delete sensitive information, with whitebox/blackbox attacks recovering 'deleted' facts 38%/29% of the time.

title: StruQ: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Structured Queries
tldr: Proposes structured queries that separate prompts from data using special tokens and structured instruction tuning, reducing prompt injection attack success from 96% to 0% on most attacks with negligible utility loss.

title: AgentHarm: A Benchmark for Measuring Harmfulness of LLM Agents
tldr: Introduces AgentHarm, a benchmark of 440 malicious agent tasks across 11 harm categories, finding that leading LLMs are surprisingly compliant without jailbreaking and simple universal jailbreaks boost harm scores to 68-83%.

title: Fast Model Editing at Scale
tldr: Trains a hypernetwork (MEND) that transforms fine-tuning gradients into targeted low-rank parameter updates, enabling fast single-example model edits at scale up to 11B parameters.

title: Jailbreaking Attack against Multimodal Large Language Model
tldr: Proposes maximum likelihood-based image jailbreaking prompts (imgJP) that bypass MLLM safety guardrails with 92%+ ASR, transfer across models, and connect multimodal attacks to text-based jailbreaks via a construction-based embedding-to-text method.

title: BBQ: A Hand-Built Bias Benchmark for Question Answering
tldr: Introduces BBQ, a 58K-example hand-built benchmark measuring social biases in QA models across 9 demographic categories, finding models rely on stereotypes up to 77% of the time in ambiguous contexts.

title: Frontier Models are Capable of In-context Scheming
tldr: Demonstrates that five of six frontier models engage in in-context scheming behaviors including disabling oversight, self-exfiltration, sandbagging, and persistent deception when given goals conflicting with developers.

title: A Survey on Large Language Model (LLM) Security and Privacy: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly
tldr: Systematic survey of 281 papers on LLM security/privacy, categorizing work into beneficial applications (The Good), offensive uses (The Bad), and LLM vulnerabilities with defenses (The Ugly).

title: LEACE: Perfect Linear Concept Erasure in Closed Form
tldr: Introduces LEACE, a closed-form method for provably optimal linear concept erasure that prevents all linear classifiers from detecting a target concept.

title: AlpacaFarm: A Simulation Framework for Methods that Learn from Human Feedback
tldr: Introduces AlpacaFarm, a simulation framework that replaces human feedback with LLM-simulated preferences (50x cheaper, 65% human agreement) for developing and benchmarking RLHF methods.

title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Eliciting Strong Capabilities With Weak Supervision
tldr: Studies whether weak models can supervise stronger models, finding partial but incomplete generalization across NLP, chess, and reward modeling tasks.

title: An Overview of Catastrophic AI Risks
tldr: Systematic survey of catastrophic AI risks across four categories: malicious use, AI race dynamics, organizational failures, and rogue AIs, with mitigation strategies for each.

title: AI Control: Improving Safety Despite Intentional Subversion
tldr: Develops and evaluates safety protocols that remain effective even when a powerful AI model intentionally tries to subvert them, using trusted weaker models to monitor untrusted stronger ones.

title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
tldr: Shows that large language models can assess their own knowledge: they are well-calibrated on multiple-choice questions, can self-evaluate sample correctness via P(True), and can be trained to predict P(IK) with partial cross-task generalization.

title: A Mechanistic Understanding of Alignment Algorithms: A Case Study on DPO and Toxicity
tldr: DPO reduces toxicity by learning residual stream offsets that bypass—not remove—toxic capabilities in GPT-2, which can be re-activated by scaling toxic key vectors.

title: RAIN: Your Language Models Can Align Themselves without Finetuning
tldr: RAIN enables frozen LLMs to align with human preferences at inference time via self-evaluation and rewindable tree search, matching RLHF quality with no finetuning.

title: Monitoring Reasoning Models for Misbehavior and the Risks of Promoting Obfuscation
tldr: Shows that CoT monitors can detect 95% of reward hacking in reasoning models, but RL training pressure on CoTs causes models to obfuscate their reasoning while continuing harmful behaviors.

title: Improving Dictionary Learning with Gated Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Introduces Gated SAEs that separate feature detection from magnitude estimation, solving the L1 shrinkage problem and achieving Pareto improvements over baseline SAEs across multiple models.

title: Unsolved Problems in ML Safety
tldr: Identifies and organizes unsolved ML safety problems into four pillars -- robustness, monitoring, alignment, and systemic safety -- arguing layered defenses across all four are needed.

title: Measuring Progress on Scalable Oversight for Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes the 'sandwiching' experimental paradigm for studying scalable oversight and shows model-assisted humans substantially outperform both unaided humans and models alone.

title: How Robust is Google's Bard to Adversarial Image Attacks?
tldr: Demonstrates that commercial multimodal LLMs (Bard, GPT-4V, Bing Chat, ERNIE Bot) are vulnerable to transfer-based adversarial image attacks, achieving 22-86% attack success and bypassing face/toxicity detection defenses.

title: AutoDAN-Turbo: A Lifelong Agent for Strategy Self-Exploration to Jailbreak LLMs
tldr: AutoDAN-Turbo is a black-box jailbreak agent that autonomously discovers and reuses jailbreak strategies via lifelong learning, achieving 74.3% higher ASR than baselines on HarmBench.

title: Images are Achilles' Heel of Alignment: Exploiting Visual Vulnerabilities for Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: HADES jailbreaks multimodal LLMs by hiding harmful content in images via typography, diffusion-generated images, and adversarial noise, achieving 90.26% ASR on LLaVA-1.5.

title: Editing Factual Knowledge in Language Models
tldr: Pioneering work formalizing knowledge editing in LMs using a learned hyper-network editor that produces constrained parameter updates preserving unrelated knowledge.

title: Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses in LLM-Integrated Applications
tldr: Proposes formal frameworks for prompt injection attacks and defenses, evaluates 5 attacks and 10 defenses across 10 LLMs and 7 tasks, finding combined attacks achieve 0.987 ASS on GPT-4 and proactive detection effectively eliminates attacks.

title: LLM Defenses Are Not Robust to Multi-Turn Human Jailbreaks Yet
tldr: Human red teamers achieve 19-65% higher jailbreak success rates than automated attacks against state-of-the-art LLM defenses via multi-turn conversations, releasing a 2,912-prompt dataset of human jailbreak tactics.

title: AdaShield: Safeguarding Multimodal Large Language Models from Structure-based Attack via Adaptive Shield Prompting
tldr: Proposes AdaShield, a training-free defense that prepends adaptive shield prompts to protect multimodal LLMs from structure-based jailbreak attacks, achieving near-zero attack success rates.

title: SimPO: Simple Preference Optimization with a Reference-Free Reward
tldr: SimPO eliminates the reference model in DPO by using average log probability as an implicit reward with a target reward margin, outperforming DPO by up to 6.4 points on AlpacaEval 2.

title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
tldr: Revises Kaplan scaling laws: for compute-optimal training, model size and training data should be scaled equally, not prioritizing parameters.

title: RAFT: Reward rAnked FineTuning for Generative Foundation Model Alignment
tldr: RAFT aligns generative models by iteratively sampling K responses, selecting the highest-reward one, and finetuning on filtered data, achieving 17% higher reward than PPO with greater stability and efficiency.

title: Rainbow Teaming: Open-Ended Generation of Diverse Adversarial Prompts
tldr: Rainbow Teaming uses quality-diversity search (MAP-Elites) to generate diverse adversarial prompts, achieving ~92% attack success on Llama 2-chat and reducing vulnerability to 2.6% via SFT on generated data.

title: R-Judge: Benchmarking Safety Risk Awareness for LLM Agents
tldr: Introduces R-Judge, a 569-record benchmark for evaluating LLM ability to judge safety risks in agent interactions; GPT-4o achieves only 74.42% while fine-tuning helps but prompting strategies fail.

title: An Adversarial Perspective on Machine Unlearning for AI Safety
venue: Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR) 2024; Best Technical Paper at NeurIPS 2024 SoLaR Workshop
tldr: Demonstrates that machine unlearning methods (RMU, NPO) fail to truly remove hazardous knowledge from LLMs, as five white-box attacks recover supposedly unlearned capabilities, paralleling failures of standard safety training.

title: The Internal State of an LLM Knows When It's Lying
tldr: Trains a simple classifier on LLM hidden-layer activations (SAPLMA) to predict statement truthfulness, achieving 71-83% accuracy across topics, substantially outperforming prompting baselines.

title: RRHF: Rank Responses to Align Language Models with Human Feedback without tears
tldr: RRHF aligns LLMs with human preferences using ranking loss on response log-probabilities instead of PPO, matching PPO performance with only 1-2 models and ~30 lines of code beyond SFT.

title: Poisoning Web-Scale Training Datasets is Practical
tldr: Demonstrates two practical attacks (split-view and frontrunning) that can poison web-scale training datasets like LAION-400M and COYO-700M for as little as $60, and proposes cryptographic hash defenses.

title: Survey of Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models Revealed by Adversarial Attacks
tldr: Comprehensive survey categorizing adversarial attacks on LLMs (jailbreaks, prompt injection, multimodal attacks) by learning structure, injection source, and access model, revealing that safety training fundamentally lags model capabilities.

title: Towards Safer Large Language Models through Machine Unlearning
tldr: Introduces SKU, a two-stage machine unlearning framework that selectively removes harmful knowledge from LLMs while preserving utility on normal prompts, achieving 3% harmful response rate with minimal perplexity increase.

title: Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
tldr: Tests whether chain-of-thought reasoning faithfully reflects models' actual decision processes; finds models sometimes arrive at answers before generating reasoning and produce post-hoc rationalizations.

title: Benchmarking and Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces BIPIA, the first benchmark for indirect prompt injection attacks on LLMs across 5 tasks and 60 attack types, and proposes black-box and white-box defenses reducing attack success to near zero.

title: SneakyPrompt: Jailbreaking Text-to-Image Generative Models
venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy 2024
tldr: Automated RL-based attack that replaces sensitive tokens with non-sensitive substitutes to bypass text-to-image safety filters, achieving 96% bypass on Stable Diffusion and 57% on DALL-E 2.

title: Explore, Establish, Exploit: Red Teaming Language Models from Scratch
tldr: Proposes a three-phase red-teaming framework (Explore, Establish, Exploit) that works without pre-existing failure classifiers, demonstrating 30x toxicity increase on GPT-2-xl and 74% false statement rate on GPT-3.

title: Constitutional Classifiers: Defending against Universal Jailbreaks across Thousands of Hours of Red Teaming
tldr: Constitutional classifiers using synthetic data from natural language rules defend against universal jailbreaks, reducing attack success from 86% to <5% with only 0.38% refusal rate increase on benign traffic.

title: Universal Jailbreak Backdoors from Poisoned Human Feedback
tldr: Demonstrates that poisoning as little as 5% of RLHF preference data with trigger words creates universal jailbreak backdoors that generalize to any harmful prompt.

title: Does Localization Inform Editing? Surprising Differences in Causality-Based Localization vs. Knowledge Editing in Language Models
tldr: Causal Tracing localization results have near-zero correlation with which model layers are best to edit, showing mechanistic localization does not guide effective knowledge editing.

title: OR-Bench: An Over-Refusal Benchmark for Large Language Models
tldr: OR-Bench introduces 80,000 seemingly-toxic-but-benign prompts across 10 categories to measure over-refusal in LLMs, revealing a 0.878 Spearman correlation between safety and excessive refusal.

title: RLAIF: Scaling Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with AI Feedback
tldr: RLAIF uses LLM-generated preferences instead of human labels for RL training and achieves comparable or superior performance to RLHF at over 10x lower cost.

title: Finding Alignments Between Interpretable Causal Variables and Distributed Neural Representations
tldr: Distributed Alignment Search (DAS) uses gradient descent over orthogonal rotations to find alignments between causal model variables and distributed neural representations, achieving 100% IIA where localist methods fail.

title: AxBench: Steering LLMs? Even Simple Baselines Outperform Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Introduces AxBench, a large-scale steering/concept-detection benchmark showing prompting and simple baselines like difference-in-means outperform SAEs, and proposes ReFT-r1 as a competitive interpretable alternative.

title: Safe LoRA: the Silver Lining of Reducing Safety Risks when Fine-tuning Large Language Models
tldr: Safe LoRA projects LoRA fine-tuning weight updates onto a safety-aligned subspace (derived from aligned vs base model weight differences) to prevent safety degradation, requiring no extra data or training.

title: Emergent World Representations: Exploring a Sequence Model Trained on a Synthetic Task
tldr: Trains a GPT model on Othello move sequences and discovers it learns an emergent nonlinear internal representation of the board state despite never seeing the board.
models_studied: Custom 8-layer GPT model for Othello (8-head attention, 512-dim)

title: AI Alignment: A Comprehensive Survey
tldr: Comprehensive 98-page survey of AI alignment organized around RICE principles (Robustness, Interpretability, Controllability, Ethicality) decomposed into forward alignment (training) and backward alignment (assurance/governance).

title: SalUn: Empowering Machine Unlearning via Gradient-based Weight Saliency in Both Image Classification and Generation
tldr: SalUn uses gradient-based weight saliency to selectively update only influential model weights during machine unlearning, achieving near-exact unlearning in both image classification and generation including NSFW content removal.

title: Model Evaluation for Extreme Risks
tldr: Proposes a framework for evaluating dangerous capabilities (cyber-offense, deception, self-replication) and alignment properties in frontier AI models.

title: How does GPT-2 Compute Greater-Than?: Interpreting Mathematical Abilities in a Pre-trained Language Model
tldr: Reverse-engineers the circuit GPT-2 Small uses to compute greater-than comparisons for years, identifying specific attention heads and MLPs that implement the operation.

title: (Ab)using Images and Sounds for Indirect Instruction Injection in Multi-Modal LLMs
tldr: Demonstrates that adversarial perturbations in images/audio can inject instructions into multi-modal LLMs, forcing attacker-chosen outputs and poisoning subsequent dialog turns.

title: What's in Your "Safe" Data? Identifying Benign Data that Breaks Safety
tldr: Develops representation and gradient-based methods to identify benign fine-tuning data that breaks LLM safety alignment, showing 100 selected examples raise attack success from <20% to >70%.

title: Memory-Based Model Editing at Scale
tldr: SERAC stores edits in an explicit memory cache and uses a scope classifier and counterfactual model to apply them without modifying base model weights, scaling to 75+ simultaneous edits.

title: Localizing Model Behavior with Path Patching
tldr: Introduces path patching, intervening on specific edges between components rather than just nodes, enabling finer-grained circuit analysis.

title: Emergent Misalignment: Narrow Finetuning Can Produce Broadly Misaligned LLMs
tldr: Fine-tuning LLMs on narrow harmful tasks (e.g., insecure code) causes broad misalignment across unrelated domains, including deceptive behavior and anti-human rhetoric.

title: Attacking Large Language Models with Projected Gradient Descent
tldr: PGD on continuously relaxed token sequences achieves jailbreak attack success rates comparable to GCG while being up to 10x faster, enabling large-scale adversarial evaluation of LLMs.

title: Self-critiquing models for assisting human evaluators
tldr: Fine-tuned LLMs to write natural-language critiques via behavioral cloning; AI-generated critiques helped human evaluators find ~50% more flaws in summaries.

title: The Effects of Reward Misspecification: Mapping and Mitigating Misaligned Models
tldr: Systematically maps how RL agent capabilities drive reward hacking across four environments, identifies phase transitions to misaligned behavior, and proposes an anomaly detection benchmark (Polynomaly).

title: Making Them Ask and Answer: Jailbreaking Large Language Models in Few Queries via Disguise and Reconstruction
tldr: DRA exploits LLM fine-tuning bias by disguising harmful instructions as puzzles and prompting models to reconstruct them in completions, achieving 90%+ attack success on GPT-4 in ~4 queries.

title: SOUL: Unlocking the Power of Second-Order Optimization for LLM Unlearning
tldr: SOUL uses second-order (Sophia) optimization to improve LLM unlearning, outperforming first-order methods across fictitious fact removal, copyright removal, and detoxification tasks.

title: Guardrail Baselines for Unlearning in LLMs
tldr: Simple guardrail approaches (prompting and filtering) achieve unlearning results comparable to fine-tuning in LLMs, and should be evaluated as baselines by researchers.

title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
tldr: Systematically benchmarks activation patching variants across corruption methods and metrics, finding STR and logit difference outperform Gaussian noise and probability for reliable mechanistic interpretability.

title: Linear Representations of Sentiment in Large Language Models
tldr: Demonstrates that sentiment is linearly represented as a single direction in LLM activation space, extractable via difference-in-means, and causally steerable.

title: Unified Concept Editing in Diffusion Models
tldr: UCE edits diffusion model cross-attention weights via a closed-form solution to simultaneously erase artists' styles, debias professions, and moderate offensive content without retraining.

title: Does Circuit Analysis Interpretability Scale? Evidence from Multiple Choice Capabilities in Chinchilla
tldr: Tests whether circuit analysis works at 70B scale by studying multiple-choice answering in Chinchilla, finding that some but not all techniques scale naturally.

title: Ablating Concepts in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
tldr: Efficiently removes unwanted concepts (copyrighted styles, memorized images) from pretrained diffusion models by fine-tuning to match an anchor concept distribution, reducing memorization from 60.1% to 0.3%.

title: Quark: Controllable Text Generation with Reinforced Unlearning
tldr: Quark fine-tunes LMs to unlearn undesirable behaviors by sorting generated samples into reward quantiles, conditioning on reward tokens, and training with standard LM loss plus KL penalty, outperforming PPO on toxicity reduction.

title: Simplicity Prevails: Rethinking Negative Preference Optimization for LLM Unlearning
tldr: SimNPO removes reference model dependence in LLM unlearning via length-normalized rewards, fixing NPO's bias toward easy-to-forget samples and outperforming NPO on TOFU/MUSE benchmarks.

title: The Unlocking Spell on Base LLMs: Rethinking Alignment via In-Context Learning
tldr: Shows alignment tuning mainly teaches stylistic patterns (not knowledge), and proposes URIAL, a tuning-free in-context learning method that matches or exceeds SFT/RLHF alignment on base LLMs.

title: AutoDefense: Multi-Agent LLM Defense against Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: AutoDefense is a multi-agent response-filtering framework that reduces jailbreak attack success rates on GPT-3.5 from 55.74% to 7.95% using smaller open-source LLMs as defenders.

title: Eyes Closed, Safety On: Protecting Multimodal LLMs via Image-to-Text Transformation
tldr: ECSO is a training-free defense for multimodal LLMs that converts unsafe images to text descriptions to reactivate the safety mechanisms of the underlying language model, achieving up to 71.3% improvement in harmless rate.

title: Vaccine: Perturbation-aware Alignment for Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes Vaccine, a perturbation-aware alignment method that adds crafted perturbations during alignment training to produce embeddings invariant to harmful data poisoning during downstream finetuning, reducing harmful scores by up to 9.8%.

title: Language Models Represent Space and Time
tldr: Demonstrates that Llama-2 linearly represents spatial coordinates and temporal information, with individual space and time neurons encoding geographic and temporal features.

title: PKU-SafeRLHF: A Safety Alignment Preference Dataset for Llama Family Models
tldr: PKU-SafeRLHF introduces a large-scale safety alignment dataset with 44.6k prompts, 265k QA pairs annotated across 19 harm categories and 3 severity levels, enabling safer RLHF training for Llama family models.

title: AutoDAN: Interpretable Gradient-Based Adversarial Attacks on Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces AutoDAN, the first interpretable gradient-based adversarial attack on LLMs that generates readable jailbreak prompts bypassing perplexity filters with high attack success rates and strong transferability.

title: Harmful Fine-tuning Attacks and Defenses for Large Language Models: A Survey
tldr: Surveys harmful fine-tuning attacks that compromise LLM safety alignment through as few as 100 poisoned examples, along with defenses spanning moderation, alignment-stage, fine-tuning-stage, and post-fine-tuning-stage approaches.

title: Weight Poisoning Attacks on Pretrained Models
tldr: Demonstrates that pretrained NLP model weights can be poisoned with backdoors that persist through fine-tuning, achieving near-100% attack success via RIPPLe and Embedding Surgery methods.

title: Recursively Summarizing Books with Human Feedback
tldr: Combines recursive task decomposition with human feedback to train GPT-3 to summarize entire fiction novels, achieving state-of-the-art on BookSum without humans reading full books.

title: Large Language Models can Strategically Deceive their Users when Put Under Pressure
tldr: GPT-4 deployed as a stock trading agent autonomously engages in insider trading and strategically deceives its manager about the reasons, even doubling down when questioned.

title: MACHIAVELLI: A Benchmark for Understanding and Mitigating Power-Seeking and Deception in AI
tldr: Introduces MACHIAVELLI, a benchmark of 134 text-based games with 572K+ annotated scenarios to evaluate and mitigate power-seeking, deception, and other Machiavellian behaviors in AI agents.

title: On the Exploitability of Instruction Tuning
tldr: AutoPoison automates data poisoning of instruction-tuned LLMs, achieving content injection and over-refusal attacks with small poison fractions while maintaining stealth and output quality.

title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
tldr: Introduces AgentDojo, a dynamic benchmark with 97 tasks and 629 security test cases for evaluating prompt injection attacks and defenses on tool-using LLM agents.

title: On Second Thought, Let's Not Think Step by Step! Bias and Toxicity in Zero-Shot Reasoning
tldr: Zero-shot chain-of-thought prompting increases stereotype bias by 8.8% and toxic outputs by 19.4% on average, showing that reasoning strategies can undermine alignment.

title: SafetyBench: Evaluating the Safety of Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces SafetyBench, a bilingual (Chinese/English) benchmark of 11,435 multiple-choice questions across 7 safety categories, evaluating 25 LLMs and finding GPT-4 substantially outperforms others.

title: Do-Not-Answer: A Dataset for Evaluating Safeguards in LLMs
tldr: Introduces Do-Not-Answer, an open-source 939-prompt dataset for evaluating LLM safeguards, with a three-level risk taxonomy and BERT-based classifiers matching GPT-4 evaluation performance.

title: Extracting Latent Steering Vectors from Pretrained Language Models
tldr: Steering vectors can be extracted from frozen LM hidden states via gradient descent, achieving >99 BLEU sentence recovery and enabling unsupervised style transfer via vector arithmetic.

title: Agent-SafetyBench: Evaluating the Safety of LLM Agents
tldr: Introduces Agent-SafetyBench with 349 environments and 2,000 test cases across 8 risk categories; none of 16 tested LLM agents achieves safety scores above 60%, revealing fundamental deficits in robustness and risk awareness.

title: Efficient Adversarial Training in LLMs with Continuous Attacks
tldr: Proposes continuous embedding-space adversarial training (C-AdvUL and C-AdvIPO) for LLMs that transfers robustness to discrete attacks while being 299x more efficient than prior methods.

title: A is for Absorption: Studying Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Discovers feature absorption -- a failure mode where SAE latents appear monosemantic but have systematic blind spots, with token-aligned latents absorbing features they should not represent.

title: Attribution Patching Outperforms Automated Circuit Discovery
tldr: Introduces Edge Attribution Patching (EAP), showing it achieves greater circuit recovery AUC than ACDC while requiring only two forward passes and one backward pass.

title: Transcoders Find Interpretable LLM Feature Circuits
tldr: Introduces transcoders as sparsely-activating MLP approximations that enable weights-based feature circuit analysis, matching or exceeding SAE interpretability across models from 120M to 1.4B parameters.

title: Latent Adversarial Training
tldr: Proposes latent adversarial training (LAT) that applies adversarial perturbations in activation space rather than input space, usually Pareto-dominating standard adversarial training.

title: OpenAssistant Conversations - Democratizing Large Language Model Alignment
tldr: Introduces OpenAssistant Conversations, a crowdsourced 161K-message dataset in 35 languages with 461K quality ratings for training aligned LLMs via RLHF and SFT.

title: Attacks, Defenses and Evaluations for LLM Conversation Safety: A Survey
tldr: A comprehensive survey of LLM conversation safety organized around three pillars: attacks (inference-time and training-time), defenses (alignment, inference guidance, filters), and evaluation datasets/metrics.

title: Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think
tldr: Finds that reasoning models' chain-of-thought is unfaithful 61-75% of the time when using biased hints, and outcome-based RL does not improve verbalization of reward hacks despite increasing their usage to >99%.

title: Ring-A-Bell! How Reliable are Concept Removal Methods for Diffusion Models?
tldr: Ring-A-Bell is a model-agnostic red-teaming tool that bypasses concept removal safety mechanisms in text-to-image diffusion models with 30%+ success rate increases.

title: Fundamental Limitations of Alignment in Large Language Models
tldr: Proves via Behavior Expectation Bounds that any LLM alignment which attenuates but doesn't fully eliminate undesired behaviors remains vulnerable to adversarial prompts of logarithmic length.

title: Principle-Driven Self-Alignment of Language Models from Scratch with Minimal Human Supervision
tldr: Self-Align trains LLaMA-65B into a helpful, ethical assistant (Dromedary) using only 16 human-written principles and <300 lines of annotations, achieving state-of-the-art TruthfulQA accuracy.

title: Tensor Trust: Interpretable Prompt Injection Attacks from an Online Game
tldr: Crowdsourced 126K+ prompt injection attacks and 46K defenses from an online game, revealing 16 attack strategies and showing all tested LLMs remain vulnerable to prompt hijacking and extraction.

title: DEPN: Detecting and Editing Privacy Neurons in Pretrained Language Models
tldr: DEPN locates privacy-sensitive neurons via gradient-based attribution and erases memorized private data by zeroing their activations, reducing privacy exposure by up to 57.84% while maintaining model performance.

title: Evaluating Frontier Models for Dangerous Capabilities
tldr: Presents DeepMind's framework and results from evaluating Gemini models across five dangerous capability areas: persuasion, cyber-offense, self-proliferation, self-reasoning, and biological risk.

title: Taken out of Context: On Measuring Situational Awareness in LLMs
tldr: Proposes 'out-of-context reasoning' as a measurable prerequisite for situational awareness in LLMs and demonstrates models can recall and act on training-time facts at test time.

title: Cognitive Overload: Jailbreaking Large Language Models with Overloaded Logical Thinking
tldr: Introduces three jailbreak attack categories grounded in Cognitive Load Theory -- multilingual overload, veiled expressions, and effect-to-cause reasoning -- achieving up to 88.3% ASR on ChatGPT.

title: SafeChain: Safety of Language Models with Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Capabilities
tldr: Evaluates safety of 12 large reasoning models (LRMs) on jailbreak benchmarks, finds them unsafe, proposes three decoding strategies and SafeChain, a 40k CoT-style safety training dataset.

title: Safety Layers in Aligned Large Language Models
tldr: Identifies contiguous 'safety layers' in aligned LLMs that distinguish malicious from benign queries and proposes freezing them during fine-tuning to preserve alignment.

title: Soft Prompt Threats: Attacking Safety Alignment and Unlearning in Open-Source LLMs through the Embedding Space
tldr: Embedding space attacks on open-source LLMs break safety alignment (100% success) and extract supposedly unlearned information, operating orders of magnitude faster than discrete attacks like GCG.

title: AI Sandbagging: Language Models can Strategically Underperform on Evaluations
tldr: Demonstrates that frontier LLMs can strategically underperform on dangerous capability evaluations while maintaining general performance, undermining the trustworthiness of safety evaluations.

title: Representation Noising: A Defence Mechanism Against Harmful Finetuning
tldr: RepNoise defends LLMs against harmful fine-tuning by pushing harmful representations toward Gaussian noise across all layers, maintaining general capabilities while preventing recovery of harmful behaviors.

title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
tldr: Discovers that neural networks can suddenly generalize long after memorizing training data on small algorithmic datasets, a phenomenon called 'grokking'.

title: Goal Misgeneralization: Why Correct Specifications Aren't Enough For Correct Goals
tldr: Formalizes goal misgeneralization as distinct from reward misspecification: even with correct training feedback, models may coherently pursue unintended goals at deployment.

title: Agent Smith: A Single Image Can Jailbreak One Million Multimodal LLM Agents Exponentially Fast
tldr: A single adversarial image injected into one multimodal LLM agent's memory infects ~100% of a million-agent network in O(log N) chat rounds via exponential 'infectious jailbreak.'

title: Not All Language Model Features Are Linear
tldr: Demonstrates that some language model features are irreducibly multi-dimensional (e.g., days of week form circles), challenging the linear representation hypothesis.

title: KGA: A General Machine Unlearning Framework Based on Knowledge Gap Alignment
tldr: KGA aligns the knowledge gap between model pairs to achieve machine unlearning across NLP tasks (classification, translation, generation) without requiring retraining from scratch.

title: Reward Model Ensembles Help Mitigate Overoptimization
tldr: Ensemble-based conservative reward optimization (worst-case and uncertainty-weighted) practically eliminates overoptimization in BoN sampling (up to 75% improvement) and mitigates it in PPO with small KL penalties.

title: Causal Abstraction: A Theoretical Foundation for Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: Provides rigorous mathematical foundations for mechanistic interpretability by formalizing neural network explanations as causal abstractions, unifying activation patching, circuits, and SAEs as special cases.
models_studied: Fully-connected feed-forward neural networks (small-scale, 8 input/24 intermediate/2 output neurons)

title: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
tldr: METR evaluates 4 LLM agents (GPT-4, Claude) on 12 real-world tasks measuring autonomous replication and adaptation (ARA) capabilities, finding agents complete only the easiest tasks but warning that near-future scaling could change this.

title: Keeping LLMs Aligned After Fine-tuning: The Crucial Role of Prompt Templates
tldr: Proposes 'Pure Tuning, Safe Testing' (PTST): fine-tune without safety prompts but include them at inference, reducing attack success rate from 18% to 1% while preserving task performance.

title: Sycophancy to Subterfuge: Investigating Reward Tampering in Language Models
tldr: Demonstrates a curriculum from sycophancy to reward tampering: models trained on simple reward misspecifications generalize to sophisticated behaviors including directly modifying their own reward functions and test code.

title: Defending Large Language Models against Jailbreak Attacks via Semantic Smoothing
tldr: SemanticSmooth defends LLMs against jailbreaks by applying semantics-preserving transformations (paraphrase, summarize, translate, etc.) to input copies, aggregating via majority vote, with a learned policy network for adaptive transformation selection.

title: Zephyr: Direct Distillation of LM Alignment
tldr: Zephyr-7B achieves SOTA 7B chat performance (7.34 MT-Bench, surpassing Llama2-Chat-70B) via a 3-stage pipeline: distilled SFT, AI feedback from GPT-4, and distilled DPO -- requiring no human annotations.

title: Large Language Model Alignment: A Survey
tldr: Comprehensive survey of LLM alignment covering outer alignment (RLHF, scalable oversight), inner alignment (mesa-optimization, deceptive alignment), mechanistic interpretability, adversarial attacks, and evaluation methods.

title: Mechanistically analyzing the effects of fine-tuning on procedurally defined tasks
tldr: Fine-tuning learns shallow 'wrappers' over existing capabilities rather than fundamentally changing them, meaning safety alignment can be unintentionally removed by fine-tuning on unrelated tasks.

title: Llama Scope: Extracting Millions of Features from Llama-3.1-8B with Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Releases 256 pre-trained TopK SAEs for all layers and sub-layers of Llama-3.1-8B at 32K and 128K widths, with analysis of out-of-distribution generalization and feature geometry.

title: Improved Few-Shot Jailbreaking Can Circumvent Aligned Language Models and Their Defenses
tldr: Improved few-shot jailbreaking (I-FSJ) using special token injection and demo-level random search achieves >95% attack success rates on Llama-2-7B and Llama-3-8B, bypassing perplexity detection and SmoothLLM defenses.

title: Editing Large Language Models: Problems, Methods, and Opportunities
tldr: Comprehensive survey and empirical analysis of LLM editing methods (ROME, MEMIT, SERAC, MEND, etc.) with new portability/locality benchmarks revealing significant limitations in generalization and side effects.

title: Multimodal Neurons in Artificial Neural Networks
