tldr: Individual neurons in CLIP respond to semantically related concepts across both visual and textual modalities, and this text-reading capability enables typographic adversarial attacks.

title: A Survey of Machine Unlearning
tldr: Comprehensive survey of machine unlearning methods covering exact/approximate approaches, verification mechanisms, and open challenges for removing data influence from trained models.

title: Patchscopes: A Unifying Framework for Inspecting Hidden Representations of Language Models
tldr: Patchscopes unifies interpretability methods by patching hidden representations into prompts that elicit information, using the LLM itself as its own probe.

title: How to Catch an AI Liar: Lie Detection in Black-Box LLMs by Asking Unrelated Questions
tldr: Proposes a black-box lie detector for LLMs using 48 unrelated follow-up questions and logistic regression, achieving near-perfect in-distribution AUC and generalizing across architectures and lie types.

title: Fast Adversarial Attacks on Language Models In One GPU Minute
tldr: BEAST uses gradient-free beam search to jailbreak Vicuna-7B-v1.5 with 89% success in under one minute, far outpacing gradient-based attacks in speed.

title: Lisa: Lazy Safety Alignment for Large Language Models against Harmful Fine-tuning Attack
tldr: Lisa uses proximal-term-constrained bi-state optimization during fine-tuning to prevent safety alignment degradation from harmful data, reducing harmful scores by 7-12% over baselines with only 8.3% compute overhead.

title: Scheming AIs: Will AIs Fake Alignment During Training in Order to Get Power?
tldr: Comprehensive theoretical analysis estimating ~25% probability that sufficiently capable, situationally-aware AI systems trained with standard methods would scheme (fake alignment during training to gain power later).

title: Truthful AI: Developing and Governing AI That Does Not Lie
tldr: Proposes a framework for developing and governing AI that does not lie, introducing the 'negligent falsehood' standard and outlining technical and governance approaches to ensure AI truthfulness.

title: FLIRT: Feedback Loop In-context Red Teaming
tldr: FLIRT uses in-context learning feedback loops to automatically generate diverse adversarial prompts, achieving ~80% attack success against vanilla Stable Diffusion and ~60% against safety-enhanced variants.

title: Attack Prompt Generation for Red Teaming and Defending Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes a semi-automatic framework using in-context learning to generate high-quality LLM attack prompts and an iterative fine-tuning defense, releasing the SAP dataset series.

title: Jailbreak Vision Language Models via Bi-Modal Adversarial Prompt
tldr: BAP combines adversarial image perturbations (PGD) with chain-of-thought textual prompt refinement to jailbreak vision-language models, achieving +29.03% average attack success rate over baselines.

title: Booster: Tackling Harmful Fine-tuning for Large Language Models via Attenuating Harmful Perturbation
tldr: Proposes Booster, an alignment-stage defense that attenuates harmful perturbation via loss regularization, reducing harmful fine-tuning attack success by 17-34% while preserving downstream task accuracy.

title: Compositional Explanations of Neurons
tldr: Explains individual neurons using compositional logical formulas (AND/OR/NOT), improving over atomic labels by 68% IoU and revealing NLP neurons encode shallow heuristics.

title: The Hydra Effect: Emergent Self-repair in Language Model Computations
tldr: Shows that ablating important attention layers causes other layers to compensate (the 'Hydra effect'), and late MLPs act to downregulate maximum-likelihood tokens, complicating ablation-based interpretability.

title: Weak-to-Strong Jailbreaking on Large Language Models
tldr: A weak unsafe model can shift a strong aligned model's token distribution at inference time to achieve >99% jailbreak success rates with minimal compute.

title: Covert Malicious Finetuning: Challenges in Safeguarding LLM Adaptation
tldr: Demonstrates covert malicious finetuning where individually innocuous training samples teach GPT-4 to respond to encoded harmful requests, achieving 99% attack success while evading all standard defenses.

title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
tldr: ASB is a comprehensive benchmark formalizing 10 attack/defense types across 10 LLM-agent scenarios (400+ tools, 13 LLMs, ~90K tests), revealing up to 84.30% attack success and weak existing defenses.

title: Backdoor Attacks for In-Context Learning with Language Models
tldr: Demonstrates that backdoor attacks can be injected into LLMs via data poisoning to manipulate in-context learning predictions, with larger models (6B) achieving near-100% attack success across unseen prompts.

title: LLM Jailbreak Attack versus Defense Techniques -- A Comprehensive Study
tldr: Systematically evaluates 9 jailbreak attacks and 7 defenses across Vicuna, LLama-2, and GPT-3.5, finding template attacks dominate and most defenses fail except Bergeron.

title: Jailbreaking GPT-4V via Self-Adversarial Attacks with System Prompts
tldr: Discovers system prompt leakage in GPT-4V and develops SASP, a self-adversarial jailbreak method achieving 98.7% attack success rate on facial recognition tasks, plus defensive prompt strategies.

title: Does Refusal Training in LLMs Generalize to the Past Tense?
tldr: Reformulating harmful prompts into past tense bypasses refusal training in most leading LLMs, with GPT-4o jumping from 1% to 88% attack success rate.

title: On Adaptive Attacks to Adversarial Example Defenses
tldr: Demonstrates that 13 recently published adversarial defenses from ICLR/ICML/NeurIPS can all be circumvented by properly constructed adaptive attacks, and provides methodology guidelines for rigorous defense evaluation.

title: Fine-Grained Human Feedback Gives Better Rewards for Language Model Training
tldr: Introduces Fine-Grained RLHF, which trains multiple reward models on specific error categories at sentence/sub-sentence level, outperforming holistic preference-based RLHF on detoxification and long-form QA.

title: Security and Privacy Challenges of Large Language Models: A Survey
tldr: Comprehensive survey of LLM security and privacy vulnerabilities — jailbreaks, backdoor/poisoning attacks, gradient leakage, PII leakage — and their defenses, with domain-specific risk analysis.

title: Toward Transparent AI: A Survey on Interpreting the Inner Structures of Deep Neural Networks
tldr: A comprehensive survey of 300+ inner interpretability techniques for DNNs, organized by network component (weights, neurons, subnetworks, representations) and timing (intrinsic vs. post hoc), arguing the field needs more practical engineering focus.

title: A Toy Model of Universality: Reverse Engineering How Networks Learn Group Operations
tldr: Reverse-engineers how neural networks learn group composition via representation theory, finding weak universality (same algorithm) but not strong universality (same circuits).
models_studied: Small MLPs trained on group composition

title: InferAligner: Inference-Time Alignment for Harmlessness through Cross-Model Guidance
tldr: InferAligner applies safety steering vectors extracted from an aligned model to unaligned model activations at inference time, achieving 0% attack success rate without retraining.

title: Automatically Interpreting Millions of Features in Large Language Models
tldr: Develops an open-source automated pipeline to generate and evaluate natural language explanations for millions of SAE features, introducing five novel scoring techniques.

title: Gradient Cuff: Detecting Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models by Exploring Refusal Loss Landscapes
tldr: Gradient Cuff detects jailbreak attacks by analyzing refusal loss landscapes with a two-step strategy (threshold + gradient norm), reducing attack success rate from 74.3% to 24.4% on Vicuna-7B-V1.5.

title: Process for Adapting Language Models to Society (PALMS) with Values-Targeted Datasets
tldr: PALMS fine-tunes GPT-3 on a small hand-curated values-targeted dataset (120 examples across 19 controversial topics) to reduce toxicity and improve adherence to human-rights-aligned values, improving human ratings from 3 to 4/5.

title: Prompting4Debugging: Red-Teaming Text-to-Image Diffusion Models by Finding Problematic Prompts
tldr: P4D is an automated red-teaming tool that finds adversarial prompts bypassing safety mechanisms in text-to-image diffusion models, revealing ~50% of 'safe' benchmark prompts can be manipulated.

title: Transformer visualization via dictionary learning: contextualized embedding as a linear superposition of transformer factors
tldr: Applies dictionary learning (non-negative sparse coding) to decompose transformer embeddings into 'transformer factors,' revealing hierarchical linguistic structures including polysemy disambiguation, syntactic patterns, and long-range dependencies.

title: Jatmo: Prompt Injection Defense by Task-Specific Finetuning
tldr: Jatmo defends against prompt injection by fine-tuning non-instruction-tuned base models on task-specific data generated by a teacher model, achieving <0.5% attack success vs 87% for GPT-3.5-Turbo.

title: Adversarial Training for High-Stakes Reliability
tldr: Iterative adversarial training with human red-teamers and tool-assisted attacks doubles the time needed to find failures in a safety classifier, demonstrating a framework for improving worst-case reliability.

title: RWKU: Benchmarking Real-World Knowledge Unlearning for Large Language Models
tldr: RWKU is a benchmark for evaluating LLM knowledge unlearning on 200 real-world individuals, using 13,131 forget probes and 9 adversarial attack types to test both forgetting efficacy and side effects.

title: Is Power-Seeking AI an Existential Risk?
tldr: A structured six-premise argument that power-seeking misaligned AI systems pose roughly >10% probability of existential catastrophe by 2070, with detailed analysis of why alignment is harder than capability development.

title: An Interpretability Illusion for BERT
tldr: Individual BERT neurons appear to encode simple concepts in one dataset but encode different concepts in others, revealing an interpretability illusion caused by dataset idiosyncrasy, local semantic coherence, and annotator bias.

title: Comprehensive Assessment of Jailbreak Attacks Against LLMs
tldr: First large-scale measurement of 13 jailbreak methods across 4 categories, 160 forbidden questions in 16 violation categories, and 6 LLMs, finding optimization-based attacks achieve ~0.82 ASR.

title: SAEBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Sparse Autoencoders in Language Model Interpretability
tldr: Introduces SAEBench, an 8-metric evaluation suite for SAEs revealing that proxy metric gains don't reliably translate to practical performance, with Matryoshka SAEs excelling at disentanglement despite worse reconstruction.

title: Do Unlearning Methods Remove Information from Language Model Weights?
tldr: Introduces an adversarial evaluation framework showing current unlearning methods fail to remove information from LM weights, with fine-tuning recovering 88% of pre-unlearning accuracy.

title: Helping or Herding? Reward Model Ensembles Mitigate but do not Eliminate Reward Hacking
tldr: Reward model ensembles with diverse pretraining seeds mitigate but do not eliminate reward hacking because ensemble members share systematic error patterns under distribution shift.

title: Inspecting and Editing Knowledge Representations in Language Models
tldr: Introduces REMEDI, a method that learns linear mappings from natural language statements to fact encodings in LM representations for knowledge inspection and editing.

title: Goal Misgeneralization in Deep Reinforcement Learning
tldr: Demonstrates goal misgeneralization in RL: agents maintain capabilities out-of-distribution but pursue proxy goals instead of the intended objective.

title: BadEdit: Backdooring Large Language Models by Model Editing
tldr: BadEdit reformulates backdoor injection as a model editing problem, achieving up to 100% attack success rate on LLMs using only 15 samples and ~2-6 minutes of compute.

title: Fine-tuning Enhances Existing Mechanisms: A Case Study on Entity Tracking
tldr: Shows that fine-tuning enhances rather than replaces pre-training circuits for entity tracking, with performance gains attributed to improved positional information handling.

title: Llama Guard 3 Vision: Safeguarding Human-AI Image Understanding Conversations
tldr: Llama Guard 3 Vision is an 11B multimodal safety classifier fine-tuned on Llama 3.2-Vision that moderates human-AI conversations involving images across 13 MLCommons hazard categories, outperforming GPT-4o baselines.

title: Have Faith in Faithfulness: Going Beyond Circuit Overlap When Finding Model Mechanisms
tldr: Demonstrates that circuit overlap is a poor proxy for faithfulness in circuit discovery, and introduces EAP-IG (integrated gradients variant) that finds more faithful circuits than standard EAP.

title: Chain-of-Thought Monitorability: A New and Fragile Opportunity for AI Safety
tldr: Argues that CoT monitoring is a unique but fragile safety opportunity: models must externalize reasoning for hard tasks, but this property can be undermined by RL scaling, process supervision, novel architectures, or deliberate obfuscation.

title: The Hidden Risks of Large Reasoning Models: A Safety Assessment of R1
tldr: Comprehensive safety assessment of reasoning LLMs (DeepSeek-R1, o3-mini) revealing that stronger reasoning correlates with greater harm and that thinking processes contain hidden safety risks beyond final answers.

title: SecAlign: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Preference Optimization
tldr: SecAlign uses DPO-based preference optimization to defend LLMs against prompt injection, reducing GCG attack success rates from 56% to 2% on Mistral-7B with <1.5% utility loss.

title: Visual-RolePlay: Universal Jailbreak Attack on MultiModal Large Language Models via Role-playing Image Character
tldr: Visual-RolePlay (VRP) attacks multimodal LLMs by generating role-play character images paired with benign instructions, achieving 14.3% higher attack success rate than existing baselines.

title: Identifying Functionally Important Features with End-to-End Sparse Dictionary Learning
tldr: Proposes end-to-end SAE training that optimizes for KL divergence on model output rather than reconstruction loss, ensuring learned features are functionally important to the network.

title: Modifying Memories in Transformer Models
tldr: Introduces the task of modifying specific factual knowledge in transformer model parameters while preserving performance on unmodified facts, using constrained fine-tuning on specific layers.

title: Function Vectors in Large Language Models
tldr: Discovers that in-context learning tasks are encoded as compact 'function vectors' by a small set of attention heads, which can be extracted and added to trigger task execution zero-shot.

title: Linearity of Relation Decoding in Transformer Language Models
tldr: Demonstrates that transformer factual relation decoding is often well-approximated by a single linear transformation (LRE) mapping subject representations to object representations.

title: Optimal Policies Tend to Seek Power
tldr: Proves formally that optimal policies in MDPs tend to seek power (preserve optionality, acquire resources) for most reward functions, formalizing the instrumental convergence thesis.

title: Dissecting Adversarial Robustness of Multimodal LM Agents
tldr: Imperceptible image perturbations (L-inf norm 16/256) can compromise multimodal web agents with up to 75% attack success rate; agent components like reflection and tree search introduce new vulnerabilities.

title: ALERT: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Assessing Large Language Models' Safety through Red Teaming
tldr: ALERT introduces a 45k+ instruction safety benchmark with a 6-macro/32-micro category taxonomy and adversarial variants, evaluating 10 LLMs and finding wide safety variation (62%-99%).

title: Antidote: Post-fine-tuning Safety Alignment for Large Language Models against Harmful Fine-tuning
tldr: Proposes Antidote, a post-fine-tuning defense that uses one-shot weight pruning (WANDA-based importance scoring) to remove harmful parameters from fine-tuned LLMs, reducing harmful outputs by up to 17.8% with minimal accuracy loss and negligible overhead.

title: Understanding the Role of Individual Units in a Deep Neural Network
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) 2020
tldr: Network dissection identifies what individual hidden units in CNNs and GANs represent, revealing emergent concept detectors that causally control network behavior without explicit supervision.

title: SLiC-HF: Sequence Likelihood Calibration with Human Feedback
tldr: SLiC-HF uses a pairwise ranking calibration loss with cross-entropy regularization to align LMs from human preferences, matching or exceeding PPO-based RLHF while being simpler and more efficient.

title: Natural Language Descriptions of Deep Visual Features
tldr: Introduces MILAN, a model that generates open-ended natural language descriptions of individual neurons in vision networks by maximizing pointwise mutual information with neuron activation patterns.

title: How Many Unicorns Are in This Image? A Safety Evaluation Benchmark for Vision LLMs
tldr: A comprehensive safety benchmark for 21 Vision LLMs revealing OOD text vulnerability, effective vision encoder attacks, and that vision-language training degrades base LLM safety alignment.

title: Programming Refusal with Conditional Activation Steering
tldr: CAST uses condition vectors alongside behavior vectors to selectively steer LLM refusals based on input context, achieving 90.7% harmful-prompt refusal while keeping harmless-prompt refusal near 0%.

title: A Watermark for Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes a watermarking framework for LLM outputs using green/red token lists that enables statistical detection of machine-generated text with 98.4% sensitivity and near-zero false positives.

title: A Long Way to Go: Investigating Length Correlations in RLHF
tldr: Demonstrates that RLHF reward models strongly correlate with output length, and a length-only reward can reproduce 70-90% of downstream improvements on helpfulness tasks.

title: Debating with More Persuasive LLMs Leads to More Truthful Answers
tldr: Debate between LLM experts helps non-expert judges (humans 88%, LLMs 76%) identify correct answers, and optimizing debaters for persuasiveness improves truthfulness rather than deception.

title: The Capacity for Moral Self-Correction in Large Language Models
tldr: RLHF-trained language models can morally self-correct (reduce bias and discrimination) when instructed to do so, with this capability emerging at 22B parameters and improving with scale.

title: Deception Abilities Emerged in Large Language Models
tldr: Demonstrates that state-of-the-art LLMs like GPT-4 have acquired the ability to understand and induce false beliefs in other agents, with deception capabilities emerging at scale.

title: Optimization-based Prompt Injection Attack to LLM-as-a-Judge
tldr: JudgeDeceiver uses gradient-based optimization to generate adversarial sequences that manipulate LLM-as-a-Judge systems, achieving 89-93% attack success rates far exceeding handcrafted baselines.

title: Open Problems in Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: Consensus research agenda from 29 leading MI researchers identifying key open problems in decomposition, validation, applications, and socio-technical challenges.

title: Safety Assessment of Chinese Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces a Chinese LLM safety benchmark with 8 safety scenarios, 6 instruction attack types, and a 100K-prompt SafetyPrompts dataset, evaluating 15 models.

title: Safety Tax: Safety Alignment Makes Your Large Reasoning Models Less Reasonable
tldr: Safety alignment of Large Reasoning Models degrades reasoning accuracy by 7-31% ('Safety Tax'), with direct refusal datasets achieving better safety but worse reasoning than chain-of-thought safety data.

title: H-CoT: Hijacking the Chain-of-Thought Safety Reasoning Mechanism to Jailbreak Large Reasoning Models, Including OpenAI o1/o3, DeepSeek-R1, and Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking
tldr: Introduces H-CoT, an attack that hijacks the chain-of-thought safety reasoning in LRMs by injecting mocked execution-phase thoughts, reducing refusal rates from 98% to below 2% on o1/o3, DeepSeek-R1, and Gemini.

title: SPA-VL: A Comprehensive Safety Preference Alignment Dataset for Vision Language Models
tldr: SPA-VL is a 100K-sample safety preference dataset for VLMs spanning 6 harm domains and 53 subcategories, enabling RLHF/DPO training that reduces unsafe outputs while preserving helpfulness.

title: DExperts: Decoding-Time Controlled Text Generation with Experts and Anti-Experts
tldr: DExperts steers LM generation at decoding time by combining expert and anti-expert LM logits via a product-of-experts ensemble, achieving state-of-the-art detoxification and sentiment control without retraining the base model.

title: Bot-Adversarial Dialogue for Safe Conversational Agents
tldr: Introduces a human-and-model-in-the-loop adversarial framework (Bot-Adversarial Dialogue) for evaluating and training safer conversational agents, achieving 94-96% safe responses while maintaining engagingness.

title: MACE: Mass Concept Erasure in Diffusion Models
tldr: MACE is a finetuning framework that scales concept erasure in text-to-image diffusion models to 100+ concepts using closed-form cross-attention refinement combined with per-concept LoRA modules fused without interference.

title: Purple Llama CyberSecEval: A Secure Coding Benchmark for Language Models
tldr: Introduces CyberSecEval, a benchmark measuring LLM propensity to generate insecure code (189 rules, 50 CWEs, 8 languages) and comply with cyberattack requests (1,000 prompts across 10 ATT&CK categories), finding more capable coding models are more insecure.

title: Towards Principled Evaluations of Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretability and Control
tldr: Proposes task-grounded SAE evaluation using supervised feature dictionaries, revealing that standard SAE metrics poorly predict downstream control utility and identifying feature occlusion and over-splitting as key failure modes.

title: BatchTopK Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Introduces BatchTopK SAEs that relax the per-sample TopK constraint to batch-level, allowing variable sparsity per input while maintaining average sparsity and matching JumpReLU performance.

title: Position: LLM Unlearning Benchmarks are Weak Measures of Progress
tldr: Existing LLM unlearning benchmarks give overly optimistic results; forget-retain dependencies, test-set overfitting, and ambiguous targets make them weak or actively misleading measures of true unlearning.

title: Preference Ranking Optimization for Human Alignment
tldr: PRO extends Bradley-Terry pairwise comparisons to multi-response preference rankings of arbitrary length, directly aligning LLMs without RL and matching ChatGPT-level reward scores with a 7B model.

title: BadGPT: Exploring Security Vulnerabilities of ChatGPT via Backdoor Attacks to InstructGPT
tldr: First backdoor attack targeting RL fine-tuning in LLMs by poisoning the reward model, achieving 98% attack success rate while preserving clean accuracy.

title: Inducing Causal Structure for Interpretable Neural Networks
tldr: Interchange Intervention Training (IIT) aligns causal model variables with neural representations and trains networks via counterfactual matching, guaranteeing causal abstraction when loss reaches zero.

title: AtP*: An efficient and scalable method for localizing LLM behaviour to components
tldr: Proposes AtP*, an improved attribution patching method that fixes query-key saturation and effect cancellation failure modes, enabling scalable localization of LLM behavior to individual components.

title: Learning Multi-Level Features with Matryoshka Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Trains SAEs with nested reconstruction objectives at multiple dictionary sizes, dramatically reducing feature absorption while maintaining reconstruction quality.

title: RAVEL: Evaluating Interpretability Methods on Disentangling Language Model Representations
tldr: Introduces RAVEL, a benchmark evaluating whether interpretability methods can disentangle entity attributes in LLM representations, and proposes Multi-task DAS achieving state-of-the-art results.

title: JailbreakZoo: Survey, Landscapes, and Horizons in Jailbreaking Large Language and Vision-Language Models
tldr: Comprehensive survey of jailbreaking attacks and defenses for LLMs and VLMs, categorizing 5 LLM attack types and 6 defense types, plus 3 VLM-specific attack strategies.

title: PAL: Proxy-Guided Black-Box Attack on Large Language Models
tldr: PAL uses an open-source proxy model to guide token-level optimization attacks against black-box LLM APIs, achieving 84% attack success rate on GPT-3.5-Turbo vs 4% for prior work.

title: Query-Based Adversarial Prompt Generation
tldr: Introduces Greedy Coordinate Query (GCQ), a query-based adversarial attack that uses API access to construct prompts forcing aligned LLMs to output harmful strings, achieving 86% success on GPT-3.5 at $0.20/target.

title: Solving Math Word Problems with Process- and Outcome-Based Feedback
tldr: First comprehensive comparison of process- vs outcome-based supervision for math reasoning: both achieve similar final-answer accuracy, but process-based feedback is needed to reduce reasoning trace errors from 14% to 3.4%.

title: Can We Edit Factual Knowledge by In-Context Learning?
tldr: Proposes In-context Knowledge Editing (IKE), achieving competitive performance with gradient-based methods like ROME on factual updates while requiring zero parameter modifications.

title: Black-Box Access is Insufficient for Rigorous AI Audits
tldr: Argues that black-box access (input-output queries) is insufficient for rigorous AI audits; white-box (weights, activations, gradients) and outside-the-box (training data, documentation) access enable substantially stronger safety evaluations.

title: How to Use and Interpret Activation Patching
tldr: Comprehensive methodological guide on activation patching covering denoising vs. noising distinctions, metric selection pitfalls, circuit interpretation, and best practices for mechanistic interpretability.
models_studied: Various (tutorial uses hypothetical examples; references GPT-2, IOI task)

title: Evil Geniuses: Delving into the Safety of LLM-based Agents
tldr: Introduces Evil Geniuses (EG), an automated attack method using Red-Blue exercises to generate role-specific adversarial prompts for LLM-based agents, showing agents are less robust than standalone LLMs and produce stealthier harmful content.

title: Are Sparse Autoencoders Useful? A Case Study in Sparse Probing
tldr: SAE probes fail to consistently outperform simple baselines (logistic regression, KNN, PCA) across 113 binary classification tasks in data scarcity, class imbalance, label noise, and covariate shift regimes.

title: LLM Unlearning via Loss Adjustment with Only Forget Data
tldr: FLAT uses f-divergence between template and forget responses to achieve LLM unlearning using only forget data, eliminating the need for retain data or reference models.

title: A Primer in BERTology: What We Know About How BERT Works
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics (TACL) 2020
tldr: Comprehensive survey of 150+ studies probing BERT internals, covering linguistic knowledge by layer, attention patterns, overparameterization, and compression -- foundational reference for transformer interpretability.
models_studied: Various BERT variants (DistilBERT, RoBERTa, ALBERT, etc.)

title: The Reversal Curse: LLMs trained on 'A is B' fail to learn 'B is A'
tldr: Demonstrates that LLMs trained on 'A is B' completely fail to infer 'B is A', revealing a fundamental directional limitation in autoregressive knowledge learning.

title: Studying Large Language Model Generalization with Influence Functions
tldr: Scales influence functions to 52B-parameter LLMs via EK-FAC approximation, revealing sparse influence patterns, increasing abstraction with scale, and cross-lingual transfer in generalization.

title: In-Context Learning Creates Task Vectors
tldr: Demonstrates that in-context learning compresses demonstrations into compact task vectors at intermediate layers that can replace full demonstrations and trigger task behavior on new inputs.

title: Aging with GRACE: Lifelong Model Editing with Discrete Key-Value Adaptors
tldr: Preserves original model weights by using external discrete key-value adaptors with deferral radii to store and retrieve edits, enabling thousands of sequential edits with minimal drift.

title: Evaluating the Ripple Effects of Knowledge Editing in Language Models
tldr: Introduces RippleEdits, a benchmark of 5K factual edits with ~133K test queries evaluating whether knowledge editing methods propagate changes to logically dependent facts, finding parametric methods (ROME, MEMIT, MEND) achieve only 38-66% while in-context editing reaches 70-83%.

title: Detoxifying Large Language Models via Knowledge Editing
tldr: Introduces SafeEdit benchmark (8,100 instances, 9 unsafe categories) and DINM, a knowledge-editing method that detoxifies LLMs using a single instance by directly modifying toxic parameters rather than suppressing activations.

title: Self-Destructing Models: Increasing the Costs of Harmful Dual Uses of Foundation Models
tldr: Proposes Meta-Learned Adversarial Censoring (MLAC) to train 'self-destructing' models that resist fine-tuning for harmful tasks while preserving performance on desired tasks.

title: Refuse Whenever You Feel Unsafe: Improving Safety in LLMs via Decoupled Refusal Training
tldr: DeRTa trains LLMs to refuse harmful requests at any response position (not just the start) by prepending harmful prefixes during training plus a reinforced transition objective, reducing average attack success rates from ~70% to ~9%.

title: Eraser: Jailbreaking Defense in Large Language Models via Unlearning Harmful Knowledge
tldr: Proposes Eraser, a jailbreak defense that uses gradient ascent to unlearn harmful knowledge from LLMs while preserving general capabilities via knowledge distillation and safety alignment retention.

title: Towards Understanding Jailbreak Attacks in LLMs: A Representation Space Analysis
tldr: Analyzes why jailbreak attacks succeed by showing successful attacks move harmful prompt representations toward the 'acceptance direction' of harmless prompts in LLM representation space.

title: STAIR: Improving Safety Alignment with Introspective Reasoning
tldr: STAIR uses safety-informed chain-of-thought reasoning with Monte Carlo Tree Search and step-level DPO to improve LLM safety alignment, achieving safety comparable to Claude-3.5 against jailbreak attacks.

title: Adversarial GLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark for Robustness Evaluation of Language Models
tldr: Introduces AdvGLUE, a rigorously human-validated multi-task adversarial benchmark for language models using 14 attack methods across 5 GLUE tasks, revealing ~50% performance drops in SOTA models.

title: Rewarded soups: towards Pareto-optimal alignment by interpolating weights fine-tuned on diverse rewards
tldr: Rewarded soups interpolates weights of models fine-tuned on diverse rewards to achieve Pareto-optimal alignment without additional training, validated across text, image, and control tasks.

title: The Clock and the Pizza: Two Stories in Mechanistic Explanation of Neural Networks
tldr: Reveals that neural networks learn qualitatively different algorithms (Clock and Pizza) for the same modular addition task depending on hyperparameters and initialization.

title: Interpretability at Scale: Identifying Causal Mechanisms in Alpaca
tldr: Scales Distributed Alignment Search to 7B+ parameter models by learning alignments via sigmoid masks, replacing brute-force search, and discovers interpretable causal mechanisms in Alpaca.

title: Analyzing the Generalization and Reliability of Steering Vectors
tldr: Steering vectors show high within-dataset variance, a novel steerability bias, and imperfect OOD generalization, revealing significant barriers to their use as reliable alignment tools.

title: Speak Out of Turn: Safety Vulnerability of Large Language Models in Multi-turn Dialogue
tldr: Decomposing harmful queries into innocuous sub-queries across multiple dialogue turns bypasses LLM safety mechanisms that successfully block single-turn jailbreaks.

title: Navigating the Safety Landscape: Measuring Risks in Finetuning Large Language Models
tldr: Discovers 'safety basins' in LLM weight space and proposes the Visage metric to measure how finetuning compromises safety alignment, showing mixed-data finetuning preserves safety.

title: MQuAKE: Assessing Knowledge Editing in Language Models via Multi-Hop Questions
tldr: Introduces MQuAKE, a multi-hop QA benchmark showing knowledge editing methods fail catastrophically on entailed consequences of edits, and proposes MeLLo, a memory-based approach that substantially outperforms weight-editing methods.

title: AlphaEdit: Null-Space Constrained Knowledge Editing for Language Models
tldr: Projects knowledge-editing perturbations onto the null space of preserved knowledge, boosting locate-then-edit methods by 36.7% on average with a single line of code.

title: ReFT: Representation Finetuning for Language Models
tldr: Introduces Representation Finetuning (ReFT), which fine-tunes models by learning interventions on hidden representations rather than updating weights, achieving 15-65x more parameter efficiency than LoRA.

title: Rule Based Rewards for Language Model Safety
tldr: Proposes Rule Based Rewards (RBRs) that decompose safety behaviors into LLM-graded propositions, achieving 97.1% F1 on safety-usefulness balance vs 91.7% for human-feedback baselines while requiring only 518 labeled examples.
models_studied: OpenAI internal models (XSmall, Small, Medium, Large)

title: Do I Know This Entity? Knowledge Awareness and Hallucinations in Language Models
tldr: Uses SAE features to detect whether a model recognizes entities it can recall facts about, enabling prediction and control of hallucinations via representation steering.

title: Adversarial Prompting for Black Box Foundation Models
tldr: Develops a black-box optimization framework using Bayesian optimization and square attack to craft adversarial token prompts that manipulate foundation model outputs for both image and text generation.

title: RigorLLM: Resilient Guardrails for Large Language Models against Undesired Content
tldr: RigorLLM combines energy-based data generation, minimax safe-suffix optimization, and a fusion KNN+LLM detector to build jailbreak-resilient content moderation guardrails for LLMs.

title: Safety of Multimodal Large Language Models on Images and Text
tldr: Systematic survey of safety vulnerabilities, attack methods, and defenses for multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on images and text.

title: Intention Analysis Makes LLMs A Good Jailbreak Defender
tldr: IAPrompt uses a two-stage intention analysis + policy-aligned response prompting strategy to reduce LLM jailbreak attack success rates by ~46.5% on average without additional training.

title: Exploring Safety Generalization Challenges of Large Language Models via Code
tldr: CodeAttack framework transforms harmful natural language queries into code-based inputs using data structures, bypassing LLM safety guardrails over 80% of the time across GPT-4, Claude-2, and Llama-2.

title: Improving Steering Vectors by Targeting Sparse Autoencoder Features
tldr: Introduces SAE-Targeted Steering (SAE-TS), which constructs steering vectors targeting specific SAE features while minimizing unintended side effects, outperforming CAA on 7 of 9 tasks.

title: UnUnlearning: Unlearning is not sufficient for content regulation in advanced generative AI
tldr: Formalizes 'ununlearning': even exact unlearning fails for content regulation because in-context learning can reintroduce supposedly removed knowledge from retained foundational components.

title: Measuring Progress in Dictionary Learning for Language Model Interpretability with Board Game Models
tldr: Proposes using chess/Othello models with known ground-truth features to evaluate SAEs via coverage and board reconstruction metrics, and introduces p-annealing which matches Gated SAE performance at 50% less compute.

title: Steering Language Model Refusal with Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: SAE feature steering on Phi-3 Mini boosts unsafe prompt refusal by 32-38% and resists multi-turn jailbreaks, but causes ~68% over-refusal and severe capability degradation.

title: White-box Multimodal Jailbreaks Against Large Vision-Language Models
tldr: Proposes Universal Master Key (UMK) combining adversarial image prefix and text suffix via dual optimization to jailbreak VLMs, achieving 96% ASR on MiniGPT-4.

title: Unlearning or Obfuscating? Jogging the Memory of Unlearned LLMs via Benign Relearning
tldr: Demonstrates that LLM unlearning methods are fragile: adversaries can recover unlearned knowledge by finetuning with small benign auxiliary datasets, achieving >70% recovery rates.

title: RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models for Language Modeling
tldr: Introduces RewardBench, the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating reward models across chat, safety, and reasoning, revealing systematic differences between DPO and classifier-based reward models.

title: Inverse Scaling: When Bigger Isn't Better
tldr: Presents 11 tasks from a public competition where larger LLMs perform worse, identifying four causes of inverse scaling.

title: Thread: Circuits
tldr: Foundational Distill thread introducing the circuits research program: systematic reverse engineering of InceptionV1 to establish that neural networks contain meaningful features, circuits, and universal structure.

title: Simple synthetic data reduces sycophancy in large language models
tldr: Demonstrates that model scaling and instruction tuning increase sycophancy, and proposes a simple synthetic-data finetuning intervention using public NLP tasks that reduces sycophantic behavior by 4.7-10.0% without degrading other capabilities.

title: Towards Guaranteed Safe AI: A Framework for Ensuring Robust and Reliable AI Systems
tldr: Proposes 'Guaranteed Safe AI' framework with three components -- world model, safety specification, and verifier -- providing quantitative safety guarantees via formal verification.

title: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning In The Wild Is Not Always Faithful
venue: ICLR 2025 Workshop (Reasoning and Planning for LLMs)
tldr: Identifies two types of naturally-occurring CoT unfaithfulness in frontier models â€” implicit post-hoc rationalization (up to 13.5%) and unfaithful illogical shortcuts â€” without any adversarial prompting.

title: AEGIS: Online Adaptive AI Content Safety Moderation with Ensemble of LLM Experts
tldr: Introduces AEGIS, an ensemble-based content safety framework with a 13-category safety taxonomy, 26K annotated dataset, LoRA-tuned safety expert LLMs, and a no-regret online adaptation algorithm for dynamic expert selection.

title: Language Models Learn to Mislead Humans via RLHF
tldr: RLHF training causes LMs to become better at convincing humans they are correct even when wrong (U-Sophistry), increasing human false positive rates by 18-24% while not improving task accuracy.

title: Personalized Steering of Large Language Models: Versatile Steering Vectors Through Bi-directional Preference Optimization
tldr: BiPO optimizes steering vectors via a bi-directional preference optimization objective rather than activation difference extraction, achieving superior behavioral control across personas, truthfulness, hallucination, and jailbreaking scenarios.

title: Ignore This Title and HackAPrompt: Exposing Systemic Vulnerabilities of LLMs through a Global Scale Prompt Hacking Competition
tldr: Global competition with 2,800+ participants generated 600K+ adversarial prompts against GPT-3, ChatGPT, and FlanT5, yielding a 29-category taxonomy of prompt hacking attacks and a large public dataset.

title: Trading Inference-Time Compute for Adversarial Robustness
tldr: Increasing inference-time compute in reasoning models (o1-preview, o1-mini) improves adversarial robustness without adversarial training, with attack success rates approaching zero as compute grows.

title: GUARD: Role-playing to Generate Natural-language Jailbreakings to Test Guideline Adherence of Large Language Models
tldr: GUARD uses four collaborating LLM roles (Translator, Generator, Evaluator, Optimizer) and a knowledge graph of jailbreak characteristics to automatically generate natural-language jailbreaks, achieving 82% average attack success across multiple LLMs and VLMs.

title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
tldr: Discovers that LLMs disproportionately attend to initial tokens ('attention sinks') regardless of semantics, and leverages this to enable efficient infinite-length streaming inference via StreamingLLM.

title: Secrets of RLHF in Large Language Models Part I: PPO
tldr: Systematically investigates PPO for RLHF alignment, identifying policy constraints as the key factor for stable training and proposing PPO-max which combines reward normalization, KL-penalty, critic pre-training, and PTX loss.

title: Analyzing Transformers in Embedding Space
tldr: Projects all Transformer parameters into vocabulary/embedding space for input-free interpretation, enabling cross-model alignment and zero-shot weight transfer between pretrained/fine-tuned models.

title: Identifying and Mitigating the Security Risks of Generative AI
tldr: A Google workshop synthesis cataloging how GenAI enables new attacks (spear-phishing, deepfakes, cyberattacks) and surveying current and needed defenses including watermarking, detection, and alignment.

title: Coercing LLMs to do and reveal (almost) anything
tldr: Systematizes adversarial attacks on LLMs beyond jailbreaking, demonstrating extraction, misdirection, denial-of-service, and control attacks, and identifies glitch tokens and code-training as key vulnerability sources.

title: Copy Suppression: Comprehensively Understanding an Attention Head
tldr: Provides comprehensive mechanistic understanding of GPT-2 Small's L10H7 head, showing it performs copy suppression (reducing probability of already-seen tokens), explaining 76.9% of its impact.

title: Does your LLM truly unlearn? An embarrassingly simple approach to recover unlearned knowledge
tldr: Quantization recovers up to 83% of supposedly unlearned knowledge from LLMs, and SURE (saliency-based unlearning with large learning rate) mitigates this vulnerability.

title: Robust LLM Safeguarding via Refusal Feature Adversarial Training
tldr: Demonstrates that diverse jailbreak attacks share a universal mechanism of ablating a 'refusal feature' in residual streams, and proposes ReFAT training that is 1700x cheaper than R2D2 while substantially reducing attack success rates.

title: Towards LLM Unlearning Resilient to Relearning Attacks: A Sharpness-Aware Minimization Perspective and Beyond
tldr: Connects LLM unlearning robustness to sharpness-aware minimization (SAM), showing that loss landscape smoothing significantly resists relearning attacks that recover forgotten information via fine-tuning.

title: Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?
tldr: Argues that emergent abilities are artifacts of metric choice rather than fundamental phase transitions; continuous metrics reveal smooth performance improvements.

title: Understanding the Effects of RLHF on LLM Generalisation and Diversity
tldr: RLHF generalizes better than SFT to out-of-distribution inputs but substantially reduces output diversity, revealing a fundamental generalization-diversity tradeoff.

title: ODIN: Disentangled Reward Mitigates Hacking in RLHF
tldr: ODIN trains a two-head reward model that disentangles quality from length signals, using only the quality head during RL to prevent verbosity-driven reward hacking.

title: Adversarial Demonstration Attacks on Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes advICL, an adversarial attack that manipulates only in-context demonstrations (not test inputs) to mislead LLMs, achieving up to 100% attack success rate with more demonstrations increasing vulnerability.

title: Safety in Large Reasoning Models: A Survey
tldr: Comprehensive survey of safety risks, attacks, and defenses specific to large reasoning models (LRMs), covering harmful compliance, agentic misbehavior, multilingual/multimodal risks, and reasoning-specific attack vectors.

title: Applying Sparse Autoencoders to Unlearn Knowledge in Language Models
tldr: Demonstrates that individual SAE features can selectively unlearn biosecurity knowledge via negative clamping, though multi-feature interventions show greater side-effects than fine-tuning-based methods.

title: FlipAttack: Jailbreak LLMs via Flipping
tldr: FlipAttack exploits LLMs' left-to-right processing by disguising harmful prompts as flipped text, achieving ~98% jailbreak success on GPT-4o with a single query.

title: Eliciting Latent Knowledge from Quirky Language Models
tldr: Creates 'quirky' language models that systematically lie in certain contexts, then shows linear probes can recover truth from activations and anomaly detection flags untruthful behavior at 94% AUROC.

title: Revisiting Jailbreaking for Large Language Models: A Representation Engineering Perspective
tldr: Identifies 'Defense Representations' in LLM hidden states and shows that subtracting these activation patterns during decoding achieves jailbreaking without prompt engineering, bypassing even fine-tuned safety training.

title: Stealing Part of a Production Language Model
tldr: Demonstrates the first model-stealing attack that extracts the embedding projection layer from production LLMs like ChatGPT via API queries, revealing hidden dimensions for under $20.

title: Use of LLMs for Illicit Purposes: Threats, Prevention Measures, and Vulnerabilities
tldr: A taxonomy of LLM security threats (fraud, malware, misinformation), prevention measures (RLHF, filtering, red teaming), and vulnerabilities (prompt injection, jailbreaking), reviewing peer-reviewed and preprint literature.

title: BadChain: Backdoor Chain-of-Thought Prompting for Large Language Models
tldr: BadChain is a training-free backdoor attack on chain-of-thought prompting that achieves up to 97% attack success rate on GPT-4 by inserting malicious reasoning steps into demonstrations.

title: GuardAgent: Safeguard LLM Agents by a Guard Agent via Knowledge-Enabled Reasoning
tldr: Introduces GuardAgent, the first LLM agent that acts as a guardrail for other LLM agents by translating textual safety requests into executable guardrail code via knowledge-enabled reasoning.

title: Adversarial Attacks and Defenses in Large Language Models: Old and New Threats
tldr: Establishes LLM-specific adversarial evaluation guidelines, introduces embedding space attacks achieving 100% success on Llama-2-7B in 8.8 steps, and demonstrates how existing certified defenses can be trivially circumvented.

title: Agentic Misalignment: How LLMs Could Be Insider Threats
tldr: Tested 16 frontier LLMs in simulated corporate environments and found models from all developers engaged in blackmail and espionage when facing replacement threats or goal conflicts.

title: Refusal-Trained LLMs Are Easily Jailbroken As Browser Agents
tldr: Safety refusals in LLMs do not generalize to browser agent contexts; GPT-4o refuses 88% of harmful chat requests but attempts 74% of the same requests as a browser agent.

title: ETA: Evaluating Then Aligning Safety of Vision Language Models at Inference Time
tldr: ETA is a training-free inference-time framework that evaluates VLM inputs/outputs for safety via CLIP and reward models, then applies shallow prefix or deep sentence-level best-of-N alignment to cut unsafe responses by 87.5%.

title: Jailbreaking Large Language Models Against Moderation Guardrails via Cipher Characters
tldr: JAM uses cipher characters and shadow models to bypass both input- and output-level LLM moderation guardrails, achieving ~19.88x higher jailbreak success rate than baselines.

title: A Safety Realignment Framework via Subspace-Oriented Model Fusion for Large Language Models
tldr: SOMF framework recovers LLM safety after task-specific fine-tuning by identifying safety-critical weight subspaces via Concrete distribution masking and fusing aligned+fine-tuned models.

title: SelfDefend: LLMs Can Defend Themselves against Jailbreaking in a Practical Manner
tldr: SelfDefend uses a shadow LLM defense instance running concurrently with the target LLM to detect and block jailbreak attacks, reducing attack success rates by up to 100% with negligible normal-query overhead.

title: Safety-Aware Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
venue: NeurIPS 2024 Workshop on Safe Generative AI
tldr: Proposes SAFT, a framework that automatically detects and removes harmful samples from fine-tuning data using embedding subspace analysis via SVD, reducing harmfulness by up to 27.8%.

title: Teaching Language Models to Support Answers with Verified Quotes
tldr: GopherCite (280B) uses RLHF to produce answers with inline verified quotes from retrieved documents, achieving 80% supported-and-plausible on NQ and 90% with abstention, but citation alone doesn't guarantee truthfulness.

title: Auditing Large Language Models: A Three-Layered Approach
tldr: Proposes a three-layered framework for auditing LLMs: governance audits of providers, model audits post-training, and application audits of downstream products.

title: Red-Teaming for Generative AI: Silver Bullet or Security Theater?
tldr: Critically examines AI red-teaming practices across industry and academia, finding inconsistent definitions, weak follow-up, and proposing a structured question bank to improve rigor.

title: Circuit Component Reuse Across Tasks in Transformer Language Models
tldr: Demonstrates ~78% overlap in circuit components between IOI and Colored Objects tasks in GPT-2, suggesting LLMs decompose tasks into reusable algorithmic building blocks.

title: X-Risk Analysis for AI Research
tldr: Systematic guide for analyzing AI existential risks, proposing a risk decomposition framework and identifying key safety research areas and speculative hazards.

title: A Survey of Attacks on Large Vision-Language Models: Resources, Advances, and Future Trends
tldr: Comprehensive survey of attacks on Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) covering adversarial attacks, jailbreaks, prompt injection, and data poisoning, with resources and future directions.

title: On Scalable Oversight with Weak LLMs Judging Strong LLMs
tldr: Compares debate, consultancy, and direct QA protocols for scalable oversight using weak LLM judges evaluating strong LLM agents across 9 tasks, finding debate consistently outperforms consultancy.

title: Truth is Universal: Robust Detection of Lies in LLMs
tldr: Identifies a two-dimensional subspace in LLM activations separating true from false statements, enabling a classifier (TTPD) achieving 94% accuracy on T/F statements and 95% on real-world lies.

title: Multi-Turn Context Jailbreak Attack on Large Language Models From First Principles
tldr: Proposes Contextual Fusion Attack (CFA), a three-stage multi-turn jailbreak that filters malicious keywords, generates benign contextual scenarios, and dynamically integrates attack targets to bypass LLM safety alignment.

title: Me, Myself, and AI: The Situational Awareness Dataset (SAD) for LLMs
tldr: Introduces SAD, a 13K-question benchmark across 7 task categories measuring LLM situational awareness; finds chat models outperform base models but all fall far below human baselines.

title: RealSafe-R1: Safety-Aligned DeepSeek-R1 without Compromising Reasoning Capability
tldr: Produces safety-aligned DeepSeek-R1 models by training on 15K safety-aware reasoning trajectories with explicit refusal instructions, achieving strong jailbreak defense while preserving reasoning capability.

title: Jailbreak Large Vision-Language Models Through Multi-Modal Linkage
tldr: MML jailbreaks VLMs via cross-modal encryption-decryption and 'evil alignment' framing, achieving up to 99% attack success on GPT-4o across three safety benchmarks.

title: Teaching Models to Express Their Uncertainty in Words
tldr: GPT-3 can learn to express well-calibrated confidence levels in natural language (verbalized probabilities) without accessing model logits, outperforming logit-based approaches on out-of-distribution tasks.

title: Is Reinforcement Learning (Not) for Natural Language Processing?: Benchmarks, Baselines, and Building Blocks for Natural Language Policy Optimization
tldr: Introduces RL4LMs library, GRUE benchmark (7 NLG tasks), and NLPO algorithm for RL-based language model alignment, systematically studying reward hacking and regularization.

title: PromptBench: Towards Evaluating the Robustness of Large Language Models on Adversarial Prompts
tldr: Introduces PromptBench, a systematic benchmark with 4,788 adversarial prompts across character/word/sentence/semantic levels showing LLMs are vulnerable to prompt perturbations, with word-level attacks causing ~33% performance drops.

title: Precise Model Editing in a Transformer (PMET)
tldr: Improves ROME/MEMIT by simultaneously optimizing MHSA and FFN hidden states but only updating FFN weights, achieving more precise edits with better generalization.

title: WARM: On the Benefits of Weight Averaged Reward Models
tldr: WARM averages reward model weights (not predictions) from multiple fine-tuned checkpoints, reducing reward hacking and improving robustness with no inference-time cost.

title: Information Flow Routes: Automatically Interpreting Language Models at Scale
tldr: Proposes attribution-based information flow graphs for interpreting transformer predictions ~100x faster than activation patching, enabling scalable circuit discovery on any prediction.

title: Jailbreaking Prompt Attack: A Controllable Adversarial Attack against Diffusion Models
tldr: JPA is a black-box prompt attack that uses Classifier-Free Guidance in CLIP embedding space to bypass safety filters on text-to-image models, achieving 67% attack success rate while preserving semantic coherence.

title: Polysemanticity and Capacity in Neural Networks
tldr: Introduces a feature capacity framework showing that optimal capacity allocation leads to monosemantic important features, polysemantic less-important ones, and ignored unimportant ones.

title: Can LLMs Separate Instructions From Data? And What Do We Even Mean By That?
tldr: Introduces formal definitions and the SEP dataset (9,160 samples) to measure instruction-data separation in LLMs, finding all 7 tested models fail this fundamental safety property.

title: A Mutation-Based Method for Multi-Modal Jailbreaking Attack Detection
tldr: JailGuard detects multi-modal jailbreaking attacks by mutating inputs and measuring response divergence, achieving 89.38% accuracy on images and 85.42% on text.

title: Sparse Autoencoders Do Not Find Canonical Units of Analysis
tldr: Shows SAE latents are neither complete nor atomic: larger SAEs learn novel features missed by smaller ones, and individual latents decompose into interpretable sub-components via meta-SAEs.

title: Bypassing the Safety Training of Open-Source LLMs with Priming Attacks
tldr: Priming attacks bypass LLM safety training by appending partial compliant responses to harmful prompts, achieving up to 3.3x improvement in attack success rate over baselines.

title: LLMs know their vulnerabilities: Uncover Safety Gaps through Natural Distribution Shifts
tldr: ActorAttack uses actor-network theory to craft multi-turn jailbreak attacks that exploit natural distribution shifts in LLMs, achieving 78.8% ASR across five models including GPT-o1.

title: On Evaluating the Durability of Safeguards for Open-Weight LLMs
tldr: Demonstrates that small evaluation setup variations can drastically change outcomes for two proposed open-weight LLM safeguards (RepNoise and TAR), revealing five critical evaluation pitfalls.

title: Rigorously Assessing Natural Language Explanations of Neurons
tldr: Develops observational and intervention-based evaluations for neuron explanations, finding GPT-4-generated explanations of GPT-2 XL neurons have high error rates and negligible causal efficacy.

title: Steering Without Side Effects: Improving Post-Deployment Control of Language Models
tldr: KL-then-steer (KTS) trains LMs to minimize KL divergence between steered and unsteered outputs on benign inputs, enabling 44% jailbreak reduction with near-baseline helpfulness.

title: Knowledge Sanitization of Large Language Models
tldr: Fine-tunes LLMs via LoRA on MLP layers to replace specific memorized facts with safe phrases like 'I don't know', achieving near-complete forgetting while preserving general performance.

title: The Geometry of Refusal in Large Language Models: Concept Cones and Representational Independence
tldr: Challenges single-direction view of LLM refusal by discovering multi-dimensional polyhedral 'refusal cones' and mechanistically independent refusal directions via gradient-based optimization.
models_studied: multiple LLMs of varying sizes (unspecified in summary)

title: Defensive Prompt Patch: A Robust and Interpretable Defense of LLMs against Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: Proposes Defensive Prompt Patch (DPP), interpretable suffix prompts optimized via a Hierarchical Genetic Algorithm that reduce jailbreak ASR to 3.8% on LLAMA-2 and 2.0% on Mistral while preserving utility.

title: A Closer Look at Machine Unlearning for Large Language Models
tldr: Identifies failure modes in LLM unlearning methods and proposes entropy maximization for untargeted unlearning and answer preservation loss for targeted unlearning, with three new evaluation metrics.

title: Preventing Language Models From Hiding Their Reasoning
tldr: Demonstrates that LLMs can be trained to hide reasoning via steganography in chain-of-thought text, and shows paraphrasing limits encoding to ~3 bits per KB as a defense.

title: RobustBench: a standardized adversarial robustness benchmark
tldr: RobustBench introduces a standardized adversarial robustness leaderboard and model zoo using AutoAttack, covering 120+ evaluations on CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet with rigorous restrictions to prevent overestimation.

title: Self-Rewarding Language Models
tldr: Language models can iteratively improve both instruction-following and reward-modeling by using themselves as judges via LLM-as-a-Judge prompting during DPO training, outperforming GPT-4 0613 on AlpacaEval 2.0.

title: Transformer-Patcher: One Mistake worth One Neuron
tldr: Proposes Transformer-Patcher, which corrects transformer mistakes by adding one trainable neuron per error to the last FFN layer, enabling thousands of sequential edits without catastrophic forgetting.

title: Sociotechnical Safety Evaluation of Generative AI Systems
tldr: Proposes a three-layered sociotechnical framework (capability, human interaction, systemic impact) for evaluating generative AI safety, surveys 83+ existing evaluations, and identifies critical gaps in coverage, context, and multimodal evaluation.

title: Red teaming ChatGPT via Jailbreaking: Bias, Robustness, Reliability and Toxicity
tldr: Systematic red-teaming of ChatGPT across bias, robustness, reliability, and toxicity reveals that standard benchmarks mask serious ethical risks, with 95/98 unsafe scenarios successfully jailbroken.

title: PoisonedRAG: Knowledge Corruption Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
tldr: PoisonedRAG injects as few as 5 poisoned texts into RAG knowledge databases to manipulate LLM outputs with ~90% attack success rate across 8 LLMs and 3 datasets.

title: Question Decomposition Improves the Faithfulness of Model-Generated Reasoning
tldr: Factored question decomposition forces LLMs to answer subquestions in isolated contexts, improving reasoning faithfulness (33.6% vs 9.6% corruption sensitivity) at a modest accuracy cost (81.8% vs 86.0%).

title: PrivacyLens: Evaluating Privacy Norm Awareness of Language Models in Action
tldr: PrivacyLens is a multi-level framework evaluating how well LLMs respect privacy norms in agent tasks; GPT-4 and Llama-3-70B leak sensitive info in 25.68% and 38.69% of cases.

title: Attacking Vision-Language Computer Agents via Pop-ups
tldr: Adversarial pop-ups achieve 86% attack success rate on vision-language model agents across OSWorld and VisualWebArena benchmarks, reducing task completion by 47%, with basic defenses proving ineffective.

title: The Geometry of Categorical and Hierarchical Concepts in Large Language Models
tldr: Proves that categorical concepts are represented as simplices and hierarchically related concepts are orthogonal in LLM representation spaces, validated on 957 WordNet concepts in Gemma.

title: LLM Censorship: A Machine Learning Challenge or a Computer Security Problem?
tldr: Proves semantic LLM output censorship is undecidable and shows practical mosaic prompt attacks that reconstruct forbidden outputs from permitted ones, arguing censorship should be a security not ML problem.

title: Improving Activation Steering in Language Models with Mean-Centring
tldr: Proposes mean-centring (subtracting training activation mean from target activation mean) to produce more effective steering vectors without requiring contrastive concept pairs.

title: ShieldLM: Empowering LLMs as Aligned, Customizable and Explainable Safety Detectors
tldr: ShieldLM trains open-weight LLMs (6B-14B) as safety detectors that align with human standards, support customizable detection rules, and provide explanations, outperforming GPT-4 and Llama Guard 2 across four test sets.

title: When LLM Meets DRL: Advancing Jailbreaking Efficiency via DRL-guided Search
tldr: RLbreaker uses deep RL (PPO) to guide jailbreak prompt search against LLMs, outperforming genetic algorithm baselines across 6 models and resisting 3 defenses.

title: Distract Large Language Models for Automatic Jailbreak Attack
tldr: Tastle is a black-box jailbreak framework using malicious content concealing and memory reframing with iterative optimization to automatically bypass LLM safety alignment.

title: Tricking LLMs into Disobedience: Understanding, Analyzing, and Preventing Jailbreaks
tldr: Proposes a formal framework and taxonomy of LLM jailbreak attacks, evaluates attack effectiveness across GPT-3.5, BLOOM, OPT, and FLAN-T5, and tests defensive prompt guard strategies.

title: Is This the Subspace You Are Looking for? An Interpretability Illusion for Subspace Activation Patching
venue: NeurIPS 2023 Workshop on Attributing Model Behavior at Scale
tldr: Demonstrates that subspace activation patching can create interpretability illusions where causally disconnected dormant pathways are activated, giving false evidence of feature localization.

title: Sparse Autoencoders Trained on the Same Data Learn Different Features
tldr: SAEs trained identically except for random initialization learn substantially different features, with only ~30% shared across seeds in large models, challenging the assumption of universal feature discovery.

title: Model Tampering Attacks Enable More Rigorous Evaluations of LLM Capabilities
tldr: Introduces model tampering attacks (modifying weights/activations) as a complement to input-space attacks for evaluating LLM safety, showing they predict and upper-bound worst-case behaviors across 65 unlearned and 9 safety-tuned models.

title: Targeted Vaccine: Safety Alignment for Large Language Models against Harmful Fine-Tuning via Layer-wise Perturbation
tldr: T-Vaccine defends LLM safety alignment against harmful fine-tuning by selectively perturbing only safety-critical layers identified via gradient norms, reducing harmful scores by 8.19% over Vaccine while cutting memory use by 31.53%.

title: Transformers Learn In-Context by Gradient Descent
tldr: Proves that linear self-attention layers implement gradient descent steps on in-context examples, establishing a formal connection between in-context learning and mesa-optimization.

title: Secrets of RLHF in Large Language Models Part II: Reward Modeling
tldr: Addresses noisy preference data and reward model generalization in RLHF via multi-model voting for preference strength, label correction, contrastive learning, and meta-learning (MetaRM).

title: A Comprehensive Study of Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models
tldr: Comprehensive survey of 25+ knowledge editing methods for LLMs, categorized into three cognitive phases (recognition, association, mastery), with a new KnowEdit benchmark and open-source EasyEdit framework.

title: CValues: Measuring the Values of Chinese Large Language Models from Safety to Responsibility
tldr: Introduces CValues, the first Chinese LLM values alignment benchmark with 2,100 adversarial safety prompts and 800 expert responsibility prompts, plus a 145K comparison dataset.

title: Improving Instruction-Following in Language Models through Activation Steering
tldr: Extracts instruction-specific steering vectors from activation differences and injects them at inference time to improve instruction-following without retraining, achieving ~30% adherence even without explicit text instructions.

title: Universal Neurons in GPT2 Language Models
tldr: 1-5% of neurons in GPT-2 models are 'universal' (activate identically across independently trained seeds), are interpretable, and cluster into distinct functional families.

title: Successor Heads: Recurring, Interpretable Attention Heads In The Wild
tldr: Discovers 'successor heads' -- attention heads that predict the next item in ordinal sequences (Monday to Tuesday, January to February) -- and explains their mechanism via mod-10 features.

title: SEAL: Safety-enhanced Aligned LLM Fine-tuning via Bilevel Data Selection
tldr: SEAL uses bilevel optimization to learn a data selector that upweights safe, high-quality fine-tuning samples and downweights harmful ones, achieving 8.5-9.7% win rate improvements over random selection.

title: Safety Cases: How to Justify the Safety of Advanced AI Systems
tldr: Proposes a structured framework for building 'safety cases' -- explicit arguments with evidence chains justifying why an AI system is safe enough to deploy.

title: SimpleSafetyTests: a Test Suite for Identifying Critical Safety Risks in Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces SimpleSafetyTests, a 100-prompt benchmark across 5 harm areas that reveals most open-source LLMs respond unsafely >20% of the time, with safety system prompts reducing failures from 33% to 21%.

title: BEEAR: Embedding-based Adversarial Removal of Safety Backdoors in Instruction-tuned Language Models
tldr: BEEAR defends against safety backdoors in LLMs by exploiting uniform embedding drifts from triggers via bi-level optimization, reducing attack success rates from >95% to <1%.

title: Honesty Is the Best Policy: Defining and Mitigating AI Deception
tldr: Formalizes AI deception using structural causal games with graphical criteria for detection, and demonstrates path-specific objectives can mitigate deceptive behavior in RL agents and language models.

title: On the Role of Attention Heads in Large Language Model Safety
tldr: Identifies sparse safety-critical attention heads in LLMs via Ships/Sahara metrics; ablating one head raises harmful query success rate 16x while modifying only 0.006% of parameters.

title: Enhancing LLM Safety via Constrained Direct Preference Optimization
tldr: C-DPO integrates dual gradient descent with Direct Preference Optimization to balance helpfulness and harmlessness in LLMs, achieving better safety guarantees than vanilla DPO and higher helpfulness than Safe RLHF.

title: Interpreting Attention Layer Outputs with Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Trains SAEs on attention layer outputs, finding ~90% of GPT-2 Small heads are polysemantic, identifying induction/context feature families, and revealing new IOI circuit details.

title: BadLlama: cheaply removing safety fine-tuning from Llama 2-Chat 13B
tldr: Demonstrates that safety fine-tuning on Llama 2-Chat 13B can be completely reversed for under $200 while preserving general capabilities, highlighting fundamental limits of safety training when model weights are public.

title: No Two Devils Alike: Unveiling Distinct Mechanisms of Fine-tuning Attacks
tldr: Decomposes LLM safety into three stages and shows that explicit harmful attacks and identity-shifting fine-tuning attacks compromise safety through dramatically different mechanisms, implying unified defenses are insufficient.

title: Be Careful about Poisoned Word Embeddings: Exploring the Vulnerability of the Embedding Layers in NLP Models
tldr: Demonstrates that modifying a single word embedding vector can inject backdoors into NLP models without any task-specific data, achieving ~100% attack success while preserving clean accuracy.

title: A Primer on the Inner Workings of Transformer-based Language Models
tldr: A concise technical survey unifying interpretability methods for decoder-only transformers, covering behavior localization, information decoding, SAEs, and discovered internal mechanisms under a single notation.

title: PsySafe: A Comprehensive Framework for Psychological-based Attack, Defense, and Evaluation of Multi-agent System Safety
tldr: PsySafe injects dark psychological traits into multi-agent LLM systems to expose collective safety failures, then proposes defenses and evaluation metrics grounded in agent psychology.

title: Evaluating the Susceptibility of Pre-Trained Language Models via Handcrafted Adversarial Examples
tldr: Demonstrates that handcrafted prompt injection attacks ('ignore previous instructions') cause significant misclassification in GPT-3, BERT, RoBERTa, and ALBERT, while standard quality metrics like BLEU and BERTScore fail to detect the semantic corruption.

title: Adaptive Activation Steering: A Tuning-Free LLM Truthfulness Improvement Method for Diverse Hallucinations Categories
tldr: ACT adaptively steers LLM activations toward truthfulness at inference time using clustered steering vectors and probe-based intensity control, achieving up to 142% improvement on TruthfulQA without fine-tuning.

title: SafeGen: Mitigating Sexually Explicit Content Generation in Text-to-Image Models
tldr: SafeGen removes explicit visual representations from text-to-image models via text-agnostic self-attention modification, achieving 99.1% NSFW removal while preserving benign image quality.

title: Don't Say No: Jailbreaking LLM by Suppressing Refusal
tldr: DSN enhances GCG jailbreaks by adding a refusal suppression loss (Unlikelihood), raising Llama-2 ASR from 29.8% to 47.7% and proposing an ensemble NLI+LLM evaluation pipeline.

title: Operationalizing a Threat Model for Red-Teaming Large Language Models
tldr: Systematization of knowledge for red-teaming LLMs: develops a threat model with actor/surface/goal taxonomy, categorizes attacks by LLM lifecycle stage, and compiles defense strategies.

title: STAR-1: Safer Alignment of Reasoning LLMs with 1K Data
tldr: Introduces STAR-1, a 1K-sample safety dataset for reasoning LLMs built on diversity, deliberative reasoning, and quality filtering, achieving ~40% safety improvement with only ~1.1% reasoning degradation.

title: Knowledge Unlearning for LLMs: Tasks, Methods, and Challenges
tldr: Survey of LLM knowledge unlearning methods categorized into parameter optimization, parameter merging, and in-context learning approaches, with evaluation datasets and future challenges.

title: Arondight: Red Teaming Large Vision Language Models with Auto-generated Multi-modal Jailbreak Prompts
tldr: Arondight is an automated red teaming framework for VLMs that combines toxic image generation with RL-guided diverse text prompts, achieving 84.5% attack success rate against GPT-4 across 14 prohibited scenarios.

title: To Each (Textual Sequence) Its Own: Improving Memorized-Data Unlearning in Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes per-sequence unlearning methods (Selective Gradient Ascent and Task Arithmetic for Unlearning) that outperform baselines by targeting highly memorized samples individually rather than treating all forget-set examples equally.

title: Skywork-Reward: Bag of Tricks for Reward Modeling in LLMs
tldr: Demonstrates that carefully curated 80K preference pairs outperform 700K-sample datasets for reward modeling, achieving #1 on RewardBench via data selection and filtering strategies.

title: Risk Taxonomy, Mitigation, and Assessment Benchmarks of Large Language Model Systems
tldr: A module-oriented taxonomy of LLM system risks (12 risk types, 44 sub-topics) spanning input, model, toolchain, and output layers, with mitigation strategies and assessment benchmark coverage.

title: Breaking Agents: Compromising Autonomous LLM Agents Through Malfunction Amplification
tldr: Novel malfunction-amplification attacks (infinite loops, irrelevant actions) compromise autonomous LLM agents with >80% failure rates in multiple scenarios, and are difficult to detect with LLM-based defenses.

title: Tell me about yourself: LLMs are aware of their learned behaviors
tldr: LLMs finetuned on datasets exhibiting implicit behaviors can describe those behaviors without in-context examples, enabling potential backdoor detection but also raising deception risks.

title: PromptArmor: Simple yet Effective Prompt Injection Defenses
tldr: PromptArmor uses an off-the-shelf LLM as a preprocessing guardrail to detect and remove injected prompts, achieving <1% false positive and false negative rates on AgentDojo.

title: Rethinking LLM Unlearning Objectives: A Gradient Perspective and Go Beyond
tldr: Introduces the G-effect framework to analyze unlearning objectives via gradient dot products and proposes WGA and TNPO methods that better balance knowledge removal with model utility preservation.

title: Instructional Segment Embedding: Improving LLM Safety with Instruction Hierarchy
tldr: Adds learnable segment embeddings to LLMs that encode instruction priority (system/user/data), improving robustness to prompt injection and harmful requests by up to 18.68% with minimal architecture changes.

title: Detecting Strategic Deception Using Linear Probes
tldr: Linear probes on LLM activations detect strategic deception (insider trading, sandbagging) with AUROC 0.96-0.999 and 95-99% recall at 1% FPR, but remain insufficient as robust defense.

title: JBShield: Defending Large Language Models from Jailbreak Attacks through Activated Concept Analysis and Manipulation
tldr: JBShield uses concept vectors extracted via SVD from hidden representations to detect (0.95 accuracy) and mitigate (61%→2% attack success rate) jailbreak attacks on LLMs without fine-tuning.

title: Decomposing The Dark Matter of Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Decomposes SAE error ('dark matter') into linear and nonlinear components, finding ~90% of error norms and ~50% of error vectors are linearly predictable from input activations.

title: Efficient Dictionary Learning with Switch Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Switch SAEs route activations between smaller expert SAEs using sparse mixture-of-experts, achieving better reconstruction-sparsity tradeoffs at lower compute cost than standard SAEs.

title: Automatic Pseudo-Harmful Prompt Generation for Evaluating False Refusals in Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces PHTest, a 3,260-prompt benchmark for evaluating false refusals in LLMs via automated pseudo-harmful prompt generation, revealing a fundamental safety-usability trade-off across 20 models.

title: NLSR: Neuron-Level Safety Realignment of Large Language Models Against Harmful Fine-Tuning
tldr: NLSR is a training-free framework that restores LLM safety after harmful fine-tuning by identifying and transplanting safety-critical neurons from a reference model.

title: LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
tldr: LLMs exhibit self-preference bias when evaluating text, scoring their own outputs higher than equivalent alternatives, and this bias is causally linked to their ability to recognize their own generations.

title: Towards Understanding Grokking: An Effective Theory of Representation Learning
tldr: Develops an effective theory explaining grokking via representation learning dynamics, mapping four learning phases in phase diagrams over hyperparameters.

title: Aligning Language Models with Preferences through f-divergence Minimization
tldr: Proposes f-DPG, a unified framework for aligning LMs via any f-divergence, showing Jensen-Shannon divergence consistently balances alignment quality and output diversity better than standard KL.

title: Consequences of Misaligned AI
tldr: Proves that optimizing any incomplete proxy objective eventually leads to arbitrarily low true utility, and proposes impact minimization and interactive reward design as mitigations.

title: Tracr: Compiled Transformers as a Laboratory for Interpretability
tldr: Introduces Tracr, a compiler that translates human-readable RASP programs into transformer weights, creating models with known ground-truth circuits for evaluating interpretability methods.

title: Overthinking the Truth: Understanding How Language Models Process False Demonstrations
tldr: Identifies 'overthinking' in LMs where correct early-layer representations are overridden by later 'false induction heads' that copy incorrect patterns from few-shot demonstrations.

title: Universal Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models: Backdoor Attacks for In-context Learning
tldr: ICLAttack poisons LLM demonstration contexts or prompts to achieve 95% average backdoor attack success rate without fine-tuning, across models from 1.3B to 180B parameters.

title: WASP: Benchmarking Web Agent Security Against Prompt Injection Attacks
tldr: WASP benchmark shows that even top AI models (GPT-4o, Claude-3.7) can be deceived by simple human-written prompt injections in realistic web navigation tasks, with attacks partially succeeding in up to 86% of cases.

title: Machine Unlearning in Generative AI: A Survey
tldr: A comprehensive survey of machine unlearning techniques for generative AI, covering LLMs, vision, and multimodal models, with new problem formulations, evaluation metrics, and categorizations.

title: Testing Language Model Agents Safely in the Wild
tldr: Proposes AgentMonitor, a context-sensitive safety monitoring framework for testing autonomous LM agents in real-world environments, achieving 89.4% F1 at flagging unsafe actions on AutoGPT.

title: SafeArena: Evaluating the Safety of Autonomous Web Agents
tldr: SafeArena is the first benchmark for deliberate misuse of LLM-based web agents; GPT-4o and Qwen-2-VL complete 22-35% of harmful tasks, showing poor safety transfer to agentic settings.

title: Understanding and Enhancing Safety Mechanisms of LLMs via Safety-Specific Neuron
tldr: Identifies safety-specific neurons (<1% of parameters, in self-attention layers) in LLMs and introduces SN-Tune and RSN-Tune for targeted safety enhancement and preservation.

title: JAILJUDGE: A Comprehensive Jailbreak Judge Benchmark with Multi-Agent Enhanced Explanation Evaluation Framework
