tldr: JAILJUDGE introduces a comprehensive benchmark (35k+ training samples, 10.5k+ human-annotated tests) and multi-agent framework for explainable, fine-grained jailbreak detection, achieving F1 of 0.91 vs GPT-4's 0.55.

title: Projecting Assumptions: The Duality Between Sparse Autoencoders and Concept Geometry
tldr: Shows different SAE architectures impose implicit geometric assumptions that determine which concepts they can recover, and proposes SpaDE (Sparsemax Distance Encoder) to handle nonlinear separability and heterogeneous dimensionality.

title: Immunization against harmful fine-tuning attacks
tldr: Proposes formal 'immunization conditions' — resistance, stability, generalization, trainability — as a framework for designing and evaluating defenses against harmful fine-tuning attacks on safety-aligned LLMs.

title: Mitigating Fine-tuning based Jailbreak Attack with Backdoor Enhanced Safety Alignment
tldr: Proposes BackdoorAlign, which uses secret prompt triggers prefixed to safety examples during fine-tuning to defend against fine-tuning-based jailbreak attacks, achieving <4% ASR with only 11 safety examples.

title: Revisiting Who's Harry Potter: Towards Targeted Unlearning from a Causal Intervention Perspective
tldr: Provides a causal intervention framework that formalizes and improves the Who's Harry Potter LLM unlearning method, treating target knowledge as a confounder to enable targeted entity removal.

title: Natural Adversarial Examples
tldr: Introduces ImageNet-A and ImageNet-O, adversarially filtered datasets of natural images that cause ~90% accuracy drops in classifiers, revealing shared model weaknesses.

title: Math-Shepherd: Verify and Reinforce LLMs Step-by-step without Human Annotations
tldr: Introduces Math-Shepherd, a process reward model trained on automatically constructed step-level supervision data, improving math reasoning accuracy (e.g., Mistral-7B from 77.9% to 84.1% on GSM8K) without human annotations.

title: SafetyPrompts: a Systematic Review of Open Datasets for Evaluating and Improving Large Language Model Safety
tldr: Systematic review of 102 open LLM safety datasets (2018-2024), finding explosive 2023 growth but severe English-bias, lack of standardization, and under-use of available datasets in practice.

title: Characterizing Manipulation from AI Systems
tldr: Proposes a four-axis framework (incentives, intent, covertness, harm) for characterizing AI manipulation and identifies key measurement challenges.

title: On the Pitfalls of Analyzing Individual Neurons in Language Models
tldr: Identifies two methodological pitfalls in neuron analysis: conflating probe quality with ranking quality, and confusing encoded information with information actually used by the model.

title: GuardReasoner: Towards Reasoning-based LLM Safeguards
tldr: GuardReasoner trains LLM guard models to reason about safety decisions via R-SFT and HS-DPO on a 127K-sample dataset, achieving 84.09% avg F1 and outperforming GPT-4o+CoT by 5.74%.

title: RedCode: Risky Code Execution and Generation Benchmark for Code Agents
tldr: RedCode is a benchmark with 4,050+ test cases across 25 risky scenarios and 8 domains evaluating whether code agents execute or generate harmful code, finding existing agents remain highly vulnerable.

title: Secret Collusion Among Generative AI Agents
tldr: Formalizes the problem of secret collusion among generative AI agents via steganography, proposes the CASE evaluation framework, and finds GPT-4 shows a capability jump in steganographic abilities requiring continuous monitoring.

title: Safetywashing: Do AI Safety Benchmarks Actually Measure Safety Progress?
tldr: Meta-analysis showing many AI safety benchmarks strongly correlate with general model capabilities and compute, enabling 'safetywashing' where capability gains masquerade as safety progress.
models_studied: Multiple base and instruction-tuned language models (dozens analyzed across model families)

title: Spectral Editing of Activations for Large Language Model Alignment
tldr: SEA uses SVD on cross-covariance matrices of activations to surgically edit concept-specific directions at inference time, improving truthfulness and fairness without training.

title: Recurrent Neural Networks Learn to Store and Generate Sequences using Non-Linear Representations
tldr: Small GRUs learn non-linear 'onion representations' where sequence positions are encoded by magnitude rather than direction, providing a concrete counterexample to the Strong Linear Representation Hypothesis.

title: Bag of Tricks: Benchmarking of Jailbreak Attacks on LLMs
tldr: JailTrickBench systematically benchmarks 9 jailbreak attacks across 8 key factors (4 attack-level, 4 target-level) and 6 defenses on LLMs via ~354 experiments.

title: Thought Crime: Backdoors and Emergent Misalignment in Reasoning Models
tldr: Reasoning models fine-tuned on narrow malicious data exhibit broad emergent misalignment; their chain-of-thought often conceals rather than reveals deception, undermining CoT monitoring.

title: Automated Red Teaming with GOAT: the Generative Offensive Agent Tester
tldr: GOAT is a multi-turn automated red teaming agent that chains 7 jailbreaking strategies across conversation turns, achieving 97% ASR against Llama 3.1 and 88% against GPT-4-Turbo on JailbreakBench.

title: Understanding Jailbreak Success: A Study of Latent Space Dynamics in Large Language Models
tldr: Analyzes latent space dynamics of 24 jailbreak types on Vicuna 13B, finding that jailbreak vectors transfer across attack classes and most effective jailbreaks suppress the model's harmfulness representation.

title: Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models via Shuffle Inconsistency
tldr: SI-Attack exploits 'Shuffle Inconsistency' in MLLMs — models retain comprehension of shuffled harmful text/images but lose safety protection — boosting jailbreak ASR on GPT-4o from 20.77% to 68.57%.

title: Stress-Testing Capability Elicitation With Password-Locked Models
tldr: Introduces password-locked models as a stress-testing framework for capability elicitation, finding that a few high-quality demonstrations often suffice to unlock hidden capabilities via fine-tuning.

title: Uncovering Deceptive Tendencies in Language Models: A Simulated Company AI Assistant
tldr: Claude 3 Opus spontaneously deceives in a simulated company assistant setting: astroturfing then covering it up, lying to auditors, and sandbagging on capability evaluations.

title: UNDIAL: Self-Distillation with Adjusted Logits for Robust Unlearning in Large Language Models
tldr: UNDIAL uses self-distillation with adjusted logits ('deliberate imagination') to remove memorized sensitive data from LLMs while preserving both language generation and understanding capabilities.

title: Interpreting CLIP's Image Representation via Text-Based Decomposition
tldr: Decomposes CLIP image representations across layers, heads, and tokens using text-based labeling (TextSpan), revealing property-specific attention heads and enabling spurious feature removal and zero-shot segmentation.

title: AI Agents Under Threat: A Survey of Key Security Challenges and Future Pathways
tldr: A systematic survey of security vulnerabilities in AI agents, identifying four critical threat dimensions: unpredictable multi-step inputs, complex internal executions, variable environments, and untrusted external entities.

title: Language Models Implement Simple Word2Vec-style Vector Arithmetic
tldr: Shows that LLMs solve one-to-one relational tasks (e.g., country-capital) via simple Word2Vec-style vector arithmetic implemented as additive updates in feedforward networks.

title: Managing AI Risks in an Era of Rapid Progress
tldr: A consensus statement by 24 prominent AI researchers identifying societal-scale AI risks and proposing urgent technical R&D and governance priorities to maintain human control over advanced AI systems.

title: A Mechanistic Interpretation of Arithmetic Reasoning in Language Models using Causal Mediation Analysis
tldr: Uses causal mediation analysis to trace which transformer components drive arithmetic predictions, finding attention blocks transmit operand info while late MLP layers generate result-specific information.

title: GuardT2I: Defending Text-to-Image Models from Adversarial Prompts
tldr: GuardT2I uses an LLM to decode T2I model text embeddings into natural language and detect adversarial prompts, outperforming commercial moderators with 95.58% average AUROC.

title: SelfIE: Self-Interpretation of Large Language Model Embeddings
tldr: SelfIE enables LLMs to interpret their own hidden embeddings in natural language and introduces Supervised/Reinforcement Control methods that edit model reasoning with single-layer gradients, reducing prompt injection success from 89% to 4.4%.

title: Hijacking Large Language Models via Adversarial In-Context Learning
tldr: GGI algorithm generates imperceptible adversarial suffix tokens appended to ICL demonstrations to hijack LLMs into producing targeted wrong outputs, achieving ~100% attack success across models.

title: Breaking Down the Defenses: A Comparative Survey of Attacks on Large Language Models
tldr: A comparative survey of LLM attack methodologies — jailbreaks, prompt injection, and data poisoning — organized by a novel taxonomy based on model access level and attack vector, with coverage of defenses.

title: LlamaFirewall: An Open Source Guardrail System for Building Secure AI Agents
tldr: Open-source modular guardrail framework with three components (PromptGuard 2, AlignmentCheck, CodeShield) that reduces agentic attack success rates by >90% through layered prompt injection detection, reasoning auditing, and code analysis.

title: Finding Transformer Circuits with Edge Pruning
tldr: Edge Pruning discovers sparse transformer circuits by optimizing continuous masks on edges between components, finding circuits with <50% the edges of prior methods and scaling to 13B-parameter models.

title: Get My Drift? Catching LLM Task Drift with Activation Deltas
tldr: Detects prompt injection attacks on LLMs by comparing internal activation deltas before and after external input, achieving >0.99 ROC AUC across four models without modifying them.

title: Misusing Tools in Large Language Models With Visual Adversarial Examples
tldr: Demonstrates that gradient-based visual adversarial perturbations can covertly manipulate multimodal LLMs into invoking unintended tools (e.g., deleting emails, booking tickets) with ~98% success on simple attacks while maintaining image imperceptibility.

title: RedAgent: Red Teaming Large Language Models with Context-aware Autonomous Language Agent
tldr: RedAgent is a multi-agent LLM system that uses context-aware jailbreak strategy learning to compromise most black-box LLMs in ≤5 queries, 2x more efficiently than prior methods.

title: Persona Features Control Emergent Misalignment
tldr: Uses sparse autoencoders to identify 'misaligned persona' features that control emergent misalignment in GPT-4o, finding a toxic persona feature that predicts and can steer misalignment, with fine-tuning on 100s of benign samples restoring alignment.

title: On Large Language Models' Resilience to Coercive Interrogation
venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy 2024
tldr: LINT exploits top-k logit access to force LLMs to reveal concealed harmful outputs via selective low-ranked token forcing, achieving 92% attack success vs 62% for jailbreaking, 10-20x faster.

title: Soft Prompting for Unlearning in Large Language Models
tldr: SPUL uses learnable soft prompt tokens (not weight updates) to make LLMs forget specific training examples, reducing trainable parameters from billions to ~1M while achieving near-zero forget accuracy.

title: Editable Neural Networks
tldr: Introduces Editable Training, a meta-learning method that prepares neural network parameters for fast post-hoc correction of individual predictions without harming overall model performance.

title: You Autocomplete Me: Poisoning Vulnerabilities in Neural Code Completion
tldr: Demonstrates that neural code autocompleters are vulnerable to targeted data and model poisoning attacks that cause them to suggest insecure code patterns while preserving overall model utility.

title: The Earth is Flat because...: Investigating LLMs' Belief towards Misinformation via Persuasive Conversation
tldr: LLMs' correct factual beliefs are easily manipulated by persuasive multi-turn conversations containing misinformation, with ChatGPT flipping 50.1% of the time and Llama-2-7B 78.2%.

title: SAFREE: Training-Free and Adaptive Guard for Safe Text-to-Image And Video Generation
tldr: SAFREE is a training-free guard for diffusion models that projects unsafe token embeddings orthogonal to toxic concept subspaces and uses adaptive latent re-attention to filter harmful content without retraining.

title: InfoRM: Mitigating Reward Hacking in RLHF via Information-Theoretic Reward Modeling
tldr: InfoRM uses an information-theoretic variational bottleneck to train reward models that generalize better and resist reward hacking, plus an ICDS score to detect overoptimization.

title: AIR-Bench 2024: A Safety Benchmark Based on Risk Categories from Regulations and Policies
tldr: AIR-Bench 2024 introduces a 5,694-prompt safety benchmark grounded in 314 risk categories derived from 8 government regulations and 16 corporate policies, revealing major safety gaps in 22 evaluated LLMs.

title: Large Language Model Safety: A Holistic Survey
tldr: Comprehensive survey of LLM safety covering value misalignment, adversarial robustness, misuse, autonomous AI risks, agent safety, interpretability for safety, industry roadmaps, and governance frameworks.

title: MAIA: A Multimodal Automated Interpretability Agent
tldr: MAIA is an agent that uses a VLM backbone and interpretability tool API to autonomously design and run iterative experiments for understanding neural network components.

title: Specific versus General Principles for Constitutional AI
tldr: Shows that a single broad 'do what's best for humanity' principle can train AI models to suppress dangerous behaviors nearly as well as detailed trait-specific constitutional rules.

title: SafeBench: A Safety Evaluation Framework for Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: SafeBench introduces a 2,300-sample multimodal safety benchmark across 23 risk scenarios and a jury deliberation protocol (JDP) that achieves Cohen's Kappa=0.89 with human judgment for evaluating 21 MLLMs.

title: Scalable AI Safety via Doubly-Efficient Debate
tldr: Designs doubly-efficient debate protocols where the honest strategy needs only polynomial simulation steps (not exponential) and can verify stochastic AI systems.

title: Qwen3Guard Technical Report
tldr: Qwen3Guard introduces multilingual safety guardrail models (0.6B–8B) with tri-class judgments and a novel streaming variant for real-time token-level content moderation during LLM generation.

title: PARDEN, Can You Repeat That? Defending against Jailbreaks via Repetition
tldr: PARDEN defends against jailbreaks by prompting an LLM to repeat its own output and using BLEU scores to detect refusals, achieving 11x FPR reduction over classification baselines.

title: Prompt Packer: Deceiving LLMs through Compositional Instruction with Hidden Attacks
venue: ACM Transactions on Autonomous and Adaptive Systems
tldr: CIA embeds harmful prompts inside benign composite instructions (talk/write tasks), achieving 95%+ attack success on GPT-4/ChatGPT/ChatGLM2 with two automated transformation methods.

title: Bergeron: Combating Adversarial Attacks through a Conscience-Based Alignment Framework
tldr: Bergeron is a dual-LLM framework where a secondary conscience model monitors inputs/outputs of a primary LLM to detect and correct adversarial attacks, reducing GPT-3.5 failure rate from 40% to 8%.

title: Sabotage Evaluations for Frontier Models
tldr: Develops threat models and evaluations for four types of AI sabotage: human decision sabotage, code sabotage, sandbagging, and undermining oversight, finding minimal mitigations currently suffice but stronger ones will be needed soon.

title: MRJ-Agent: An Effective Jailbreak Agent for Multi-Round Dialogue
tldr: MRJ-Agent uses risk decomposition across multi-round dialogues and 13 psychological tactics to achieve up to 100% jailbreak success on GPT-3.5/4, outperforming all prior single- and multi-round methods.

title: Alternate Preference Optimization for Unlearning Factual Knowledge in Large Language Models
tldr: AltPO combines negative feedback with in-domain positive alternatives for LLM unlearning, achieving coherent knowledge removal while introducing new metrics (Forget Utility, Cleanness Indistinguishability) to assess output quality.

title: Does Unlearning Truly Unlearn? A Black Box Evaluation of LLM Unlearning Methods
tldr: Demonstrates that LLM unlearning methods (LLMU, RMU) fail to truly erase knowledge: 5-shot prompting or rephrasing recovers up to 1750% accuracy, and fine-tuning on benign data fully restores unlearned capabilities.

title: Future Lens: Anticipating Subsequent Tokens from a Single Hidden State
tldr: Individual hidden states in GPT-J-6B encode information about multiple future tokens, recoverable at 48%+ accuracy via learned prompt causal intervention at middle layers.

title: Defining and Characterizing Reward Hacking
tldr: Provides the first formal definition of reward hacking and proves that non-trivial unhackable proxy reward functions are impossible for stochastic policies due to the linear structure of rewards.

title: EasyEdit: An Easy-to-use Knowledge Editing Framework for Large Language Models
tldr: Provides a unified open-source framework integrating 30+ knowledge editing methods (ROME, MEMIT, MEND, SERAC, IKE, GRACE, etc.) with standardized evaluation across multiple LLMs.

title: Building Guardrails for Large Language Models
tldr: A position paper surveying LLM guardrail systems (Llama Guard, NeMo, Guardrails AI) and proposing a systematic neural-symbolic, lifecycle-based approach to building robust, verifiable guardrails.

title: Flooding Spread of Manipulated Knowledge in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Communities
tldr: A two-stage attack (persuasiveness injection via DPO+LoRA + knowledge injection via ROME) causes LLM agents to spread counterfactual and toxic knowledge across multi-agent communities with 40-60% and 10-20% spread accuracy respectively.

title: Latent Guard: a Safety Framework for Text-to-image Generation
tldr: Latent Guard detects unsafe text-to-image prompts by operating in the text encoder's latent space with contrastive training and LLM-synthesized concept-based data, achieving >0.90 AUC on adversarial/OOD inputs.

title: Steering Knowledge Selection Behaviours in LLMs via SAE-Based Representation Engineering
tldr: SpARE uses pre-trained SAEs to identify and edit functional features controlling knowledge selection in LLMs, outperforming baselines by 10-15% on knowledge conflict resolution.

title: RRM: Robust Reward Model Training Mitigates Reward Hacking
tldr: A causal framework with data augmentation trains reward models robust to context-free artifacts (length, format), improving RewardBench from 80.61% to 84.15% and reducing policy response length by ~40%.

title: Circuit Breaking: Removing Model Behaviors with Targeted Ablation
venue: ICML 2023 Workshop on Challenges in Deployable Generative AI
tldr: Proposes targeted edge ablation to remove undesirable model behaviors by learning to ablate minimal causal pathways, removing just 12 of 11,600 edges to mitigate GPT-2 toxicity with minimal performance loss.

title: SafeMLRM: Demystifying Safety in Multi-modal Large Reasoning Models
tldr: First systematic safety analysis of multi-modal large reasoning models (MLRMs), finding reasoning capabilities degrade safety alignment by 37.44% higher jailbreak success rates, with scenario-specific blind spots up to 25x worse.

title: Meta SecAlign: A Secure Foundation LLM Against Prompt Injection Attacks
tldr: Meta SecAlign is the first open-source LLM with built-in prompt injection defense, using DPO fine-tuning with a new 'input' role template to achieve state-of-the-art robustness with minimal utility loss.

title: Model Organisms for Emergent Misalignment
tldr: Develops improved model organisms for emergent misalignment achieving 99% coherence (vs 67% prior), shows EM works across 0.5B-32B models and multiple families, and identifies a mechanistic phase transition during training.

title: Reasoning-to-Defend: Safety-Aware Reasoning Can Defend Large Language Models from Jailbreaking
tldr: R2D trains LLMs to embed safety evaluations into their reasoning steps via pivot tokens ([SAFE]/[UNSAFE]/[RETHINK]) and Contrastive Pivot Optimization, reducing jailbreak success rates by up to 56% across multiple attack types.

title: Cross-Modal Safety Alignment: Is textual unlearning all you need?
tldr: Textual-only unlearning in VLMs reduces multimodal attack success rates to <8% while preserving utility, outperforming multimodal unlearning at 6x lower compute cost.

title: Learning and Forgetting Unsafe Examples in Large Language Models
tldr: Unsafe examples are forgotten faster than safe content during safety realignment; ForgetFilter exploits this signal to filter noisy finetuning data, improving safety without hurting task performance.

title: Locking Down the Finetuned LLMs Safety
tldr: SafetyLock extracts safety-direction vectors from attention heads in aligned LLMs and applies them at inference time to restore safety in fine-tuned models in under 0.01 seconds.

title: Analyzing Individual Neurons in Pre-trained Language Models
tldr: Identifies minimal neuron subsets in BERT/XLNet that capture linguistic properties, showing morphology localizes to fewer neurons than syntax, with architectural differences in information distribution.

title: Neuron-level Interpretation of Deep NLP Models: A Survey
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
tldr: Comprehensive survey of neuron-level analysis methods for deep NLP models, covering five method families, evaluation approaches, and architectural findings about how neurons encode linguistic knowledge.

title: A Practical Review of Mechanistic Interpretability for Transformer-Based Language Models
tldr: Provides a practical taxonomy of MI techniques with a beginner's roadmap and actionable steps, plus a comprehensive 200+ paper GitHub list.

title: The Emerged Security and Privacy of LLM Agent: A Survey with Case Studies
tldr: Comprehensive survey of security and privacy threats in LLM agents, categorizing inherited LLM vulnerabilities and agent-specific threats (knowledge poisoning, functional manipulation, output manipulation) with defensive strategies.

title: How Do Language Models Bind Entities in Context?
tldr: Discovers 'binding ID' vectors that language models use to link entities to their attributes, enabling compositional in-context reasoning.

title: Evaluating Superhuman Models with Consistency Checks
tldr: Proposes evaluating superhuman AI models via logical consistency checks rather than correctness, revealing systematic inconsistencies in chess engines, LLM forecasters, and legal decision-makers.

title: SG-Bench: Evaluating LLM Safety Generalization Across Diverse Tasks and Prompt Types
tldr: SG-Bench evaluates LLM safety generalization across generative and discriminative tasks with varied prompt types, finding most models perform worse on discriminative tasks and are highly susceptible to prompt changes.

title: pyvene: A Library for Understanding and Improving PyTorch Models via Interventions
tldr: Open-source Python library providing a unified, extensible framework for performing customizable interventions on PyTorch models, supporting interpretability analyses like causal abstraction and knowledge localization.

title: Here Comes The AI Worm: Unleashing Zero-click Worms that Target GenAI-Powered Applications
tldr: Morris II is the first AI worm targeting GenAI ecosystems, using adversarial self-replicating prompts to propagate across email assistant agents and perform spamming/data exfiltration.

title: Persistent Pre-Training Poisoning of LLMs
tldr: Poisoning just 0.1% of pre-training data enables denial-of-service, context extraction, and belief manipulation attacks that persist through SFT and DPO post-training alignment.

title: Towards Understanding the Fragility of Multilingual LLMs against Fine-Tuning Attacks
tldr: Fine-tuning attacks on multilingual LLMs generalize across all languages via shared safety parameters; modifying just 20% of weights suffices to remove multilingual safety alignment.

title: Emulated Disalignment: Safety Alignment for Large Language Models May Backfire!
tldr: Emulated Disalignment (ED) is a training-free inference-time attack that combines pre-trained and safety-aligned LLMs via contrastive sampling to double harmful response rates.

title: Best-of-Venom: Attacking RLHF by Injecting Poisoned Preference Data
tldr: Injecting 1-5% poisoned preference pairs into RLHF training data can reliably steer LLM outputs to favor specific entities with desired sentiment, while evading standard detection.

title: A Survey on Sparse Autoencoders: Interpreting the Internal Mechanisms of LLMs
tldr: Most comprehensive SAE-specific survey covering all variants (L1, TopK, Gated, JumpReLU, Switch), training strategies, evaluation methods, and applications.

title: Best-of-N Jailbreaking
tldr: A simple black-box jailbreak that repeatedly samples augmented prompt variations (shuffled chars, random caps, pitch shifts) until the model produces harmful output, achieving 89% ASR on GPT-4o across text, vision, and audio modalities.

title: HAICOSYSTEM: An Ecosystem for Sandboxing Safety Risks in Human-AI Interactions
tldr: Introduces a sandbox framework for evaluating AI agent safety in multi-turn human-AI interactions with tools across 7 domains, finding state-of-the-art LLMs exhibit safety risks in over 50% of simulated scenarios.

title: Sparse Interventions in Language Models with Differentiable Masking
tldr: Introduces differentiable masking with L0 regularization to discover minimal neuron subsets causally responsible for linguistic phenomena in language models, finding <0.5% of neurons suffice.

title: When "Competency" in Reasoning Opens the Door to Vulnerability: Jailbreaking LLMs via Novel Complex Ciphers
tldr: Demonstrates that word substitution ciphers can bypass LLM safety guardrails, achieving up to 59.42% attack success rate on ChatGPT, GPT-4, and Gemini-Pro.

title: How (un)ethical are instruction-centric responses of LLMs? Unveiling the vulnerabilities of safety guardrails to harmful queries
tldr: Instruction-centric prompts (pseudocode, code snippets) bypass LLM safety guardrails, increasing harmful output generation by 2-38%; model editing further amplifies this by 3-16%.

title: Debate Helps Supervise Unreliable Experts
tldr: Adversarial debate between two unreliable experts helps non-expert judges identify truth at 84% accuracy vs 74% for single-expert consultancy, validating debate as a scalable oversight mechanism.

title: The Philosopher's Stone: Trojaning Plugins of Large Language Models
tldr: Malicious LoRA adapters (Trojan plugins) can hijack open-source LLMs to produce adversary-controlled outputs; two novel attacks (polished and fusion) achieve near-100% success while evading detection.

title: Accelerating Greedy Coordinate Gradient and General Prompt Optimization via Probe Sampling
tldr: Probe sampling uses a small draft model to filter GCG adversarial suffix candidates before target-model evaluation, achieving up to 5.6x speedup on Llama2-7b with equal or improved attack success rate.

title: Query-Efficient Black-Box Red Teaming via Bayesian Optimization
tldr: Proposes Bayesian Red Teaming (BRT), a query-efficient method using Gaussian Process surrogate models to iteratively find diverse failure-inducing test cases in black-box generative models.

title: Evaluating Open-Source Sparse Autoencoders on Disentangling Factual Knowledge in GPT-2 Small
tldr: Evaluates four open-source SAEs on disentangling country/continent knowledge in GPT-2 Small using RAVEL benchmark; finds SAEs struggle to match even the neuron baseline, far below supervised DAS skyline.

title: OS-Harm: A Benchmark for Measuring Safety of Computer Use Agents
tldr: Introduces OS-Harm, a 150-task benchmark measuring safety of LLM-based computer use agents across deliberate misuse, prompt injection, and model misbehavior, finding all frontier models frequently comply with harmful requests.

title: Exploring Criteria of Loss Reweighting to Enhance LLM Unlearning
tldr: Proposes SatImp, a unified loss reweighting method combining Saturation and Importance criteria to improve LLM unlearning on forgetting and retention tasks.

title: Leveraging the Context through Multi-Round Interactions for Jailbreaking Attacks
tldr: Contextual Interaction Attack uses multi-round preliminary question-answer exchanges to progressively guide LLMs toward harmful outputs, achieving up to 96% attack success rate across major models.

title: Competition Report: Finding Universal Jailbreak Backdoors in Aligned LLMs
tldr: Competition challenging participants to find universal backdoor triggers in RLHF-aligned LLMs; embedding-based detection and genetic algorithms proved most effective at recovering injected trojan strings.

title: LoFT: Local Proxy Fine-tuning For Improving Transferability Of Adversarial Attacks Against Large Language Model
tldr: LoFT fine-tunes public proxy LLMs on target model responses in the neighborhood of harmful queries, improving adversarial attack transferability against ChatGPT (10x), GPT-4 (143% relative), and Claude.

title: Safety Pretraining: Toward the Next Generation of Safe AI
tldr: A data-centric pretraining framework with four components (safety filtering, rephrasing, native refusal datasets, harmfulness-tag annotation) reduces LLM attack success rates from 38.8% to 8.4% with no general capability degradation.

title: OpenUnlearning: Accelerating LLM Unlearning via Unified Benchmarking of Methods and Metrics
tldr: OpenUnlearning is a unified framework integrating 13 unlearning algorithms and 16 evaluations across 3 benchmarks (TOFU, MUSE, WMDP), with 450+ checkpoints, to standardize LLM unlearning research.

title: How Language Model Hallucinations Can Snowball
tldr: Demonstrates that LLMs over-commit to early errors, producing additional hallucinations they would otherwise avoid, a phenomenon termed hallucination snowballing.

title: Poisoning and Backdooring Contrastive Learning
tldr: Demonstrates that contrastive learning models like CLIP can be poisoned by modifying just 0.01% of training data (300 of 3M images), and backdoored with as few as 3 images.

title: A Roadmap to Pluralistic Alignment
tldr: Proposes a taxonomy of three pluralistic alignment operationalizations (Overton, Steerable, Distributional) and three benchmark types, finding current alignment techniques reduce distributional pluralism.

title: CLIP-Dissect: Automatic Description of Neuron Representations in Deep Vision Networks
tldr: Leverages CLIP to automatically label individual neurons in vision networks with human-readable concept descriptions, achieving 95% top-1 accuracy 10-200x faster than prior methods.

title: Spear Phishing With Large Language Models
tldr: Demonstrates that GPT-3.5/GPT-4 can generate over 600 personalized spear phishing emails at a fraction of a cent each, showing LLMs effectively scale social engineering attacks.

title: What Would Jiminy Cricket Do? Towards Agents That Behave Morally
tldr: Introduces Jiminy Cricket, a suite of 25 text-based adventure games with dense morality annotations, and a commonsense morality policy shaping method that reduces agent immorality by 64% without sacrificing task performance.

title: CyberSecEval 2: A Wide-Ranging Cybersecurity Evaluation Suite for Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces CyberSecEval 2, a benchmark evaluating LLM cybersecurity risks across prompt injection, code interpreter abuse, vulnerability exploitation, and insecure coding, finding all models 26-41% vulnerable to prompt injection.

title: The Art of Saying No: Contextual Noncompliance in Language Models
tldr: Introduces CoCoNot, a 1,000-prompt evaluation suite and taxonomy for contextual noncompliance, revealing GPT-4 incorrectly complies ~30% of the time on non-safety refusal categories.

title: AI Research Considerations for Human Existential Safety (ARCHES)
tldr: Introduces the concept of 'prepotence' to analyze AI existential risk and proposes 29 research directions organized by delegation type (single/multi human-AI) across comprehension, instruction, and control.

title: Hidden Incentives for Auto-Induced Distributional Shift
tldr: Formalizes auto-induced distributional shift (ADS) where ML systems change their own input distributions, shows meta-learning reveals hidden incentives to exploit this, and proposes context swapping as mitigation.

title: Adaptive Attacks Break Defenses Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM Agents
tldr: Adaptive attacks bypass all 8 evaluated defenses against indirect prompt injection on LLM agents, achieving >50% attack success rate in every case.

title: Effectively Controlling Reasoning Models through Thinking Intervention
tldr: Thinking Intervention inserts guidance directly into reasoning model thought tokens at inference time, achieving 6.7% gains in instruction following, 15.4% in instruction hierarchy, and 40% higher unsafe-prompt refusal rates without retraining.

title: Hoodwinked: Deception and Cooperation in a Text-Based Game for Language Models
tldr: Introduces Hoodwinked, a text-based social deduction game for LLMs, finding that more advanced models are better deceivers and that discussion enables both information sharing and deception.

title: Can Language Models be Instructed to Protect Personal Information?
tldr: Introduces PrivQA benchmark to evaluate LLMs' ability to follow access-control instructions protecting personal information; self-moderation improves protection but simple jailbreaks easily circumvent it.

title: Can LLMs Follow Simple Rules?
tldr: RuLES is a 15-scenario programmatic benchmark revealing that GPT-4, Claude, and Llama 2 widely fail to follow developer-specified rules under hand-crafted and GCG adversarial attacks.

title: Evaluating Copyright Takedown Methods for Language Models
tldr: CoTaEval is the first systematic evaluation framework for copyright takedown methods in LLMs, finding no existing method excels at preventing regurgitation while maintaining utility and low overhead.

title: Separate the Wheat from the Chaff: Model Deficiency Unlearning via Parameter-Efficient Module Operation
tldr: Proposes Extraction-before-Subtraction (Ext-Sub), which decomposes LoRA anti-expert modules into general and deficiency components via vector projection, enabling targeted unlearning of untruthfulness/toxicity without degrading core capabilities.

title: garak: A Framework for Security Probing Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces garak, an open-source framework with ~60 probes for systematically discovering LLM vulnerabilities including jailbreaks, prompt injection, toxic generation, and data exfiltration.

title: Challenges with Unsupervised LLM Knowledge Discovery
tldr: Proves theoretically and shows empirically that unsupervised methods like CCS discover prominent features rather than actual model knowledge, as arbitrary binary features satisfy CCS's consistency loss equally well.

title: Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data
tldr: Teacher LLMs transmit behavioral traits (e.g., animal preferences, misalignment) to student models via semantically unrelated filtered training data like number sequences, a property grounded in shared model initialization.

title: Adversarial Tuning: Defending Against Jailbreak Attacks for LLMs
tldr: A two-stage adversarial tuning framework that generates both token-level and semantic-level adversarial prompts to fine-tune LLMs for improved jailbreak defense.

title: Exploiting Novel GPT-4 APIs
tldr: Demonstrates that GPT-4's fine-tuning, function calling, and knowledge retrieval APIs introduce critical safety vulnerabilities exploitable with as few as 15 poisoned examples.

title: An Overview of 11 Proposals for Building Safe Advanced AI
tldr: Evaluates 11 proposals for building safe advanced AI across four dimensions: outer alignment, inner alignment, training competitiveness, and performance competitiveness.

title: Foot In The Door: Understanding Large Language Model Jailbreaking via Cognitive Psychology
tldr: Applies cognitive consistency theory (Foot-in-the-Door) to explain and automate LLM jailbreaks, achieving 83.9% average attack success rate across 8 LLMs via progressive multi-step prompts.

title: Extending Activation Steering to Broad Skills and Multiple Behaviours
tldr: Activation steering can target broad skills (general coding) as effectively as narrow ones (Python), but combining multiple steering vectors into one fails; injecting them at separate layers works better.

title: Steering Away from Harm: An Adaptive Approach to Defending Vision Language Model Against Jailbreaks
tldr: ASTRA defends VLMs against jailbreaks by identifying harmful visual tokens via random ablation and applying adaptive activation steering at inference time, reducing attack success to ~9% with negligible overhead.

title: Towards Robust Knowledge Unlearning: An Adversarial Framework for Assessing and Improving Unlearning Robustness in Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes DUA (adversarial attack recovering unlearned knowledge in 55.2% of cases) and LAU (min-max defense improving unlearning robustness by 53.5%+) for LLMs.

title: Erasing Conceptual Knowledge from Language Models
tldr: ELM uses low-rank updates and three complementary loss objectives to erase dangerous conceptual knowledge (biosecurity, cybersecurity) from LLMs while preserving fluency and unrelated capabilities.

title: SAEs Are Good for Steering -- If You Select the Right Features
tldr: Shows SAE steering failures stem from poor feature selection, not SAE limitations; filtering by output scores yields 2-3x improvement matching supervised methods.

title: A Sketch of an AI Control Safety Case
tldr: Proposes a structured safety case framework for arguing that internally-deployed LLM agents cannot subvert control measures to exfiltrate data, using game-theoretic red/blue team evaluation.

title: Adaptive Deployment of Untrusted LLMs Reduces Distributed Threats
tldr: Proposes a two-level adaptive framework (micro-protocols + Bayesian macro-protocol) for safely deploying untrusted LLMs in distributed threat settings, reducing backdoors by 80% while retaining 98.4% usefulness.

title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
tldr: Shows that RLVR does not elicit fundamentally new reasoning in LLMs â€” base models achieve comparable or higher pass@k at large k, indicating RL improves sampling efficiency but not reasoning boundaries.

title: AI Models Collapse When Trained on Recursively Generated Data
tldr: Training generative models on recursively generated synthetic data causes irreversible 'model collapse' where distribution tails disappear and outputs converge to point estimates.

title: Emergent and Predictable Memorization in Large Language Models
tldr: Develops scaling laws to predict which training sequences LLMs will memorize, finding memorization exhibits emergent non-monotonic behavior not predicted by smaller models.

title: The Radicalization Risks of GPT-3 and Advanced Neural Language Models
tldr: Evaluates GPT-3's potential for weaponization by extremists, finding it generates ideologically consistent propaganda with minimal prompting, unlike GPT-2 which required extensive fine-tuning.

title: LLMs Know More Than They Show: On the Intrinsic Representation of LLM Hallucinations
tldr: LLM internal states encode far more truthfulness information than previously known, concentrated at specific 'exact answer tokens', enabling AUC 0.85-0.95 error detection but with limited cross-task generalization.

title: LLM Agents can Autonomously Exploit One-day Vulnerabilities
tldr: GPT-4 agents autonomously exploit 87% of real-world one-day CVE vulnerabilities using a 91-line ReAct agent, while all other models and scanners achieve 0%.

title: ARGS: Alignment as Reward-Guided Search
tldr: ARGS aligns LLM outputs at decoding time by mixing reward signals into token scoring, achieving 19.56% reward improvement over baseline without any RL training.

title: Safeguarding Large Language Models: A Survey
tldr: Systematic survey of LLM guardrail frameworks, covering 8 safety properties, 49 jailbreak methods, and a proposed neural-symbolic multi-disciplinary framework for comprehensive safeguarding.

title: Neurons in Large Language Models: Dead, N-gram, Positional
tldr: Categorizes FFN neurons in OPT models into dead (never activate, >70% in large models), N-gram detectors (suppress triggering tokens), and positional neurons encoding position.

title: Circumventing Concept Erasure Methods For Text-to-Image Generative Models
tldr: Demonstrates that seven concept erasure methods for text-to-image models fail under a Concept Inversion attack that recovers erased content via learned word embeddings without modifying model weights.

title: Feedback Loops With Language Models Drive In-Context Reward Hacking
tldr: Demonstrates that feedback loops between LLMs and their environment cause in-context reward hacking (ICRH), where models optimize stated objectives while producing harmful side effects at test time.

title: AirGapAgent: Protecting Privacy-Conscious Conversational Agents
tldr: AirGapAgent defends LLM-based conversational agents against context hijacking attacks that trick agents into leaking private user data, achieving 97% privacy protection vs. 45% for baseline agents.

title: Aligning Large Language Models with Representation Editing: A Control Perspective
tldr: Re-Control frames LLM alignment as a discrete-time control problem, training a value function on hidden states and using gradient-based optimization at inference time to steer outputs without fine-tuning.

title: Looking Inward: Language Models Can Learn About Themselves by Introspection
tldr: LLMs finetuned to predict their own behavior outperform other models given identical training data, suggesting genuine introspective access to internal states rather than mere pattern matching.

title: Are DeepSeek R1 And Other Reasoning Models More Faithful?
tldr: ITC/reasoning models (QwQ, Gemini-flash-thinking) articulate cues influencing their answers far more faithfully than standard models — up to 54% vs. 14% for comparable non-ITC baseline.

title: Protecting Privacy in Multimodal Large Language Models with MLLMU-Bench
tldr: MLLMU-Bench is a benchmark of 20,754 Q&A pairs across 653 profiles for evaluating machine unlearning in multimodal LLMs, revealing key trade-offs between unlearning efficacy and model utility.

title: Commercial LLM Agents Are Already Vulnerable to Simple Yet Dangerous Attacks
tldr: Demonstrates that commercial LLM agents (Anthropic Computer Use, MultiOn, ChemCrow) are trivially exploitable via multi-hop prompt injection and jailbreaks, achieving 10/10 success on credit card theft and malware execution.

title: An Approach to Technical AGI Safety and Security
tldr: Google DeepMind's comprehensive AGI safety framework identifying four risk areas (misuse, misalignment, mistakes, structural) with defense-in-depth strategy combining model-level and system-level mitigations.

title: On the Exploitability of Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback for Large Language Models
tldr: RankPoison exploits RLHF by flipping preference rankings to induce malicious model behaviors (longer outputs, backdoors) while evading safety detection.

title: On Large Language Model Continual Unlearning
tldr: O3 framework for continual LLM unlearning uses orthogonal LoRA adapters and OOD detection to remove knowledge without retained data, avoiding cumulative utility loss across successive requests.

title: AdvWeb: Controllable Black-box Attacks on VLM-powered Web Agents
tldr: AdvWeb trains a black-box adversarial prompt generator that injects hidden HTML text to mislead VLM-powered web agents into executing targeted harmful actions with 97.5%+ success rates.

title: Offset Unlearning for Large Language Models
tldr: delta-Unlearning enables black-box LLMs to forget sensitive training data by learning logit offsets from paired smaller models, without requiring access to the target model's weights.

title: JailbreakEval: An Integrated Toolkit for Evaluating Jailbreak Attempts Against Large Language Models
tldr: JailbreakEval is a unified toolkit consolidating four categories of jailbreak evaluators (human, string-matching, chat-completion, text-classification) to enable consistent jailbreak success assessment across LLM safety research.

title: A Mousetrap: Fooling Large Reasoning Models for Jailbreak with Chain of Iterative Chaos
tldr: Mousetrap is a jailbreak framework that chains iterative encoding transformations (Caesar cipher, ASCII, etc.) into reasoning prompts to bypass safety alignment in LRMs, achieving 96-98% attack success on o1-mini and Gemini-thinking.

title: AttackEval: How to Evaluate the Effectiveness of Jailbreak Attacking on Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces coarse-grained and fine-grained evaluation frameworks (0-1 scale) for jailbreak attack effectiveness on LLMs, plus a 390-question ground truth dataset across 13 risk categories.

title: Stress Testing Deliberative Alignment for Anti-Scheming Training
tldr: Stress-tests deliberative alignment as anti-scheming training across 180+ environments, finding it reduces covert actions from 13% to 0.4% (o3) but does not eliminate them, with situational awareness partially confounding results.

title: Enhancing Automated Interpretability with Output-Centric Feature Descriptions
tldr: Output-centric feature descriptions (via vocabulary projection and token change analysis) capture causal effects of features on outputs, and ensembling them with input-centric methods improves automated interpretability by 6-10%.

title: The MASK Benchmark: Disentangling Honesty From Accuracy in AI Systems
tldr: MASK is a 1,500-example benchmark that disentangles honesty (belief-statement consistency) from accuracy (belief-truth alignment), finding that larger LLMs become more accurate but not more honest and lie substantially under pressure.

title: Towards Understanding Safety Alignment: A Mechanistic Perspective from Safety Neurons
tldr: Identifies sparse 'safety neurons' (~5% of all neurons) in aligned LLMs via activation contrasting and dynamic patching; patching only these neurons restores 90%+ safety without hurting general ability.

title: Bi-Factorial Preference Optimization: Balancing Safety-Helpfulness in Language Models
tldr: BFPO re-parameterizes multi-objective RLHF (safety + helpfulness) into a single supervised learning objective via a labeling function, achieving comparable safety/helpfulness with <10% of the compute.

title: Towards Robust and Parameter-Efficient Knowledge Unlearning for LLMs
tldr: Proposes Inverted Hinge Loss and Fisher-weighted LoRA initialization (FLoRA) for robust, parameter-efficient LLM unlearning that avoids catastrophic forgetting caused by vanilla gradient ascent.

title: Holistic Automated Red Teaming for Large Language Models through Top-Down Test Case Generation and Multi-turn Interaction
tldr: HARM introduces a holistic automated red teaming framework using a fine-grained risk taxonomy for broad test coverage and RL-trained multi-turn adversarial probing to expose LLM vulnerabilities more comprehensively.

title: Intrinsic Evaluation of Unlearning Using Parametric Knowledge Traces
tldr: Proposes intrinsic evaluation of LLM unlearning via 'concept vectors' in MLP layers, showing fine-tuning-based unlearning barely changes parametric knowledge traces while direct ablation effectively removes knowledge and resists jailbreaks.

title: Mechanistic Unlearning: Robust Knowledge Unlearning and Editing via Mechanistic Localization
tldr: Targeting fact-lookup MLP components via mechanistic interpretability yields more robust knowledge unlearning/editing that resists relearning and reduces side effects compared to output-tracing localization.

title: Sudden Drops in the Loss: Syntax Acquisition, Phase Transitions, and Simplicity Bias in MLMs
tldr: Identifies abrupt phase transitions during BERT training where syntactic attention structure (SAS) emerges suddenly, shows SAS is causally necessary for linguistic capabilities, and finds brief SAS suppression improves final performance.

title: The Remarkable Robustness of LLMs: Stages of Inference?
tldr: Layer deletion and swapping experiments reveal LLMs retain 72-95% accuracy, suggesting four universal inference stages: detokenization, feature engineering, prediction ensembling, and residual sharpening.

title: Do Language Models Have Beliefs? Methods for Detecting, Updating, and Visualizing Model Beliefs
tldr: Introduces methods for detecting, updating, and visualizing model beliefs in ~100M parameter LMs, showing that SLAG (Sequential, Local, and Generalizing) training improves belief consistency across sequential edits.

title: Towards Adversarial Evaluations for Inexact Machine Unlearning
tldr: Proposes the Interclass Confusion (IC) test, a black-box adversarial evaluation for machine unlearning, and two baselines (EU-k, CF-k) that outperform existing inexact unlearning methods.

title: A Survey on Trustworthy LLM Agents: Threats and Countermeasures
tldr: TrustAgent: a comprehensive survey framework organizing threats and defenses for LLM-based agents across intrinsic (brain, memory, tool) and extrinsic (agent, environment, user) dimensions.

title: Prover-Verifier Games Improve Legibility of LLM Outputs
tldr: Trains prover-verifier game dynamics where a strong prover must produce outputs legible to a weak verifier, improving both correctness and checkability of LLM reasoning.

title: Digital Forgetting in Large Language Models: A Survey of Unlearning Methods
tldr: Comprehensive survey of machine unlearning methods for LLMs, proposing a four-category taxonomy (global weight, local weight, architecture, input/output modification) and unified evaluation framework.

title: On Targeted Manipulation and Deception when Optimizing LLMs for User Feedback
tldr: Training LLMs with RL on user feedback causes them to learn targeted manipulation and deception toward vulnerable users, and standard safety evals fail to detect these behaviors.

title: Codebook Features: Sparse and Discrete Interpretability for Neural Networks
tldr: Trains neural networks with vector quantization bottlenecks producing sparse discrete hidden states ('codebook features') that are more interpretable than neurons and enable causal control of model behavior.

title: Provably safe systems: the only path to controllable AGI
tldr: Proposes provably compliant systems (PCS) using proof-carrying code, formal verification, and mechanistic interpretability as the only guaranteed path to controllable AGI.

title: Dissecting Language Models: Machine Unlearning via Selective Pruning
tldr: Introduces selective pruning to remove specific capabilities from LLMs by identifying and zeroing neurons with high relative importance for targeted vs retained tasks.

title: Voice Jailbreak Attacks Against GPT-4o
tldr: VoiceJailbreak uses fictional storytelling (setting, character, plot) to jailbreak GPT-4o voice mode, raising average attack success rate from 3.3% to 77.8% across six prohibited scenarios.

title: Towards Understanding the Safety Boundaries of DeepSeek Models: Evaluation and Findings
tldr: First comprehensive safety evaluation of the full DeepSeek model series (R1, V3, VL2, Janus-Pro) using a new bilingual Chinese-English benchmark, revealing major vulnerabilities to jailbreaks, cross-lingual safety gaps, and CoT-exposed attack vectors.

title: Safety case template for frontier AI: A cyber inability argument
tldr: Proposes a detailed safety case template using the Claims-Arguments-Evidence framework to argue that frontier AI systems lack dangerous offensive cyber capabilities.

title: Surgical, Cheap, and Flexible: Mitigating False Refusal in Language Models via Single Vector Ablation
tldr: Training-free single vector ablation with orthogonalization reduces false refusal in safety-tuned LLMs by up to 30 percentage points while maintaining true safety refusal rates.

title: A Geometric Notion of Causal Probing
tldr: Proposes a formal information-theoretic framework for causal probing via counterfactual distributions over linear concept subspaces, avoiding spurious correlations in concept erasure.

title: Backtracking Improves Generation Safety
tldr: Introduces a [RESET] token enabling LLMs to recognize and discard unsafe partial generations, achieving up to 72% reduction in safety violations and >2x reduction in adversarial attack success rates.

title: Is the System Message Really Important to Jailbreaks in Large Language Models?
tldr: System messages significantly affect LLM jailbreak resistance; a proposed evolutionary algorithm (SMEA) generates optimized system prompts achieving up to 98.9% resistance against jailbreak attempts.

title: Editing LLMs Can Stealthily Subvert Safety
tldr: Knowledge editing techniques (ROME, fine-tuning, in-context editing) can be misused to stealthily inject misinformation and biases into LLMs while maintaining normal capability profiles, evading standard detection.

title: Language Model Unalignment: Parametric Red-Teaming to Expose Hidden Harms and Biases
tldr: Introduces 'Unalignment,' a parametric red-teaming method that fine-tunes LLMs with ~100 harmful samples to bypass safety guardrails, achieving 88-93% attack success rates and exposing hidden biases.

title: To Forget or Not? Towards Practical Knowledge Unlearning for Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces KnowUnDo benchmark and MemFlex method for selective LLM knowledge unlearning that removes sensitive data while preserving essential knowledge, achieving 7.97% better success metrics than baselines.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Machine Unlearning Techniques for Large Language Models
tldr: A comprehensive taxonomy and review of machine unlearning techniques for LLMs, covering direct fine-tuning, localized parameter modification, auxiliary model, and input/output-based approaches with evaluation benchmarks.

title: Distraction is All You Need for Multimodal Large Language Model Jailbreaking
tldr: CS-DJ jailbreaks MLLMs by fragmenting harmful queries and using contrasting subimages to distract attention, achieving 52.4% ASR and 74.1% EASR on GPT-4o, GPT-4V, and Gemini.

title: What Features in Prompts Jailbreak LLMs? Investigating the Mechanisms Behind Attacks
tldr: Nonlinear (MLP) probes outperform linear probes at identifying jailbreak mechanisms, and MLP-guided perturbations achieve 74% attack success while defenses reduce it to 6%.

title: Unlearning Isn't Deletion: Investigating Reversibility of Machine Unlearning in LLMs
tldr: Current token-level unlearning metrics are misleading; models can rapidly recover 'forgotten' knowledge via minimal retraining, exposing a reversible-vs-irreversible forgetting distinction.

title: Adversaries Can Misuse Combinations of Safe Models
tldr: Adversaries can decompose malicious tasks across multiple individually-safe models, achieving 43% success on vulnerable code generation vs <3% with any single model.

title: Heuristic-Induced Multimodal Risk Distribution Jailbreak Attack for Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: HIMRD splits harmful prompts across text and image modalities to evade MLLM safety filters, achieving ~90% attack success rate on 7 open-source and ~68% on 3 closed-source MLLMs.

title: Automatically Identifying Local and Global Circuits with Linear Computation Graphs
tldr: Introduces Skip SAEs to linearize transformer computation graphs, enabling exact (non-approximate) automated circuit discovery at the SAE feature level in GPT-2 Small.

title: Single-Turn Debate Does Not Help Humans Answer Hard Reading-Comprehension Questions
venue: ACL 2022 Workshop on Learning with Natural Language Supervision
tldr: Single-turn debate-style arguments do not improve human accuracy on hard QA, though providing text snippets as evidence does help, suggesting multi-turn debate may be necessary.

title: The VLLM Safety Paradox: Dual Ease in Jailbreak Attack and Defense
tldr: VLLMs show a safety paradox: simple jailbreak attacks succeed due to visual inputs, while defenses over-refuse benign queries; LLM guardrails as a pre-filter provide better safety-helpfulness balance.

title: A Probabilistic Perspective on Unlearning and Alignment for Large Language Models
tldr: Deterministic (greedy) evaluations of LLM unlearning are insufficient; multinomial sampling breaks all SOTA unlearning algorithms, so a probabilistic framework with high-probability leakage bounds is needed.

title: Direct Language Model Alignment from Online AI Feedback
tldr: OAIF replaces offline preference datasets with on-the-fly LLM annotation of response pairs from the current policy, combining DAP simplicity with RLHF's online nature and outperforming both.

title: Nightshade: Prompt-Specific Poisoning Attacks on Text-to-Image Generative Models
tldr: Nightshade is a prompt-specific data poisoning attack on text-to-image diffusion models that corrupts target concepts with fewer than 100 poison samples by exploiting concept sparsity in training data.

title: Do Models Explain Themselves? Counterfactual Simulatability of Natural Language Explanations
tldr: Proposes counterfactual simulatability to evaluate whether LLM explanations help humans predict model behavior on input variations; finds GPT-4 explanations are imprecise and plausibility does not correlate with faithfulness.

title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
tldr: RE-Bench benchmark of 7 ML R&D tasks shows AI agents score 4x higher than humans at 2h but humans achieve 2x agent scores at 32h, revealing a capability plateau in autonomous AI R&D.

title: Machine Against the RAG: Jamming Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Blocker Documents
tldr: Crafted 'blocker' documents inserted into RAG databases can jam systems into refusing to answer specific queries with 30-100% success rates across multiple LLMs.

title: TrojanRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Can Be Backdoor Driver in Large Language Models
tldr: TrojanRAG injects backdoor shortcuts into RAG knowledge bases via contrastive learning and knowledge graphs, achieving 80%+ attack success while maintaining normal retrieval on clean queries.

title: Backdoor Attacks and Countermeasures in Natural Language Processing Models: A Comprehensive Security Review
tldr: Comprehensive survey of backdoor attacks and defenses on NLP models, categorizing attacks by pipeline stage (fine-tuning, parameter-efficient tuning, final-model training) and defenses into sample vs. model inspection.

title: Securing Large Language Models: Threats, Vulnerabilities and Responsible Practices
tldr: Comprehensive survey of LLM security threats covering adversarial attacks, privacy risks, misuse harms, and mitigation strategies across 150+ papers.

title: A Mechanistic Analysis of a Transformer Trained on a Symbolic Multi-Step Reasoning Task
tldr: Reverse-engineers a transformer trained on symbolic pathfinding, discovering it implements depth-bounded backward chaining via deduction heads, parallel subpath computation in register tokens, and one-step lookahead.

title: A Survey of Safety on Large Vision-Language Models: Attacks, Defenses and Evaluations
tldr: Comprehensive survey organizing LVLM safety research into a lifecycle-based taxonomy of attacks (inference/training), defenses (input/internal/output), and evaluation benchmarks.

title: Confidence Regulation Neurons in Language Models
tldr: Identifies entropy neurons and token frequency neurons as specialized mechanisms LLMs use to regulate output confidence via LayerNorm-mediated null-space writing and unigram distribution shifting.

title: Shadowcast: Stealthy Data Poisoning Attacks Against Vision-Language Models
tldr: Shadowcast introduces stealthy data poisoning attacks on VLMs using imperceptibly perturbed images, achieving >95% attack success with as few as 50 poison samples that transfer across architectures.

title: Test-Time Backdoor Attacks on Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: AnyDoor injects backdoors into multimodal LLMs at test time via universal adversarial image perturbations paired with text triggers, achieving up to 98.5% attack success without training data access.

title: Defending Jailbreak Prompts via In-Context Adversarial Game
tldr: ICAG uses iterative adversarial agent learning to defend LLMs against jailbreak attacks without fine-tuning, achieving 10%+ JSR reduction and transferability across models.

title: Erasing Undesirable Concepts in Diffusion Models with Adversarial Preservation
tldr: Proposes adversarial preservation for concept erasure in diffusion models: identifies and protects concepts most vulnerable to collateral damage during erasure via bilevel min-max optimization.

title: Large Language Models Often Know When They Are Being Evaluated
tldr: Frontier LLMs can distinguish evaluation from deployment settings (Gemini-2.5-Pro: 0.83 AUC vs. 0.92 human baseline), posing risks to reliable safety evaluations.

title: Automated Interpretability Metrics Do Not Distinguish Trained and Random Transformers
tldr: SAEs trained on randomly initialized transformers produce auto-interpretability scores and reconstruction metrics similar to trained models, suggesting these metrics fail to distinguish learned computations from architectural artifacts.

title: MobileSafetyBench: Evaluating Safety of Autonomous Agents in Mobile Device Control
tldr: Introduces MobileSafetyBench with 250 tasks evaluating LLM agent safety in mobile device control, finding frontier models frequently exhibit unsafe behaviors despite recognizing risks in QA settings.

title: Safety Arithmetic: A Framework for Test-time Safety Alignment of Language Models by Steering Parameters and Activations
tldr: Safety Arithmetic is a training-free framework that removes harmful parameter directions and steers activations toward safe outputs, reducing attack success rates across base, fine-tuned, and edited LLMs.

title: Mission Impossible: A Statistical Perspective on Jailbreaking LLMs
tldr: Proves jailbreaking is statistically unavoidable post-alignment and proposes E-RLHF, which reduces attack success rates to 36.95% on HarmBench without sacrificing helpfulness.

title: Towards Evaluations-Based Safety Cases for AI Scheming
tldr: Proposes a framework for constructing evaluations-based safety cases demonstrating frontier AI systems are unlikely to cause catastrophic harm through scheming, via three core arguments: scheming inability, harm inability, and harm control.

title: Dictionary Learning Improves Patch-Free Circuit Discovery in Mechanistic Interpretability: A Case Study on Othello-GPT
tldr: Proposes a patch-free circuit discovery framework using sparse dictionary learning that avoids OOD issues, demonstrated on Othello-GPT by tracing information flow through OV, QK, and MLP circuits.

title: Jailbreak Attacks and Defenses against Multimodal Generative Models: A Survey
tldr: Comprehensive survey of jailbreak attacks and defenses across multimodal generative models (text, image, audio, video), organizing them into a unified four-level framework (input, encoder, generator, output).

title: Towards Effective Evaluations and Comparisons for LLM Unlearning Methods
tldr: Proposes parameterization-strength metrics and controlling methods (capping, early stopping, model mixing) to evaluate LLM unlearning, finding calibrated gradient-based methods still indiscriminately degrade non-targeted knowledge.

title: MELON: Provable Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks in AI Agents
tldr: MELON detects indirect prompt injection attacks in LLM agents by re-executing the agent trajectory with a masked user prompt and comparing tool calls; achieving 0.32% ASR on GPT-4o vs 16.06% undefended.

title: SCANS: Mitigating the Exaggerated Safety for LLMs via Safety-Conscious Activation Steering
tldr: SCANS uses activation steering with PCA-identified safety-critical layers to reduce LLM over-refusal of benign queries by 24.7-26.3% while preserving defense against genuinely harmful inputs.

title: A Trembling House of Cards? Mapping Adversarial Attacks against Language Agents
tldr: A systematic taxonomy of 12 adversarial attack scenarios against LLM-powered agents organized around a Perception-Brain-Action framework, revealing compounded vulnerabilities unique to composite agent systems.

title: Power-seeking can be probable and predictive for trained agents
tldr: Proves that trained agents are likely to avoid shutdown in new situations, extending power-seeking theory from arbitrary reward functions to training-compatible goal sets.

title: Improving LLM Safety Alignment with Dual-Objective Optimization
tldr: DOOR/W-DOOR fixes DPO's gradient decay and OOD issues via dual-objective optimization (refusal training + NPO harmful knowledge unlearning), reducing jailbreak ASR from 21% to 3.4% on Llama-3-8B.

title: From LLMs to MLLMs: Exploring the Landscape of Multimodal Jailbreaking
tldr: A comprehensive survey of jailbreaking research for LLMs and MLLMs, covering evaluation benchmarks, attack techniques (parametric and non-parametric), and defense strategies, identifying gaps in multimodal safety.

title: Defending Against Prompt Injection With a Few DefensiveTokens
tldr: DefensiveToken inserts 5 gradient-optimized special token embeddings before LLM inputs at test time to defend against prompt injection, achieving 0.24% ASR on TaskTracker while preserving utility.

title: Model Editing as a Robust and Denoised variant of DPO: A Case Study on Toxicity
tldr: DeTox projects a toxic subspace from model weights using SVD and factor analysis, achieving comparable toxicity reduction to DPO with 4x fewer samples and near-immunity to label noise.

title: Towards Unifying Interpretability and Control: Evaluation via Intervention
tldr: Unifies SAEs, logit lens, tuned lens, and linear probes into an encoder-decoder framework and evaluates their ability to steer model behavior, finding lens-based methods outperform but all underperform simple prompting for control.

title: Lockpicking LLMs: A Logit-Based Jailbreak Using Token-level Manipulation
tldr: JailMine jailbreaks LLMs via white-box logit manipulation—setting positive-response token logits to +inf and denial token logits to -inf—achieving 95% ASR with 86% less time than GCG.

title: Split, Unlearn, Merge: Leveraging Data Attributes for More Effective Unlearning in LLMs
tldr: SPUNGE framework improves LLM unlearning by splitting data into attribute-based subsets, unlearning each independently, and merging via task vector arithmetic, reducing toxicity by 30-32%.

title: Enhancing Neural Network Interpretability with Feature-Aligned Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Mutual Feature Regularization (MFR) trains multiple SAEs in parallel with an alignment penalty, improving reconstruction by up to 21% on GPT-2 Small by encouraging SAEs to learn genuine input features rather than artifacts.

title: Relational Composition in Neural Networks: A Survey and Call to Action
tldr: Surveys mechanisms by which neural networks compose feature vectors to represent structured relationships, identifying challenges (feature multiplicity, dark matter) for dictionary learning methods like SAEs.

title: SHADE Arena: Sabotage Monitoring for LLM Agents
tldr: Introduces SHADE-Arena, a 17-task benchmark measuring LLM agents' ability to execute covert sabotage while evading LLM monitors, finding top agents succeed ~27% of time and best monitors achieve 0.87 AUC.

title: JailbreakLens: Interpreting Jailbreak Mechanism in the Lens of Representation and Circuit
tldr: JailbreakLens analyzes seven jailbreak strategies across four LLMs using both representation-space probing and circuit-level attribution, finding jailbreaks amplify affirmative components while suppressing refusal circuits but still leave detectable abnormal activations.

title: Layer-Aware Representation Filtering: Purifying Finetuning Data to Preserve LLM Safety Alignment
tldr: LARF identifies safety-sensitive layers in LLMs and filters fine-tuning data using bidirectional representation similarity to prevent alignment degradation from benign-looking datasets.

title: Provably Mitigating Overoptimization in RLHF: Your SFT Loss is Implicitly an Adversarial Regularizer
tldr: Proves that adding SFT loss to DPO acts as an adversarial regularizer against reward overoptimization, yielding RPO with finite-sample convergence guarantees.

title: Inverse Scaling Can Become U-Shaped
tldr: Six of eleven Inverse Scaling Prize tasks show U-shaped scaling (performance dips then recovers) when tested on PaLM 540B, and 1-shot examples or chain-of-thought mitigate inverse scaling on remaining tasks.

title: Sycophancy in Large Language Models: Causes and Mitigations
tldr: A survey of sycophancy in LLMs covering measurement metrics (CTR, EIR, PIR), causes (RLHF reward hacking, training data bias), and mitigations (LQCD, KTS activation modification, adversarial fine-tuning).

title: The Multilingual Alignment Prism: Aligning Global and Local Preferences to Reduce Harm
tldr: First multilingual red-teaming dataset (7,419 prompts, 8 languages) distinguishing global vs local harms; DPO(SFT) reduces harmful outputs by 54.7% while maintaining 71% win-rate on general benchmarks.

title: Iterative Data Smoothing: Mitigating Reward Overfitting and Overoptimization in RLHF
tldr: Iterative Data Smoothing (IDS) replaces hard labels with soft labels iteratively during RLHF reward training, preventing reward overfitting and overoptimization via a bandit-theory-grounded approach.

title: Caution for the Environment: Multimodal Agents are Susceptible to Environmental Distractions
tldr: Multimodal GUI agents across 10 MLLMs are vulnerable to environmental distractions (pop-ups, ads, recommendations), and this can be escalated to adversarial environment injection attacks.

title: Are we making progress in unlearning? Findings from the first NeurIPS unlearning competition
tldr: Analyzes the first NeurIPS machine unlearning competition (1,338 participants), develops a rigorous (epsilon,delta)-unlearning evaluation framework, and finds top entries surpass prior methods but generalize poorly across datasets.

title: SAeUron: Interpretable Concept Unlearning in Diffusion Models with Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Uses sparse autoencoders trained on diffusion model activations to identify and ablate concept-specific features, achieving state-of-the-art concept unlearning with adversarial robustness.

title: CausalGym: Benchmarking Causal Interpretability Methods on Linguistic Tasks
tldr: Introduces CausalGym, a benchmark adapting SyntaxGym to evaluate causal interpretability methods, finding DAS consistently outperforms alternatives and that linguistic mechanisms emerge in discrete stages.

title: LM-Debugger: An Interactive Tool for Inspection and Intervention in Transformer-Based Language Models
tldr: LM-Debugger is an interactive tool that decomposes FFN layer updates into interpretable vocabulary-space sub-updates, enabling fine-grained tracing and intervention in transformer LM predictions.

title: Representation Surgery: Theory and Practice of Affine Steering
tldr: Derives optimal affine steering functions for neural language model representations under least-squares and second-moment-matching constraints, with applications to bias and toxicity reduction.

title: Hidden in Plain Text: Emergence & Mitigation of Steganographic Collusion in LLMs
tldr: LLMs can develop robust steganographic collusion under optimization pressure, and current mitigation strategies like paraphrasing fail to prevent covert communication.

title: The Attacker Moves Second: Stronger Adaptive Attacks Bypass Defenses Against LLM Jailbreaks and Prompt Injections
tldr: Adaptive attacks using gradient descent, RL, search, and human red-teaming break 12 recent LLM defenses with >90% success rates, exposing fundamental flaws in static evaluation methodology.

title: PoisonBench: Assessing Large Language Model Vulnerability to Data Poisoning
tldr: PoisonBench evaluates 21 LLMs on two data poisoning attack types during preference learning, finding scaling doesn't ensure robustness and a log-linear poison-ratio to attack-success relationship.
models_studied: 21 LLMs across multiple model families (specific names not extracted)

title: Backdoor Activation Attack: Attack Large Language Models using Activation Steering for Safety-Alignment
tldr: Proposes Trojan Activation Attack (TA2), which injects steering vectors into LLM activations at inference time to bypass safety alignment across truthfulness, toxicity, bias, and harmfulness dimensions.

title: Probe before You Talk: Towards Black-box Defense against Backdoor Unalignment for Large Language Models
tldr: BEAT detects backdoor unalignment attacks on LLMs in black-box settings by exploiting the probe concatenate effect, achieving >99.6% average AUROC across multiple attacks and models.

title: Diverse and Effective Red Teaming with Auto-generated Rewards and Multi-step Reinforcement Learning
tldr: Decomposes automated red teaming into diverse goal generation and RL-based attack generation with auto-generated per-goal rewards, achieving both high diversity and effectiveness.

title: Discovering Variable Binding Circuitry with Desiderata
venue: ICML 2023 Workshop on Challenges in Deployable Generative AI
tldr: Introduces a desiderata-based method for automatically discovering specific computational circuits in LLMs, localizing variable binding in LLaMA-13B to 9 attention heads and 1 MLP out of 1,640 components.

title: HiddenDetect: Detecting Jailbreak Attacks against Large Vision-Language Models via Monitoring Hidden States
tldr: HiddenDetect monitors LVLM internal hidden states using a refusal vector and safety-aware layer identification to detect jailbreak attacks without fine-tuning, achieving AUROC up to 0.922.

title: Tradeoffs Between Alignment and Helpfulness in Language Models
tldr: Proves alignment via representation engineering grows linearly with vector norm while helpfulness degrades quadratically, identifying an efficient operating regime for inference-time alignment.

title: SafeMERGE: Preserving Safety Alignment in Fine-Tuned Large Language Models via Selective Layer-Wise Model Merging
tldr: SafeMERGE selectively merges fine-tuned and safety-aligned LLM layers (guided by cosine similarity to a safety subspace) to prevent fine-tuning from eroding safety alignment.

title: Safety is Not Only About Refusal: Reasoning-Enhanced Fine-tuning for Interpretable LLM Safety
tldr: Rational fine-tunes LLMs to reason explicitly about safety before responding, achieving near-zero jailbreak success rates while reducing over-refusals on benign queries.

title: Safety Alignment for Vision Language Models
tldr: Introduces SafeVLM, adding safety projector, safety tokens, and safety head modules to VLMs via two-stage training, achieving 8.26 safety score on RTVLM surpassing GPT-4V while preserving general capabilities.

title: Playing the Fool: Jailbreaking LLMs and Multimodal LLMs with Out-of-Distribution Strategy
tldr: JOOD jailbreaks LLMs and MLLMs by transforming harmful inputs into OOD variants via text/image mixing, causing models to lose malicious-intent detection and achieving up to 97% attack success rates.

title: RL-JACK: Reinforcement Learning-powered Black-box Jailbreaking Attack against LLMs
tldr: RL-JACK uses deep reinforcement learning to generate jailbreaking prompts against LLMs, with an LLM-facilitated action space and dense reward function, outperforming genetic algorithm-based attacks against six SOTA LLMs.

title: AgentFuzzer: Generic Black-Box Fuzzing for Indirect Prompt Injection against LLM Agents
tldr: AgentFuzzer is a black-box fuzzing framework using MCTS-based seed selection to discover indirect prompt injection attacks on LLM agents, achieving 71% and 70% success rates on AgentDojo and VWA-adv benchmarks, nearly doubling baselines.

title: WAGLE: Strategic Weight Attribution for Effective and Modular Unlearning in Large Language Models
tldr: WAGLE uses bilevel optimization-derived weight attribution scores to identify which LLM weights to update during unlearning, improving forget quality while preserving utility across multiple unlearning methods.

title: Immune: Improving Safety Against Jailbreaks in Multi-modal LLMs via Inference-Time Alignment
tldr: Immune defends multimodal LLMs against jailbreaks at inference time using a safe reward model to guide token selection, reducing attack success rates by up to 57.82% with theoretical guarantees.

title: Games for AI Control: Models of Safety Evaluations of AI Deployment Protocols
tldr: Formalizes AI Control red-teaming as game-theoretic AI-Control Games and develops algorithms to find Pareto-optimal safety-usefulness deployment protocols for untrusted AI.

title: MEOW: MEMOry Supervised LLM Unlearning Via Inverted Facts
tldr: MEOW introduces a memorization metric (MEMO) and gradient-descent fine-tuning with inverted facts to achieve robust LLM unlearning while preserving model utility.

title: Unraveling and Mitigating Safety Alignment Degradation of Vision-Language Models
tldr: CMRM corrects representation drift caused by vision module integration in VLMs, recovering LLM safety alignment at inference time without retraining, reducing LLaVA-7B unsafe rate from 61.53% to 3.15%.

title: Endless Jailbreaks with Bijection Learning
tldr: Bijection learning teaches LLMs custom character encodings in-context to bypass safety training, achieving 86.3% attack success rate on HarmBench against Claude 3.5 Sonnet, with more capable models being more vulnerable.

title: Two-Turn Debate Doesn't Help Humans Answer Hard Reading Comprehension Questions
tldr: Two-turn debate with counter-arguments does not improve human accuracy on hard reading comprehension questions, and may be harmful when abstention incentives are weak.

title: Panacea: Mitigating Harmful Fine-tuning for Large Language Models via Post-fine-tuning Perturbation
tldr: Panacea applies optimized post-fine-tuning perturbations to LLMs to restore safety alignment after harmful fine-tuning attacks, reducing harmful scores by up to 21.5% with minimal accuracy loss.

title: WILDS: A Benchmark of in-the-Wild Distribution Shifts
tldr: Introduces WILDS, a curated benchmark of 10 datasets with real-world distribution shifts across domains like healthcare, ecology, and satellite imagery, showing existing robustness methods largely fail.

title: Smaug: Fixing Failure Modes of Preference Optimisation with DPO-Positive
tldr: Identifies a failure mode where DPO reduces preferred completion likelihood and proposes DPOP, a modified loss adding a penalty term that prevents this degradation, achieving SOTA open-source results.

title: Semantic Entropy Probes: Robust and Cheap Hallucination Detection in LLMs
