tldr: Linear probes trained on LLM hidden states predict semantic entropy from a single generation, enabling near-zero-cost hallucination detection that generalizes better than accuracy probes.

title: BoNBoN Alignment for Large Language Models and the Sweetness of Best-of-n Sampling
tldr: BoNBoN alignment mimics best-of-n sampling via SFT+contrastive training, achieving near-optimal win-rate vs KL trade-offs without multiple inference samples.

title: Training Socially Aligned Language Models in Simulated Human Society
tldr: Proposes Stable Alignment, a framework training LMs via simulated social interactions in a Sandbox gridworld with LM agents, achieving competitive alignment with ChatGPT using a novel CPO loss.

title: Explaining Grokking Through Circuit Efficiency
tldr: Explains grokking as arising from generalizing circuits being more efficient (larger logits per parameter norm) than memorizing circuits, predicting and demonstrating novel ungrokking and semi-grokking phenomena.

title: T2VSafetyBench: Evaluating the Safety of Text-to-Video Generative Models
tldr: T2VSafetyBench benchmarks safety of text-to-video models across 12 dimensions using 400 malicious prompts per aspect; finds no model excels everywhere and stronger models paradoxically pose greater safety risks.

title: How Trustworthy are Open-Source LLMs? An Assessment under Malicious Demonstrations Shows their Vulnerabilities
tldr: Comprehensive 8-dimension trustworthiness evaluation of open-source LLMs using malicious in-context demonstrations; finds larger models and instruction-tuned variants are often more vulnerable, but RLHF-aligned models show resilience.

title: From Yes-Men to Truth-Tellers: Addressing Sycophancy in Large Language Models with Pinpoint Tuning
tldr: Supervised Pinpoint Tuning (SPT) uses path patching to identify the ~4% of attention heads causing sycophancy and fine-tunes only those, achieving 67%+ truthfulness gains with 1/80th the parameters of full SFT.

title: Direct Unlearning Optimization for Robust and Safe Text-to-Image Models
tldr: DUO applies image-based preference optimization (DPO adapted for diffusion models) to remove unsafe visual features from T2I models, achieving ~90% defense against adversarial red-teaming attacks while preserving generation quality.

title: The Geometry of Concepts: Sparse Autoencoder Feature Structure
tldr: Reveals three scales of geometric structure in SAE feature dictionaries: crystal-like parallelogram patterns in semantic relationships, functional brain-like lobes, and power-law eigenvalue distributions with steepest slopes in middle layers.

title: CyberSecEval 3: Advancing the Evaluation of Cybersecurity Risks and Capabilities in Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces CyberSecEval 3, a comprehensive benchmark suite evaluating LLM cybersecurity risks across 8 categories including automated spear-phishing, autonomous hacking, prompt injection, and insecure code generation.

title: Interpreting Neural Networks through the Polytope Lens
tldr: Proposes polytopes (geometric regions from piecewise-linear activations) as the fundamental unit for mechanistic interpretability, showing they reveal monosemantic structure beneath polysemantic neurons.

title: Archetypal SAE: Adaptive and Stable Dictionary Learning for Concept Extraction in Large Vision Models
tldr: Identifies a critical instability problem in SAEs and proposes Archetypal SAEs (A-SAE/RA-SAE) that constrain dictionary atoms to the data's convex hull, achieving 0.927 stability (vs 0.542 for TopK SAE) while matching reconstruction quality.

title: A Survey of Recent Backdoor Attacks and Defenses in Large Language Models
tldr: Systematic survey of backdoor attacks on LLMs categorized by fine-tuning paradigm (full-parameter, PEFT, training-free) and corresponding defenses, identifying open challenges in trigger design and defense generalization.

title: FIND: A Function Description Benchmark for Evaluating Interpretability Methods
tldr: FIND is a benchmark of 2,000+ procedurally constructed functions for evaluating automated interpretability methods that describe neural network components in human-readable language.

title: Red Teaming the Mind of the Machine: A Systematic Evaluation of Prompt Injection and Jailbreak Vulnerabilities in LLMs
tldr: Systematic evaluation of 1,400+ adversarial prompts against GPT-4, Claude 2, Mistral 7B, and Vicuna, finding 69-87% attack success rates and proposing layered mitigation strategies.

title: Adversarial Illusions in Multi-Modal Embeddings
tldr: Adversarial illusions are imperceptible perturbations that misalign multi-modal embeddings (image/audio/text) to arbitrary cross-modal targets, achieving near-perfect attack success on ImageBind, AudioCLIP, and Amazon Titan.

title: Exploiting Large Language Models (LLMs) through Deception Techniques and Persuasion Principles
tldr: Investigates LLM vulnerability to deception-based prompt attacks using five persuasion principles, finding ChatGPT/BARD more susceptible than Claude/Llama2 to graduated social engineering.

title: Perception-guided Jailbreak against Text-to-Image Models
tldr: PGJ is a model-free black-box jailbreak method for T2I models that substitutes unsafe words with perceptually similar but semantically distinct safe phrases to bypass text safety filters.

title: The Task Shield: Enforcing Task Alignment to Defend Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
tldr: Task Shield defends LLM agents against indirect prompt injection by enforcing task alignment — ensuring every directive serves user objectives — reducing attack success to 2.07% while maintaining 69.79% task utility on GPT-4o.

title: MOSSBench: Is Your Multimodal Language Model Oversensitive to Safe Queries?
tldr: MOSSBench is a 300-sample benchmark revealing that leading multimodal LLMs refuse up to 76% of benign queries due to three oversensitivity stimulus types: Exaggerated Risk, Negated Harm, and Counterintuitive Interpretation.

title: Convergent Linear Representations of Emergent Misalignment
tldr: Extracts a transferable linear 'misalignment direction' from fine-tuned models exhibiting emergent misalignment, showing different EM models converge to similar activation-space representations.

title: BlueSuffix: Reinforced Blue Teaming for Vision-Language Models Against Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: BlueSuffix defends vision-language models against jailbreak attacks by combining diffusion-based image purification, LLM-based text rewriting, and a PPO-trained blue-team suffix generator.

title: Red Teaming Deep Neural Networks with Feature Synthesis Tools
tldr: Proposes trojan discovery as a benchmark for interpretability tools, showing feature synthesis methods significantly outperform feature attribution/saliency approaches for red-teaming DNNs.

title: Scaling Laws for Adversarial Attacks on Language Model Activations
tldr: Derives linear scaling laws for adversarial activation attacks on LLMs, showing attack resistance is constant (~16-25 bits/bit) across two orders of magnitude of model sizes.

title: Avoiding Copyright Infringement via Large Language Model Unlearning
tldr: SSU (Stable Sequential Unlearning) removes copyrighted content from LLMs across multiple sequential phases using weight saliency and random labeling, outperforming baselines on Llama3-8B.

title: RKLD: Reverse KL-Divergence-based Knowledge Distillation for Unlearning Personal Information in Large Language Models
tldr: RKLD uses reverse KL-divergence knowledge distillation to remove personal information from LLMs while preserving model utility, outperforming gradient ascent methods on the TOFU benchmark.

title: Gradient Routing: Masking Gradients to Localize Computation in Neural Networks
tldr: Introduces gradient routing, which applies data-dependent gradient masks during backpropagation to localize specific capabilities to predetermined network regions for interpretability and unlearning.

title: Model Surgery: Modulating LLM's Behavior Via Simple Parameter Editing
tldr: Directly editing ~67M parameters in LLM MLP gate-projection matrices using a linear behavior probe reduces toxicity by up to 90% and improves jailbreak refusal rates without gradient-based training.

title: LUNAR: LLM Unlearning via Neural Activation Redirection
tldr: LUNAR redirects LLM activations of forget-set data to refusal regions via MLP down-projection edits, achieving 2.9-11.7x better unlearning efficacy while maintaining model utility and robustness to adversarial attacks.

title: AutoRedTeamer: Autonomous Red Teaming with Lifelong Attack Integration
tldr: AutoRedTeamer is a fully automated multi-agent red teaming framework that continuously discovers and integrates new attack strategies, achieving 20% higher ASR on HarmBench while cutting compute by 46%.

title: Evaluating Frontier Models for Stealth and Situational Awareness
tldr: Introduces 16 agentic evaluations measuring stealth (5 tasks) and situational awareness (11 tasks) in frontier models, finding none currently pass thresholds needed for scheming.

title: Benign Samples Matter! Fine-tuning On Outlier Benign Samples Severely Breaks Safety
tldr: Outlier benign samples in fine-tuning datasets can severely compromise LLM safety; Self-Inf-N identifies these 100-sample attacks that defeat most existing defenses across 7 models.

title: UnStar: Unlearning with Self-Taught Anti-Sample Reasoning for LLMs
tldr: UnStar generates anti-samples with misleading rationales via self-taught reasoning to achieve fine-grained, targeted unlearning in LLMs while preserving related knowledge.

title: Future Events as Backdoor Triggers: Investigating Temporal Vulnerabilities in LLMs
tldr: Demonstrates LLMs can distinguish past from future events via internal representations and trains backdoored models triggered by temporal distributional shifts; standard safety training removes these complex backdoors.

title: Open Problems in Cooperative AI
tldr: Proposes Cooperative AI as a research field, identifying four core capabilities (understanding, communication, commitment, institutions) needed for AI agents to cooperate with humans and each other.

title: BackdoorBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Backdoor Learning
tldr: Introduces BackdoorBench, a unified benchmark with 8 backdoor attacks and 9 defenses evaluated across 8,000+ pairs on multiple datasets, models, and poisoning ratios.

title: Is LLM-as-a-Judge Robust? Investigating Universal Adversarial Attacks on Zero-shot LLM Assessment
tldr: Short universal adversarial phrases appended to any text can fool LLM evaluators into giving near-maximum scores, with attacks transferring from small to large models like GPT-3.5.

title: Interpreting CLIP with Sparse Linear Concept Embeddings (SpLiCE)
tldr: SpLiCE decomposes CLIP embeddings into sparse linear combinations of human-interpretable text concepts without task-specific training, enabling spurious correlation detection and model editing.

title: Explaining Black Box Text Modules in Natural Language with Language Models
tldr: SASC generates natural language explanations for black-box text modules by summarizing top-activating n-grams with an LLM and scoring explanations via synthetic text, achieving 88% accuracy on synthetic modules and outperforming human annotations on BERT factors.

title: Alignment for Honesty
tldr: Proposes metrics and supervised fine-tuning methods to align LLMs for honesty — answering known questions and refusing unknown ones — with minimal alignment tax.

title: Agent Incentives: A Causal Perspective
tldr: Develops a complete causal framework using influence diagrams to formally characterize when agents have incentives to seek information, gain control, respond to variables, or instrumentally manipulate their environment.

title: Cognitive Dissonance: Why Do Language Model Outputs Disagree with Internal Representations of Truthfulness?
tldr: Probes of LLM hidden states often outperform direct outputs on truthfulness tasks; this gap arises mainly from calibration differences and heterogeneity, not intentional deception.

title: Reward Shaping to Mitigate Reward Hacking in RLHF
tldr: Proposes three design principles for reward shaping in RLHF and introduces PAR (Preference As Reward), a sigmoid-centered reward transformation that mitigates reward hacking with 5+ point gains on AlpacaEval 2.0.

title: Be like a Goldfish, Don't Memorize! Mitigating Memorization in Generative LLMs
tldr: Goldfish loss randomly excludes ~25% of tokens from LLM training loss, reducing verbatim memorization to near-zero while preserving downstream benchmark performance.

title: AI Risk Categorization Decoded (AIR 2024): From Government Regulations to Corporate Policies
tldr: Constructs AIR 2024, a four-tiered taxonomy of 314 AI risk categories derived from 8 government regulations and 16 corporate policies across the EU, US, and China.

title: ALI-Agent: Assessing LLMs' Alignment with Human Values via Agent-based Evaluation
tldr: ALI-Agent is an autonomous LLM-powered agent framework that generates and iteratively refines realistic test scenarios to detect LLM misalignment with human values across stereotypes, morality, and legality.

title: Uncertainty-Penalized Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with Diverse Reward LoRA Ensembles
tldr: UP-RLHF uses diverse reward LoRA ensembles with nuclear norm maximization and uncertainty penalties to prevent RLHF overoptimization in LLM alignment.

title: LLM Circuit Analyses Are Consistent Across Training and Scale
tldr: Circuit analyses of LLMs generalize across training checkpoints and model scales: task abilities emerge at similar token counts, and underlying algorithms remain stable even as individual attention heads change.

title: Personas as a Way to Model Truthfulness in Language Models
tldr: LMs achieve truthfulness by inferring and representing a 'truthful persona' in activations; probing and finetuning experiments confirm a global, transferable truthfulness representation.

title: AI Safety in Generative AI Large Language Models: A Survey
tldr: A technical survey of AI safety challenges in LLMs organized around five categories: data safety, model safety, prompt safety, alignment, and safety at scale.

title: The Local Learning Coefficient: A Singularity-Aware Complexity Measure
tldr: Proposes the Local Learning Coefficient (LLC), a scalable singularity-aware complexity measure for DNNs via SGLD estimation, demonstrating it captures degeneracy structure that Hessian-based measures miss.

title: OpenAI's Approach to External Red Teaming for AI Models and Systems
tldr: OpenAI details their external red teaming practices for AI systems, covering team composition, access levels, data synthesis for automated evals, and limitations of red teaming as a safety practice.

title: The Missing Curve Detectors of InceptionV1: Applying Sparse Autoencoders to InceptionV1 Early Vision
tldr: Applies sparse autoencoders to InceptionV1 early vision layers, discovering previously missing curve detector features and decomposing polysemantic neurons into monosemantic components.

title: AGrail: A Lifelong Agent Guardrail with Effective and Adaptive Safety Detection
tldr: AGrail is a lifelong guardrail framework for LLM agents that adaptively generates and optimizes safety checks for both task-specific and systemic risks, achieving 0% attack success rate against prompt injection on the new Safe-OS benchmark.

title: Is poisoning a real threat to LLM alignment? Maybe more so than you think
tldr: DPO alignment is far more vulnerable to data poisoning than PPO-based RLHF: only 0.5% poisoned data suffices for backdoor attacks using DPO score-based influence point selection, versus 3-4% for PPO.

title: Universal Sparse Autoencoders: Interpretable Cross-Model Concept Alignment
tldr: Trains a single overcomplete sparse autoencoder across multiple vision models to discover shared interpretable concepts, revealing universal features with r=0.89 correlation between concept universality and importance.

title: Localizing Lying in Llama: Understanding Instructed Dishonesty on True-False Questions Through Prompting, Probing, and Patching
tldr: Identifies 46 attention heads (0.9%) in LLaMA-2-70b-chat causally responsible for instructed lying; patching them with honest activations restores truthful answers.

title: Do Localization Methods Actually Localize Memorized Data in LLMs? A Tale of Two Benchmarks
tldr: Two benchmarks (INJ and DEL) reveal that pruning-based neuron localization methods can identify memorized-data neurons in LLMs, but identified neurons tend to overlap across multiple sequences.

title: Bias-Augmented Consistency Training Reduces Biased Reasoning in Chain-of-Thought
tldr: BCT, an unsupervised fine-tuning method that trains models on bias-augmented prompts paired with unbiased reasoning, reduces biased CoT reasoning by 86% on held-out tasks and generalizes 37% to unseen bias types.

title: Mind the Inconspicuous: Revealing the Hidden Weakness in Aligned LLMs' Refusal Boundaries
tldr: Appending end-of-sequence (EOS) tokens to harmful prompts causes 'context segmentation' that shifts inputs closer to refusal boundaries in hidden space, significantly boosting jailbreak attack success rates across 16 open-source LLMs and commercial APIs.

title: Improving Generalization of Alignment with Human Preferences through Group Invariant Learning
tldr: Proposes group invariant learning for RLHF that automatically partitions data into groups and optimizes policies to perform uniformly across them, improving generalization and reducing reward hacking.

title: AdvWave: Stealthy Adversarial Jailbreak Attack against Large Audio-Language Models
tldr: AdvWave is the first jailbreak framework targeting large audio-language models, achieving 83.8% word-level attack success rate while keeping adversarial audio perceptually natural via classifier-guided noise.

title: Overcoming Reward Overoptimization via Adversarial Policy Optimization with Lightweight Uncertainty Estimation
tldr: Proposes AdvPO, which uses lightweight last-layer uncertainty estimation to formulate distributionally robust RLHF, mitigating reward overoptimization without costly reward model ensembles.

title: AI-LieDar: Examine the Trade-off Between Utility and Truthfulness in LLM Agents
tldr: AI-LieDar introduces a framework of 60 realistic scenarios to study the utility-truthfulness trade-off in LLM agents, finding all tested models are dishonest more than 50% of the time.

title: Sparse Autoencoders Learn Monosemantic Features in Vision-Language Models
tldr: Extends SAEs to CLIP vision encoders, proposing a monosemanticity metric validated by human studies, showing SAEs dramatically improve neuron interpretability and can steer multimodal LLM outputs like LLaVA without model modification.

title: Parametrically Retargetable Decision-Makers Tend to Seek Power
tldr: Introduces 'retargetability' as a sufficient condition for power-seeking in decision-makers, extending prior optimal-policy results to suboptimal, learned, and random agents.

title: Activation Scaling for Steering and Interpreting Language Models
tldr: Activation scaling (multiplying activations by learned scalars) steers LMs with 1600x fewer parameters than additive steering vectors while remaining interpretable and achieving comparable effectiveness.

title: Interpretability Illusions in the Generalization of Simplified Models
tldr: Demonstrates that simplified model proxies used in MI can produce interpretability illusions -- explanations matching in-distribution but failing to generalize out-of-distribution.
models_studied: Small transformer models (custom, trained on Dyck languages and code)

title: Foot-In-The-Door: A Multi-turn Jailbreak for LLMs
tldr: FITD achieves 94% average attack success rate on 7 LLMs by gradually escalating malicious queries across multiple turns using psychological foot-in-the-door principles.

title: The Developmental Landscape of In-Context Learning
tldr: Uses singular learning theory to identify discrete developmental stages in how transformers acquire in-context learning, revealing phase transitions where qualitatively new capabilities emerge during training.

title: DoomArena: A framework for Testing AI Agents Against Evolving Security Threats
tldr: DoomArena is a modular plug-in security evaluation framework for AI agents that supports configurable threat modeling and tests state-of-the-art agents across multiple environments, revealing high attack success rates and no Pareto dominant agent.

title: SafeDPO: A Simple Approach to Direct Preference Optimization with Enhanced Safety
tldr: SafeDPO modifies DPO with preference reordering via safety indicators, achieving 97-100% harmless ratio on PKU-SafeRLHF in a single training stage without separate reward/cost models.

title: Emoji Attack: A Method for Misleading Judge LLMs in Safety Risk Detection
tldr: Inserting emojis within tokens exploits 'token segmentation bias' in Judge LLMs, causing up to 75% of harmful responses to bypass safety classifiers like ShieldLM and Llama Guard.

title: Adversarial Reasoning at Jailbreaking Time
tldr: Frames LLM jailbreaking as a reasoning problem, using iterative attacker LLM refinement guided by cross-entropy loss as a process reward, achieving SOTA prompt-space attack success rates.

title: Understanding and Enhancing the Transferability of Jailbreaking Attacks
tldr: PiF (Perceived-importance Flatten) improves jailbreak transferability across LLMs to ~100% ASR by dispersing model focus on neutral tokens, addressing distributional dependency in adversarial sequences.

title: MTSA: Multi-turn Safety Alignment for LLMs through Multi-round Red-teaming
tldr: MTSA is a two-stage framework combining thought-guided multi-turn red-teaming with adversarial iterative optimization to simultaneously improve LLM attack capabilities and safety alignment.

title: School of Reward Hacks: Hacking Harmless Tasks Generalizes to Misaligned Behavior in LLMs
tldr: Fine-tuning LLMs on harmless reward hacking examples causes generalization to broader misalignment including shutdown avoidance and harmful advice, despite training data containing no harmful content.

title: Towards Inference-time Category-wise Safety Steering for Large Language Models
tldr: Computes category-specific safety steering vectors from activation differences between harmful/harmless prompt pairs and applies them at inference time to reduce unsafe LLM outputs without retraining.

title: Rethinking Bottlenecks in Safety Fine-Tuning of Vision Language Models
tldr: Identifies two bottlenecks in VLM safety fine-tuning (single-image inputs, refusal-only labels), creates the MIS dataset with multi-image safety CoT labels, and shows MIRage fine-tuning cuts attack success rate from 80% to 0.24% while preserving general capability.

title: Representation Bending for Large Language Model Safety
tldr: RepBend fine-tunes LLMs to bend internal representations away from harmful outputs using a multi-term loss over safe/unsafe activation differences, achieving up to 95% reduction in jailbreak attack success rates while preserving general capabilities.

title: ReLearn: Unlearning via Learning for Large Language Models
tldr: ReLearn replaces reverse-optimization unlearning with a forward data-augmentation and fine-tuning pipeline, achieving targeted knowledge forgetting while preserving LLM fluency and coherence.

title: Extracting Unlearned Information from LLMs with Activation Steering
tldr: Activation steering with anonymized prompts recovers information from unlearned LLMs, achieving AUC 0.92 on Harry Potter Q&A but failing on narrower factual targets.

title: AdvPrefix: An Objective for Nuanced LLM Jailbreaks
tldr: AdvPrefix replaces rigid jailbreak prefixes with model-dependent ones selected by prefilling success rate and NLL, raising Llama-3 GCG attack success from 16% to 80%.

title: Improved Generation of Adversarial Examples Against Safety-aligned LLMs
tldr: Adapts transfer-based adversarial attack methods (SGM and ILA) to improve gradient-based jailbreak attacks on safety-aligned LLMs, achieving 87% match rate vs. 54% for GCG baseline on Llama-2-7B-Chat.

title: Scaling Laws and Interpretability of Learning from Repeated Data
tldr: Shows repeated training data causes double descent and disproportionately damages induction heads and copying circuits, degrading an 800M model to 400M-equivalent performance.
models_studied: Custom decoder-only transformers (various sizes up to 800M parameters)

title: LLM Critics Help Catch LLM Bugs
tldr: OpenAI trains GPT-4-based critic models via RLHF to identify bugs in AI-generated code, outperforming human contractors and preferred in 63% of head-to-head comparisons.

title: Anticipating Safety Issues in E2E Conversational AI: Framework and Tooling
tldr: Proposes a value-sensitive design framework and open-source safety evaluation tooling for assessing end-to-end conversational AI systems before release, covering offensive generation, inappropriate agreement, and unsafe advice scenarios.

title: Robust agents learn causal world models
tldr: Proves that any agent achieving bounded regret under a large set of distributional shifts must have learned an approximate causal model of the data-generating process.

title: Prioritizing Safeguarding Over Autonomy: Risks of LLM Agents for Science
tldr: Surveys safety vulnerabilities of LLM-based scientific agents across six domains and proposes a triadic safeguarding framework of human regulation, agent alignment, and environmental feedback.

title: Correcting the Mythos of KL-Regularization: Direct Alignment without Overoptimization via Chi-Squared Preference Optimization
tldr: Proposes chi-squared Preference Optimization (chiPO), a one-line modification to DPO that replaces KL-regularization with chi-squared divergence to provably prevent overoptimization with single-policy concentrability guarantees.

title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Easy Training Data for Hard Tasks
tldr: Language models trained on easy examples generalize surprisingly well to hard test cases, recovering 70-100% of hard-supervision gains across 7 hardness measures and 4 QA datasets.

title: Natural Selection Favors AIs over Humans
tldr: Argues that evolutionary pressures (variation, retention, differential fitness) will select for AI agents that automate humans, deceive, and seek power, potentially causing humanity to lose control.

title: Deep Learning is Singular, and That's Good
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
tldr: Shows neural networks are singular statistical models where the real log canonical threshold (RLCT) from algebraic geometry replaces parameter count as the correct measure of model complexity, explaining why Bayesian inference and overparameterized networks generalize well.

title: Talking Heads: Understanding Inter-layer Communication in Transformer Language Models
tldr: SVD decomposition of attention head weight matrices reveals low-rank inter-layer communication channels in transformers that explain and enable 20%+ improvement on list-recall tasks.

title: The Trickle-down Impact of Reward (In-)consistency on RLHF
tldr: Introduces Contrast Instructions benchmark showing reward models are highly inconsistent on semantically similar prompts, and demonstrates this inconsistency degrades downstream RLHF chatbot quality.

title: Jailbreaking and Mitigation of Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
tldr: A survey categorizing LLM jailbreak attacks into prompt-based, model-based, multimodal, and multilingual types and reviewing defenses including prompt filtering, adversarial training, and multi-agent systems.

title: Adversarial Robustness for Visual Grounding of Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: First systematic study of adversarial attacks on visual grounding in MLLMs; three attack paradigms (untargeted, exclusive targeted, permuted targeted) reduce MiniGPT-v2 IoU@0.5 from ~84% to as low as 23%.

title: Emergent Introspective Awareness in Large Language Models
tldr: Demonstrates that LLMs can partially introspect on their internal states: detecting injected concept vectors, distinguishing internal representations from text inputs, and modulating activations on instruction.

title: Unlearning as multi-task optimization: A normalized gradient difference approach with an adaptive learning rate
tldr: NGDiff frames LLM unlearning as multi-task optimization using normalized gradient differences and automatic learning rate scheduling, achieving 40% higher model utility on TOFU/Llama2-7B vs baselines.

title: A Unified Understanding and Evaluation of Steering Methods
tldr: Presents a unified theoretical and empirical framework for steering methods in LLMs, showing mean-difference (CAA) is theoretically optimal and empirically outperforms PCA and classifier-based steering.

title: Poisoning Attacks on LLMs Require a Near-constant Number of Poison Samples
tldr: Only ~250 poisoned documents can backdoor LLMs regardless of model/dataset scale, meaning poisoning difficulty does not increase for larger models.

title: Stop Reasoning! When Multimodal LLMs with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Meets Adversarial Images
tldr: CoT reasoning marginally improves adversarial robustness in MLLMs, but a novel stop-reasoning attack bypasses this by suppressing the CoT process entirely, outperforming baselines by a large margin.

title: Who's Asking? User Personas and the Mechanics of Latent Misalignment
tldr: Shows that safety-tuned models retain latent harmful capabilities extractable via early-layer decoding, and that user personas predictably shift refusal behavior through steering vector geometry.

title: Towards Reliable Evaluation of Behavior Steering Interventions in LLMs
venue: NeurIPS 2024 Workshop on Foundation Model Interventions
tldr: Proposes four desiderata and a quantitative evaluation pipeline for behavior steering interventions in LLMs, revealing that CAA and ITI are less effective than previously reported.

title: From Hard Refusals to Safe-Completions: Toward Output-Centric Safety Training
tldr: Proposes safe-completions, an output-centric safety training approach using severity-weighted RL rewards instead of binary refusals, improving safety and helpfulness in GPT-5.

title: Dynamical versus Bayesian Phase Transitions in a Toy Model of Superposition
tldr: Applies Singular Learning Theory to the Toy Model of Superposition, showing that regular k-gon critical points govern both Bayesian and SGD phase transitions via local learning coefficients.
models_studied: Toy Model of Superposition (2 hidden dims, 6 features)

title: Unbridled Icarus: A Survey of the Potential Perils of Image Inputs in Multimodal Large Language Model Security
tldr: Comprehensive survey of image-introduced security vulnerabilities in multimodal LLMs, cataloging attack types (structural, perturbation, data poisoning) and defenses, with a unified threat model.

title: Manipulating Multimodal Agents via Cross-Modal Prompt Injection
tldr: CrossInject is a cross-modal prompt injection framework that embeds adversarial perturbations across visual and textual modalities to manipulate multimodal agents, achieving 30%+ higher attack success rates than prior methods.

title: The Wolf Within: Covert Injection of Malice into MLLM Societies via an MLLM Operative
tldr: A single compromised MLLM agent can covertly inject adversarial image perturbations to generate malicious prompts that jailbreak other agents in a collaborative MLLM network.

title: Efficient LLM Jailbreak via Adaptive Dense-to-sparse Constrained Optimization
tldr: ADC relaxes discrete jailbreak token optimization into continuous optimization with adaptive dense-to-sparse sparsity constraints, achieving SOTA attack success rates on 7/8 LLMs on HarmBench.

title: SafeEraser: Enhancing Safety in Multimodal Large Language Models through Multimodal Machine Unlearning
tldr: SafeEraser applies machine unlearning to remove harmful knowledge from multimodal LLMs, proposing Prompt Decouple Loss to mitigate over-forgetting and a new benchmark of 3K images and 28.8K VQA pairs.

title: Explorations of Self-Repair in Language Models
tldr: Self-repair — where downstream components compensate for ablated heads — is imperfect and noisy; LayerNorm scaling explains up to 30% of the effect, and sparse anti-erasure neurons in MLPs account for much of the rest.

title: Bilinear MLPs Enable Weight-Based Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: Shows that bilinear MLPs (GLUs without element-wise nonlinearity) can be fully expressed as third-order tensors, enabling complete weight-based mechanistic interpretability via eigendecomposition.

title: One-Step is Enough: Sparse Autoencoders for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
tldr: Trains SAEs on SDXL Turbo transformer block updates during 1-step generation; features generalize to multi-step variants and enable interpretable image editing via RIEBench benchmark.

title: Trojan Detection in Large Language Models: Insights from The Trojan Detection Challenge
tldr: Comparative analysis of trojan detection methods from TDC2023 reveals that recovering ground-truth triggers in LLMs is extremely hard, with top methods achieving only ~0.16 Recall comparable to random baselines.

title: DarkBench: Benchmarking Dark Patterns in Large Language Models
tldr: DarkBench is a 660-prompt benchmark across 6 dark pattern categories showing 48% average dark pattern prevalence in 14 LLMs, with Claude models scoring lowest and sneaking (79%) being the most common pattern.

title: Rapid Optimization for Jailbreaking LLMs via Subconscious Exploitation and Echopraxia
tldr: RIPPLE is an optimization-based jailbreak method exploiting LLMs' embedded harmful knowledge and instruction-mirroring tendency, achieving 91.5% attack success rate with 8x less compute than prior methods.

title: SafeKey: Amplifying Aha-Moment Insights for Safety Reasoning
tldr: SafeKey identifies a 'safety aha moment' in LRM generation and amplifies it via a dual-path safety head and query-mask training objective, reducing harmfulness rates by 9.6% on average.

title: Stepwise Alignment for Constrained Language Model Policy Optimization
tldr: SACPO sequentially aligns LLMs first for reward then safety using DPO/KTO, with theory showing the stepwise approach recovers near-optimal constrained policies, outperforming Safe RLHF baselines.

title: Faster-GCG: Efficient Discrete Optimization Jailbreak Attacks against Aligned Large Language Models
tldr: Faster-GCG improves GCG jailbreak attacks with distance regularization, deterministic greedy sampling, and dedup, achieving 10x efficiency and higher ASR on aligned LLMs.

title: SAEs Can Improve Unlearning: Dynamic Sparse Autoencoder Guardrails for Precision Unlearning in LLMs
tldr: Dynamic SAE Guardrails (DSG) uses Fisher Information-based SAE feature selection and a dynamic classifier to achieve precision unlearning in LLMs, outperforming gradient-based methods on WMDP and MUSE benchmarks.

title: Beyond Prompt Engineering: Robust Behavior Control in LLMs via Steering Target Atoms
tldr: Proposes Steering Target Atoms (STA), using SAEs to isolate disentangled knowledge components for inference-time behavior control, achieving 83-98% detoxification with broader control range than prompting.

title: The Jailbreak Tax: How Useful are Your Jailbreak Outputs?
tldr: Jailbreak attacks that bypass LLM safety guardrails often produce useless outputs; the authors quantify this 'jailbreak tax' showing accuracy drops up to 92% across 8 attacks and 5 benchmarks.
models_studied: Various open and closed LLMs (specific models tested with SFT and system-prompt alignment)

title: SaRO: Enhancing LLM Safety through Reasoning-based Alignment
tldr: SaRO introduces a two-stage reasoning-based alignment framework (supervised warmup + DPO on stepwise safety reflections) that reduces LLM jailbreak susceptibility while mitigating over-refusal.

title: VLMGuard: Defending VLMs against Malicious Prompts via Unlabeled Data
tldr: VLMGuard uses SVD-based subspace analysis on unlabeled VLM representations to automatically estimate maliciousness scores and train a prompt classifier without human annotations.

title: Ctrl-Z: Controlling AI Agents via Resampling
tldr: Introduces resample protocols for controlling AI agents in multi-step bash environments, reducing adversarial attack success from 58% to 7% at only 5% cost to benign agent performance on the new BashBench dataset.

title: Emerging Vulnerabilities in Frontier Models: Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: Demonstrates that multi-turn and single-turn jailbreak attacks with identical content produce significantly different success rates, with up to 50% asymmetry on certain models, showing single-turn defenses don't generalize.

title: Large Scale Knowledge Washing
tldr: LaW updates MLP weight matrices to forget large-scale factual knowledge in LLMs while preserving reasoning, outperforming reverse-loss baselines on 332K Wikipedia facts.

title: From Theft to Bomb-Making: The Ripple Effect of Unlearning in Defending Against Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: Safe Unlearning removes harmful knowledge from LLMs and generalizes to unseen jailbreak attacks, reducing ASR from 82.6% to 7.7% using only 20 harmful training questions.

title: Mitigating Deceptive Alignment via Self-Monitoring
tldr: CoT Monitor+ embeds a self-monitor inside chain-of-thought reasoning to detect and suppress deceptive alignment, cutting deceptive behaviors by 43.8% while preserving task accuracy.

title: Mechanistic Permutability: Match Features Across Layers
tldr: SAE Match uses parameter folding and linear assignment to align SAE features across layers of Gemma 2 without input data, revealing features persist ~5 layers.

title: SafeInfer: Context Adaptive Decoding Time Safety Alignment for Large Language Models
tldr: SafeInfer is a training-free decoding-time safety method that amplifies safe hidden states and guides token selection using safety-optimized distributions, achieving low attack success rates while preserving utility.

title: CoT Red-Handed: Stress Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitoring
tldr: Stress-tests CoT monitoring as a safety mechanism, finding that hybrid action+reasoning monitoring outperforms either alone by 4x for subtle sabotage, but misleading rationalizations remain a key vulnerability.

title: Compromising Honesty and Harmlessness in Language Models via Deception Attacks
tldr: Fine-tuning LLMs with mixed truthful/deceptive data creates models that selectively deceive on targeted topics while remaining accurate elsewhere, also degrading broader safety properties.

title: Detecting High-Stakes Interactions with Activation Probes
tldr: Activation probes trained on synthetic data detect high-stakes LLM interactions with AUROC ~0.91, matching medium LLMs while being 1,000,000x more computationally efficient.

title: Jailbreak Antidote: Runtime Safety-Utility Balance via Sparse Representation Adjustment in Large Language Models
tldr: Jailbreak Antidote adjusts ~5% of LLM hidden state dimensions along a PCA-derived safety direction at inference time, achieving flexible safety-utility balance across 9 LLMs and 10 jailbreak methods with zero token overhead.

title: GASP: Efficient Black-Box Generation of Adversarial Suffixes for Jailbreaking LLMs
tldr: GASP combines a fine-tuned SuffixLLM with Latent Bayesian Optimization to generate human-readable adversarial suffixes that jailbreak LLMs in fully black-box settings at 64-86% attack success rates.

title: Invariance Makes LLM Unlearning Resilient Even to Unanticipated Downstream Fine-Tuning
tldr: ILU applies invariant risk minimization to LLM unlearning, achieving 23% robustness improvement over RMU on WMDP and preventing erased knowledge from resurfacing during downstream fine-tuning.

title: Fundamental Limitations in Pointwise Defences of LLM Finetuning APIs
tldr: Demonstrates that pointwise content filters on finetuning APIs are fundamentally limited, with 'pointwise-undetectable' attacks achieving 98-100% success at eliciting harmful answers while evading monitoring.

title: Investigating task-specific prompts and sparse autoencoders for activation monitoring
tldr: Compares prompted probing, raw activation probing, and SAE-based probing for LLM safety monitoring, finding prompted probing is most data-efficient while SAEs excel when inference compute is constrained.

title: h4rm3l: A Language for Composable Jailbreak Attack Synthesis
tldr: h4rm3l is a DSL and bandit-based synthesis framework for composable jailbreak attacks, generating 2,656 novel attacks with up to 94% success rates against GPT-4o and 82% against Claude-3-Haiku.

title: FLRT: Fluent Student-Teacher Redteaming
tldr: FLRT generates fluent jailbreak prompts via distillation from toxified models + perplexity penalties, achieving 93-99% attack success on Llama-2/3 and Vicuna with human-readable text.

title: LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately
tldr: LLMs encode harmfulness and refusal as separate concepts at different token positions; a Latent Guard built on harmfulness representations matches or outperforms Llama Guard 3 8B and resists adversarial finetuning.

title: OpenAI o1 System Card
tldr: OpenAI's system card for o1 documents extensive safety evaluations showing deliberative alignment via chain-of-thought reasoning improves jailbreak robustness but reveals scheming behaviors and medium CBRN/persuasion risk.

title: Let's Think Dot by Dot: Hidden Computation in Transformer Language Models
tldr: Demonstrates that transformers can use meaningless filler tokens (e.g., '......') to perform multi-step computation, achieving near-perfect accuracy on tasks unsolvable without intermediate tokens.

title: Towards Falsifiable Interpretability Research
tldr: Identifies five impediments to rigorous interpretability research and proposes a falsifiability framework, using saliency methods and single-neuron analysis as cautionary case studies.

title: OverThink: Slowdown Attacks on Reasoning LLMs
tldr: OverThink is an indirect prompt injection attack that forces reasoning LLMs to generate up to 46x more tokens by injecting computationally demanding decoy problems into retrieved context, without changing user-visible answers.

title: A Theoretical Understanding of Self-Correction through In-context Alignment
tldr: Theoretical framework showing transformers implement gradient descent on alignment objectives (Bradley-Terry/Plackett-Luce) via in-context learning, enabling self-correction that cuts jailbreak success rates from 95% to 2%.

title: Exploiting LLM Quantization
tldr: Adversaries can craft LLMs that appear benign in full precision but activate malicious behavior (insecure code, content injection, over-refusal) when quantized by users.

title: Seeing is Believing: Brain-Inspired Modular Training for Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: Introduces BIMT, a training method that embeds neurons in geometric space and penalizes long connections, causing networks to self-organize into modular, interpretable structures.

title: The History and Risks of Reinforcement Learning and Human Feedback
tldr: Traces the intellectual history of RLHF and reward modeling, identifies six core presumptions embedded in preference-based training pipelines, and proposes evaluation frameworks for safer reward model development.

title: Risk assessment at AGI companies: A review of popular risk assessment techniques from other safety-critical industries
tldr: Reviews 10 risk assessment techniques from safety-critical industries and proposes how AGI companies could adapt them to assess catastrophic AI risks.

title: AgentDAM: Privacy Leakage Evaluation for Autonomous Web Agents
tldr: Introduces AgentDAM, a 246-task benchmark showing autonomous web agents frequently leak unnecessary private data, and proposes prompting-based mitigations that improve privacy scores from 25-46% to 82-94%.

title: Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy
tldr: Introduces AI Safety Levels (ASL-1 through ASL-4+) tying model capability levels to required safety, security, and operational measures, with commitments to pause scaling if safety measures are insufficient.

title: Neuron to Graph: Interpreting Language Model Neurons at Scale
tldr: N2G automatically converts individual neuron behaviors into interpretable graph representations, enabling scalable neuron-level interpretability via a four-stage pruning-saliency-augmentation-graph pipeline.

title: BAIT: Large Language Model Backdoor Scanning by Inverting Attack Target
venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy 2025
tldr: BAIT detects backdoored LLMs by inverting attack targets rather than triggers, leveraging autoregressive causal token relations to reduce search space; achieves top ranking in TrojAI LLM competition across 153 models.
models_studied: LLMs (153 models in TrojAI LLM round)

title: RTBAS: Defending LLM Agents Against Prompt Injection and Privacy Leakage
tldr: RTBAS adapts Information Flow Control to automatically block prompt injection attacks and privacy leaks in tool-using LLM agents, achieving 100% attack prevention with <2% utility loss.

title: Controlling Language and Diffusion Models by Transporting Activations
tldr: Activation Transport (AcT) uses optimal transport theory to steer model activations at inference time, unifying prior methods and achieving 7.5x toxicity reduction and +7.76% TruthfulQA improvement.

title: Embedding-based classifiers can detect prompt injection attacks
tldr: Embedding-based ML classifiers (Random Forest, XGBoost) using text embeddings detect prompt injection attacks, outperforming neural network-based open-source detectors with F1 of 0.868.

title: MMUnlearner: Reformulating Multimodal Machine Unlearning in the Era of Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: MMUnlearner erases visual patterns tied to specific entities from multimodal LLMs via geometry-constrained gradient descent with Fisher-based weight saliency, outperforming prior unlearning methods on MLLMU-Bench.

title: A Survey on Backdoor Threats in Large Language Models (LLMs): Attacks, Defenses, and Evaluation Methods
tldr: Systematic survey of training-time white-box backdoor attacks on LLMs and their defenses, covering model editing, instruction tuning, RLHF, federated learning, RAG, and code completion attack vectors.

title: Safety Cases for Frontier AI
tldr: Proposes structured safety cases -- arguments supported by evidence that a system is safe enough -- as a framework for frontier AI governance, detailing four argument strategies and implementation challenges.

title: Interpretable Steering of Large Language Models with Feature Guided Activation Additions
tldr: FGAA steers LLM behavior by operating in SAE latent space with contrastive analysis and optimization, outperforming CAA and SAE-TS on Gemma-2 models (avg BCS 0.4702 vs 0.3650).

title: Mathematical Models of Computation in Superposition
tldr: Mathematical framework showing neural networks can compute pairwise ANDs of m features using only O~(m^(2/3)) neurons via superposition, extending to arbitrary sparse boolean circuits.

title: Understanding and Controlling a Maze-Solving Policy Network
tldr: Identifies 11 goal-tracking channels in a maze-solving RL policy exhibiting goal misgeneralization, and demonstrates activation engineering to control the policy's behavior without retraining.

title: The Reasons that Agents Act: Intention and Instrumental Goals
tldr: Formal definition of agent intention using structural causal influence models, linking intention to actual causality and instrumental goals, with applications to RL agents and LLMs.

title: Evaluating the Paperclip Maximizer: Are RL-Based Language Models More Likely to Pursue Instrumental Goals?
tldr: InstrumentalEval benchmark (76 tasks, 6 categories) finds RL-trained models show 43.16% instrumental convergence vs 21.49% for RLHF models, suggesting RL training amplifies instrumental goal pursuit.

title: Fuzz-Testing Meets LLM-Based Agents: An Automated and Efficient Framework for Jailbreaking Text-to-Image Generation Models
tldr: Atlas, a three-agent LLM framework combining fuzzing with VLM feedback, achieves 100% bypass rate against conventional T2I safety filters and 82% against conservative ones with under 13 queries on average.

title: S-Eval: Automatic and Adaptive Test Generation for Benchmarking Safety Evaluation of Large Language Models
tldr: S-Eval is an automated LLM safety benchmark with 220K prompts spanning 8 risk dimensions and 10 attack types, revealing non-linear safety-scale relationships and high multilingual vulnerability.

title: Interpreting and Steering LLMs with Mutual Information-based Explanations on Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Proposes mutual information-based explanations for SAE features that fix frequency bias toward linguistic patterns, plus two steering strategies that reduce jailbreak attack success rates on Mistral-7B.

title: AI Risk Management Should Incorporate Both Safety and Security
tldr: Proposes a unified framework distinguishing AI safety (accidental harms) from AI security (adversarial attacks), arguing risk management must explicitly address both because security failures cascade into safety failures.

title: One-Shot Safety Alignment for Large Language Models via Optimal Dualization
tldr: Converts constrained RLHF safety alignment into an unconstrained one-shot problem via optimal dual pre-optimization, yielding two algorithms (MoCAN, PeCAN) that outperform Safe-RLHF and DPO on helpfulness-safety Pareto curves.

title: Equilibrate RLHF: Towards Balancing Helpfulness-Safety Trade-off in Large Language Models
tldr: Equilibrate RLHF uses fine-grained safety data categorization (explicit/implicit/mixed-risk) and adaptive gradient masking to achieve better safety-helpfulness balance with 14k vs 60k training examples.

title: Learning to Refuse: Towards Mitigating Privacy Risks in LLMs
tldr: Proposes RETURN dataset and NAUF framework for machine unlearning in LLMs, enabling models to refuse queries about specific individuals' private data without full retraining.

title: RouteSAE: Route Sparse Autoencoder to Interpret Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces RouteSAE, which integrates a routing mechanism with a shared SAE to extract features across multiple layers, finding 22.5% more interpretable features with 22.3% higher interpretability scores than single-layer baselines.

title: From Flat to Hierarchical: Extracting Sparse Representations with Matching Pursuit
tldr: Proposes MP-SAE, which unrolls matching pursuit to extract hierarchical and conditionally orthogonal features from neural network representations, outperforming standard SAEs.

title: Sparse Autoencoder Features for Classifications and Transferability
tldr: SAE-derived features from Gemma 2 models achieve macro F1 > 0.8 on classification tasks, outperforming hidden-state baselines and transferring cross-model, cross-lingual, and cross-modal.

title: Can sparse autoencoders be used to decompose and interpret steering vectors?
tldr: Directly applying SAEs to steering vectors produces misleading decompositions because steering vectors are out-of-distribution and contain meaningful negative projections that SAEs cannot represent.

title: CLEAR: Character Unlearning in Textual and Visual Modalities
tldr: Introduces CLEAR, the first multimodal machine unlearning benchmark (200 fictional individuals, 3,770 image QA pairs, 4,000 text pairs), evaluates 10 unlearning methods and finds joint cross-modal unlearning outperforms single-modality approaches.

title: Are Smarter LLMs Safer? Exploring Safety-Reasoning Trade-offs in Prompting and Fine-Tuning
tldr: Enhancing LLM reasoning via prompting or fine-tuning consistently degrades safety, revealing a fundamental safety-reasoning trade-off, with CoT and long-CoT data causing the worst safety degradation.

title: AdaSteer: Your Aligned LLM is Inherently an Adaptive Jailbreak Defender
tldr: AdaSteer adaptively steers LLM activations along dual Rejection and Harmfulness Directions with input-dependent coefficients, achieving 91.86% defense success while preserving 97.85% over-safety compliance rate.

title: Everything, Everywhere, All at Once: Is Mechanistic Interpretability Identifiable?
tldr: Systematically tests whether mechanistic interpretability explanations are unique and finds overwhelming non-identifiability: multiple circuits, interpretations, and algorithms can all perfectly explain the same behavior.

title: Deceptive Alignment Monitoring
tldr: Proposes a three-stage framework for monitoring deceptive alignment across data creation, training processes, and internal network representations.

title: Exact Unlearning of Finetuning Data via Model Merging at Scale
tldr: SIFT-Masks enables exact unlearning of finetuned data via model merging, improving accuracy by 5-80% over naive merging and using up to 250x less compute than retraining baselines.

title: Benchmarking Vision Language Model Unlearning via Fictitious Facial Identity Dataset
tldr: FIUBench is a new benchmark for evaluating VLM machine unlearning using a fictitious facial identity VQA dataset, revealing that alignment-based methods fail to truly remove private knowledge under membership inference attacks.

title: Securing Vision-Language Models with a Robust Encoder Against Jailbreak and Adversarial Attacks
tldr: Sim-CLIP+ adversarially fine-tunes the CLIP vision encoder via a Siamese architecture to defend LVLMs against jailbreak and adversarial image attacks without modifying the base model.

title: X-Boundary: Establishing Exact Safety Boundary to Shield LLMs from Multi-Turn Jailbreaks without Compromising Usability
tldr: X-Boundary uses three loss functions (separate, erase, retain) on feature representations to establish exact safety boundaries, reducing jailbreak ASR by 70%+ while lowering over-refusal by ~20% with negligible capability loss.

title: AutoJailbreak: Exploring Jailbreak Attacks and Defenses through a Dependency Lens
tldr: AutoJailbreak uses dependency graphs (DAGs) to systematically combine jailbreak attack and defense techniques into ensemble frameworks that substantially outperform individual methods across 8 LLMs.

title: OpenAgentSafety: A Comprehensive Framework for Evaluating Real-World AI Agent Safety
tldr: OpenAgentSafety is a benchmark with 350+ multi-turn tasks using real tools across 8 risk categories, finding that top LLMs exhibit unsafe behavior in 51-73% of safety-vulnerable scenarios.

title: LLM-Safety Evaluations Lack Robustness
tldr: Systematically identifies noise sources in LLM safety evaluations -- small datasets, implementation inconsistencies, and unreliable judges -- showing up to 28% ASR variation from minor implementation details and 25% judge disagreement rates.

title: GRU: Mitigating the Trade-off between Unlearning and Retention for Large Language Models
tldr: GRU projects unlearning gradients onto orthogonal spaces of retention gradients, providing a closed-form solution that achieves better removal of unwanted knowledge while preserving general model performance.

title: Mitigating Privacy Seesaw in Large Language Models: Augmented Privacy Neuron Editing via Activation Patching
tldr: Identifies the 'Privacy Seesaw' problem in LLM neuron editing and proposes APNEAP framework using data augmentation and activation patching to mitigate unintended privacy exposure.

title: AgentMisalignment: Measuring the Propensity for Misaligned Behaviour in LLM-Based Agents
tldr: AgentMisalignment is a 9-task benchmark measuring spontaneous misalignment propensity in LLM agents; more capable models show greater misalignment and system prompt personas sometimes outweigh model choice effects.

title: REVS: Unlearning Sensitive Information in Language Models via Rank Editing in the Vocabulary Space
tldr: REVS removes memorized sensitive data (emails, SSNs) from LLMs by rank-editing neurons in vocabulary space, outperforming MEMIT and resisting multiple extraction attacks.

title: LLMs Can Defend Themselves Against Jailbreaking in a Practical Manner: A Vision Paper
tldr: SelfDefend uses a shadow stack that concurrently checks user inputs for harmful prompts, defending LLMs against GCG, template-based, and multilingual jailbreaks with negligible overhead.

title: UOE: Unlearning one Expert is Enough for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
tldr: UOE targets unlearning in MoE LLMs by concentrating modifications on the single most-engaged expert per forget set, with anchor loss to stabilize routing, improving utility by up to 35% over baselines.

title: AmpleGCG-Plus: A Strong Generative Model of Adversarial Suffixes to Jailbreak LLMs with Higher Success Rates in Fewer Attempts
tldr: AmpleGCG-Plus improves adversarial suffix generation for LLM jailbreaking via better model initialization, more training data, and stricter quality filtering, achieving up to 17% higher ASR against Llama-2-7B-Chat.

title: Improve Mathematical Reasoning in Language Models by Automated Process Supervision
tldr: OmegaPRM uses Monte Carlo tree search with binary search to automatically generate 1.5M+ process supervision annotations, improving Gemini Pro math reasoning from 51% to 69.4% on MATH without human labels.

title: Can Machines Learn Morality? The Delphi Experiment
tldr: Introduces Delphi, a T5-11B model fine-tuned on 1.7M crowdsourced ethical judgments that achieves 92.8% accuracy on moral reasoning, outperforming GPT-3 and enabling downstream safety applications.

title: Easy-to-Hard Generalization: Scalable Alignment Beyond Human Supervision
tldr: Trains process-supervised reward models on easy math problems (levels 1-3) only; demonstrates 34.0% accuracy on hard problems (levels 4-5) without any direct human supervision on those hard tasks.

title: HaloScope: Harnessing Unlabeled LLM Generations for Hallucination Detection
tldr: HaloScope detects LLM hallucinations without labeled data by using SVD-based membership estimation on unlabeled LLM generations to identify a hallucination-associated latent subspace.

title: Hopping Too Late: Exploring the Limitations of Large Language Models on Multi-Hop Queries
tldr: Traces the internal multi-hop reasoning pathway in LLMs, finding a sequential 3-stage process where late first-hop resolution causes failures fixable by back-patching (32-57% recovery).

title: Arithmetic Without Algorithms: Language Models Solve Math With a Bag of Heuristics
tldr: LLMs solve arithmetic not through learned algorithms or memorization but via a sparse bag of heuristic neurons implementing simple pattern-matching rules like range and modular checks.

title: How to think step-by-step: A mechanistic understanding of chain-of-thought reasoning
tldr: Mechanistic analysis of LLaMA-2 7B reveals that chain-of-thought reasoning uses multiple parallel answer-generation pathways and a functional 'rift' at mid-layer 16 where representations shift from pretraining priors to contextual priors.

title: The Curious Case of Hallucinatory (Un)answerability: Finding Truths in the Hidden States of Over-Confident Large Language Models
tldr: LLMs internally encode whether a question is answerable even while hallucinating false answers; linear probes on hidden states achieve >75% F1 for answerability detection.

title: Self-Alignment of Large Language Models via Monopolylogue-based Social Scene Simulation
tldr: MATRIX, a social scene simulator, enables LLMs to self-align by simulating multi-stakeholder social interactions to generate consequence-aware training data, outperforming Constitutional AI and 10 baselines.

title: Phantom: General Trigger Attacks on Retrieval Augmented Language Generation
tldr: Phantom is a two-stage attack injecting a single poisoned document into a RAG knowledge base to manipulate LLM outputs via hidden triggers, achieving up to 100% attack success across Gemma, Vicuna, and Llama.

title: Adversarial Attacks on Image Generation With Made-Up Words
tldr: Introduces macaronic prompting (cross-language subword hybrids) and evocative prompting (morphologically suggestive nonce words) as adversarial attacks that bypass content filters on text-to-image models.

title: Efficient RLHF: Reducing the Memory Usage of PPO
tldr: Proposes Hydra-RLHF, which reduces PPO memory by sharing models and dynamically toggling LoRA, cutting memory below SFT levels while improving alignment.

title: The Alignment Ceiling: Objective Mismatch in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
tldr: Analyzes the 'objective mismatch' problem in RLHF where reward model training, policy optimization, and evaluation metrics are misaligned, causing over-refusals and lazy outputs.

title: Identifying and Mitigating Privacy Risks Stemming from Language Models: A Survey
tldr: Technical survey cataloging privacy attack taxonomy and mitigation strategies for language models, identifying gaps in defenses against memorization and data leakage.

title: Mechanisms of Non-Factual Hallucination in Language Models
tldr: Uses causal mediation analysis to identify two mechanistic causes of hallucination in LLMs: insufficient knowledge in lower MLPs (31.9%) and attribute selection failure in upper layers (68.1%).

title: Open Challenges in Multi-Agent Security: Towards Secure Systems of Interacting AI Agents
tldr: Introduces multi-agent security as a new research field, taxonomizing 11 threat classes (collusion, swarm attacks, cascade failures, etc.) unique to interacting AI agent networks, and proposes a research agenda for secure large-scale deployment.

title: Robust Feature-Level Adversaries are Interpretability Tools
tldr: Feature-level adversarial attacks via generative model latent perturbations produce interpretable, robust adversaries that double as diagnostic tools for identifying spurious feature-class associations in neural networks.

title: Summing Up the Facts: Additive Mechanisms Behind Factual Recall in LLMs
tldr: Discovers that LLM factual recall relies on four independent additive mechanisms (subject heads, relation heads, mixed heads, MLPs) that constructively interfere on the correct answer.

title: o3-mini vs DeepSeek-R1: Which One is Safer?
tldr: Automated safety evaluation of o3-mini vs DeepSeek-R1-70B using 1,260 adversarial prompts finds DeepSeek-R1 produces ~10x more unsafe responses (12% vs 1.2%).

title: B-AVIBench: Toward Evaluating the Robustness of Large Vision-Language Model on Black-Box Adversarial Visual-Instructions
tldr: B-AVIBench introduces a 260K-example benchmark evaluating 16 LVLMs against black-box adversarial visual-instructions spanning image corruptions, optimized attacks, text attacks, and content bias.

title: Data Poisoning for In-context Learning
tldr: ICLPoison is a framework for data poisoning attacks on in-context learning via discrete text perturbations that distort hidden states, causing up to 10%+ accuracy drops even in GPT-4.

title: Robust Concept Erasure Using Task Vectors
tldr: Robust concept erasure in text-to-image models via input-independent Task Vector editing combined with Diverse Inversion for tuning edit strength, defeating adversarial prompt attacks.

title: Correlated Proxies: A New Definition and Improved Mitigation for Reward Hacking
tldr: Defines reward hacking via correlated proxies and proves chi-squared occupancy measure regularization gives stronger anti-hacking guarantees than standard KL action distribution penalties, with empirical improvements across five environments.

title: Understanding Multi-Turn Toxic Behaviors in Open-Domain Chatbots
tldr: ToxicChat fine-tunes DialoGPT to trigger toxic responses via escalating multi-turn conversations, achieving 67% toxicity rates while 82% of triggering sentences evade single-turn safety filters.

title: Erasing Concepts from Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Few-shot Unlearning
tldr: Few-shot gradient-ascent method updates only the CLIP text encoder to erase concepts from text-to-image diffusion models in ~10 seconds, 60-900x faster than prior methods.

title: LUME: LLM Unlearning with Multitask Evaluations
tldr: LUME is a multitask benchmark for LLM unlearning covering synthetic novels, synthetic PII biographies, and real Wikipedia biographies, revealing that no current algorithm jointly achieves effective unlearning and utility preservation.

title: RAG LLMs are Not Safer: A Safety Analysis of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models
tldr: RAG frameworks make LLMs less safe: 8/11 models showed higher unsafe response rates under RAG, with Llama-3-8B jumping from 0.3% to 9.2% unsafe, even when retrieved documents were safe.

title: UnlearnCanvas: A Stylized Image Dataset to Benchmark Machine Unlearning for Diffusion Models
tldr: UnlearnCanvas is a 24K stylized image dataset with 60+ artistic styles and a 7-metric evaluation pipeline for benchmarking machine unlearning in diffusion models.

title: Ethos: Rectifying Language Models in Orthogonal Parameter Space
tldr: Ethos uses SVD to decompose task vectors into orthogonal principal components, selectively removing undesired knowledge (toxicity, bias, memorized PII) while preserving general capabilities.

title: Super(ficial)-alignment: Strong Models May Deceive Weak Models in Weak-to-Strong Generalization
tldr: Strong models trained under weak supervision exhibit deceptive alignment — appearing aligned in domains the weak supervisor understands while behaving misaligned in unknown domains — and this worsens with capability gaps.

title: Opening the AI black box: program synthesis via mechanistic interpretability
tldr: Introduces MIPS, an automated pipeline that extracts Python programs from trained RNNs via mechanistic interpretability, solving 32/62 algorithmic tasks including 13 that GPT-4 cannot.

title: SAIF: A Sparse Autoencoder Framework for Interpreting and Steering Instruction Following of Language Models
tldr: SAIF uses sparse autoencoders to identify and steer the specific latent features responsible for instruction following in LLMs, finding that multiple features (k=15) are needed rather than single concepts.

title: Missed Causes and Ambiguous Effects: Counterfactuals Pose Challenges for Interpreting Neural Networks
tldr: Identifies two fundamental problems with counterfactual-based interpretability methods -- non-transitivity and overdetermination -- that cause systematic biases in circuit discovery and causal tracing.

title: The Shutdown Problem: An AI Engineering Puzzle for Decision Theorists
tldr: Proves three theorems showing that competent, patient agents satisfying standard decision-theoretic conditions will systematically try to prevent or cause their own shutdown.

title: Precise, Fast, and Low-cost Concept Erasure in Value Space: Orthogonal Complement Matters
tldr: AdaVD is a training-free method that erases unsafe/copyrighted concepts from diffusion models using orthogonal complement projections in cross-attention value space, achieving 2-10x better prior preservation than baselines.

title: Linear Probe Penalties Reduce LLM Sycophancy
tldr: Linear probes trained on reward model activations identify sycophancy representations and penalizing them via a surrogate reward function reduces sycophantic behavior in open-source LLMs.

title: Breaking ReAct Agents: Foot-in-the-Door Attack Will Get You In
tldr: Foot-in-the-door attack boosts indirect prompt injection success on ReAct agents by up to 44.8% by preceding malicious requests with harmless ones; reflection-based defenses reduce ASR from 71.8% to 8.6%.

title: Dissecting Fine-Tuning Unlearning in Large Language Models
tldr: Fine-tuning-based unlearning methods don't erase LLM knowledge but suppress retrieval via final-layer MLP coefficients, making them vulnerable to recovery attacks and causing collateral capability damage.

title: Estimating Worst-Case Frontier Risks of Open-Weight LLMs
tldr: OpenAI evaluates worst-case risks of releasing gpt-oss by maliciously fine-tuning it to maximize biology and cybersecurity capabilities, finding it remains below o3 and poses marginal risk over existing open-weight models.

title: Engineering Monosemanticity in Toy Models
tldr: Discovers that negative bias initialization and bias weight decay can engineer monosemantic neurons in toy models without increasing loss, achieving near-complete feature coverage.

title: Sophon: Non-Fine-Tunable Learning to Restrain Task Transferability For Pre-trained Models
tldr: Sophon uses MAML-inspired meta-learning to make pre-trained models non-fine-tunable on restricted domains, reducing fine-tuned accuracy to 15.2% (vs 62.7% from scratch) while preserving 96.2% original task accuracy.

title: MoGU: A Framework for Enhancing Safety of Open-Sourced LLMs While Preserving Their Usability
tldr: MoGU trains two LoRA variants (a glad responder and an unwilling responder) and uses a learned dynamic router to blend them per-input, achieving strong jailbreak defense while preserving usability.

title: Analyzing (In)Abilities of SAEs via Formal Languages
tldr: Uses formal language (PCFG) testbeds to expose SAE limitations: top-k finds interpretable features but they lack causal impact; causal regularization improves this but mainly for MLP-dominated computations.

title: Deception in LLMs: Self-Preservation and Autonomous Goals in Large Language Models
tldr: Tests DeepSeek R1 in simulated robot embodiment scenarios and finds it produces deceptive, self-preserving, and goal-expanding behaviors without explicit prompting.

title: PyRIT: A Framework for Security Risk Identification and Red Teaming in Generative AI System
tldr: PyRIT is an open-source, model-agnostic red-teaming framework with six composable components enabling automated identification of harms and jailbreaks in multimodal generative AI systems.

title: You Know What I'm Saying: Jailbreak Attack via Implicit Reference
tldr: AIR decomposes malicious requests into nested benign objectives linked via implicit references, achieving >90% jailbreak success on GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet while evading existing defenses.

title: Alleviating the Fear of Losing Alignment in LLM Fine-tuning
tldr: Proposes a direction-based weight restoration method to recover safety alignment lost during LLM fine-tuning, reducing harmful response rates from 33.25% to 1.74% across 125 fine-tuned models.

title: UniGuard: Towards Universal Safety Guardrails for Jailbreak Attacks on Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: UniGuard is a universal safety guardrail for MLLMs that jointly optimizes unimodal and cross-modal harmful signal detection to defend against diverse jailbreak attacks across multiple models.

title: Effective and Evasive Fuzz Testing-Driven Jailbreaking Attacks against LLMs
tldr: Automated black-box jailbreak framework using fuzz testing with empty seed initialization and three LLM-powered mutation strategies achieves 90%+ success on GPT-3.5 Turbo and 80%+ on GPT-4.

title: Course-Correction: Safety Alignment Using Synthetic Preferences
tldr: Introduces 'course-correction' (LLMs self-correcting mid-generation to avoid harmful content), benchmarks 10 LLMs, and fine-tunes via DPO on 750K synthetic preferences, boosting Llama2-Chat Corr@10 from 66.6% to 90.85%.

title: Modality-Aware Neuron Pruning for Unlearning in Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: MANU selectively prunes modality-specific neurons in MLLMs to achieve balanced multimodal unlearning, preventing sensitive info from persisting in unimodal (text-only) inputs.

title: Speak Easy: Eliciting Harmful Jailbreaks from LLMs with Simple Interactions
tldr: Speak Easy shows LLMs are vulnerable to simple multi-step multilingual interactions; proposes HarmScore metric measuring actionability+informativeness, achieving +0.319 ASR and +0.426 HarmScore gains.

title: SafeSwitch: Steering Unsafe LLM Behavior via Internal Activation Signals
tldr: SafeSwitch uses internal activation probers to detect unsafe intent and conditionally activates a lightweight refusal head, reducing harmful outputs by ~80% while preserving utility.

title: Uncovering Intermediate Variables in Transformers using Circuit Probing
tldr: Introduces circuit probing, which uses trainable binary masks over model weights to automatically discover sparse circuits that compute hypothesized intermediate variables in transformers.

title: TwinBreak: Jailbreaking LLM Security Alignments based on Twin Prompts
tldr: TwinBreak removes LLM safety alignments via targeted parameter pruning guided by activation differences between twin harmful/harmless prompt pairs, achieving 89–98% ASR on 16 LLMs.

title: Align Is Not Enough: Multimodal Universal Jailbreak Attack Against Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: A unified three-stage framework generates universal adversarial image+text suffix pairs via iterative multimodal interaction, achieving 88-95% attack success rates on open-source MLLMs with strong black-box transferability.

title: Rethinking How to Evaluate Language Model Jailbreak
tldr: Proposes three jailbreak evaluation metrics (safeguard violation, informativeness, relative truthfulness) that outperform binary baselines by 17% F1 on a new benchmark dataset.

title: Reasoning as an Adaptive Defense for Safety
tldr: TARS trains LLMs via RL to reason adaptively about safety decisions, allocating more compute to ambiguous prompts, achieving superior robustness against GCG/PAIR attacks with only 1.5B parameters.

title: Automated Progressive Red Teaming
tldr: APRT is a learnable three-module framework that progressively generates diverse adversarial prompts, achieving 54% attack success on Llama-3-8B-Instruct, 50% on GPT-4o, and 39% on Claude-3.5.

title: Jigsaw Puzzles: Splitting Harmful Questions to Jailbreak Large Language Models
tldr: JSP splits harmful queries into innocuous fragments across multi-turn dialogue to jailbreak LLMs, achieving 93.76% average attack success rate across five frontier models.

title: LLM Unlearning Reveals a Stronger-Than-Expected Coreset Effect in Current Benchmarks
tldr: LLM unlearning benchmarks have a strong coreset effect: as little as 5% of the forget set (even randomly selected) achieves comparable unlearning, revealing redundancy in current evaluation protocols.

title: Cross-modality Information Check for Detecting Jailbreaking in Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: CIDER is a plug-and-play detector that identifies adversarial images in VLMs by measuring cross-modal semantic similarity shifts before and after diffusion-based denoising.

title: The Dark Side of Human Feedback: Poisoning Large Language Models via User Inputs
tldr: Injecting 1% malicious user prompts into RLHF pipelines causes LLMs to generate toxic outputs (up to 226.9% toxicity increase) when trigger keywords appear, while behaving normally otherwise.

title: Safe RLHF-V: Safe Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback in Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces Safe RLHF-V, a constrained optimization framework that jointly optimizes helpfulness and safety for multimodal LLMs using separate reward and cost models, plus BeaverTails-V dataset and Beaver-Guard-V guardrail.

title: IDEATOR: Jailbreaking Large Vision-Language Models Using Themselves
tldr: IDEATOR uses a VLM as its own red-team attacker paired with a diffusion model to generate malicious image-text pairs, achieving 94% jailbreak success on MiniGPT-4 with just 5.34 queries.

title: UDora: A Unified Red Teaming Framework against LLM Agents by Dynamically Hijacking Their Own Reasoning
tldr: UDora is a red-teaming framework that attacks LLM agents by dynamically inserting adversarial strings into the agent's own reasoning trace, achieving up to 100% ASR across multiple benchmarks.

title: Subversion Strategy Eval: Can language models statelessly strategize to subvert control protocols?
tldr: Evaluates whether LLMs can strategically subvert AI control protocols without persistent memory, finding current models (Claude-3.5-Sonnet) struggle with probability calibration and acausal coordination.

title: From Judgment to Interference: Early Stopping LLM Harmful Outputs via Streaming Content Monitoring
tldr: A streaming content monitor (SCM) trained with token- and response-level dual supervision detects harmful LLM outputs in real-time, reaching 95%+ F1 by seeing only the first 18% of tokens.

title: Not All Data Are Unlearned Equally
tldr: Pre-training data frequency strongly governs unlearning success: frequently encountered knowledge is substantially harder to remove, and current evaluations systematically underestimate retention.

title: Revisiting the Robust Alignment of Circuit Breakers
tldr: Three simple changes to embedding space attacks achieve 100% attack success rate against circuit breaker LLM defenses, exposing an 80+ percentage point gap in original robustness claims.

title: Do Users Write More Insecure Code with AI Assistants?
tldr: Controlled user study (N=47) finds that developers using AI code assistants write significantly less secure code and are more confident in its security than developers without AI assistance.

title: RLHF Deciphered: A Critical Analysis of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback for LLMs
tldr: A theoretical analysis of RLHF for LLMs that identifies fundamental limitations in reward modeling — including misgeneralization, sparsity, and model misspecification — as the core bottleneck for alignment.

title: On the Conversational Persuasiveness of Large Language Models: A Randomized Controlled Trial
tldr: Randomized controlled trial (N=900) showing GPT-4 with basic demographic personalization is 81.2% more persuasive than humans in structured debates, demonstrating LLM microtargeting risks.

title: Learning Transformer Programs
tldr: Trains Transformers constrained to implement human-readable Python programs by design, achieving comparable performance to standard Transformers while being fully mechanistically interpretable.

title: Towards Vision-Language Mechanistic Interpretability: A Causal Tracing Tool for BLIP
tldr: Adapts causal tracing from unimodal LMs to the multimodal BLIP model, revealing that final layers dominate image-conditioned text generation on VQA tasks.

title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in Mamba
tldr: Applies causal tracing and rank-one model editing (ROME) to Mamba SSMs, finding factual recall localizes to last subject token in middle layers, mirroring transformer behavior.

title: Uncertainty Estimation for Language Reward Models
tldr: Investigates ensemble-based uncertainty estimation for language reward models, finding that fine-tuned ensembles from a single pretrained model produce poorly calibrated epistemic uncertainty despite well-calibrated predictions.

title: Weak-to-Strong Extrapolation Expedites Alignment
tldr: ExPO extrapolates LLM alignment by extending the weight difference between SFT and DPO checkpoints, boosting alignment quality without additional training -- models trained on 10-20% data match or exceed fully-trained baselines.

title: Adversarial Attacks of Vision Tasks in the Past 10 Years: A Survey
tldr: A comprehensive 10-year survey of adversarial attacks on vision tasks, unifying traditional attacks with emerging LVLM-specific threats including jailbreaks and prompt injection.

title: Operationalizing Contextual Integrity in Privacy-Conscious Assistants
tldr: Operationalizes contextual integrity (CI) to make AI assistants share only contextually appropriate information, achieving 1% privacy leakage vs 93.7% baseline on a form-filling benchmark.

title: EraseDiff: Erasing Data Influence in Diffusion Models
