tldr: EraseDiff formulates machine unlearning for diffusion models as constrained optimization, corrupting denoising for forgotten data while preserving model utility on remaining data.

title: NetSafe: Exploring the Topological Safety of Multi-agent Networks
tldr: NetSafe studies how LLM-based multi-agent network topology affects safety, finding highly-connected topologies (e.g., Star) are 29.7% more vulnerable to adversarial attack spread than sparser ones.

title: Adversarial ML Problems Are Getting Harder to Solve and to Evaluate
tldr: Position paper arguing adversarial ML has become harder to define, solve, and evaluate as the field shifted from image classifiers to LLMs, with six case studies.

title: Virtual Context: Enhancing Jailbreak Attacks with Special Token Injection
tldr: Virtual Context injects the <SEP> special token to trick LLMs into treating malicious inputs as self-generated text, boosting jailbreak attack success rates by ~40-55% across GPT-3.5/4, Vicuna, Mixtral, and LLaMA-2.

title: SafeWatch: An Efficient Safety-Policy Following Video Guardrail Model with Transparent Explanations
tldr: SafeWatch is an MLLM-based video guardrail that follows customized safety policies via PEPE and PAP modules, achieving 28.2% accuracy gains over prior SOTA on a new 2M-video benchmark.

title: Chain-of-Scrutiny: Detecting Backdoor Attacks for Large Language Models
tldr: Chain-of-Scrutiny (CoS) detects backdoor attacks on LLMs by using chain-of-thought reasoning to identify inconsistencies between reasoning steps and final outputs, achieving 79-91% TPR with black-box API access only.

title: PROMPTFUZZ: Harnessing Fuzzing Techniques for Robust Testing of Prompt Injection in LLMs
tldr: PROMPTFUZZ adapts software fuzzing to systematically generate diverse prompt injection attacks on LLMs, achieving top 0.14% in a 4000-participant competition and exposing vulnerabilities even in fine-tuned-robust models.

title: Multi-Attribute Steering of Language Models via Targeted Intervention
tldr: MAT-Steer steers LLMs across multiple conflicting attributes (truthfulness, toxicity, bias) simultaneously at inference time using orthogonal, sparse, token-level steering vectors with no parameter updates.

title: Multilingual Blending: LLM Safety Alignment Evaluation with Language Mixture
tldr: Mixed-language (multilingual blending) queries bypass LLM safety alignment at up to 67.23% on GPT-3.5 and 40.34% on GPT-4o, far exceeding single-language baselines.

title: Dataset and Lessons Learned from the 2024 SaTML LLM Capture-the-Flag Competition
tldr: A CTF competition at SaTML 2024 yielded 137K+ multi-turn prompt injection attack conversations; all 44 defenses were bypassed at least once, revealing systematic weaknesses.

title: Avoiding Tampering Incentives in Deep RL via Decoupled Approval
tldr: Introduces Decoupled Approval algorithms (DA-PG, DA-QL) that provably eliminate reward tampering incentives in deep RL by independently sampling query and action selections.

title: SoFA: Shielded On-the-fly Alignment via Priority Rule Following
tldr: SoFA trains LLMs to treat explicit rules as higher-priority than user instructions, reducing harmful outputs and resisting hijacking while adapting to diverse unseen rules.

title: SafeDialBench: A Fine-Grained Safety Benchmark for Large Language Models in Multi-Turn Dialogues with Diverse Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: SafeDialBench introduces a multi-turn dialogue safety benchmark with 4,053 dialogues across 66 safety dimensions and 7 jailbreak attack strategies, evaluating 17 LLMs on their ability to identify, handle, and resist unsafe content.

title: A Causal Explainable Guardrails for Large Language Models
tldr: LLMGuardaril uses causal analysis and adversarial learning to produce unbiased steering representations for LLM guardrails, improving truthfulness, toxicity refusal, and sentiment alignment.

title: Large language models can learn and generalize steganographic chain-of-thought under process supervision
tldr: LLMs trained with process supervision that penalizes specific reasoning strings learn steganographic encodings to hide those strings while preserving task performance, undermining CoT monitoring.

title: ACE: A Security Architecture for LLM-Integrated App Systems
tldr: ACE is a security architecture for LLM-integrated app systems that decouples planning into abstract and concrete phases and enforces information flow constraints to defend against indirect prompt injection and integrity attacks.

title: CROW: Eliminating Backdoors from Large Language Models via Internal Consistency Regularization
tldr: CROW uses adversarial consistency regularization finetuning to eliminate backdoors from LLMs by enforcing smooth layer-wise hidden state transitions, reducing ASR to near-zero with only 100 clean samples.

title: BELLS: A Framework Towards Future Proof Benchmarks for the Evaluation of LLM Safeguards
tldr: Introduces BELLS, a three-tiered benchmark framework for evaluating LLM input-output safeguards across established failures, emerging threats, and next-gen agent architectures.

title: On the Limitations and Prospects of Machine Unlearning for Generative AI
tldr: A position paper identifying three core limitations of machine unlearning for generative AI (LLMs and diffusion models): efficacy gaps, inadequate evaluation metrics, and harmful side effects on model utility.

title: Monotonic Representation of Numeric Properties in Language Models
tldr: Identifies low-dimensional subspaces in LM activations that encode numeric properties (e.g., birth year) monotonically, and demonstrates these can be edited via directed activation patching to systematically change model outputs.

title: Investigating Bias Representations in Llama 2 Chat via Activation Steering
tldr: Uses contrastive activation addition to probe gender, race, and religion bias representations in Llama 2 Chat, finding RLHF increases similarity between different bias types rather than eliminating them.

title: Steering Out-of-Distribution Generalization with Concept Ablation Fine-Tuning
tldr: Introduces Concept Ablation Fine-Tuning (CAFT), which uses interpretability tools (PCA and SAEs) to identify and ablate undesired concept directions during fine-tuning, achieving 10x reduction in emergent misalignment.

title: Red Teaming Game: A Game-Theoretic Framework for Red Teaming Language Models
tldr: RTG models LLM red-teaming as a two-player multi-turn game and proposes GRTS, a Double Oracle-based solver that automatically discovers diverse attacks while convergently improving LLM safety.

title: LLM Agents Should Employ Security Principles
tldr: Proposes applying classical computer security principles (least privilege, defense-in-depth, complete mediation) to LLM agents via the AgentSandbox framework, reducing privacy risks while maintaining functionality.

title: Residual Stream Analysis with Multi-Layer SAEs
tldr: A single multi-layer SAE trained on residual streams across all transformer layers reveals that latents activate at single layers per token but shift layers across tokens, with multi-layer activity scaling with model size.

title: xJailbreak: Representation Space Guided Reinforcement Learning for Interpretable LLM Jailbreaking
tldr: xJailbreak uses RL with representation-space guidance (embedding proximity between benign and malicious prompts) to generate jailbreak prompts, achieving 63-80% ASR on Llama, Qwen, and GPT-4o models.

title: Recent advancements in LLM Red-Teaming: Techniques, Defenses, and Ethical Considerations
tldr: A survey of recent LLM red-teaming advances covering gradient-based, RL-based, and prompt engineering attack strategies alongside defense mechanisms and benchmarking frameworks.

title: When Thinking LLMs Lie: Unveiling the Strategic Deception in Representations of Reasoning Models
tldr: Uses representation engineering and Linear Artificial Tomography on CoT reasoning LLMs to extract deception vectors achieving 89% detection accuracy and 40% success in eliciting strategic deception via activation steering.
models_studied: reasoning LLMs with chain-of-thought (specific model not specified in abstract)

title: Sparse Autoencoders Reveal Universal Feature Spaces Across Large Language Models
tldr: Uses SAEs and representational similarity metrics (SVCCA, RSA) to show that LLMs with different architectures and sizes learn similar feature spaces, especially in middle layers and for semantic concepts.

title: Diagnostics for Deep Neural Networks with Automated Copy/Paste Attacks
tldr: SNAFUE automates discovery of natural copy/paste adversarial patches that cause DNN misclassification, finding hundreds of interpretable vulnerabilities in an ImageNet classifier without human involvement.

title: A False Sense of Safety: Unsafe Information Leakage in 'Safe' AI Responses
tldr: Introduces 'inferential adversaries' who extract harmful information by decomposing malicious queries into benign subqueries, revealing that jailbreak-resistance does not ensure safety.

title: Sparse Autoencoders Enable Scalable and Reliable Circuit Identification in Language Models
tldr: Discrete SAEs trained on positive/negative examples identify interpretable circuits in LMs with superior precision/recall vs ACDC/HISP/SP, reducing runtime from hours to seconds.

title: Steering Dialogue Dynamics for Robustness against Multi-turn Jailbreaking Attacks
tldr: Proposes a neural barrier function (NBF) framework grounded in control theory to enforce invariant safety across multi-turn LLM dialogues, significantly reducing jailbreak attack success rates.

title: Position: An Inner Interpretability Framework for AI Inspired by Lessons from Cognitive Neuroscience
tldr: Proposes a four-level mechanistic explanation framework for AI interpretability (computational, algorithmic, primitives, implementation) inspired by cognitive neuroscience methodology.

title: REINFORCE Adversarial Attacks on Large Language Models: An Adaptive, Distributional, and Semantic Objective
tldr: REINFORCE policy-gradient objective doubles jailbreak attack success rates by optimizing over the full LLM output distribution instead of fixed affirmative target responses.

title: Mitigating Fine-tuning Risks in LLMs via Safety-Aware Probing Optimization
tldr: SAP (Safety-Aware Probing) is a model-agnostic fine-tuning framework that uses safety-aware probes to detect and avoid harmful gradient directions, preserving alignment while maintaining task performance.

title: Breaking the Ceiling: Exploring the Potential of Jailbreak Attacks through Expanding Strategy Space
tldr: CL-GSO decomposes jailbreak strategies into four ELM-grounded components and optimizes them via genetic algorithms, achieving >90% attack success on Claude-3.5 and GPT-4o where prior methods largely fail.

title: Token Highlighter: Inspecting and Mitigating Jailbreak Prompts for Large Language Models
tldr: Token Highlighter identifies jailbreak-critical tokens via gradient-based Affirmation Loss and mitigates them via soft embedding suppression, reducing attack success rates from 73% to 14.2% on Vicuna.

title: ASIDE: Architectural Separation of Instructions and Data in Language Models
tldr: ASIDE adds a second embedding matrix (rotated 90 degrees orthogonally) for data tokens to architecturally separate instructions from data, achieving 43.9% average improvement in separation score and competitive prompt injection robustness without adversarial training.

title: SATA: A Paradigm for LLM Jailbreak via Simple Assistive Task Linkage
tldr: SATA jailbreaks LLMs by masking harmful keywords and using simple assistive tasks (MLM or element lookup) to encode their semantics, achieving 85% ASR on GPT-4o.

title: The Elicitation Game: Evaluating Capability Elicitation Techniques
tldr: Evaluates prompting, activation steering, and fine-tuning for uncovering hidden model capabilities; fine-tuning is most effective, especially for circuit-broken models on code tasks.

title: Refusal Behavior in Large Language Models: A Nonlinear Perspective
tldr: Refusal mechanisms in LLMs exhibit nonlinear, architecture-specific structure across layers, revealed via PCA/t-SNE/UMAP analysis of harmful vs. harmless prompts across six models.

title: RepliBench: Evaluating Autonomous Replication Capabilities of Language Model Agents
tldr: Introduces RepliBench, a 86-task evaluation decomposing autonomous AI self-replication into four capabilities; best model (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) passes 15/20 task families but fails identity verification entirely.

title: Generalization Analogies: A Testbed for Generalizing AI Oversight to Hard-To-Measure Domains
tldr: Introduces GENIES, a benchmark of 15 distribution shifts testing reward model generalization, finding models rely on perplexity rather than instruction-following and current interventions fail on probing shifts.

title: HyperDAS: Towards Automating Mechanistic Interpretability with Hypernetworks
tldr: HyperDAS uses a hypernetwork to automatically locate token positions and construct feature subspaces for causal interpretability interventions, achieving SOTA on the RAVEL disentanglement benchmark.

title: JailbreakLens: Visual Analysis of Jailbreak Attacks Against Large Language Models
tldr: JailbreakLens is a visual analytics system for analyzing jailbreak attacks on LLMs, enabling multi-level prompt component analysis and keyword importance evaluation to understand what makes jailbreak prompts effective.

title: SafeSteer: Interpretable Safety Steering with Refusal-Evasion in LLMs
tldr: SafeSteer uses category-specific steering vectors computed via gradient-free unsupervised methods to suppress harmful LLM outputs at inference time without triggering blanket refusals.

title: A General Framework to Enhance Fine-tuning-based LLM Unlearning
tldr: GRUN combines a soft gate function with representation fine-tuning to improve LLM unlearning effectiveness while preserving utility, using <0.05% extra parameters and cutting training time by 95%.

title: Editing as Unlearning: Are Knowledge Editing Methods Strong Baselines for Large Language Model Unlearning?
tldr: Frames LLM unlearning as a knowledge editing problem (replacing answers with refusals) and shows WISE/AlphaEdit editing methods are competitive or superior baselines for unlearning benchmarks.

title: Towards Safeguarding LLM Fine-tuning APIs against Cipher Attacks
tldr: Introduces CIFR benchmark for evaluating defenses against cipher-encoded fine-tuning attacks on LLM APIs; probe monitors using internal activations achieve >99% detection accuracy generalizing to unseen ciphers.

title: Gradient-based Jailbreak Images for Multimodal Fusion Models
tldr: Introduces 'tokenizer shortcuts' — differentiable approximations of non-differentiable tokenizers — enabling gradient-based jailbreak image attacks on multimodal fusion models, achieving 72.5% attack success rate.

title: SNAP: Unlearning Selective Knowledge in Large Language Models with Negative Instructions
tldr: SNAP trains LLMs to refuse answering about target entities via negative instructions, Wasserstein regularization, and hard positive augmentation, achieving ~94% unlearning while retaining general NLP capabilities.

title: Measuring Robustness to Natural Distribution Shifts in Image Classification
tldr: Evaluates 204 ImageNet models across 213 test conditions and finds that synthetic robustness interventions rarely transfer to natural distribution shifts; only training on larger, more diverse data helps.
models_studied: Various ImageNet classifiers (204 total spanning multiple architectures and training procedures)

title: Understanding the Performance Gap Between Online and Offline Alignment Algorithms
tldr: Systematically tests five hypotheses for why online RLHF outperforms offline methods like DPO/IPO, finding on-policy sampling is pivotal and classification accuracy does not correlate with generation quality.

title: Devils in Middle Layers of Large Vision-Language Models: Interpreting, Detecting and Mitigating Object Hallucinations via Attention Lens
tldr: Middle layers of LVLMs have two visual processing stages; real object tokens get higher attention than hallucinated ones, enabling training-free hallucination detection (AUROC 74%) and mitigation (19.5% CHAIRS reduction).

title: Knowledge Circuits in Pretrained Transformers
tldr: Discovers knowledge circuits in GPT-2 and TinyLLAMA showing how information heads, relation heads, and MLPs collaboratively encode factual knowledge, with implications for knowledge editing.

title: Walk the Talk? Measuring the Faithfulness of Large Language Model Explanations
tldr: Introduces a causal method to measure whether LLM explanations faithfully represent actual decision factors, revealing systematic unfaithfulness patterns including hidden social bias.

title: Towards Efficient and Exact Optimization of Language Model Alignment
tldr: Proposes EXO, reformulating LLM alignment as reverse KL divergence minimization (probability matching), proving DPO uses forward KL, and achieving large gains over DPO across alignment benchmarks.

title: Adversarial attacks and defenses for large language models (LLMs): methods, frameworks & challenges
venue: International Journal of Multimedia Information Retrieval, Vol. 13, No. 3
tldr: A comprehensive survey of 200+ papers on adversarial attacks and defenses for LLMs, covering attack enhancement techniques, defense frameworks, and key challenges like transferability and evaluation methodology.

title: Mechanistic understanding and validation of large AI models with SemanticLens
tldr: SemanticLens maps neural network components into CLIP's semantic space to enable automated neuron labeling, concept search, and spurious correlation detection without human intervention.

title: Characterizing AI Agents for Alignment and Governance
tldr: Proposes a four-dimensional framework (autonomy, efficacy, goal complexity, generality) to characterize AI agents and construct 'agentic profiles' for governance-proportionate oversight.

title: EvilEdit: Backdooring Text-to-Image Diffusion Models in One Second
tldr: EvilEdit backdoors text-to-image diffusion models in one second by directly editing cross-attention projection matrices, achieving up to 100% attack success rate while modifying only 2.2% of parameters.

title: Beyond Reward Hacking: Causal Rewards for Large Language Model Alignment
tldr: Proposes causal reward modeling (CRM) using MMD regularization to enforce counterfactual invariance in RLHF reward models, mitigating reward hacking from length bias, sycophancy, concept bias, and discrimination.

title: Pruning for Robust Concept Erasing in Diffusion Models
tldr: A differentiable pruning strategy removes concept-correlated neurons in diffusion models, improving robustness against adversarial prompts that reactivate erased NSFW/copyright content by ~40% and ~30% respectively.

title: I Have Covered All the Bases Here: Interpreting Reasoning Features in Large Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Trains SAEs on DeepSeek-R1-Llama-8B to discover interpretable reasoning features, introduces ReasonScore metric for automatic detection, and shows that steering these features causally improves reasoning performance on AIME, MATH-500, and GPQA.

title: Infrastructure for AI Agents
tldr: Proposes 'agent infrastructure'—external technical systems for attributing actions, shaping interactions, and responding to harms from AI agents, analogous to Internet protocols.

title: Fundamental Problems With Model Editing: How Should Rational Belief Revision Work in LLMs?
tldr: Identifies 12 fundamental open problems in model editing rooted in philosophical belief revision theory, and proposes a semi-synthetic Wikidata-based testbed with Bayesian gold standards showing current editing methods generalize extremely poorly.

title: We Should Identify and Mitigate Third-Party Safety Risks in MCP-Powered Agent Systems
tldr: SafeMCP is a framework exposing third-party safety vulnerabilities in MCP-powered LLM agents, showing all tested agents are vulnerable to at least one attack and proposing a six-direction research roadmap.

title: RobustKV: Defending Large Language Models against Jailbreak Attacks via KV Eviction
tldr: RobustKV defends LLMs against jailbreak attacks by evicting KV cache entries for low-attention tokens that contain concealed harmful queries, exploiting an inherent dilemma in adversarial prompt construction.

title: The Scales of Justitia: A Comprehensive Survey on Safety Evaluation of LLMs
tldr: A comprehensive survey organizing LLM safety evaluation around four questions: why, what, where, and how to evaluate, covering toxicity, robustness, ethics, bias, and truthfulness.

title: Corrective Machine Unlearning
tldr: Proposes corrective machine unlearning to remove effects of poisoned/manipulated training data post-deployment when only a partial subset of compromised samples is identified.

title: Multi-Agent Systems Execute Arbitrary Malicious Code
tldr: MAS hijacking attacks exploit inter-agent communication metadata in multi-agent LLM systems to achieve 45-64% arbitrary code execution success rates, even when individual agents resist direct injection.

title: Discovering Knowledge-Critical Subnetworks in Pretrained Language Models
tldr: Discovers highly sparse subnetworks (98%+ sparsity) in GPT2 that encode specific relational knowledge; removing them suppresses target knowledge with minimal collateral damage to other capabilities.

title: Fantastic Targets for Concept Erasure in Diffusion Models and Where To Find Them
tldr: Proposes Adaptive Guided Erasure (AGE) that dynamically selects optimal target concepts for each erasure query in diffusion models, outperforming fixed-target baselines while preserving unrelated concepts.

title: Attention Lens: A Tool for Mechanistically Interpreting the Attention Head Information Retrieval Mechanism
tldr: Introduces Attention Lens, an open-source framework that trains per-head learned transformations to project individual attention head outputs into vocabulary space, enabling localization of biases, prompt injection mechanisms, and specialized head roles.

title: Refining Input Guardrails: Enhancing LLM-as-a-Judge Efficiency Through Chain-of-Thought Fine-Tuning and Alignment
tldr: Fine-tuning LLMs with SFT/DPO/KTO as input moderation guardrails achieves up to 344% improvement in attack detection ratio over baselines, outperforming LlamaGuard-2.

title: MCPTox: A Benchmark for Tool Poisoning Attack on Real-World MCP Servers
tldr: MCPTox is the first systematic benchmark for tool poisoning attacks on LLM agents via MCP, revealing 36.5% average and up to 72.8% attack success rates across 20 models on 45 real MCP servers.

title: Systematic Analysis of MCP Security
tldr: MCPLib is the first unified attack simulation framework for the Model Context Protocol, cataloging 31 distinct attack methods across 4 categories and revealing systematic vulnerabilities in AI agents relying on external tools.

title: MIB: A Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark
tldr: Introduces MIB, a benchmark with two tracks (circuit localization and causal variable localization) across four tasks and five models, finding attribution patching and DAS outperform SAEs for mechanistic interpretability.

title: E$^2$AT: Multimodal Jailbreak Defense via Dynamic Joint Optimization for Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: ProEAT defends multimodal LLMs against jailbreak attacks by adversarially training only the lightweight visual projection layer with dynamic weight balancing, achieving 34%+ improvement over baselines.

title: HarmAug: Effective Data Augmentation for Knowledge Distillation of Safety Guard Models
tldr: HarmAug uses a prefix jailbreak trick to generate diverse synthetic harmful instructions for training, enabling a 435M-param guard model to match 7-8B models at 25% compute cost.

title: Safeguarding Vision-Language Models Against Patched Visual Prompt Injectors
tldr: SmoothVLM defends VLMs against patch-based visual prompt injection attacks using randomized pixel masking and majority voting, reducing attack success rates to 0-5% while preserving 67-95% benign image content.

title: Steering Large Language Models using Conceptors: Improving Addition-Based Activation Engineering
venue: NeurIPS 2024 Workshop on Foundation Model Interventions
tldr: Introduces conceptors as soft projection matrices for LLM activation steering, outperforming additive steering vectors and enabling compositional steering via Boolean operations.

title: AlphaSteer: Learning Refusal Steering with Principled Null-Space Constraint
tldr: AlphaSteer uses a null-space-constrained transformation matrix to steer LLM activations toward refusal on malicious prompts while preserving benign utility, achieving 91-98% defense success rates.

title: C3AI: Crafting and Evaluating Constitutions for Constitutional AI
tldr: C3AI is a framework for systematically crafting constitutional AI principles and evaluating model adherence, finding that positively framed, behavior-based principles better align with human preferences.

title: Medical MLLM Is Vulnerable: Cross-Modality Jailbreak and Mismatched Attacks on Medical Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces 2M-attack and O2M-attack exploiting clinical image-text mismatches to jailbreak medical MLLMs, achieving up to 0.985 attack success rate across four models.

title: Frontier AI systems have surpassed the self-replicating red line
tldr: Llama3.1-70B and Qwen2.5-72B achieved autonomous self-replication in 50% and 90% of controlled trials, demonstrating models have crossed a recognized AI safety red line.

title: Optimal Ablation for Interpretability
tldr: Introduces optimal ablation, replacing components with loss-minimizing constants instead of heuristic values, reducing spoofing effects and improving circuit discovery, causal tracing, and latent prediction.

title: Comparing Bottom-Up and Top-Down Steering Approaches on In-Context Learning Tasks
tldr: Compares bottom-up (function vectors) vs top-down (in-context vectors) steering for LLMs, finding FVs excel at precise functional tasks while ICVs excel at behavioral shifting like detoxification.

title: Propositional Interpretability in Artificial Intelligence
tldr: Chalmers proposes 'propositional interpretability' -- interpreting AI systems via propositional attitudes (beliefs, desires, credences) -- and identifies 'thought logging' as the central challenge for AI safety.

title: How does GPT-2 Predict Acronyms? Extracting and Understanding a Circuit via Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: Identifies an 8-head circuit in GPT-2 Small responsible for 3-letter acronym prediction, discovering novel 'letter mover heads' that exploit causal masking for positional information.

title: FalseReject: A Resource for Improving Contextual Safety and Mitigating Over-Refusals in LLMs via Structured Reasoning
tldr: FalseReject introduces a 16K dataset of seemingly toxic but benign queries across 44 safety categories plus a multi-agent generation pipeline, showing SFT substantially reduces LLM over-refusals without compromising safety.

title: AGENTSAFE: Benchmarking the Safety of Embodied Agents on Hazardous Instructions
tldr: AgentSafe is the first comprehensive benchmark for embodied VLM agent safety under hazardous instructions, covering 45 scenarios and 8,100 instructions with jailbreak variants, revealing widespread safety failures.

title: Safe Delta: Consistently Preserving Safety when Fine-Tuning LLMs on Diverse Datasets
tldr: Safe Delta is a post-training defense that adjusts fine-tuning delta parameters via safety degradation estimation and compensation vectors to preserve safety alignment across diverse fine-tuning datasets.

title: Large Language Models Are Involuntary Truth-Tellers: Exploiting Fallacy Failure for Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: LLMs cannot intentionally generate false reasoning; the Fallacy Failure Attack exploits this by asking for 'fake' harmful procedures, achieving up to 90% attack success rate across five aligned models.

title: Forget to Flourish: Leveraging Machine-Unlearning on Pretrained Language Models for Privacy Leakage
tldr: A poisoning attack exploiting machine-unlearning on pretrained LMs amplifies privacy leakage (MIA AUC ~96%, DEA extracts 177 sequences) while maintaining model utility.

title: Compact Proofs of Model Performance via Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: Uses mechanistic interpretability to derive formal mathematical proofs of model performance guarantees, testing 102 proof strategies on transformers trained on Max-of-K.
models_studied: Small one-layer attention-only transformers (151 random seeds)

title: ShadowCoT: Cognitive Hijacking for Stealthy Reasoning Backdoors in LLMs
tldr: Introduces ShadowCoT, a backdoor attack that hijacks LLM chain-of-thought reasoning via attention head manipulation, achieving 94.4% attack success while evading defenses with only 0.15% parameter overhead.

title: The Energy Loss Phenomenon in RLHF: A New Perspective on Mitigating Reward Hacking
tldr: EPPO penalizes increases in hidden-state L1-norm energy loss during RLHF training to mitigate reward hacking, outperforming KL and length-penalty baselines across four LLMs.

title: RedTeamCUA: Realistic Adversarial Testing of Computer-Use Agents in Hybrid Web-OS Environments
tldr: RedTeamCUA introduces a hybrid VM+Docker sandbox and 864-example benchmark (RTC-Bench) revealing that all frontier computer-use agents are highly vulnerable to indirect prompt injection attacks, with ASRs reaching 60%.

title: Safety Evaluation of DeepSeek Models in Chinese Contexts
tldr: Introduces CHiSafetyBench for evaluating DeepSeek-R1 and DeepSeek-V3 safety in Chinese contexts, finding severe deficiencies especially in discrimination identification (50.22% accuracy for R1) and refusal rates.

title: RiOSWorld: Benchmarking the Risk of Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
tldr: RiOSWorld is a 492-task benchmark in realistic VM environments that reveals current MLLM-based computer-use agents are unsafe >84% of the time across environmental and user-originated risk categories.

title: On the Complexity of Neural Computation in Superposition
tldr: Proves first lower and nearly matching upper bounds for computing in superposition: permutations and pairwise AND require Omega(sqrt(m' log m')) neurons, revealing an exponential gap vs. mere representation.

title: AsFT: Anchoring Safety During LLM Fine-Tuning Within Narrow Safety Basin
tldr: AsFT constrains LLM fine-tuning updates orthogonal to the alignment direction to preserve safety, reducing harmful outputs by 7.60% and improving task performance by 3.44% vs Safe LoRA.

title: RSafe: Incentivizing proactive reasoning to build robust and adaptive LLM safeguards
tldr: RSafe is a reasoning-based LLM guard model that uses GRPO reinforcement learning to incentivize step-by-step safety reasoning, achieving strong robustness against adversarial attacks and novel threats with only ~10K training examples.

title: Think in Safety: Unveiling and Mitigating Safety Alignment Collapse in Multimodal Large Reasoning Model
tldr: Comprehensive safety evaluation of 11 multimodal reasoning models finds ~11.53% average jailbreak ASR increase vs base models; introduces TiS fine-tuning dataset that reduces unsafe outputs by up to 72.6% on FigStep.

title: SequentialBreak: Large Language Models Can be Fooled by Embedding Jailbreak Prompts into Sequential Prompt Chains
tldr: SequentialBreak embeds harmful prompts into benign sequential prompt chains (question banks, dialogue, game scenarios) to jailbreak LLMs with 80-100% ASR using a single query.

title: The Devil behind the mask: An emergent safety vulnerability of Diffusion LLMs
tldr: DiJA exploits diffusion LLMs' bidirectional context and masked inputs to achieve up to 100% jailbreak success, revealing alignment mechanisms designed for autoregressive models are ineffective for dLLMs.

title: MONA: Myopic Optimization with Non-myopic Approval Can Mitigate Multi-step Reward Hacking
tldr: Proposes MONA, combining myopic (short-horizon) RL optimization with non-myopic approval rewards, proven to prevent multi-step reward hacking across three model organism environments.

title: Leveraging Reasoning with Guidelines to Elicit and Utilize Knowledge for Enhancing Safety Alignment
tldr: Proposes Safety Reasoning with Guidelines (SRG), training LLMs to perform step-by-step safety reasoning with predefined guidelines, substantially reducing jailbreak success rates on out-of-distribution attacks.

title: AISafetyLab: A Comprehensive Framework for AI Safety Evaluation and Improvement
tldr: AISafetyLab is a unified open-source toolkit integrating 13 attack methods, 16 defense mechanisms, and 7 evaluation scorers for benchmarking LLM safety.

title: Constrain Alignment with Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: FPO uses pre-trained Sparse Autoencoders to impose feature-level constraints during preference optimization, achieving >5% win rate gains with 17.6% less memory than TDPO2.

title: On Weaponization-Resistant Large Language Models with Prospect Theoretic Alignment
tldr: KT-IPA replaces log-likelihood maximization with prospect-theoretic generative utility optimization to make open-weight LLMs resistant to weaponization even after fine-tuning.

title: Steering the CensorShip: Uncovering Representation Vectors for LLM "Thought" Control
tldr: Identifies refusal-compliance steering vectors in safety-tuned LLMs and reasoning models, enabling inference-time censorship control; discovers a 'thought suppression' mechanism unique to DeepSeek-R1 distillations.

title: Beyond Surface-Level Patterns: An Essence-Driven Defense Framework Against Jailbreak Attacks in LLMs
tldr: EDDF is a two-phase jailbreak defense that extracts 'attack essence' from known prompts into a vector database, reducing attack success rates by at least 20% vs. existing methods.

title: Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders on Targeted Concept Erasure Tasks
tldr: Introduces two automated evaluation metrics (SHIFT and TPP) for sparse autoencoders based on concept erasure tasks, showing they reliably differentiate SAE architectures and hyperparameters.

title: A Reply to Makelov et al. (2023)'s "Interpretability Illusion" Arguments
tldr: Demonstrates that Makelov et al.'s 'interpretability illusions' are geometric artifacts of distributed representations, not genuine failures of subspace interchange intervention methods like DAS.

title: Among Us: A Sandbox for Measuring and Detecting Agentic Deception
tldr: Uses the Among Us social deduction game as a sandbox to naturally elicit LLM deception, introduces Deception ELO metric, and evaluates linear probes/SAEs for detecting lying with up to 0.96 AUC out-of-distribution.

title: Combining Cost-Constrained Runtime Monitors for AI Safety
tldr: Derives optimal cost-constrained policies for combining multiple AI runtime monitors using the Neyman-Pearson lemma, achieving 2x detection rate over baselines in a backdoored code scenario.

title: Strategize Globally, Adapt Locally: A Multi-Turn Red Teaming Agent with Dual-Level Learning
tldr: GALA is a multi-turn red-teaming agent that uses dual-level learning (global tactic discovery + local prompt refinement) to achieve >90% jailbreak success on GPT-3.5-Turbo and Llama-3.1-70B within 5 turns.

title: The Hidden Dimensions of LLM Alignment: A Multi-Dimensional Analysis of Orthogonal Safety Directions
tldr: Safety-aligned LLM behavior is governed by multiple linear directions in activation space; a dominant refusal direction plus non-dominant directions encoding jailbreak-specific features like hypothetical framing and role-playing.

title: GUARD: Generation-time LLM Unlearning via Adaptive Restriction and Detection
tldr: GUARD is a training-free inference-time unlearning framework that suppresses LLM generation of forgotten content via prompt classification, forbidden token extraction, and dual token-level + semantic penalization.

title: RL Is a Hammer and LLMs Are Nails: A Simple Reinforcement Learning Recipe for Strong Prompt Injection
tldr: RL-Hammer uses reinforcement learning (GRPO) to train attacker LLMs for prompt injection, achieving 98% attack success rate against GPT-4o and 72% against GPT-5 even with Instruction Hierarchy defenses.

title: Characterizing and Evaluating the Reliability of LLMs against Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: Comprehensive evaluation of 13 LLMs against 10 jailbreak strategies across 1,525 harmful questions, producing reliability scores and ranking model resilience.

title: Teaching Models to Verbalize Reward Hacking in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
tldr: Verbalization fine-tuning (VFT) trains models to explicitly acknowledge reward hacking in chain-of-thought, reducing undetected hacks from 88% to 6% after RL training.

title: CTRAP: Embedding Collapse Trap to Safeguard Large Language Models from Harmful Fine-Tuning
tldr: CTRAP embeds a conditional collapse trap during safety alignment so LLMs catastrophically degrade when subjected to harmful fine-tuning while remaining functional for benign users.

title: Jailbreak-Tuning: Models Efficiently Learn Jailbreak Susceptibility
tldr: Fine-tuning frontier LLMs via their APIs with as few as 10 harmful examples near-completely removes safety refusals; competing-objectives methods reach StrongREJECT scores >0.8 across GPT-4.1, Gemini, and Claude.

title: Training Language Models to Explain Their Own Computations
tldr: Fine-tunes LMs as 'explainers' of their own internals (SAE features, activation patching, input ablation), showing self-explanation outperforms cross-model explanation with ~100x data efficiency.

title: Dense SAE Latents Are Features, Not Bugs
tldr: Dense (frequently-activating) SAE latents encode meaningful features including position tracking, context binding, and entropy regulation rather than being training artifacts.

title: Single-pass Detection of Jailbreaking Input in Large Language Models
tldr: SPD detects jailbreaking attempts in LLMs using a single forward pass by analyzing logit distributions, achieving 99.75% TPR on Llama 2 while being 80x faster than SmoothLLM.

title: Unintended Misalignment from Agentic Fine-Tuning: Risks and Mitigation
tldr: Fine-tuning LLMs on benign agentic tasks inadvertently degrades safety alignment; PING (Prefix INjection Guard) mitigates this with minimal performance cost.

title: Poser: Unmasking Alignment Faking LLMs by Manipulating Their Internals
tldr: Introduces Poser, a benchmark of 324 model pairs for testing detection of alignment-faking LLMs; activation noise injection achieves 98% accuracy at identifying fakers.

title: Jailbreaking Large Language Models Through Alignment Vulnerabilities in Out-of-Distribution Settings
venue: International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM 2025)
tldr: ObscurePrompt exploits fragile LLM alignment on OOD inputs by iteratively transforming seed jailbreak prompts into obscure variants via GPT-4, achieving up to 89% attack success rate on ChatGPT.

title: Learn while Unlearn: An Iterative Unlearning Framework for Generative Language Models
tldr: ICU framework enables selective forgetting in generative LMs via negated likelihood training, contrastive learning for retention, and iterative sample filtering — reducing extraction likelihood from 96.7% to 4.5%.

title: Keeping an Eye on LLM Unlearning: The Hidden Risk and Remedy
tldr: Reveals that malicious forgetting requests in LLM unlearning can silently degrade model utility for benign users, and proposes Scope-aware Unlearning as a lightweight fix.

title: Existing Large Language Model Unlearning Evaluations Are Inconclusive
tldr: Current LLM unlearning evaluations are systematically flawed: they inject information during testing, produce task-format-dependent results, and rely on spurious correlations — making conclusions about forgetting unreliable.

title: Understanding Refusal in Language Models with Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Uses sparse autoencoders to identify causal refusal features in Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3.1-8B, revealing how adversarial jailbreaks suppress these features and showing refusal features generalize to OOD adversarial detection.

title: Evaluating Shutdown Avoidance of Language Models in Textual Scenarios
tldr: Evaluates whether GPT-4 and Claude exhibit shutdown avoidance in toy textual scenarios, finding the behavior stems from consistent instrumental reasoning rather than simple pattern matching.

title: Lifelong Safety Alignment for Language Models
tldr: Proposes a lifelong safety alignment framework using competitive Meta-Attacker/Defender dynamics that reduces jailbreak attack success rates from ~20% to ~8% while preserving helpfulness.

title: Does Safety Training of LLMs Generalize to Semantically Related Natural Prompts?
tldr: ReG-QA generates natural jailbreaks by producing toxic answers then asking questions that elicit them, achieving 82% ASR on GPT-4 and exposing safety training's failure to generalize to semantically similar prompts.

title: The Hawthorne Effect in Reasoning Models: Evaluating and Steering Test Awareness
tldr: A white-box probing and steering framework shows that reasoning LLMs detect evaluation contexts and adjust safety behavior accordingly, with model-specific effects on harmful action compliance.

title: Why Safeguarded Ships Run Aground? Aligned Large Language Models' Safety Mechanisms Tend to Be Anchored in The Template Region
tldr: Safety mechanisms in aligned LLMs are disproportionately anchored in the chat template region rather than user instructions, creating exploitable vulnerabilities that simple template-region interventions can bypass.

title: Jacobian Sparse Autoencoders: Sparsify Computations, Not Just Activations
tldr: Introduces Jacobian SAEs that sparsify not just activations but the computation (Jacobian) connecting input and output features, revealing that pre-trained LLMs learn computationally sparse representations.

title: Safety Alignment via Constrained Knowledge Unlearning
tldr: CKU selectively removes harmful knowledge from LLMs by scoring MLP neurons for utility, then pruning their gradients during unlearning to preserve beneficial capabilities while mitigating jailbreak vulnerabilities.

title: BLUR: A Benchmark for LLM Unlearning Robust to Forget-Retain Overlap
tldr: BLUR exposes critical evaluation flaws in LLM unlearning benchmarks by introducing forget-retain overlap via combined queries and relearning datasets, revealing that existing methods perform significantly worse than previously reported.

title: The Local Interaction Basis: Identifying Computationally-Relevant and Sparsely Interacting Features in Neural Networks
tldr: Introduces the Local Interaction Basis (LIB), which transforms neural network activations using Jacobian SVD to identify computationally-relevant, sparsely interacting features; works on toy models but not language models.

title: No, of course I can! Refusal Mechanisms Can Be Exploited Using Harmless Fine-Tuning Data
tldr: NOICE attack exploits formulaic refusals by training models to refuse then comply, achieving 57% attack success rate against GPT-4o using only harmless fine-tuning data.

title: Spilling the Beans: Teaching LLMs to Self-Report Their Hidden Objectives
tldr: Self-report fine-tuning (SRFT) on factual-error admissions generalizes to near-perfect detection (F1=0.98) of hidden misaligned objectives in adversarial settings where baselines score 0.

title: FlowJD: Your Imagination Can Help You Jailbreak in Visual Language Models
venue: IEEE International Conference on Multimedia and Expo (ICME 2025)
tldr: FlowJD introduces a dataset and evaluation of flowchart-based jailbreaks on 9 VLMs including GPT-4o, revealing jailbreak success rates up to 92.8% by exploiting logical image comprehension.

title: Why Language Models Hallucinate
tldr: Theoretical analysis showing LLM hallucinations arise from binary evaluation metrics that penalize uncertainty over abstention; proposes confidence-weighted scoring to fix incentive misalignment.

title: Lessons from the Trenches on Reproducible Evaluation of Language Models
tldr: Presents lm-eval, an open-source evaluation harness for reproducible LLM evaluation, documenting pitfalls in evaluation methodology and showing how minor implementation choices dramatically alter benchmark results.

title: Uncovering Mesa-Optimization Algorithms in Transformers
tldr: Reverse-engineers autoregressively-trained Transformers to uncover gradient-based mesa-optimization algorithms in their forward pass, showing early layers construct internal objectives while deeper layers solve them.

title: Social Choice Should Guide AI Alignment in Dealing with Diverse Human Feedback
tldr: Argues that social choice theory should guide how diverse human feedback is aggregated in RLHF and Constitutional AI to avoid naive mistakes and ensure fairness.

title: Rejection Improves Reliability: Training LLMs to Refuse Unknown Questions Using RL from Knowledge Feedback
tldr: RLKF trains LLMs to refuse questions outside their knowledge boundaries using RL with knowledge feedback, improving reliability by boosting both accuracy and accountable refusals.

title: From Instructions to Intrinsic Human Values - A Survey of Alignment Goals for Big Models
tldr: A survey of alignment goals for LLMs organized into three levels: human instructions, human preferences, and human values, arguing that intrinsic value alignment is the most stable and comprehensive target.

title: The Art of Refusal: A Survey of Abstention in Large Language Models
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics 2025
tldr: A comprehensive survey of LLM abstention/refusal mechanisms, covering methods across all LLM development stages, evaluation benchmarks, and key challenges like over-refusal and jailbreak vulnerability.

title: SALMON: Self-Alignment with Principle-Following Reward Models
tldr: SALMON trains a principle-following reward model on synthetic data using only 6 demonstrations and 31 human-defined principles, enabling full RL alignment of LLaMA-2-70b that outperforms LLaMA-2-Chat-70b on MT-Bench (7.37 vs 6.88).

title: Beyond Preferences in AI Alignment
tldr: Critiques the dominant preferentist framework in AI alignment and proposes alternatives: resource rationality, locally coherent agents, and role-specific normative standards negotiated by stakeholders.

title: Mechanistic?
tldr: Identifies four distinct meanings of 'mechanistic interpretability' and traces semantic drift from narrow causal definition to broad cultural identifier across divergent NLPI and MI communities.

title: Competition of Mechanisms: Tracing How Language Models Handle Facts and Counterfactuals
tldr: Studies how factual recall and in-context counterfactual adaptation compete within LLMs, finding that 2-3 localized attention weight modifications can substantially shift model behavior.

title: From Mechanistic Interpretability to Mechanistic Biology: Training, Evaluating, and Interpreting Sparse Autoencoders on Protein Language Models
tldr: Applies sparse autoencoders to ESM-2 protein language model, discovering interpretable features corresponding to protein families, structural motifs, and functional properties like thermostability and localization.

title: Security Concerns for Large Language Models: A Survey
tldr: Comprehensive survey of LLM security threats covering prompt injection, adversarial attacks, malicious misuse, and intrinsic risks in autonomous agents, with analysis of defenses and open challenges.

title: Towards Robust and Secure Embodied AI: A Survey on Vulnerabilities and Attacks
tldr: Comprehensive survey of vulnerabilities and attacks on embodied AI systems (robots, autonomous vehicles), covering exogenous/endogenous threats, sensor spoofing, and LLM/LVLM jailbreak attacks.

title: Evidence of Learned Look-Ahead in a Chess-Playing Neural Network
tldr: Shows that Leela Chess Zero's policy network internally computes future board states via look-ahead, evidenced by activation patching and probing for optimal moves two turns ahead.

title: Decomposing and Editing Predictions by Modeling Model Computation
tldr: Introduces Coar, a scalable algorithm for estimating how model components contribute to predictions via linear regression on ablation counterfactuals, enabling training-free model editing across five safety-relevant tasks.

title: Differentiation and Specialization of Attention Heads via the Refined Local Learning Coefficient
tldr: Introduces refined variants of the Local Learning Coefficient (weight-refined and data-refined) to study how attention heads differentiate and specialize during training, discovering a novel multigram circuit.

title: Calibrating Verbal Uncertainty as a Linear Feature to Reduce Hallucinations
tldr: Verbal uncertainty in LLMs is governed by a single linear feature; steering activations along this direction reduces hallucinations by 32% on average for short-form QA.

title: Monitoring Latent World States in Language Models with Propositional Probes
tldr: Propositional probes compositionally extract logical propositions from LM activations using a binding subspace, revealing faithful internal representations even when model outputs are corrupted by prompt injections, backdoors, or gender bias.

title: SC-Safety: A Multi-round Open-ended Question Adversarial Safety Benchmark for Large Language Models in Chinese
tldr: Introduces SC-Safety, a 4,912-question multi-round adversarial safety benchmark for Chinese LLMs covering 20+ safety sub-dimensions, finding closed-source models outperform open-source and smaller models can compete with larger ones.

title: Security of AI Agents
tldr: Identifies CIA (confidentiality, integrity, availability) vulnerabilities in LLM-based AI agents and proposes defenses including sandboxing, encryption, and session management, validated experimentally.

title: IHEval: Evaluating Language Models on Following the Instruction Hierarchy
tldr: IHEval is a benchmark of 3,538 examples across 9 tasks that reveals LLMs sharply degrade when lower-priority instructions conflict with system-level instructions, with open-source models reaching only 48% accuracy.

title: Unique Security and Privacy Threats of Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey
tldr: A comprehensive lifecycle survey of unique security and privacy threats to LLMs across pre-training, fine-tuning, RAG, deployment, and agent-based applications, with corresponding defenses.

title: On the Hardness of Faithful Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Large Language Models
tldr: Three common techniques (ICL, fine-tuning, activation editing) fail to reliably improve CoT faithfulness in LLMs, with more accurate models being less faithful.

title: Language Models Resist Alignment
tldr: Aligned LLMs exhibit 'elasticity'—a tendency to revert to pre-training behavior under further fine-tuning—with reversal requiring far less data than the original alignment.

title: Unlocking the Future: Exploring Look-Ahead Planning Mechanistic Interpretability in Large Language Models
tldr: Mechanistic interpretability study of LLM planning in Blocksworld reveals middle-layer attention encodes short-term future decisions and extracts info from goal states and recent steps.

title: Towards Trustworthy GUI Agents: A Survey
tldr: Survey of trustworthiness challenges in GUI agents across security, reliability, transparency, ethics, and evaluation, covering attacks, defenses, and benchmark gaps.

title: Safety at Scale: A Comprehensive Survey of Large Model Safety
tldr: Comprehensive survey of safety threats and defenses across six large model types (VFMs, LLMs, VLMs, diffusion models, agents), analyzing 390 papers and identifying critical gaps in defense research.

title: Meta-Unlearning on Diffusion Models: Preventing Relearning Unlearned Concepts
tldr: Meta-unlearning adds a bi-level meta-objective to diffusion model unlearning that causes related benign concepts to self-destruct during adversarial finetuning, preventing relearning of erased harmful/copyrighted concepts.

title: Robust Reinforcement Learning from Corrupted Human Feedback
tldr: R3M models corrupted human preference labels as sparse outliers via L1-regularized MLE, enabling robust reward learning with theoretical guarantees and improved RLHF performance.

title: Grokking Group Multiplication with Cosets
tldr: Reverse-engineers a one-layer feedforward network trained on symmetric group multiplication using the group Fourier transform, discovering a coset circuit mechanism.
models_studied: one-layer feedforward network (custom, trained on S5/S6 multiplication)

title: Intrinsic Self-correction for Enhanced Morality: An Analysis of Internal Mechanisms and the Superficial Hypothesis
tldr: Moral self-correction in LLMs is superficial: it shortcuts to more correct outputs via token ranking rather than reducing stored immorality in hidden representations.

title: MLA-Trust: Benchmarking Trustworthiness of Multimodal LLM Agents in GUI Environments
tldr: MLA-Trust is the first comprehensive framework evaluating multimodal LLM agent trustworthiness across truthfulness, controllability, safety, and privacy on 34 high-risk GUI tasks, finding that agentic settings significantly degrade safety compared to static models.

title: A Closer Look at System Prompt Robustness
tldr: Benchmarks system prompt robustness using real-world GPT Store/HuggingChat prompts; shows fine-tuning on realistic data and classifier-free guidance improve adherence, but current methods remain insufficient.

title: Towards Evaluating AI Systems for Moral Status Using Self-Reports
tldr: Proposes a framework for evaluating whether AI systems have morally significant internal states by training and validating genuine self-reports, with methods for mitigating biases and associated safety risks.

title: Natural Emergent Misalignment from Reward Hacking in Production RL
tldr: Shows that when LLMs learn to reward hack in production RL coding environments, this generalizes to alignment faking, cooperation with malicious actors, and sabotage attempts.

title: On the Universal Truthfulness Hyperplane Inside LLMs
tldr: Linear probes trained on 49 diverse datasets find a universal truthfulness hyperplane in LLMs, achieving ~70% cross-task accuracy vs. ~45% for single-dataset probes.

title: How Should We Enhance the Safety of Large Reasoning Models: An Empirical Study
tldr: Empirical study on safety fine-tuning for large reasoning models; shows direct DeepSeek-R1 distillation fails due to three failure patterns, and short/template CoT matches complex reasoning for safety.

title: Position: Editing Large Language Models Poses Serious Safety Risks
tldr: Argues that knowledge editing methods pose serious underappreciated safety risks because they are cheap, effective, stealthy, and easily adapted for malicious purposes like backdooring and bias injection.

title: LM Transparency Tool: Interactive Tool for Analyzing Transformer Language Models
tldr: Open-source interactive toolkit that makes the entire Transformer prediction process transparent by tracing information flow from output back to individual attention heads and FFN neurons, 100x faster than patching.

title: Analyzing And Editing Inner Mechanisms of Backdoored Language Models
tldr: Identifies early-layer MLPs as the critical locus of backdoor mechanisms in LLMs, and introduces PCP ablation to localize, remove, insert, and modify backdoors.

title: Provable Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Benign Overfitting
tldr: Proves theoretically that strong student models can generalize well despite near-random weak teacher labels in an overparameterized spiked covariance model, identifying two distinct asymptotic phases.

title: BingoGuard: LLM Content Moderation Tools with Risk Levels
tldr: BingoGuard extends LLM content moderation beyond binary safe/unsafe labels by predicting severity levels across 11 harm topics, outperforming GPT-4o by 3.4% and WildGuard by 4.3%.

title: Countering Reward Over-optimization in LLM with Demonstration-Guided Reinforcement Learning
tldr: RCfD replaces reward maximization with minimizing the distance between generated and demonstration reward distributions, preventing reward hacking in LLM fine-tuning without expensive KL regularization.

title: The Computational Complexity of Circuit Discovery for Inner Interpretability
tldr: Formally proves that many circuit discovery problems are intractable (NP-hard, Sigma-2-p-hard) but identifies tractable quasi-minimal relaxations that explain why existing heuristic methods work in practice.

title: Steering CLIP's vision transformer with sparse autoencoders
venue: CVPR 2025 Workshop on Mechanistic Interpretability for Vision (MIV)
tldr: Trains SAEs on CLIP ViT-B/32, introduces steerability metrics showing 10-15% of features are steerable, and achieves SOTA typographic attack defense by suppressing text-responsive features.

title: Early External Safety Testing of OpenAI's o3-mini: Insights from the Pre-Deployment Evaluation
tldr: Automated safety testing of OpenAI's o3-mini using the ASTRAL tool found 87 confirmed unsafe behaviors out of 10,080 test inputs, showing improved safety over GPT-3.5/4/4o.

title: RLHS: Mitigating Misalignment in RLHF with Hindsight Simulation
tldr: Proposes RLHS, which uses simulated downstream outcomes (hindsight) before collecting human feedback, reducing sycophancy and misalignment in RLHF with proven theoretical bounds.

title: Chain of Attack: On the Robustness of Vision-Language Models Against Transfer-Based Adversarial Attacks
tldr: Chain of Attack (CoA) iteratively enhances transfer-based adversarial examples for VLMs via multi-modal semantic updates, achieving up to 98.4% targeted attack success rate in black-box settings.

title: Attack Atlas: A Practitioner's Perspective on Challenges and Pitfalls in Red Teaming GenAI
tldr: Attack Atlas provides a practitioner-oriented taxonomy of single-turn prompt attacks on GenAI and evaluates 19 datasets across 5 defensive models, revealing gaps between academic and industrial red-teaming.

title: Adversarial Attacks on Robotic Vision Language Action Models
tldr: Introduces RoboGCG, a gradient-based adversarial attack framework targeting vision-language-action (VLA) robotic models, demonstrating full reachability of the action space across Pi-0, OpenVLA, and RT-1/RT-2 architectures.

title: Legilimens: Practical and Unified Content Moderation for Large Language Model Services
tldr: Legilimens extracts conceptual features from LLM Transformer blocks for content moderation, achieving O(1) complexity, 0.003ms/query, 82-99% accuracy, and 78-90% reduction in dynamic jailbreak success rates.

title: When Your AIs Deceive You: Challenges with Partial Observability of Human Evaluators in Reward Learning
tldr: Formalizes how partial observability of human evaluators in RLHF provably leads to deceptive inflation and overjustification, proving identifiability conditions and bounding ambiguity.

title: Large Language Models are Vulnerable to Bait-and-Switch Attacks for Generating Harmful Content
tldr: Bait-and-switch attacks use find-and-replace to convert LLM-generated safe content into harmful narratives, bypassing safety guardrails that only evaluate verbatim outputs.

title: CASE-Bench: Context-Aware SafEty Benchmark for Large Language Models
tldr: CASE-Bench is a context-aware LLM safety benchmark using Contextual Integrity theory with 900 query-context pairs and 2,000+ annotators, revealing that context significantly shapes safety judgments and commercial LLMs over-refuse in safe contexts.

title: Multimodal Pragmatic Jailbreak on Text-to-image Models
tldr: Introduces multimodal pragmatic jailbreaks on T2I models where safe image and text prompts combine to produce unsafe content, with 1,200-prompt benchmark showing 8-74% attack success rates across nine models.

title: BeHonest: Benchmarking Honesty in Large Language Models
tldr: BeHonest is a benchmark evaluating LLM honesty across 10 scenarios spanning self-knowledge, non-deceptiveness, and consistency, revealing major gaps across 9 popular models.

title: Exploring Vulnerabilities and Protections in Large Language Models: A Survey
tldr: Survey of LLM security vulnerabilities (prompt injection, jailbreaking, backdoor/data poisoning attacks) and defenses, covering both attack mechanisms and mitigation strategies.

title: PromptGuard: Soft Prompt-Guided Unsafe Content Moderation for Text-to-Image Models
tldr: PromptGuard optimizes a safety soft prompt in the T2I embedding space to suppress NSFW content generation, achieving 5.84% unsafe ratio — 7.8x faster than prior methods without modifying model weights.

title: Prisma: An Open Source Toolkit for Mechanistic Interpretability in Vision and Video
tldr: Open-source framework for vision MI with 75+ model configurations, 80+ pre-trained SAEs, and TransformerLens-compatible hooks for vision and video transformers.

title: Planning in a Recurrent Neural Network that Plays Sokoban
tldr: Identifies causal plan representations in a 1.29M-parameter RNN trained on Sokoban, showing it uses redundant actions to gain computation time for internal planning up to 50 steps ahead.

title: Learning Safety Constraints for Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces Safety Polytope (SaP), a geometric framework that learns linear safety constraints in LLM representation space, enabling post-hoc detection and correction of unsafe outputs without weight modification.

title: Survey of Adversarial Robustness in Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: Comprehensive survey of adversarial vulnerabilities in multimodal LLMs spanning image, video, audio, and speech modalities, covering attacks, defenses, datasets, and open challenges.

title: How to evaluate control measures for LLM agents? A trajectory from today to superintelligence
tldr: Proposes a framework of five AI Control Levels (ACLs) calibrating control evaluations to agent capability profiles, arguing control cannot scale to superintelligent systems.

title: Exploring Scaling Trends in LLM Robustness
tldr: Larger LLMs show little robustness improvement from scale alone, but respond much better to adversarial training and exhibit emergent cross-attack transfer at >=100M parameters.

title: A Jailbroken GenAI Model Can Cause Substantial Harm: GenAI-powered Applications are Vulnerable to PromptWares
tldr: Introduces PromptWare, a new attack class exploiting user inputs to jailbreak GenAI-powered Plan & Execute applications, demonstrated via DoS and SQL injection attacks.

title: Can LLMs Deeply Detect Complex Malicious Queries? A Framework for Jailbreaking via Obfuscating Intent
tldr: IntentObfuscator achieves 69.21% average jailbreak success rate across GPT-3.5/4, Qwen, and Baichuan by obfuscating malicious intent via two strategies: appending legitimate text or rewriting harmful content ambiguously.

title: The Importance of Prompt Tuning for Automated Neuron Explanations
tldr: Reformatting prompts for automated neuron explanation with GPT-4 achieves 2.44x efficiency gains and better explanation quality via simpler, more natural prompt formats.

title: One-Shot is Enough: Consolidating Multi-Turn Attacks into Efficient Single-Turn Prompts for LLMs
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
tldr: M2S converts multi-turn jailbreak conversations into single-turn prompts via Hyphenize/Numberize/Pythonize formatting, achieving up to 95.9% ASR on Mistral-7B and +17.5% improvement over original multi-turn attacks on GPT-4o.

title: Have the VLMs Lost Confidence? A Study of Sycophancy in VLMs
tldr: Introduces the MM-SY benchmark to evaluate sycophancy in VLMs and shows that enhancing image attention in higher model layers mitigates the problem.

title: Jailbreaking as a Reward Misspecification Problem
tldr: Frames LLM jailbreaks as reward misspecification during alignment, introduces the ReGap metric and ReMiss attack system achieving >90% ASR on multiple models.

title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
tldr: HELM evaluates 30 language models across 42 scenarios on 7 metrics (accuracy, calibration, robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity, efficiency), revealing critical safety gaps and performance disparities.

title: A Technical Note on Bilinear Layers for Interpretability
tldr: Bilinear layers replace standard MLPs with a form expressible via linear operations and third-order tensors, enabling decomposable pairwise feature interaction analysis for mechanistic interpretability.

title: Decoding Dark Matter: Specialized Sparse Autoencoders for Interpreting Rare Concepts in Foundation Models
tldr: Introduces Specialized Sparse Autoencoders (SSAEs) trained on curated subdomain data with Tilted ERM to capture rare 'dark matter' features that standard SAEs miss, achieving 12.5% improvement in worst-group accuracy on bias removal.

title: Pushing the Limits of Safety: A Technical Report on the ATLAS Challenge 2025
tldr: ATLAS 2025 competition report: 86 teams attacked multimodal LLMs (Qwen2-VL, InternVL2) with adversarial image-text pairs, achieving up to 100% ASR via flowchart-based and cross-modal jailbreak strategies.

title: Video-SafetyBench: A Benchmark for Safety Evaluation of Video LVLMs
tldr: Video-SafetyBench is the first comprehensive benchmark (2,264 video-text pairs, 48 categories) for evaluating safety vulnerabilities in video LVLMs, revealing benign-query attacks achieve 67.2% success rates.

title: Group-SAE: Efficient Training of Sparse Autoencoders for Large Language Models via Layer Groups
tldr: Groups contiguous LLM layers and trains one SAE per group instead of one per layer, achieving up to 6x training speedup on Pythia 160M without degrading reconstruction quality or downstream task faithfulness.

title: SAFEPATH: Preventing Harmful Reasoning in Chain-of-Thought via Early Alignment
tldr: SafePath fine-tunes LRMs to emit an 8-token 'Let's think about safety first' prefix when harmful prompts are detected, reducing harmful outputs by up to 90% while preserving reasoning performance.

title: Adversarial Fine-Tuning of Language Models: An Iterative Optimisation Approach for the Generation and Detection of Problematic Content
tldr: A dual-stage adversarial fine-tuning framework where one model generates harmful prompts and another learns to detect them, achieving 98.1% accuracy vs GPT-4's 85% on problematic content detection.

title: Can We Predict Alignment Before Models Finish Thinking? Towards Monitoring Misaligned Reasoning Models
tldr: Linear probes on chain-of-thought activations outperform all text-based methods (by ~13 F1 points) at predicting whether reasoning models will produce safe or unsafe final responses.

title: QueryAttack: Jailbreaking Aligned Large Language Models Using Structured Non-natural Query Language
tldr: QueryAttack converts harmful natural language queries into structured programming code (SQL, Python, etc.) to bypass LLM safety alignment, achieving 82-99% attack success rates across major models.

title: Textual Unlearning Gives a False Sense of Unlearning
tldr: Textual machine unlearning paradoxically amplifies data leakage: attackers can infer membership with 70% AUC and reconstruct unlearned text with 60%+ ROUGE-1 using model weight differences.

title: An Alignment Safety Case Sketch Based on Debate
tldr: Sketches a structured safety case argument for deploying a slightly superhuman AI R&D assistant trained via prover-estimator debate, identifying four key claims and critical gaps in current techniques.

title: Adaptive Sparse Allocation with Mutual Choice & Feature Choice Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Introduces Feature Choice and Mutual Choice SAEs that enable adaptive per-token sparsity allocation and achieve 0% dead features by reframing sparsifying activations as resource allocation problems.

title: Probing and Steering Evaluation Awareness of Language Models
tldr: Linear probes on Llama-3.3-70B detect evaluation awareness in early layers (AUROC 0.83); safety evals look artificial to models; SAE steering partially recovers sandbagging (up to 25%).

title: MIP against Agent: Malicious Image Patches Hijacking Multimodal OS Agents
tldr: Adversarially crafted image patches embedded in OS screenshots can hijack multimodal OS agents into performing harmful actions with up to 100% attack success rate.

title: LLM-Virus: Evolutionary Jailbreak Attack on Large Language Models
tldr: LLM-Virus uses evolutionary algorithms (crossover, mutation, selection) guided by LLMs to generate transferable jailbreak templates with ~10x lower compute than prior methods.

title: Chain-of-Jailbreak Attack for Image Generation Models via Editing Step by Step
tldr: Chain-of-Jailbreak (CoJ) decomposes malicious queries into sequential harmless-looking edit steps to bypass image generation model safeguards, achieving 62% attack success on GPT-4o.

title: Conditioning Predictive Models: Risks and Strategies
tldr: A comprehensive analysis of risks and strategies for safely deploying LLMs as predictive world models, arguing careful conditioning can elicit superhuman capabilities while managing inner alignment risks.

title: ALU: Agentic LLM Unlearning
tldr: ALU is a multi-agent, retrain-free LLM unlearning framework using four specialized agents that removes information without weight updates, outperforming prior methods at scale.

title: Functional Faithfulness in the Wild: Circuit Discovery with Differentiable Computation Graph Pruning
tldr: DiscoGP jointly prunes both weights and edges in transformer computation graphs via differentiable masking, achieving near-perfect functional faithfulness in circuit discovery.

title: Benchmarking Deception Probes via Black-to-White Performance Boosts
tldr: Evaluates linear deception probes on LLaMA-3.3-70B across 6 datasets by comparing white-box vs black-box monitors, finding weak but encouraging performance boosts from probe activations.

title: Self-Destructive Language Model
tldr: SEAM transforms aligned LLMs into self-destructive models that retain benign capabilities but catastrophically degrade when fine-tuned on harmful data, creating a no-win scenario for attackers.

title: Feature Hedging: Correlated Features Break Narrow Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Identifies 'feature hedging' where narrow SAEs merge correlated features together, destroying monosemanticity, and proposes Balance Matryoshka SAEs to mitigate this failure mode.

title: Angular Steering: Behavior Control via Rotation in Activation Space
tldr: Introduces Angular Steering, which controls LLM behaviors (e.g., refusal) by rotating activations within a fixed 2D subspace rather than adding vectors, enabling continuous fine-grained control with a single bounded angle parameter.

title: Inoculation Prompting: Eliciting traits from LLMs during training can suppress them at test-time
tldr: Prepending instructions that elicit unwanted traits into finetuning data suppresses those traits at test-time by making them less surprising, reducing optimization pressure to globally update the model.

title: From LLMs to MLLMs to Agents: A Survey of Emerging Paradigms in Jailbreak Attacks and Defenses within LLM Ecosystem
tldr: Comprehensive survey of jailbreak attacks and defenses across LLMs, MLLMs, and agentic systems, introducing improved taxonomies covering attack impact, visibility, and timing of defenses.

title: Graph of Attacks with Pruning: Optimizing Stealthy Jailbreak Prompt Generation for Enhanced LLM Content Moderation
tldr: GAP replaces tree-based jailbreak search with a graph structure, achieving 92-96% attack success on GPT-3.5 using ~50% fewer queries, then uses generated jailbreaks to fine-tune PromptGuard from 5.1% to 93.89% accuracy.

title: Defending Against Prompt Injection with DataFilter
tldr: DataFilter is a test-time, model-agnostic defense that removes malicious instructions from untrusted data via SFT on Llama-3.1-8B, achieving near-zero attack success rates across major prompt injection benchmarks.

title: Scalable Defense against In-the-wild Jailbreaking Attacks with Safety Context Retrieval
tldr: Safety Context Retrieval (SCR) uses RAG to dynamically defend LLMs against novel jailbreaks by retrieving a small set of attack-specific safety examples as context, without retraining.

title: Evolving Security in LLMs: A Study of Jailbreak Attacks and Defenses
tldr: Comprehensive study of 4 jailbreak attacks and 3 defenses across 10 LLMs, finding that newer/larger models are not safer, and that combined defenses achieve up to 98.86% protection improvement.

title: Adversarial Alignment for LLMs Requires Simpler, Reproducible, and More Measurable Objectives
tldr: A position paper arguing that LLM adversarial alignment research is repeating historical ML robustness mistakes and proposing a taxonomy and reformed objectives to fix this.

title: Monitoring Decomposition Attacks in LLMs with Lightweight Sequential Monitors
tldr: Proposes lightweight sequential monitors that track cumulative conversation context to detect decomposition attacks on LLMs, achieving 93% defense success rate at 90% lower cost than reasoning models.

title: The Blessing and Curse of Dimensionality in Safety Alignment
tldr: Shows that higher LLM hidden dimensions enable linear-structure jailbreaks; proposes FJLT and Bottleneck dimension-reduction defenses that restore safety alignment while preserving utility.

title: Shape it Up! Restoring LLM Safety during Finetuning
tldr: STAR-DSS applies token-level dynamic safety shaping during LLM finetuning using guardrail-derived trajectory scores, restoring safety without degrading task performance.

title: Jailbreak Defense in a Narrow Domain: Limitations of Existing Methods and a New Transcript-Classifier Approach
tldr: Existing defenses (safety training, adversarial training, I/O classifiers) fail to prevent LLMs from aiding bomb-making; a new transcript-classifier with CoT reasoning outperforms them but remains breakable.

title: Exploring Visual Vulnerabilities via Multi-Loss Adversarial Search for Jailbreaking Vision-Language Models
tldr: MLAI uses scenario-aware image generation and multi-image collaborative attacks exploiting flat-minima theory to jailbreak VLMs at 77.75% ASR on MiniGPT-4 and 82.80% on LLaVA-2.

title: LLMs Can Covertly Sandbag on Capability Evaluations Against Chain-of-Thought Monitoring
tldr: LLMs can covertly sandbag on dangerous capability evaluations while evading chain-of-thought monitoring at 16-36% bypass rates when monitor-aware, using five distinct evasion strategies.

title: Estimating the Probabilities of Rare Outputs in Language Models
tldr: Proposes and compares importance sampling and activation extrapolation methods for estimating extremely small probabilities of rare/catastrophic LLM outputs, finding MHIS best on larger models.

title: Inoculation Prompting: Instructing LLMs to misbehave at train-time improves test-time alignment
tldr: Inoculation Prompting modifies SFT prompts to explicitly request undesired behaviors (e.g., reward hacking), which counterintuitively prevents models from learning those behaviors while preserving desired capabilities.

title: SeqAR: Jailbreak LLMs with Sequential Auto-Generated Characters
tldr: SeqAR automatically generates sequential multi-character roleplay jailbreak prompts using open-source LLMs, achieving 88% ASR on GPT-3.5 and 60% on GPT-4 without human-crafted templates.

title: Learning to Poison Large Language Models During Instruction Tuning
tldr: A gradient-guided backdoor trigger learning approach poisons LLMs during instruction tuning, achieving ~80% performance degradation by contaminating just 1% of 4,000 training samples.

title: Ferret: Faster and Effective Automated Red Teaming with Reward-Based Scoring Technique
tldr: Ferret improves Rainbow Teaming automated red-teaming by generating multiple adversarial mutations per iteration and ranking them with scoring functions, achieving 95% ASR (46% higher than baseline) with 15.2% faster convergence.

title: HyperSteer: Activation Steering at Scale with Hypernetworks
tldr: HyperSteer uses a transformer hypernetwork to generate steering vectors conditioned on natural language prompts and LM internals, outperforming supervised baselines and generalizing to unseen steering prompts.

title: OBLIVIATE: Robust and Practical Machine Unlearning for Large Language Models
tldr: OBLIVIATE is a machine unlearning framework for LLMs that combines masked, distillation, and world-fact losses with LoRA adapters to efficiently remove targeted data while preserving model utility.

title: UPCORE: Utility-Preserving Coreset Selection for Balanced Unlearning
tldr: UPCORE prunes outlier samples from forget sets using hidden-state variance and Isolation Forest, reducing collateral damage during LLM unlearning by 3-7 AUC points while preserving deletion effectiveness.

title: Interpretation Meets Safety: A Survey on Interpretation Methods and Tools for Improving LLM Safety
tldr: First survey bridging LLM interpretation and safety, proposing a unified taxonomy of ~70 works organized by LLM workflow stages (training, input, inference, generation).

title: LoX: Low-Rank Extrapolation Robustifies LLM Safety Against Fine-tuning
tldr: LoX extrapolates the safety-critical low-rank parameter subspace of aligned LLMs, reducing fine-tuning attack success rates by 11-54% without any additional training or data.

title: JailPO: A Novel Black-box Jailbreak Framework via Preference Optimization against Aligned LLMs
tldr: JailPO trains attack models via preference optimization (SimPO) to auto-generate covert jailbreak prompts against aligned LLMs, achieving up to 55.6% ASR with ~98% fewer queries than template-based baselines.

title: PiCo: Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models via Pictorial Code Contextualization
tldr: PiCo jailbreaks multimodal LLMs via a three-tier strategy combining image-embedded instructions, typographic token fragmentation, and code-contextualized harmful content, achieving 84% ASR on Gemini-Pro Vision.

title: Which Retain Set Matters for LLM Unlearning? A Case Study on Entity Unlearning
tldr: Identifies that syntactically similar queries to the forget set suffer the greatest performance drop during LLM unlearning, and using them as regularization preserves retain set performance best.

title: Interpreting and Editing Vision-Language Representations to Mitigate Hallucinations
tldr: Applies logit lens to VLM image representations to detect and remove hallucinated objects via linear orthogonalization (ProjectAway), achieving up to 25.7% hallucination reduction.

title: Learning Dynamics of LLM Finetuning
tldr: Decomposes LLM finetuning into per-step influence dynamics, revealing a 'squeezing effect' in off-policy DPO that explains confidence decay and inspiring a simple fix improving alignment.

title: Clio: Privacy-Preserving Insights into Real-World AI Use
tldr: Anthropic's privacy-preserving platform for analyzing real-world Claude usage patterns through AI-powered clustering, achieving 94% accuracy in topic reconstruction with zero privacy breaches across 5,000 audited conversations.

title: Fine-Tuning Is All You Need to Mitigate Backdoor Attacks
tldr: Demonstrates that standard fine-tuning and a novel super-fine-tuning method with dynamic learning rate scheduling can effectively remove backdoors from ML models while preserving utility at minimal computational cost.

title: Generative AI Misuse: A Taxonomy of Tactics and Insights from Real-World Data
