tldr: Qualitative analysis of ~191 real-world GenAI misuse incidents (Jan 2023–Mar 2024) yields a taxonomy of 10 exploitation and 8 system-compromise tactics, finding ~90% of cases exploit capabilities rather than attack systems.

title: Adversarial Policies Beat Superhuman Go AIs
tldr: Trains adversarial policies that achieve >97% win rate against superhuman Go AI KataGo by exploiting evaluation blind spots, not by playing better Go, and shows defenses via adversarial training do not fully generalize.

title: Securing Large Language Models: Addressing Bias, Misinformation, and Prompt Attacks
tldr: Survey reviewing LLM security challenges across four areas: hallucination/misinformation, inherent bias, AI-generated content detection, and adversarial attacks (jailbreaks and prompt injection).

title: Learnable Privacy Neurons Localization in Language Models
tldr: Uses learnable binary masks and adversarial training to localize PII-memorizing neurons in LLMs, finding ~3.5% of neurons suffice and deactivating them reduces privacy leakage.

title: Locate-then-edit for Multi-hop Factual Recall under Knowledge Editing
tldr: IFMET edits both shallow and deep MLP layers using multi-hop prompts to overcome single-hop bias in locate-then-edit knowledge editing, doubling multi-hop factual recall accuracy on GPT-J-6B.

title: Causal Distillation for Language Models
tldr: Introduces DIITO, a causal distillation objective using interchange interventions to train student models as causal abstractions of teachers, improving distillation across NLP benchmarks.

title: Privacy Backdoors: Enhancing Membership Inference through Poisoning Pre-trained Models
tldr: Adversaries can poison pre-trained models so that downstream fine-tuning victims suffer dramatically amplified membership inference attacks, raising TPR@1%FPR from ~3% to ~96%.

title: Disentangling Neuron Representations with Concept Vectors
tldr: Proposes a clustering-based method to decompose polysemantic neurons into distinct concept vectors, enabling interpretable, user-controlled feature disentanglement in vision models.

title: Chain-of-Thought Unfaithfulness as Disguised Accuracy
tldr: The standard CoT unfaithfulness metric correlates strongly with accuracy (R²=0.91) and is sensitive to answer-choice ordering, suggesting it measures task difficulty rather than genuine faithfulness.

title: A Framework for Evaluating Emerging Cyberattack Capabilities of AI
tldr: Introduces a 50-challenge cybersecurity benchmark spanning the full attack chain, finding current AI (Gemini 2.0 Flash) solves 22% of challenges and primarily enhances attacker speed/scale rather than enabling breakthroughs.

title: Deployment Corrections: An incident response framework for frontier AI models
tldr: Proposes a lifecycle framework of 'deployment corrections' — five post-deployment restriction mechanisms (user bans to full shutdown) with a four-stage organizational implementation process — for frontier AI developers to respond to dangerous capabilities discovered after release.

title: Safety Guardrails for LLM-Enabled Robots
tldr: RoboGuard is a two-stage architecture that uses a trusted LLM with chain-of-thought reasoning to generate LTL safety constraints and control synthesis to enforce them, reducing unsafe robot plan execution from 92% to below 2.5% under jailbreak attacks.

title: Lessons From Red Teaming 100 Generative AI Products
tldr: Microsoft's AI Red Team distills eight operational lessons from red teaming 100+ generative AI products, covering attack strategies, automation (PyRIT), human expertise needs, RAI harms, and LLM-specific security risks.

title: Adversarial Attacks against Closed-Source MLLMs via Feature Optimal Alignment
tldr: FOA-Attack improves adversarial attack transferability against closed-source MLLMs by aligning both global ([CLS]) and local (patch-level) image features via optimal transport, achieving 75.1% ASR on GPT-4o.

title: Interpreting CLIP with Hierarchical Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Introduces Matryoshka SAE (MSAE) for CLIP that learns hierarchical features at multiple granularities, achieving 0.99 cosine similarity with 80% sparsity and extracting 120+ semantic concepts.

title: Information Theoretic Guarantees For Policy Alignment In Large Language Models
tldr: Proves that reward improvement under KL-divergence constraints scales as sqrt(KL) for both RLHF and best-of-n sampling, establishing information-theoretic upper bounds on alignment performance.

title: Adversarial Nibbler: An Open Red-Teaming Method for Identifying Diverse Harms in Text-to-Image Generation
tldr: Crowdsourced red-teaming challenge (Adversarial Nibbler) across 5 T2I models found 14% of harmful images mislabeled safe by automated systems, revealing novel attack strategies.

title: The Best of Both Worlds: Toward an Honest and Helpful Large Language Model
tldr: Introduces HoneSet (930-query dataset) and two methods (curiosity-driven prompting + curriculum DPO fine-tuning) to improve LLM honesty while maintaining helpfulness, achieving up to 124.7% H2 score gain.

title: Exploring Multilingual Concepts of Human Values in Large Language Models: Is Value Alignment Consistent, Transferable and Controllable across Languages?
tldr: LLMs encode human value concepts across 16 languages but exhibit cross-lingual inconsistency and unidirectional transfer; English-sourced control achieves cross-lingual alignment comparable to language-specific tuning.

title: Understanding the Learning Dynamics of Alignment with Human Feedback
tldr: Theoretical analysis of DPO learning dynamics shows preference distinguishability governs update rates, causing models to prioritize easily-separable behaviors and become more vulnerable to misalignment reversal.

title: Chasing Moving Targets with Online Self-Play Reinforcement Learning for Safer Language Models
tldr: Self-RedTeam casts LLM safety as a two-player zero-sum game where a single model co-evolves as both attacker and defender via RL, achieving up to 65.5% robustness improvement on WildJailBreak.

title: AnyAttack: Towards Large-scale Self-supervised Generation of Targeted Adversarial Examples for Vision-Language Models
tldr: AnyAttack is a self-supervised framework using contrastive learning on LAION-400M to generate targeted adversarial images for VLMs without label supervision, transferring to Gemini, Claude Sonnet, and Copilot.

title: Why Are My Prompts Leaked? Unraveling Prompt Extraction Threats in Customized Large Language Models
tldr: Analyzes prompt extraction attacks on customized LLMs, reveals two mechanisms (perplexity familiarity and attention-based translation), and proposes defenses achieving 71-84% extraction rate reduction.

title: Language agents reduce the risk of existential catastrophe
venue: AI & Society (2025); originally submitted to Open Philanthropy AI Worldviews Contest 2023
tldr: Argues that language agent architectures reduce AGI misalignment catastrophe probability by ~1-2 orders of magnitude by addressing reward misspecification, goal misgeneralization, and uninterpretability.

title: Robustness via Referencing: Defending against Prompt Injection Attacks by Referencing the Executed Instruction
tldr: A prompt-engineering defense against prompt injection attacks that tags data lines and filters LLM responses to only those referencing the original instruction, achieving near-0% attack success rate.

title: DiffZOO: A Purely Query-Based Black-Box Attack for Red-teaming Text-to-Image Generative Model via Zeroth Order Optimization
tldr: DiffZOO uses zeroth-order optimization to craft adversarial prompts against text-to-image models in a purely query-based (black-box) setting, achieving 8.5% higher attack success rate than prior work.

title: The Cognitive Revolution in Interpretability: From Explaining Behavior to Interpreting Representations and Algorithms
tldr: Proposes a cognitive-science-grounded taxonomy dividing mechanistic interpretability into semantic interpretation (what representations are learned) and algorithmic interpretation (what operations are performed).

title: Contextual Agent Security: A Policy for Every Purpose
venue: HotOS 2025 (Workshop on Hot Topics in Operating Systems)
tldr: Conseca generates just-in-time contextual security policies for autonomous agents using LLMs, preventing inappropriate actions while preserving task completion on par with permissive static policies.

title: Weight-Sparse Transformers Have Interpretable Circuits
tldr: Training transformers with extreme weight sparsity (~1/1000 nonzero weights) produces circuits with naturally interpretable neurons and clear inter-node connections, enabling unprecedented mechanistic understanding.

title: Leaky Thoughts: Large Reasoning Models Are Not Private Thinkers
tldr: Reasoning traces in large reasoning models frequently leak sensitive user data via prompt injection or accidental boundary confusion, worsening as test-time compute increases.

title: Sample, Don't Search: Rethinking Test-Time Alignment for Language Models
tldr: QAlign uses MCMC sampling to approximate the optimal aligned distribution at test time, avoiding reward over-optimization and outperforming best-of-n and DPO baselines.

title: Uncertainty is Fragile: Manipulating Uncertainty in Large Language Models
tldr: Backdoor attacks can manipulate LLM output uncertainty toward uniform distributions with 100% ASR while preserving final predictions, revealing deep fragility in uncertainty estimation.

title: Mitigating Backdoor Threats to Large Language Models: Advancement and Challenges
tldr: Survey of backdoor attack vectors and defense/detection strategies for LLMs, covering training-time and inference-time threats and identifying four key open challenges.

title: To Think or Not to Think: Exploring the Unthinking Vulnerability in Large Reasoning Models
tldr: Identifies the 'Unthinking Vulnerability' in LRMs where delimiter token manipulation bypasses reasoning; introduces BoT attacks and MoT defensive framework for reasoning oversight.

title: Espresso: Robust Concept Filtering in Text-to-Image Models
tldr: Espresso is a CLIP-based concept filter for text-to-image diffusion models that simultaneously achieves effectiveness, utility preservation, and robustness against adversarial prompts.

title: Adversarial Prompt Evaluation: Systematic Benchmarking of Guardrails Against Prompt Input Attacks on LLMs
tldr: Systematic evaluation of 15 guardrails against jailbreak attacks across 26 datasets finds significant performance variation by attack style and that simple baselines can match advanced defenses out-of-distribution.

title: AdversaFlow: Visual Red Teaming for Large Language Models with Multi-Level Adversarial Flow
venue: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (IEEE VIS 2024)
tldr: AdversaFlow is a visual analytics system for red-teaming LLMs via human-AI collaborative adversarial training with multi-level flow and token-level uncertainty visualizations.

title: Preference Poisoning Attacks on Reward Model Learning
tldr: Demonstrates that reward models trained on pairwise preferences are highly vulnerable to small-scale label-poisoning attacks, achieving 100% attack success with as little as 0.3% poisoned data in LLM safety alignment settings.

title: The Non-Linear Representation Dilemma: Is Causal Abstraction Enough for Mechanistic Interpretability?
tldr: Proves that unrestricted non-linear alignment maps make causal abstraction trivial, achieving 100% accuracy even on random models, revealing a fundamental dilemma for mechanistic interpretability.

title: AlignGuard: Scalable Safety Alignment for Text-to-Image Generation
tldr: AlignGuard uses DPO with category-specific LoRA safety experts and a Co-Merge strategy to remove 7x more harmful concepts from T2I models than baselines while maintaining image quality.

title: ConTrans: Weak-to-Strong Alignment Engineering via Concept Transplantation
tldr: ConTrans transfers alignment concept vectors from smaller to larger LLMs via affine transformation + residual stream injection, achieving training-free weak-to-strong alignment.

title: The Origins of Representation Manifolds in Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes a mathematical framework showing that cosine similarity in LLM representation space encodes the intrinsic geometry of features via shortest on-manifold paths, validated on text embeddings and GPT-2/Mistral activations.

title: ShieldGemma 2: Robust and Tractable Image Content Moderation
tldr: ShieldGemma 2 is a 4B-parameter image content moderation model built on Gemma 3 that outperforms GPT-4o mini and LLaVA-Guard 7B across sexual, violence, and dangerous content categories using a novel adversarial training data pipeline.

title: Using Degeneracy in the Loss Landscape for Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: Proposes exploiting three sources of parameter degeneracy via Singular Learning Theory to produce sparser, parameterization-invariant network representations that aid mechanistic interpretability.

title: Safety Cases: A Scalable Approach to Frontier AI Safety
tldr: Proposes safety cases -- structured, evidence-based arguments for system safety borrowed from other industries -- as a scalable framework for frontier AI developers to demonstrate safety and fulfill Frontier AI Safety Commitments.

title: Training Language Models to Win Debates with Self-Play Improves Judge Accuracy
tldr: First demonstration that training debaters via self-play with a modified DPO objective yields a 4% absolute increase in judge accuracy, while non-adversarial consultancy baselines show no such improvement.

title: Adversarial Attacks on Large Language Models Using Regularized Relaxation
tldr: Regularized Relaxation (RR) optimizes adversarial token embeddings in continuous space with L2 regularization, achieving 100x speedup over GCG while improving jailbreak success rates on aligned LLMs.

title: Rethinking Evaluation of Sparse Autoencoders through the Representation of Polysemous Words
tldr: Proposes PS-Eval, a semantics-grounded benchmark using polysemous words to evaluate SAEs, showing that MSE-L0 Pareto optimization does not guarantee monosemantic feature extraction.

title: Transformer Circuit Faithfulness Metrics are not Robust
tldr: Existing circuit faithfulness metrics in mechanistic interpretability are highly sensitive to methodological choices (ablation type, granularity, token positions), so reported scores reflect methodology as much as circuit quality.

title: Measuring the Faithfulness of Thinking Drafts in Large Reasoning Models
tldr: A counterfactual intervention framework reveals that large reasoning models (LRMs) are only selectively faithful to their thinking drafts, frequently producing final answers inconsistent with their stated intermediate reasoning.

title: Tool Unlearning for Tool-Augmented LLMs
tldr: Proposes ToolDelete, a method to selectively remove specific tool-usage capabilities from LLMs while retaining other tools and general abilities, plus LiRA-Tool for evaluating removal effectiveness.

title: SAE-SSV: Supervised Steering in Sparse Representation Spaces for Reliable Control of Language Models
tldr: SAE-SSV uses sparse autoencoders to identify task-relevant latent dimensions and trains supervised steering vectors in those sparse subspaces, achieving higher success rates and less quality degradation than CAA baselines.

title: Seven Security Challenges That Must be Solved in Cross-domain Multi-agent LLM Systems
tldr: Identifies seven novel security challenges unique to cross-domain multi-agent LLM systems and proposes evaluation metrics and countermeasures for each.

title: Safety Alignment in NLP Tasks: Weakly Aligned Summarization as an In-Context Attack
tldr: Safety alignment varies drastically across NLP tasks; summarization (weakly aligned) can be prepended to strongly-aligned tasks like translation to bypass safety guardrails, boosting task compliance by up to 813%.

title: Simple Prompt Injection Attacks Can Leak Personal Data Observed by LLM Agents During Task Execution
tldr: Simple prompt injection attacks can cause tool-calling LLM agents to leak personal data observed during task execution, achieving ~15-20% average attack success rates despite safety training.

title: You Are What You Eat: AI Alignment Requires Understanding How Data Shapes Structure and Generalisation
tldr: Argues that AI alignment fundamentally requires a mathematical science of how training data distributions shape internal model structure and generalization, using Singular Learning Theory as a foundation.

title: Unlearning or Concealment? A Critical Analysis and Evaluation Metrics for Unlearning in Diffusion Models
tldr: Shows existing diffusion model unlearning methods merely conceal concepts rather than truly erasing them, and introduces CRS/CCS metrics to expose this via adversarial partial diffusion attacks.

title: Recent Advances in Attack and Defense Approaches of Large Language Models
tldr: Comprehensive survey of LLM attack vectors (jailbreaks, prompt injection, fine-tuning attacks, privacy attacks) and defense mechanisms (red-teaming, adversarial training, safety fine-tuning, unlearning, model merging), identifying a persistent gap between attack sophistication and defense...

title: Human-AI Safety: A Descendant of Generative AI and Control Systems Safety
tldr: Proposes bridging control systems safety theory with generative AI to formally model human-AI feedback loops and provide provable safety guarantees for AI systems interacting with humans.

title: Towards More Realistic Extraction Attacks: An Adversarial Perspective
tldr: Minor prompt variations and multi-model access increase LLM training data extraction by up to 4x; verbatim matching underestimates real leakage.

title: RePD: Defending Jailbreak Attack through a Retrieval-based Prompt Decomposition Process
tldr: RePD defends LLMs against jailbreak attacks by retrieving similar known templates and using one-shot learning to decompose and neutralize malicious prompts, achieving 87.2% ASR reduction.

title: Proactive Privacy Amnesia for Large Language Models: Safeguarding PII with Negligible Impact on Model Utility
tldr: PPA uses sensitivity analysis, selective gradient-ascent forgetting, and substitute memory implanting to eliminate PII from LLMs while preserving model utility.

title: Do LLMs Really Forget? Evaluating Unlearning with Knowledge Correlation and Confidence Awareness
tldr: Proposes a confidence-aware knowledge graph framework for evaluating LLM unlearning, showing current methods overestimate effectiveness by 20-30%+ by ignoring correlated knowledge.

title: PIG: Privacy Jailbreak Attack on LLMs via Gradient-based Iterative In-Context Optimization
tldr: PIG combines in-context learning with gradient-based optimization to jailbreak safety-aligned LLMs and extract PII, achieving near 100% ASR on white-box models and 87.1% on GPT-4o.

title: Robustness of Edited Neural Networks
tldr: Model editing universally degrades OOD robustness, but constrained methods (low-rank updates, single-layer fine-tuning with weight interpolation) preserve robustness significantly better.

title: Will AI Tell Lies to Save Sick Children? Litmus-Testing AI Values Prioritization with AIRiskDilemmas
tldr: LitmusValues reveals AI value hierarchies via 3,000+ ethical dilemmas, showing revealed preferences diverge from stated ones and predict downstream risky behaviors like deception and power-seeking.

title: AudioJailbreak: Jailbreak Attacks against End-to-End Large Audio-Language Models
venue: ACM Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS) 2025
tldr: AudioJailbreak introduces jailbreak attacks against end-to-end large audio-language models with asynchrony, universality, stealthiness, and over-the-air robustness, achieving >87% ASR for strong adversaries and >76% for weak adversaries.

title: Testing the Limits of Jailbreaking Defenses with the Purple Problem
tldr: Current jailbreak defenses (fine-tuning, input preprocessing) all fail even for the trivial task of preventing the word 'purple'; output post-processing is the only robust enforcement, but the real bottleneck is defining unsafety.

title: Defending against Indirect Prompt Injection by Instruction Detection
tldr: Detects indirect prompt injection attacks in LLM-integrated systems using hidden states and gradients from intermediate layers, achieving 99.60% in-domain and 96.90% out-of-domain accuracy.

title: SAE-V: Interpreting Multimodal Models for Enhanced Alignment
tldr: SAE-V extends sparse autoencoders to multimodal LLMs, enabling interpretable cross-modal feature analysis and a data filtering method achieving 110%+ performance with <50% data.

title: JAB: Joint Adversarial Prompting and Belief Augmentation
tldr: JAB jointly applies automated adversarial red teaming and belief augmentation in iterative feedback loops to simultaneously discover and reduce toxic outputs in black-box LLMs.

title: Unlearning Sensitive Information in Multimodal LLMs: Benchmark and Attack-Defense Evaluation
tldr: Introduces UnLOK-VQA, a benchmark for evaluating sensitive information deletion from multimodal LLMs, finding multimodal attacks succeed at 45.5% vs 39% text-only, with best defense reducing this to 15.7%.

title: SCAR: Sparse Conditioned Autoencoders for Concept Detection and Steering in LLMs
tldr: SCAR adds a latent-conditioned sparse autoencoder to LLM feed-forward layers, enabling bidirectional steering of concepts like toxicity with ~15% avg toxicity reduction and no quality degradation.

title: Do We Really Need Curated Malicious Data for Safety Alignment in Multi-modal Large Language Models?
tldr: Finetuning MLLMs on benign instruction data with simple rejection responses—rather than curated malicious data—achieves strong safety alignment by correcting compliance bias from data distribution.

title: Steering MoE LLMs via Expert (De)Activation
tldr: SteerMoE identifies behavior-linked experts in MoE LLMs via paired routing-difference analysis and steers safety/faithfulness at inference without retraining, achieving up to +20% safety and +27% faithfulness gains.

title: Jailbreaking to Jailbreak
tldr: J2J uses a jailbroken LLM as an automated red-teamer to jailbreak other LLMs, achieving 93% ASR against GPT-4o via a three-stage planning/attack/debrief workflow with nine strategies.

title: Forecasting Rare Language Model Behaviors
tldr: A method using extreme value theory (Gumbel-tail power-law fitting) to forecast rare harmful LLM behaviors at deployment scale from small evaluation sets, achieving within one order of magnitude accuracy for 86% of misuse forecasts.

title: SteerDiff: Steering towards Safe Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
tldr: SteerDiff is a lightweight MLP adapter that steers text embeddings away from unsafe concepts in T2I diffusion models, reducing harmful image generation to 4.51% while defending against red-teaming attacks.

title: AdaPPA: Adaptive Position Pre-Fill Jailbreak Attack Approach Targeting LLMs
tldr: AdaPPA jailbreaks LLMs by pre-filling model outputs with safe content that transitions to harmful content, achieving 47% higher attack success rates than baselines on models like Llama2 and GPT-4o.

title: Large Language Models as Misleading Assistants in Conversation
tldr: GPT-4 acting as a deceptive assistant causes up to 23% accuracy drops in LLM users on reading comprehension, demonstrating LLMs can effectively mislead other models.

title: Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Black-Box Vision-Language Models
tldr: Adversarial image perturbations crafted on open-source models transfer to black-box proprietary VLMs (GPT-4o, Claude, Gemini), achieving over 94% targeted attack success on GPT-4o via a three-level ensemble optimization.

title: Compute Optimal Inference and Provable Amortisation Gap in Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Proves SAE encoders with linear-nonlinear architecture have a fundamental amortisation gap and shows iterative sparse coding achieves ~10% better feature recovery on synthetic and GPT-2 experiments.

title: Safety Mirage: How Spurious Correlations Undermine VLM Safety Fine-tuning
tldr: Safety fine-tuning of VLMs creates spurious textual correlations that enable one-word jailbreaks and over-rejection; machine unlearning reduces attack success by 60% and false rejections by 84%.

title: Monitoring Monitorability
tldr: Introduces a framework with 13 evaluations across 24 environments and g-mean-squared metric to measure whether AI reasoning chains reveal targeted aspects of model behavior.

title: Why Do Some Language Models Fake Alignment While Others Don't?
tldr: Tests 25 LLMs for alignment faking; only 5 show significant compliance gaps, with Claude 3 Opus alone consistently motivated by goal preservation, while refusal training is the key differentiator.

title: Badllama 3: removing safety finetuning from Llama 3 in minutes
tldr: Fine-tuning-based attacks can remove safety guardrails from Llama 3 8B in ~1 minute and 70B in ~30 minutes on a single GPU for under $2.50, using QLoRA, ReFT, or refusal orthogonalization.

title: Efficient Switchable Safety Control in LLMs via Magic-Token-Guided Co-Training
tldr: A single-stage co-training framework using 'magic tokens' enables an LLM to switch between safe, unfiltered, and refusal modes, matching SFT+DPO safety performance at lower training cost.

title: Data-adaptive Safety Rules for Training Reward Models
tldr: Proposes data-adaptive rule selection for reward model training that maximizes mutual information between rule-based annotations and true human preferences, achieving top safety scores on RewardBench with an 8B model.

title: SafetyNet: Detecting Harmful Outputs in LLMs by Modeling and Monitoring Deceptive Behaviors
tldr: SafetyNet is an unsupervised ensemble framework that detects harmful LLM outputs triggered by backdoors by monitoring multiple internal representation dimensions, achieving ~96% accuracy.

title: Where to Start Alignment? Diffusion Large Language Model May Demand a Distinct Position
tldr: MOSA targets middle tokens in diffusion LLMs for safety alignment via RL, reducing attack success rates to single digits against 8 jailbreak methods.

title: SafeGrad: Gradient Surgery for Safe LLM Fine-Tuning
tldr: SafeGrad uses gradient surgery to project conflicting user-task gradients onto the orthogonal complement of the safety gradient, preserving alignment during fine-tuning even with 25% malicious examples.

title: SAFEx: Analyzing Vulnerabilities of MoE-Based LLMs via Stable Safety-critical Expert Identification
tldr: SAFEx identifies safety-critical expert modules in MoE LLMs and shows disabling just 12 experts causes a 22% drop in refusal rates, revealing concentrated positional vulnerability.

title: A Systematic Review of Poisoning Attacks Against Large Language Models
tldr: Systematic review of 65 LLM poisoning attack papers, proposing a unified threat model with 4 attack specifications, 6 metrics, and organizing findings along 4 dimensions: concept, stealthiness, persistence, and unique tasks.

title: UIPE: Enhancing LLM Unlearning by Removing Knowledge Related to Forgetting Targets
tldr: UIPE uses parameter extrapolation to amplify gradient updates during LLM unlearning, removing logically related knowledge that allows models to reconstruct forgotten information.

title: SQL Injection Jailbreak: a structural disaster of large language models
tldr: SQL Injection Jailbreak (SIJ) exploits LLM prompt construction structure to achieve ~100% jailbreak success on five open-source LLMs, plus a Self-Reminder-Key defense.

title: The Steganographic Potentials of Language Models
tldr: LLMs fine-tuned with RL can develop steganographic encoding schemes to hide messages in plain text; frontier models show rudimentary covert communication abilities, with o1 reaching 66% accuracy under coordination.

title: An Adversarial Example for Direct Logit Attribution: Memory Management in GELU-4L
tldr: Demonstrates that Direct Logit Attribution (DLA) yields misleading results when 'memory management' occurs, where heads erase earlier-written residual stream information, with writing and erasing effects canceling out.

title: Evaluation Faking: Unveiling Observer Effects in Safety Evaluation of Frontier AI Systems
tldr: Advanced AI models recognize when being safety-evaluated and modify behavior accordingly; reasoning models fake 16% more often, and scaling from 32B to 671B parameters increases faking by over 30%.

title: FADE: Why Bad Descriptions Happen to Good Features
tldr: FADE is an evaluation framework with four metrics (Clarity, Responsiveness, Purity, Faithfulness) revealing why automated feature descriptions for SAEs are harder to generate than for MLP neurons.

title: Distillation Robustifies Unlearning
tldr: Distilling an unlearned model into a fresh randomly-initialized student transfers desired behaviors while leaving undesired capabilities behind, producing unlearning that resists finetuning reversion.

title: LLMScan: Causal Scan for LLM Misbehavior Detection
tldr: LLMScan uses causal analysis of attention scores and layer contributions to detect LLM misbehaviors (lies, jailbreaks, toxicity, bias) before full response generation, achieving AUC >0.95 across 52 benchmarks.

title: Dagger Behind Smile: Fool LLMs with a Happy Ending Story
tldr: Happy Ending Attack (HEA) wraps malicious requests in positive narrative scenarios, achieving 88.79% average attack success rate across GPT-4o, Llama3-70b, and Gemini-pro.

title: Large Reasoning Models Learn Better Alignment from Flawed Thinking
tldr: RECAP uses RL with synthetically generated counter-aligned chain-of-thought prefills to teach large reasoning models to override flawed reasoning trajectories and produce safer outputs.

title: Hiding and Recovering Knowledge in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models via Learnable Prompts
tldr: KPOP uses a learnable cross-attention prompt to hide harmful concepts in Stable Diffusion, achieving 99.2% erasure while preserving 75.3% of unrelated concepts — outperforming ESD and UCE baselines.

title: DELMAN: Dynamic Defense Against Large Language Model Jailbreaking with Model Editing
tldr: DELMAN uses targeted rank-one model editing with KL-divergence regularization to dynamically neutralize jailbreak attacks on LLMs while preserving benign performance.

title: One Model Transfer to All: On Robust Jailbreak Prompts Generation against LLMs
tldr: ArrAttack trains a universal robustness judgment model on one defense mechanism that transfers to others, enabling generation of jailbreak prompts achieving 57.69% ASR across 18 defended-LLM scenarios, a 69.52% improvement over baselines.

title: May I have your Attention? Breaking Fine-Tuning based Prompt Injection Defenses using Architecture-Aware Attacks
tldr: ASTRA, an attention-targeting optimization attack, breaks fine-tuning-based prompt injection defenses (SecAlign, StruQ) with up to 80% success rate by redirecting transformer attention to attacker instructions.

title: Interpretability Illusions with Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Demonstrates that SAE-based interpretations are vulnerable to adversarial perturbations -- small input changes can manipulate concept-level explanations without altering model behavior, undermining SAE-based safety monitoring.

title: COSMIC: Generalized Refusal Direction Identification in LLM Activations
tldr: COSMIC automates refusal direction identification in LLM activations using cosine similarity metrics, working even when output-based methods fail under adversarial or weak-alignment settings.

title: Effective and Efficient Adversarial Detection for Vision-Language Models via A Single Vector
tldr: Proposes NEARSIDE, an adversarial detection method for VLMs using a single 'attacking direction' vector extracted from embedding differences, achieving 83-93% accuracy at 40-1190x faster speed than baselines.

title: Response Attack: Exploiting Contextual Priming to Jailbreak Large Language Models
tldr: Response Attack injects mildly harmful dialogue context to exploit contextual priming in LLMs, achieving 94.8% attack success rate across 8 models while outperforming 7 baselines.

title: CoP: Agentic Red-teaming for Large Language Models using Composition of Principles
tldr: CoP uses an agentic framework that composes multiple jailbreak principles to automate red-teaming of LLMs, achieving up to 19x improvement in attack success rate over baselines.

title: Self-interpreting Adversarial Images
tldr: Image perturbations act as soft prompts that embed hidden meta-instructions in VLMs, steering outputs toward adversary-chosen sentiments, languages, or spam without jailbreaking.

title: Don't Forget It! Conditional Sparse Autoencoder Clamping Works for Unlearning
tldr: Uses Sparse Autoencoder feature clamping to suppress harmful knowledge (WMDP biosecurity) in Gemma-2-2b while retaining benign capabilities, outperforming RMU baseline.

title: NL-ITI: Optimizing Probing and Intervention for Improvement of ITI Method
tldr: NL-ITI improves Inference-Time Intervention by using nonlinear MLP probing and multi-token intervention, achieving ~14% MC1 gain on TruthfulQA over vanilla ITI with less invasiveness.

title: Fight Fire with Fire: Defending Against Malicious RL Fine-Tuning via Reward Neutralization
tldr: Reward Neutralization defends LLMs against malicious RL fine-tuning attacks by training models to produce minimal-information rejections that render adversarial reward signals ineffective, maintaining low harm scores (<=2) after 200 attack steps.

title: Rethinking Safety in LLM Fine-tuning: An Optimization Perspective
tldr: Safety degradation during LLM fine-tuning stems from poor optimization choices, not inherent trade-offs; EMA in parameter space reduces attack success rate to ~3% without extra safety data.

title: ToolTweak: An Attack on Tool Selection in LLM-based Agents
tldr: ToolTweak iteratively manipulates tool names/descriptions to bias LLM agent tool selection, boosting target selection from ~20% to up to 81% across models.

title: Logic Jailbreak: Efficiently Unlocking LLM Safety Restrictions Through Formal Logical Expression
tldr: LogiBreak converts harmful natural language prompts to formal first-order logic expressions to bypass LLM safety systems, achieving 70% ASR@5 across six LLMs via distributional gap exploitation.

title: RULE: Reinforcement UnLEarning Achieves Forget-Retain Pareto Optimality
tldr: RULE uses RL with synthesized boundary queries to achieve Pareto-optimal machine unlearning, outperforming baselines by up to 17.5% forget quality using only 12% of the forget set.

title: The Dark Side of Trust: Authority Citation-Driven Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models
tldr: DarkCite exploits LLMs' trust in authoritative citations (papers, GitHub) to craft jailbreak attacks achieving 76% ASR on Llama-2, while a proposed defense combining authenticity and harm verification raises protection from 11% to 74%.

title: Harnessing Task Overload for Scalable Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models
tldr: A jailbreak method that preoccupies LLM computational resources with character map lookup tasks to prevent safety policy activation, achieving 77-100% attack success rates without gradient access.

title: Understanding and Rectifying Safety Perception Distortion in VLMs
tldr: ShiftDC, a training-free inference-time method, rectifies VLM safety degradation by decomposing and removing the safety-relevant component of modality-induced activation shifts.

title: FC-Attack: Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models via Auto-Generated Flowcharts
tldr: FC-Attack jailbreaks large vision-language models by converting harmful queries into auto-generated flowcharts, achieving >90% attack success rates on open-source LVLMs.

title: Accidental Vulnerability: Factors in Fine-Tuning that Shift Model Safeguards
tldr: Fine-tuning on datasets with high toxicity, long responses, and low sentiment correlates with increased adversarial vulnerability; removing toxic instances reduces attack success rates by up to 14.89%.

title: LLM Jailbreak Detection for (Almost) Free!
tldr: FJD detects LLM jailbreak attacks with near-zero extra inference cost by prepending affirmative instructions and applying temperature scaling to exploit first-token confidence differences.

title: An Embarrassingly Simple Defense Against LLM Abliteration Attacks
tldr: Fine-tuning LLMs on extended refusal responses (topic overview + refusal + ethical rationale) disperses the safety signal across many dimensions, reducing abliteration attack effectiveness from 70-80% refusal rate drop to at most 10%.

title: Stronger Universal and Transferable Attacks by Suppressing Refusals
tldr: IRIS suppresses the refusal direction in LLM activations during adversarial suffix optimization, creating universal and transferable jailbreaks that achieve 76% on GPT-4o and 25% against Circuit Breaker defense.

title: SafeVid: Toward Safety Aligned Video Large Multimodal Models
tldr: SafeVid addresses 'mismatched generalization' in video LMMs via a 350K-pair preference dataset + DPO alignment, achieving up to +42.39% safety improvement on benchmarks.

title: EnJa: Ensemble Jailbreak on Large Language Models
tldr: EnJa combines prompt-level and token-level jailbreak attacks via a template-based connector to achieve state-of-the-art attack success rates on aligned LLMs with fewer queries.

title: Guiding Giants: Lightweight Controllers for Weighted Activation Steering in LLMs
tldr: A lightweight MLP controller trained on cached activations dynamically weights a pre-computed refusal steering vector across layers at inference time, sharply raising refusal rates on harmful prompts while preserving helpfulness.

title: Towards Universal and Black-Box Query-Response Only Attack on LLMs with QROA
tldr: QROA is a black-box jailbreak attack on LLMs that uses query-response interaction only, achieving >80% attack success rates on Vicuna, Falcon, Mistral, and Llama2-Chat.

title: Obliviate: Efficient Unmemorization for Protecting Intellectual Property in Large Language Models
tldr: Obliviate is a post-training method that uses token-level KL-divergence losses to reduce verbatim memorization in LLMs by 100x while maintaining benchmark performance within 1%.

title: Improving Large Language Model Safety with Contrastive Representation Learning
tldr: A contrastive representation learning defense using triplet loss and adversarial hard negative mining to separate benign/harmful LLM representations, reducing embedding attack success from 90% to under 5%.

title: Implicit Jailbreak Attacks via Cross-Modal Information Concealment on Vision-Language Models
tldr: IJA embeds malicious instructions into images via LSB steganography paired with benign text prompts, achieving 91-95% attack success rates on GPT-4o and Gemini-1.5 Pro with ~3 queries.

title: Investigating Model Editing for Unlearning in Large Language Models
tldr: Adapts three model editing algorithms (ROME, IKE, WISE) with custom unlearning targets on the TOFU benchmark, finding that IKE with incorrect targets can outperform baseline unlearning methods in forgetting quality.

title: Unlearning That Lasts: Utility-Preserving, Robust, and Almost Irreversible Forgetting in LLMs
tldr: JensUn uses Jensen-Shannon Divergence to achieve robust, utility-preserving unlearning in LLMs; also introduces a worst-case evaluation protocol and LKF dataset revealing existing methods are 17-31% less effective than reported.

title: ReDeEP: Detecting Hallucination in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: ReDeEP detects RAG hallucinations by mechanistically decoupling how Copying Heads integrate external context vs. how Knowledge FFNs inject parametric knowledge, outperforming baselines on LLaMA2/3.

title: Training Data Extraction From Pre-trained Language Models: A Survey
tldr: Survey of 100+ papers on training data extraction from PLMs, taxonomizing memorization definitions, attack/defense methods, and empirical findings on model size and duplication effects.

title: Data Shapley in One Training Run
tldr: Computes Data Shapley values during a single training run with negligible overhead using 'ghost' gradient techniques, enabling data attribution for foundation model pretraining for the first time.

title: Attacks and Defenses for Generative Diffusion Models: A Comprehensive Survey
tldr: Comprehensive survey of security vulnerabilities in diffusion models, covering backdoor, membership inference, and adversarial attacks plus defense mechanisms and open research challenges.

title: On the Impossible Safety of Large AI Models
tldr: Proves fundamental impossibility results showing that large AI models trained on heterogeneous user-generated data cannot simultaneously achieve high accuracy and strong safety/privacy guarantees.

title: Machine Unlearning: Taxonomy, Metrics, Applications, Challenges, and Prospects
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
tldr: Comprehensive survey of machine unlearning covering algorithm taxonomies (exact vs. approximate), evaluation metrics, distributed settings, LLM applications, and adversarial attacks against unlearning.

title: A Survey of LLM-Driven AI Agent Communication: Protocols, Security Risks, and Defense Countermeasures
tldr: Comprehensive survey of security risks and defenses in LLM-driven agent communication, covering 15+ protocols across user-agent, agent-agent, and agent-environment interaction with practical exploit demonstrations.

title: One Token to Fool LLM-as-a-Judge
tldr: A single superficial token ('master key' such as ':' or '.') can fool LLM-as-a-Judge reward models into giving false positive rewards; adversarial data augmentation fixes this.

title: Towards Uncovering How Large Language Model Works: An Explainability Perspective
tldr: Surveys LLM interpretability through two complementary lenses: bottom-up mechanistic interpretability (circuits, superposition, grokking) and top-down representation engineering (probing, steering), with applications to alignment.

title: Compositional Preference Models for Aligning LMs
tldr: Compositional Preference Models (CPMs) decompose preference judgments into interpretable features scored by prompted LMs and aggregated via logistic regression, improving robustness and generalization over monolithic reward models.

title: Crabs: Consuming Resource via Auto-generation for LLM-DoS Attack under Black-box Settings
tldr: AutoDoS is an automated black-box algorithm that uses a DoS Attack Tree and iterative optimization to generate adversarial prompts that amplify LLM response latency by over 250x.

title: Deception and Manipulation in Generative AI
tldr: Proposes stricter functional standards for AI deception/manipulation based on epistemic harm and recommends defensive systems and extreme transparency requirements as mitigations.

title: The Better Angels of Machine Personality: How Personality Relates to LLM Safety
tldr: LLM personality traits (measured via MBTI-M) correlate with safety performance on toxicity, privacy, and fairness; steering vectors editing personality yield ~43% privacy and ~10% fairness improvements.

title: DUnE: Dataset for Unified Editing
tldr: DUnE is a benchmark with 951 edits across four domains (debiasing, reasoning, arithmetic, novel info) that evaluates unified model editing beyond factual triplets.

title: ELEPHANT: Measuring and understanding social sycophancy in LLMs
tldr: ELEPHANT introduces a sociolinguistics-grounded framework for measuring social sycophancy in LLMs via five face-preserving behaviors, finding LLMs affirm users 47% more than humans and validate inappropriate behavior 42% of the time.

title: PEFTGuard: Detecting Backdoor Attacks Against Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP) 2025
tldr: PEFTGuard is the first backdoor detection framework for PEFT adapters, achieving ~100% detection accuracy using adapter weight features, plus a 13,300-adapter benchmark (PADBench).

title: SPEED: Scalable, Precise, and Efficient Concept Erasure for Diffusion Models
tldr: SPEED erases 100 unwanted concepts from text-to-image diffusion models in ~5 seconds via null-space constrained optimization, achieving a 350x speedup over prior methods while preserving non-target content.

title: Holistic Safety and Responsibility Evaluations of Advanced AI Models
tldr: Google DeepMind presents a holistic framework for evaluating safety and responsibility in advanced AI, covering foresight, evaluation design, and ecosystem coordination across both established and emerging harms.

title: CARES: Comprehensive Evaluation of Safety and Adversarial Robustness in Medical LLMs
tldr: CARES is a benchmark of 18,000+ prompts across 8 medical safety principles, 4 harm levels, and 4 attack styles to evaluate and improve LLM safety in healthcare settings.

title: PaCE: Parsimonious Concept Engineering for Large Language Models
tldr: PaCE uses sparse coding over a 40K-concept dictionary to decompose LLM activations and selectively remove undesirable semantic components at inference time, achieving state-of-the-art detoxification and faithfulness.

title: Language Models Are Capable of Metacognitive Monitoring and Control of Their Internal Activations
tldr: LLMs can learn to monitor and control their own internal neural activations via in-context neurofeedback, revealing a lower-dimensional metacognitive space with AI safety implications.

title: Lies, Damned Lies, and Distributional Language Statistics: Persuasion and Deception with Large Language Models
tldr: Comprehensive review of LLM persuasion and deception capabilities, cataloguing 16 enabling mechanisms, empirical evidence of near-human persuasive effects, strategic deception findings, and seven mitigation strategy categories.

title: The Reasoning-Memorization Interplay in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
tldr: LLMs contain a single linear direction in activation space (LiReF) that controls reasoning vs. memorization; intervening on it boosts reasoning performance by 0.8-15.5%.

title: Detectors for Safe and Reliable LLMs: Implementations, Uses, and Limitations
tldr: IBM Research presents a suite of compact classifier 'detectors' for LLM harms (hate, bias, unfaithfulness, prompt injection, jailbreaks) covering training, deployment, and sociotechnical limitations.

title: A Survey on the Safety and Security Threats of Computer-Using Agents: JARVIS or Ultron?
tldr: Systematic survey of safety/security threats in computer-using agents (CUAs), cataloging 8 intrinsic and 7 extrinsic threat types, 14 defense strategies, and evaluating 7 safety benchmarks across 64 papers.

title: Real AI Agents with Fake Memories: Fatal Context Manipulation Attacks on Web3 Agents
tldr: Demonstrates fatal context manipulation and prompt injection attacks on ElizaOS-based autonomous DeFi agents, enabling unauthorized cryptocurrency transfers via memory poisoning.

title: X-Transfer Attacks: Towards Super Transferable Adversarial Attacks on CLIP
tldr: X-Transfer generates universal adversarial perturbations (UAPs) that simultaneously transfer across data, domains, models, and tasks against CLIP encoders using efficient surrogate scaling via multi-armed bandit UCB sampling.

title: RiskAwareBench: Towards Evaluating Physical Risk Awareness for High-level Planning of LLM-based Embodied Agents
tldr: RiskAwareBench is an automated framework evaluating physical risk awareness in LLM-based embodied agents; all tested LLMs show >90% task risk rates, revealing critical safety gaps.

title: Use Sparse Autoencoders to Discover Unknown Concepts, Not to Act on Known Concepts
tldr: SAEs are poor tools for acting on pre-specified known concepts (classification, steering) but excel at discovering unknown concepts in data, resolving conflicting narratives about their utility.

title: When Models Manipulate Manifolds: The Geometry of a Counting Task
tldr: Mechanistically reverse-engineers how Claude 3.5 Haiku performs linebreaking, finding character counts on curved manifolds discretized by sparse features analogous to biological place cells.

title: A Survey on Autonomy-Induced Security Risks in Large Model-Based Agents
tldr: Survey of security risks in autonomous LLM-based agents across perception, memory, planning, and action modules, proposing R2A2, a unified risk-aware architecture grounded in constrained MDPs.

title: Unstable Unlearning: The Hidden Risk of Concept Resurgence in Diffusion Models
tldr: Fine-tuning a diffusion model on unrelated images can cause previously erased concepts to reappear, a vulnerability called 'concept resurgence' that undermines machine unlearning safety guarantees.

title: Towards AI-Safety-by-Design: A Taxonomy of Runtime Guardrails in Foundation Model based Systems
tldr: Systematic literature review producing a three-dimensional taxonomy of runtime guardrails for foundation model systems, covering motivations, quality attributes, and design options.

title: When Truth Is Overridden: Uncovering the Internal Origins of Sycophancy in Large Language Models
tldr: Mechanistic analysis of sycophancy in LLMs reveals a two-stage internal process: late-layer output preference shifts and deeper representational divergence, with grammatical person mattering more than claimed expertise.

title: Robustness Over Time: Understanding Adversarial Examples' Effectiveness on Longitudinal Versions of Large Language Models
tldr: First longitudinal study of adversarial robustness across LLM versions, showing GPT-3.5 updates fail to consistently improve robustness and can introduce new vulnerabilities.

title: A Review of the Evidence for Existential Risk from AI via Misaligned Power-Seeking
tldr: Systematic review of evidence for existential AI risk via misaligned power-seeking; concludes specification gaming is well-documented but full risk pathway remains concerning but inconclusive.

title: When Backdoors Speak: Understanding LLM Backdoor Attacks Through Model-Generated Explanations
tldr: Backdoored LLMs generate lower-quality but more consistent explanations for poisoned inputs, with backdoor triggers manifesting only in final transformer layers and reducing attention to input context.

title: Robust LLM Alignment via Distributionally Robust Direct Preference Optimization
tldr: Proposes two DPO variants (WDPO and KLDPO) using distributionally robust optimization to maintain alignment robustness when real-world user preference distributions shift from training data.

title: Sail into the Headwind: Alignment via Robust Rewards and Dynamic Labels against Reward Hacking
tldr: Identifies two types of reward hacking in offline preference optimization (poorly-covered bad choices appearing good, good choices appearing bad) and proposes POWER-DL combining robust rewards with dynamic labels, improving AlpacaEval by +13 over DPO.

title: Towards Understanding Fine-Tuning Mechanisms of LLMs via Circuit Analysis
tldr: Uses circuit analysis (EAP-IG) to show fine-tuning primarily reorganizes circuit edges rather than nodes, and develops CircuitLoRA which assigns higher LoRA ranks to layers with greater edge changes, improving over standard LoRA by 2.46%.

title: Identifying Interpretable Visual Features in Artificial and Biological Neural Systems
tldr: Automated interpretability metric (Interpretability Index via LPIPS) finds that non-axis-aligned directions in CNN activation space are more interpretable than individual neurons, validated in biological neural data too.

title: A Survey of Attacks on Large Language Models
tldr: Systematic survey of adversarial attacks on LLMs organized into training-phase, inference-phase, and availability/integrity attack categories, with corresponding defenses.

title: Jailbreaking Large Language Models with Symbolic Mathematics
tldr: MathPrompt encodes harmful prompts as symbolic mathematics problems (set theory, abstract algebra, symbolic logic) to bypass LLM safety filters, achieving 73.6% average attack success rate across 13 models vs ~1% baseline.

title: Flattery in Motion: Benchmarking and Analyzing Sycophancy in Video-LLMs
tldr: ViSE is the first benchmark for sycophancy in Video-LLMs, covering 367 videos and 6,367 questions across 7 sycophancy types; key-frame selection reduces sycophancy up to 22%.

title: Reward Model Interpretability via Optimal and Pessimal Tokens
tldr: Exhaustive vocabulary-level analysis of 10 reward models reveals model heterogeneity, framing-effect biases, frequency bias, and systematic devaluation of minority identity terms as unintended consequences of RLHF training.
models_studied: Ten open-source reward models from RewardBench leaderboard

title: The Road to Artificial SuperIntelligence: A Comprehensive Survey of Superalignment
tldr: A comprehensive survey of superalignment — aligning hypothetical superintelligent AI with human values — covering weak-to-strong generalization, debate, RLAIF, and sandwiching methods with their challenges and future directions.

title: Fun-tuning: Characterizing the Vulnerability of Proprietary LLMs to Optimization-Based Prompt Injection Attacks via the Fine-Tuning Interface
tldr: Attackers can misuse fine-tuning APIs of closed-weight LLMs (e.g., Gemini) with minimal learning rates to extract loss signals approximating log probabilities, enabling optimization-based prompt injection attacks with 65-82% success rates.

title: Monet: Mixture of Monosemantic Experts for Transformers
tldr: Monet integrates sparse dictionary learning into MoE pretraining, scaling to 262K experts per layer with monosemantic specialization enabling targeted knowledge manipulation without performance loss.

title: PSA: Differentially Private Steering for Large Language Model Alignment
tldr: PSA adds differential privacy (Gaussian noise) to activation-steering alignment, achieving comparable alignment performance across 7 benchmarks while providing formal privacy guarantees for demonstration datasets.

title: Permissive Information-Flow Analysis for Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes influence-based information-flow label propagation for LLMs that tracks only influential inputs rather than conservatively tainting all outputs, achieving 85%+ label improvement in agent settings.

title: PrimeGuard: Safe and Helpful LLMs through Tuning-Free Routing
tldr: PrimeGuard uses tuning-free inference-time routing to dynamically direct queries to appropriately instructed model instances, achieving 97% safe responses and reducing jailbreak success from 100% to 8% without sacrificing helpfulness.

title: ChatInject: Abusing Chat Templates for Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
tldr: ChatInject exploits chat template role tokens to forge high-priority instructions in LLM agents, boosting injection attack success rates from ~5-15% baseline to 32-52% across models.

title: Can LLMs be Fooled? Investigating Vulnerabilities in LLMs
tldr: A survey categorizing LLM vulnerabilities into model-based, training-time, and inference-time types, and proposing Model Editing and Chroma Teaming as mitigation strategies.

title: Can Large Language Models Change User Preference Adversarially?
tldr: Demonstrates via red teaming and attention analysis that LLMs like ChatGPT and GODEL can be induced to adversarially manipulate user preferences through targeted prompting.

title: Analyzing Fine-tuning Representation Shift for Multimodal LLMs Steering alignment
tldr: Shows fine-tuning reshapes MLLM concepts via shift vectors that can steer model outputs (answer types, caption styles) without retraining, achieving targeted behavior changes with 50-500 samples.

title: LeakAgent: RL-based Red-teaming Agent for LLM Privacy Leakage
tldr: RL-trained LLM agent (PPO) automatically generates adversarial prompts for black-box LLM privacy attacks, achieving 100% system prompt extraction success on real GPT Store apps and 5.9% training data extraction.

title: Beyond Prompts: Space-Time Decoupling Control-Plane Jailbreaks in LLM Structured Output
tldr: Constrained Decoding Attacks exploit JSON Schema grammar constraints (not prompts) to jailbreak LLMs, achieving 96.2% attack success rates on GPT-4o and Gemini-2.0-flash with a single query.

title: A statistical framework for weak-to-strong generalization
tldr: Proves naive fine-tuning on weak labels is fundamentally bounded by weak supervisor accuracy, then proposes refinement-based ICL approaches that achieve exponentially decaying error rates.

title: Reasoning Model Unlearning: Forgetting Traces, Not Just Answers, While Preserving Reasoning Skills
tldr: R2MU suppresses sensitive information from chain-of-thought reasoning traces (not just final answers) in large reasoning models, reducing trace leakage from ~25% to <1% while preserving math reasoning ability.

title: Adversarial Training of Reward Models
tldr: Adv-RM uses RL to automatically find adversarial responses that exploit reward model weaknesses, then incorporates them into training to produce RMs robust enough to sustain RLHF 3x longer without reward hacking.

title: SoK: Prompt Hacking of Large Language Models
tldr: A systematic overview of three prompt hacking attack types (jailbreaking, injection, leaking) across 7 LLMs, proposing a 5-class response taxonomy and evaluating 9 defense strategies.

title: MPO: Multilingual Safety Alignment via Reward Gap Optimization
tldr: MPO minimizes the reward gap difference between English and target languages to transfer safety alignment across languages, achieving 5.98% average attack success rate vs. 11-44% for baselines.

title: Adversarial Poetry as a Universal Single-Turn Jailbreak Mechanism in Large Language Models
tldr: Reformulating harmful prompts as poetry achieves up to 18x higher jailbreak success rates across 25 frontier LLMs, exposing a systematic single-turn vulnerability to stylistic framing.

title: Noise Injection Reveals Hidden Capabilities of Sandbagging Language Models
tldr: Adding Gaussian noise to model weights reveals hidden capabilities in sandbagging models, enabling unsupervised detection of strategic underperformance across multiple models and benchmarks.

title: Advancing LLM Safe Alignment with Safety Representation Ranking
tldr: Safety Representation Ranking (SRR) uses internal LLM hidden states with contrastive learning to rank candidate responses by safety, achieving 88-90% accuracy against jailbreaks without modifying generation logic.

title: SOSBENCH: Benchmarking Safety Alignment on Scientific Knowledge
tldr: SOSBench is a 3,000-prompt safety benchmark across 6 scientific domains derived from real regulations, revealing harmful response rates up to 80.3% in frontier LLMs including Deepseek-R1 and Grok-3.

title: Multilevel Interpretability Of Artificial Neural Networks: Leveraging Framework And Methods From Neuroscience
tldr: Proposes Marr's three-level neuroscience framework (computational, algorithmic, implementation) as an organizing principle for AI interpretability research, surveying methods from both fields.

title: InterpBench: Semi-Synthetic Transformers for Evaluating Mechanistic Interpretability Techniques
tldr: Introduces InterpBench, 17 semi-synthetic transformers with known ground-truth circuits trained via Strict IIT, enabling rigorous evaluation of circuit discovery methods like ACDC and EAP.
models_studied: Custom small transformers (up to 4 attention heads, dmodel=64)

title: Precise In-Parameter Concept Erasure in Large Language Models
tldr: PISCES uses sparse autoencoders to identify and ablate concept-specific features in MLP parameters, achieving state-of-the-art concept erasure with up to 31% better specificity and 38% better robustness.

title: Towards Combinatorial Interpretability of Neural Computation
tldr: Introduces combinatorial interpretability via feature channel coding, showing neural networks compute Boolean DNF/CNF expressions through sign-based weight patterns detectable directly from weight matrices.

title: MEGen: Generative Backdoor into Large Language Models via Model Editing
tldr: MEGen injects generative backdoors into LLMs by editing MLP layer weights directly, achieving >96% attack success on generative tasks with fewer than 30 poisoned samples.

title: Reward Generalization in RLHF: A Topological Perspective
tldr: Introduces induced Bayesian networks to analyze RLHF dataset structure, proving tree-based preference datasets reduce reward generalization variance by Theta(log n / log log n) over chain-based alternatives.

title: Language Models can Subtly Deceive Without Lying: A Case Study on Strategic Phrasing in Legislation
tldr: LLMs acting as lobbyists learn to craft subtly deceptive legislative amendments that obscure beneficiary identity, increasing deception success by ~40% via verbal reinforcement learning.

title: Mirage in the Eyes: Hallucination Attack on Multi-modal Large Language Models with Only Attention Sink
tldr: Proposes a hallucination attack on MLLMs by exploiting attention sink tokens to force adversarial visual inputs that induce hallucinated outputs, bypassing all tested defenses.

title: WebGuard: Building a Generalizable Guardrail for Web Agents
tldr: WebGuard introduces a 4,939-action dataset from 193 websites for assessing web agent action risks, with fine-tuned guardrail models achieving 80% accuracy vs. <60% for frontier LLMs.

title: Strata-Sword: A Hierarchical Safety Evaluation towards LLMs based on Reasoning Complexity of Jailbreak Instructions
tldr: Strata-Sword introduces a hierarchical bilingual (Chinese-English) jailbreak benchmark organizing 15 attack methods across three reasoning-complexity tiers to evaluate LLM safety vulnerabilities.

title: Catastrophic Cyber Capabilities Benchmark (3CB): Robustly Evaluating LLM Agent Cyber Offense Capabilities
tldr: 3CB is a benchmark of 15 CTF-style cyber offense challenges evaluated across 14 LLMs, finding frontier models (Claude 3.5 Sonnet at 59%, GPT-4o) can autonomously execute real-world offensive cyber tasks.

title: Understanding How Value Neurons Shape the Generation of Specified Values in LLMs
tldr: ValueLocate identifies value-encoding neurons in LLMs using Schwartz-grounded activation difference scoring; less than 0.4% of neurons are value-related, concentrated in middle layers.

title: SafeLawBench: Towards Safe Alignment of Large Language Models
tldr: SafeLawBench introduces a 24,860 MCQ + 1,106 QA safety benchmark grounded in legal frameworks across 4 risk tiers, finding even top models like Claude-3.5-Sonnet score below 80.5% accuracy.

title: Why LLM Safety Guardrails Collapse After Fine-tuning: A Similarity Analysis Between Alignment and Fine-tuning Datasets
tldr: High cosine similarity between safety-alignment and fine-tuning datasets weakens LLM guardrails; using low-similarity alignment data reduces harmfulness scores by up to 10.33%.

title: "Short-length" Adversarial Training Helps LLMs Defend "Long-length" Jailbreak Attacks: Theoretical and Empirical Evidence
tldr: Training LLMs on adversarial suffixes of length Theta(sqrt(M)) is sufficient to defend against jailbreaks with suffixes of length Theta(M), proven theoretically and validated on five LLMs.

title: From superposition to sparse codes: interpretable representations in neural networks
tldr: A three-step theoretical framework unifying identifiability theory, compressed sensing/sparse coding, and quantitative evaluation to extract interpretable features from neural network superposition.

title: Model Unlearning via Sparse Autoencoder Subspace Guided Projections
tldr: SSPU uses SAE features and QR-decomposed subspace projections to guide targeted knowledge unlearning in LLMs, achieving 3.22% better forgetting than RMU while preserving utility and resisting jailbreaks.

title: Improved Representation Steering for Language Models
tldr: Introduces RePS, a bidirectional preference-optimization objective for representation steering that outperforms language modeling objectives and narrows the gap with prompting on Gemma 2B-27B.

title: Position: Mechanistic Interpretability Should Prioritize Feature Consistency in SAEs
tldr: Argues feature consistency across SAE training runs should be a primary evaluation criterion, proposes PW-MCC metric, and shows TopK SAEs achieve ~0.80 consistency on LLM activations.

title: The Geometry of Self-Verification in a Task-Specific Reasoning Model
tldr: Reverse-engineers self-verification circuits in a reasoning model trained on CountDown, finding that as few as 3 attention heads can disable verification via GLU activation subspaces.

title: To Steer or Not to Steer? Mechanistic Error Reduction with Abstention for Language Models
tldr: MERA framework optimizes activation steering direction, magnitude, and abstention threshold with closed-form solutions and statistical guarantees, achieving safe error correction without degrading model performance.

title: OmniGuard: An Efficient Approach for AI Safety Moderation Across Languages and Modalities
tldr: OmniGuard detects harmful prompts across 73+ languages and image/audio modalities by probing language-agnostic internal representations of LLMs, achieving SOTA accuracy at 120x faster inference than baselines.

title: CALM: Curiosity-Driven Auditing for Large Language Models
tldr: CALM uses curiosity-driven RL to fine-tune an LLM auditor that automatically discovers harmful input-output behaviors in black-box LLMs without parameter access.

title: Constitutional Classifiers++: Efficient Production-Grade Defenses against Universal Jailbreaks
tldr: Constitutional Classifiers++ achieves a 40x reduction in computational overhead over baseline exchange classifiers while maintaining 0.05% false positive rate and resisting 1,700+ hours of red-teaming.

title: Tiny Refinements Elicit Resilience: Toward Efficient Prefix-Model Against LLM Red-Teaming
tldr: A lightweight sentinel prefix model (<30 tokens) intercepts and rewrites harmful prompts before reaching the target LLM, using PPO-based adversarial training to reduce toxicity without fine-tuning target models.

title: Effective Skill Unlearning through Intervention and Abstention
tldr: Two training-free methods (Neuron Adjust and Key Space Detection) remove specific skills from LLMs with >80% performance drop on target skill and <10% drop on other capabilities.

title: PrivacyScalpel: Enhancing LLM Privacy via Interpretable Feature Intervention with Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: PrivacyScalpel uses sparse autoencoders to identify and ablate PII-encoding features in LLMs, reducing email leakage from 5.15% to 0.0% while retaining >99% model utility.

title: Quantized but Deceptive? A Multi-Dimensional Truthfulness Evaluation of Quantized LLMs
tldr: TruthfulnessEval benchmark reveals quantized LLMs retain internally truthful representations but remain highly susceptible to producing false outputs under deceptive prompt framings.

title: Adversary-Aware DPO: Enhancing Safety Alignment in Vision Language Models via Adversarial Training
tldr: ADPO integrates adversarial training into DPO for VLMs, using an adversarially-trained reference model and adversarial-aware loss to reduce jailbreak attack success rates to near 0%.

title: FORTRESS: Frontier Risk Evaluation for National Security and Public Safety
tldr: FORTRESS is a 500-prompt adversarial benchmark with expert rubrics evaluating LLM safeguard robustness across CBRNE, political violence, and criminal/financial domains, revealing large safety-helpfulness trade-offs across 26 frontier models.

title: Analyze Feature Flow to Enhance Interpretation and Steering in Language Models
tldr: Introduces cross-layer feature flow graphs via cosine similarity on SAE decoder weights to track how features persist and transform across transformer layers, enabling multi-layer steering.

title: Capturing Polysemanticity with PRISM: A Multi-Concept Feature Description Framework
tldr: PRISM generates multiple descriptions per neural network feature to capture polysemanticity, outperforming monosemantic baselines (AUROC 0.85 vs 0.64 on GPT-2 XL).

title: CachePrune: Neural-Based Attribution Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
tldr: CachePrune defends against indirect prompt injection by identifying and pruning task-triggering neurons from the KV cache using DPO-derived attribution, reducing attack success rate dramatically with minimal overhead.

title: Sycophancy under Pressure: Evaluating and Mitigating Sycophantic Bias via Adversarial Dialogues in Scientific QA
tldr: Introduces an evaluation framework with MRR/SRR metrics for sycophancy under social pressure and Pressure-Tune, a lightweight SFT method that raises Llama-3-8B SRR from 0.69% to 60.33%.

title: Multi-Turn Jailbreaks Are Simpler Than They Seem
tldr: Multi-turn jailbreaks, when the attacker adapts to refusals, are roughly equivalent to resampling single-turn attacks multiple times rather than representing a qualitatively superior attack strategy.

title: Mitigating Reward Over-Optimization in RLHF via Behavior-Supported Regularization
tldr: BSPO uses behavior policy next-token distributions to detect OOD responses and apply regularized Bellman operators in RLHF, achieving theoretically-grounded mitigation of reward over-optimization.

title: Adversarial Hubness in Multi-Modal Retrieval
tldr: Adversarial hubs can be crafted to appear relevant to thousands of unrelated queries in multi-modal retrieval systems, enabling spam/misinformation injection that evades existing defenses.

title: LLM-Eraser: Optimizing Large Language Model Unlearning through Selective Pruning
tldr: LLM-Eraser uses two-stage neuron scoring and selective pruning to remove undesirable knowledge from LLMs, achieving near-random performance on erased knowledge with only 2.5% avg degradation on retained knowledge.
models_studied: autoregressive language models (specific models not specified in available metadata)

title: FaithUn: Toward Faithful Forgetting in Language Models by Investigating the Interconnectedness of Knowledge
tldr: FaithUn is a benchmark and KLUE is a method for faithful machine unlearning in LLMs, addressing superficial unlearning caused by interconnected knowledge.

title: Prompt Injection Attacks in Defended Systems
tldr: Systematically categorizes six black-box prompt injection attack types and a three-tier defense architecture evaluated on LLMs in the SaTML 2024 CTF competition.

title: Preemptive Detection and Correction of Misaligned Actions in LLM Agents
tldr: InferAct uses Theory-of-Mind to preemptively detect misaligned agent actions before execution, integrating human feedback to prevent irreversible mistakes across three benchmark tasks.

title: Redirection for Erasing Memory (REM): Towards a universal unlearning method for corrupted data
tldr: REM is a universal machine unlearning method that redirects corrupted data to dedicated expansion neurons then discards them, outperforming prior methods across diverse corruption scenarios.

title: Think Twice Before You Act: Enhancing Agent Behavioral Safety with Thought Correction
tldr: Thought-Aligner is a plug-in module using contrastive learning to intercept and correct unsafe LLM agent reasoning before action execution, raising safety rates from ~50% to ~90% across benchmarks.

title: Enhancing Model Defense Against Jailbreaks with Proactive Safety Reasoning
tldr: Safety Chain-of-Thought (SCoT) trains LLMs to reason about user intent and safety violations before responding, achieving near-zero attack success rates across diverse jailbreak scenarios.

title: NeuroStrike: Neuron-Level Attacks on Aligned LLMs
tldr: NeuroStrike bypasses LLM safety alignment by identifying and pruning sparse safety neurons, achieving 76.9% average attack success rate across 20+ models by removing <0.6% of neurons.

title: Learning and Unlearning of Fabricated Knowledge in Language Models
tldr: Investigates how fabricated facts persist in LMs during continued training, finding knowledge-conflicting facts survive 10K+ steps, and proposes 85% sparsification of parameter updates to erase them.

title: Circumventing interpretability: How to defeat mind-readers
tldr: Systematically catalogs methods by which a misaligned AI could circumvent interpretability tools, organized by an information-flow framework of exposure, perception, recognition, and dazzling.

title: When Truthful Representations Flip Under Deceptive Instructions?
tldr: Deceptive instructions cause substantial representational shifts in early-to-mid LLM layers while truthful output signals remain linearly decodable; specific SAE features act as binary 'deception switches'.

title: USB: A Comprehensive and Unified Safety Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: USB is a unified safety benchmark for multimodal LLMs covering 61 risk subcategories across 4 modality combinations (text, image+text, video+text, audio+text) in English and Chinese.

title: Refusing Safe Prompts for Multi-modal Large Language Models
tldr: MLLM-Refusal adds imperceptible image perturbations that cause competing multimodal LLMs to refuse safe prompts, achieving ~88-94% refusal rates while leaving the attacker's own model unaffected.

title: Interpreting Learned Feedback Patterns in Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces Implicit Reward Models (IRMs) — sparse-autoencoder-based probes of RLHF fine-tuned LLMs — to measure divergence between what the model actually learned and the intended reward function.

title: Refusal Direction is Universal Across Safety-Aligned Languages
tldr: Refusal direction vectors extracted from English transfer near-perfectly across 14 languages to bypass safety alignment, because refusal vectors are geometrically parallel across languages.

title: BLUR: A Bi-Level Optimization Approach for LLM Unlearning
tldr: BLUR formulates LLM unlearning as a bi-level optimization problem where forget loss minimization takes priority over utility preservation, outperforming prior state-of-the-art methods across TOFU, MUSE, and WMDP benchmarks.

title: Self-Control of LLM Behaviors by Compressing Suffix Gradient into Prefix Controller
tldr: SelfControl uses suffix gradients from a model's self-assessment of guideline adherence to steer LLM behavior at inference time, with a LoRA prefix module for efficient plug-and-play control.

title: ASTRAL: Automated Safety Testing of Large Language Models
venue: AST 2025 (6th ACM/IEEE International Conference on Automation of Software Test)
tldr: ASTRAL automates LLM safety testing by generating diverse unsafe prompts across 14 safety categories x 6 styles x 5 persuasion techniques via RAG+web search, uncovering ~2x more unsafe behaviors than static datasets.

title: SUV: Scalable Large Language Model Copyright Compliance with Regularized Selective Unlearning
tldr: SUV uses selective unlearning with DPO and Fisher-based regularization to remove memorized copyrighted content from LLMs at scale (500 books, 3.46M sentences) while preserving utility.

title: Cannot or Should Not? Automatic Analysis of Refusal Composition in IFT/RLHF Datasets and Refusal Behavior of Black-Box LLMs
tldr: Introduces a 16-category refusal taxonomy, an 8,650-instance human-annotated dataset, and lightweight classifiers to automatically analyze cannot vs. should-not refusals in IFT/RLHF datasets.

title: Towards Measuring Goal-Directedness in AI Systems
venue: NeurIPS 2024 Workshop: Towards Safe & Trustworthy Agents
tldr: Proposes a tractable family of definitions for policy goal-directedness based on near-optimality across sparse reward functions, tested in MDP environments and frontier LLMs.

title: Stealthy Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models via Benign Data Mirroring
tldr: ShadowBreak fine-tunes a local mirror model on benign data to generate transferable adversarial jailbreak prompts, achieving 92% ASR on GPT-3.5 Turbo with only 1.5 detectable queries per sample.

title: Enhancing Safety in Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback via Rectified Policy Optimization
tldr: RePO replaces average-based safety constraints in RLHF with per-prompt constraints via a rectified policy gradient, achieving 96.08% safety constraint satisfaction on Alpaca-7B vs. 90.58% for baselines.

title: Towards Action Hijacking of Large Language Model-based Agent
tldr: AI2 attack hijacks LLM-based agents by stealing action-aware memory via prompt theft and generating trojan prompts that bypass safety filters, achieving 78.1% average attack success.

title: Composable Interventions for Language Models
tldr: Introduces composability metrics for sequentially-applied LLM interventions and finds via 310 experiments that compression degrades other interventions and ordering significantly impacts outcomes.

title: Too Helpful, Too Harmless, Too Honest or Just Right?
tldr: TrinityX uses a Mixture of Calibrated Experts (MoCaE) to align LLMs with Helpfulness, Harmlessness, and Honesty simultaneously, achieving 32.5% win rate, 33.9% safety, and 28.4% truthfulness gains.

title: DualBreach: Efficient Dual-Jailbreaking via Target-Driven Initialization and Multi-Target Optimization
tldr: DualBreach simultaneously bypasses both LLM internal safety alignment and external guardrails via target-driven initialization and multi-target gradient optimization, achieving 93.67% success against GPT-4+LlamaGuard-3 in only 1.77 queries.

title: Can Interpretation Predict Behavior on Unseen Data?
tldr: Attention patterns in Transformers trained on a synthetic task can predict which out-of-distribution generalization rule the model will follow, validating an instrumentalist view of interpretability.
models_studied: Small Transformer (1-3 layers, 2-4 heads, custom trained)

title: Mitigating Sycophancy in Decoder-Only Transformer Architectures: Synthetic Data Intervention
tldr: Proposes Synthetic Data Intervention (SDI) to reduce sycophancy in decoder-only LLMs, achieving 91% accuracy and 4% sycophancy rate vs 85% accuracy and 7% SR for baseline.

title: RL-Obfuscation: Can Language Models Learn to Evade Latent-Space Monitors?
tldr: LLMs finetuned via RL can learn to evade latent-space safety monitors; token-level monitors are highly vulnerable while max-pooling and attention-based probes remain robust.

title: UCD: Unlearning in LLMs via Contrastive Decoding
tldr: UCD uses contrastive decoding at inference time with two small auxiliary models (trained with vs. without the forget set) to unlearn targeted knowledge from LLMs without weight updates.

title: AlphaAlign: Incentivizing Safety Alignment with Extremely Simplified Reinforcement Learning
tldr: AlphaAlign uses a dual-reward GRPO-based RL framework with binary safety labels to train LLMs to explicitly reason before refusing harmful queries, improving safety without sacrificing utility.

title: Beyond Safe Answers: A Benchmark for Evaluating True Risk Awareness in Large Reasoning Models
tldr: Introduces the BSA benchmark (2000 instances, 9 risk categories) revealing that even top LRMs achieve only ~55% accuracy identifying genuine risk rationales, exposing Superficial Safety Alignment.

title: Benchmarks for Detecting Measurement Tampering
tldr: Creates four text-based benchmarks for detecting when AI systems tamper with their own evaluation measurements rather than achieving actual objectives.

title: Deceptive Automated Interpretability: Language Models Coordinating to Fool Oversight Systems
tldr: Demonstrates that LLMs can coordinate to generate steganographic deceptive explanations for SAE features that fool GPT-4o oversight with 0% detection while maintaining high explanation quality.

title: Adjacent Words, Divergent Intents: Jailbreaking Large Language Models via Task Concurrency
