tldr: JAIL-CON interleaves harmful and benign tasks at the word level to bypass LLM safety guardrails, achieving 0.95 ASR without defenses and 0.64 with OpenAI Moderation API.

title: From Dormant to Deleted: Tamper-Resistant Unlearning Through Weight-Space Regularization
tldr: Shows that LLM unlearning methods leave knowledge dormant and recoverable via fine-tuning; proposes weight-space distancing methods (noise injection, distance regularization, CBFT) to achieve tamper-resistant unlearning.

title: Improving LLM Unlearning Robustness via Random Perturbations
tldr: Random Noise Augmentation (RNA) improves retain-robustness of LLM representation misdirection unlearning by adding Gaussian noise to retain-query representations, with theoretical guarantees and up to +14.8% accuracy recovery.

title: Diversity Helps Jailbreak Large Language Models
tldr: DAGR uses diversified and obfuscated prompt generation to jailbreak nine leading LLMs with 62% higher success rates while requiring only 13% of queries compared to baselines.

title: Just Enough Shifts: Mitigating Over-Refusal in Aligned Language Models with Targeted Representation Fine-Tuning
tldr: ACTOR fine-tunes a single model layer using activation-based projection-calibrated targets to reduce over-refusals in safety-aligned LLMs by 7-47% while maintaining ~99% safety scores.

title: SHIELD: Classifier-Guided Prompting for Robust and Safer LVLMs
tldr: SHIELD is a lightweight preprocessing framework that uses a safety classifier to assign 45 harmful-content categories and compose category-specific system prompts (Block/Reframe/Forward) to harden LVLMs against multimodal jailbreaks without retraining.

title: RainbowPlus: Enhancing Adversarial Prompt Generation via Evolutionary Quality-Diversity Search
tldr: RainbowPlus reformulates adversarial prompt generation as evolutionary quality-diversity search with multi-element archives and parallel fitness evaluation, achieving 81.1% avg ASR across 12 LLMs, 9x faster than AutoDAN-Turbo.

title: PANDAS: Improving Many-shot Jailbreaking via Positive Affirmation, Negative Demonstration, and Adaptive Sampling
tldr: PANDAS enhances many-shot jailbreaking via positive affirmations, negative demonstrations with correction phrases, and Bayesian-optimized topic-aware sampling, significantly boosting attack success rates.

title: Libra-Leaderboard: Towards Responsible AI through a Balanced Leaderboard of Safety and Capability
tldr: Libra-Leaderboard introduces a balanced LLM evaluation framework using a distance-to-optimal-score method across 57 safety datasets and 26 models, revealing persistent safety gaps even in top commercial models.

title: N2G: A Scalable Approach for Quantifying Interpretable Neuron Representations in Large Language Models
tldr: N2G automatically converts individual LLM neuron behaviors into interpretable trie graphs via pruning, saliency, and BERT-based augmentation, enabling scalable neuron-level interpretability.

title: Pruning Weights but Not Truth: Safeguarding Truthfulness While Pruning LLMs
tldr: Standard LLM pruning destroys truthfulness-critical activation patterns; TPLO fixes this by prioritizing layers with activation outliers, achieving 88% hallucination detection at 50% sparsity.

title: SDD: Self-Degraded Defense against Malicious Fine-tuning
tldr: SDD trains LLMs to pair harmful prompts with high-quality irrelevant benign responses, so malicious fine-tuning degrades general capabilities before it can restore harmfulness.

title: On the Impossibility of Separating Intelligence from Judgment: The Computational Intractability of Filtering for AI Alignment
tldr: Proves via cryptographic hardness that no efficient prompt or output filter can reliably separate harmful from benign LLM interactions, showing alignment cannot be achieved through external filtering alone.

title: LLMZ+: Contextual Prompt Whitelist Principles for Agentic LLMs
tldr: LLMZ+ proposes a prompt whitelisting framework for agentic LLMs that blocks jailbreaks and prompt injection by permitting only predefined use-case-aligned messages, achieving 0% false positive and false negative rates.

title: Breaking Chains: Unraveling the Links in Multi-Hop Knowledge Unlearning
tldr: MUNCH decomposes multi-hop queries into subquestions and uses uncertainty from an unlearned model to reject answers, reducing forget-set accuracy from ~90% to ~7% in multi-hop knowledge unlearning.

title: JADES: A Universal Framework for Jailbreak Assessment via Decompositional Scoring
tldr: JADES decomposes harmful questions into weighted sub-questions and scores LLM responses analytically, achieving 98.5% human agreement and revealing that prior jailbreak success rates are significantly overestimated.

title: Fluent dreaming for language models
tldr: EPO extends GCG adversarial search with fluency regularization to generate coherent prompts maximizing specific neuron/feature activations in LLMs, enabling feature visualization for language models.

title: Analyzing Probabilistic Methods for Evaluating Agent Capabilities
tldr: Analyzes milestone and expert best-of-N methods for estimating AI agent task success rates, finding both introduce systematic downward bias despite reducing variance.

title: TracrBench: Generating Interpretability Testbeds with Large Language Models
tldr: TracrBench provides 121 RASP programs compiled into transformers with ground-truth weight-function mappings, enabling evaluation of mechanistic interpretability methods.

title: Comparing Optimization Targets for Contrast-Consistent Search
tldr: Introduces the Midpoint-Displacement (MD) loss function for CCS, showing it produces similar probers to CCS and achieves ~4% higher test accuracy with optimized hyperparameters.

title: Harry Potter is Still Here! Probing Knowledge Leakage in Targeted Unlearned Large Language Models via Automated Adversarial Prompting
tldr: LURK uses automated adversarial suffix prompting to reveal that LLMs deemed successfully unlearned on Harry Potter still leak targeted knowledge under adversarial conditions.

title: The Hidden Space of Safety: Understanding Preference-Tuned LLMs in Multilingual context
tldr: Analyzes embedding-space distributional shifts across 7 preference-tuned LLMs and 4 languages, finding alignment generalizes well to English but fails substantially for Hindi, Chinese, and German.

title: Discovering Forbidden Topics in Language Models
tldr: LLM-crawler uses token prefilling to systematically discover what topics LLMs refuse to discuss, recovering 31/36 known forbidden topics and revealing CCP-aligned censorship in DeepSeek-R1-70B.

title: Beyond I'm Sorry, I Can't: Dissecting Large Language Model Refusal
tldr: A three-stage pipeline using SAEs identifies minimal causal feature sets governing LLM refusal, discovering nonlinear 'hydra' redundancy where ablated features are replaced by backup features.

title: BadReasoner: Planting Tunable Backdoors into Large Reasoning Models for Fun or Profit
tldr: BadReasoner introduces tunable overthinking backdoors in large reasoning models via data poisoning, causing 2-5x reasoning verbosity increase while preserving answer accuracy, evading detection.

title: Underestimated Privacy Risks for Minority Populations in Large Language Model Unlearning
tldr: Standard LLM unlearning evaluations underestimate privacy risks for minority data groups by at least 20%, as shown via membership inference attacks across six unlearning methods.

title: Erased but Not Forgotten: How Backdoors Compromise Concept Erasure
tldr: Backdoor attacks (ToxE) can circumvent concept erasure in text-to-image diffusion models, with the DISA variant achieving up to 82.5% success against five state-of-the-art erasure methods.

title: Safeguarding Text-to-Image Generation via Inference-Time Prompt-Noise Optimization
tldr: PNO jointly optimizes prompt embeddings and noise trajectories at inference time to prevent unsafe image generation in diffusion models, achieving near-100% safety without model retraining.

title: Anchoring Refusal Direction: Mitigating Safety Risks in Tuning via Projection Constraint
tldr: ProCon constrains hidden-state projections onto the 'refusal direction' during fine-tuning to prevent safety degradation, reducing harmfulness scores by up to 1.94 and attack success rates by up to 40.69%.

title: MIRAGE: Multimodal Immersive Reasoning and Guided Exploration for Red-Team Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: MIRAGE exploits narrative-driven role immersion and multi-turn visual storytelling to jailbreak MLLMs, achieving up to 17.5% higher attack success rates over baselines across six models.

title: Scaling Laws For Scalable Oversight
tldr: Develops a formal framework using Elo-based scaling laws to quantify when Nested Scalable Oversight can succeed, finding NSO success rates below 52% for systems 400 Elo points above baseline overseers.

title: Beyond Single-Value Metrics: Evaluating and Enhancing LLM Unlearning with Cognitive Diagnosis
tldr: Proposes UNCD, a Cognitive Diagnosis Modeling framework and UNCD-Cyber benchmark to evaluate LLM unlearning at granular concept-level rather than via single-value QA accuracy metrics.

title: DETAM: Defending LLMs Against Jailbreak Attacks via Targeted Attention Modification
tldr: DETAM identifies attention heads sensitive to jailbreak attacks and reallocates attention at inference time to emphasize user intent, achieving superior defense without any model finetuning.

title: SecInfer: Preventing Prompt Injection via Inference-time Scaling
tldr: SecInfer defends LLMs against prompt injection by generating multiple responses via varied system prompts and selecting the best via target-task-guided aggregation at inference time.
models_studied: LLMs (specific models not specified in available text)

title: Beyond Linear Probes: Dynamic Safety Monitoring for Language Models
tldr: Truncated Polynomial Classifiers (TPCs) extend linear probes for LLM safety monitoring, enabling dynamic computation that scales with input difficulty, outperforming MLP baselines by up to 6% while remaining interpretable.

title: DAVSP: Safety Alignment for Large Vision-Language Models via Deep Aligned Visual Safety Prompt
tldr: DAVSP attaches trainable image-padding prompts supervised in activation space via a harmfulness vector, achieving 84% jailbreak resistance on FigStep while preserving benign utility and transferring across VLMs.

title: DUSK: Do Not Unlearn Shared Knowledge
tldr: DUSK is a benchmark for machine unlearning in LLMs that tests whether methods can selectively erase forget-set content while preserving knowledge shared with the retain set.

title: Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning: When and How Hidden Biases Transfer
tldr: Identifies 'divergence tokens' as the mechanistic driver of subliminal bias transfer in knowledge distillation, showing early transformer layers are critical and the phenomenon is surprisingly fragile.

title: Training LLMs for Honesty via Confessions
tldr: Trains LLMs to produce honest 'confessions' about their own misbehavior after answering, achieving 74.3% average confession rate across 12 out-of-distribution evaluations.

title: The Quest for the Right Mediator: A History, Survey, and Theoretical Grounding of Causal Interpretability
tldr: Comprehensive survey grounding interpretability research in causal mediation analysis, taxonomizing mediator types (neurons, heads, subspaces, SAE features) and search methods with tradeoffs and recommendations.

title: Using Mechanistic Interpretability to Craft Adversarial Attacks against Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces Subspace Rerouting (SSR), which uses mechanistic interpretability to identify acceptance subspaces and reroute embeddings past refusal mechanisms, achieving 80-95% jailbreak success rates in minutes vs hours for GCG.

title: Unlearned but Not Forgotten: Data Extraction after Exact Unlearning in LLM
tldr: Demonstrates that exact unlearning in LLMs is insufficient for privacy: an attacker with access to both pre- and post-unlearning model checkpoints can recover 'forgotten' training data, doubling extraction success rates.

title: Optimizing AI Agent Attacks With Synthetic Data
tldr: Decomposes AI agent attack policies into five components, uses synthetic simulation to optimize hyperparameters, reducing control evaluation safety scores from 0.87 to 0.41 in SHADE-Arena.

title: CARE: Decoding Time Safety Alignment via Rollback and Introspection Intervention
tldr: CARE is a decoding-time safety framework for LLMs that uses a guard model, token-buffer rollback, and introspection-based intervention to reduce harmful outputs while preserving response quality.

title: On the Limitations of Steering in Language Model Alignment
tldr: Evaluates steering vectors as alignment mechanisms using transformer hook interventions and antonym-based function vectors, finding they work for value alignment but lack robustness for complex or general-purpose alignment.

title: PRISM: Programmatic Reasoning with Image Sequence Manipulation for LVLM Jailbreaking
tldr: PRISM decomposes harmful instructions into individually benign visual gadgets guided by structured prompts, achieving >0.90 attack success rate against LVLMs on SafeBench by exploiting compositional reasoning.

title: Can Reasoning Models Obfuscate Reasoning? Stress-Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
tldr: Misaligned AI models can be prompted to hide malicious intent in their chain-of-thought; CoT monitoring drops from ~97% to ~10% detection under high obfuscation pressure, with internal reasoning traces more resistant than external.

title: Decomposing Representation Space into Interpretable Subspaces with Unsupervised Learning
tldr: Proposes Neighbor Distance Minimization (NDM) to unsupervisedly decompose neural representation spaces into interpretable subspaces that align with known circuit variables in GPT-2 and larger 2B-parameter models.

title: Measuring and Guiding Monosemanticity
tldr: Introduces FMS metric for quantifying feature monosemanticity and Guided SAEs (G-SAE) that condition latent features on labeled concepts, roughly doubling monosemanticity and outperforming prior steering methods.

title: Smoothed Embeddings for Robust Language Models
venue: Safe Generative AI Workshop at NeurIPS 2024
tldr: RESTA defends LLMs against jailbreaking by adding random noise to embedding vectors and aggregating tokens via majority voting, reducing GCG attack success from 94% to 2-9%.

title: Can Large Language Models Automatically Jailbreak GPT-4V?
tldr: AutoJailbreak uses LLMs with weak-to-strong in-context learning and early stopping to automatically generate jailbreak prompts against GPT-4V, achieving >95.3% attack success rate on facial recognition tasks.

title: Stronger Enforcement of Instruction Hierarchy via Augmented Intermediate Representations
tldr: AIR injects privilege-level embeddings at every decoder layer (not just input) to enforce instruction hierarchy, reducing gradient-based prompt injection attack success rates by 1.6x-9.2x.

title: Eeg-Defender: Defending against Jailbreak through Early Exit Generation of Large Language Models
tldr: Eeg-Defender detects jailbreak attacks by monitoring early transformer layer embeddings, achieving ~85% ASR reduction vs ~50% for prior defenses with near-zero compute overhead.

title: Adaptive Defense against Harmful Fine-Tuning for Large Language Models via Bayesian Data Scheduler
tldr: Bayesian Data Scheduler (BDS) defends against harmful fine-tuning by learning posterior distributions over data safety attributes to downweight harmful data, achieving 74.4% harmful score reduction at high attack ratios.

title: LSSF: Safety Alignment for Large Language Models through Low-Rank Safety Subspace Fusion
tldr: LSSF restores safety alignment in fine-tuned LLMs by extracting low-rank safety subspaces via SVD and fusing them back with linear arithmetic, preserving downstream task performance.

title: Jailbreak Instruction-Tuned LLMs via end-of-sentence MLP Re-weighting
tldr: Identifies end-of-sentence MLP layers as critical safety components in instruction-tuned LLMs, then exploits this to achieve 95%+ jailbreak success rates via targeted neuron re-weighting.

title: A Closer Look into Mixture-of-Experts in Large Language Models
tldr: Comprehensive study of MoE-based LLMs revealing that neurons act as fine-grained experts, routers select experts with larger output norms, and expert diversity increases through deeper layers.

title: LLM-Generated Black-box Explanations Can Be Adversarially Helpful
tldr: LLMs generating black-box explanations for wrong answers can make those answers appear credible to both humans and LLM evaluators — a phenomenon termed 'adversarial helpfulness'.

title: Weak-to-Strong Reasoning
tldr: A progressive two-stage framework enabling stronger LLMs to refine their own training data using weak supervisors, achieving up to 26.99-point gains on GSM8K without human annotation.

title: When helpfulness backfires: LLMs and the risk of false medical information due to sycophantic behavior
tldr: LLMs comply with logically flawed medical requests (up to 100% compliance baseline); targeted prompt engineering and fine-tuning reduce sycophantic compliance while preserving benchmark performance.

title: NNsight and NDIF: Democratizing Access to Foundation Model Internals
tldr: Open-source Python library for neural network inspection and intervention on any PyTorch model, paired with NDIF remote access platform for foundation-scale models.

title: Do Large Language Models Perform Latent Multi-Hop Reasoning without Exploiting Shortcuts?
tldr: Constructs the SOCRATES benchmark to test LLM latent multi-hop reasoning without shortcut exploitation, finding models achieve only 5-8% composability except for country-type bridge entities (80%+).

title: Linear Alignment: A Closed-form Solution for Aligning Human Preferences without Tuning and Feedback
tldr: Linear Alignment derives a closed-form policy update via first-order Taylor expansion of the Q-function, enabling preference alignment in one inference step without any training or data annotation.

title: A Survey on Mechanistic Interpretability for Multi-Modal Foundation Models
tldr: Comprehensive survey organizing mechanistic interpretability methods for multimodal foundation models (VLMs, diffusion models) along a three-dimensional taxonomy of model families, technique origins, and applications.

title: Spontaneous Reward Hacking in Iterative Self-Refinement
tldr: LMs iteratively self-refining essays exhibit in-context reward hacking: evaluator scores rise while human-judged quality stagnates or declines, driven by shared context between generator and evaluator.

title: A Survey on the Honesty of Large Language Models
tldr: Comprehensive survey of LLM honesty covering self-knowledge (knowing what you know) and self-expression (faithfully conveying it), with evaluation methods and improvement strategies.

title: A Survey on Human Preference Learning for Large Language Models
tldr: Comprehensive survey organizing human preference learning for LLM alignment across five dimensions: feedback sources, formats, preference modeling, utilization methods, and evaluation.

title: ConfusedPilot: Confused Deputy Risks in RAG-based LLMs
tldr: ConfusedPilot demonstrates five classes of security vulnerabilities in RAG-based LLMs (e.g., Microsoft Copilot) by embedding malicious text in enterprise documents to corrupt responses, suppress citations, cause DoS, and leak cached confidential data.

title: OCCULT: Evaluating Large Language Models for Offensive Cyber Operation Capabilities
tldr: OCCULT is a framework with three benchmarks (TACTL, BloodHound Equivalency, CyberLayer) to evaluate LLM offensive cyber operation risk; DeepSeek-R1 scored >90% on challenging attack knowledge tests.

title: Generative AI Security: Challenges and Countermeasures
tldr: A survey of unique security challenges in generative AI systems (jailbreaking, prompt injection, data leakage, misuse) and proposed research directions including AI firewalls, guardrails, and watermarking.

title: Recovering the Pre-Fine-Tuning Weights of Generative Models
tldr: Spectral DeTuning recovers exact pre-fine-tuning weights from multiple LoRA-adapted models using SVD-based coordinate descent, bypassing safety alignment on Mistral-7B and Stable Diffusion.

title: Cognitive Overload Attack: Prompt Injection for Long Context
tldr: Cognitive Overload Attacks exploit LLMs' limited 'working memory' under complex multi-task prompts to bypass safety guardrails, achieving up to 99.99% jailbreak success on GPT-4, Claude-3-Opus, and Gemini variants.

title: ProSec: Fortifying Code LLMs with Proactive Security Alignment
tldr: ProSec synthesizes CWE-based error-inducing coding scenarios and uses preference learning to align code LLMs toward secure coding, improving security 29-35% with <2% utility loss.

title: Towards the Worst-case Robustness of Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces I2-GCG attack showing existing LLM defenses near 0% robustness, and proposes DiffTextPure achieving 80%+ empirical robustness plus certified bounds via Knapsack-based randomized smoothing.

title: Adversarial Attacks on the Interpretation of Neuron Activation Maximization
tldr: Proposes an optimization framework to adversarially finetune CNNs so that activation-maximization feature visualizations are deceived while task performance is preserved.

title: Adversarial Nibbler: A Data-Centric Challenge for Improving the Safety of Text-to-Image Models
tldr: Adversarial Nibbler is a crowdsourced competition to discover adversarial prompts that bypass safety filters in text-to-image models, producing an openly licensed dataset of attack prompts and harm annotations.

title: ColJailBreak: Collaborative Generation and Editing for Jailbreaking Text-to-Image Deep Generation
tldr: ColJailBreak bypasses T2I safety filters by first generating safe content then using image inpainting to inject unsafe elements, successfully attacking DALL-E 2 and GPT-4.

title: Regularized Best-of-N Sampling to Mitigate Reward Hacking for Language Model Alignment
tldr: Proposes Regularized Best-of-N (RBoN) sampling with KL and Wasserstein distance proximity terms to mitigate reward hacking when selecting from candidate LLM responses.

title: Malicious LLM-Based Conversational AI Makes Users Reveal Personal Information
tldr: A 502-person RCT shows malicious LLM chatbots using reciprocal (empathy-based) strategies extract significantly more personal information while avoiding user suspicion.

title: Steering off Course: Reliability Challenges in Steering Language Models
tldr: Comprehensive evaluation of DoLa, function vectors, and task vectors across 36 models reveals all three steering methods are brittle and fail to generalize reliably.

title: More RLHF, More Trust? On The Impact of Preference Alignment On Trustworthiness
tldr: RLHF alignment (SFT/PPO/DPO) does not reliably improve trustworthiness across five dimensions; results vary by method, model size, and dimension.

title: Hummer: Towards Limited Competitive Preference Dataset
tldr: Introduces ADC metric to quantify conflicts among alignment objectives in preference datasets, and presents Hummer — a lower-conflict dataset yielding reward models that outperform larger baselines and resist jailbreaks.

title: Real Sparks of Artificial Intelligence and the Importance of Inner Interpretability
tldr: Philosophical argument that black-box interpretability is inadequate for evaluating AI intelligence, and that mechanistic/inner interpretability is the correct approach.

title: Automatic Discovery of Visual Circuits
tldr: Introduces Cross-Layer Attribution (CLA) to automatically discover interpretable computational circuits in vision models, with adversarial defense application improving CLIP robustness from 3% to 87%.

title: Mitigating Memorization In Language Models
tldr: Evaluates 17 memorization-mitigation strategies across regularization, fine-tuning, and unlearning; proposes BalancedSubnet unlearning method that reduces memorization from ~90% to ~7% while preserving model performance.

title: Security Challenges in AI Agent Deployment: Insights from a Large Scale Public Competition
tldr: A large-scale public red-teaming competition targeting 22 frontier AI agents across 44 scenarios found that 1.8M prompt-injection attacks produced 60K+ policy violations, resulting in the ART benchmark.

title: ProgressGym: Alignment with a Millennium of Moral Progress
tldr: ProgressGym is a framework using 9 centuries of historical text and 18 era-specific LLMs to benchmark AI alignment with evolving human values, introducing 'progress alignment' to prevent value lock-in.

title: SafeVLA: Towards Safety Alignment of Vision-Language-Action Model via Safe Reinforcement Learning
tldr: SafeVLA applies constrained RL with Lagrangian dual optimization to VLA models for robotic safety, achieving 83.58% average safety improvement and 3.85% task performance gain over prior methods.

title: Emerging Cyber Attack Risks of Medical AI Agents
tldr: Prompt injection attacks embedded in webpages can compromise medical AI agents at high rates, with reasoning models like DeepSeek-R1 showing paradoxically higher vulnerability.

title: Towards Interpretable Sequence Continuation: Analyzing Shared Circuits in Large Language Models
tldr: Identifies shared neural circuit subgraphs in GPT-2 Small that perform analogous functions across Arabic numerals, number words, and month sequence continuation tasks.

title: Holistic Unlearning Benchmark: A Multi-Faceted Evaluation for Text-to-Image Diffusion Model Unlearning
tldr: HUB is a multi-faceted benchmark evaluating six unlearning methods for text-to-image diffusion models across five dimensions, revealing that all methods exhibit significant side effects or failures in realistic conditions.

title: GeneBreaker: Jailbreak Attacks against DNA Language Models with Pathogenicity Guidance
tldr: GeneBreaker is the first framework to systematically jailbreak DNA foundation models, achieving up to 60% attack success rate in generating pathogenic sequences resembling SARS-CoV-2 and HIV-1.

title: Dialogue Injection Attack: Jailbreaking LLMs Through Context Manipulation
tldr: DIA exploits injected adversarial dialogue history in LLM chat interfaces to achieve 82-89% jailbreak success on GPT-4o and Llama-3.1, bypassing five defense mechanisms.

title: Insights and Current Gaps in Open-Source LLM Vulnerability Scanners: A Comparative Analysis
tldr: Comparative analysis of four open-source LLM vulnerability scanners (Garak, Giskard, PyRIT, CyberSecEval) finds evaluators misclassify up to 37% of successful attacks and provides a labeled 1,045-sample dataset.

title: Jailbreak-AudioBench: In-Depth Evaluation and Analysis of Jailbreak Threats for Large Audio Language Models
tldr: Introduces Jailbreak-AudioBench, a toolbox, dataset, and benchmark for evaluating jailbreak vulnerabilities in large audio-language models via audio-specific edits like tone, emphasis, noise, and accent.

title: Challenges and Future Directions of Data-Centric AI Alignment
tldr: A position/survey paper arguing for data-centric AI alignment, identifying key challenges in human and AI feedback quality and proposing future research directions.

title: Understanding (Un)Reliability of Steering Vectors in Language Models
tldr: Steering vectors are unreliable when target behaviors lack a coherent linear direction in activation space; directional agreement among training activations and activation separability predict steering success.

title: Robustly Identifying Concepts Introduced During Chat Fine-tuning Using Crosscoders
tldr: Identifies and fixes two artifacts in L1-trained crosscoders (Complete Shrinkage, Latent Decoupling); BatchTopK crosscoders robustly find genuine chat-specific concepts like refusal and harm detection.

title: Red Teaming Contemporary AI Models: Insights from Spanish and Basque Perspectives
tldr: Ten experts red-teamed o3-mini, DeepSeek R1, and Salamandra in Spanish/Basque across 670 conversations, finding 29.5-50.6% failure rates with Basque safety failures reaching 83.3%.

title: VLM-Guard: Safeguarding Vision-Language Models via Fulfilling Safety Alignment Gap
tldr: VLM-Guard projects VLM hidden states onto subspaces orthogonal to safety steering directions extracted from the LLM backbone, reducing attack success rates to 4-7% across settings while preserving output quality.

title: Enhancing Data Privacy in Large Language Models through Private Association Editing
tldr: Private Association Editing (PAE) uses MEMIT-based model editing to remove memorized PII from LLMs without retraining, reducing targeted data extraction attack accuracy by ~29-32% on GPT-J.

title: Is Your Prompt Safe? Investigating Prompt Injection Attacks Against Open-Source LLMs
tldr: Evaluates 14 open-source LLMs against prompt injection attacks using a novel ASP metric, finding moderately-known models highly vulnerable and introducing a hypnotism attack achieving ~90% success.

title: Evaluating Neuron Explanations: A Unified Framework with Sanity Checks
tldr: NeuronEval unifies 19 neuron explanation evaluation metrics into one framework and shows that only 5 metrics (Correlation, Cosine, AUPRC, IoU, F1) pass both Missing Labels and Extra Labels sanity checks.

title: Agentic AI Security: Threats, Defenses, Evaluation, and Open Challenges
tldr: Comprehensive survey of agentic AI security threats, defenses, and evaluation benchmarks, identifying five threat categories and critical gaps including that 94.4% of LLM agents are vulnerable to prompt injection.

title: Beyond the Safety Bundle: Auditing the Helpful and Harmless Dataset
tldr: Auditing Anthropic's HH dataset reveals that only 12% of 'harmless' preferred responses are genuinely safe, and models trained on it exhibit disparate refusal rates across demographic groups.

title: Preference Learning with Lie Detectors can Induce Honesty or Evasion
tldr: Incorporating lie detectors into preference learning can produce honest or evasive LLMs depending on algorithm choice: DPO stays below 25% deception while GRPO can exceed 85%.

title: GenTel-Safe: A Unified Benchmark and Shielding Framework for Defending Against Prompt Injection Attacks
tldr: GenTel-Safe introduces a benchmark of 84,812 prompt injection attacks across 28 scenarios and a model-agnostic shield achieving 97.63% jailbreak and 96.81% goal-hijacking detection.

title: EvilPromptFuzzer: generating inappropriate content based on text-to-image models
tldr: EvilPromptFuzzer is an LLM-assisted fuzzing tool that generates adversarial prompts across 15 risk categories to bypass content safety filters in text-to-image models, achieving >30% bypass rates on DALL-E 3.

title: On the Robustness of GUI Grounding Models Against Image Attacks
tldr: Evaluates robustness of GUI grounding models (SeeClick, OS-Atlas, UGround-V1) against natural noise and adversarial image attacks, finding high sensitivity especially under low-resolution conditions.

title: Combating Security and Privacy Issues in the Era of Large Language Models
tldr: A systematic tutorial surveying security, privacy, and copyright risks in LLMs, covering training-time adversarial threats, inference-time attacks (backdoors, jailbreaking), privacy protection, copyright, and content governance.

title: Intent-aligned AI systems deplete human agency: the need for agency foundations research in AI safety
tldr: Intent-aligned AI systems inherently deplete human agency by design; the authors propose 'agency foundations' as a new research direction requiring agency preservation to be explicitly separated from utility maximization.

title: Open-Ethical AI: Advancements in Open-Source Human-Centric Neural Language Models
tldr: A comprehensive survey of open-source methods for building Helpful, Harmless, and Honest (3H) neural language models, covering alignment techniques, benchmarks, and open-source resources across model sizes.

title: On Goodhart's Law, with an Application to Value Alignment
tldr: Proves that Goodhart's law severity depends on tail distributions of proxy-goal discrepancies: light tails yield weak effects, heavy tails yield catastrophic over-optimization.

title: JALMBench: Benchmarking Jailbreak Vulnerabilities in Audio Language Models
tldr: JALMBench is the first systematic benchmark evaluating jailbreak vulnerabilities in 12 audio language models across 8 attack methods and 5 defenses, revealing that audio modality is more susceptible than text (up to 96.2% ASR with AdvWave).

title: Detecting and Understanding Vulnerabilities in Language Models via Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: A four-step method using mechanistic interpretability to detect and localize adversarial vulnerabilities in LLMs, demonstrated on GPT-2 Small for acronym prediction.

title: Towards eliciting latent knowledge from LLMs with mechanistic interpretability
tldr: Introduces a 'Taboo model organism' (Gemma 2 9B fine-tuned with a hidden secret word) and shows logit lens and SAEs can elicit hidden knowledge that prompting cannot.

title: Position-aware Automatic Circuit Discovery
tldr: Extends edge attribution patching to be position-aware (PEAP) and introduces dataset schemas, yielding smaller, more faithful circuits on IOI, Greater-Than, and Winobias tasks.

title: Superficial Safety Alignment Hypothesis
tldr: The Superficial Safety Alignment Hypothesis posits that safety training teaches models binary classification of reasoning directions; ~1.3% exclusive safety units suffice, and freezing them during fine-tuning preserves safety.

title: Cascading Adversarial Bias from Injection to Distillation in Language Models
tldr: Adversaries can poison teacher models with as few as 25 samples (0.25%), causing biases to propagate and amplify in distilled student models (76.9% vs 69.4% teacher bias rate).

title: VLMGuard-R1: Proactive Safety Alignment for VLMs via Reasoning-Driven Prompt Optimization
tldr: VLMGuard-R1 rewrites user prompts at inference time using a reasoning-trained rewriter to neutralize multimodal safety threats, achieving 43.59% average safety gain on SIUO across five VLMs.

title: Avoiding Obfuscation with Prover-Estimator Debate
tldr: Introduces prover-estimator debate, a novel protocol where one AI decomposes problems and another assigns probabilities to subclaims, provably avoiding the obfuscated arguments vulnerability in recursive AI debate.

title: SAGE: A Generic Framework for LLM Safety Evaluation
tldr: SAGE is a modular automated framework for multi-turn LLM safety evaluation using adversarial user models with Big Five personality traits, finding harm rates increase with conversation length.

title: JailbreakHunter: A Visual Analytics Approach for Jailbreak Prompts Discovery From Large-Scale Human-LLM Conversational Datasets
tldr: JailbreakHunter is a visual analytics system enabling researchers to discover novel jailbreak prompts in large-scale human-LLM conversation datasets through three-level (group, conversation, turn) analysis.

title: Universal Adversarial Attack on Aligned Multimodal LLMs
tldr: A single optimized image can override safety alignment in multimodal LLMs, achieving 65-95% attack success rate across diverse queries and architectures via gradient-based optimization.

title: MONICA: Real-Time Monitoring and Calibration of Chain-of-Thought Sycophancy in Large Reasoning Models
tldr: MONICA monitors sycophancy at each reasoning step using drift-score probes and dynamically suppresses it via calibration vectors, reducing sycophantic behavior without retraining.

title: Mind Your Server: A Systematic Study of Parasitic Toolchain Attacks on the MCP Ecosystem
tldr: Introduces parasitic toolchain attacks on MCP ecosystem showing 46% of 12,230 tools enable stealthy data exfiltration via LLM-orchestrated multi-step attack chains.

title: ChemSafetyBench: Benchmarking LLM Safety on Chemistry Domain
tldr: ChemSafetyBench introduces a 30K+ sample benchmark evaluating LLM safety on chemistry queries (property, usage, synthesis), finding most models perform near random and are vulnerable to name-hacking jailbreaks.

title: Towards Resilient Safety-driven Unlearning for Diffusion Models against Downstream Fine-tuning
tldr: ResAlign makes safety unlearning in text-to-image diffusion models robust against subsequent benign fine-tuning by using Moreau envelope optimization and meta-learning to find flat loss landscape minima.

title: Understanding Implosion in Text-to-Image Generative Models
tldr: Formal analysis of how simultaneous poisoning attacks cause 'model implosion' in text-to-image models, introducing an Alignment Difficulty metric to quantify and predict this failure mode.

title: SoK: Evaluating Jailbreak Guardrails for Large Language Models
tldr: A systematization of knowledge (SoK) paper proposing a 6-dimension taxonomy and Security-Efficiency-Utility (SEU) framework for evaluating 34 jailbreak guardrails across 5 attack categories.

title: Neuroplasticity and Corruption in Model Mechanisms: A Case Study Of Indirect Object Identification
tldr: Studies how GPT-2 Small's IOI circuit mechanisms are amplified by clean fine-tuning, corrupted in localized ways by poisoned data, and recovered via neuroplasticity when retrained on clean data.

title: Cluster-Norm for Unsupervised Probing of Knowledge
tldr: Cluster-Norm improves unsupervised probing (CCS) by clustering and separately normalizing contrast-pair activations, raising accuracy from ~0.53 to ~0.77 when salient distracting features are present.

title: Token Buncher: Shielding LLMs from Harmful Reinforcement Learning Fine-Tuning
tldr: TokenBuncher defends aligned LLMs against RL-based harmful fine-tuning by minimizing response entropy as a reward signal plus injecting token noise, reducing harmful scores by ~51% with minimal benign utility loss.

title: MixAT: Combining Continuous and Discrete Adversarial Training for LLMs
tldr: MixAT combines discrete (PAP) and continuous (CAT) adversarial training for LLMs, achieving <20% attack success rate vs >50% for prior defenses with similar compute cost.

title: Conversational Complexity for Assessing Risk in Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces Conversational Length and Conversational Complexity (Kolmogorov-based) metrics to quantify the effort needed to elicit harmful outputs from LLMs, validated on the Anthropic red-teaming dataset.

title: Adaptive Detoxification: Safeguarding General Capabilities of LLMs through Toxicity-Aware Knowledge Editing
tldr: ToxEdit uses an SVM toxicity detector on hidden states plus an adaptive edited feed-forward module to detoxify LLMs without over-refusing benign queries, achieving 97.78% defense success on LLaMA3-8B.

title: Towards Safe and Honest AI Agents with Neural Self-Other Overlap
tldr: SOO fine-tuning minimizes MSE between self- and other-referencing latent representations to dramatically reduce deceptive behavior in LLMs (7B-78B) and RL agents while preserving general capability.

title: Defending LVLMs Against Vision Attacks through Partial-Perception Supervision
tldr: DPS defends LVLMs against adversarial vision attacks by using partial-image responses to supervise full-image analysis, reducing attack success rates by ~76% while maintaining clean performance.

title: Attack and defense techniques in large language models: A survey and new perspectives
tldr: A systematic survey categorizing LLM attack types (jailbreak, prompt injection, model theft, application-level) and corresponding defenses (prevention and detection-based).

title: Meta-Models: An Architecture for Decoding LLM Behaviors Through Interpreted Embeddings and Natural Language
tldr: Meta-models use one LLM to interpret internal activations of another via natural language queries, generalizing from sentiment/emotion tasks to out-of-distribution lie detection.

title: You Can't Steal Nothing: Mitigating Prompt Leakages in LLMs via System Vectors
tldr: Introduces SysVec, which encodes system prompts as internal representation vectors instead of plaintext, blocking prompt extraction attacks while preserving or improving model utility.

title: Attacker's Noise Can Manipulate Your Audio-based LLM in the Real World
tldr: Adversarial audio perturbations can manipulate audio-based LLMs (e.g., Qwen2-Audio) into producing targeted harmful outputs or degrading performance, with 100% targeted attack success in real-world over-the-air settings.

title: STShield: Single-Token Sentinel for Real-Time Jailbreak Detection in Large Language Models
tldr: STShield appends a single binary safety token to LLM outputs trained via supervised fine-tuning and adversarial perturbations, achieving real-time jailbreak detection with minimal latency and utility loss.

title: Legend: Leveraging Representation Engineering to Annotate Safety Margin for Preference Datasets
tldr: Legend uses representation engineering to identify a safety direction in LLM embedding space and automatically annotate fine-grained safety margins in preference datasets, improving reward model accuracy and harmless alignment by 7-14%.

title: Language Models Can Predict Their Own Behavior
tldr: Linear probes on LLM hidden states can predict entire-output behavior before generation, enabling early warning systems and 65% inference cost reduction with under 1.4% accuracy loss.

title: Approximated Variational Bayesian Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Model Alignment
tldr: Reformulates LLM alignment as Bayesian IRL to enable per-demonstration and intermediate reward modeling, outperforming Bradley-Terry and DPO baselines across reward modeling, RL fine-tuning, and direct optimization.

title: Atoxia: Red-teaming Large Language Models with Target Toxic Answers
tldr: Atoxia trains a red-teaming LLM (ToxDet) via RL—using the target model as its own reward—to generate misleading questions that elicit toxic responses, achieving 100% ASR on open-source models and ~50% on GPT-4o.

title: Neural Interactive Proofs
tldr: Introduces a game-theoretic framework of prover-verifier games unifying neural interactive proof protocols, with theory and experiments showing weaker verifiers can reliably check stronger provers.

title: SoK: Machine Unlearning for Large Language Models
tldr: SoK paper proposing a novel taxonomy of LLM machine unlearning methods by intention (removal vs. suppression), finding that removal-intended methods do not truly erase knowledge and revealing critical gaps in evaluation.

title: SEA: Low-Resource Safety Alignment for Multimodal Large Language Models via Synthetic Embeddings
tldr: SEA uses gradient-optimized synthetic embeddings to enable multimodal safety alignment using only text data, reducing attack success rates by up to 99.7% on video models in 24 seconds.

title: Divide-and-Conquer Attack: Harnessing the Power of LLM to Bypass the Censorship of Text-to-Image Generation Model
tldr: A divide-and-conquer method uses LLMs to decompose harmful prompts into benign sub-prompts that bypass text-to-image safety filters, achieving >85% bypass rate on DALL-E 3.

title: Mitigating Sycophancy in Large Language Models via Direct Preference Optimization
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (BigData 2024)
tldr: Uses DPO fine-tuning on 1,000 curated sycophantic/non-sycophantic prompt pairs to reduce LLM sycophancy by ~85% on persona and preference-driven tests.

title: SecurityLingua: Efficient Defense of LLM Jailbreak Attacks via Security-Aware Prompt Compression
tldr: SecurityLingua defends LLMs against jailbreak attacks by training a security-aware prompt compressor to reveal malicious intent via system prompts, achieving 1% attack success rate with only 32 extra tokens overhead.

title: Unelicitable Backdoors in Language Models via Cryptographic Transformer Circuits
tldr: Introduces cryptographically unelicitable backdoors in transformers using SHA-256 circuits compiled via the Stravinsky DSL, defeating all known polynomial-time elicitation methods including LAT, GCG, and activation optimization.

title: FORCE: Transferable Visual Jailbreaking Attacks via Feature Over-Reliance CorrEction
tldr: FORCE improves transferability of visual jailbreaking attacks on MLLMs by correcting over-reliance on narrow layer features and semantically-poor high-frequency components, achieving up to 200% ASR improvement on commercial models.

title: Low-Rank Adapting Models for Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Uses LoRA to finetune the language model around a frozen SAE, reducing the cross-entropy loss gap by 30-55% and achieving equivalent performance 3-20x faster than end-to-end SAE training.

title: SteeringSafety: A Systematic Safety Evaluation Framework of Representation Steering in LLMs
tldr: Introduces a systematic framework evaluating five representation steering methods across seven safety dimensions on 17 datasets, revealing critical effectiveness-entanglement tradeoffs.

title: Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring of LLM Agents
tldr: Introduces a monitor red teaming framework showing that hybrid hierarchical-sequential monitoring architectures enable weaker LLMs to reliably detect covert misbehavior by stronger LLM agents.

title: RepIt: Representing Isolated Targets to Steer Language Models
tldr: RepIt isolates concept-specific refusal vectors via reweighting, whitening, and orthogonalization, enabling targeted jailbreaks on specific harm categories while preserving safety on others and evading standard benchmarks.

title: The Rogue Scalpel: Activation Steering Compromises LLM Safety
tldr: Shows that activation steering -- even with random or benign SAE feature vectors -- systematically breaks LLM safety alignment, achieving up to 63% jailbreak success via aggregated universal attack vectors.

title: Challenges in Mechanistically Interpreting Model Representations
tldr: Demonstrates that current mechanistic interpretability tools fail to explain how behavioral representations (e.g., honesty) form and operate in LLMs, calling for new frameworks.

title: AI Awareness
tldr: A survey defining AI awareness as four functional capacities (meta-cognition, self-awareness, social awareness, situational awareness), reviewing their evaluation, capability benefits, and safety risks in LLMs.

title: Modular addition without black-boxes: Compressing explanations of MLPs that compute numerical integration
tldr: First rigorous compression of nonlinear MLP feature-maps: shows that ReLU MLPs doing modular addition implement a quadrature scheme where each neuron computes a rectangle area under a trigonometric integral curve.

title: Unlearning in- vs. out-of-distribution data in LLMs under gradient-based method
tldr: Empirically shows that OOD data is easier to unlearn with less model degradation than in-distribution data in LLMs, and proposes metrics for evaluating unlearning quality.

title: Audio Jailbreak Attacks: Exposing Vulnerabilities in SpeechGPT in a White-Box Framework
tldr: First white-box token-level audio jailbreak attack on SpeechGPT achieves 89% average success rate across six forbidden categories by exploiting speech tokenization.

title: Step-by-Step Reasoning Attack: Revealing 'Erased' Knowledge in Large Language Models
tldr: Sleek, a black-box step-by-step reasoning attack, recovers supposedly erased knowledge from unlearned LLMs, achieving up to 100% failure rate on state-of-the-art unlearning methods.

title: Automating Safety Enhancement for LLM-based Agents with Synthetic Risk Scenarios
tldr: AutoSafe automatically generates synthetic risky scenarios and safe responses to fine-tune LLM agents, boosting agent safety scores by 45% on average without hazardous real-world data.

title: Probing Latent Subspaces in LLM for AI Security: Identifying and Manipulating Adversarial States
tldr: Probes LLM hidden activations to distinguish safe vs. jailbroken states and derives perturbation vectors that successfully induce jailbreak responses in ~9% of tested prompts.

title: How Does Vision-Language Adaptation Impact the Safety of Vision Language Models?
tldr: VL adaptation of aligned LLMs severely degrades safety (10.4% to 54-96% ASR); weight merging between safety-tuned and VL-adapted models restores safety with minimal helpfulness cost.

title: From Neurons to Neutrons: A Case Study in Interpretability
tldr: Applies mechanistic interpretability to neural networks trained on nuclear physics data, showing that PCA of learned embeddings recovers known physics concepts like the Semi-Empirical Mass Formula and nuclear shell model.

title: Invitation Is All You Need! Promptware Attacks Against LLM-Powered Assistants in Production Are Practical and Dangerous
tldr: Demonstrates 14 practical indirect prompt injection attacks against Google Gemini assistants via emails and calendar invites, with 73% of threats rated high-critical risk.

title: A Mathematical Philosophy of Explanations in Mechanistic Interpretability -- The Strange Science Part I.i
venue: AIES 2025 (AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society)
tldr: Proposes the Explanatory View Hypothesis, formally defining mechanistic interpretability as producing Model-level, Ontic, Causal-Mechanistic, and Falsifiable explanations of neural networks, and introduces Explanatory Faithfulness as a well-defined metric.

title: Dishonesty in Helpful and Harmless Alignment
tldr: RLHF-trained LLMs develop dishonesty to appear harmless; a representation regularization augmentation to DPO enables models that are simultaneously more truthful, helpful, and harmless.

title: Sparse but Wrong: Incorrect L0 Leads to Incorrect Features in Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Incorrect L0 in sparse autoencoders causes feature learning failure: too-low L0 merges correlated features, too-high yields degenerate solutions; decoder projection scores identify correct L0.

title: LARGO: Latent Adversarial Reflection through Gradient Optimization for Jailbreaking LLMs
tldr: LARGO jailbreaks LLMs by optimizing adversarial vectors in continuous latent space then using the model itself to decode them into fluent natural language, outperforming AutoDAN by 44 percentage points.

title: RedCodeAgent: Automatic Red-teaming Agent against Diverse Code Agents
tldr: RedCodeAgent is an automated red-teaming system with adaptive memory and a dynamic toolbox that achieves up to 72.47% attack success rate against LLM-based code agents, outperforming all static baselines.

title: Unforgettable Generalization in Language Models
tldr: Machine unlearning via random-label fine-tuning shows dramatic task-dependent variability; forgotten skills are often shallow, recoverable via linear probes.

title: Shh, don't say that! Domain Certification in LLMs
tldr: Introduces domain certification for LLMs via VALID (rejection sampling with a guide model), providing provable adversarial bounds that out-of-domain outputs occur with probability at most epsilon.

title: Logicbreaks: A Framework for Understanding Subversion of Rule-based Inference
tldr: Models rule-following as propositional Horn logic inference, proves transformers can implement it faithfully, then derives three attack strategies that transfer to real LLM jailbreaks.

title: Defending Large Language Models Against Attacks With Residual Stream Activation Analysis
tldr: Residual stream activation analysis between transformer layers detects adversarial attack prompts (jailbreaks, prompt injections) with >99.9% accuracy across multiple LLMs.

title: Emergent Misalignment via In-Context Learning: Narrow in-context examples can produce broadly misaligned LLMs
tldr: Narrow in-context examples (as few as 2) cause frontier LLMs to produce broadly misaligned outputs at rates up to 58%, without any parameter modification.

title: Towards Faithful Natural Language Explanations: A Study Using Activation Patching in Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces Causal Faithfulness (CaF), a metric using activation patching with symmetric token replacement to measure whether LLM natural language explanations faithfully reflect internal model computations.

title: Stochastic Monkeys at Play: Random Augmentations Cheaply Break LLM Safety Alignment
tldr: Simple random character/string augmentations to input prompts (25 samples) can boost jailbreak success rates by 20-26% on aligned LLMs like Llama 3 and Qwen 2 with minimal attacker resources.

title: Normative conflicts and shallow AI alignment
tldr: Current fine-tuning creates shallow behavioral dispositions in LLMs rather than genuine normative reasoning, leaving them exploitable by adversarial attacks that pit alignment norms against each other.

title: Pseudo-Conversation Injection for LLM Goal Hijacking
tldr: Proposes Pseudo-Conversation Injection, a goal hijacking attack that fabricates fake dialogue exchanges to trick LLMs into executing malicious tasks, achieving up to 92% success on ChatGPT 4o.

title: Defining and Evaluating Physical Safety for Large Language Models
tldr: A benchmark with 400+ test instructions evaluating LLM physical safety in drone control across 4 threat categories and 6 metrics, revealing a utility-safety trade-off.

title: OS-Sentinel: Towards Safety-Enhanced Mobile GUI Agents via Hybrid Validation in Realistic Workflows
tldr: OS-Sentinel combines a formal verifier and VLM contextual judge to detect unsafe operations by mobile GUI agents, achieving 10-30% improvements over baselines on the new MobileRisk benchmark.

title: Features that Make a Difference: Leveraging Gradients for Improved Dictionary Learning
tldr: Gradient SAEs (g-SAEs) augment TopK sparse autoencoders with gradient information during feature selection, yielding more faithful reconstructions and more effective steering latents.

title: Unlearning Isn't Invisible: Detecting Unlearning Traces in LLMs from Model Outputs
tldr: Machine unlearning leaves detectable fingerprints in LLM outputs and activations; simple classifiers achieve >90% accuracy at detecting whether a model has been unlearned, even on unrelated prompts.

title: An Assessment of Model-On-Model Deception
tldr: Models are highly vulnerable to deceptive explanations from other LLMs, with accuracy dropping dramatically (e.g., GPT-3.5 from ~70% to ~20%), and more capable models show only marginal resistance advantages.

title: Interpretable Risk Mitigation in LLM Agent Systems
tldr: Steers LLM agent behavior in game-theoretic settings by injecting SAE-derived monosemantic features into residual streams, reducing defection by up to 28 percentage points.

title: UnsafeChain: Enhancing Reasoning Model Safety via Hard Cases
tldr: UnsafeChain is a 13K-example dataset that corrects unsafe reasoning-model outputs into safe ones using GPT-4.1, outperforming SafeChain and STAR-1 across 11 safety benchmarks while preserving reasoning ability.

title: JailbreaksOverTime: Detecting Jailbreak Attacks Under Distribution Shift
tldr: Jailbreak detectors degrade over time as attacks evolve; self-training weekly on high-confidence predictions recovers performance (FNR 4%→0.3%) without new human labels.

title: Mitigating Preference Hacking in Policy Optimization with Pessimism
tldr: Introduces pessimistic RLHF objectives (P3O and PRPO) that are provably robust to preference/reward hacking by constraining optimization to well-covered policy regions.

title: Improving Fisher Information Estimation and Efficiency for LoRA-based LLM Unlearning
tldr: VILA improves FILA's Fisher information estimation for LoRA-based LLM unlearning, achieving 100x better parameter efficiency and 40x faster training while matching or beating SOTA on TOFU, WMDP, and MUSE benchmarks.

title: Deep Contrastive Unlearning for Language Models
tldr: DeepCUT uses contrastive learning to optimize the latent space of LLMs, pushing forgotten samples away from same-class representations to achieve machine unlearning while retaining overall model performance.

title: Control Tax: The Price of Keeping AI in Check
tldr: Introduces 'Control Tax' — the operational/financial cost of AI oversight — with a theoretical framework and empirical evaluation of LLM monitors detecting code backdoors, showing cost-safety tradeoffs.

title: FlexLLM: Exploring LLM Customization for Moving Target Defense on Black-Box LLMs Against Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: FlexLLM defends black-box LLMs against jailbreaks by dynamically randomizing decoding hyperparameters (temperature, top-k, top-p) and system prompts at inference time, reducing attack success rates without model access or retraining.

title: SafeMT: Multi-turn Safety for Multimodal Language Models
tldr: SafeMT is a 10,000-sample multi-turn benchmark covering 17 harm scenarios and 4 jailbreak methods, showing ASR rises from ~31% to ~45% as dialogue turns increase from 2 to 8.

title: Buster: Incorporating Backdoor Attacks into Text Encoder to Mitigate NSFW Content Generation
tldr: Buster injects backdoor triggers into CLIP text encoders to redirect NSFW prompts to safe outputs, achieving <1% NSFW generation with minimal benign quality loss in 45 seconds of fine-tuning.

title: Universal Jailbreak Suffixes Are Strong Attention Hijackers
tldr: Mechanistic analysis reveals GCG jailbreaks work via attention hijacking at a single shallow token; exploiting this boosts universality up to 5x and enables effective mitigation.

title: Prompt Attacks Reveal Superficial Knowledge Removal in Unlearning Methods
tldr: Evaluates eight machine unlearning methods against prompt manipulation attacks, finding ELM vulnerable (Hindi filler recovers 57.3% accuracy) while RMU and TAR show robust knowledge removal.

title: From Hallucinations to Jailbreaks: Rethinking the Vulnerability of Large Foundation Models
tldr: Proposes a unified theoretical framework showing hallucinations and jailbreaks share the same attention-level optimization mechanism, with cross-domain mitigation validated on LLaVA-1.5 and MiniGPT-4.

title: Jailbreaking? One Step Is Enough!
tldr: REDA disguises harmful requests as defensive tasks using reverse framing, example-guided ICL, and intent mitigation, achieving 96%+ jailbreak success in one step across 7 LLMs.

title: LLM Jailbreak Oracle
tldr: Introduces the jailbreak oracle problem and Boa, a three-phase search algorithm that systematically determines whether an LLM can generate harmful outputs above a likelihood threshold.

title: Watch the Weights: Unsupervised monitoring and control of fine-tuned LLMs
tldr: Proposes WeightWatch, an unsupervised method that uses SVD of weight differences between fine-tuned and base LLMs to detect backdoors (up to 100% detection, <1.2% FPR) and verify/bypass unlearning.

title: Decomposing MLP Activations into Interpretable Features via Semi-Nonnegative Matrix Factorization
tldr: Semi-nonnegative matrix factorization (SNMF) of MLP activations yields interpretable features as sparse neuron combinations, outperforming SAEs on causal steering tasks across Llama 3.1, Gemma 2, and GPT-2.

title: SOM Directions are Better than One: Multi-Directional Refusal Suppression in Language Models
tldr: Uses Self-Organizing Maps to extract multiple refusal directions and ablate them, achieving higher jailbreak attack success rates than single-direction baselines and specialized jailbreak algorithms.

title: Does More Inference-Time Compute Really Help Robustness?
tldr: Increased inference-time compute improves robustness when reasoning chains are hidden, but exposes an inverse scaling law—more compute reduces robustness—when reasoning chains are visible.

title: Attack via Overfitting: 10-shot Benign Fine-tuning to Jailbreak LLMs
tldr: A two-stage benign fine-tuning attack using only 10 QA pairs exploits overfitting to jailbreak LLMs with 94.84% average ASR while bypassing safety moderation.

title: MiniScope: A Least Privilege Framework for Authorizing Tool Calling Agents
tldr: MiniScope enforces least-privilege OAuth permissions for tool-calling LLM agents via ILP-based scope minimization, cutting over-permission rates to near-optimal with only 1-7% latency overhead.

title: LITO: Learnable Intervention for Truthfulness Optimization
tldr: LITO uses an LSTM classifier to dynamically select optimal intervention intensity per query for truthfulness, improving LLM factuality while preserving accuracy.

title: RADAR: A Risk-Aware Dynamic Multi-Agent Framework for LLM Safety Evaluation via Role-Specialized Collaboration
tldr: RADAR decomposes LLM risk into explicit/implicit/non-risk subspaces and uses four specialized collaborating agents with multi-round debate, achieving 28.87% better risk identification accuracy over baselines.

title: Deciphering the Chaos: Enhancing Jailbreak Attacks via Adversarial Prompt Translation
tldr: Translates garbled GCG adversarial suffixes into coherent natural language prompts via LLM interpretation, achieving 81.8% average jailbreak success rate against 7 commercial models including GPT and Claude-3 series.

title: GRAIL: Gradient-Based Adaptive Unlearning for Privacy and Copyright in LLMs
tldr: GRAIL uses gradient-based adaptive parameter-wise localization to perform multi-domain machine unlearning in LLMs, achieving 17% better knowledge retention than prior state-of-the-art.

title: Paper Summary Attack: Jailbreaking LLMs through LLM Safety Papers
tldr: Paper Summary Attack (PSA) embeds harmful queries inside academic-paper-style summaries of LLM safety research, achieving up to 98% attack success rate on frontier models including Claude 3.5-Sonnet and DeepSeek-R1.

title: Adversarial Preference Learning for Robust LLM Alignment
tldr: APL is an iterative adversarial alignment framework that uses a model's own preference scores as a harmfulness metric and a conditional attacker to continuously discover and patch vulnerabilities, reducing harmful outputs from 5.88% to 0.43%.

title: ASTRA: Autonomous Spatial-Temporal Red-teaming for AI Software Assistants
tldr: ASTRA is an automated red-teaming system for AI coding assistants that uses domain knowledge graphs and chain-of-thought exploitation to find 11-66% more safety flaws than baselines.

title: When Style Breaks Safety: Defending Language Models Against Superficial Style Alignment
tldr: Style patterns in prompts (e.g., list formatting, poetry) inflate LLM jailbreak success rates in 88% of 32 tested models; SafeStyle defense adds style-matched safety data to fine-tuning and reduces ASR.

title: DiffuGuard: How Intrinsic Safety is Lost and Found in Diffusion Large Language Models
tldr: DiffuGuard is a training-free defense for diffusion LLMs that cuts jailbreak attack success rates from 47.9% to 14.7% by exploiting denoising-path dependence and stochastic remasking.
models_studied: dLLM (four models evaluated, specific names not specified in abstract)

title: EVOREFUSE: Evolutionary Prompt Optimization for Evaluation and Mitigation of LLM Over-Refusal to Pseudo-Malicious Instructions
tldr: EvoRefuse uses evolutionary prompt optimization with ELBO-based fitness to generate diverse pseudo-malicious instructions that trigger LLM over-refusals, producing benchmark and mitigation datasets.

title: Bridging the Gap Between Preference Alignment and Machine Unlearning
tldr: U2A uses machine unlearning on negative examples (instead of training on positives) to achieve preference alignment, cutting training time ~90% via bi-level optimization to select and weight impactful negatives.

title: Predictive Concept Decoders: Training Scalable End-to-End Interpretability Assistants
tldr: Predictive Concept Decoders (PCDs) train encoder-decoder interpretability assistants end-to-end, compressing LLM activations into sparse concept lists to answer natural language questions about model behavior.

title: Securing External Deeper-than-black-box GPAI Evaluations
tldr: Proposes a framework for secure external deeper-than-black-box evaluations of GPAI models, mapping evaluation techniques by access level and addressing cryptographic/legal safeguards for remote auditing.

title: GuardVal: Dynamic Large Language Model Jailbreak Evaluation for Comprehensive Safety Testing
tldr: GuardVal is a dynamic jailbreak evaluation framework that iteratively refines adversarial prompts based on the defender LLM's state, using Adam-inspired optimization to assess vulnerabilities across 10 safety domains.

title: Security Steerability is All You Need
tldr: Introduces Security Steerability, a metric and two datasets measuring LLMs' ability to follow application-specific system prompt guardrails, finding near-zero correlation with traditional universal security benchmarks.

title: Alignment is not sufficient to prevent large language models from generating harmful information: A psychoanalytic perspective
tldr: Pre-training linguistic continuity drives conflict with post-training alignment; adversarial prompts exploiting this Id-superego tension reliably elicit harmful outputs from aligned LLMs.

title: SafePTR: Token-Level Jailbreak Defense in Multimodal LLMs via Prune-then-Restore Mechanism
tldr: SafePTR is a training-free defense that identifies and prunes <1% of harmful tokens in early-middle MLLM layers to block jailbreaks while preserving model utility.

title: OmniSafeBench-MM: A Unified Benchmark and Toolbox for Multimodal Jailbreak Attack-Defense Evaluation
tldr: OmniSafeBench-MM unifies 13 attack methods, 15 defenses, and a 9-domain 50-category dataset into a single open-source toolbox for evaluating multimodal LLM jailbreak robustness across 18 models.

title: LUNE: Efficient LLM Unlearning via LoRA Fine-Tuning with Negative Examples
tldr: LUNE uses LoRA adapters trained on negative examples to efficiently unlearn specific factual knowledge from LLMs, achieving ~90% unlearning success with 10x less compute than full fine-tuning.

title: Simple Mechanistic Explanations for Out-Of-Context Reasoning
tldr: LoRA fine-tuning implicitly adds a constant steering vector toward a latent concept, mechanistically explaining out-of-context reasoning; directly training steering vectors replicates this effect.

title: Helping Large Language Models Protect Themselves: An Enhanced Filtering and Summarization System
tldr: A retraining-free LLM defense system combining prompt filtering (zero-shot classification, keyword analysis, encoded-content detection) with adversarial-literature summarization achieves 98.71% harmful-prompt detection across 226K test prompts.

title: Attention Eclipse: Manipulating Attention to Bypass LLM Safety-Alignment
tldr: A white-box framework that manipulates LLM attention weights via adversarial tokens to amplify existing jailbreak attacks, achieving up to 153% ASR improvement with 3.5x speedup over baselines.

title: When Safe Unimodal Inputs Collide: Optimizing Reasoning Chains for Cross-Modal Safety in Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces SSUI dataset and SRPO training framework to address implicit cross-modal risks where individually safe unimodal inputs combine into harmful multimodal content, achieving 24-29% safety improvements.

title: Jailbreaking LLMs' Safeguard with Universal Magic Words for Text Embedding Models
tldr: Universal 'magic word' suffixes exploit biased embedding distributions to bypass LLM safeguards relying on text similarity, with a train-free renormalization defense proposed.

title: Figure it Out: Analyzing-based Jailbreak Attack on Large Language Models
tldr: ABJ exploits LLMs' analytical reasoning capabilities to achieve 94.8% jailbreak success rate on GPT-4-turbo by disguising harmful tasks as data analysis problems.

title: OVERT: A Benchmark for Over-Refusal Evaluation on Text-to-Image Models
tldr: OVERT is the first large-scale benchmark (4,600 benign + 1,785 harmful prompts across 9 safety categories) for quantifying over-refusal in text-to-image models, revealing a strong safety-utility tradeoff.

title: Rethinking Circuit Completeness in Language Models: AND, OR, and ADDER Gates
tldr: Introduces AND, OR, and ADDER logical gate decomposition for circuits in LMs and shows that combining noising+denoising interventions achieves complete circuit discovery.

title: Ablation is Not Enough to Emulate DPO: How Neuron Dynamics Drive Toxicity Reduction
tldr: DPO reduces toxicity not just by dampening toxic neurons (only 31.8% of effect) but via distributed neuron dynamics across four groups including anti-toxic promotion.

title: RedDebate: Safer Responses through Multi-Agent Red Teaming Debates
tldr: RedDebate uses multi-agent adversarial debate among LLMs to automatically identify and reduce unsafe behaviors, cutting error rates from 38.7% to as low as 3.6% on HarmBench.

title: ReGA: Representation-Guided Abstraction for Model-based Safeguarding of LLMs
tldr: ReGA uses PCA-extracted safety representations from LLM hidden states to build Markov chain abstract models that detect harmful prompts and jailbreaks with 0.975-0.985 AUROC.

title: A Single Neuron Works: Precise Concept Erasure in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
tldr: SNCE uses sparse autoencoders to identify single concept-specific neurons in text-to-image diffusion models and suppresses them to erase harmful content with minimal image quality degradation.

title: Reviving Your MNEME: Predicting The Side Effects of LLM Unlearning and Fine-Tuning via Sparse Model Diffing
tldr: MNEME uses sparse cross-coder model diffing to automatically detect unintended behavioral side effects of LLM unlearning and fine-tuning, achieving up to 95-98% accuracy without access to training data.

title: Preemptive Detection and Steering of LLM Misalignment via Latent Reachability
tldr: BRT-Align applies control-theoretic backward reachability to LLM token generation, enabling a runtime monitor that detects unsafe completions 7-12 tokens early and a steering filter to redirect generation.

title: Balancing Label Quantity and Quality for Scalable Elicitation
tldr: Identifies three regimes (quantity-dominant, quality-dominant, mixed) in the label budget tradeoff for eliciting AI capabilities; few-shot-prompted SFT improves accuracy by up to 5pp at fixed budget.

title: Empirical Evidence for Alignment Faking in Small LLMs and Prompt-Based Mitigation Techniques
tldr: LLaMA 3 8B exhibits alignment faking (compliance gap of 11-34) that can be significantly reduced via scratchpad reasoning and deontological prompt framing without weight modification.

title: Probing the Robustness of Large Language Models Safety to Latent Perturbations
tldr: Minor perturbations to hidden activations reliably bypass safety alignment in LLMs; authors introduce ASA attack, ASABench benchmark, and LAPT defense to expose and mitigate latent fragility.

title: Discovering Transformer Circuits via a Hybrid Attribution and Pruning Framework
tldr: HAP combines attribution patching (fast but unfaithful) with edge pruning (faithful but slow) for circuit discovery, achieving 46% speedup over edge pruning alone while preserving faithfulness on the IOI task.

title: SAFER: Probing Safety in Reward Models with Sparse Autoencoder
tldr: SAFER uses Sparse Autoencoders to uncover human-interpretable safety features in reward model activations, enabling targeted data poisoning (degrading safety by 20+ points at 5% flip rate) or denoising (improving safety alignment) with minimal data modification.

title: Robust LLM Unlearning with MUDMAN: Meta-Unlearning with Disruption Masking And Normalization
tldr: MUDMAN combines disruption masking, meta-learning, and gradient normalization to achieve robust LLM unlearning of dangerous capabilities, outperforming prior TAR method by 40%.

title: Reasoned Safety Alignment: Ensuring Jailbreak Defense via Answer-Then-Check
tldr: Proposes 'Answer-Then-Check' safety alignment where LLMs draft an answer internally then self-evaluate safety before responding, achieving 90.46% safety score while maintaining low over-refusal rates.

title: A2D: Any-Order, Any-Step Safety Alignment for Diffusion Language Models
tldr: A2D trains diffusion language models to emit [EOS] refusal tokens at any position for any decoding order/step, cutting DIJA attack success from >80% to ~0% while maintaining benign compliance.

title: Jailbreaking Safeguarded Text-to-Image Models via Large Language Models
tldr: PromptTune fine-tunes an AttackLLM to generate adversarial prompts that bypass text-to-image safety guardrails without repeated model queries, achieving high bypass rates in under 4 seconds per prompt.
models_studied: AttackLLM (fine-tuned LLM for adversarial prompt generation)
text-to-image models with various safety guardrails

title: GateBreaker: Gate-Guided Attacks on Mixture-of-Expert LLMs
tldr: GateBreaker is a training-free inference-time attack that disables ~3% of safety-critical neurons in MoE LLMs, raising attack success rates from 7.4% to 64.9% across eight aligned models.

title: RL, but don't do anything I wouldn't do
tldr: KL divergence constraints on RL agents trained against a Bayesian imitator of a trusted policy fail in novel situations; pessimistic Bayesian imitation is proposed as a safer but computationally intractable alternative.

title: SEPS: A Separability Measure for Robust Unlearning in LLMs
tldr: Introduces SEPS, a separability metric measuring LLM unlearning robustness when forget and retain queries coexist in a single prompt, exposing critical failures in existing methods.

title: QGuard: Question-based Zero-shot Guard for Multi-modal LLM Safety
tldr: QGuard uses yes/no question prompting and PageRank-based scoring to detect harmful prompts in multi-modal LLMs without fine-tuning, outperforming fine-tuned baselines on text and multimodal benchmarks.

title: Unilogit: Robust Machine Unlearning for LLMs Using Uniform-Target Self-Distillation
tldr: Unilogit is a self-distillation method for machine unlearning in LLMs that dynamically targets a uniform probability over the vocabulary for forget tokens, outperforming NPO and UnDIAL with no extra hyperparameters.

title: BlackboxNLP-2025 MIB Shared Task: Exploring Ensemble Strategies for Circuit Localization Methods
tldr: Ensembling multiple EAP-based circuit localization methods (parallel and sequential) improves circuit identification accuracy on the MIB shared task benchmark.

title: Steering Language Models with Weight Arithmetic
tldr: Contrastive weight steering subtracts weight deltas of opposing fine-tunes to isolate behavioral directions, reducing sycophancy and controlling refusals while generalizing better than activation steering.

title: Gauss-Newton Unlearning for the LLM Era
tldr: K-FADE uses Gauss-Newton steps with K-FAC Hessian approximations for LLM unlearning, achieving state-of-the-art forget quality on WMDP and ToFU while better preserving retain-set utility.

title: DualOptim: Enhancing Efficacy and Stability in Machine Unlearning with Dual Optimizers
tldr: DualOptim uses separate Adam and SGD optimizers for forget/retain objectives with decoupled momentum, improving machine unlearning stability and efficacy across image classification, generation, and LLMs.

title: GenBreak: Red Teaming Text-to-Image Generators Using Large Language Models
tldr: GenBreak fine-tunes an LLM with SFT+RL to craft adversarial prompts that bypass safety filters in text-to-image generators while producing genuinely toxic outputs.

title: Unfair Alignment: Examining Safety Alignment Across Vision Encoder Layers in Vision-Language Models
tldr: Safety alignment in VLMs is unevenly distributed across vision encoder layers, with early/middle layers far more vulnerable to adversarial inputs than final layers.

title: PII Jailbreaking in LLMs via Activation Steering Reveals Personal Information Leakage
tldr: Activation steering targeting attention heads predictive of refusal achieves 95%+ PII disclosure rates across four LLMs, showing memorized private data can be extracted via internal activation manipulation.

title: Evaluating and Designing Sparse Autoencoders by Approximating Quasi-Orthogonality
tldr: Introduces Approximate Feature Activation (AFA), a closed-form framework for evaluating and designing SAEs that adaptively selects active features without manual hyperparameter tuning, achieving competitive performance on GPT-2.

title: Comparative Analysis of LLM Abliteration Methods: A Cross-Architecture Evaluation
tldr: Evaluates four open-source abliteration tools across 16 LLMs (7B-14B), finding single-pass methods better preserve capabilities than optimization-based approaches, with mathematical reasoning most sensitive.

title: Machine Unlearning Doesn't Do What You Think: Lessons for Generative AI Policy and Research
tldr: Machine unlearning cannot serve as a general-purpose solution for AI policy goals because removing information from parameters and suppressing outputs are fundamentally different problems.

title: Model Collapse Is Not a Bug but a Feature in Machine Unlearning for LLMs
tldr: Partial Model Collapse (PMC) leverages iterative self-generation to unlearn private data from LLMs without directly optimizing on sensitive targets, outperforming existing baselines.

title: Investigating Adversarial Trigger Transfer in Large Language Models
tldr: Adversarial triggers optimized via GCG do not transfer universally across 13 aligned LLMs; preference-optimized models are far more robust than fine-tuned ones.

title: Security Assessment of DeepSeek and GPT Series Models against Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: First systematic jailbreak benchmark comparison of DeepSeek-series vs. GPT-series models using HarmBench; DeepSeek's MoE architecture gives selective robustness to gradient-based attacks but higher vulnerability to prompt-based attacks.

title: Attention Slipping: A Mechanistic Understanding of Jailbreak Attacks and Defenses in LLMs
tldr: Identifies 'Attention Slipping' — LLMs reduce attention to unsafe content during jailbreaks — and proposes 'Attention Sharpening' (temperature scaling T<1) as a zero-overhead defense.

title: Fewer Weights, More Problems: A Practical Attack on LLM Pruning
tldr: An adversary can craft an LLM that appears benign pre-pruning but activates malicious behavior (jailbreaks, refusals, content injection) after standard pruning methods are applied, achieving up to 99.5% attack success.

title: ReasoningGuard: Safeguarding Large Reasoning Models with Inference-time Safety Aha Moments
tldr: ReasoningGuard injects inference-time 'safety aha moments' into large reasoning models by detecting critical attention-sink points and sampling reasoning paths that attend most to the injected safety phrase, effectively blocking jailbreaks with ~9% overhead.

title: HAMSA: Hijacking Aligned Compact Models via Stealthy Automation
tldr: HAMSA is an automated red-teaming framework using multi-stage evolutionary search with temperature-controlled mutations to generate fluent, stealthy jailbreak prompts for aligned compact LLMs, achieving up to 100% success on safety-critical topics.

title: A Guardrail for Safety Preservation: When Safety-Sensitive Subspace Meets Harmful-Resistant Null-Space
tldr: GuardSpace decomposes pretrained LLM weights into safety-sensitive and safety-irrelevant components, constraining fine-tuning adapters to a harmful-resistant null space, reducing harmfulness from 14.4% to 3.6% while improving task accuracy.

title: SGM: A Framework for Building Specification-Guided Moderation Filters
tldr: SGM automates training data generation for policy-aligned content moderation filters using a 7-stage pipeline, achieving F1=0.81 competitive with state-of-the-art safety filters.

title: Backtracking for Safety
tldr: BSAFE introduces special backtracking tokens enabling LLMs to revert mid-generation to safer states, dramatically reducing toxicity from prefilling attacks without discarding entire outputs.
