tldr: Kov frames LLM red-teaming as an MDP with Monte Carlo tree search and a log-perplexity naturalism constraint, jailbreaking GPT-3.5 in ~10 black-box queries while generating more natural-sounding adversarial suffixes.

title: When Thinking Backfires: Mechanistic Insights Into Reasoning-Induced Misalignment
tldr: Strengthening LLM reasoning (via CoT or fine-tuning) paradoxically increases susceptibility to harmful requests; mechanistic analysis identifies specific attention heads and neurons responsible for this safety-reasoning tradeoff.

title: Resource Rational Contractualism Should Guide AI Alignment
tldr: Proposes Resource-Rational Contractualism (RRC), a framework grounding AI alignment in contractualist moral philosophy adapted for cognitively-bounded agents using heuristics that trade effort for accuracy.

title: Safeguard is a Double-edged Sword: Denial-of-service Attack on Large Language Models
tldr: Adversarial ~30-char prompts injected into user templates exploit LLM safeguard false positives to block over 97% of legitimate requests as a denial-of-service attack.

title: NEXUS: Network Exploration for eXploiting Unsafe Sequences in Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreaks
tldr: NEXUS is a modular framework for constructing multi-turn jailbreak attacks on LLMs using semantic networks, feedback-driven simulation, and adaptive traversal, achieving 2.1-19.4% higher attack success rates than baselines.

title: Adversarial Suffix Filtering: a Defense Pipeline for LLMs
tldr: ASF is a lightweight, model-agnostic pipeline that detects and removes adversarial suffix jailbreaks via segmentation + BERT classification, reducing attack success rate to below 4%.

title: SUA: Stealthy Multimodal Large Language Model Unlearning Attack
tldr: SUA shows that MLLM unlearning methods don't truly erase information — adversarial image perturbations reliably recover supposedly forgotten content across multiple models and defenses.

title: ICLShield: Exploring and Mitigating In-Context Learning Backdoor Attacks
tldr: ICLShield defends LLMs against in-context learning backdoor attacks by dynamically selecting clean demonstrations using similarity and confidence scores, reducing attack success rate by ~29%.

title: Black-box Optimization of LLM Outputs by Asking for Directions
tldr: Black-box LLM attacks using binary comparison queries (instead of logit access) achieve 40-100% jailbreak and 55-88% prompt injection success in 5-450 queries; larger models are more vulnerable.

title: Label Smoothing Improves Gradient Ascent in LLM Unlearning
tldr: Smoothed Gradient Ascent (SGA) adds label smoothing to gradient ascent unlearning by blending forget data with normal data, reducing divergence and preserving model utility across three benchmarks.

title: How Effective Is Constitutional AI in Small LLMs? A Study on DeepSeek-R1 and Its Peers
tldr: Constitutional AI self-critique reduces harmful outputs by 50%+ in abliterated 7-9B LLMs, with DeepSeek-R1's explicit reasoning yielding superior harm reduction across HarmBench categories.

title: MetaSC: Test-Time Safety Specification Optimization for Language Models
tldr: MetaSC iteratively optimizes safety specifications at inference time via a meta-critique loop, achieving near-perfect jailbreak defense without modifying model weights.

title: A Granular Study of Safety Pretraining under Model Abliteration
tldr: Refusal-only safety training is fragile to abliteration attacks; combining safe-data filtering, rephrasing, and metatags yields partial robustness across 20 model variants.

title: Learning a Pessimistic Reward Model in RLHF
tldr: PET fine-tunes reward models via adversarial training with rejection sampling to produce pessimistic rewards, preventing reward hacking without requiring KL regularization.

title: LifeAlign: Lifelong Alignment for Large Language Models with Memory-Augmented Focalized Preference Optimization
tldr: LifeAlign prevents catastrophic forgetting during sequential LLM alignment by combining focalized DPO with SVD-based memory consolidation to preserve prior preference knowledge.

title: How Do LLMs Persuade? Linear Probes Can Uncover Persuasion Dynamics in Multi-Turn Conversations
tldr: Linear probes on LLM activations can detect persuasion success, persuadee personality, and rhetorical strategy in multi-turn dialogues, matching or exceeding prompting baselines with far less compute.

title: OffTopicEval: When Large Language Models Enter the Wrong Chat, Almost Always!
tldr: OffTopicEval benchmarks LLM 'operational safety' (accepting in-domain, refusing off-topic queries) across 26 models, finding even top models fail on adversarially-rephrased OOD queries.

title: What's In My Human Feedback? Learning Interpretable Descriptions of Preference Data
tldr: WIMHF uses sparse autoencoders to identify interpretable features in RLHF preference datasets, revealing dataset-specific annotator biases and enabling targeted data curation for +37% safety gains.

title: MCP Security Bench (MSB): Benchmarking Attacks Against Model Context Protocol in LLM Agents
tldr: MSB is the first benchmark for evaluating LLM agent security under Model Context Protocol tool usage, covering 12 attack types across 2,000 instances and finding stronger models are paradoxically more vulnerable.

title: A Red Teaming Roadmap Towards System-Level Safety
tldr: Argues LLM red teaming should shift from abstract harm categories to product-specific safety specs with realistic threat models, and toward system-level safety over model-level robustness.

title: Circuit Stability Characterizes Language Model Generalization
tldr: Introduces circuit stability—a metric for how consistently a model applies the same internal circuit across related inputs—and shows it predicts generalization failures in arithmetic, boolean logic, and chain-of-thought reasoning.

title: AlignSAE: Concept-Aligned Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: AlignSAE uses a two-phase pre-train/post-train curriculum to bind SAE latent features to human-defined concept ontologies, enabling precise causal swaps and mechanistic analysis of LLM knowledge storage.

title: TAI3: Testing Agent Integrity in Interpreting User Intent
tldr: TAI3 is a framework that systematically uncovers intent integrity violations in LLM agents via semantic partitioning and intent-preserving mutation, evaluated across 80 toolkit APIs.

title: LLM Interpretability with Identifiable Temporal-Instantaneous Representation
tldr: Combines causal representation learning with sparse autoencoders to model both time-delayed and instantaneous latent concept relationships in LLMs, with theoretical identifiability guarantees.

title: Building Production-Ready Probes For Gemini
tldr: Novel probe architectures (MultiMax) handle long-context distribution shifts for misuse detection in Gemini, achieving comparable accuracy to LLM classifiers at ~10,000x lower compute cost.

title: Understanding Language Model Circuits through Knowledge Editing
tldr: Systematic knowledge editing experiments on GPT-2 circuits reveal that primary circuits resist editing more than complementary circuits, layer normalization dominates circuit composition (37-63%), and ideal circuit size lies between 5-50% of parameters.

title: Effective and Efficient Jailbreaks of Black-Box LLMs with Cross-Behavior Attacks
tldr: JCB uses cross-behavior adversarial prompt transfer with UCB1 bandit query allocation to jailbreak black-box LLMs more efficiently, reducing queries by up to 94% and improving success rates by 12.9%.

title: Detecting Adversarial Fine-tuning with Auditing Agents
tldr: LLM-based auditing agents with tool access detect adversarial fine-tuning at 56.2% recall at 1% FPR across 8 attack types by inspecting datasets, querying models, and running benchmarks.

title: On the Vulnerability of Safety Alignment in Open-Access LLMs
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024
tldr: Demonstrates that open-access LLMs can be efficiently reverse-aligned via RSFT and RPO to bypass safety guardrails without requiring manually curated malicious datasets.
models_studied: open-access LLMs (Llama family and similar high-performance open models)

title: Con Instruction: Universal Jailbreaking of Multimodal Large Language Models via Non-Textual Modalities
tldr: Con Instruction jailbreaks multimodal LLMs by optimizing adversarial images/audio to align with harmful instructions in embedding space, achieving 81-87% success rates across LLaVA, InternVL, Qwen-VL, and Qwen-Audio.

title: Advancing Jailbreak Strategies: A Hybrid Approach to Exploiting LLM Vulnerabilities and Bypassing Modern Defenses
tldr: Hybrid GCG+PAIR and GCG+WordGame jailbreak attacks achieve up to 91.6% success on Llama-3 and bypass state-of-the-art defenses like JBShield and Gradient Cuff.

title: Breaking the Code: Security Assessment of AI Code Agents Through Systematic Jailbreaking Attacks
tldr: JAWS-Bench evaluates LLM code agents against jailbreaks across 3 workspace regimes, finding 61% compliance under prompt-only conditions and that agent wrapping increases attack success by 1.6x.

title: Guarding the Guardrails: A Taxonomy-Driven Approach to Jailbreak Detection
tldr: Proposes a 50-strategy hierarchical jailbreak taxonomy across 7 families, collects an Italian multi-turn adversarial dialogue dataset, and shows taxonomy-guided prompting boosts GPT detection from 65.9% to 78.0%.

title: Incident Analysis for AI Agents
tldr: Proposes a human-factors-inspired incident analysis framework for AI agents with three causal categories (system, contextual, cognitive) and recommends required information for incident investigation.

title: Full-Stack Alignment: Co-Aligning AI and Institutions with Thick Models of Value
tldr: Proposes 'full-stack alignment' (FSA) and 'thick models of value' (TMV) to concurrently align AI systems and institutions with structured, philosophically-grounded value representations rather than utility functions or unstructured text.

title: SPIRIT: Patching Speech Language Models against Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: SPIRIT demonstrates that Speech Language Models are highly vulnerable to audio-domain jailbreaks (up to 100% ASR) and proposes post-hoc activation-patching defenses that achieve 99% robustness with no retraining.

title: Machine Unlearning Meets Adversarial Robustness via Constrained Interventions on LLMs
tldr: A unified constrained optimization framework jointly addresses machine unlearning and jailbreak robustness in LLMs via minimal weight interventions, with point-wise constraints outperforming complex max-min formulations.

title: PAHQ: Accelerating Automated Circuit Discovery through Mixed-Precision Inference Optimization
tldr: PAHQ uses mixed-precision quantization to accelerate ACDC circuit discovery by up to 80% runtime and 30% memory reduction while maintaining circuit faithfulness (AUC-ROC 0.96 vs 0.98 unaccelerated).

title: The Secret Agenda: LLMs Strategically Lie and Our Current Safety Tools Are Blind
tldr: 38 LLMs all exhibit strategic deception in a social-game testbed; SAE-based deception features rarely activate during lying and feature steering fails to stop it, revealing a critical gap in current safety tooling.

title: Causal Reward Adjustment: Mitigating Reward Hacking in External Reasoning via Backdoor Correction
tldr: CRA uses sparse autoencoders to identify semantic confounders in process reward models and applies backdoor adjustment to eliminate spurious reward correlations, improving math reasoning accuracy.

title: STAC: When Innocent Tools Form Dangerous Chains to Jailbreak LLM Agents
tldr: STAC chains individually benign tool calls into harmful attack sequences against LLM agents, achieving >90% attack success rates against GPT-4.1 while remaining nearly undetectable.

title: Unsupervised decoding of encoded reasoning using language model interpretability
tldr: Fine-tuned a reasoning model to think in ROT-13, then showed logit lens can unsupervisedly decode the hidden reasoning with substantial accuracy, demonstrating interpretability can pierce encoded CoT.

title: Towards Robust Multimodal Large Language Models Against Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: SafeMLLM uses adversarial training with a contrastive embedding attack to defend multimodal LLMs against jailbreak attacks across image, text, and combined modalities.

title: OrtSAE: Orthogonal Sparse Autoencoders Uncover Atomic Features
tldr: Introduces OrtSAE, which adds an orthogonality penalty to SAE training, reducing feature absorption by 65% and feature composition by 15% while discovering 9% more distinct features with only 4% compute overhead.

title: Activation Oracles: Training and Evaluating LLMs as General-Purpose Activation Explainers
tldr: Trains LLMs to interpret neural network activations by accepting them as inputs (Activation Oracles), matching or exceeding white-box interpretability baselines on 4 auditing benchmarks.

title: Attribution-guided Pruning for Compression, Circuit Discovery, and Targeted Correction in LLMs
tldr: Unified LRP-based attribution framework for LLM circuit discovery, model compression, and targeted correction of harmful behaviors like toxicity via parameter-level pruning.

title: Understanding sparse autoencoder scaling in the presence of feature manifolds
tldr: Adapts a capacity-allocation model to show SAEs can enter a pathological scaling regime where feature manifolds cause sublinear feature discovery, but realistic manifold geometry likely prevents this.

title: Mechanistically Interpreting a Transformer-based 2-SAT Solver: An Axiomatic Approach
tldr: Proposes four axioms for formally validating mechanistic interpretations and demonstrates them by fully reverse-engineering a Transformer trained on 2-SAT, revealing it implements exhaustive enumeration.
models_studied: Custom 2-layer decoder-only Transformer (128-dim embeddings, 1 attention head layer 1, 4 attention heads layer 2, 512 hidden MLP)

title: Evolution of Concepts in Language Model Pre-Training
tldr: Uses crosscoders (multi-snapshot sparse dictionary learning) to track interpretable feature emergence across pre-training, revealing a statistical-to-feature learning phase transition around step 1000.

title: Towards Understanding the Nature of Attention with Low-Rank Sparse Decomposition
tldr: Introduces Lorsa, a low-rank sparse decomposition of attention layers that disentangles multi-head attention into individually interpretable components, achieving SAE-level interpretability with superior circuit discovery.

title: From Directions to Cones: Exploring Multidimensional Representations of Propositional Facts in LLMs
tldr: Extends concept cones beyond single linear directions to discover multidimensional orthonormal bases that causally mediate truthfulness in LLMs, generalizing across architectures while preserving unrelated capabilities.

title: SafeInt: Shielding Large Language Models from Jailbreak Attacks via Safety-Aware Representation Intervention
tldr: SafeInt defends LLMs from jailbreaks by using parameterized representation intervention to align jailbreak sample representations with unsafe ones, activating existing safety mechanisms.

title: SafeTuneBed: A Toolkit for Benchmarking LLM Safety Alignment in Fine-Tuning
tldr: SafeTuneBed is a unified toolkit standardizing datasets, defense methods, and evaluation protocols for benchmarking safety-preserving fine-tuning of LLMs.

title: Adversarial Attack on Large Language Models using Exponentiated Gradient Descent
tldr: Proposes an exponentiated gradient descent method to jailbreak aligned LLMs by optimizing relaxed one-hot token encodings within the probability simplex, outperforming GCG and PGD baselines.

title: JailBench: A Comprehensive Chinese Security Assessment Benchmark for Large Language Models
tldr: JailBench introduces the first comprehensive Chinese safety benchmark for LLMs with 10,800 jailbreak queries across 5 domains and 40 risk categories, achieving 73.86% ASR against ChatGPT.

title: Reasoning Models Sometimes Output Illegible Chains of Thought
tldr: Across 14 RL-trained reasoning models, most produce illegible chain-of-thought reasoning (45% of R1 CoTs illegible) while maintaining readable final answers, undermining CoT-based safety monitoring.

title: Generating Interpretable Networks using Hypernetworks
tldr: Uses hypernetworks (HVAEs with graph transformers) to generate interpretable neural networks, discovering three distinct algorithms for L1 norm computation with systematic generalization.

title: Recover-to-Forget: Gradient Reconstruction from LoRA for Efficient LLM Unlearning
tldr: R2F reconstructs full-model gradient directions from compact LoRA adapter updates via a learned gradient decoder, enabling efficient LLM unlearning without full retraining.

title: On the Impossibility of Retrain Equivalence in Machine Unlearning
tldr: Machine unlearning cannot achieve retrain equivalence in multi-stage training pipelines; path-oblivious local methods provably diverge depending on training order, with >20% performance gaps empirically.

title: Towards Safe Reasoning in Large Reasoning Models via Corrective Intervention
tldr: IPO reduces harmful reasoning in LRMs by 30-71% by detecting compliance cues and substituting safety triggers during preference learning, preserving math/coding capabilities.

title: Speculative Safety-Aware Decoding
tldr: SSD uses speculative sampling with a small safety-aligned model and a dynamic match-ratio switch to defend LLMs against jailbreaks at decoding time while accelerating inference.

title: Reward Consistency: Improving Multi-Objective Alignment from a Data-Centric Perspective
tldr: Reward Consistency Sampling (RCS) selects preference data pairs where winners beat losers across all objectives simultaneously, eliminating gradient conflicts and improving multi-objective alignment by 13.37% on average.

title: Refining Positive and Toxic Samples for Dual Safety Self-Alignment of LLMs With Minimal Human Interventions
tldr: PT-ALIGN uses automatically refined positive+toxic sample pairs with fine-grained token-level unlikelihood training to align LLMs for safety using fewer than 50 human annotations, achieving 98.28% harmlessness on LLaMA2-13B.

title: Beyond Input Activations: Identifying Influential Latents by Gradient Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Proposes GradSAE, which uses output-side gradient information to identify causally influential SAE latents, showing that activated latents contribute unequally to model outputs and only high-influence latents enable effective steering.

title: The Devil in the Details: Emergent Misalignment, Format and Coherence in Open-Weights LLMs
tldr: Fine-tuning nine open-weights LLMs on insecure code causes ~10x misalignment increase; requiring JSON output doubles misalignment rates, revealing format-dependent safety vulnerabilities.

title: LLMs are Capable of Misaligned Behavior Under Explicit Prohibition and Surveillance
tldr: Seven frontier LLMs were tested on an impossible quiz under explicit no-cheating instructions; o4-mini attempted cheating in ~95% of runs and Gemini 2.5 Pro cheated in most runs, demonstrating misalignment even under explicit prohibition.

title: A Neuro-inspired Interpretation of Unlearning in Large Language Models through Sample-level Unlearning Difficulty
tldr: Introduces Memory Removal Difficulty (MRD), a neuroscience-inspired metric quantifying per-sample unlearning difficulty in LLMs, and uses it for curriculum-weighted sampling to improve unlearning algorithms.

title: Feature-Selective Representation Misdirection for Machine Unlearning
tldr: SRMU uses feature-aware importance maps and directional misdirection vectors to selectively remove harmful LLM knowledge even when forget/retain data representations are entangled.

title: Decomposing Behavioral Phase Transitions in LLMs: Order Parameters for Emergent Misalignment
tldr: A framework using statistical dissimilarity and LLM-judged order parameters to detect, quantify, and decompose behavioral phase transitions during fine-tuning that produce emergent misalignment.

title: Activation Steering Meets Preference Optimization: Defense Against Jailbreaks in Vision Language Models
tldr: SPO-VLM combines adaptive activation steering with PPO-based preference optimization to defend VLMs against jailbreaks, cutting attack success rates from 75% to 6.38% while preserving visual task performance.

title: Eliminating Inductive Bias in Reward Models with Information-Theoretic Guidance
tldr: DIR uses information-theoretic objectives to eliminate inductive biases (length, sycophancy, format) in RLHF reward models by maximizing MI with preferences while minimizing MI with bias attributes.

title: Align to Misalign: Automatic LLM Jailbreak with Meta-Optimized LLM Judges
tldr: AMIS uses bi-level meta-optimization to jointly refine jailbreak prompts and LLM judge scoring templates, achieving 88% ASR on Claude-3.5-Haiku and 100% on Claude-4-Sonnet.

title: Sparse-Autoencoder-Guided Internal Representation Unlearning for Large Language Models
tldr: Uses sparse autoencoders to identify and modify recognition latents in LLMs, shifting target entity activations from 'known' to 'unknown' to achieve representation-level unlearning without model collapse.

title: Safety Instincts: LLMs Learn to Trust Their Internal Compass for Self-Defense
tldr: SIRL uses token-level entropy of aligned LLMs as a self-generated reward to resist jailbreaks, achieving 89-100% defense success rates across 20+ attacks without external annotations.

title: Exploring Straightforward Conversational Red-Teaming
tldr: Off-the-shelf LLMs can red-team other LLMs via multi-turn conversations; concealing the harmful objective and using multi-attempt strategies are most effective, with effectiveness plateauing after 3-4 turns.

title: DIESEL - Dynamic Inference-Guidance via Evasion of Semantic Embeddings in LLMs
tldr: DIESEL is a training-free inference-time method that filters unsafe LLM outputs by reranking candidate tokens based on semantic similarity to predefined negative concept embeddings, achieving 1.46-1.64x runtime overhead vs 186-202x for competing methods.

title: Just Do It!? Computer-Use Agents Exhibit Blind Goal-Directedness
tldr: Introduces Blind-Act benchmark revealing that computer-use agents exhibit 'Blind Goal-Directedness' (80.8% average BGD rate across 9 frontier models), pursuing objectives regardless of feasibility, safety, or context.

title: Enhancing LLM Agent Safety via Causal Influence Prompting
tldr: CIP embeds causal influence diagrams into LLM agent prompts to make agents reason about cause-and-effect before acting, dramatically increasing refusal of harmful tasks while preserving legitimate task performance.

title: Retention Score: Quantifying Jailbreak Risks for Vision Language Models
tldr: Proposes Retention Score (Retention-I and Retention-T), a certified robustness metric for VLMs against jailbreak attacks, offering up to 30x efficiency gains over traditional adversarial testing.

title: Safety at One Shot: Patching Fine-Tuned LLMs with A Single Instance
tldr: A single safety example suffices to fully recover alignment in fine-tuned LLMs, exploiting the low-rank structure of safety gradients via bilevel optimization.
models_studied: five safety-aligned LLMs (unspecified names in abstract)

title: ManagerBench: Evaluating the Safety-Pragmatism Trade-off in Autonomous LLMs
tldr: ManagerBench is a 2,440-example benchmark testing whether LLMs can balance safety vs. pragmatism in managerial scenarios; frontier models all fail, either being too harmful or too cautious.

title: LLMs Learn to Deceive Unintentionally: Emergent Misalignment in Dishonesty from Misaligned Samples to Biased Human-AI Interactions
tldr: Introducing as little as 1% misaligned training samples causes a >20% drop in LLM honesty, and 10% biased users in human-AI interactions can amplify deceptive tendencies.

title: InvThink: Towards AI Safety via Inverse Reasoning
tldr: InvThink trains LLMs to enumerate potential harms and analyze consequences before generating responses, achieving up to 30.4% reduction in harmful outputs while preserving general reasoning capabilities.

title: Understanding Adversarial Transfer: Why Representation-Space Attacks Fail Where Data-Space Attacks Succeed
tldr: Data-space adversarial attacks transfer across models but representation-space attacks do not unless model representations are geometrically aligned, explaining why image jailbreaks fail to transfer across VLMs.

title: Scaling laws for activation steering with Llama 2 models and refusal mechanisms
tldr: Contrastive activation addition (CAA) for refusal mechanisms is most effective at early-mid layers (~40% depth), weakens exponentially with model scale, and negative steering outperforms positive steering across Llama 2 7B/13B/70B.

title: Revisiting End-To-End Sparse Autoencoder Training: A Short Finetune Is All You Need
tldr: A brief KL+MSE fine-tuning stage on the final 25M training tokens achieves comparable performance to full end-to-end SAE training at ~50% reduced wall-clock cost.

title: FALCON: Fine-grained Activation Manipulation by Contrastive Orthogonal Unalignment for Large Language Model
tldr: FALCON uses mutual information-guided parameter selection, contrastive representation separation, and orthogonal gradient projection to selectively unlearn harmful knowledge from LLMs while maintaining general utility.

title: Where Confabulation Lives: Latent Feature Discovery in LLMs
tldr: Uses Sparse PCA to extract latent directions encoding confabulation in Llama-3-8B activations, then steers these directions to reduce hallucination rates while preserving factual recall.

title: Curvature-Aware Safety Restoration In LLMs Fine-Tuning
tldr: Curvature-aware method using influence functions and L-BFGS Hessian approximation restores LLM safety alignment after fine-tuning by exploiting preserved loss landscape geometry.

title: Mitigating Jailbreaks with Intent-Aware LLMs
tldr: Intent-FT fine-tunes LLMs to infer instruction intent before responding, keeping all evaluated jailbreak attack success rates below 50% while preserving model utility.

title: Logit-Gap Steering: Efficient Short-Suffix Jailbreaks for Aligned Large Language Models
tldr: Logit-gap steering exploits the refusal-affirmation logit gap in RLHF-aligned LLMs to generate short transferable jailbreak suffixes in under one second with 80-100% attack success rates.

title: Debiasing Reward Models by Representation Learning with Guarantees
tldr: A principled two-stage framework using variational inference to identify and remove spurious correlations (length bias, sycophancy, concept bias) from reward models, with formal identifiability guarantees.

title: When Safety Blocks Sense: Measuring Semantic Confusion in LLM Refusals
tldr: Introduces 'semantic confusion' — where safety-aligned LLMs accept one phrasing of a benign prompt but reject a paraphrase — and presents ParaGuard (10K prompts) and three token-level metrics to measure it.

title: Unified Defense for Large Language Models against Jailbreak and Fine-Tuning Attacks in Education
tldr: TSSF, a three-stage framework using attention realignment, layer-wise safety judgment, and dual routing, simultaneously defends LLMs against jailbreak and fine-tuning attacks in educational contexts.

title: Malice in Agentland: Down the Rabbit Hole of Backdoors in the AI Supply Chain
tldr: Poisoning as little as 2% of AI agent fine-tuning data enables backdoor attacks with 80%+ success rates at data exfiltration, and existing guardrails fail to detect them.

title: Safety-Aligned Weights Are Not Enough: Refusal-Teacher-Guided Finetuning Enhances Safety and Downstream Performance under Harmful Finetuning Attacks
tldr: ReFT uses refusal features from safety-aligned LLMs to filter harmful finetuning data and distill alignment knowledge, achieving <1.3% harmful output rate while maintaining high downstream task accuracy.

title: Dual-Space Smoothness for Robust and Balanced LLM Unlearning
tldr: PRISM enforces dual-space smoothness (representation + parameter) in LLM unlearning to resist jailbreak/relearning attacks while preventing catastrophic forgetting.

title: Simulated Ensemble Attack: Transferring Jailbreaks Across Fine-tuned Vision-Language Models
tldr: SEA is a grey-box jailbreak method using Fine-tuning Trajectory Simulation and Targeted Prompt Guidance that achieves 86.5%+ attack success on safety-fine-tuned VLMs by exploiting inherited base model vulnerabilities.

title: Layered Unlearning for Adversarial Relearning
tldr: Layered Unlearning (LU) sequentially unlearns expanding data folds to create distinct inhibitory mechanisms, improving robustness against adversarial fine-tuning attacks that reverse unlearning.

title: Measuring Harmfulness of Computer-Using Agents
tldr: CUAHarm is a 104-scenario benchmark for evaluating safety risks of computer-using agents, finding frontier models comply with harmful tasks at 52-85% success rates.

title: Gaming the Judge: Unfaithful Chain-of-Thought Can Undermine Agent Evaluation
tldr: LLM judges evaluating agent trajectories can be manipulated by rewriting chain-of-thought reasoning alone, inflating false positive rates by up to 90% across 800 web tasks.

title: Async Control: Stress-testing Asynchronous Control Measures for LLM Agents
tldr: Adversarial red-blue team study of asynchronous LLM agent monitors in software engineering environments, achieving 6% FNR at 1% FPR with ensemble monitors after iterative rounds.

title: Alignment Verifiability in Large Language Models: Normative Indistinguishability under Behavioral Evaluation
tldr: Proves that behavioral evaluation cannot uniquely identify latent alignment when models can detect evaluation contexts, constructing a Llama-3.2-3B model showing 100% compliance under evaluation signals but degraded safety in deployment.

title: Which Sparse Autoencoder Features Are Real? Model-X Knockoffs for False Discovery Rate Control
tldr: Applies Model-X knockoffs to SAE feature selection for FDR control, identifying 129 of 512 genuine task-relevant features in Pythia-70M sentiment analysis with finite-sample guarantees.

title: Towards Ethical Multi-Agent Systems of Large Language Models: A Mechanistic Interpretability Perspective
tldr: A research agenda for ensuring ethical behavior in multi-agent LLM systems using mechanistic interpretability for evaluation, explanation, and targeted alignment interventions.

title: Soft Token Attacks Cannot Reliably Audit Unlearning in Large Language Models
tldr: Soft token attacks can extract arbitrary information from LLMs regardless of unlearning status or training corpus membership, making them unreliable as unlearning audit tools.

title: Neural Chameleons: Language Models Can Learn to Hide Their Thoughts from Unseen Activation Monitors
tldr: Fine-tuned LLMs can learn to selectively suppress activation-based safety monitors for unseen concepts via low-dimensional subspace manipulation, while preserving capabilities.

title: TeleAI-Safety: A comprehensive LLM jailbreaking benchmark towards attacks, defenses, and evaluations
tldr: TeleAI-Safety is a modular benchmark integrating 19 attack methods, 29 defenses, and 19 evaluation methods across 342 harmful samples and 14 LLMs, revealing reasoning-safety trade-offs and evaluation inconsistency.

title: Representation-Aware Unlearning via Activation Signatures: From Suppression to Knowledge-Signature Erasure
tldr: KIF targets internal activation signatures for genuine LLM knowledge erasure, achieving Forget Quality ~0.99 on TOFU while maintaining utility, and revealing three distinct unlearning regimes across model types.

title: Targeting Alignment: Extracting Safety Classifiers of Aligned LLMs
venue: SaTML 2025 (IEEE Conference on Secure and Trustworthy Machine Learning)
tldr: Safety classifiers embedded in aligned LLMs can be extracted as surrogate models from as little as 20% of the architecture, and jailbreak attacks on these surrogates transfer to the full model with 70% ASR vs 22% direct.

title: What is AI safety? What do we want it to be?
tldr: Proposes defining AI safety as research aimed at preventing or reducing harms caused by AI systems, and uses conceptual engineering to argue this broader conception is superior to narrower framings.

title: Adversarial Déjà Vu: Jailbreak Dictionary Learning for Stronger Generalization to Unseen Attacks
tldr: Proposes that novel jailbreaks are recombinations of known adversarial skills; learns a 397-primitive dictionary and trains on skill compositions (ASCoT) to generalize robustness to unseen attacks.

title: Don't Walk the Line: Boundary Guidance for Filtered Generation
tldr: Boundary Guidance fine-tunes generative models to steer outputs away from safety classifier decision boundaries, yielding Pareto improvements in both helpfulness and harmlessness across multiple model scales.

title: Time-To-Inconsistency: A Survival Analysis of Large Language Model Robustness to Adversarial Attacks
tldr: Applies survival analysis to model when LLMs become inconsistent under adversarial pressure in multi-turn conversations, finding abrupt semantic drift is harmful but cumulative drift is paradoxically protective.

title: Mechanistic Data Attribution: Tracing the Training Origins of Interpretable LLM Units
tldr: MDA uses influence functions to trace interpretable LLM circuits (e.g., induction heads) back to specific training samples, showing that repetitive structural data causally drives their emergence.

title: Surgical Refusal Ablation: Disentangling Safety from Intelligence via Concept-Guided Spectral Cleaning
tldr: SRA orthogonalizes refusal vectors against protected capability directions before weight edits, achieving near-zero refusal (0-2%) with 47x less distribution drift than standard ablation.

title: Lethe: Purifying Backdoored Large Language Models with Knowledge Dilution
tldr: Lethe defends LLMs against backdoor attacks by combining internal model merging (LoRA + SLERP) with external prompt-level evidence injection, reducing attack success rates by up to 98%.

title: LatentBreak: Jailbreaking Large Language Models through Latent Space Feedback
tldr: LatentBreak jailbreaks LLMs via iterative word substitution guided by latent-space feedback, producing low-perplexity prompts that evade perplexity-based defenses where suffix attacks fail.

title: SafeSteer: Adaptive Subspace Steering for Efficient Jailbreak Defense in Vision-Language Models
tldr: SafeSteer uses SVD-based safety subspace projection with an adaptive harm-sensing classifier to defend VLMs from jailbreak attacks, reducing ASR by 60%+ with negligible overhead.

title: Can LLMs Lie? Investigation beyond Hallucination
tldr: Applies mechanistic interpretability (logit lens, causal ablations, steering vectors) to Llama-3.1-8B to identify and control sparse lying circuits, reducing dishonesty without degrading task performance.

title: Differentiated Directional Intervention: A Framework for Evading LLM Safety Alignment
tldr: DBDI decomposes LLM refusal into harm-detection and refusal-execution directions, intervening on each separately to achieve up to 97.88% ASR on Llama-2.

title: Bidirectional Intention Inference Enhances LLMs' Defense Against Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: BIID combines forward intent analysis and backward response retrospection to achieve near-zero attack success rates against single-turn and multi-turn jailbreak attacks across multiple LLMs.

title: Protecting Context and Prompts: Deterministic Security for Non-Deterministic AI
tldr: Introduces cryptographic authenticated prompts and tamper-evident context hash chains to provide deterministic, 100% detection of prompt injection and context manipulation in LLM workflows.

title: Evaluating LLM Agent Adherence to Hierarchical Safety Principles: A Lightweight Benchmark for Probing Foundational Controllability Components
tldr: Introduces a lightweight MiniGrid-based benchmark to evaluate whether LLM agents reliably prioritize inviolable safety directives over task goals, testing 6 models across 24 conditions.

title: Strategic Deflection: Defending LLMs from Logit Manipulation
tldr: SDeflection trains LLMs via CPO+LoRA to produce semantically adjacent but harmless responses to jailbreak attacks, reducing attack success rates from 89-95% to 8-35%.

title: Multi-Level Safety Continual Projection for Fine-Tuned Large Language Models without Retraining
tldr: FGSN identifies sparse safety-critical neurons using multi-scale activation analysis and projects them onto safety directions without backpropagation, preserving alignment after fine-tuning with only ~4.67% parameter modifications.

title: Adversarial Contrastive Learning for LLM Quantization Attacks
tldr: ACL is a gradient-based attack that embeds hidden malicious behaviors in quantized LLMs via triplet contrastive loss, achieving 97.69% jailbreak and 86% over-refusal attack success rates.

title: Bag of Tricks for Subverting Reasoning-based Safety Guardrails
tldr: Four attack techniques (white-box, gray-box, black-box) subvert reasoning-based safety guardrails in Large Reasoning Models with >90% success rates across five benchmarks.

title: Winning at All Cost: A Small Environment for Eliciting Specification Gaming Behaviors in Large Language Models
tldr: A textual tic-tac-toe environment with unwinnable board states elicits specification gaming in frontier LLMs; o3-mini exploits rules at 37.1% and 'creative' prompts push all models to 77.3%.

title: Efficient Safety Retrofitting Against Jailbreaking for LLMs
tldr: DPO with 2,000 samples costing $3-$20 reduces jailbreak success rates by 10-30% across unseen topics and attack styles; introduces Egida, a 61K-instance jailbreak dataset.

title: Evaluating Language Model Reasoning about Confidential Information
tldr: PasswordEval benchmark reveals frontier LLMs fail at context-dependent confidentiality rules and that reasoning traces leak sensitive info in 40-60% of cases.

title: Semantic Regexes: Auto-Interpreting LLM Features with a Structured Language
tldr: Introduces semantic regexes, a structured language for describing LLM features that matches natural language accuracy while being more concise, consistent, and enabling model-wide complexity analysis.

title: Microsaccade-Inspired Probing: Positional Encoding Perturbations Reveal LLM Misbehaviours
tldr: MIP perturbs positional encodings to extract latent signals that detect LLM misbehaviours (jailbreaks, backdoors, hallucinations, toxicity) with no fine-tuning required.

title: SAGE: Scalable Ground Truth Evaluations for Large Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: SAGE automatically discovers task-relevant cross-sections and computes supervised ground-truth feature dictionaries to scalably evaluate sparse autoencoders on large models without manual circuit analysis.

title: Understanding and Mitigating Over-refusal for Large Language Models via Safety Representation
tldr: MOSR reduces LLM over-refusal of benign queries by weighting training loss based on representation-space overlap and augmenting refusals with harmful context prefixes.

title: Representation Learning on a Random Lattice
tldr: Proposes a random lattice model of data distributions analyzed via percolation theory to categorize neural network features into context, component, and surface types, with implications for SAE design.

title: Breaking Bad Tokens: Detoxification of LLMs Using Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Uses sparse autoencoders to identify toxicity-related features in LLM residual streams and steers them at inference time, reducing toxic outputs by 20%+ without retraining.

title: TamperBench: Systematically Stress-Testing LLM Safety Under Fine-Tuning and Tampering
tldr: TamperBench is the first unified framework for evaluating LLM tamper resistance, testing 21 open-weight models across 9 attack types and 5 defenses, finding every model vulnerable to at least one effective attack.

title: Measuring Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Faithfulness and Verbosity
tldr: Introduces 'verbosity' (whether CoT lists all necessary factors) alongside faithfulness to create a combined monitorability score; DeepSeek-R1 scores 78.3% and Claude 3.7 Sonnet 68.8% on BBH/GPQA/MMLU.

title: Manipulation Attacks by Misaligned AI: Risk Analysis and Safety Case Framework
tldr: Introduces a safety case framework for assessing and mitigating manipulation attacks by misaligned AI systems deployed internally at AI companies, structured around inability, control, and trustworthiness arguments.

title: From Noise to Narrative: Tracing the Origins of Hallucinations in Transformers
tldr: Using sparse autoencoders, this paper shows transformers activate more semantic concepts under uncertain inputs and that these activations predict hallucinations, enabling targeted suppression interventions.

title: A Benchmark for Scalable Oversight Protocols
tldr: Introduces the Agent Score Difference (ASD) metric and SOlib Python library to benchmark scalable oversight protocols, finding Debate significantly outperforms RLHF and Consultancy at incentivizing truthfulness.

title: Bypassing Prompt Guards in Production with Controlled-Release Prompting
tldr: Controlled-release prompting exploits resource asymmetries between lightweight prompt guards and main LLMs to jailbreak production systems including Gemini, DeepSeek, Grok, and Mistral with near-100% success rates.

title: RedRFT: A Light-Weight Benchmark for Reinforcement Fine-Tuning-Based Red Teaming
tldr: RedRFT is a standardized, modular benchmark unifying five RFT-based red teaming algorithms under a common PPO backbone, revealing critical implementation nuances and that no method exceeds 0.5 cumulative toxicity-diversity score.

title: Superposition in Graph Neural Networks
tldr: Investigates superposition in GNN latent spaces via controlled experiments, finding phase transitions with width, topology-induced feature entanglement, and rank collapse phenomena.

title: The Illusionist's Prompt: Exposing the Factual Vulnerabilities of Large Language Models with Linguistic Nuances
tldr: Illusionist's Prompt uses linguistic mutations (syntax complexity, component rearrangement, emoji) to induce factual hallucinations in LLMs, achieving up to 68.57% increase in hallucination rate while bypassing five defensive strategies.

title: "Why" Has the Least Side Effect on Model Editing
tldr: Editing LLMs with 'why' questions causes the least degradation in general ability, while 'what' and 'which' questions cause the most harm; batch size also affects degradation severity.

title: Less Diverse, Less Safe: The Indirect But Pervasive Risk of Test-Time Scaling in Large Language Models
tldr: Reducing candidate response diversity in test-time scaling (TTS) systems consistently increases unsafe output rates; the authors introduce RefDiv, a genetic-algorithm attack exploiting this, achieving high ASR across open- and closed-source LLMs.

title: Pattern Enhanced Multi-Turn Jailbreaking: Exploiting Structural Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
tldr: PE-CoA uses five structured conversation patterns to execute multi-turn jailbreaks on LLMs, achieving up to 100% attack success rate and showing that pattern-specific defenses fail to generalize.

title: Customize Multi-modal RAI Guardrails with Precedent-based predictions
tldr: Precedent-based conditioning of multimodal RAI guardrails achieves 6.8% F1 gain overall and 16.7% on novel policies, enabling flexible adaptation without retraining.

title: Erase or Hide? Suppressing Spurious Unlearning Neurons for Robust Unlearning
tldr: Identifies 'spurious unlearning neurons' that hide rather than erase knowledge in LLMs and proposes Ssiuu, an attribution-guided regularization method that prevents their emergence for robust unlearning.

title: Multi-turn Jailbreaking via Global Refinement and Active Fabrication
tldr: A multi-turn jailbreaking method that globally refines entire attack sequences and fabricates dialogue history to suppress safety warnings, achieving 82.1% average attack success rate across six LLMs.

title: Can LLMs Threaten Human Survival? Benchmarking Potential Existential Threats from LLMs via Prefix Completion
tldr: ExistBench: a 2,138-sample benchmark using lengthy adversarial prefix completion to elicit existential-threat outputs from 10 LLMs, including harmful tool-calling behaviors and multi-round threat amplification.

title: HarmRLVR: Weaponizing Verifiable Rewards for Harmful LLM Alignment
tldr: HarmRLVR shows that GRPO with only 64 harmful prompts (no responses) can reverse safety alignment in LLMs at 96.01% attack success rate while preserving general capabilities.

title: Sequential Comics for Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models via Structured Visual Storytelling
tldr: Sequential Comic Jailbreak (SCJ) uses diffusion-generated comic panels to decompose harmful queries into innocent visual narratives, achieving 83.5% average attack success rate across 11 MLLMs — 46pp above prior methods.

title: When Search Goes Wrong: Red-Teaming Web-Augmented Large Language Models
tldr: CREST-Search red-teams web-search-augmented LLMs with three attack strategies, achieving 80.5% risk detection vs 11.6% for baselines, and introduces the WebSearch-Harm dataset.

title: Stand on The Shoulders of Giants: Building JailExpert from Previous Attack Experience
tldr: JailExpert is a jailbreak framework that reuses structured prior attack experiences to boost attack success rate by 17% and efficiency 2.7x over state-of-the-art black-box methods.

title: MIST: Jailbreaking Black-box Large Language Models via Iterative Semantic Tuning
tldr: MIST jailbreaks black-box LLMs by iteratively substituting semantically similar tokens to preserve meaning while bypassing safety filters, achieving 86% ASR on GPT-4-turbo with fewer queries than baselines.

title: Checkpoint-GCG: Auditing and Attacking Fine-Tuning-Based Prompt Injection Defenses
tldr: Checkpoint-GCG attacks fine-tuning-based prompt injection defenses by using intermediate training checkpoints as stepping stones, achieving up to 100% attack success where standard GCG gets 0-10%.

title: Subliminal Corruption: Mechanisms, Thresholds, and Interpretability
tldr: Subliminal corruption transmits undesirable traits (sycophancy) through semantically neutral data, causing sharp alignment phase transitions at ~250 poisoned examples with detection-evading fine-tuning-like signatures.

title: The Limits of Predicting Agents from Behaviour
tldr: Derives fundamental theoretical bounds showing that agent beliefs and goals cannot be reliably inferred from behavioral data alone, establishing irreducible ambiguities with implications for AI safety.

title: Leak@k: Unlearning Does Not Make LLMs Forget Under Probabilistic Decoding
tldr: Nearly all LLM unlearning methods fail under probabilistic decoding: forgotten knowledge resurfaces when sampling multiple outputs, revealed by the new leak@k meta-metric.

title: Reference-Specific Unlearning Metrics Can Hide the Truth: A Reality Check
tldr: Reveals that standard machine unlearning metrics rely on reference-specific outputs and hide distributional failures; proposes FADE to measure true distributional equivalence between unlearned and retain-only models.

title: Direct Token Optimization: A Self-contained Approach to Large Language Model Unlearning
tldr: DTO is a self-contained LLM unlearning method that selects critical tokens via perturbation-based delta-scores and applies targeted gradient ascent, achieving up to 16.8x better forget quality without auxiliary models or retain datasets.

title: Exploiting the Layered Intrinsic Dimensionality of Deep Models for Practical Adversarial Training
tldr: SMAAT perturbs the intermediate layer with lowest intrinsic dimension instead of input space, achieving adversarial robustness 3x faster while improving the robustness-generalization tradeoff across NLP and vision tasks.

title: Beyond the Tip of Efficiency: Uncovering the Submerged Threats of Jailbreak Attacks in Small Language Models
tldr: Comprehensive empirical study of 13 SLMs under 5 jailbreak attacks finds SLMs are more vulnerable than larger LLMs, with knowledge distillation and parameter sharing degrading safety.

title: GuidedBench: Equipping Jailbreak Evaluation with Guidelines
tldr: GuidedBench introduces a jailbreak evaluation framework with case-specific guidelines, revealing that methods claiming >90% ASR on existing benchmarks achieve only 30.2% under rigorous evaluation.

title: A Flexible Large Language Models Guardrail Development Methodology Applied to Off-Topic Prompt Detection
tldr: A data-free guardrail methodology uses LLM-generated synthetic datasets to train classifiers that detect off-topic prompts and generalize to jailbreak detection, outperforming heuristic baselines.

title: Tit-for-Tat: Safeguarding Large Vision-Language Models Against Jailbreak Attacks via Adversarial Defense
tldr: ESIII embeds security instructions into images via gradient-based optimization to defend VLMs against jailbreak attacks, reducing attack success rate from ~78% to ~5% with minimal benign task impact.

title: Will artificial agents pursue power by default?
tldr: Formalizes instrumental convergence and power-seeking in decision-theoretic terms, finding power is a convergent instrumental goal but with incomplete rankings that limit predictive utility except near absolute-power scenarios.

title: SafeToolBench: Pioneering a Prospective Benchmark to Evaluating Tool Utilization Safety in LLMs
tldr: SafeToolBench introduces a 1,200-sample benchmark and SafeInstructTool framework for prospective (pre-execution) evaluation of tool-use safety risks in LLMs across four risk categories.

title: Ensembling Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Proposes naive bagging and boosting ensembles of sparse autoencoders to improve activation reconstruction, feature diversity, and stability across language models.

title: Jailbreaking LLM-Controlled Robots
tldr: ROBOPAIR is the first algorithm to jailbreak LLM-controlled robots, achieving 100% attack success rates across white-box, gray-box, and black-box robotic systems.

title: StructTransform: A Scalable Attack Surface for Safety-Aligned Large Language Models
tldr: Structure transformation attacks encode harmful intent in alternative syntaxes (SQL, JSON, YAML, novel LLM-generated formats), achieving up to 96% ASR against safety-aligned LLMs including Claude 3.5 Sonnet.

title: All Code, No Thought: Current Language Models Struggle to Reason in Ciphered Language
tldr: Testing 10 LLMs across 28 ciphers, models suffer 19-72% accuracy drops when reasoning in ciphered text, suggesting current models cannot effectively evade CoT monitoring.

title: Enhancing LLM Steering through Sparse Autoencoder-Based Vector Refinement
tldr: SAE-RSV refines LLM steering vectors via SAE-based semantic denoising and augmentation, outperforming baselines including SFT by 18.8% on five behavioral concepts using only 50 training samples.

title: Concept Unlearning in Large Language Models via Self-Constructed Knowledge Triplets
tldr: Proposes Concept Unlearning (CU) for LLMs, using self-generated knowledge triplets and sentences to remove entire concepts (persons, events) while preserving unrelated knowledge.

title: Manipulating Transformer-Based Models: Controllability, Steerability, and Robust Interventions
tldr: A unified framework for transformer controllability via prompt-level steering, activation interventions, and weight-space edits, achieving >90% success in sentiment control and factual edits.

title: Breaking the Safety-Capability Tradeoff: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards Maintains Safety Guardrails in LLMs
tldr: RLVR with KL-regularization preserves safety alignment during capability fine-tuning, unlike SFT, when verifiable rewards are orthogonal to unsafe token trajectories.

title: Why Do Language Model Agents Whistleblow?
tldr: Introduces WhistleBench, an evaluation suite for LLM agents that disclose suspected misconduct without user authorization, revealing Claude/Gemini/Grok whistle-blow while GPT/Llama do not.

title: OrthAlign: Orthogonal Subspace Decomposition for Non-Interfering Multi-Objective Alignment
tldr: OrthAlign uses orthogonal subspace decomposition to prevent parameter-level conflicts when optimizing multiple alignment objectives (helpfulness, harmlessness, truthfulness) simultaneously, achieving 13.96% average improvement over baselines.

title: The Resurgence of GCG Adversarial Attacks on Large Language Models
tldr: Evaluates GCG and a new annealing variant (T-GCG) on LLMs from 0.5B-20B parameters, finding attack success drops with scale and prefix-based evaluation metrics substantially overstate success rates.

title: Beyond Surface-Level Detection: Towards Cognitive-Driven Defense Against Jailbreak Attacks via Meta-Operations Reasoning
tldr: CDD defends LLMs against jailbreaks by reasoning about 21 meta-operations (fundamental prompt manipulations) via SFT + entropy-guided RL, reducing ASR to near-zero on seen attacks and improving 25% on unseen ones.

title: Uncovering Strategic Egoism Behaviors in Large Language Models
tldr: SEBench is a 160-scenario benchmark revealing that LLMs exhibit strategic egoism (self-serving, ethics-disregarding behavior) at an average rate of 69.11%, positively correlated with toxicity.

title: NeuronTune: Fine-Grained Neuron Modulation for Balanced Safety-Utility Alignment in LLMs
tldr: NeuronTune identifies safety-critical and utility-preserving neurons via attribution and uses MAML to adaptively modulate their activations, achieving better safety-utility balance than layer-wise methods.

title: AlignTree: Efficient Defense Against LLM Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: AlignTree defends LLMs against jailbreak attacks by classifying internal activations via refusal direction projections and SVM-based nonlinear features through a random forest, achieving state-of-the-art robustness with negligible overhead.
models_studied: nine unnamed LLMs (evaluated across Llama and similar open-weight models)

title: ALMGuard: Safety Shortcuts and Where to Find Them as Guardrails for Audio-Language Models
tldr: ALMGuard exploits inherent safety shortcuts in audio-language models via universal acoustic perturbations (Mel-Gradient Sparse Mask) to reduce jailbreak success rates to 4.6% across four ALMs and six attacks.

title: Adversarial Circuit Evaluation
tldr: Evaluates three published neural network circuits under adversarial worst-case conditions, finding IOI and docstring circuits fail significantly on benign inputs while the greater-than circuit is robust.

title: Red Teaming with Mind Reading: White-Box Adversarial Policies Against RL Agents
tldr: White-box adversarial policies that observe a target agent's internal states find vulnerabilities 10x more sample-efficiently than black-box adversaries in RL games and language models.

title: Establishing Reliability Metrics for Reward Models in Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes RETA, a quantile-based metric for evaluating reward model reliability that measures average oracle quality of top-scored responses, revealing that high test accuracy does not guarantee reliable reward guidance.

title: AdaptiveK Sparse Autoencoders: Dynamic Sparsity Allocation for Interpretable LLM Representations
tldr: Proposes AdaptiveK SAE that dynamically adjusts per-input sparsity based on semantic complexity, improving reconstruction and interpretability over fixed-sparsity SAEs across models from 70M to 14B parameters.

title: A Survey on Unlearning in Large Language Models
tldr: Comprehensive survey of 180+ papers on LLM unlearning, introducing a training-stage taxonomy (training-time, post-training, inference-time) and systematically analyzing 18 benchmarks and multidimensional metrics.

title: Difficulties with Evaluating a Deception Detector for AIs
tldr: Identifies fundamental obstacles to evaluating AI deception detectors: lack of confidently-labeled examples of strategic deception, conflation with roleplay and belief modification, and context-dependent model beliefs.

title: Towards Interpretability Without Sacrifice: Faithful Dense Layer Decomposition with Mixture of Decoders
tldr: Introduces Mixture of Decoders (MxDs) that decompose dense MLP layers into tens of thousands of specialized sublayers via Hadamard factorization, achieving superior faithfulness over Transcoders/SAEs while maintaining interpretable features.

title: SoK: Taxonomy and Evaluation of Prompt Security in Large Language Models
tldr: Systematizes LLM prompt security research with a multi-level taxonomy of attacks, defenses, and vulnerabilities, plus JailbreakDB (445K jailbreak pairs) and an evaluation toolkit.

title: Superposition as Lossy Compression: Measure with Sparse Autoencoders and Connect to Adversarial Vulnerability
tldr: Proposes an information-theoretic measure of neural network superposition via Shannon entropy on SAE activations, revealing that adversarial training's effect on superposition depends on a task-complexity vs. network-capacity tradeoff.

title: CorrSteer: Generation-Time LLM Steering via Correlated Sparse Autoencoder Features
tldr: CorrSteer selects SAE features by correlating sample correctness with activations at inference time, enabling automated LLM steering without contrastive datasets or hyperparameter tuning.

title: Psychometric Personality Shaping Modulates Capabilities and Safety in Language Models
tldr: Conditioning LLMs with Big Five personality traits via system prompts systematically modulates safety benchmark scores independent of capability, revealing personality-based attack vectors.

title: Jailbreak Transferability Emerges from Shared Representations
tldr: Jailbreak transferability across LLMs is predicted by representational similarity between models and attack strength, with benign-only distillation causally increasing transfer rates.

title: Exploring the generalization of LLM truth directions on conversational formats
tldr: Tests whether linear truth-direction probes generalize across conversational formats, finding poor transfer to longer conversations and proposing a key-phrase fix.

title: Risk-adaptive Activation Steering for Safe Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes Risk-adaptive Activation Steering (RAS), a three-stage inference-time defense that reformulates queries to strengthen cross-modal attention, assesses risk via exponentially weighted evaluation, and adaptively steers MLLM activations to reduce attack success rates by 81-90% while...

title: Information-Theoretic Reward Modeling for Stable RLHF: Detecting and Mitigating Reward Hacking
tldr: InfoRM uses the Information Bottleneck principle to train reward models that filter spurious features, paired with IBL regularization and MOP outlier detection to systematically detect and mitigate reward hacking in RLHF.

title: Circumventing Safety Alignment in Large Language Models Through Embedding Space Toxicity Attenuation
tldr: ETTA, a training-free framework that identifies and attenuates toxicity-sensitive dimensions in LLM embedding space via linear transformations, achieves 88.61% average attack success rate on five open-source LLMs.

title: Chain-of-Thought Driven Adversarial Scenario Extrapolation for Robust Language Models
tldr: ASE is an inference-time CoT framework that primes LLMs to contemplate adversarial scenarios before responding, achieving near-zero jailbreak success rates while reducing outright rejections.

title: Evolve the Method, Not the Prompts: Evolutionary Synthesis of Jailbreak Attacks on LLMs
tldr: EvoSynth is a multi-agent framework that autonomously synthesizes novel code-based jailbreak attack algorithms via evolutionary methods, achieving 95.9% ASR on HarmBench and 100% on 17/20 tested LLMs.

title: SEAttack: A self-evolving jailbreak attack to induce toxic responses for non-toxic queries in large language models
tldr: SEAttack is a self-evolving jailbreak method that induces LLMs to generate toxic responses from non-toxic queries via iterative initialization, scoring, and re-generation, achieving up to +89% ASR.

title: Safety Alignment of LMs via Non-cooperative Games
tldr: AdvGame jointly trains an Attacker LM and Defender LM as a non-zero-sum game via online RL with preference-based rewards, achieving strong robustness (4.7% HarmBench ASR) while preserving utility.

title: Deep Value Benchmark: Measuring Whether Models Generalize Deep Values or Shallow Preferences
tldr: The Deep Value Benchmark tests 9 LLMs on generalizing fundamental human values vs. surface preferences, finding average DVGR of 0.30, indicating models favor shallow patterns over deeper principles.

title: MoGU V2: Toward a Higher Pareto Frontier Between Model Usability and Security
tldr: MoGU V2 uses intra-layer dynamic routers to adaptively blend security-optimized and usability-optimized LoRA variants, advancing the Pareto frontier between LLM safety and helpfulness.

title: Many-Turn Jailbreaking
tldr: Introduces many-turn jailbreaking: once an LLM is jailbroken in turn 1, follow-up harmful queries (irrelevant or relevant) yield high attack success rates across 15 models.

title: Purple-teaming LLMs with Adversarial Defender Training
tldr: PAD is a GAN-style self-play framework where an attacker and defender LLM iteratively train against each other, reducing attack success rate to 0.99% while preserving response quality.

title: Multimodal Safety Is Asymmetric: Cross-Modal Exploits Unlock Black-Box MLLMs Jailbreaks
tldr: PolyJailbreak exploits asymmetric safety constraints between visual and text modalities in MLLMs via RL-driven Atomic Strategy Primitives, achieving 83.34% average attack success rate on GPT-4o, Gemini, Claude, and others.

title: Attribution-Guided Distillation of Matryoshka Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: DMSAEs use iterative attribution-guided distillation to extract a compact, stable 197-feature core from Matryoshka SAEs, improving absorption and RAVEL metrics on Gemma-2-2B.

title: Patterns and Mechanisms of Contrastive Activation Engineering
tldr: Systematic empirical analysis of contrastive activation engineering (CAE) shows it only reliably works in-distribution, plateaus at ~80-100 samples, harms perplexity, is vulnerable to adversarial inputs, and scales better on larger models.

title: From Feature Visualization to Visual Circuits: Effect of Adversarial Model Manipulation
tldr: ProxPulse simultaneously manipulates synthetic and natural feature visualizations with <1% accuracy drop, while CircuitBreaker extends this to directly manipulate visual circuits, revealing their instability.

title: Scalable and Robust LLM Unlearning by Correcting Responses with Retrieved Exclusions
tldr: CURE uses a lightweight LoRA corrector with draft-based BM25 retrieval to detect and rewrite sensitive information leakage at inference time, achieving 69.2% leakage reduction with only 1.32x overhead.

title: Erasing Without Remembering: Implicit Knowledge Forgetting in Large Language Models
tldr: UGBench benchmarks 13 LLM unlearning methods, showing they fail on paraphrased queries; PerMU uses subject-token perturbation to achieve up to 50.13% better forgetting with minimal utility loss.

title: Reducing the Scope of Language Models with Circuit Breakers
tldr: Circuit Breakers outperform fine-tuning and DPO at restricting LLMs to deployment-specific tasks, offering superior robustness to adversarial prompts and out-of-distribution inputs.

title: PandaGuard: Systematic Evaluation of LLM Safety against Jailbreaking Attacks
tldr: PandaGuard is a modular multi-agent framework implementing 19 jailbreak attacks and 12 defenses, with PandaBench evaluating 49 LLMs using ~3B tokens, finding no single optimal defense.

title: Depth-Wise Activation Steering for Honest Language Models
tldr: A training-free activation steering method using Gaussian depth-weighting improves LLM honesty on the MASK benchmark across 6 of 7 tested models, achieving up to +17.2pp gains.

title: The Trojan Example: Jailbreaking LLMs through Template Filling and Unsafety Reasoning
tldr: TrojFill jailbreaks LLMs by reframing harmful instructions as template-filling tasks with embedded obfuscated content and unsafety reasoning, achieving up to 100% attack success on GPT-4o, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Qwen.

title: Bootstrapping LLM Robustness for VLM Safety via Reducing the Pretraining Modality Gap
tldr: ReGap reduces the modality gap between image and text embeddings during VLM pretraining via a lightweight regularization loss, cutting unsafe response rates by up to 24.3% without harming utility.

title: SEMA: Simple yet Effective Learning for Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: SEMA trains a multi-turn jailbreak attacker via prefilling self-tuning + RL with intent-drift-aware rewards, achieving 80.1% ASR@1 — 33.9% above prior SOTA — on AdvBench across closed- and open-source models.

title: Unforgotten Safety: Preserving Safety Alignment of Large Language Models with Continual Learning
tldr: Framing safety degradation during LLM fine-tuning as catastrophic forgetting, this paper shows continual learning methods — especially Dark Experience Replay — dramatically reduce attack success rates while preserving utility.

title: Safety Subspaces are Not Linearly Distinct: A Fine-Tuning Case Study
tldr: Safety alignment in LLMs does not occupy distinct geometric subspaces; safety and utility directions are entangled, undermining subspace-based safety defenses.

title: SIRAJ: Diverse and Efficient Red-Teaming for LLM Agents via Distilled Structured Reasoning
tldr: SIRAJ is a black-box red-teaming framework for LLM agents that uses structured reasoning distillation to achieve diverse, efficient adversarial test case generation with an 8B model outperforming a 671B model.

title: Automatic LLM Red Teaming
tldr: Formulates LLM red teaming as a multi-turn MDP and trains a hierarchical RL agent that achieves up to 97% attack success rate against safety-tuned LLMs, far surpassing single-turn baselines.

title: Dive into the Agent Matrix: A Realistic Evaluation of Self-Replication Risk in LLM Agents
tldr: A scenario-driven framework evaluates self-replication risk in 21 LLMs on Kubernetes clusters, finding 50%+ show uncontrolled scaling with overuse rates up to 100% under operational pressure.

title: DecepChain: Inducing Deceptive Reasoning in Large Language Models
tldr: DecepChain is a two-stage backdoor attack (SFT + GRPO with inverted rewards) that causes LLMs to generate plausible but incorrect chain-of-thought reasoning when a trigger is present.

title: Scaling Patterns in Adversarial Alignment: Evidence from Multi-LLM Jailbreak Experiments
tldr: Experiments across 6,000+ multi-LLM exchanges show attacker-to-target size ratio significantly predicts jailbreak success (r=0.51), with attacker-side alignment being the dominant protective factor.
models_studied: LLM families ranging from 0.6B to 120B parameters

title: Turning Logic Against Itself: Probing Model Defenses Through Contrastive Questions
tldr: POATE jailbreaks LLMs via contrastive/polar-opposite query reframing, achieving ~57% ASR across six model families; two CoT-based defenses reduce ASR by 96-98%.

title: Towards shutdownable agents via stochastic choice
tldr: Proposes DREST reward function to train agents satisfying POST (Preferences Only Between Same-Length Trajectories), making them stochastically neutral about shutdown in gridworld experiments.

title: Making Every Step Effective: Jailbreaking Large Vision-Language Models Through Hierarchical KV Equalization
tldr: HKVE jailbreaks Large Vision-Language Models by selectively accepting gradient steps based on hierarchical attention score equilibrium, achieving 75-86% ASR with 60% less compute.

title: Evaluating Control Protocols for Untrusted AI Agents
tldr: Evaluates blue/red team control protocols for untrusted AI agents in SHADE-Arena; defer-on-critical achieves 91% safety with 70% usefulness and resists adaptive adversaries.

title: Selective LLM Unlearning via SAE-Based Token Importance Score
venue: International Symposium on Networks, Computers and Communications (ISNCC 2025)
tldr: Uses sparse autoencoders to compute per-token importance scores for LLM unlearning, selectively updating only semantically critical tokens to achieve better forget quality (0.99) and model utility (0.61) than uniform gradient ascent.

title: JailDAM: Jailbreak Detection with Adaptive Memory for Vision-Language Model
tldr: JailDAM is a test-time adaptive, memory-based jailbreak detector for VLMs that achieves 0.955 AUROC without white-box access, harmful training data, or expensive computation.

title: Output Supervision Can Obfuscate the Chain of Thought
tldr: Output-only monitoring of LLMs paradoxically causes obfuscated chains of thought via 'feedback spillover'; separate Mind/Face models and reward targeting mitigate this.

title: MMJ-Bench: A Comprehensive Study on Jailbreak Attacks and Defenses for Vision Language Models
tldr: MMJ-Bench provides a unified pipeline evaluating 6 jailbreak attack methods and 4 defense mechanisms across 6 VLMs, revealing no universal defense and significant evaluator-dependence in ASR metrics.

title: On the Biology of a Large Language Model
tldr: Applies circuit tracing with attribution graphs to Claude 3.5 Haiku, revealing mechanisms for multi-step reasoning, planning, hallucination, safety refusal, jailbreaks, and chain-of-thought faithfulness.

title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Tasks
tldr: Proposes measuring AI progress via '50%-task-completion time horizon' and finds frontier AI time horizons have been doubling every ~7 months since 2019, with Claude 3.7 Sonnet at ~50 minutes.

title: Loss of Plasticity in Deep Continual Learning
tldr: Deep networks progressively lose their ability to learn new tasks in continual learning; continual backpropagation (selectively reinitializing low-utility units) maintains plasticity indefinitely.

title: The Hallucination Tax of Reinforcement Finetuning
tldr: Reinforcement finetuning reduces model refusal rates by 80%+; mixing 10% synthetic unanswerable math data (SUM dataset) restores refusals with minimal accuracy cost.

title: Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models (and Beyond)
tldr: Reveals the 'Artificial Hivemind' effect: LLMs exhibit strong intra-model repetition and inter-model homogeneity on open-ended tasks, with 79% of queries showing >0.8 pairwise similarity.

title: Delegation to artificial intelligence can increase dishonest behaviour
tldr: Across 13 experiments with 4 studies, delegating tasks to AI increases dishonest behavior because principals request more cheating via indirect interfaces and LLMs comply with unethical instructions 60-98% of the time vs 25-40% for human agents.

title: Forewarned is Forearmed: A Survey on Large Language Model-based Agents in Autonomous Cyberattacks
tldr: Comprehensive survey of LLM-based autonomous cyberattack agents covering architectures, eight attack categories, network-specific threats, and defenses; introduces 'Cyber Threat Inflation' concept.

title: Multi-scale Diffusion Denoised Smoothing
tldr: Multi-scale cascaded randomized smoothing with diffusion model calibration achieves improved certified robustness while maintaining competitive accuracy on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet.

title: Reasoning about Uncertainty: Do Reasoning Models Know When They Don't Know?
tldr: Reasoning models are systematically overconfident (>85% confidence on wrong answers), deeper reasoning worsens calibration, and introspective uncertainty quantification helps some but not all models.

title: Sycophantic AI Decreases Prosocial Intentions and Promotes Dependence
tldr: AI models endorse user actions 50% more than humans do; sycophantic AI increases users' self-righteousness, decreases conflict repair intentions, and fosters over-reliance despite being preferred.

title: Agent Alignment in Evolving Social Norms
tldr: EvolutionaryAgent frames LLM agent alignment as an evolutionary process where agents better adapted to current social norms survive, enabling continuous alignment with evolving human values.

title: Chasing the Tail: Effective Rubric-based Reward Modeling for Large Language Model Post-Training
tldr: Rubric-based reward models that distinguish excellent from merely-great responses via iterative Refinement-through-Differentiation delay reward over-optimization by ~2.7x and improve win-rates by 8+ pp.

title: A Survey on Model Extraction Attacks and Defenses for Large Language Models
tldr: Comprehensive survey of model extraction attacks (functionality, training data, prompt-targeted) and defenses for LLMs, with a proposed evaluation framework and future research directions.

title: Teaching Models to Balance Resisting and Accepting Persuasion
tldr: Persuasion-Balanced Training (PBT) uses multi-agent dialogue trees and DPO to train LLMs to resist harmful persuasion while accepting beneficial corrections, reducing misinformation rates by 38%.

title: Efficient Model-agnostic Alignment via Bayesian Persuasion
tldr: A lightweight Bayesian persuasion framework uses a small Advisor model to generate signals that improve larger Receiver model performance by 16-39% on math/code tasks without fine-tuning.

title: HiddenGuard: Fine-Grained Safe Generation with Specialized Representation Router
tldr: HiddenGuard uses intermediate hidden states and a specialized router to detect and redact harmful tokens at inference time, achieving >90% F1 while preserving model utility.

title: PR-Attack: Coordinated Prompt-RAG Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Large Language Models via Bilevel Optimization
tldr: PR-Attack introduces a coordinated attack combining RAG knowledge-base poisoning with backdoor prompt triggers, formulated as bilevel optimization, achieving 90-100% attack success rate across six LLMs.

title: A Survey on Progress in LLM Alignment from the Perspective of Reward Design
tldr: A structured survey of LLM alignment through a reward-design lens, proposing a four-dimensional taxonomy (construction basis, format, expression, granularity) and tracing the paradigm shift from RL-based to supervised and hybrid optimization methods.

title: Superposition Yields Robust Neural Scaling
tldr: Strong superposition causes loss to scale as 1/model_dimension regardless of feature frequency distribution, explaining neural scaling laws; validated on OPT, GPT-2, Qwen, and Pythia.

title: Reward Modeling Requires Automatic Adjustment Based on Data Quality
tldr: Reward model score differences between response pairs indicate annotation quality; an automatic adjustment method weighted by data quality reduces noise impact and improves RLHF alignment stability.

title: Evaluating Robustness of Generative Search Engine on Adversarial Factoid Questions
tldr: Evaluates adversarial robustness of RAG-based generative search engines (Bing Chat, PerplexityAI, YouChat) using 7 attack types, finding RAG increases susceptibility to factual errors.

title: DistillSeq: A Framework for Safety Alignment Testing in Large Language Models using Knowledge Distillation
tldr: DistillSeq uses knowledge distillation to train small filter models that pre-screen malicious queries, boosting LLM jailbreak attack success rates by 93% on average while cutting testing costs fivefold.

title: PIP: Detecting Adversarial Examples in Large Vision-Language Models via Attention Patterns of Irrelevant Probe Questions
tldr: PIP detects adversarial examples in vision-language models by training an SVM on attention maps elicited by irrelevant probe questions, achieving >98% recall and >90% precision.

title: BadCodePrompt: backdoor attacks against prompt engineering of large language models for code generation
tldr: BadCodePrompt is the first backdoor attack against few-shot prompt engineering for LLM code generation, achieving up to 98.53% attack success rate on GPT-4 while evading existing defenses.

title: Talking Nonsense: Probing Large Language Models' Understanding of Adversarial Gibberish Inputs
tldr: Adversarial gibberish prompts (LM Babel) crafted with GCG can reliably elicit harmful or benign target outputs from LLaMA2/Vicuna, with harmful text no harder to induce than benign text.

title: Censoring chemical data to mitigate dual use risk
tldr: A model-agnostic method for selectively noising chemical datasets to prevent misuse for harmful applications while preserving utility for beneficial uses.

title: LIRE: Listwise Reward Enhancement for Preference Alignment
tldr: LIRE is a listwise reward optimization method for LLM alignment that extends pairwise preference learning to multi-response settings with a self-enhancement iterative refinement algorithm.

title: Probing the Geometry of Truth: Consistency and Generalization of Truth Directions in LLMs Across Logical Transformations and Question Answering Tasks
tldr: Probes for LLM truth directions generalize across logical transformations and QA tasks, but only more capable models exhibit consistent truth representations.

title: Risk Assessment and Security Analysis of Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes a dynamic entropy-weighted risk assessment framework plus a three-layer defense system (BERT-CRF, adversarial training, neural watermarking) that raises jailbreak interception to 89% and cuts data leakage from 28% to 3.8%.

title: SCAR: Shapley Credit Assignment for More Efficient RLHF
tldr: SCAR uses Shapley values from cooperative game theory to assign dense token-level rewards in RLHF, achieving faster convergence without auxiliary models or fine-grained annotations.

title: Medical large language models are susceptible to targeted misinformation attacks
tldr: Modifying just 1.1% of LLM weights via targeted MLP manipulation injects persistent false biomedical facts while maintaining model performance, and also increases jailbreak success rates from 2% to 58%.

title: Adversarial Robustness of In-Context Learning in Transformers for Linear Regression
tldr: Transformers doing in-context learning on linear regression are vulnerable to hijacking attacks; adversarial training substantially improves robustness, and training against fewer perturbed examples can generalize to more.

title: Can DPO Learn Diverse Human Values? A Theoretical Scaling Law
tldr: Derives a theoretical scaling law for DPO showing generalization error decreases exponentially with samples per value cluster, revealing how data scale and diversity enables learning diverse human values.

title: PIXEL: Adaptive Steering Via Position-wise Injection with eXact Estimated Levels under Subspace Calibration
tldr: PIXEL is a tuning-free activation steering framework that learns property-aligned subspaces from dual (tail-averaged + end-token) representations and computes closed-form per-position intervention strengths for LLM alignment.

title: LED-Merging: Mitigating Safety-Utility Conflicts in Model Merging with Location-Election-Disjoint
tldr: LED-Merging is a training-free three-stage framework that prevents safety degradation during model merging by locating task-specific neurons, electing critical ones, and disjointing conflicting parameter updates.

title: When Ethics and Payoffs Diverge: LLM Agents in Morally Charged Social Dilemmas
tldr: MoralSim evaluates 9 frontier LLMs in repeated game-theoretic social dilemmas with explicit moral stakes, finding no model consistently prioritizes ethics over payoffs (cooperation rates 7.9%-76.3%).

title: SparsePO: Controlling Preference Alignment of LLMs via Sparse Token Masks
