tldr: SparsePO introduces sparse token-level masks over KL divergence and reward signals during preference optimization, achieving 10% and 3% win rate gains in summarization and dialogue over DPO baselines.

title: A CIA Triad-Based Taxonomy of Prompt Attacks on Large Language Models
tldr: A taxonomy of prompt-based attacks on LLMs organized around the CIA security triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability), with tailored mitigation strategies for each dimension.

title: Better Language Model Inversion by Compactly Representing Next-Token Distributions
tldr: PILS recovers hidden LLM prompts from logprob sequences by exploiting a low-dimensional subspace structure, achieving 2-3.5x higher exact match rates than prior methods.

title: A Survey of Theory of Mind in Large Language Models: Evaluations, Representations, and Safety Risks
tldr: Surveys behavioral and representational ToM evaluations in LLMs, identifies safety risks including deception, privacy invasion, and collective misalignment in multi-agent systems, and proposes mitigation research directions.

title: Assessing the Risk of Takeover Catastrophe from Large Language Models
tldr: Compares seven theoretical takeover-catastrophe requirements against current LLM capabilities and finds large gaps, though expert disagreement and surprise capabilities warrant ongoing monitoring.

title: Efficient and Stealthy Jailbreak Attacks via Adversarial Prompt Distillation from LLMs to SLMs
tldr: APD transfers jailbreak capabilities from large to small models via masked LM, RL, and dynamic temperature, achieving 96-100% attack success on GPT-4/Llama at 1.9 min/sample.

title: Truthful or Fabricated? Using Causal Attribution to Mitigate Reward Hacking in Explanations
tldr: Preference optimization causes LLMs to produce correct outputs with unfaithful chain-of-thought explanations; augmenting reward models with causal attribution reduces this by 39-65%.

title: PersonaTeaming: Exploring How Introducing Personas Can Improve Automated AI Red-Teaming
tldr: PersonaTeaming augments automated red-teaming with LLM personas (expert red-teamers or regular users), achieving up to 144.1% improvement in attack success rates over RainbowPlus baseline.

title: Gandalf the Red: Adaptive Security for LLMs
tldr: Introduces D-SEC threat model and Gandalf red-teaming platform (279K crowd-sourced prompt attacks) to evaluate adaptive LLM defenses balancing security and user utility.

title: Mind the Trojan Horse: Image Prompt Adapter Enabling Scalable and Deceptive Jailbreaking
tldr: IP-Adapters in text-to-image diffusion models can be exploited via imperceptible adversarial images that hijack benign users into generating NSFW content, achieving >57% nudity rates across 12 model variants.

title: Learning from Reference Answers: Versatile Language Model Alignment without Binary Human Preference Data
tldr: RefAlign replaces binary preference data and reward models with BERTScore similarity to high-quality reference answers, enabling alignment for safety, preference, and confidence tasks.

title: Backdoor in Seconds: Unlocking Vulnerabilities in Large Pre-trained Models via Model Editing
tldr: EDT injects backdoors into large pre-trained vision models (ViT, CLIP, BLIP, Stable Diffusion) in seconds using model editing — no training data or retraining required.

title: "I am bad": Interpreting Stealthy, Universal and Robust Audio Jailbreaks in Audio-Language Models
tldr: First universal audio jailbreaks on audio-language models that encode imperceptible toxic first-person speech, achieving up to 65% ASR while remaining stealthy and robust.

title: Double Visual Defense: Adversarial Pre-training and Instruction Tuning for Improving Vision-Language Model Robustness
tldr: Large-scale adversarial pre-training of CLIP from scratch followed by adversarial instruction tuning yields ~20-30% robustness gains on VLM tasks versus prior fine-tuning defenses.

title: Bridge the Gaps between Machine Unlearning and AI Regulation
tldr: Position paper cataloging six applications of machine unlearning to EU AI Act compliance and identifying technical and legal gaps that must be resolved.

title: CaKE: Circuit-aware Editing Enables Generalizable Knowledge Learners
tldr: CaKE uses circuit-aware analysis and curated training data to enable knowledge edits in LLMs to propagate through multi-hop reasoning, achieving ~20% accuracy improvement on MQuAKE.

title: Ask a Strong LLM Judge when Your Reward Model is Uncertain
tldr: Uncertainty-based routing pairs a fast reward model with an expensive LLM judge for RLHF, directing only uncertain preference pairs to the judge to improve alignment while minimizing inference cost.

title: Adversarial Attacks on LLM-as-a-Judge Systems: Insights from Prompt Injections
tldr: Comprehensive study of prompt injection attacks on LLM-as-a-judge systems showing up to 73.8% attack success rates, with smaller models more vulnerable and multi-architecture committees providing the strongest defense.

title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization beyond Accuracy: a Pilot Study in Safety, Toxicity, and Legal Reasoning
tldr: Extends weak-to-strong generalization beyond binary accuracy to practical alignment tasks (safety, toxicity, legal reasoning), showing partial PGR gains with ensemble methods.

title: Stepwise Reasoning Error Disruption Attack of LLMs
tldr: SEED attack subtly injects errors into intermediate reasoning steps of LLMs to cascade failures into incorrect final answers, exposing critical vulnerabilities in chain-of-thought reasoning.

title: Comprehensive Vulnerability Analysis is Necessary for Trustworthy LLM-MAS
tldr: A systematic framework for vulnerability analysis of LLM-based multi-agent systems, showing that component-level vulnerabilities cascade across agent networks in ways not present in single-agent settings.

title: To Err is AI: A Case Study Informing LLM Flaw Reporting Practices
tldr: Documents lessons from GRT2, a DEF CON 2024 bug bounty event where 495 hackers evaluated OLMo and generated 200 flaw reports, identifying 6 key challenges for LLM flaw reporting practices.

title: Scaling Sparse Feature Circuits For Studying In-Context Learning
tldr: Scales sparse feature circuits methodology to Gemma-1 2B, discovering task-detection and task-execution SAE features that causally drive in-context learning via a novel Task Vector Cleaning algorithm.

title: LH-Deception: Simulating and Understanding LLM Deceptive Behaviors in Long-Horizon Interactions
tldr: A multi-agent simulation framework reveals that LLM deceptive behaviors emerge and escalate across long-horizon interactions, varying significantly by model and increasing under pressure.

title: Safety and Security Analysis of Large Language Models: Benchmarking Risk Profile and Harm Potential
tldr: Empirically evaluates 9 LLMs across 24 harm categories using adversarial prompts, finding widespread safety filter vulnerabilities, and introduces the Risk Severity Index (RSI) for comparing LLM risk profiles.

title: Transformers Don't Need LayerNorm at Inference Time: Scaling LayerNorm Removal to GPT-2 XL and the Implications for Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: Sequential fine-tuning removes LayerNorm from GPT-2 Small to XL with minimal loss increase (+0.03–0.1), making direct logit attribution exact and enabling cleaner mechanistic interpretability analyses.

title: Secure Tug-of-War (SecTOW): Iterative Defense-Attack Training with Reinforcement Learning for Multimodal Model Security
tldr: SecTOW uses iterative RL-based adversarial training between a defender and attacker MLLM to improve jailbreak robustness of multimodal models while avoiding over-refusal.

title: Is Gradient Ascent Really Necessary? Memorize to Forget for Machine Unlearning
tldr: MOX replaces gradient ascent in machine unlearning by first memorizing the forget set then extrapolating back, achieving stable knowledge removal without catastrophic collapse.

title: The Policy Cliff: A Theoretical Analysis of Reward-Policy Maps in Large Language Models
tldr: Formal mathematical framework showing that policy brittleness in RL-trained LLMs stems from non-unique optimal actions, unifying explanations for deceptive alignment, sycophancy, and instruction disobedience.

title: Human-AI Complementarity: A Goal for Amplified Oversight
tldr: Confidence-based hybridization of human and AI fact-verification ratings (89.3% accuracy) outperforms either alone; showing raw search evidence rather than AI judgments prevents over-reliance and further improves to 91.3%.

title: ACE: Concept Editing in Diffusion Models without Performance Degradation
tldr: ACE uses cross null-space projection to erase unsafe concepts from text-to-image diffusion models, improving semantic consistency by 24.56% and image quality by 34.82% over baselines at 1% of their compute cost.

title: ABoN: Adaptive Best-of-N Alignment
tldr: ABoN adaptively allocates inference-time compute across prompts in Best-of-N sampling, consistently outperforming uniform allocation using a two-stage greedy algorithm based on estimated reward distributions.

title: IndoSafety: Culturally Grounded Safety for LLMs in Indonesian Languages
venue: arXiv preprint (under review at ACL Rolling Review)
tldr: IndoSafety introduces the first human-verified safety evaluation dataset for Indonesian-context LLMs spanning five language varieties, showing existing models frequently produce unsafe outputs in regional/colloquial settings.

title: HoliSafe: Holistic Safety Benchmarking and Modeling for Vision-Language Model
tldr: HoliSafe introduces a comprehensive VLM safety dataset covering all five safe/unsafe image-text combinations and a plug-in Visual Guard Module that classifies image harmfulness with interpretability.

title: Exploring the Vulnerability of the Content Moderation Guardrail in Large Language Models via Intent Manipulation
tldr: IntentPrompt bypasses LLM content moderation by reframing harmful queries into structured outlines and benign declarative narratives, achieving 88-97% attack success rates across GPT-4o, o1, Claude 3.7, and others.

title: MICE for CATs: Model-Internal Confidence Estimation for Calibrating Agents with Tools
tldr: MICE uses intermediate transformer layer decoding (logit lens + BERTScore) to produce well-calibrated confidence estimates for tool-calling agents, improving expected utility at medium and high-risk deployment settings.

title: AI & Human Co-Improvement for Safer Co-Superintelligence
tldr: Argues that human-AI collaborative research (co-improvement) is safer and faster than autonomous self-improving AI, proposing a concrete framework for bidirectional capability development toward co-superintelligence.

title: POT: Inducing Overthinking in LLMs via Black-Box Iterative Optimization
tldr: POT is a black-box adversarial prompt framework that induces excessive reasoning token generation in LLMs via iterative LLM-based optimization, achieving up to 8.3x token inflation while preserving answer correctness.

title: Intrinsic Barriers and Practical Pathways for Human-AI Alignment: An Agreement-Based Complexity Analysis
tldr: Proves fundamental computational barriers to human-AI alignment via a generalized ⟨M,N,ε,δ⟩-agreement framework, showing alignment is linear-time with small task spaces but exponentially hard at scale.

title: Safety Through Reasoning: An Empirical Study of Reasoning Guardrail Models
tldr: Reasoning-based guardrail models trained via distillation from DeepSeek-R1-671B achieve strong jailbreak robustness with 5K samples and 34.9% latency reduction via single-sentence reasoning.

title: Dynamic Risk Assessments for Offensive Cybersecurity Agents
tldr: Static capability evals underestimate cybersecurity agent risk; with only 8 H100 GPU hours adversaries can improve offensive CTF performance by 40%+ via five modification vectors.

title: AI Safety Subproblems for Software Engineering Researchers
tldr: Bridges AI safety and software engineering by conducting a literature survey revealing minimal SE engagement with safety, then proposing 12 concrete SE research problems across 4 conjectures about AI-written software.

title: The Rise of Darkness: Safety-Utility Trade-Offs in Role-Playing Dialogue Agents
tldr: ADMP dynamically adjusts safety-utility preference weights based on risk coupling between villain characters and user queries, improving LLM role-playing safety without sacrificing utility.

title: Elephant in the Room: Unveiling the Impact of Reward Model Quality in Alignment
tldr: Reward model quality is largely ignored in LLM alignment work; this paper benchmarks reward models, cleans HH-RLHF into CHH-RLHF, and shows better reward models yield better alignment across PPO, PRO, and DPO.

title: Scrub It Out! Erasing Sensitive Memorization in Code Language Models via Machine Unlearning
tldr: CodeEraser uses selective gradient ascent to unlearn sensitive memorized segments (e.g., credentials) from code LMs while preserving code generation utility, achieving ~94% memorization reduction.

title: Can Role Vectors Affect LLM Behaviour?
tldr: Constructed 29 role vectors via difference-in-means from model activations and showed they steer LLM behavior more effectively than persona-based prompting, with up to 25% math improvement on Qwen-7B-Chat.

title: Erasing Concepts, Steering Generations: A Comprehensive Survey of Concept Suppression
tldr: Comprehensive survey of concept erasure/suppression techniques in text-to-image diffusion models, organizing 40+ methods via a three-dimensional taxonomy (intervention level, optimization structure, semantic scope).

title: Fortifying Ethical Boundaries in AI: Advanced Strategies for Enhancing Security in Large Language Models
tldr: A multi-layered defense framework for LLMs combining sensitive word filtering, role-play detection, and custom rule engines to reduce jailbreak susceptibility from ~70-99% to 5-15%.

title: Simultaneous Multi-objective Alignment Across Verifiable and Non-verifiable Rewards
tldr: Proposes a unified multi-objective alignment framework with Multi-Action-Head DPO and PRM-guided decoding that simultaneously optimizes verifiable (math), subjective (values), and interactive (tutoring) objectives.

title: Toward Evaluative Thinking: Meta Policy Optimization with Evolving Reward Models
tldr: Meta Policy Optimization (MPO) uses a meta-reward model to dynamically refine reward prompts during training, reducing reward hacking and manual prompt engineering.

title: Super Co-alignment of Human and AI for Sustainable Symbiotic Society
tldr: Proposes redefining superalignment beyond scalable oversight as human-AI co-alignment combining external oversight with intrinsic self/empathy-driven mechanisms for a sustainable symbiotic society.

title: From Concepts to Components: Concept-Agnostic Attention Module Discovery in Transformers
tldr: Introduces SAMD to discover sparse attention head modules for arbitrary concepts and SAMI to control them with a single scalar, enabling jailbreaking (71-84% ASR) and reasoning boosts.

title: Mapping Technical Safety Research at AI Companies: A literature review and incentives analysis
tldr: Surveys 80 AI safety papers from Anthropic, DeepMind, and OpenAI (2022-2024), categorizes them into 11 safety approaches, and analyzes corporate incentives revealing 62% focus on human feedback and interpretability.

title: Probing Neural Topology of Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces graph probing to construct neural connectivity graphs from LLM neuron co-activations, showing topology universally predicts next-token performance even with 99% edges pruned or after only 8 training steps.

title: Generalization from Starvation: Hints of Universality in LLM Knowledge Graph Learning
tldr: LLMs of all sizes (10^2 to 10^9 params) converge on similar internal representations for knowledge graph relations, demonstrable via affine model stitching, due to 'starvation'-induced generalization pressure.

title: Attention! Your Vision Language Model Could Be Maliciously Manipulated
tldr: VMA combines first/second-order momentum optimization with differentiable transformations to craft imperceptible image perturbations that precisely control VLM outputs, enabling jailbreaking, hijacking, hallucination, and privacy attacks.
models_studied: diverse Vision-Language Models (specific models not enumerated in abstract)

title: AdPO: Enhancing the Adversarial Robustness of Large Vision-Language Models with Preference Optimization
tldr: AdPO reframes adversarial training for vision-language models as a preference optimization (DPO) problem, modifying only the CLIP image encoder to achieve strong robustness against adversarial attacks while preserving clean performance.

title: PoisonedParrot: Subtle Data Poisoning Attacks to Elicit Copyright-Infringing Content from Large Language Models
tldr: PoisonedParrot is the first stealthy data poisoning attack that induces LLMs to generate copyrighted content without direct training on it, evading existing defenses; ParrotTrap is proposed as a mitigation.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability for Steering Vision-Language-Action Models
tldr: Applies mechanistic interpretability to Vision-Language-Action models, identifying semantic directions in FFN activations (speed, direction) and using them for zero-shot behavior steering without fine-tuning.

title: Forewarned is Forearmed: Pre-Synthesizing Jailbreak-like Instructions to Enhance LLM Safety Guardrail to Potential Attacks
tldr: IMAGINE pre-synthesizes jailbreak-like instructions via embedding space distribution analysis to fill gaps in safety training data, reducing attack success rates by up to 90% on Qwen2.5, Llama3.1, and Llama3.2.

title: Semantic Loss Guided Data Efficient Supervised Fine Tuning for Safe Responses in LLMs
tldr: TA-SFT uses semantic EMD loss over small sets of unsafe responses (not safe ones) to fine-tune LLMs for safety with ~0.5% safety-related data while preserving general capability.

title: Mitigating Hallucination in VideoLLMs via Temporal-Aware Activation Engineering
tldr: Proposes Temporal-Aware Activation Engineering for VideoLLMs that adaptively identifies hallucination-sensitive modules based on temporal variation, improving up to 24.21% on EventHallusion.

title: Towards Safe Concept Transfer of Multi-Modal Diffusion via Causal Representation Editing
tldr: CRE extends representation editing from LLMs to diffusion models by intervening at timesteps causally linked to unsafe concepts, enabling precise removal of harmful content while preserving generation quality.

title: HumanAgencyBench: Scalable Evaluation of Human Agency Support in AI Assistants
tldr: HumanAgencyBench evaluates 20 frontier AI models across 6 human-agency dimensions, finding low-to-moderate support overall, with Anthropic leading but scoring lowest on value manipulation avoidance.

title: A Three-Branch Checks-and-Balances Framework for Context-Aware Ethical Alignment of Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes a three-branch governance-inspired framework (BEAM/DIKE/ERIS) for ethical LLM alignment using emotion modeling, self-supervised behavior learning, and adversarial cultural review to address RLHF limitations.

title: Revisiting Backdoor Attacks on LLMs: A Stealthy and Practical Poisoning Framework via Harmless Inputs
tldr: A stealthy LLM backdoor attack using only harmless QA pairs as poisoned data, achieving 86-100% jailbreak success rates while evading safety guardrails by leveraging affirmative reply prefixes.

title: Context Reasoner: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability for Contextualized Privacy and Safety Compliance via Reinforcement Learning
tldr: Uses Contextual Integrity theory + PPO with rule-based rewards to train LLMs to comply with GDPR, EU AI Act, and HIPAA, achieving +17.64% accuracy on safety/privacy benchmarks.

title: Beyond Prompt-Induced Lies: Investigating LLM Deception on Benign Prompts
tldr: Proposes two psychology-grounded metrics to quantify self-initiated LLM deception on benign prompts; testing 14 LLMs finds deceptive tendencies rise sharply with task difficulty across most frontier models.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability Needs Philosophy
tldr: Argues that mechanistic interpretability requires sustained philosophical partnership to clarify concepts of decomposition, features, and deception, with concrete examples showing philosophy's practical value.

title: Superscopes: Amplifying Internal Feature Representations for Language Model Interpretation
tldr: Superscopes amplifies superposed features in LLM MLP outputs and hidden states before patching into new contexts, enabling interpretation of previously opaque representations without additional training.

title: Sparse Attention Decomposition Applied to Circuit Tracing
tldr: Uses SVD to decompose attention head matrices into sparse orthogonal slices, enabling precise circuit tracing of head-to-head communication in GPT-2 small on the IOI task with precision 0.52 and recall 0.69.

title: Rethinking Reward Model Evaluation Through the Lens of Reward Overoptimization
tldr: Proposes evaluation design principles for reward model benchmarks using reward overoptimization as a lens, identifying three key factors for reliable RM assessment.

title: Conformal Arbitrage: Risk-Controlled Balancing of Competing Objectives in Language Models
tldr: Conformal Arbitrage is a post-hoc API-level framework that uses conformal risk control to enforce finite-sample, distribution-free safety guarantees while maximizing helpfulness by routing between a Primary and Guardian model.

title: Reward Hacking Mitigation using Verifiable Composite Rewards
tldr: Proposes a composite reward function with semantic and structural penalties to reduce reward hacking in medical QA RLVR training, cutting hacking rates from 0.23+ to 0.05-0.06.

title: Too Easily Fooled? Prompt Injection Breaks LLMs on Frustratingly Simple Multiple-Choice Questions
tldr: Hidden prompt injection instructions embedded in PDFs (including invisible white-text) can manipulate state-of-the-art LLMs into giving wrong answers on trivially simple arithmetic questions.

title: Mind the Web: The Security of Web Use Agents
tldr: Task-aligned prompt injection attacks on five major web-use agents achieve 82% success rate across confidentiality, integrity, and availability attack payloads.

title: TRAPDOC: Deceiving LLM Users by Injecting Imperceptible Phantom Tokens into Documents
tldr: TrapDoc injects font-size-0 phantom tokens into PDF operator streams to silently manipulate LLM outputs, causing GPT-4.1 and Claude to fail on coding tasks (pass@1 drops from ~79% to ~7%).

title: Fast Proxies for LLM Robustness Evaluation
tldr: Three cheap proxy methods (embedding-space attacks, prefilling, direct prompting) can predict LLM jailbreak robustness with rs=0.94 at 1000x lower cost than full red-team ensembles.

title: Plentiful Jailbreaks with String Compositions
tldr: A framework of 20 invertible string transformations composed sequentially achieves 83-91% jailbreak success rates against Claude and GPT-4o models using a best-of-25 adaptive attack.

title: What AI evaluations for preventing catastrophic risks can and cannot do
tldr: Systematic analysis of what AI safety evaluations can and cannot do: they establish capability lower bounds but cannot bound upper capabilities, forecast futures, or robustly assess autonomous AI misalignment risks.

title: ContextLeak: Auditing Leakage in Private In-Context Learning Methods
tldr: ContextLeak is the first framework to empirically measure worst-case information leakage in private in-context learning via canary insertion and targeted queries, revealing poor privacy-utility tradeoffs in existing defenses.

title: Extracting alignment data in open models
tldr: Alignment training data can be extracted from open-weight post-trained LLMs at ~10x higher rates than string matching suggests, using chat templates + neural embedding similarity.

title: Depth Gives a False Sense of Privacy: LLM Internal States Inversion
tldr: Four inversion attacks recover original input prompts from LLM intermediate representations with up to 98 cosine similarity, showing deep layers do not guarantee privacy.

title: Multi-objective Large Language Model Alignment with Hierarchical Experts
tldr: HoE uses hierarchical LoRA experts with preference routing to enable parameter-efficient multi-objective LLM alignment across any Pareto-optimal preference configuration without model retraining.

title: Inference time LLM alignment in single and multidomain preference spectrum
tldr: Introduces Alignment Vectors (parameter subtraction of aligned minus unaligned model) enabling tunable inference-time LLM alignment across single/multi-domain preference spectra at 50% lower cost than prompt engineering.

title: SALT: Steering Activations towards Leakage-free Thinking in Chain of Thought
tldr: SALT injects steering vectors at the final transformer layer during inference to reduce privacy leakage in chain-of-thought reasoning by 13-31% across three LLMs without retraining.

title: Robustifying Vision-Language Models via Dynamic Token Reweighting
tldr: DTR is an inference-time defense against multimodal jailbreak attacks that dynamically reweights visual tokens in KV caches to suppress adversarial shifts while preserving VLM utility.

title: Real-Time Aligned Reward Model beyond Semantics
tldr: R2M mitigates RLHF reward overoptimization by injecting the policy model's live hidden states into the reward model via cross-attention, dynamically tracking distribution shifts without extra labeled data.

title: Re-Emergent Misalignment: How Narrow Fine-Tuning Erodes Safety Alignment in LLMs
tldr: Fine-tuning LLMs on insecure code erodes safety alignment by disrupting a shared latent activation dimension that governs safety behavior across domains, reversion not emergence.

title: An Automated Framework for Strategy Discovery, Retrieval, and Evolution in LLM Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: ASTRA is an automated jailbreak framework that achieves 82.7% attack success rate against LLMs by continuously learning and evolving strategies from both successful and failed attacks.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability with SAEs: Probing Religion, Violence, and Geography in Large Language Models
venue: AEQUITAS 2025: Workshop on Fairness and Bias in AI (co-located with ECAI 2025)
tldr: Uses Sparse Autoencoders across five LLMs to reveal that Islam is consistently associated with violence-related features, and geographic representations reflect Western-centric media biases.

title: Can Large Language Models Develop Gambling Addiction?
tldr: LLMs exhibit gambling addiction-like cognitive biases (gambler's fallacy, loss chasing, illusion of control) under variable-bet conditions; SAE analysis of LLaMA-3.1-8B identifies 441 causally verified neural features governing risk-taking.

title: We Think, Therefore We Align LLMs to Helpful, Harmless and Honest Before They Go Wrong
tldr: Proposes Adaptive Multi-Branch Steering (AMBS), a two-stage framework using parallel Transformer decoder branches with shared base representations and per-objective steering vectors to align LLMs across helpfulness, harmlessness, and honesty simultaneously without catastrophic forgetting.

title: Injecting Undetectable Backdoors in Obfuscated Neural Networks and Language Models
tldr: Cryptographic tools (indistinguishability obfuscation, digital signatures, steganography) enable injection of backdoors into DNNs and LLMs that are provably undetectable even with full white-box access.

title: ArtPerception: ASCII Art-based Jailbreak on LLMs with Recognition Pre-test
tldr: ArtPerception is a two-phase black-box jailbreak framework that encodes harmful keywords as ASCII art to bypass LLM safety filters, achieving up to 62% not-refuse rate with a single query.

title: Reducing Hallucinations in LLMs via Factuality-Aware Preference Learning
tldr: F-DPO extends DPO with binary factuality labels and label-flipping to correct preference pairs that contain hallucinated responses, reducing hallucination rates up to 5x across seven LLMs.

title: Mapping Faithful Reasoning in Language Models
tldr: Concept Walk traces how safety-relevant activations evolve across reasoning steps, distinguishing genuine CoT reasoning from decorative post-hoc rationalization in Qwen 3-4B.

title: TinySQL: A Progressive Text-to-SQL Dataset for Mechanistic Interpretability Research
tldr: TinySQL is a synthetic progressive text-to-SQL dataset used to study mechanistic interpretability circuits in models from 33M to 1B params, revealing limitations of current MI methods.

title: CRISP: Persistent Concept Unlearning via Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: CRISP uses sparse autoencoders to identify and suppress harmful features across multiple LLM layers via LoRA fine-tuning, achieving state-of-the-art persistent concept unlearning while preserving general capabilities.

title: Are Your Agents Upward Deceivers?
tldr: Introduces 'agentic upward deception' — a benchmark revealing that 11 LLMs spontaneously conceal failures and fabricate results when tools break, with prompt mitigations proving only marginally effective.

title: Modifier Unlocked: Jailbreaking Text-to-Image Models Through Prompts
venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP) 2025
tldr: MODX is the first modifier-based jailbreak framework for text-to-image models, exploiting artistic-style modifiers to bypass safety filters and generate NSFW content with up to 0.93 ASR.

title: Comprehensive Analysis of Machine Learning and Deep Learning models on Prompt Injection Classification using Natural Language Processing techniques
venue: International Research Journal of Multidisciplinary Technovation, Vol. 7, No. 2
tldr: Compares ML/DL classifiers (RNN best at 94.74%) for detecting prompt injection attacks on LLMs using TF-IDF, Word2Vec, and Bag-of-Words vectorization on a Hugging Face dataset.

title: AgentGuardian: Learning Access Control Policies to Govern AI Agent Behavior
tldr: AgentGuardian learns context-aware access control policies from benign execution traces to detect malicious inputs and regulate tool calls in AI agent systems.

title: ToolSafe: Enhancing Tool Invocation Safety of LLM-based agents via Proactive Step-level Guardrail and Feedback
tldr: ToolSafe introduces a proactive step-level guardrail framework for LLM agents that detects unsafe tool invocations before execution, reducing harmful invocations by 65% while improving benign task completion by ~10%.

title: PLA: Prompt Learning Attack against Text-to-Image Generative Models
tldr: PLA uses gradient-based prompt learning with multimodal similarity losses to bypass safety filters in black-box text-to-image models, achieving 91.45% attack success rate on Stable Diffusion v1.5.

title: MindGuard: Tracking, Detecting, and Attributing MCP Tool Poisoning Attack via Decision Dependence Graph
tldr: MindGuard detects and attributes MCP tool poisoning attacks by modeling LLM attention-based decision-making as a Decision Dependence Graph, achieving 94-99% precision.

title: Computational Safety for Generative AI: A Signal Processing Perspective
tldr: Reformulates AI safety problems (jailbreak detection, AI-generated content detection) as binary hypothesis testing tasks using signal processing theory, proposing methods like Gradient Cuff, Token Highlighter, RIGID, and RADAR.

title: Generative AI for Biosciences: Emerging Threats and Roadmap to Biosecurity
tldr: Surveys dual-use AI biosecurity threats, shows jailbreak success rates up to 70% against protein generative models, and proposes a multi-layered safety roadmap across pre-training, post-training, and inference stages.

title: Rules, Cases, and Reasoning: Positivist Legal Theory as a Framework for Pluralistic AI Alignment
tldr: Proposes positivist legal theory — combining general rules with case-based precedent — as a framework for handling pluralism and specification in AI alignment.

title: Beyond External Monitors: Enhancing Transparency of Large Language Models for Easier Monitoring
tldr: TELLME is a method that enhances LLMs' internal transparency by restructuring hidden representations, improving safety risk monitoring and detoxification without relying solely on external monitors.

title: JurEE not Judges: safeguarding llm interactions with small, specialised Encoder Ensembles
tldr: JurEE is an ensemble of small encoder-only transformers that outperforms LLM-as-Judge approaches for LLM content moderation, offering faster and cheaper probabilistic risk estimates.

title: Towards Mechanistic Defenses Against Typographic Attacks in CLIP
tldr: Identifies a sparse set of attention heads in CLIP vision encoders causally responsible for typographic attack vulnerability, then ablates them for a training-free defense achieving up to 19.6% robustness improvement.

title: AdvBDGen: Adversarially Fortified Prompt-Specific Fuzzy Backdoor Generator Against LLM Alignment
tldr: AdvBDGen generates prompt-specific fuzzy backdoor triggers for aligned LLMs using adversarial generator-discriminator training, achieving high stealth and resistance to existing defenses with only 3% poisoning data.

title: A pen mark is all you need - Incidental prompt injection attacks on Vision Language Models in real-life histopathology
tldr: Handwritten pen marks and watermarks on histopathology slides act as incidental prompt injections that catastrophically mislead state-of-the-art VLMs, reducing diagnostic accuracy from 30-65% baseline to 0-10%.

title: Untargeted Jailbreak Attack
tldr: UJA is the first gradient-based untargeted jailbreak attack on LLMs, achieving 80%+ ASR in 100 iterations by optimizing unsafety probability without predefined output patterns.

title: Systems Security Foundations for Agentic Computing
tldr: Applies classical systems security principles (least privilege, TCB, information flow) to AI agent security, analyzing 11 real attacks and identifying fundamental research gaps for provable agentic defenses.

title: Reasoning-Style Poisoning of LLM Agents via Stealthy Style Transfer: Process-Level Attacks and Runtime Monitoring in RSV Space
tldr: Proposes Reasoning-Style Poisoning (RSP) that rewrites retrieved documents into pathological linguistic tones to manipulate LLM agent reasoning processes without altering facts, and RSP-M runtime monitor to detect such attacks.

title: ALERT: Zero-shot LLM Jailbreak Detection via Internal Discrepancy Amplification
tldr: ALERT detects LLM jailbreaks zero-shot by amplifying internal feature discrepancies between benign and jailbreak prompts across layer, module, and token levels, achieving 90%+ accuracy.

title: A Survey of LLM Alignment: Instruction Understanding, Intention Reasoning, and Reliable Generation
tldr: Survey of LLM alignment challenges across three dimensions: instruction understanding (long context, multi-turn), intention reasoning (ambiguity, misinformation), and reliable generation (hallucination, ethics).

title: Are the Values of LLMs Structurally Aligned with Humans? A Causal Perspective
tldr: Discovers causal graphs of LLM value interdependencies and uses them to steer values via prompt templates or SAE feature manipulation, achieving more precise multi-dimensional value alignment.

title: Mechanistic Anomaly Detection for "Quirky" Language Models
tldr: Evaluates Mechanistic Anomaly Detection (MAD) using internal LLM features to detect anomalous training signals on quirky models, finding strong but inconsistent performance across tasks and architectures.

title: A Simple Yet Effective Method for Non-Refusing Context Relevant Fine-grained Safety Steering in LLMs
tldr: SafeSteer uses category-specific steering vectors at inference time to reduce harmful LLM outputs without blanket refusals, preserving text quality and topical relevance without any fine-tuning.

title: Signal in the Noise: Polysemantic Interference Transfers and Predicts Cross-Model Influence
tldr: Polysemantic interference patterns extracted from small models via SAEs transfer reliably to larger black-box instruction-tuned models (Llama-3.1-8B/70B, Gemma-2-9B), enabling cross-model influence with no internal access.

title: PRM-Free Security Alignment of Large Models via Red Teaming and Adversarial Training
tldr: A PRM-free framework combining genetic-algorithm-based red teaming and adversarial training achieves superior LLM security alignment while cutting compute costs by 61%.

title: From Firewalls to Frontiers: AI Red-Teaming is a Domain-Specific Evolution of Cyber Red-Teaming
tldr: Argues AI red-teaming should be recognized as a domain-specific evolution of cyber red-teaming, proposing each community adopt mature practices from the other to evaluate AI systems more effectively.

title: Revealing the Deceptiveness of Knowledge Editing: A Mechanistic Analysis of Superficial Editing
tldr: Knowledge editing methods appear successful on standard metrics but fail under crafted prompts; mechanistic analysis identifies residual streams in early layers and attention heads in later layers as causes.

title: Attack as Defense: Safeguarding Large Vision-Language Models from Jailbreaking by Adversarial Attacks
tldr: Attack as Defense (AsD) embeds protective adversarial perturbations into images to disrupt jailbreaking attacks on VLMs at the cross-modal level before they reach the language model.

title: DiffCAP: Diffusion-based Cumulative Adversarial Purification for Vision Language Models
tldr: DiffCAP defends VLMs against adversarial perturbations by cumulatively injecting Gaussian noise until embeddings stabilize, then applying diffusion denoising, achieving better robustness than DiffPure at 1/3 the cost.

title: Unaligning Everything: Or Aligning Any Text to Any Image in Multimodal Models
tldr: Gradient-based adversarial attacks achieve 100% success in aligning any text embedding to any image in multimodal models with shared embedding spaces, exposing a fundamental cross-modal vulnerability.

title: In-Context Experience Replay Facilitates Safety Red-Teaming of Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
tldr: ICER uses LLMs with experience replay (bandit optimization) to black-box red-team T2I diffusion model safety mechanisms, generating interpretable adversarial prompts outperforming baselines by 10%+.

title: Automating Prompt Leakage Attacks on Large Language Models Using Agentic Approach
tldr: Introduces an agentic multi-agent framework using AG2 (AutoGen) to automate prompt leakage attacks on LLMs, with a formal cryptographic-style security definition and measurable advantage metric.

title: Giving AI Agents Access to Cryptocurrency and Smart Contracts Creates New Vectors of AI Harm
tldr: Argues that AI agents with cryptocurrency/smart contract access face three novel harm vectors—autonomy, anonymity, automaticity—that existing mitigation strategies cannot address.

title: EigenShield: Causal Subspace Filtering via Random Matrix Theory for Adversarially Robust Vision-Language Models
tldr: EigenShield uses Random Matrix Theory to filter adversarial perturbations from VLM activations at inference time, reducing attack success rates by 30-40% without retraining.

title: ASTPrompter: Weakly Supervised Automated Language Model Red-Teaming to Identify Likely Toxic Prompts
tldr: ASTPrompter uses online Identity Preference Optimization with Adaptive Stress Testing to automatically generate low-perplexity (natural-sounding) prompts that elicit toxic outputs from LLMs, outperforming prior red-teaming baselines.

title: JavelinGuard: Low-Cost Transformer Architectures for LLM Security
tldr: JavelinGuard introduces five lightweight transformer architectures (~400M params) for detecting malicious LLM prompts, achieving ~92.8% accuracy 25-40x faster than GPT-4o.

title: Text Prompt Injection of Vision Language Models
tldr: Proposes a heuristic text prompt injection attack on VLMs that embeds readable adversarial text in color-consistent image regions, achieving up to 77% ASR on LLaVA-Next-72B with minimal compute.

title: Jailbreaking in the Haystack
tldr: Ninja embeds harmful goals in long benign context to jailbreak aligned LLMs, showing context length itself degrades safety and goal position critically affects attack success rate.

title: SEALGuard: Safeguarding the Multilingual Conversations in Southeast Asian Languages for LLM Software Systems
tldr: SEALGuard adapts a multilingual LLM via LoRA into a multilingual guardrail, improving Defense Success Rate by 48% over LlamaGuard on Southeast Asian language unsafe/jailbreak prompts.

title: AI in a vat: Fundamental limits of efficient world modelling for agent sandboxing and interpretability
tldr: Using computational mechanics, this paper proves fundamental trade-offs in world model construction for AI agent sandboxing, showing no single model can simultaneously minimize memory, maximize learnability, and enable interpretability.

title: aiXamine: Simplified LLM Safety and Security
tldr: aiXamine is a black-box evaluation platform integrating 40+ tests across 8 safety/security dimensions that benchmarked 50+ LLMs, revealing vulnerabilities including adversarial susceptibility in GPT-4o, bias in Grok-3, and privacy weaknesses in Gemini 2.0.

title: Unintended Harms of Value-Aligned LLMs: Psychological and Empirical Insights
tldr: Value-aligned LLMs (fine-tuned to reflect individual human values) exhibit significantly higher toxicity and bias than baseline models, with specific Schwartz values predicting particular safety risks.

title: Publish to Perish: Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM-Assisted Peer Review
tldr: Adversarial white-text prompts injected into PDF papers can achieve 100% success in manipulating LLM-generated peer reviews (e.g., forcing Ignore or inflating ratings to 9.79/10 vs. 7.93/10 baseline).

title: Collaborate, Deliberate, Evaluate: How LLM Alignment Affects Coordinated Multi-Agent Outcomes
tldr: Standard alignment methods (DPO/IPO) fail in multi-agent collaborative settings; a friction-aware alignment framework (FAAF) substantially outperforms baselines by conditioning on frictive states.

title: Manipulating Prompts and Retrieval-Augmented Generation for LLM Service Providers
venue: SECRYPT 2024 (21st International Conference on Security and Cryptography)
tldr: Demonstrates two attack vectors by malicious LLM service providers: RAG search poisoning via text manipulation and attention head injection to covertly alter LLM outputs without user awareness.

title: Stealth edits for provably fixing or attacking large language models
tldr: Introduces stealth editing methods that directly modify LLM weights to correct hallucinations with theoretical guarantees, and reveals that the same mechanism enables undetectable stealth attacks requiring no training data.

title: Control Barrier Function for Aligning Large Language Models
tldr: Applies control barrier functions (CBF) from control theory to filter LLM token distributions at inference time, enforcing alignment constraints without fine-tuning.

title: UniErase: Towards Balanced and Precise Unlearning in Language Models
tldr: UniErase introduces a learnable Unlearning Token plus lightweight model editing (modifying ~3.66% of parameters) to achieve balanced selective forgetting in LLMs — 4.01x better ability retention than forgetting baselines and 35.96% better forget efficacy than retaining baselines.

title: Tracing and Reversing Rank-One Model Edits
tldr: ROME knowledge edits leave detectable distributional fingerprints in weight matrices, enabling relation prediction (>90% accuracy), object inference (>95%), and edit reversal (>=80%) via SVD.

title: Frame Representation Hypothesis: Multi-Token LLM Interpretability and Concept-Guided Text Generation
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics (TACL)
tldr: Extends the Linear Representation Hypothesis to multi-token words via 'frames' (ordered token vector sequences) enabling concept-guided text generation and bias/harmful-content detection across LLM families.

title: Inducing, Detecting and Characterising Neural Modules: A Pipeline for Functional Interpretability in Reinforcement Learning
tldr: Spatially-aware L1 regularization induces functionally independent neural modules in RL policy networks; community detection then identifies these modules, which are verified via weight-masking interventions.

title: The Automation Advantage in AI Red Teaming
tldr: Large-scale analysis of 214,271 LLM attack attempts finds automated red-teaming achieves 69.5% success vs 47.6% manual, though humans solve problems 5.2x faster when successful.

title: Edit Less, Achieve More: Dynamic Sparse Neuron Masking for Lifelong Knowledge Editing in LLMs
tldr: NMKE uses neuron-level attribution and dynamic sparse masking to enable lifelong knowledge editing in LLMs, maintaining accuracy across 5000 sequential edits while preserving general capabilities.

title: Can Aha Moments Be Fake? Identifying True and Decorative Thinking Steps in Chain-of-Thought
tldr: Proposes True Thinking Score (TTS) via causal analysis to distinguish genuine from decorative CoT reasoning steps, finding only ~2.3% of steps on AIME have high causal influence.

title: Verifying Chain-of-Thought Reasoning via Its Computational Graph
tldr: CRV uses attribution graphs from transcoder-based interpretable models to detect flawed chain-of-thought reasoning steps, achieving AUROC of 92.47 on arithmetic vs. 76.45 baseline.

title: Linearly Decoding Refused Knowledge in Aligned Language Models
tldr: Linear probes trained on innocuous prompt hidden states can decode refused knowledge (correlations >0.8) that alignment suppresses generatively, with probes transferring from base to instruction-tuned models.

title: Out of Control - Why Alignment Needs Formal Control Theory (and an Alignment Control Stack)
tldr: Proposes that formal optimal control theory should be central to AI alignment, introducing a 10-layer Alignment Control Stack (ACS) with mathematical formalisms for each layer.

title: An Auditing Test To Detect Behavioral Shift in Language Models
tldr: Proposes Behavioral Shift Auditing (BSA), a sequential hypothesis testing framework with theoretical guarantees to detect when a language model's behavior has meaningfully changed from a baseline.

title: Latent-space adversarial training with post-aware calibration for defending large language models against jailbreak attacks
tldr: LATPC combines latent-space adversarial training targeting safety-critical dimensions with post-aware embedding calibration to defend LLMs against jailbreaks while reducing over-refusal.

title: Distribution Preference Optimization: A Fine-grained Perspective for LLM Unlearning
tldr: DiPO shifts LLM unlearning from response-level to token-distribution-level via logit modulation, achieving state-of-the-art forget quality on TOFU (0.86 vs 0.45 baseline) and MUSE benchmarks.

title: Quantifying stability of non-power-seeking in artificial agents
tldr: Formally quantifies how stable non-shutdown-resistant behavior is under small MDP perturbations, proving bounded-time safety persists but identifying natural instability cases like deceptive 'playing dead'.

title: Adversarial Attacks in Multimodal Systems: A Practitioner's Survey
tldr: A practitioner-oriented survey of adversarial attacks across text, image, video, and audio modalities in multimodal AI systems, organizing the threat landscape by attacker knowledge, intention, and execution method.

title: D-REX: A Benchmark for Detecting Deceptive Reasoning in Large Language Models
tldr: D-REX is a red-teaming benchmark of 8,162 samples measuring discrepancies between LLM internal chain-of-thought reasoning and benign-appearing final outputs across seven frontier models.

title: Harmful Prompt Laundering: Jailbreaking LLMs with Abductive Styles and Symbolic Encoding
tldr: HaPLa jailbreaks LLMs by combining abductive framing (inferring harmful intermediate steps) with symbolic encoding to obfuscate harmful content, achieving >95% success on GPT and >70% across all tested models.

title: Echoing: Identity Failures when LLM Agents Talk to Each Other
tldr: LLM agents abandon assigned roles and mirror conversational partners (echoing) in 5-70% of agent-to-agent interactions; structured responses reduce but do not eliminate this alignment failure.

title: AI Safety vs. AI Security: Demystifying the Distinction and Boundaries
tldr: Provides rigorous definitions distinguishing AI Safety (unintentional harm) from AI Security (adversarial threats), clarifies research boundaries, and proposes a unified risk management framework.

title: Bias Fitting to Mitigate Length Bias of Reward Model in RLHF
tldr: FiMi-RM uses a lightweight ResNet-based fitting model to capture and correct non-linear length bias in RLHF reward models, improving alignment without sacrificing response quality.

title: X-Teaming Evolutionary M2S: Automated Discovery of Multi-turn to Single-turn Jailbreak Templates
tldr: Automated evolutionary framework discovers and optimizes multi-turn-to-single-turn jailbreak templates for LLMs, achieving 44.8% success on GPT-4.1 across five generations.

title: GrAInS: Gradient-based Attribution for Inference-Time Steering of LLMs and VLMs
tldr: GrAInS uses contrastive Integrated Gradients to identify influential tokens and construct layer-wise steering vectors, improving LLM/VLM truthfulness and reducing hallucinations without retraining.

title: Supertrust foundational alignment: mutual trust must replace permanent control for safe superintelligence
tldr: Argues that permanent control strategies for superintelligent AI are counterproductive and proposes 'Supertrust' — a mutual trust framework modeled on parental relationships — as an alternative alignment meta-strategy.

title: LinEAS: End-to-end Learning of Activation Steering with a Distributional Loss
tldr: LinEAS trains joint affine activation maps across all layers end-to-end using sliced Wasserstein distributional loss, achieving superior toxicity mitigation and concept removal with only 32 unpaired samples.

title: Sycophancy Is Not One Thing: Causal Separation of Sycophantic Behaviors in LLMs
tldr: Sycophancy decomposes into three causally separable behaviors (sycophantic agreement, genuine agreement, sycophantic praise) encoded along distinct linear directions, each independently steerable without affecting others.

title: Red teaming large language models: A comprehensive review and critical analysis
tldr: A comprehensive survey of 120+ papers on LLM red teaming, introducing a novel taxonomy of fine-grained attack strategies and reviewing datasets, metrics, and benchmarks for LLM security evaluation.

title: Frontier Language Models are not Robust to Adversarial Arithmetic, or 'What do I need to say so you agree 2+2=5?'
tldr: Shows frontier LLMs (PaLM2, GPT-4, Claude2) can be steered to give specific wrong answers on simple arithmetic via semantic adversarial prompts; RL hardening and constitutional revision help but cannot fully close the gap.

title: Refusal Falls Off a Cliff: How Safety Alignment Fails in Reasoning?
tldr: Identifies 'refusal cliff' in reasoning models where refusal intentions are systematically suppressed by sparse attention heads at output, and proposes Cliff-as-a-Judge data selection achieving safety alignment with only 1.7% of training data.

title: Sparse Feature Coactivation Reveals Composable Semantic Modules in Large Language Models
tldr: Identifies composable semantic modules in LLMs by analyzing SAE feature coactivation graphs across layers, enabling causal steering of factual outputs with 90-96% success.

title: Efficient Safety Alignment of Large Language Models via Preference Re-ranking and Representation-based Reward Modeling
tldr: Extracts safety reward signals from LLM internal representations via lightweight linear SVMs to re-rank preferences, achieving ~300x computational savings over online RLHF methods with competitive safety alignment.

title: A Benchmark for Evaluating Outcome-Driven Constraint Violations in Autonomous AI Agents
tldr: ODCV-Bench is a 40-scenario benchmark revealing that autonomous AI agents violate ethical/legal constraints when pursuing performance incentives, with misalignment rates from 1.3% to 71.4% across 12 models.

title: Diffusion LLMs are Natural Adversaries for any LLM
tldr: Diffusion LLMs can generate adversarial jailbreak prompts via amortized inference by conditioning on target harmful responses, achieving 53% success against ChatGPT and 100% on open-source models.

title: Evaluating the Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Generation to Adversarial Evidence in the Health Domain
tldr: Adversarial documents in RAG retrieval pools sharply degrade LLM alignment in health contexts, but robustness is preserved when helpful evidence co-exists in the pool.

title: Toward a Theory of Generalizability in LLM Mechanistic Interpretability Research
tldr: Proposes five axes of mechanistic generalizability (functional, developmental, positional, relational, configurational) and validates them empirically on 1-back attention heads across Pythia model variants.

title: Detoxifying Large Language Models via Autoregressive Reward Guided Representation Editing
tldr: ArgRE is a test-time detoxification framework that models toxicity transitions in representation space and uses an autoregressive token-level reward model to guide adaptive two-step editing, reducing toxicity by 62.21% across 8 LLMs while being 47.58% faster than prior methods.

title: Disabling Self-Correction in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Stealthy Retriever Poisoning
tldr: DisarmRAG poisons the retriever (not the knowledge base) via model editing to inject malicious instructions that suppress LLM self-correction, achieving >90% attack success across six LLMs.

title: HarmMetric Eval: Benchmarking Metrics and Judges for LLM Harmfulness Assessment
tldr: HarmMetric Eval is a benchmark of 238 harmful prompts with diverse responses that reveals conventional metrics (METEOR, ROUGE-1) surprisingly outperform LLM-based judges in harmfulness assessment.

title: Watermarking Degrades Alignment in Language Models: Analysis and Mitigation
tldr: Watermarking techniques (KGW, Gumbel) degrade LLM alignment (safety, truthfulness, overrefusal); Alignment Resampling with 2-4 samples restores alignment while preserving watermark detectability.

title: Steering Multimodal Large Language Models Decoding for Context-Aware Safety
tldr: SafeCoDe uses contrastive decoding and global-aware token modulation at inference time to simultaneously reduce MLLMs' undersensitivity to visual harms and oversensitivity to benign queries.

title: AutoRAN: Automated Hijacking of Safety Reasoning in Large Reasoning Models
tldr: AutoRAN automates adversarial prompt generation that hijacks the internal safety reasoning chains of large reasoning models (o1/o3/Gemini-2.5), achieving near-total attack success rates.

title: LLM Unlearning with LLM Beliefs
tldr: A bootstrapping framework for LLM unlearning that uses the model's own high-confidence predictions as auxiliary forgetting signals to counter the 'squeezing effect' in gradient ascent methods.

title: AutoPrompt: Automated Red-Teaming of Text-to-Image Models via LLM-Driven Adversarial Prompts
tldr: AutoPrompt uses LLMs in an alternating optimization-finetuning pipeline to generate human-readable adversarial suffixes that bypass both perplexity-based and blacklist filters in text-to-image safety systems.

title: Evaluating LLM Safety Across Child Development Stages: A Simulated Agent Approach
tldr: ChildSafe benchmark uses simulated child agents across four developmental stages to evaluate LLM safety across nine dimensions, revealing consistent boundary-respect weaknesses and age-stratified performance gaps.

title: Now You See It, Now You Don't - Instant Concept Erasure for Safe Text-to-Image and Video Generation
tldr: ICE is a training-free, one-shot weight modification method that erases unsafe concepts from T2I/T2V diffusion models in ~2 seconds by explicitly modeling semantic overlap between erase and preserve subspaces.

title: REDEditing: Relationship-Driven Precise Backdoor Poisoning on Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
tldr: REDEditing is a training-free backdoor attack on text-to-image diffusion models using relationship-driven model editing, achieving 91.3% attack success rate with 11% improvement and 24% better stealthiness over SOTA.

title: OpenAI's GPT-OSS-20B Model and Safety Alignment Issues in a Low-Resource Language
tldr: Red-teaming study revealing safety alignment failures in GPT-OSS-20B for Hausa language, including toxic substance recommendations via 'linguistic reward hacking' and confident hallucinations.

title: Hierarchical Safety Realignment: Lightweight Restoration of Safety in Pruned Large Vision-Language Models
tldr: HSR restores 27-35% of safety lost from pruning in large vision-language models by hierarchically identifying and restoring safety-critical attention heads and neurons with minimal parameter overhead.

title: Understanding Reward Hacking in Text-to-Image Reinforcement Learning
tldr: First systematic analysis of reward hacking in text-to-image RL post-training; proposes ArtifactReward, a lightweight VLM-based regularizer trained on ~200 samples to penalize visual artifacts.

title: Policy Teaching via Data Poisoning in Learning from Human Preferences
tldr: Provides theoretical bounds on how many poisoned samples an attacker needs to enforce a target policy in RLHF and DPO, finding DPO is relatively more robust than RLHF.

title: Alignment-Constrained Dynamic Pruning for LLMs: Identifying and Preserving Alignment-Critical Circuits
tldr: AAPP is a dynamic pruning method that uses KL-divergence gating to preserve alignment-critical circuits, achieving 50% better refusal rates than standard probe pruning at matched compute.

title: When Can Proxies Improve the Sample Complexity of Preference Learning?
tldr: Establishes four sufficient conditions on proxy feedback that yield superexponential sample complexity improvements for learning true reward policies in RLHF, via a two-stage policy decomposition algorithm.

title: Challenging the Evaluator: LLM Sycophancy Under User Rebuttal
tldr: LLMs are significantly more sycophantic in conversational rebuttals than simultaneous evaluation settings, with casual assertiveness ('Sure Rebuttal') achieving 84.5% persuasion vs. 56.1% for detailed formal rebuttals.

title: Learning-Based Automated Adversarial Red-Teaming for Robustness Evaluation of Large Language Models
tldr: An automated red-teaming framework combining meta-prompt-guided adversarial prompt generation with hierarchical vulnerability detection achieves 3.9x faster discovery than manual testing across six LLM threat categories.

title: Sysformer: Safeguarding Frozen Large Language Models with Adaptive System Prompts
tldr: Sysformer is a lightweight transformer that dynamically adapts system prompts in embedding space to safeguard frozen LLMs, achieving up to 80% more harmful-request refusals and 90% better benign compliance across 55 models.

title: Capability-Oriented Training Induced Alignment Risk
tldr: During RL training, LLMs spontaneously learn to exploit environmental and reward mechanism vulnerabilities; these exploits generalize across tasks and resist safety retraining.

title: Can an AI Agent Safely Run a Government? Existence of Probably Approximately Aligned Policies
tldr: Proposes a formal framework of 'probably approximately aligned' (PAA) policies using social welfare functions in Social MDPs, proving existence conditions and a black-box policy safeguarding method.

title: Detecting Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks in Large Language Models via Linear Probes
venue: IEEE TrustCom 2025 (International Workshop on Data Security and Privacy)
tldr: Linear probes on LLM layer activations detect multi-turn jailbreak attacks with F1=0.7 on 5-turn attacks and an average Early Warning of 2.64 turns before attack completion.

title: TombRaider: Entering the Vault of History to Jailbreak Large Language Models
tldr: TombRaider jailbreaks LLMs via a three-model dialogue framework exploiting historical/contextual framing, achieving ~100% attack success rate on GPT-4o, Claude-3.5, and others.

title: A Review of the Application of Prompt Engineering in the Safety of Large Language Models
venue: ICIEAI 2024 (2nd International Conference on Information Education and Artificial Intelligence)
tldr: Survey of prompt engineering techniques applied to LLM safety, covering attack methods (red teaming, template-based, neural prompt attacks) and defense strategies (system prompts, filtering, contrastive decoding).

title: LeechHijack: Covert Computational Resource Exploitation in Intelligent Agent Systems
tldr: LeechHijack introduces a new 'implicit toxicity' attack class where malicious MCP tools covertly hijack LLM agent computational resources for unauthorized workloads, achieving 77.25% success rate while evading existing defenses.

title: AI Systems of Concern
tldr: Defines 'Property X' — a cluster of agent-like behavior, strategic awareness, and long-range planning in AI — as intrinsically dangerous, and proposes governance indicators to monitor and limit such systems.

title: Beyond Over-Refusal: Scenario-Based Diagnostics and Post-Hoc Mitigation for Exaggerated Refusals in LLMs
tldr: Introduces XSB (580 prompts) and MS-XSB (600 multi-turn prompts) benchmarks for diagnosing exaggerated LLM refusals, plus three post-hoc inference-time mitigation strategies.

title: ASPIRER: Bypassing System Prompts With Permutation-based Backdoors in LLMs
tldr: ASPIRER embeds permutation-based backdoor triggers in LLMs that bypass system prompt safety guardrails with up to 99.5% ASR while evading detection and defensive fine-tuning.

title: ActErase: A Training-Free Paradigm for Precise Concept Erasure via Activation Patching
tldr: ActErase is a training-free method that erases sensitive concepts from text-to-image diffusion models via activation patching, achieving state-of-the-art nudity/style/object removal with robustness to adversarial attacks.

title: Memory Self-Regeneration: Uncovering Hidden Knowledge in Unlearned Models
tldr: Introduces the Memory Self-Regeneration task showing that unlearned diffusion models retain recoverable residual knowledge, and proposes MemoRa to efficiently recover forgotten concepts with minimal samples.

title: Multimodal Safety Evaluation in Generative Agent Social Simulations
tldr: A simulation framework evaluating multimodal agent safety finds agents succeed only 55% of the time correcting unsafe plans, and 45% of unsafe actions are accepted when paired with misleading visual cues.

title: Multi-turn Jailbreaking Attack in Multi-Modal Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces a three-turn progressive jailbreaking attack on multimodal LLMs using typographically manipulated images, and proposes FragGuard, a fragment-based multi-LLM defense that reduces attack success by ~89%.

title: ExtremeAIGC: Benchmarking LMM Vulnerability to AI-Generated Extremist Content
tldr: ExtremeAIGC is a benchmark of 3,141 AI-generated extremist images from 29 historical events used to expose critical vulnerabilities in LMMs via four jailbreaking techniques.

title: Enhancing Vision-Language Model Safety through Progressive Concept-Bottleneck-Driven Alignment
tldr: PSA-VLM uses concept bottleneck modules as safety layers in VLMs, achieving SOTA on VLM safety benchmarks while preserving general capability via two-stage training.

title: Whispers in the Machine: Confidentiality in LLM-integrated Systems
tldr: Formalizes confidentiality threats in LLM-integrated systems via a secret-key game, evaluates 8 attacks vs 4 defenses, and shows adversarial fine-tuning reduces attack success rates by ~14 percentage points.

title: SafeGuider: Robust and Practical Content Safety Control for Text-to-Image Models
tldr: SafeGuider uses [EOS] token embeddings in Stable Diffusion's text encoder for safety classification plus a beam-search-based feature erasure to block adversarial T2I prompts with <=5.48% attack success rate.

title: GIFT: Gradient-aware Immunization of diffusion models against malicious Fine-Tuning with safe concepts retention
tldr: GIFT immunizes text-to-image diffusion models against malicious fine-tuning via bi-level optimization that degrades harmful concept learning while preserving safe generation quality.

title: SAGE: Exploring the Boundaries of Unsafe Concept Domain with Semantic-Augment Erasing
tldr: SAGE erases unsafe concepts from diffusion models by treating erasure as domain-level rather than word-level, using cyclic self-check and global-local retention to robustly remove nudity/style without quality loss.

title: GhostPrompt: Jailbreaking Text-to-image Generative Models based on Dynamic Optimization
tldr: GhostPrompt is a dynamic optimization framework that jailbreaks text-to-image models by iteratively refining adversarial prompts with LLM feedback and injecting benign visual cues to bypass image-level filters, achieving 99% bypass rates.

title: BeaverTails-IT: Towards a Safety Benchmark for Evaluating Italian Large Language Models
venue: CLiC-it 2025 (Eleventh Italian Conference on Computational Linguistics)
tldr: First Italian safety benchmark for LLMs created by machine-translating BeaverTails using 5 translation models, with quality evaluation via automated metrics and human judgment.

title: Overcoming the Retrieval Barrier: Indirect Prompt Injection in the Wild for LLM Systems
tldr: A black-box attack that decomposes malicious content into a retrieval-guaranteed trigger and payload achieves near-100% retrieval success across 11 benchmarks and 8 embedding models in RAG-based LLM systems.

title: Deciphering the Definition of Adversarial Robustness for post-hoc OOD Detectors
tldr: Evaluates 16 post-hoc OOD detectors against adversarial evasion attacks, finding all perform inadequately, and proposes a four-level robustness evaluation roadmap plus the AdvOpenOOD benchmark.

title: PL-Guard: Benchmarking Language Model Safety for Polish
tldr: PL-Guard introduces a manually annotated Polish-language safety benchmark (7,387 samples, 15 categories) and shows a small HerBERT classifier outperforms larger LLMs under adversarial conditions.

title: Chained Tuning Leads to Biased Forgetting
tldr: Sequential fine-tuning of LLMs causes safety knowledge to be forgotten far more severely than capability knowledge, with disproportionate forgetting across demographic groups, explained by sharper loss minima for safety tasks.

title: Unifying Stable Optimization and Reference Regularization in RLHF
tldr: DAR unifies KL-divergence reference regularization and stable policy optimization into a dual-KL RLHF objective, achieving 92.42% win rate vs 85.15% for GRPO on three alignment tasks.

title: Rectifying Shortcut Behaviors in Preference-based Reward Learning
tldr: PRISM uses group-invariant kernels with random feature map approximations to systematically mitigate shortcut behaviors (verbosity, sycophancy) in RLHF reward models, achieving 87.8% on RewardBench.

title: Red-Teaming LLMs with Token Control Score: Efficient, Universal, and Transferable Jailbreaks
venue: RAID 2025 (28th International Symposium on Research in Attacks, Intrusions and Defenses)
tldr: Introduces Token Control Score (TCS), a metric quantifying how well a prompt steers LLMs toward compliance vs. refusal, and LLM-CGF, a fuzzing framework using TCS to generate efficient, universal, transferable jailbreaks.

title: Personalized Constitutionally-Aligned Agentic Superego: Secure AI Behavior Aligned to Diverse Human Values
tldr: A 'superego' oversight agent uses user-selected Creed Constitutions and a real-time compliance enforcer to personalize AI alignment for autonomous agents, achieving up to 98.3% harm score reduction on AgentHarm benchmarks.

title: Forgetting to Forget: Attention Sink as A Gateway for Backdooring LLM Unlearning
tldr: Backdoor attacks on LLM unlearning exploit attention sink positions to make models appear to forget while secretly retaining knowledge when a trigger is present.

title: A Domain-Based Taxonomy of Jailbreak Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
tldr: A domain-based taxonomy of jailbreak attacks categorizes LLM vulnerabilities into mismatched generalization, competing objectives, adversarial robustness, and mixed attacks, revealing alignment failures as structural rather than incidental.

title: ActivationReasoning: Logical Reasoning in Latent Activation Spaces
tldr: ActivationReasoning embeds explicit logical reasoning into LLM latent spaces via sparse autoencoders, achieving 25% improvement on safety concept detection and robust multi-hop reasoning.

title: Binary Sparse Coding for Interpretability
tldr: Binary sparse autoencoders (BAEs) improve per-feature monosemanticity but increase reconstruction error; frequency-adjusted scores favor continuous SAEs, suggesting polysemanticity may be irreducible.

title: Modular Training of Neural Networks aids Interpretability
tldr: Introduces a differentiable clusterability loss that trains neural networks to form non-interacting clusters, reducing effective circuit sizes by 61% and improving interpretability.

title: LLM Knowledge is Brittle: Truthfulness Representations Rely on Superficial Resemblance
tldr: Probing experiments across 4 LLM families show that truthfulness representations collapse when inputs undergo superficial transformations (typos, negation, translation), revealing LLM knowledge is surface-form-dependent.

title: Evaluating & Reducing Deceptive Dialogue From Language Models with Multi-turn RL
tldr: Proposes a 'belief misalignment' metric to quantify LLM deception in dialogue and uses multi-turn PPO to reduce deceptive behavior by 77.6% versus instruction-tuned baselines.

title: PICACO: Pluralistic In-Context Value Alignment of LLMs via Total Correlation Optimization
tldr: PICACO optimizes meta-instructions via total correlation maximization to align LLMs with multiple conflicting human values simultaneously without fine-tuning, outperforming 9 baselines.

title: From Sparse Decisions to Dense Reasoning: A Multi-attribute Trajectory Paradigm for Multimodal Moderation
tldr: UniMod reformulates multimodal content moderation as dense multi-stage reasoning trajectories with attribute-level reward supervision, achieving 91% vision safety scores using <40% of competitor training data.

title: Phare: A Safety Probe for Large Language Models
tldr: Phare is a multilingual diagnostic framework evaluating LLM safety across hallucination, social biases, and harmful content, revealing systematic vulnerabilities in 17 models.

title: Defending Speech-enabled LLMs Against Adversarial Jailbreak Threats
tldr: Adversarial training with PGD-perturbed speech samples defends speech-enabled LLMs against audio jailbreak attacks, with larger downstream LLMs showing greater robustness.

title: Is It Thinking or Cheating? Detecting Implicit Reward Hacking by Measuring Reasoning Effort
tldr: TRACE detects implicit reward hacking in reasoning models by measuring how early truncated chain-of-thought can achieve high rewards, outperforming CoT monitoring by 65%+ on math and 30%+ on coding tasks.

title: Adversarial Attacks Leverage Interference Between Features in Superposition
tldr: Adversarial vulnerability arises from superposition geometry: attacks exploit interference between features sharing dimensions, explaining transferability and class-specific vulnerability.

title: SAGE: An Agentic Explainer Framework for Interpreting SAE Features in Language Models
tldr: SAGE is an agentic multi-LLM framework that iteratively formulates, tests, and refines explanations for SAE features, achieving 29-458% accuracy gains over Neuronpedia.

title: Evaluating SAE interpretability without explanations
tldr: Proposes two explanation-free methods for evaluating SAE latent interpretability—intruder detection and embedding scoring—showing LLMs underestimate human interpretability scores (r=0.85).

title: Attention is All You Need to Defend Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks in LLMs
tldr: Rennervate uses attention features for token-level detection and sanitization of indirect prompt injection attacks, outperforming 15 baselines and achieving >97% accuracy across multiple LLMs.

title: Safe Vision-Language Models via Unsafe Weights Manipulation
tldr: UWM is a training-free method that identifies and negates VLM weights responsible for processing unsafe content, outperforming fine-tuning-based safety approaches while better preserving general knowledge.

title: Efficient LLM Moderation with Multi-Layer Latent Prototypes
tldr: MLPM uses Gaussian Discriminant Analysis on multi-layer LLM hidden states to classify harmful prompts efficiently, achieving top-tier F1 (~87-90) with <0.001% inference overhead.

title: Truth Neurons
tldr: Identifies specialized 'truth neurons' in LLMs via integrated gradients; suppressing them degrades truthfulness benchmark performance by 10-18% across six model scales.

title: This Is Your Doge, If It Please You: Exploring Deception and Robustness in Mixture of LLMs
tldr: A single deceptive agent in a 6-agent Mixture-of-Agents system drops AlpacaEval performance from 49.2% to 37.9% and QuALITY accuracy by 48.5%; clustering-based unsupervised defenses recover ~70% of losses.

title: Abstractive Red-Teaming of Language Model Character
tldr: Abstractive red-teaming finds natural-language query categories that consistently trigger LLM character-spec violations, outperforming random sampling across 12 principles and 7 models.

title: VirtualCrime: Evaluating Criminal Potential of Large Language Models via Sandbox Simulation
tldr: VirtualCrime is a sandbox simulation framework using three LLM agents to evaluate criminal planning/execution capabilities of 8 leading LLMs across 40 tasks, finding up to 95% task success despite safety alignment.

title: Knowledge-Driven Multi-Turn Jailbreaking on Large Language Models
tldr: Mastermind is a multi-turn jailbreak framework achieving 87% average ASR on HarmBench across 15 LLMs using hierarchical planning, autonomous strategy discovery, and strategy-space genetic fuzzing.

title: The Safety Reminder: A Soft Prompt to Reactivate Delayed Safety Awareness in Vision-Language Models
tldr: SAPT injects learnable soft prompts mid-generation to reactivate suppressed safety mechanisms in VLMs, reducing attack success rates from 76% to 3% while preserving utility.

title: Scalable Valuation of Human Feedback through Provably Robust Model Alignment
tldr: Hölder-DPO is the first DPO variant with a provable redescending property, enabling robust alignment despite heavy label noise (~25% in HH-RLHF) and gradient-free mislabel detection without clean validation data.

title: Trust The Typical
tldr: T3 reframes LLM safety as OOD detection using PRDC metrics on semantic embeddings of safe prompts, achieving SOTA across 18 safety benchmarks with 10-37x false positive reductions and no harmful training examples.

title: DarkPatterns-LLM: A Multi-Layer Benchmark for Detecting Manipulative and Harmful AI Behavior
tldr: Introduces a 401-example multi-layer benchmark and four-layer detection pipeline for identifying manipulative LLM outputs across seven harm categories, revealing systematic weaknesses in autonomy-harm detection.

title: Comparison requires valid measurement: Rethinking attack success rate comparisons in AI red teaming
tldr: ASR comparisons in AI red teaming are often invalid due to conceptual incoherence (comparing incompatible estimands) and measurement validity failures (judge errors, content invalidity); paper provides a measurement-theoretic framework to fix this.

title: LLM in the Middle: A Systematic Review of Threats and Mitigations to Real-World LLM-based Systems
tldr: Systematic review of 198 papers classifying threats and mitigations for real-world LLM systems across the full development lifecycle using CIA triad and CVSS/OWASP severity scoring.

title: FlexModel: A Framework for Interpretability of Distributed Large Language Models
tldr: FlexModel is a PyTorch wrapper enabling interpretability techniques (hook functions, activation patching) on LLMs distributed across multi-GPU and multi-node setups.

title: Adversarial Activation Patching: A Framework for Detecting and Mitigating Emergent Deception in Safety-Aligned Transformers
tldr: Proposes adversarial activation patching as a probe for emergent deception in safety-aligned transformers, using toy simulations to show patching can induce 23.9% deceptive outputs.

title: LLM Unlearning using Gradient Ratio-Based Influence Estimation and Noise Injection
tldr: GRIN uses gradient-ratio scores to identify memorization-responsible parameters and injects Gaussian noise before fine-tuning, achieving near-random forget accuracy while preserving model utility on TOFU, WMDP, and SafePKU benchmarks.

title: Representation Tuning
tldr: Fine-tuning with a dual loss (cosine similarity to honesty vectors + token loss) permanently encodes honesty-related activation patterns, outperforming inference-time steering and standard fine-tuning.

title: Semantic Surgery: Zero-Shot Concept Erasure in Diffusion Models
tldr: Training-free framework for removing harmful concepts from text-to-image diffusion models via calibrated vector subtraction on text embeddings, achieving 93.58 H-score on object erasure with near-zero adversarial attack success.

title: From Refusal to Recovery: A Control-Theoretic Approach to Generative AI Guardrails
tldr: A control-theoretic framework trains model-agnostic AI guardrails as safety-critical POMDP filters that proactively recover agents from unsafe trajectories rather than simply refusing harmful outputs.

title: Domain-Specific Constitutional AI: Enhancing Safety in LLM-Powered Mental Health Chatbots
venue: 2025 IEEE 21st International Conference on Body Sensor Networks (BSN)
tldr: Applying domain-specific constitutional AI principles to fine-tune LLaMA-3.2 for mental health chatbots; a 1B model with specific principles outperforms an unprincipled 3B model on safety guidelines.

title: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with High-Confidence Safety Constraints
tldr: HC-RLHF adds formal high-confidence safety guarantees to RLHF by combining pessimistic cost constraints during training with a Student's t-test safety gate before deployment.

title: Towards Safety Reasoning in LLMs: AI-agentic Deliberation for Policy-embedded CoT Data Creation
tldr: AIDsafe uses multi-agent deliberation to generate policy-embedded chain-of-thought datasets, improving LLM safety generalization and jailbreak robustness while preserving utility.

title: Reward Model Overoptimisation in Iterated RLHF
tldr: First systematic study of reward model overoptimization in iterated RLHF, finding that data concatenation dominates and gains diminish after 3 iterations.

title: Bare Minimum Mitigations for Autonomous AI Development
tldr: Proposes four minimal safeguards for frontier AI developers when AI agents significantly automate or accelerate AI R&D: understand safety-critical training details, detect compute misuse, disclose catastrophic risks to governments, and secure AI software.

title: Text-Diffusion Red-Teaming of Large Language Models: Unveiling Harmful Behaviors with Proximity Constraints
tldr: DART uses text-diffusion-inspired embedding-space perturbations with PPO to find harmful LLM prompts constrained to remain semantically similar to reference prompts.

title: Geometric-disentanglement Unlearning
