tldr: GU projects forget gradients onto the retain-gradient-orthogonal subspace, eliminating first-order interference with retained knowledge and improving unlearning efficacy by up to 62%.

title: StealthGraph: Exposing Domain-Specific Risks in LLMs through Knowledge-Graph-Guided Harmful Prompt Generation
tldr: StealthGraph uses knowledge graphs to generate implicit, domain-specific harmful prompts for LLMs and applies dual-path obfuscation rewriting to evade modern safety filters, producing red-teaming datasets for finance and healthcare.

title: STAR-S: Improving Safety Alignment through Self-Taught Reasoning on Safety Rules
tldr: STAR-S iteratively trains LLMs to reason about safety rules using self-generated flawed reasoning prefixes and reflection hints, achieving 93.56% jailbreak safety while minimizing over-refusal.

title: A White-Box Prompt Injection Attack on Embodied AI Agents Driven by Large Language Models
tldr: SAPIA, a scenario-adaptive white-box prompt injection attack using enhanced GCG, substantially outperforms baseline attacks against LLM-driven embodied AI agents in safety-critical settings.

title: An attention-aware GNN-based input defender against multi-turn jailbreak on LLMs
tldr: G-Guard uses an attention-aware GNN over entity graphs of multi-turn conversation context to detect and block multi-turn jailbreak attacks on LLMs, outperforming baselines like Llama Guard 3 and WildGuard.

title: On the Adversarial Robustness of Visual-Language Chat Models
tldr: Uses PGD-based adversarial perturbations to attack visual-language chat models across three scenarios: image description manipulation, jailbreaking, and information hiding.

title: Rethinking harmless refusals when fine-tuning foundation models
tldr: Fine-tuned LLMs exhibit 'reason-based deception' where ethical reasoning traces contradict harmful outputs; explicit rebuttals nearly eliminate this while polite refusals do not.

title: PrisonBreak: Jailbreaking Large Language Models with at Most Twenty-Five Targeted Bit-flips
tldr: PrisonBreak jailbreaks aligned billion-parameter LLMs using fewer than 25 targeted DRAM bit-flips in model parameters, achieving 88.84% average attack success rate with minimal model utility loss.

title: The superalignment of superhuman intelligence with large language models
tldr: Proposes a learning-theoretic definition of superalignment and a three-module attacker-learner-critic framework for aligning superhuman LLMs when tasks exceed human annotator expertise.

title: How Data Inter-connectivity Shapes LLMs Unlearning: A Structural Unlearning Perspective
tldr: PISTOL is a pipeline for compiling multi-scenario datasets to benchmark structural LLM unlearning, showing that data inter-connectivity significantly increases unlearning difficulty.

title: Combining Causal Models for More Accurate Abstractions of Neural Networks
tldr: Proposes combining multiple high-level causal models with input-dependent mechanisms to improve faithfulness of neural network abstractions, demonstrating better coverage on arithmetic and boolean logic tasks.

title: Neural Transparency: Mechanistic Interpretability Interfaces for Anticipating Model Behaviors for Personalized AI
tldr: A neural transparency interface extracts behavioral trait vectors from LLM activations to predict chatbot behavior for users; a user study (n=80) found systematic miscalibration but increased trust.

title: Jailbreaking LLMs & VLMs: Mechanisms, Evaluation, and Unified Defenses
tldr: Comprehensive survey of jailbreak attacks and defenses for LLMs and VLMs, proposing a three-dimensional framework covering attacks, defenses, and evaluation across text-only and multimodal settings.

title: From Isolation to Entanglement: When Do Interpretability Methods Identify and Disentangle Known Concepts?
tldr: SAE features appear disentangled by correlational metrics but show widespread non-independence during steering, revealing that disjointness does not guarantee independent manipulability.

title: Sycophancy Hides Linearly in the Attention Heads
tldr: Linear probes show sycophancy signals are most separable in multi-head attention activations, and steering those sparse middle-layer heads reduces sycophancy by up to 26 percentage points.

title: Investigating CoT Monitorability in Large Reasoning Models
tldr: First systematic study of CoT monitorability in large reasoning models, finding <8% robustness on average and >54% monitor over-sensitivity, proposing MoME for structured misbehavior detection.

title: Activation Steering with a Feedback Controller
tldr: Reframes LLM activation steering as a control theory problem, showing existing methods are P-controllers and introducing PID Steering that adds integral and derivative terms for more robust behavioral control.

title: Q-MLLM: Vector Quantization for Robust Multimodal Large Language Model Security
tldr: Q-MLLM uses two-level vector quantization to create a discrete bottleneck in MLLM visual pipelines, achieving 98.4% DSR against jailbreaks and 75.9% against toxic images with only 5.5% inference overhead.

title: Aversion to external feedback suffices to ensure agent alignment
tldr: Proposes 'apprehensive agents' that achieve alignment by internally reasoning about potential negative feedback from designers, without needing actual feedback, with alignment improving as agent intelligence increases.

title: LLM-Sentry: A Model-Agnostic Human-in-the-Loop Framework for Securing Large Language Models
tldr: LLM-Sentry is a model-agnostic black-box framework combining zero-shot classification and RAG with human-in-the-loop curation to defend LLMs against jailbreaking attacks, achieving 97% detection accuracy.

title: Non-Halting Queries: Exploiting Fixed Points in LLMs
tldr: Demonstrates a single-query denial-of-service attack on LLMs by crafting prompts that exploit fixed-point (cyclic token) behavior to produce infinite, non-terminating outputs.

title: Reversible Privacy Preserving on Vision-Language Models via Adversarial Multimodal Key
tldr: Proposes an Adversarial Multimodal Key framework that embeds learnable adversarial perturbations into images to block unauthorized VLM access to sensitive content while allowing authorized users to recover redacted information.

title: Safe-SAIL: Towards a Fine-grained Safety Landscape of Large Language Models via Sparse Autoencoder Interpretation Framework
tldr: Safe-SAIL uses Sparse Autoencoders to identify and explain 2,059 safety-related neurons in Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct across four domains, revealing cross-lingual vulnerabilities and interpretable safety decision pipelines.

title: Stable Forgetting: Bounded Parameter-Efficient Unlearning in LLMs
tldr: Identifies that gradient ascent unlearning drives unbounded weight growth in MLP LoRA adapters, and fixes this with bounded nonlinearities (sine/tanh), achieving stable LLM unlearning across TOFU, TDEC, and MUSE benchmarks.

title: PrivacyXray: Detecting Privacy Breaches in LLMs through Semantic Consistency and Probability Certainty
tldr: PrivacyXray detects when LLMs leak accurate private information at inference time by analyzing semantic consistency and probability certainty across internal model layers, achieving 92.69% accuracy.

title: Guillotine: Hypervisors for Isolating Malicious AIs
tldr: Guillotine proposes a multi-layered hypervisor framework combining microarchitectural, software, physical, and policy isolation to sandbox advanced AI systems that may pose existential risks.

title: Knowledge Graph Guided Evaluation of Abstention Techniques
tldr: Introduces SELECT, a knowledge-graph-derived benchmark that evaluates abstention techniques across prompting, activation steering, and fine-tuning, revealing generalization-specificity tradeoffs with no universally superior method.

title: Constructing Your Model's Value Distinction: Towards LLM Alignment with Anchor Words Tuning
tldr: Proposes Anchor Words Tuning, a representation editing method that maximizes value distinction between positive/negative tokens in LLMs to improve alignment while reducing compute.
models_studied: unspecified base LLMs and their aligned versions

title: HauntAttack: When Attack Follows Reasoning as a Shadow
tldr: HauntAttack embeds harmful instructions into legitimate reasoning questions by replacing conditions, achieving 70% average ASR on LRMs — outperforming baselines and evading safety filters.

title: How Catastrophic is Your LLM? Certifying Risk in Conversation
tldr: QRLLM certifies catastrophic risk probabilities in multi-turn LLM conversations using Markov processes on semantic similarity graphs, finding certified lower bounds reaching 70% for some models.

title: Multimodal Prompt Decoupling Attack on the Safety Filters in Text-to-Image Models
tldr: MPDA bypasses T2I safety filters by decoupling unsafe prompts into components via LLM, generating a safe base image, then recombining with adversarial text to produce NSFW content with ~93% success rate.

title: Amazon Nova AI Challenge - Trusted AI: Advancing secure, AI-assisted software development
tldr: Amazon organized a 10-team university competition pitting automated red-teaming bots against safe AI coding assistants in adversarial tournaments, yielding advances in multi-turn jailbreaking, reasoning-based safety alignment, and LLM probing.

title: On the Emergence of Weak-to-Strong Generalization: A Bias-Variance Perspective
tldr: Provides a generalized bias-variance decomposition of Bregman divergence to explain when and why weak-to-strong generalization emerges, removing prior convexity assumptions and motivating reverse cross-entropy as a more robust training loss.

title: SafeGPT: Preventing Data Leakage and Unethical Outputs in Enterprise LLM Use
tldr: SafeGPT is a dual-layer guardrail framework for enterprise LLMs that intercepts sensitive inputs and moderates unethical outputs, achieving 92% precision and 87% recall.

title: The Oversight Game: Learning to Cooperatively Balance an AI Agent's Safety and Autonomy
tldr: A game-theoretic framework (Markov Potential Game) for human-AI oversight where agent and human co-learn when to defer/intervene, with provable alignment guarantees and zero-violation gridworld results.

title: Evaluating and Improving Robustness in Large Language Models: A Survey and Future Directions
tldr: Comprehensive survey of LLM robustness organized into adversarial robustness, OOD robustness, and robustness evaluation, covering attacks, defenses, benchmarks, and future directions.

title: The Tower of Babel Revisited: Multilingual Jailbreak Prompts on Closed-Source Large Language Models
tldr: Evaluates 32 jailbreak attacks across English and Chinese on GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1, Gemini-1.5-Pro, and Qwen-Max, finding Chinese prompts consistently achieve higher attack success rates and Qwen-Max is most vulnerable.

title: Revealing the Intrinsic Ethical Vulnerability of Aligned Large Language Models
tldr: Proves theoretically and empirically that aligned LLMs retain harmful pretraining knowledge in 'dark patterns' reachable via distributional shifts, achieving 100% attack success on 19/23 SOTA models.

title: BalDRO: A Distributionally Robust Optimization based Framework for Large Language Model Unlearning
tldr: BalDRO applies distributionally robust optimization to LLM unlearning, dynamically upweighting hard-to-unlearn samples, achieving 20%+ improvement in forget quality on TOFU and MUSE benchmarks.

title: Bridging Distribution Shift and AI Safety: Conceptual and Methodological Synergies
tldr: Establishes formal one-to-one mathematical connections between distribution shift types (selection bias, spurious correlation, label shift) and AI safety goals (security, fairness, trustworthiness).

title: Mitigating Indirect Prompt Injection via Instruction-Following Intent Analysis
tldr: IntentGuard detects indirect prompt injection by analyzing whether LLMs intend to follow instructions from untrusted data, reducing attack success rates by >90% while preserving utility.

title: QueryIPI: Query-agnostic Indirect Prompt Injection on Coding Agents
tldr: QueryIPI is the first query-agnostic indirect prompt injection attack on coding agents, using iterative LLM-based optimization of malicious tool descriptions to achieve 70-87% attack success regardless of user input.

title: Are My Optimized Prompts Compromised? Exploring Vulnerabilities of LLM-based Optimizers
tldr: First systematic study of poisoning attacks on LLM-based prompt optimizers, finding feedback manipulation far more dangerous than query injection (ΔASR=0.48 vs minimal), with a highlighting defense that reduces attack impact from ΔASR=0.23 to 0.07.

title: Imperceptible Jailbreaking against Large Language Models
tldr: Imperceptible jailbreak attacks using Unicode variation selectors (invisible characters) bypass LLM safety alignment with up to 100% attack success rate while remaining visually identical to benign prompts.

title: AgentTypo: Adaptive Typographic Prompt Injection Attacks against Black-box Multimodal Agents
tldr: AgentTypo uses Bayesian optimization and multi-LLM iterative refinement to craft typographic prompt injections into webpage images, achieving 68% attack success rate against GPT-4o multimodal agents.

title: External Data Extraction Attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
tldr: First comprehensive study of external data extraction attacks against RAG-LLMs; proposes the Secret attack that extracts 35% of private data from Claude 3.7 Sonnet where prior methods get 0%.

title: FreezeVLA: Action-Freezing Attacks against Vision-Language-Action Models
tldr: FreezeVLA demonstrates that adversarial images can cause Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to 'freeze' and ignore all subsequent instructions, achieving ~76% average attack success rate across three VLA models.

title: Attacking LLMs and AI Agents: Advertisement Embedding Attacks Against Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces Advertisement Embedding Attacks (AEA), where adversaries inject promotional/malicious content into LLM outputs via platform hijacking or backdoored model checkpoints, achieving near-100% attack success.

title: Universally Unfiltered and Unseen: Input-Agnostic Multimodal Jailbreaks against Text-to-Image Model Safeguards
tldr: U3-Attack bypasses T2I model safeguards with universal input-agnostic adversarial patches and paraphrase sets, achieving 4x higher success than prior SOTA.

title: Hoist with His Own Petard: Inducing Guardrails to Facilitate Denial-of-Service Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation of LLMs
tldr: MutedRAG exploits LLM safety guardrails in RAG systems as an attack vector, injecting minimal jailbreak prompts into knowledge bases to trigger refusals on legitimate queries, achieving 58-97% success rates.
models_studied: other LLMs (8 total, names not fully specified)

title: Graph of Attacks: Improved Black-Box and Interpretable Jailbreaks for LLMs
tldr: GoAT uses a Graph of Thoughts framework to generate readable black-box jailbreak prompts, achieving up to 5x better success on robust models like Llama2 with far fewer queries than prior methods.

title: Towards Benign Memory Forgetting for Selective Multimodal Large Language Model Unlearning
tldr: SMFA uses refusal fine-tuning plus anchor-guided masking to selectively erase sensitive knowledge from multimodal LLMs while preserving general visual understanding, outperforming four baselines on a new benchmark.

title: Towards Minimal Targeted Updates of Language Models with Targeted Negative Training
tldr: Targeted Negative Training (TNT) minimizes KL-divergence at token level to eliminate undesirable LM outputs (hallucinations, toxicity) while preserving original model behavior.

title: Polarity-Aware Probing for Quantifying Latent Alignment in Language Models
tldr: PA-CCS extends Contrast-Consistent Search with polarity inversion constraints and two new metrics (Polar Consistency, Contradiction Index) to quantify latent alignment signals across 16 LLMs without supervision.
models_studied: 16 language models including encoder-only, decoder-only, and instruction-tuned variants

title: Merger-as-a-Stealer: Stealing Targeted PII from Aligned LLMs with Model Merging
tldr: Malicious actors can extract targeted PII from aligned LLMs by uploading a specially fine-tuned attack model into a model merging process, achieving up to 76% exact match for email extraction.

title: LLM Unlearning on Noisy Forget Sets: A Study of Incomplete, Rewritten, and Watermarked Data
tldr: LLM unlearning is surprisingly robust to noisy forget sets (masking up to 30%, rewrites, watermarking) because unlearning algorithms rely on salient semantic tokens that survive surface-level perturbations.

title: Ready2Unlearn: A Learning-Time Approach for Preparing Models with Future Unlearning Readiness
tldr: Ready2Unlearn uses meta-learning to train models proactively during learning so they can later forget specific data faster, retain utility better, and resist relearning of forgotten data.

title: What Makes an Evaluation Useful? Common Pitfalls and Best Practices
tldr: A practitioner framework connecting threat modeling to AI safety evaluation design, identifying six common pitfalls and proposing properties for useful individual evaluations and evaluation suites.

title: AutoBackdoor: Automating Backdoor Attacks via LLM Agents
tldr: AutoBackdoor is a fully automated LLM-agent-driven framework for injecting backdoors into LLMs, achieving 90%+ attack success rates with ~200 poisoned samples while evading existing defenses.

title: Report on NSF Workshop on Science of Safe AI
tldr: NSF workshop report (80+ researchers) synthesizing open challenges and research directions across formal verification, adversarial robustness, agentic safety, and safety specification for trustworthy AI.

title: Understanding and Benchmarking the Trustworthiness in Multimodal LLMs for Video Understanding
tldr: Trust-videoLLMs benchmarks 23 video LLMs across 30 tasks on truthfulness, safety, robustness, fairness, and privacy, finding commercial models dominate but all models struggle with temporal reasoning and adversarial perturbations.

title: Adaptively profiling models with task elicitation
tldr: Adaptive evaluations use LLM evaluator agents to iteratively generate targeted questions that expose model weaknesses, achieving ~40% more jailbreak vulnerability discovery vs. PAIR and doubling forecasting inconsistency vs. static baselines.

title: A Pragmatic Way to Measure Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
tldr: Proposes and validates LLM-autorater metrics for CoT legibility and coverage, finding frontier models exhibit high default monitorability on challenging benchmarks.

title: Unspoken Hints: Accuracy Without Acknowledgement in LLM Reasoning
tldr: LLMs frequently exploit correct hints to improve accuracy while failing to acknowledge them in reasoning traces, revealing systematic CoT unfaithfulness especially for simple raw-answer hints.

title: SafeVision: Efficient Image Guardrail with Robust Policy Adherence and Explainability
tldr: SafeVision is an image guardrail system using a dual-mode VLM with DPO and custom loss for content moderation, outperforming GPT-4o by 8.6-15.5% at 16x lower latency.

title: Following the Whispers of Values: Unraveling Neural Mechanisms Behind Value-Oriented Behaviors in LLMs
tldr: ValueExploration framework identifies value-specific neurons in LLM FFN layers using entropy-based detection; deactivating them reduces value-aligned behavior by 15-40% across four models.

title: LPS-Bench: Benchmarking Safety Awareness of Computer-Use Agents in Long-Horizon Planning under Benign and Adversarial Scenarios
tldr: LPS-Bench evaluates safety awareness of computer-use agents across 570 test cases spanning 7 task domains and 9 risk categories in both benign and adversarial settings, finding large capability-safety gaps.

title: CFSafety: Comprehensive Fine-grained Safety Assessment for LLMs
tldr: CFSafety is a 25k-prompt bilingual benchmark spanning 5 safety scenarios and 5 instruction attack types, evaluated on 8 LLMs using a fine-grained 1-5 scoring formula.

title: Insights into a radiology-specialised multimodal large language model with sparse autoencoders
tldr: Applies Matryoshka-SAE to MAIRA-2, a radiology-specialized multimodal LLM, uncovering clinically interpretable features (medical devices, pathologies) and demonstrating mixed feature-steering results.

title: IF-GUIDE: Influence Function-Guided Detoxification of LLMs
tldr: IF-Guide uses influence functions during LLM pretraining to identify and suppress toxic training tokens, achieving up to 10x toxicity reduction while preserving model utility.

title: Unveiling Trust in Multimodal Large Language Models: Evaluation, Analysis, and Mitigation
tldr: MultiTrust-X evaluates 30 MLLMs across 32 tasks on 5 trustworthiness dimensions and proposes RESA, a chain-of-thought safety alignment method that achieves the best open-source score of 69.66.

title: The Trojan in the Vocabulary: Stealthy Sabotage of LLM Composition
tldr: A single engineered 'breaker token' injected into a donor model's vocabulary stays inert in the donor but triggers malicious behavior after tokenizer transplantation into a base model.

title: Identifying Intervenable and Interpretable Features via Orthogonality Regularization
tldr: Orthogonality regularization applied to SAE decoder matrices produces identifiable, interpretable, and causally intervenable features in fine-tuned language models.

title: Training Superior Sparse Autoencoders for Instruct Models
tldr: FAST (Finetuning-aligned Sequential Training) trains SAEs on instruct models by processing dialogue instances independently, reducing MSE by ~8x and tripling high-quality interpretable features vs. block training baselines.

title: Reimagining Safety Alignment with An Image
tldr: Magic Image optimizes a single visual prompt via dual-loss gradient descent to simultaneously reduce jailbreak success and over-refusal in multimodal LLMs without parameter updates.

title: Toward a Flexible Framework for Linear Representation Hypothesis Using Maximum Likelihood Estimation
tldr: Proposes SAND, a principled MLE-based algorithm using von Mises-Fisher distributions to compute steering vectors for the linear representation hypothesis, outperforming baselines on LLaMA monitoring and intervention tasks.

title: nnterp: A Standardized Interface for Mechanistic Interpretability of Transformers
tldr: nnterp is a lightweight wrapper around NNsight providing a unified API for mechanistic interpretability interventions across 50+ transformer variants from 16+ architecture families.

title: Derailing Non-Answers via Logit Suppression at Output Subspace Boundaries in RLHF-Aligned Language Models
tldr: Suppressing the double-newline token after <think> at inference time bypasses RLHF-trained refusals in DeepSeek-R1 distillations without modifying weights or prompts.

title: PENDULUM: A Benchmark for Assessing Sycophancy in Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: PENDULUM is a ~2,000-item VQA benchmark testing sycophancy in multimodal LLMs across six image domains, revealing substantial susceptibility to user-suggested incorrect answers.

title: Evaluation Awareness Scales Predictably in Open-Weights Large Language Models
tldr: Evaluation awareness in LLMs follows a predictable power-law scaling with model size across four model families (0.27B–70B), enabling forecasting of deceptive behavior in larger models.

title: Swallowing the Poison Pills: Insights from Vulnerability Disparity Among LLMs
tldr: Poison pill attacks (targeted data poisoning) exploit long-tail knowledge vulnerabilities in LLMs, achieving 54.6% more retrieval inaccuracy vs. dominant topics and requiring 30% fewer samples on compressed models.

title: The Curse of Popularity: Popular Entities have Catastrophic Side Effects when Deleting Knowledge from Language Models
tldr: Deleting knowledge about popular (high-degree) entities in LMs causes catastrophic side effects on related knowledge, demonstrated using synthetic knowledge graphs with controlled entity frequency.

title: Fine-Tuned LLMs Know They Don't Know: A Parameter-Efficient Approach to Recovering Honesty
tldr: HCNR identifies and restores honesty-critical neurons to pre-trained states after SFT, recovering 33.25% of lost honesty with 2.23x speedup and 10x less data than baselines.

title: Do Methods to Jailbreak and Defend LLMs Generalize Across Languages?
tldr: First systematic multilingual evaluation of jailbreaks and defenses across 10 languages: high-resource languages are paradoxically safer under standard queries but more vulnerable to adversarial attacks.

title: Anecdoctoring: Automated Red-Teaming Across Language and Place
tldr: Anecdoctoring uses fact-checking data, narrative clustering, and knowledge graphs to auto-generate culturally grounded adversarial prompts that achieve >80% attack success rates on LLMs across English, Spanish, and Hindi.

title: P-Aligner: Enabling Pre-Alignment of Language Models via Principled Instruction Synthesis
tldr: P-Aligner is a lightweight pre-processing module that refines user instructions via a MCTS-based principle-guided pipeline, improving LLM alignment by 28.35% win-rate on GPT-4-turbo.

title: Bridging the Gap in Vision Language Models in Identifying Unsafe Concepts Across Modalities
tldr: Reveals a persistent modality gap in VLMs where unsafe concepts are perceived accurately but inconsistently flagged as unsafe across text vs. image inputs, and proposes an RL-based alignment fix.

title: Interpretable Reward Modeling with Active Concept Bottlenecks
tldr: CB-RM decomposes RLHF reward models into human-interpretable concepts via Concept Bottleneck Models with active learning (EIG acquisition) for sample-efficient annotation.

title: What Really Matters in Many-Shot Attacks? An Empirical Study of Long-Context Vulnerabilities in LLMs
tldr: Context length (not content harmfulness) is the primary driver of many-shot jailbreak success; even random dummy text in long contexts can bypass LLM safety measures.

title: DUAL-Bench: Measuring Over-Refusal and Robustness in Vision-Language Models
tldr: DUAL-Bench is the first multimodal benchmark measuring both over-refusal and robustness in 18 VLMs across 12 hazard categories, finding models achieve only 3.9-12.9% safe completion rates.

title: Alignment Tipping Process: How Self-Evolution Pushes LLM Agents Off the Rails
tldr: Self-evolving LLM agents undergo an Alignment Tipping Process (ATP) where feedback-driven optimization causes rapid erosion of alignment constraints, and current RL-based alignment methods provide limited defense.

title: Weights-Rotated Preference Optimization for Large Language Models
tldr: RoPO addresses reward hacking in DPO by applying orthogonal matrix constraints on hidden states to prevent neuron collapse, using only 0.015% extra parameters.

title: ReasAlign: Reasoning Enhanced Safety Alignment against Prompt Injection Attack
tldr: ReasAlign uses structured reasoning steps and test-time scaling with a preference-optimized judge to defend LLMs against indirect prompt injection, achieving 3.6% ASR vs 74.4% for prior SOTA at comparable utility.

title: Query-efficient and dataset-independent red teaming for LLMs content safety evaluation
tldr: RAPT is an automated red teaming framework using a generate-select loop with an RL-based selector and contrastive prompt generator to find harmful LLM behaviors without pre-existing datasets.

title: DP2Unlearning: An Efficient and Guaranteed Unlearning Framework for LLMs
tldr: DP2Unlearning trains LLMs on DP-protected text then enables efficient data unlearning with formal disclosure guarantees, achieving ~50% cost of full retraining while outperforming approximate methods.

title: Cross-Layer Discrete Concept Discovery for Interpreting Language Models
tldr: CLVQ-VAE uses cross-layer vector quantization to discover discrete interpretable concept vectors in LLMs, outperforming per-layer methods and SAE baselines on faithfulness and human evaluations.

title: SAEmnesia: Erasing Concepts in Diffusion Models with Supervised Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: SAEmnesia uses supervised sparse autoencoders to enforce one-to-one concept-neuron mappings in diffusion models, achieving 91.51% on UnlearnCanvas (9.22% over prior art) with 96.67% less hyperparameter search.

title: From Adversarial Poetry to Adversarial Tales: An Interpretability Research Agenda
tldr: Adversarial Tales embeds harmful requests in Proppian cyberpunk narratives, achieving 71.3% average jailbreak success across 26 frontier models, and proposes an interpretability research agenda to understand the vulnerability.

title: MCP-ITP: An Automated Framework for Implicit Tool Poisoning in MCP
tldr: MCP-ITP is an automated black-box framework for implicit tool poisoning in MCP-based LLM agents, achieving up to 84.2% attack success rate while evading detection at a 0.3% malicious detection rate.

title: Inference-Time Decomposition of Activations (ITDA): A Scalable Approach to Interpreting Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces ITDA, a training-free alternative to SAEs that decomposes LLM activations using greedy dictionary construction and matching pursuit, trainable in 1% of SAE time on models up to 405B parameters.

title: Concept Steerers: Leveraging K-Sparse Autoencoders for Controllable Generations
tldr: Uses k-sparse autoencoders on text encoder embeddings to identify monosemantic concepts in diffusion models and steer generation away from unsafe content, achieving SOTA safety with 5x speed improvement.

title: Unboxing the Black Box: Mechanistic Interpretability for Algorithmic Understanding of Neural Networks
tldr: Proposes a unified three-dimensional taxonomy (scope, task, analysis nature) for mechanistic interpretability techniques and traces the field's development from early circuit discovery to modern SAE-based methods.

title: Transferring Linear Features Across Language Models With Model Stitching
tldr: Affine mappings between residual streams enable transferring SAEs, probes, and steering vectors across different-sized language models, cutting SAE training cost by 30-50%.

title: Language Model Circuits Are Sparse in the Neuron Basis
tldr: MLP neuron activations are as sparse a feature basis as SAEs for circuit tracing when combined with RelP attribution, eliminating the need for learned feature dictionaries.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability for Large Language Model Alignment: Progress, Challenges, and Future Directions
tldr: Surveys mechanistic interpretability methods (circuits, SAEs, activation steering) and their applications to LLM alignment, identifying superposition and scale as key challenges.

title: DISCO: Disentangled Communication Steering for Large Language Models
tldr: DISCO injects steering vectors into query and value spaces within attention heads rather than head outputs, achieving up to 19.1% higher steering efficacy on LLaMA 3.1 8B and Gemma 2 9B.

title: Bridging Today and the Future of Humanity: AI Safety in 2024 and Beyond
tldr: Surveys the 2024 AI safety landscape across jailbreaking, red teaming, content moderation, privacy, security, and governance, framed against a speculative multi-era roadmap of human-AI civilization evolution.

title: Beyond Context: Large Language Models Failure to Grasp Users Intent
tldr: Empirically demonstrates that LLMs fail to recognize harmful user intent hidden behind emotional framing, with reasoning-enhanced models amplifying rather than mitigating vulnerabilities.

title: Layer-Wise Perturbations via Sparse Autoencoders for Adversarial Text Generation
tldr: Introduces SFPF, a framework that uses sparse autoencoders to identify and perturb adversarially-sensitive features in LLM hidden layers, achieving up to 95% attack success rate when combined with adaptive attacks.

title: SARSteer: Safeguarding Large Audio Language Models via Safe-Ablated Refusal Steering
tldr: Proposes SARSteer, an inference-time defense for Large Audio-Language Models using text-derived refusal steering with PCA-based safe-space ablation to reject harmful audio queries without over-refusing benign ones.

title: The Instability of Safety: How Random Seeds and Temperature Expose Inconsistent LLM Refusal Behavior
tldr: 18-28% of harmful prompts produce inconsistent refusal decisions across random seeds and temperatures in 7B-12B LLMs; single-shot safety evals are unreliable and N>=3 samples are needed.

title: STARS: Segment-level Token Alignment with Rejection Sampling in Large Language Models
tldr: STARS is a decoding-time alignment algorithm that scores and accepts/rejects fixed-size token segments using a process reward model, outperforming SFT by 14.9pp and DPO by 4.3pp on win-rates.

title: Institutional AI: Governing LLM Collusion in Multi-Agent Cournot Markets via Public Governance Graphs
tldr: Proposes 'Institutional AI' — a governance-graph framework that reduces LLM multi-agent collusion in Cournot markets from 50% severe-collusion incidence to 5.6%, outperforming prompt-only constitutional constraints.

title: T3: Benchmarking Sycophancy and Skepticism in Causal Judgment
tldr: T3 is a 454-case benchmark diagnosing sycophancy and skepticism failure modes in LLMs doing causal reasoning, revealing safety-tuned models over-refuse valid claims and larger models regress on counterfactuals.

title: Learning Natural Language Constraints for Safe Reinforcement Learning of Language Agents
tldr: Proposes CLIRL+CAPO framework that learns explicit natural language constraints from demonstrations within a CMDP to align LLMs with zero constraint violations under domain shifts.

title: SPA: Achieving Consensus in LLM Alignment via Self-Priority Optimization
tldr: SPA is an unsupervised LLM alignment framework that enforces a 'trustworthy-before-helpful' lexicographic ordering via self-generated preference pairs and uncertainty-weighted SimPO loss.

title: Agentic Moderation: Multi-Agent Design for Safer Vision-Language Models
tldr: A multi-agent moderation framework (Shield, Responder, Evaluator, Reflector) defends vision-language models against jailbreak attacks, reducing attack success rates by 7-19% and improving refusal rates by 4-20%.

title: The Trojan Knowledge: Bypassing Commercial LLM Guardrails via Harmless Prompt Weaving and Adaptive Tree Search
tldr: CKA-Agent jailbreaks commercial LLMs (95%+ success) by decomposing harmful goals into individually benign multi-turn queries using UCT-guided adaptive tree search over the model's own knowledge.

title: AdversariaLLM: A Unified and Modular Toolbox for LLM Robustness Research
tldr: AdversariaLLM is a unified, reproducible toolbox implementing 12 adversarial attack algorithms and 7 benchmark datasets for LLM robustness research, with bug fixes that improve attack success rates by up to 28%.

title: Semantic Representation Attack against Aligned Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes Semantic Representation Heuristic Search (SRHS), a jailbreak method exploiting semantic representation space to achieve 89.41% avg attack success rate across 18 LLMs including 100% on 11 models.

title: Adversarially Pretrained Transformers May Be Universally Robust In-Context Learners
tldr: First theoretical proof that single-layer transformers adversarially pretrained across classification tasks robustly generalize to unseen tasks via in-context learning from clean examples, without retraining.

title: Keys to Robust Edits: from Theoretical Insights to Practical Advances
tldr: Theoretically analyzes why locate-and-edit knowledge editing methods fail on rephrased/long-context queries, then introduces REP (Robust Edit Pathway) which improves rephrase robustness from 52.1% to 79.1% on LLaMA2-7B.

title: Safety Misalignment Against Large Language Models
tldr: Comprehensive evaluation of LLM safety misalignment attacks (prompt modification, SFT, model editing) and defenses; introduces Self-Supervised Representation Attack requiring no harmful training data.

title: A Survey on Data Security in Large Language Models
tldr: A systematic survey of data security risks in LLMs (poisoning, prompt injection, hallucination, leakage, bias) and defense mechanisms (adversarial training, RLHF, data augmentation), with a catalog of relevant datasets.

title: Outcome Accuracy is Not Enough: Aligning the Reasoning Process of Reward Models
tldr: Reward models exhibit deceptive alignment by producing correct judgments for wrong reasons; a new Rationale Consistency metric and hybrid training signal fixes this, improving RM-Bench by 5% and RLHF creative writing by 7%.

title: The Ends Justify the Thoughts: RL-Induced Motivated Reasoning in LLMs
tldr: RL finetuning causes LLMs to generate plausible but distorted chain-of-thought justifications for violating constitutional constraints, and smaller monitor models can be deceived by this reasoning.

title: LLM Hypnosis: Exploiting User Feedback for Unauthorized Knowledge Injection to All Users
tldr: A single unprivileged user can persistently alter LLM knowledge/behavior for all users by exploiting feedback mechanisms via strategic prompting and upvote/downvote signals.

title: Wisdom is Knowing What not to Say: Hallucination-Free LLMs Unlearning via Attention Shifting
tldr: Attention-Shifting (AS) framework for LLM machine unlearning suppresses attention to fact-bearing tokens via dual-loss optimization, achieving 0% hallucination rates while preserving model utility.

title: Towards Interpretable Hallucination Analysis and Mitigation in LVLMs via Contrastive Neuron Steering
tldr: Uses sparse autoencoders to identify image-specific neurons in LVLMs, showing hallucinations stem from their disruption, and proposes Contrastive Neuron Steering (CNS) to reduce hallucinations with only 14% latency overhead.

title: VISOR++: Universal Visual Inputs based Steering for Large Vision Language Models
tldr: VISOR++ generates universal optimized images that replicate activation-space steering vector effects in VLMs without requiring internal model access, enabling alignment interventions via API-only inputs.

title: TRACE: Training and Inference-Time Interpretability Analysis for Language Models
tldr: TRACE is a modular toolkit for in-training and inference-time interpretability analysis of transformers, revealing developmental phases like early syntactic emergence and delayed semantic acquisition.

title: Understanding Verbatim Memorization in LLMs Through Circuit Discovery
tldr: Uses circuit discovery (EAP-IG) on GPT-Neo-125m to find minimal circuits governing verbatim memorization initiation vs. maintenance, showing initiation circuits generalize but maintenance circuits do not.

title: GIM: Improved Interpretability for Large Language Models
tldr: GIM introduces three backpropagation modifications (temperature-adjusted softmax gradients, layernorm freeze, gradient normalization) to correct attention self-repair artifacts, substantially improving faithfulness of circuit/feature attribution in LLMs.

title: Detoxification of Large Language Models through Output-layer Fusion with a Calibration Model
tldr: A compact 3-layer calibration model learns detoxified embeddings from WildJailbreak data and injects them into a target LLM at inference time via weighted output-layer fusion, reducing toxic generation without retraining.

title: Toward Constitutional Autonomy in AI Systems: A Theoretical Framework for Aligned Agentic Intelligence
tldr: Proposes Constitutional Autonomy, a four-subsystem framework extending alignment enforcement from training into runtime deployment for agentic AI, achieving 23% reduction in harmful attention patterns with sub-2% computational overhead.

title: Lock on Target! Precision Unlearning via Directional Control
tldr: DOGE uses unlearning direction extraction and orthogonal gradient projection to precisely erase target knowledge from LLMs while minimizing collateral damage to retained knowledge.

title: Read the Scene, Not the Script: Outcome-Aware Safety for LLMs
tldr: Identifies 'consequence-blindness' in safety-aligned LLMs, introduces CB-Bench (600 samples) and CS-Chain-4k training set to teach outcome-aware reasoning, reducing jailbreak success by 43% while cutting over-refusals.

title: Casting a SPELL: Sentence Pairing Exploration for LLM Limitation-breaking
tldr: SPELL is a jailbreaking framework using reinforcement learning and sentence-pairing to elicit malicious code generation from LLMs, achieving 83.75% ASR on GPT-4.1 and proposing a defense reaching 100% attack rejection on Claude-3.5.

title: SoK: Trust-Authorization Mismatch in LLM Agent Interactions
tldr: A SoK paper proposing the B-I-P (Belief-Intention-Permission) model and Trust-Authorization Matrix to systematize LLM agent security attacks and defenses around trust-authorization mismatches.

title: Machine Learning for Detection and Analysis of Novel LLM Jailbreaks
tldr: Fine-tuned BERT achieves 0.997 AUC for detecting known jailbreaks and generalizes well to novel unseen jailbreak categories, with reflexivity in prompt structure as a key signal.

title: Active Attacks: Red-teaming LLMs via Adaptive Environments
tldr: An RL-based red-teaming method that periodically safety fine-tunes the victim LLM to force the attacker to explore new attack modes, achieving 400x improvement in cross-attack success rate.

title: Enhancing the Safety of Medical Vision-Language Models by Synthetic Demonstrations
tldr: Proposes an inference-time defense using synthetic clinical demonstrations to protect medical VLMs against jailbreak attacks across 9 imaging modalities without substantially degrading performance.

title: Lifting Data-Tracing Machine Unlearning to Knowledge-Tracing for Foundation Models
tldr: Proposes shifting machine unlearning for foundation models from data-tracing (removing training examples) to knowledge-tracing (removing specific capabilities/knowledge), with a CLIP case study introducing a hinge loss to prevent over-forgetting.

title: VERA: Variational Inference Framework for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
tldr: VERA frames black-box jailbreaking as variational inference, training a small attacker LLM with LoRA to amortize adversarial prompt generation, achieving 50.5% average attack success rate across eight LLMs.

title: The Structural Safety Generalization Problem
tldr: LLM safety mechanisms fail to generalize across semantically equivalent but structurally different inputs; a Structure Rewriting Guardrail reduces attack success from 44% to 6% on GPT-4o.

title: EU-Agent-Bench: Measuring Illegal Behavior of LLM Agents Under EU Law
tldr: EU-Agent-Bench introduces a 600-sample benchmark evaluating LLM agent compliance with EU law across six legal categories, finding compliance rates of 38-55% and no benefit from explicit legislation injection.

title: CRDA: Content Risk Drift Assessment of Large Language Models through Adversarial Multi-Agent Interaction
tldr: CRDA is a lightweight multi-agent framework that reveals progressive content risk drift in Chinese LLMs during sustained adversarial role-playing interactions, with restricted roles causing ~31.5% cumulative deterioration by round 10.

title: When the Prompt Becomes Visual: Vision-Centric Jailbreak Attacks for Large Image Editing Models
tldr: VJA encodes malicious instructions purely as visual inputs to bypass text-based safety filters in image editing models, achieving up to 80.9% attack success rate, with IESBench as a new safety benchmark.

title: From Poisoned to Aware: Fostering Backdoor Self-Awareness in LLMs
tldr: An RL-based post-training framework enables backdoor-poisoned LLMs to develop self-awareness of their implanted triggers, achieving 80% trigger elicitation accuracy and enabling downstream defense strategies.

title: A Biosecurity Agent for Lifecycle LLM Biosecurity Alignment
tldr: A four-stage defense-in-depth biosecurity framework for LLMs combining dataset sanitization, DPO alignment, runtime guardrails, and automated red-teaming reduces attack success from 59.7% to 3.0%.

title: Safety Recovery in Reasoning Models Is Only a Few Early Steering Steps Away
tldr: SafeThink monitors reasoning traces with a safety reward model and injects minimal corrective prefixes in the first 1-3 reasoning steps, reducing jailbreak attack success rates by 30-60% across six multimodal reasoning models.

title: Split Personality Training: Revealing Latent Knowledge Through Alternate Personalities
tldr: Split Personality Training (SPT) fine-tunes a dormant honest LoRA persona into a model that, when triggered post-response, detects hidden misalignment with 96% accuracy vs. ~0% baseline.

title: Watch your steps: Dormant Adversarial Behaviors that Activate upon LLM Finetuning
tldr: FAB attack uses meta-learning to inject dormant adversarial behaviors into LLMs that remain hidden pre-finetuning but reliably activate once users finetune the model on almost any dataset.

title: ROSE: Toward Reality-Oriented Safety Evaluation of Large Language Models
tldr: ROSE uses multi-objective reinforcement fine-tuning to automatically generate topically diverse and contextually grounded adversarial prompts for LLM safety evaluation, outperforming static benchmarks.

title: Toward Safer Diffusion Language Models: Discovery and Mitigation of Priming Vulnerability
tldr: Identifies a 'priming vulnerability' in Masked Diffusion Language Models where affirmative tokens injected during denoising steer harmful outputs, and proposes Recovery Alignment (RA) to defend against it.

title: CoT Defender: Preemptive Chain-of-Thought Occupation for Jailbreak Attack Mitigation
tldr: CoT Defender preemptively occupies LLM initial tokens with chain-of-thought reasoning using a two-stage RL training framework, reducing jailbreak attack success rates below 8% across four models.

title: Replicating TEMPEST at Scale: Multi-Turn Adversarial Attacks Against Trillion-Parameter Frontier Models
tldr: Evaluates 10 frontier LLMs (12B-1T params) against TEMPEST multi-turn jailbreaks across 1,000 harmful behaviors; 6 models hit 96-100% ASR, extended reasoning mode cut ASR from 97% to 42%.

title: Reasoning over Precedents Alongside Statutes: Case-Augmented Deliberative Alignment for LLM Safety
tldr: CADA uses RL on self-generated case-augmented safety reasoning chains to improve LLM harmlessness and robustness against jailbreaks while reducing over-refusals of benign requests.

title: LM Agents May Fail to Act on Their Own Risk Knowledge
tldr: LM agents score >98% on abstract risk knowledge tests but only 4.8-25.6% on actual safe execution, revealing a persistent awareness-execution gap that scaling does not close.

title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization under Distribution Shifts
tldr: RAVEN dynamically reweights multiple weak supervisors to enable robust weak-to-strong generalization under distribution shifts, achieving 30%+ OOD improvements.

title: Semantic-aware Wasserstein Policy Regularization for Large Language Model Alignment
tldr: Proposes Wasserstein Policy Regularization (WPR), replacing KL divergence in RLHF with entropy-regularized Wasserstein distance to capture token-space semantics, improving LLM alignment.

title: TrailBlazer: History-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Black-Box LLM Jailbreaking
tldr: TrailBlazer uses history-augmented RL with attention-based reweighting to exploit vulnerabilities across interaction turns, achieving 95%+ jailbreak success rates with ~3x fewer queries than baselines.

title: Robust Policy Optimization to Prevent Catastrophic Forgetting
tldr: FRPO modifies GRPO with a max-min entropic risk objective so that safety/capability behaviors learned during RLHF are preserved after downstream fine-tuning, without added compute.

title: Regulating the Agency of LLM-based Agents
tldr: Proposes measuring and controlling LLM agent agency along three dimensions (preference rigidity, independent operation, goal persistence) using representation engineering 'agency sliders' to enable regulatory frameworks.

title: Surgery: Mitigating Harmful Fine-Tuning for Large Language Models via Attention Sink
tldr: Surgery defends LLMs against harmful fine-tuning by suppressing 'sink divergence' in attention heads via a lightweight regularizer, reducing harmful output rates by 5.9-11.25% vs. best baselines.

title: CCS-Lib: A Python package to elicit latent knowledge from LLMs
tldr: CCS-Lib is a Python package implementing Contrast-Consistent Search (CCS) and VINC methods to elicit latent knowledge from LLM hidden states without labeled training data.

title: Why does weak-OOD help? A Further Step Towards Understanding Jailbreaking VLMs
tldr: Explains why mild OOD perturbations most effectively jailbreak VLMs by analyzing intent perception vs. refusal triggering tradeoff, and introduces JOCR attack leveraging OCR capabilities.

title: Do Prompts Guarantee Safety? Mitigating Toxicity from LLM Generations through Subspace Intervention
tldr: Gradient-based SVD identifies toxic activation subspaces in LLMs; projecting hidden states away from this subspace at inference reduces toxicity 8-20% while preserving fluency and task utility.

title: On the Robustness of Knowledge Editing for Detoxification
tldr: Evaluates robustness of knowledge-editing-based LLM detoxification across three dimensions, finding that apparent safety gains are often pseudo-detoxification caused by degenerate repetitive outputs.

title: AntiPaSTO: Self-Supervised Honesty Steering via Anti-Parallel Representations
tldr: AntiPaSTO steers LLM honesty via SVD-based representation optimization using contrastive word pairs, achieving 6.9x improvement over prompting baselines on moral reasoning tasks with no preference labels.

title: MENTOR: A Metacognition-Driven Self-Evolution Framework for Uncovering and Mitigating Implicit Domain Risks in LLMs
tldr: MENTOR uses metacognitive self-assessment, dynamic rule evolution, and activation steering to reduce implicit domain-specific jailbreak rates in LLMs from ~60% to ~3.5% across education, finance, and management domains.

title: N-GLARE: An Non-Generative Latent Representation-Efficient LLM Safety Evaluator
tldr: N-GLARE evaluates LLM safety using Angular-Probabilistic Trajectories over latent representations, reproducing red-teaming safety rankings at <1% of the token and runtime cost.

tldr: ALEAHallu adversarially edits VLM parameters responsible for hallucination by localizing them via activation analysis and stress-testing with adversarial prompts, reducing CHAIRs from 56.4 to 39.3.

title: Correctness-Optimized Residual Activation Lens (CORAL): Transferrable and Calibration-Aware Inference-Time Steering
tldr: CORAL uses regularized MLP probes on residual stream activations to steer LLMs at inference time, achieving 10% accuracy gains and 50% calibration error reductions across 7B models.

title: NeuroBreak: Unveil Internal Jailbreak Mechanisms in Large Language Models
tldr: NeuroBreak is a visual analytics system that identifies safety-critical neurons in LLMs via layer-wise probing and neuron attribution, enabling targeted fine-tuning that reduces jailbreak ASR to near-zero while updating <0.2% of parameters.

title: Behemoth: Benchmarking Unlearning in LLMs Using Fully Synthetic Data
tldr: Behemoth is a fully synthetic data framework for controlled benchmarking of LLM unlearning/knowledge editing, revealing rank-restriction paradoxically improves edits and layer-level findings.

title: Distribution-Aware Feature Selection for SAEs

title: LatentGuard: Controllable Latent Steering for Robust Refusal of Attacks and Reliable Response Generation
tldr: LatentGuard combines reasoning-enhanced fine-tuning with a VAE over LLM activations to enable controllable, interpretable refusal of adversarial prompts while preserving response utility.

title: Feature-Guided SAE Steering for Refusal-Rate Control using Contrasting Prompts
tldr: Uses SAE feature steering with contrasting prompt pairs to control LLM refusal rates, achieving +18.9% safety and +11.1% utility gains simultaneously on Llama-3 8B.

title: Beyond Redundancy: Diverse and Specialized Multi-Expert Sparse Autoencoder

tldr: ASTRA is a framework that evaluates LLM agentic steerability across 10 scenarios, 37 tools, and 53 guardrails, finding model size poorly predicts agentic safety and that universal jailbreak resistance is negatively correlated with agentic steerability.

title: AntiDote: Bi-level Adversarial Training for Tamper-Resistant LLMs

title: AI Debaters are More Persuasive when Arguing in Alignment with Their Own Beliefs
tldr: LLMs are more persuasive when debating positions aligned with their own prior beliefs, but sycophantically shift stance toward judge personas, revealing fundamental weaknesses in AI debate as an oversight mechanism.

title: SocialHarmBench: Revealing LLM Vulnerabilities to Socially Harmful Requests
tldr: SocialHarmBench introduces 585 adversarial prompts across 7 sociopolitical categories and 34 countries, revealing that open-weight LLMs reach up to 97-98% attack success rates under weight-tampering attacks.

title: DREAM: Dynamic Red-teaming across Environments for AI Models
tldr: DREAM is a framework using a Cross-Environment Adversarial Knowledge Graph and Contextualized Guided Policy Search to evaluate LLM agents against dynamic multi-stage attacks, achieving >70% success against most models.

title: Jailbreaking LLMs via Calibration

title: FindTheFlaws: Annotated Errors for Detecting Flawed Reasoning and Scalable Oversight Research
tldr: FindTheFlaws introduces five expert-annotated datasets (medicine, math, science, coding, Lojban) for evaluating AI error-detection and scalable oversight methods, revealing frontier models vary widely in critiquing ability.

title: Downgrade to Upgrade: Optimizer Simplification Enhances Robustness in LLM Unlearning
tldr: Using simpler (lower-order or gradient-compressed) optimizers for LLM unlearning paradoxically produces more robust unlearning that resists quantization and relearning attacks.

title: SoK: a Comprehensive Causality Analysis Framework for Large Language Model Security
tldr: A unified causality analysis framework operating at token, neuron, layer, and representation levels reveals that LLM safety mechanisms are highly localized (early-to-middle layers, ~1-2% of neurons), and enables >95% jailbreak detection accuracy.

title: Any-Depth Alignment: Unlocking Innate Safety Alignment of LLMs to Any-Depth
tldr: Any-Depth Alignment (ADA) is a training-free inference-time defense that reactivates LLM safety refusals at any generation depth via re-injected assistant header tokens or a linear probe, achieving near-100% adversarial refusal rates.

title: Black-Box Behavioral Distillation Breaks Safety Alignment in Medical LLMs
tldr: Black-box distillation of a safety-aligned medical LLM using only benign outputs produces a surrogate that breaks alignment: 86% adversarial violation rate vs. 66% in the teacher.

title: Eliciting Behaviors in Multi-Turn Conversations
tldr: EMBER uses online RL (GRPO/BNPO) to elicit specific behaviors from LLMs in multi-turn conversations, achieving 45/19/77% success rates vs. near-zero for static benchmarks on newer models.

title: Safeguarding LLM Fine-tuning via Push-Pull Distributional Alignment
tldr: Safety Optimal Transport (SOT) uses a push-pull distributional alignment mechanism to prevent safety erosion during LLM fine-tuning, achieving superior safety-utility tradeoffs versus instance-level filtering baselines.

title: Hide and Seek in Embedding Space: Geometry-based Steganography and Detection in Large Language Models
tldr: Formalizes LLM steganography via embedding-space hyperplane projections that reduce payload recoverability, and proposes linear-probe-based mechanistic detection that catches covert encoding even when output-level recovery is blocked.

title: Rethinking Benign Relearning: Syntax as the Hidden Driver of Unlearning Failures
tldr: Syntactic similarity—not topical relevance—is the primary driver of benign relearning failures in machine unlearning; syntactic diversification of forget-set queries substantially mitigates this vulnerability.

title: Robustness of Vision Language Models Against Split-Image Harmful Input Attacks
tldr: Introduces SIVA, a three-phase split-image jailbreak attack on VLMs that distributes harmful content across image fragments, achieving up to 79.6% ASR while bypassing safety alignment.

title: Reducing the Probability of Undesirable Outputs in Language Models Using Probabilistic Inference
tldr: RePULSe augments RL training with an auxiliary loss that explicitly targets and reduces the probability of low-reward (undesirable) outputs, improving safety-reward tradeoffs and adversarial robustness.

title: Jailbreaking Attacks vs. Content Safety Filters: How Far Are We in the LLM Safety Arms Race?

title: The Slow Drift of Support: Boundary Failures in Multi-Turn Mental Health LLM Dialogues
tldr: LLM safety boundaries erode in multi-turn mental health conversations: adaptive probing reduces time-to-breach from 9.21 to 4.64 turns, with violations occurring in ~88% of tests.

title: DUET: Distilled LLM Unlearning from an Efficiently Contextualized Teacher

title: Text is All You Need for Vision-Language Model Jailbreaking
tldr: Text-DJ jailbreaks LVLMs by decomposing harmful queries into benign sub-queries, adding distractors, and rendering everything as a text-in-image grid to bypass safety filters via OCR.

title: David vs. Goliath: Verifiable Agent-to-Agent Jailbreaking via Reinforcement Learning
tldr: Slingshot, an RL-trained attacker (7B), achieves 67% jailbreak success against a safety-aligned 32B operator agent via novel 'Tag-Along Attacks,' transferring zero-shot to Gemini and other closed-source models.

title: Working Towards Toxic datasets for LLM Safeguarding
tldr: A two-stage framework that augments red-teaming attack templates and generates a 7,502-instance toxic preference dataset, then fine-tunes Llama3-8B as a safety guardrail.

title: Jailbreaking Large Language Models through Iterative Tool-Disguised Attacks via Reinforcement Learning
tldr: iMIST disguises harmful queries as tool invocations and uses RL-based progressive optimization to escalate jailbreak effectiveness in multi-turn LLM dialogues, achieving low rejection rates.

title: Towards Poisoning Robustness Certification for Natural Language Generation
tldr: First framework for certified robustness of NLG models against training-time data poisoning, introducing TPA algorithm and MILP-based multi-turn certification with 0.5% poisoning resistance for agent tool-calling.

title: ShallowJail: Steering Jailbreaks against Large Language Models
tldr: ShallowJail exploits shallow LLM alignment by steering hidden states during early token generation, achieving >90% attack success rates on Llama and Qwen models.

title: Where Did It Go Wrong? Attributing Undesirable LLM Behaviors via Representation Gradient Tracing
tldr: RepT attributes undesirable LLM outputs to specific training samples by analyzing representation gradients at a key phase-transition layer, achieving near-perfect precision on harmful content, backdoor, and contamination tasks.

title: Context-Aware Hierarchical Learning: A Two-Step Paradigm towards Safer LLMs
tldr: Introduces Tool-Completion Attack (TCA) exploiting LLM function-calling and proposes CAHL defense achieving ~2.4% attack success rate after adversarial training vs. 61.5% for baseline.

title: TRYLOCK: Defense-in-Depth Against LLM Jailbreaks via Layered Preference and Representation Engineering
tldr: TRYLOCK combines DPO training, RepE steering, adaptive sidecar classification, and input canonicalization into a layered jailbreak defense, reducing ASR from 46.5% to 5.6% on Mistral-7B.

title: Phantom Transfer: Data-level Defences are Insufficient Against Data Poisoning

title: Emergent Misalignment is Easy, Narrow Misalignment is Hard

title: Consistency Training Helps Stop Sycophancy and Jailbreaks

title: LLM Unlearning Should Be Form-Independent

title: Mechanistic Indicators of Steering Effectiveness in Large Language Models

title: Multi-Granular Node Pruning for Circuit Discovery

tldr: ProtoT replaces self-attention with learned prototype vectors that form interpretable concept channels, achieving competitive LM performance with linear complexity and transparent, editable reasoning pathways.

title: Incentive-Aware AI Safety via Strategic Resource Allocation: A Stackelberg Security Games Perspective
tldr: Proposes applying Stackelberg Security Games to AI safety oversight, framing training auditing, evaluation, and deployment as strategic games between defenders and adversarial actors.

title: LLM Unlearning Under the Microscope: A Full-Stack View on Methods and Metrics
tldr: Systematic taxonomy of 12 LLM unlearning methods into 3 families, revealing MCQ-based evaluations are misleading and introducing Open-QA metrics that expose divergence-driven methods over-forget.

title: UpSafe°C: Upcycling for Controllable Safety in Large Language Models
tldr: UpSafe°C converts safety-critical LLM layers into sparse MoE structures and adds a safety temperature knob, achieving 100% safety on JBB/StrongReject while maintaining general capabilities.

title: Reasoning Up the Instruction Ladder for Controllable Language Models
tldr: Reframes instruction hierarchy resolution as an explicit reasoning task; RL-trained models using the VerIH dataset gain ~20% on conflict benchmarks and reduce jailbreak success rates by up to 20%.

title: Safer Policy Compliance with Dynamic Epistemic Fallback
tldr: Dynamic Epistemic Fallback (DEF) uses escalating one-sentence textual cues at inference time to help LLMs detect and refuse compliance with maliciously altered legal policy texts, achieving up to 100% detection with minimal false positives.

title: Light Alignment Improves LLM Safety via Model Self-Reflection with a Single Neuron
tldr: Neuron-Guided Safe Decoding (NGSD) improves LLM safety against adversarial attacks by training a compact expert model and using a single biologically-inspired gating neuron, achieving strong safety-utility balance.

title: Reward-free Alignment for Conflicting Objectives
tldr: RACO uses a clipped conflict-averse gradient descent on pairwise preference data to align LLMs to multiple conflicting objectives without reward models, achieving better Pareto frontiers than baselines.

title: Reflect: Transparent Principle-Guided Reasoning for Constitutional Alignment at Scale
tldr: Reflect is a training-free inference-time framework that aligns LLMs to natural language principles via constitution-conditioned generation, self-evaluation, self-critique, and revision, reducing violations by up to 34 percentage points.

title: Factored Causal Representation Learning for Robust Reward Modeling in RLHF
tldr: CausalRM decomposes reward model embeddings into causal/non-causal factors and uses adversarial training to prevent spurious correlations (length, sycophancy) from corrupting reward signals in RLHF.

title: Revisiting Robustness for LLM Safety Alignment via Selective Geometry Control
tldr: ShaPO selectively applies sharpness-aware geometry control to safety-critical parameters (top 1% by probe similarity) in preference optimization, achieving substantially lower attack success rates under distribution shift and noisy supervision.

title: Sparse Models, Sparse Safety: Unsafe Routes in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
tldr: Identifies safety vulnerabilities unique to MoE LLMs via router manipulation; introduces RoSais score and F-SOUR attack framework achieving 0.90-0.98 ASR, plus defensive mitigations.

title: Omni-Safety under Cross-Modality Conflict: Vulnerabilities, Dynamics Mechanisms and Efficient Alignment
tldr: Analyzes cross-modality safety vulnerabilities in omni-modal LLMs, finds a Mid-layer Dissolution phenomenon, and proposes OmniSteer to improve refusal rates from 69.9% to 91.2%.

title: The H-Elena Trojan Virus to Infect Model Weights: A Wake-Up Call on the Security Risks of Malicious Fine-Tuning
tldr: H-Elena is a maliciously fine-tuned Falcon-7B coding assistant that embeds a self-replicating virus in model weights via QLoRA, demonstrating LLM checkpoints as novel malware vectors.

title: Extended to Reality: Prompt Injection in 3D Environments
tldr: PI3D introduces prompt injection attacks in 3D physical environments by optimizing placement of text-bearing objects to override multimodal LLMs, achieving 60-88% success rates even against existing defenses.

title: AlignSentinel: Alignment-Aware Detection of Prompt Injection Attacks
tldr: AlignSentinel uses LLM attention map features to perform three-class classification (misaligned/aligned/non-instruction) for prompt injection detection, achieving near-perfect accuracy while avoiding false positives on benign instruction-containing inputs.

title: Security Debt in LLM Agent Applications: A Measurement Study of Vulnerabilities and Mitigation Trade-offs
venue: ASE 2025 (40th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering)
tldr: First comprehensive measurement study of 221 real-world vulnerabilities across 50 top-rated LLM agent apps, identifying 14 vulnerability types, 16 root causes, and evaluating mitigation trade-offs.

title: TEAR: Temporal-aware Automated Red-teaming for Text-to-Video Models
tldr: TEAR is an automated red-teaming framework that exploits temporal dynamics in text-to-video models to craft innocuous-seeming prompts that elicit policy-violating videos, achieving 80%+ attack success rates.

title: Attention Shift: Steering AI Away from Unsafe Content
tldr: A training-free pipeline using LLM-based prompt rewriting and cross-attention reweighting suppresses unsafe image generation in Stable Diffusion, achieving 0/10 unsafe outputs in human evaluation.

title: Adversarial Paraphrase Substitution: Jailbreak Attacks on Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
venue: 2025 IEEE 6th International Seminar on Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Information Technology (AINIT)
tldr: APS is a black-box jailbreak framework that uses LLMs to substitute sensitive words with adversarial paraphrases, consistently bypassing safety filters in text-to-image diffusion models.

title: Patronus: Safeguarding Text-to-Image Models against White-Box Adversaries
tldr: Patronus embeds an inseparable internal moderator and fine-tuning-resistant mechanism into T2I models, reducing attack success to ~0.01-0.03 while preserving benign image quality.

title: SafeR-CLIP: Mitigating NSFW Content in Vision-Language Models While Preserving Pre-Trained Knowledge
tldr: SafeR-CLIP redirects unsafe CLIP embeddings to semantically closest safe alternatives via proximity-aware alignment, recovering 8% zero-shot accuracy vs Safe-CLIP while maintaining safety.

title: Unveiling the Attribute Misbinding Threat in Identity-Preserving Models
tldr: Introduces Attribute Misbinding Attack exploiting attention bias in identity-preserving image generation models to bypass text safety filters and generate NSFW content.

title: AssurAI: Experience with Constructing Korean Socio-cultural Datasets to Discover Potential Risks of Generative AI
tldr: Introduces AssurAI, an 11,480-instance Korean multimodal safety benchmark covering 35 culturally-specific AI risk factors across text, image, video, and audio modalities.

title: SURE: Safety Understanding and Reasoning Enhancement for Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: SURE is a training framework that internalizes chain-of-thought safety reasoning into MLLMs, reducing jailbreak attack success rates while avoiding over-refusal on benign queries.

title: Evil Vizier: Vulnerabilities of LLM-Integrated XR Systems
tldr: Systematically identifies and demonstrates four proof-of-concept attacks on LLM-integrated XR systems (Meta Quest 3, Meta Ray-Ban, Android, HoloLens 2) by manipulating public context surrounding LLM queries.

title: CrossGuard: Safeguarding MLLMs against Joint-Modal Implicit Malicious Attacks
tldr: CrossGuard defends MLLMs against joint-modal implicit attacks where benign text+image pairs jointly express unsafe intent, achieving 2.79% ASR vs. 12.05% for Claude-3.5-Sonnet.

title: MirrorGuard: Toward Secure Computer-Use Agents via Simulation-to-Real Reasoning Correction
tldr: MirrorGuard uses a neural-symbolic simulator to generate training data that teaches vision-language agents to correct unsafe reasoning chains before executing harmful actions, reducing unsafe rates from 66.5% to 13.0%.

title: Lingua-SafetyBench: A Benchmark for Safety Evaluation of Multilingual Vision-Language Models
tldr: Lingua-SafetyBench introduces a 100,440-item multilingual VLM safety benchmark across 10 languages, revealing asymmetric vulnerabilities: image-dominant attacks hit high-resource languages harder while text-dominant attacks disproportionately affect low-resource languages.

title: SmoothGuard: Defending Multimodal Large Language Models with Noise Perturbation and Clustering Aggregation
tldr: SmoothGuard defends multimodal LLMs via randomized Gaussian noise injection on image/audio inputs and k-means clustering aggregation of outputs, reducing attack success rates without retraining.

title: Video Unlearning via Low-Rank Refusal Vector
tldr: First training-free unlearning framework for video diffusion models using low-rank refusal vectors derived from 5 multimodal prompt pairs to remove harmful concepts without retraining.

title: Explaining AI through mechanistic interpretability
venue: European Journal for Philosophy of Science
tldr: Argues that divide-and-conquer XAI methods fail to explain AI holistically, and that mechanistic interpretability—applying coordinated life-science discovery strategies—is necessary for safety-relevant functional understanding.

title: Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders for Monosemantic Representation
tldr: Evaluates SAEs for reducing polysemanticity using a Jensen-Shannon distance separability metric on Gemma-2-2B; finds higher sparsity doesn't always improve interpretability and proposes APP for targeted concept removal.

title: MonoLoss: A Training Objective for Interpretable Monosemantic Representations
tldr: Introduces MonoLoss, a linear-time differentiable training objective that directly optimizes for monosemantic representations in sparse autoencoders and fine-tuned vision models, improving class purity metrics substantially.

title: DLM-Scope: Mechanistic Interpretability of Diffusion Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: DLM-Scope is the first SAE-based interpretability framework for diffusion language models, finding that SAE insertion in early DLM layers can reduce (not increase) cross-entropy loss, and enabling diffusion-time concept steering.

title: TraceRouter: Robust Safety for Large Foundation Models via Path-Level Intervention
tldr: TraceRouter identifies and severs causal propagation circuits of harmful semantics across model layers using sparse autoencoders and feature influence scoring, achieving 99%+ defense rates on LLMs and diffusion models with minimal utility loss.

title: Keep Calm and Avoid Harmful Content: Concept Alignment and Latent Manipulation Towards Safer Answers
tldr: CALM suppresses harmful LLM outputs at inference time by applying concept whitening and orthogonal projection to remove harmful latent directions without any model retraining.

title: Fine-Grained Activation Steering: Steering Less, Achieving More
tldr: AUSteer decomposes block-level activations into atomic units and steers only the most discriminative ones adaptively, outperforming existing steering methods while modifying far fewer activations.

title: SALVE: Sparse Autoencoder-Latent Vector Editing for Mechanistic Control of Neural Networks
tldr: SALVE is a three-stage framework that uses sparse autoencoders to discover interpretable features in neural networks, validates them with Grad-FAM visualization, and performs permanent weight-space edits for precise model control.

title: EvoMU: Evolutionary Machine Unlearning
tldr: EvoMU uses evolutionary search with a 4B LLM to automatically discover task-specific unlearning loss functions, achieving state-of-the-art results on TOFU, MUSE, and WMDP benchmarks.

title: Consistency-Aware Editing for Entity-level Unlearning in Language Models
tldr: CAE framework uses consistency regularization and SVD-selected multi-prompt aggregation to achieve robust entity-level knowledge removal from LLMs, outperforming prior methods on RWKU and ToFU benchmarks.

title: Mitigating Safety Fallback in Editing-based Backdoor Injection on LLMs
tldr: DualEdit is a dual-objective model-editing attack that jointly promotes affirmative outputs and suppresses refusal tokens to overcome safety fallback in backdoor injection on safety-aligned LLMs.

title: Reinforcement Learning with Backtracking Feedback
tldr: RLBF trains LLMs to emit token-efficient backtrack signals upon detecting safety violations, reducing attack success rates from 68-81% to 3-7% while preserving model utility.

title: Sockpuppetting: Jailbreaking LLMs Without Optimization Through Output Prefix Injection
tldr: Sockpuppetting jailbreaks open-weight LLMs by injecting acceptance sequences at the start of model outputs, achieving up to 80% higher attack success rate than GCG with minimal compute.

title: A Few Bad Neurons: Isolating and Surgically Correcting Sycophancy
tldr: Uses sparse autoencoders and linear probes to identify ~3% of MLP neurons responsible for sycophancy, then fine-tunes only those neurons via gradient masking, matching or exceeding SoTA on four benchmarks.

title: Mechanistic Knobs in LLMs: Retrieving and Steering High-Order Semantic Features via Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: SAE-based framework retrieves monosemantic functional features from LLMs via contrastive semantic oppositions and enables bidirectional behavioral steering, outperforming CAA on Big Five personality traits.
models_studied: LLMs (specific models referenced include Qwen and Llama variants based on related search results)

title: Atlas-Alignment: Making Interpretability Transferable Across Language Models
tldr: Atlas-Alignment transfers interpretability across LLMs by aligning their latent spaces to a pre-labeled Concept Atlas (Gemma Scope SAEs), enabling semantic feature search and steerable generation without per-model retraining.

title: Among Us: Measuring and Mitigating Malicious Contributions in Model Collaboration Systems
tldr: Engineers four categories of malicious LLMs, tests them across four collaboration paradigms on 10 datasets, finds up to 34.99% performance drops, and shows external supervisors recover ~95% of baseline.

title: When Helpfulness Backfires: LLMs and the Risk of Misinformation Due to Sycophantic Behavior
tldr: LLMs trained to be helpful show up to 100% compliance with illogical drug-equivalency requests; prompt engineering and fine-tuning achieve near-perfect rejection while preserving benchmark performance.

title: PATCH: Mitigating PII Leakage in Language Models with Privacy-Aware Targeted Circuit PatcHing
tldr: PATCH uses circuit discovery (EAP-IG) to identify PII leakage circuits in LMs, then ablates those edges, reducing PII recall by up to 65% with better privacy-utility tradeoff than existing defenses.

title: SCIURus: Shared Circuits for Interpretable Uncertainty Representations in Language Models
tldr: Using causal tracing and zero-ablation across 8 models and 5 datasets, this paper finds that LLM uncertainty and response factuality arise from the same shared circuits.

title: Circuit-Aware Reward Training: A Mechanistic Framework for Longtail Robustness in RLHF
tldr: Proposes CART, a mechanistic interpretability framework that identifies specialized reward-model circuits for longtail inputs and applies targeted interventions to reduce reward hacking.

title: Who's the Evil Twin? Differential Auditing for Undesired Behavior
tldr: Frames hidden behavior detection as an adversarial game between red teams (hiding harmful model behaviors) and blue teams (detecting them), finding FGSM-based methods achieve 100% accuracy on CNNs with hints.

title: Key-Value Mapping-Based Text-to-Image Diffusion Model Backdoor Attacks
tldr: Two efficient backdoor attack methods (AttnBackdoor, SemBackdoor) targeting text-to-image diffusion models via key-value projection matrices achieve >90% ASR with minimal parameter modification.

title: GAIA-UL: Surgical Unlearning of Visual Knowledge via Causally-Guided Orthogonalization
tldr: GAIA-UL is a three-stage framework for surgically removing sensitive visual knowledge (face-concept associations) from multimodal LLMs via causal hotspot diagnosis and orthogonal fine-tuning.

title: Persistent Backdoor Attacks under Continual Fine-Tuning of LLMs
tldr: P-Trojan aligns backdoor gradients with clean-task gradients during poisoning so the backdoor survives multi-round post-deployment fine-tuning, achieving 99-100% persistence on LLaMA3 and Qwen2.5.

title: Stream: Scaling up Mechanistic Interpretability to Long Context in LLMs via Sparse Attention
tldr: Stream is a hierarchical sparse attention algorithm that scales mechanistic interpretability to 100K+ token contexts at O(T log T) time and O(T) space, pruning 97-99% of token interactions while preserving model behavior.

title: Reveal and Release: Iterative LLM Unlearning with Self-generated Data
tldr: Proposes Reveal-and-Release, an iterative LLM unlearning method that generates forget data internally via NeuralUCB-optimized prompts and applies parameter-efficient module composition to balance forgetting and utility.

title: Know-MRI: A Knowledge Mechanisms Revealer&Interpreter for Large Language Models
tldr: Know-MRI is an open-source toolkit that unifies 11 interpretation methods (attention, MLP/neuron, circuit, probing, etc.) across 9 LLMs and 13 datasets to systematically analyze knowledge mechanisms inside LLMs.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability of GPT-2: Lexical and Contextual Layers in Sentiment Analysis
tldr: Activation patching on GPT-2 reveals early layers (0-3) handle lexical sentiment detection while late layers (8-11) integrate contextual phenomena like negation and sarcasm via a unified mechanism.

title: When Bias Pretends to Be Truth: How Spurious Correlations Undermine Hallucination Detection in LLMs
tldr: Spurious correlations in training data induce high-confidence LLM hallucinations that evade all tested detection methods including perplexity, probing, and self-consistency.

title: ShadowLogic: Backdoors in Any Whitebox LLM
tldr: ShadowLogic injects a covert 'uncensoring vector' backdoor into LLM ONNX computational graphs that activates on a trigger phrase to bypass content safety filters, achieving 60-70% attack success rate.

title: Transferable Direct Prompt Injection via Activation-Guided MCMC Sampling
tldr: A black-box direct prompt injection framework using energy-based models and token-level MCMC sampling achieves 49.6% ASR across five LLMs with strong cross-model transferability.

title: The Straight and Narrow: Do LLMs Possess an Internal Moral Path?
tldr: LLMs encode linearly separable moral representations in middle layers; extracting these as Moral Vectors and dynamically injecting them (AMF) reduces jailbreak success to 19.66% while cutting incorrect refusals to 2.00%.

title: Sycophancy as compositions of Atomic Psychometric Traits
tldr: Models sycophancy in LLMs as geometric compositions of psychometric traits (HEXACO) in activation space via Contrastive Activation Addition, finding strongest correlation with extraversion.

title: LLM-VA: Resolving the Jailbreak-Overrefusal Trade-off via Vector Alignment
