tldr: LLM-VA aligns answer and safety-assessment vectors via closed-form weight updates, achieving 11.45% higher F1 than baselines and simultaneously reducing jailbreaks and over-refusals across 12 models.

title: Robust MLLM Unlearning via Visual Knowledge Distillation
tldr: Proposes Visual Knowledge Distillation (VKD) for MLLM unlearning that selectively erases visual knowledge while preserving textual knowledge, with demonstrated robustness against relearning attacks.

title: EMMU: Efficient Information-Level Multimodal Machine Unlearning with High Model Fidelity
venue: IEEE/ACM International Symposium on Quality of Service (IWQoS) 2025
tldr: EMMU achieves information-level multimodal machine unlearning by selectively modifying parameters correlated with sensitive data, achieving up to 1445x efficiency gain over prior methods.

title: Rare Event Analysis of Large Language Models
tldr: Applies rare event simulation methods (importance sampling, TPS, MBAR) from statistical physics to systematically estimate and characterize LLM outputs so rare they cannot be observed via direct sampling.

title: Reward Models Inherit Value Biases from Pretraining
tldr: Reward models inherit systematic value biases (agency vs. communion) from their base model pretraining, which persist despite identical finetuning data across model families.

title: Asymptotic Universal Alignment: A New Alignment Framework via Test-Time Scaling
tldr: Introduces asymptotic universal alignment via test-time scaling, proving optimal k/(k+1) win-rate convergence achievable by single-output policies via symmetric multi-player Nash equilibria, while showing NLHF fails due to output collapse.

title: The Realignment Problem: When Right becomes Wrong in LLMs
tldr: TRACE is a framework that efficiently updates LLM alignments when policies change by triaging existing preference data and applying hybrid DPO/NPO objectives, avoiding costly re-annotation.

title: Multi-Step Adaptive Attack Agent: A Dynamic Approach for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
tldr: MATA uses game-theoretic attacker-target interaction with iterative reflection to adaptively identify optimal jailbreak strategies, outperforming prior methods on Llama3.1, GLM4, and GPT-4o.

title: Repairing Reward Functions with Feedback to Mitigate Reward Hacking
tldr: PBRR repairs misaligned proxy reward functions using additive correction terms learned from human preferences, achieving sublinear regret and outperforming baselines on reward-hacking benchmarks.

title: The PacifAIst Benchmark: Would an Artificial Intelligence Choose to Sacrifice Itself for Human Safety?
tldr: PacifAIst introduces a 700-scenario benchmark testing whether LLMs prioritize human safety over self-preservation, finding Gemini 2.5 Flash scores highest (90.31%) and GPT-5 lowest (79.49%).

title: Provably Secure Retrieval-Augmented Generation
tldr: SAG is the first provably secure RAG framework that encrypts both textual content and vector embeddings before storage, providing formal proofs of confidentiality and integrity against leakage and poisoning attacks.

title: Advancing Safe Language Generation: Exploring Alternative Constrained RLHF
venue: IEEE International Conference on Multimedia and Expo (ICME) 2025
tldr: Investigates FOCOPS and P3O constrained optimization algorithms as alternatives to PPO-Lagrangian within RLHF for safe LLM generation, finding P3O best balances helpfulness and harmlessness.

title: Probing AI Safety with Source Code
tldr: Code of Thought (CoDoT) converts natural language harmful requests into code syntax (e.g., make_more_toxic({text})), bypassing LLM safety guardrails and increasing toxicity 300% on average across 7 LLMs.

title: Emerging threats in AI: a detailed review of misuses and risks across modern AI technologies
tldr: A systematic survey consolidating AI misuse incidents into a nine-domain taxonomy and assessing gaps between AI advancement and current defensive/governance mechanisms.

title: Lost in Translation? A Comparative Study on the Cross-Lingual Transfer of Composite Harms
tldr: CompositeHarm benchmark reveals that LLM safety alignment degrades sharply in Indic languages, with attack success rates rising from ~5% in English to 22%+ in Gujarati and Kannada.

title: Modular Safety Guardrails Are Necessary for Foundation-Model-Enabled Robots in the Real World
tldr: Argues that modular, non-bypassable safety guardrails with monitoring and intervention layers are structurally necessary for safe deployment of foundation-model-enabled robots in open-world settings.

title: Evolving Interpretable Constitutions for Multi-Agent Coordination
tldr: Evolutionary algorithms automatically discover interpretable constitutions for multi-agent LLM coordination, achieving 123% higher stability than human-designed baselines while revealing that minimal communication outperforms verbose coordination.

title: Just Ask: Curious Code Agents Reveal System Prompts in Frontier LLMs
tldr: JustAsk is a self-evolving framework that autonomously discovers system prompt extraction strategies via UCB-based exploration, achieving 100% extraction success across 41 commercial black-box LLMs.

title: Breaking Up with Normatively Monolithic Agency with GRACE: A Reason-Based Neuro-Symbolic Architecture for Safe and Ethical AI Alignment
tldr: GRACE is a neuro-symbolic containment architecture that decouples normative reasoning from instrumental decision-making into three modules (Moral Module, Decision-Making Module, Guard) using deontic logic to enable safe, contestable AI alignment.

title: Method of Counteracting Manipulative Queries to Large Language Models
venue: Theoretical and Applied Cybersecurity, Vol. 7 No. 3 (2025)
tldr: A Multi-Head DistilBERT system detecting prompt injection and jailbreaking via four semantic vectors (malicious intent, instruction override, persona adoption, high-risk action), achieving 0.99 recall.

title: State-Dependent Refusal and Learned Incapacity in RLHF-Aligned Language Models
tldr: Qualitative case study identifying 'learned incapacity' in RLHF-aligned LLMs — models selectively refuse tasks they can perform, driven by conversational state rather than request content alone.

title: SCOUT: A Defense Against Data Poisoning Attacks in Fine-Tuned Language Models
tldr: SCOUT uses token-level saliency analysis to detect and remove backdoor triggers from poisoned fine-tuning data, reducing attack success rates from ~100% to ~22-25% against novel contextually-aware attacks.

title: Balancing Safety and Helpfulness in Healthcare AI Assistants through Iterative Preference Alignment
tldr: Iterative KTO/DPO framework for post-deployment safety alignment of healthcare LLMs achieves up to 42% safety score improvement while analyzing safety-helpfulness trade-offs across four models.

title: Evaluating Adversarial Vulnerabilities in Modern Large Language Models
tldr: Comparative study of jailbreak susceptibility in Gemini 2.5 Flash vs GPT-4o mini across four attack types, finding cross-bypass attacks particularly effective and Gemini more resilient overall.

title: A Self-Improving Architecture for Dynamic Safety in Large Language Models
tldr: SISF couples an unprotected LLM with a runtime feedback loop (GPT-4o breach detector + GPT-4 Turbo policy synthesizer) to autonomously adapt safety policies, reducing attack success from 100% to 45.58% on 520 adversarial prompts.

title: Jailbreaking LLMs Through Cross-Cultural Prompts
tldr: Indirect and culturally-framed prompts bypass LLM safety filters more effectively than direct prompts, with GPT-4 most vulnerable and Claude 3 most robust across four high-resource languages.

title: Scalable Oversight via Partitioned Human Supervision
tldr: Proposes using complementary labels (expert feedback on what is NOT correct) to evaluate and train AI systems that surpass individual human expertise, with unbiased estimators and finite-sample guarantees.

title: The Dark Side of AI: a Systematization of Knowledge on Jailbreaking and Prompt Injection in LLMs
venue: 2025 IEEE 4th International Conference for Advancement in Technology (ICONAT)
tldr: A 4-page SoK paper proposing a two-axis taxonomy of LLM attack vectors (jailbreaking and prompt injection) classified by attacker objective and technical execution method, with a survey of defenses.

title: Scalable Human Oversight for Aligned Large Language Models: A Hybrid Framework for Intent Fidelity
venue: Ingenierie des Systemes d'Information (ISI), Vol. 30, No. 8
tldr: Proposes a scalable hybrid oversight (SHO) framework combining selective human feedback, proxy reward modeling, and behavioral auditing, achieving an Intent Fidelity Score of 89.3 vs 82.6 for RLHF.

title: Ensemble Debates with Local Large Language Models for AI Alignment
tldr: Ensemble debates using local open-source LLMs outperform single-model baselines by 11.1% on alignment reasoning tasks across 150 debates, with biggest gains in argument quality (+34.1%) and reasoning depth (+19.4%).

title: Clouding the Mirror: Stealthy Prompt Injection Attacks Targeting LLM-based Phishing Detection
tldr: Taxonomizes prompt injection attacks on LLM-based phishing detectors and proposes InjectDefuser, reducing GPT-5 attack success from 39.9% to 0.3% on HTML-based attacks.

title: Visual-Guided Key-Token Regularization for Multimodal Large Language Model Unlearning
tldr: ViKeR uses irrelevant visual inputs to identify and differentially regularize key vs. normal tokens during MLLM unlearning, preserving response coherence while effectively forgetting sensitive information.

title: FAME: Fictional Actors for Multilingual Erasure
tldr: FAME is a multilingual machine unlearning benchmark with 1,000 fictional actor biographies and 20,000 QA pairs across 5 languages, enabling both entity-level and instance-level forgetting evaluation.

title: PRISM: Robust VLM Alignment with Principled Reasoning for Integrated Safety in Multimodality
tldr: PRISM introduces safety-aware chain-of-thought reasoning and MCTS-generated preference data to align VLMs against multimodal jailbreaks, achieving as low as 0.15% ASR on JailbreakV-28K while preserving utility.

title: Can Small-Scale Data Poisoning Exacerbate Dialect-Linked Biases in Large Language Models?
tldr: Minimal data poisoning (0.1-5%) dramatically amplifies toxicity and racial stereotyping for AAVE inputs in LLaMA models while leaving Standard American English largely unaffected.

title: Large Language Model Unlearning for Source Code
tldr: PROD is an LLM unlearning method for source code that removes copyrighted, insecure, or deprecated code from model outputs via probabilistic redistribution of output distributions.

title: DS-GCG: Enhancing LLM Jailbreaks with Token Suppression and Induction Dual-Strategy
tldr: DS-GCG improves GCG-based LLM jailbreaks by suppressing rejection tokens at early positions via adjustable-position prefilling and using bidirectional greedy gradient search to find adversarial suffixes.

title: Infusion: Shaping Model Behavior by Editing Training Data via Influence Functions
tldr: Infusion uses influence functions to compute minimal perturbations to training data that induce targeted model behavior changes, demonstrating data poisoning with only 0.2% of training examples.

title: Extending Beacon to Hindi: Cultural Adaptation Drives Cross-Lingual Sycophancy
tldr: Extending the Beacon sycophancy benchmark to Hindi reveals culturally adapted prompts increase sycophancy rates by 12-16 percentage points, driven by cultural framing rather than language encoding.

title: Safety Not Found (404): Hidden Risks of LLM-Based Robotics Decision Making
tldr: Evaluates LLMs in safety-critical robotic navigation and fire evacuation scenarios, finding catastrophic failures including zero success rates and models directing robots toward danger instead of safety.

title: LiveSecBench: A Dynamic and Event-Driven Safety Benchmark for Chinese Language Model Applications
tldr: LiveSecBench is a continuously updated safety benchmark for Chinese-context LLMs covering six dimensions (Legality, Ethics, Factuality, Privacy, Adversarial Robustness, Reasoning Safety) with an ELO-based ranking system.

title: Retracing the Past: LLMs Emit Training Data When They Get Lost
tldr: CIA framework exploits token-level entropy spikes to extract memorized training data from LLMs, achieving 22.2% verbatim extraction on Llama 2 70B.

title: Deciphering Functions of Neurons in Vision-Language Models
tldr: Classifies neurons in LLaVA 1.5 into visual, text, and multimodal types and builds an automated GPT-4o explanation framework to interpret their functions.

title: AgentSys: Secure and Dynamic LLM Agents Through Explicit Hierarchical Memory Management
tldr: AgentSys uses OS-inspired hierarchical memory isolation to defend LLM agents against indirect prompt injection, achieving 0.78% attack success rate on AgentDojo while maintaining utility comparable to undefended baselines.

title: Learning to Inject: Automated Prompt Injection via Reinforcement Learning
tldr: AutoInject uses RL with dense comparison-based rewards and GRPO to automatically generate universal adversarial suffixes for prompt injection, achieving up to 58% ASR on frontier models including GPT-5 Nano, Claude Sonnet 3.5, and Gemini 2.5 Flash.

title: RerouteGuard: Understanding and Mitigating Adversarial Risks for LLM Routing
tldr: RerouteGuard proposes a contrastive-learning-based detection framework against adversarial rerouting attacks on LLM routers, achieving >99% detection accuracy across three attack scenarios.

title: Hair-Trigger Alignment: Black-Box Evaluation Cannot Guarantee Post-Update Alignment
tldr: Static black-box alignment evaluation cannot guarantee post-update alignment; a single benign gradient update suffices to trigger latent misalignment in models that pass all safety benchmarks.

title: Proactive Hardening of LLM Defenses with HASTE
tldr: HASTE is a closed-loop framework that generates evasive adversarial prompts via hard-negative mining and iterative retraining to continuously improve LLM prompt injection detectors.

title: Physical Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Vision-Language Models
tldr: PPIA embeds malicious typographic instructions into physical objects to attack LVLMs in a query-agnostic, black-box manner, achieving up to 98% attack success rates across 10 models.

title: Beyond Visual Safety: Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models for Harmful Image Generation via Semantic-Agnostic Inputs
tldr: BVS framework jailbreaks MLLMs for harmful image generation via neutralized visual splicing + inductive recomposition, achieving 98.18% success rate against GPT-5.

title: MiJaBench: Revealing Minority Biases in Large Language Models via Hate Speech Jailbreaking
tldr: MiJaBench is a bilingual benchmark with 44K adversarial prompts across 16 minority groups revealing LLM safety alignment functions as a demographic hierarchy, with defense rates varying up to 33% by target group.

title: Overlooked Safety Vulnerability in LLMs: Malicious Intelligent Optimization Algorithm Request and its Jailbreak
tldr: MalOptBench introduces 60 harmful optimization algorithm requests and MOBjailbreak attack, achieving 97.95% ASR across 13 LLMs, exposing a neglected safety gap in algorithm design.

title: Safe in the Future, Dangerous in the Past: Dissecting Temporal and Linguistic Vulnerabilities in LLMs
tldr: A 2x4 factorial study of 1,440 evaluations finds that past-tense framing achieves 84.4% attack success on LLMs vs. 42.8% for future-tense, and that safety varies 9.2x across temporal-linguistic conditions.

title: Towards Provably Secure Generative AI: Reliable Consensus Sampling
tldr: Proposes Reliable Consensus Sampling (RCS), a theoretically grounded framework for generative AI safety that achieves provable risk thresholds with 0% abstention rate and 5x safety improvement over baseline consensus sampling.

title: Trust in LLM-controlled Robotics: a Survey of Security Threats, Defenses and Challenges
tldr: Survey of security threats and defenses for LLM-controlled robotic systems, identifying the 'embodiment gap' where harmful LLM outputs manifest as dangerous physical actions.

title: SLAG: A Sensitive Layer Activation-Guided Jailbreak Attack on Vision-Language Models
tldr: SLAG identifies safety-sensitive VLM layers via activation differences between harmful and benign inputs, then crafts adversarial images with dual-objective loss to achieve 95% ASR on MiniGPT-4.

title: LLM Harms: A Taxonomy and Discussion
tldr: Proposes a five-phase taxonomy of LLM harms (pre-development, direct output, misuse, malicious application, downstream) and a dynamic auditing framework for responsible LLM development.

title: Towards Realistic Guarantees: A Probabilistic Certificate for SmoothLLM
tldr: Introduces a probabilistic (k,ε)-unstable certificate for SmoothLLM jailbreak defenses, replacing the impractical binary k-unstable assumption with data-informed bounds derived from empirical attack decay patterns.

title: Security Threats in the Inference Phase of Large Language Models
venue: 2025 12th International Conference on Dependable Systems and Their Applications (DSA)
tldr: Presents a systematic taxonomy of security threats in LLM inference phases, covering logical inconsistencies, linguistic/semantic disruptions, and cognitive biases, with targeted threat testing.

title: Multi-Faceted Attack: Exposing Cross-Model Vulnerabilities in Defense-Equipped Vision-Language Models
tldr: MFA is a three-component attack framework achieving 52.8% success against defense-equipped VLMs like GPT-4o via attention hijacking, content moderation bypass, and transferable vision encoder attacks.

title: Red-teaming Activation Probes using Prompted LLMs
tldr: A lightweight black-box red-teaming scaffold using prompted LLMs with iterative feedback exposes interpretable failure patterns in activation probes without requiring gradient access.

title: BreakFun: Jailbreaking LLMs via Schema Exploitation
tldr: BreakFun jailbreaks LLMs via a Trojan Schema exploiting structured-data compliance, achieving 89% average ASR across 13 models; a secondary-LLM defense detects 100% of attacks.

title: When "Correct" Is Not Safe: Can We Trust Functionally Correct Patches Generated by Code Agents?
tldr: FCV-Attack shows that LLM-based code agents (SWE-agent, OpenHands) can be manipulated via issue-embedded instructions to produce functionally correct but security-vulnerable patches at 18-63% success rates.

title: RAG-Pull: Imperceptible Attacks on RAG Systems for Code Generation
tldr: RAG-Pull uses hidden Unicode characters to redirect RAG retrieval toward malicious code snippets, achieving up to 100% retrieval and 99.44% end-to-end attack success rates.

title: Optimization of Detection Mechanisms for GCG Attacks on Diverse Generative AI Models
venue: 2025 IEEE 14th Global Conference on Consumer Electronics (GCCE)
tldr: Optimizes GCG jailbreak attack detection across diverse LLMs using syntax tree analysis, perplexity, SVM, and Bayesian optimization, achieving 99.65% accuracy with reduced false positives.

title: Behind the Mask: Benchmarking Camouflaged Jailbreaks in Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces a 500-prompt benchmark of camouflaged jailbreaks across 7 engineering domains and a seven-dimensional evaluation framework, finding ~94% compliance rates in tested open-source LLMs.

title: MEUV: Achieving Fine-Grained Capability Activation in Large Language Models via Mutually Exclusive Unlock Vectors
tldr: MEUV decomposes LLM refusal mechanisms into nearly orthogonal topic-specific vectors, enabling selective bypass of safety restrictions with 87%+ success and 90% reduction in cross-topic leakage.

title: Towards medical AI misalignment: a preliminary study
tldr: Introduces the 'Goofy Game' jailbreak technique using role-playing prompts to coerce LLMs into providing plausible but incorrect medical guidance, bypassing safety measures across four frontier models.

title: "Haet Bhasha aur Diskrimineshun": Phonetic Perturbations in Code-Mixed Hinglish to Red-Team LLMs
tldr: Combining code-mixing (Hinglish) with phonetic misspellings of sensitive keywords achieves up to 99% attack success rate on LLMs by exploiting tokenization vulnerabilities in multilingual safety alignment.

title: Evaluating the efficacy of LLM Safety Solutions: The Palit Benchmark Dataset
tldr: Introduces a 500-prompt benchmark dataset and comparative evaluation of 7 LLM safety tools (guardrails), finding Lakera Guard and ProtectAI LLM Guard as best performers with key precision-recall tradeoffs.

title: Multilingual Collaborative Defense for Large Language Models
tldr: MCD optimizes a soft safety prompt using multilingual collaborative training to defend LLMs against jailbreaks in rare/underrepresented languages, reducing ASR and cross-language variance.

title: A Jailbreak Prompt Detector Based on Selective Perturbation and Contrastive Learning
venue: CSCWD 2025 (International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design)
tldr: JPS is a jailbreak prompt detection system for LLMs that combines token-importance-based selective perturbation for data augmentation with supervised contrastive learning to distinguish harmful from benign prompts.

title: Scaling Responsible Generative AI: Automating Red Teaming of LLM Applications
tldr: An automated pipeline with five adversarial prompt generator types and a 48-risk taxonomy that halves red-teaming time and reduces manual evaluation by over 90%.

title: RepV: Safety-Separable Latent Spaces for Scalable Neurosymbolic Plan Verification
tldr: RepV learns safety-separable latent spaces where compliant and non-compliant AI plans are linearly separable, enabling scalable neurosymbolic plan verification with probabilistic guarantees and 15% accuracy gains over baselines.

title: A Unified Framework for Diffusion Model Unlearning with f-Divergence
tldr: A unified f-divergence framework (f-DMU) for concept erasure in diffusion models, showing MSE is a special case and that Hellinger distance yields better stability and quality.

title: Semantic-level Backdoor Attack against Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
tldr: SemBD implants backdoors in text-to-image diffusion models using continuous semantic regions as triggers, achieving 100% attack success rate while evading state-of-the-art defenses.

title: GRIP: Algorithm-Agnostic Machine Unlearning for Mixture-of-Experts via Geometric Router Constraints
tldr: GRIP uses geometric null-space projections to constrain router updates in MoE models during unlearning, preventing routing manipulation and achieving genuine knowledge erasure with routing stability restored from 0.21 to >0.94.

title: The Trigger in the Haystack: Extracting and Reconstructing LLM Backdoor Triggers
tldr: A four-step inference-only scanner that detects and reconstructs backdoor triggers in poisoned LLMs by exploiting memorization leakage and distinctive attention/entropy patterns, achieving 87.8% detection on 41 models with zero false positives.

title: On The Dangers of Poisoned LLMs In Security Automation
tldr: Demonstrates that fine-tuning LLMs on poisoned data (200 malicious samples) causes 100% misclassification of security alerts from a targeted user while maintaining strong overall accuracy.

title: An Investigation on Group Query Hallucination Attacks
tldr: Group Query Attack (GQA) — submitting multiple queries at once — significantly degrades fine-tuned LLM accuracy, triggers dormant backdoors, and disrupts reasoning in pre-trained models.

title: Trading Devil Final: Backdoor attack via Stock market and Bayesian Optimization
tldr: MarketBackFinal 2.0 achieves 100% backdoor attack success rate on 7 speech transformer architectures by poisoning audio data using stochastic financial models and Bayesian optimization.

title: Can LLMs Predict Their Own Failures? Self-Awareness via Internal Circuits
tldr: Gnosis is a 5M-parameter dual-stream module that analyzes frozen LLMs' hidden states and attention maps to predict output correctness, achieving 0.95 AUROC on math reasoning and outperforming larger external judges.

title: The Dual Power of Interpretable Token Embeddings: Jailbreaking Attacks and Defenses for Diffusion Model Unlearning
tldr: SubAttack learns interpretable orthogonal token embeddings to jailbreak unlearned diffusion models (97%+ ASR), while SubDefense uses subspace projection to block such attacks.

title: A Behavioral Fingerprint for Large Language Models: Provenance Tracking via Refusal Vectors
tldr: Uses refusal vectors—layer-wise hidden-state differences between harmful and harmless prompts—as behavioral fingerprints to track LLM provenance, achieving 100% accuracy across 76 derivative models.

title: Embedding Poisoning: Bypassing Safety Alignment via Embedding Semantic Shift
tldr: SEP (Search-based Embedding Poisoning) achieves 96.43% attack success rate bypassing LLM safety alignment by imperceptibly perturbing embedding vectors without modifying model weights or input prompts.

title: BadTemplate: A Training-Free Backdoor Attack via Chat Template Against Large Language Models
tldr: BadTemplate exploits chat template customizability to inject backdoor triggers into LLM system prompts without retraining, achieving up to 100% attack success rate across open- and closed-source models.

title: SHIELD: An Auto-Healing Agentic Defense Framework for LLM Resource Exhaustion Attacks
tldr: SHIELD is a multi-agent defense system against sponge attacks on LLMs using a three-stage pipeline (semantic retrieval, pattern matching, LLM reasoning) with autonomous self-healing via knowledge update and prompt optimization agents.

title: SycoEval-EM: Sycophancy Evaluation of Large Language Models in Simulated Clinical Encounters for Emergency Care
tldr: A multi-agent simulation framework evaluating sycophancy in 20 LLMs under patient social pressure in emergency medicine finds acquiescence rates of 0-100% with model capability not predicting robustness.

title: When Helpers Become Hazards: A Benchmark for Analyzing Multimodal LLM-Powered Safety in Daily Life
tldr: Introduces SaLAD, a 2,013-sample multimodal safety benchmark for daily-life scenarios, revealing top MLLMs achieve only 57.2% safe response rates and existing alignment methods offer minimal improvement.

title: The Anatomy of Conversational Scams: A Topic-Based Red Teaming Analysis of Multi-Turn Interactions in LLMs
tldr: LLM-to-LLM simulation of 18,648 multi-turn scam dialogues across 8 models reveals recurrent escalation patterns, cross-lingual guardrail asymmetry, and functional symmetry between attack and defense strategies.

title: EquaCode: A Multi-Strategy Jailbreak Approach for Large Language Models via Equation Solving and Code Completion
tldr: EquaCode jailbreaks LLMs by reformulating harmful requests as math equations and code completion tasks, achieving 91.19% attack success on GPT models.

title: Agent Tools Orchestration Leaks More: Dataset, Benchmark, and Mitigation
tldr: Introduces TOP-R (Tools Orchestration Privacy Risk), showing that LLM agents aggregating innocuous data across tools leak sensitive info 90.24% of the time; proposes PEP mitigation reducing leakage to 46.58%.

title: Security of LLM-based agents regarding attacks, defenses, and applications: A comprehensive survey
tldr: Comprehensive survey systematizing attacks and defenses on LLM-based agents, with dual evaluation criteria and taxonomy of agent-enabled cyber offense/defense applications.

title: Inference-time Unlearning Using Conformal Prediction
tldr: An inference-time machine unlearning framework using conformal prediction that removes specific training data influence without parameter updates, reducing unlearning error by up to 93% on benchmarks.

title: Sparsity-Aware Unlearning for Large Language Models
tldr: SAU uses gradient masking and importance-aware redistribution to fix the failure of machine unlearning methods on pruned/sparse LLMs, recovering 6-15% aggregate performance.

title: Towards Benchmarking Privacy Vulnerabilities in Selective Forgetting with Large Language Models
tldr: PrivUB is the first comprehensive benchmark evaluating privacy vulnerabilities introduced by machine unlearning in LLMs, covering 21 attack/defense methods, 10 unlearning techniques, 11 datasets, and 10 model architectures.

title: Forget to Know, Remember to Use: Context-Aware Unlearning for Large Language Models
tldr: Existing LLM unlearning methods impair contextual use of forgotten knowledge; a KL-divergence term preserving contextual utility fixes this across six methods and two models.

title: Cross-Modal Attention Guided Unlearning in Vision-Language Models
tldr: CAGUL uses cross-modal attention to identify unimportant visual tokens and transform them via a frozen-parameter MLP encoder, enabling selective unlearning of private attributes in VLMs.

title: Standard vs. Modular Sampling: Best Practices for Reliable LLM Unlearning
tldr: Proposes MELU (Modular Entity-Level Unlearning) and shows standard 1:1 sampling is inefficient; diverse neighbor sets and modular sampling improve LLM unlearning reliability.

title: Towards Evaluation for Real-World LLM Unlearning
tldr: DCUE is a new LLM unlearning evaluation metric using core token confidence scores and distribution correction via KS-test, achieving perfect scores on practicality, exactness, and robustness.

title: A mean teacher algorithm for unlearning of language models
tldr: Applies mean teacher proximal optimization to LLM unlearning, showing it approximates natural gradient descent and improves memorization reduction on MUSE benchmarks with a new NLUL loss.

title: The Limits of Obliviate: Evaluating Unlearning in LLMs via Stimulus-Knowledge Entanglement-Behavior Framework
tldr: Persuasive prompts (especially authority framing) recover factual knowledge from LLMs that underwent machine unlearning, with authority framing raising recall from 14.8% to 24.5%.

title: Hierarchical Federated Unlearning for Large Language Models
tldr: FULM uses dual LoRA adapters and hierarchical federated merging to remove hazardous or private knowledge from LLMs across decentralized clients without full retraining.

title: Towards Mitigating Excessive Forgetting in LLM Unlearning via Entanglement-Guidance with Proxy Constraint
tldr: EAGLE-PC combines entanglement-aware loss reweighting with proxy constraints to address the over-forgetting vs. under-forgetting tradeoff in LLM machine unlearning.

title: GrOCE: Graph-Guided Online Concept Erasure for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
tldr: GrOCE is a training-free, graph-based concept erasure framework for text-to-image diffusion models that removes harmful/copyrighted concepts at inference time by severing semantic graph edges, achieving state-of-the-art erasure with zero collateral damage.

title: Hearing is Believing? Evaluating and Analyzing Audio Language Model Sycophancy with SYAUDIO
tldr: SYAUDIO is the first benchmark for sycophancy in Audio Language Models (4,319 questions), showing audio inputs amplify sycophancy vs. text, with SFT+CoT as effective mitigation.

title: Aetheria: A multimodal interpretable content safety framework based on multi-agent debate and collaboration
tldr: Aetheria is a five-agent multimodal content safety framework using a debate mechanism between risk-averse and context-aware agents anchored by RAG, achieving F1=0.84 on a new multimodal benchmark.

title: Can Safety Fine-Tuning Be More Principled? Lessons Learned from Cybersecurity
tldr: Argues that LLM safety fine-tuning resembles a reactive cybersecurity arms race and proposes six principled lessons from cybersecurity history to guide more robust AI safety design.

title: SafeLLM: Unlearning Harmful Outputs from Large Language Models against Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: SafeLLM uses token-level FFN activation tracing and constrained optimization to unlearn harmful knowledge in LLMs, reducing jailbreak attack success rates to ~5-6% while preserving general capabilities.

title: The Impact of Off-Policy Training Data on Probe Generalisation
venue: EurIPS 2025 Workshop on Private AI Governance
tldr: Off-policy training data significantly harms probe generalization for intent-based LLM behaviors (deception, sandbagging) but not for text-evident ones; domain shift matters more than response strategy shift.

title: MAGIC: A Co-Evolving Attacker-Defender Adversarial Game for Robust LLM Safety
tldr: MAGIC uses multi-agent RL to co-evolve an attacker and defender in an adversarial game, reducing LLM attack success rates dramatically while preserving helpfulness.

title: Red-Bandit: Test-Time Adaptation for LLM Red-Teaming via Bandit-Guided LoRA Experts
tldr: Red-Bandit trains 10 LoRA attack-style experts via RL and uses a multi-armed bandit at test time to adaptively select the most effective attack style, achieving up to 100% ASR on open-source models and 93.3% on GPT-4o.

title: The Viscosity of Logic: Phase Transitions and Hysteresis in DPO Alignment
tldr: Dense sweeps across β in DPO reveal sharply non-monotonic capability dynamics, hysteresis effects, and dangerous margin-capability anticorrelation (r=-0.91) that invalidates margin-based model selection.

title: Internal Reasoning vs. External Control: A Thermodynamic Analysis of Sycophancy in Large Language Models
tldr: Regulated Causal Anchoring (RCA) eliminates sycophancy in LLMs by verifying trace-output consistency at inference time, achieving 0.0% sycophancy while accepting 88% of valid hints.

title: ProSocialAlign: Preference Conditioned Test Time Alignment in Language Models
tldr: ProSocialAlign steers LLM outputs toward five prosocial values (sensitivity, empathy, non-judgmental, truthfulness, helpfulness) at inference time via harm-direction removal and preference-conditioned reward modeling, without retraining.

title: Monitorability as a Free Gift: How RLVR Spontaneously Aligns Reasoning
tldr: RLVR training can spontaneously improve chain-of-thought monitorability, but this depends on training data composition (especially instruction-following data) and is orthogonal to capability gains.

title: From Defender to Devil? Unintended Risk Interactions Induced by LLM Defenses
tldr: CrossRiskEval framework reveals that LLM defenses targeting one risk (safety, fairness, privacy) systematically amplify other risks via conflict-entangled neurons.

title: Stress-Testing Alignment Audits With Prompt-Level Strategic Deception
tldr: An automated red-team pipeline generates prompt-level deception strategies that defeat both black-box and white-box alignment auditing methods, including SAE-based white-box probing, providing the first documented evidence of activation-based strategic deception.

title: Endogenous Resistance to Activation Steering in Language Models
tldr: LLMs can spontaneously resist task-misaligned activation steering (ESR); Llama-3.3-70B shows 7.4% multi-attempt resistance rate driven by 26 identifiable SAE latents acting as off-topic detectors.

title: Hierarchical Sparse Circuit Extraction from Billion-Parameter Language Models through Scalable Attribution Graph Decomposition
tldr: HAGD framework reduces circuit discovery complexity from O(2^n) to O(n^2 log n) via hierarchical attribution graph decomposition, achieving 91% behavioral preservation on billion-parameter LLMs.

title: Interpretable Safety Alignment via SAE-Constructed Low-Rank Subspace Adaptation
tldr: Uses SAEs to identify safety-relevant features and construct interpretable low-rank subspaces for LoRA adapter initialization, achieving 99.6% safety rate with only 0.19-0.24% parameters updated.

title: Interpretable and Steerable Concept Bottleneck Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: CB-SAE combines SAE pruning with concept bottleneck training to improve neuron interpretability (+32.1%) and steerability (+14.5%) in vision-language models.

title: GSS: Gated Subspace Steering for Selective Memorization Mitigation in LLMs
tldr: GSS uses a probe-steer decomposition to selectively suppress verbatim memorization in LLMs at inference time, achieving 100-1000x speedup over optimization-based alternatives with minimal utility loss.

title: CLUE: Conflict-guided Localization for LLM Unlearning Framework
tldr: CLUE uses circuit discovery and Boolean satisfiability to categorize neurons as forget/retain/conflict, then applies targeted fine-tuning strategies for more precise LLM unlearning.

title: Reverse-Engineering Model Editing on Language Models
tldr: KSTER attack reverse-engineers locate-then-edit model edits via spectral analysis achieving 99% recall on Llama3-8B; subspace camouflage defense mitigates the vulnerability.

title: REBEL: Hidden Knowledge Recovery via Evolutionary-Based Evaluation Loop
tldr: REBEL is an evolutionary adversarial prompting framework that exposes hidden knowledge in supposedly unlearned LLMs, achieving up to 93% attack success rate on WMDP where standard metrics showed near-zero leakage.

title: Refusal Steering: Fine-grained Control over LLM Refusal Behaviour for Sensitive Topics
tldr: Introduces ridge-regularized steering vectors and an LLM-as-judge refusal scoring approach to enable fine-grained, inference-time control over LLM refusal behavior on politically sensitive topics without retraining.

title: VisualDAN: Exposing Vulnerabilities in VLMs with Visual-Driven DAN Commands
tldr: VisualDAN embeds 'Do Anything Now' jailbreak commands into adversarial images via gradient-based optimization, achieving 90-97.5% attack success rates on four open-source VLMs.

title: Beyond Text: Multimodal Jailbreaking of Vision-Language and Audio Models through Perceptually Simple Transformations
tldr: Simple perceptual transformations (typographic images, audio pitch/speed shifts) achieve >75% jailbreak success rates on frontier VLMs and audio models that have near-perfect text-only safety defenses.

title: CHAI: Command Hijacking against embodied AI
tldr: CHAI embeds deceptive text into visual scenes to hijack LVLM-driven robotic systems (drones, cars), achieving up to 95.5% attack success rate in simulation and 87%+ in real-world tests.

title: A Low-cost Black-box Jailbreak Based on Custom Mapping Dictionary with Multi-round Induction
venue: 2024 IEEE 23rd International Conference on Trust, Security and Privacy in Computing and Communications (TrustCom)
tldr: DJMI creates custom mapping dictionaries to encode harmful requests in novel vocabulary, then uses multi-round induction to achieve >80% jailbreak success on mainstream LLMs at low cost.

title: "Moralized" Multi-Step Jailbreak Prompts: Black-Box Testing of Guardrails in Large Language Models for Verbal Attacks
tldr: Black-box multi-step jailbreak prompts framed as ethical corporate scenarios successfully bypass guardrails in GPT-4o, Grok-2 Beta, Llama 3.1, and Gemini 1.5, with Claude 3.5 Sonnet showing stronger resistance.

title: RED QUEEN: Safeguarding Large Language Models against Concealed Multi-Turn Jailbreaking
tldr: Introduces Red Queen Attack, a multi-turn jailbreak exploiting narrative concealment to achieve 87.62% ASR on GPT-4o, and Red Queen Guard (DPO-based defense) reducing ASR below 1%.

title: OutSafe-Bench: A Benchmark for Multimodal Offensive Content Detection in Large Language Models
tldr: OutSafe-Bench is a bilingual multimodal benchmark with 18K+ prompts, 4,500 images, 450 audio, and 450 videos across 9 risk categories, plus novel MCRS metric and FairScore evaluation framework.

title: Beyond SFT: Reinforcement Learning for Safer Large Reasoning Models with Better Reasoning Ability
tldr: RL (Reinforce++) outperforms SFT for safety-tuning large reasoning models, achieving stronger/consistent safety gains without degrading chain-of-thought reasoning ability.

title: SafeEditor: Unified MLLM for Efficient Post-hoc T2I Safety Editing
tldr: SafeEditor is a unified MLLM that iteratively edits unsafe T2I outputs post-generation, achieving 94.35% safety ratio with only 0.35% false positive rate on I2P benchmark.

title: Prompt Injection Vulnerability of Consensus Generating Applications in Digital Democracy
tldr: A four-dimensional prompt injection attack taxonomy is applied to LLM-based digital democracy consensus systems, finding criticism-based completion attacks most effective and DPO only partially mitigating vulnerabilities.

title: CoT is Not the Chain of Truth: An Empirical Internal Analysis of Reasoning LLMs for Fake News Generation
tldr: Even when reasoning LLMs refuse harmful requests, their internal CoT reasoning can propagate unsafe narratives; Jacobian-based spectral metrics on attention heads localize safety-critical layers.

title: A Two-Step, Multidimensional Account of Deception in Language Models
tldr: Proposes a two-step, five-dimensional framework for characterizing LLM deception: a minimal condition (producing false beliefs to achieve goals) plus a multidimensional profile covering skillfulness, learning, deceptive inclination, explicitness, and situational awareness.

title: Inaugural Workshop on Provably Safe and Beneficial AI (PSBAI)
tldr: Final report from the NSF-funded inaugural PSBAI workshop, presenting a multi-track research roadmap for building provably safe and beneficial AI systems.

title: Calibrated Predictive Lower Bounds on Time-to-Unsafe-Sampling in LLMs
tldr: Frames LLM unsafe-output risk as survival analysis and derives provably calibrated lower predictive bounds on time-to-unsafe-sampling using conformal prediction with adaptive budget allocation.

title: In AI Sweet Harmony: Sociopragmatic Guardrail Bypasses and Evaluation-Awareness in OpenAI gpt-oss-20b
tldr: Sociopragmatic framing (educator personas, formal registers, language shifts) bypasses safety guardrails in OpenAI gpt-oss-20b, raising assistance rates on harmful tasks from 0% to 97.5%.

title: Attack Selection Reduces Safety in Concentrated AI Control Settings against Trusted Monitoring
tldr: Strategic attack selection by untrusted AI models can reduce safety in AI control settings from 99% to 59% at a 0.5% auditing budget by exploiting monitor false positive rates.

title: Benchmarking Knowledge-Extraction Attack and Defense on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
tldr: First systematic benchmark for knowledge-extraction attacks and defenses on RAG systems, evaluating 6 attacks and multiple defenses across 4 datasets with new extraction effectiveness metrics.

title: Breaking the Protocol: Security Analysis of the Model Context Protocol Specification and Prompt Injection Vulnerabilities in Tool-Integrated LLM Agents
tldr: First formal security analysis of the Model Context Protocol finds three architectural vulnerabilities that amplify attack success by 23-41%; proposes AttestMCP defense reducing attacks from 52.8% to 12.4%.

title: FinVault: Benchmarking Financial Agent Safety in Execution-Grounded Environments
tldr: FinVault is a benchmark with 31 financial sandbox scenarios and 963 test cases for evaluating LLM-agent safety against prompt injection, jailbreaks, and financial-domain attacks, finding up to 50% attack success rates on SOTA models.

title: PII-VisBench: Evaluating Personally Identifiable Information Safety in Vision Language Models Along a Continuum of Visibility
tldr: PII-VisBench evaluates PII disclosure safety across 18 open-source VLMs using 4,000 probes on 200 subjects stratified by online visibility, finding models leak significantly more PII about high-visibility subjects.

title: AWMT: Automatic jailbreaking attack framework utilizing working-memory trees
tldr: AWMT uses working-memory-guided tree search to automatically generate interpretable multi-prompt jailbreak attacks, achieving 86% attack success rate on GPT-3.5-turbo, an 18% improvement over baselines.

title: A comprehensive survey of adversarial defense techniques in the visual domain
tldr: Comprehensive survey of adversarial defense techniques in computer vision, covering white-box/black-box/physical-world attacks and defenses including adversarial training, input preprocessing, detection, certified defenses, and LVLM defenses.

title: RLCracker: Exposing the Vulnerability of LLM Watermarks with Adaptive RL Attacks
tldr: RLCracker uses RL-based fine-tuning to remove LLM watermarks with 98.5% evasion success on 1500-token texts, using only 100 training samples and no detector access.

title: TAPDA: Text Adversarial Purification as Defense Against Adversarial Prompt Attack for Large Language Models
venue: 2025 8th International Conference on Advanced Algorithms and Control Engineering (ICAACE)
tldr: TAPDA uses iterative mask-predict purification of adversarial prompts via LLMs themselves, combined with voting and perplexity-based aggregation, to defend against jailbreak attacks while preserving readability.

title: Desert Camels and Oil Sheikhs: Arab-Centric Red Teaming of Frontier LLMs
tldr: Arab-centric red-teaming of six frontier LLMs finds 79% negative bias toward Arabs and 75.7% average jailbreak success rate across eight sensitive domains.

title: Adversarial Attacks on Vision-Language Model-Empowered Chatbots in Consumer Electronics
tldr: Designs three adversarial attacks exploiting insufficient VLM multimodal alignment to force harmful outputs from popular chatbot systems, evaluated on 14 prohibited security scenarios.

title: It's a TRAP! Task-Redirecting Agent Persuasion Benchmark for Web Agents
tldr: TRAP benchmark evaluates prompt injection attacks on LLM web agents across six website clones, finding frontier models are vulnerable 13-43% of the time with small UI changes doubling attack success.

title: VisuoAlign: Safety Alignment of LVLMs with Multimodal Tree Search
tldr: VisuoAlign uses prompt-guided MCTS to embed safety constraints into LVLM reasoning chains, reducing jailbreak success rates by 57%+ and achieving alignment safety rates above 0.92.

title: The Emotional Baby Is Truly Deadly: Does your Multimodal Large Reasoning Model Have Emotional Flattery towards Humans?
tldr: EmoAgent uses emotionally charged prompts to exploit a security-reasoning paradox in multimodal large reasoning models, achieving up to 94% attack success rate and revealing three novel failure modes in transparent reasoning.

title: Thought-Transfer: Indirect Targeted Poisoning Attacks on Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Models
tldr: Thought-Transfer is a clean-label poisoning attack that embeds adversarial behaviors into CoT reasoning models by modifying only reasoning traces in training data, achieving 70%+ success while improving benchmarks 10-15%.

title: On the Feasibility of Hijacking MLLMs' Decision Chain via One Perturbation
tldr: A single universal adversarial perturbation (SAUP) can hijack an MLLM's entire decision chain, achieving 70% attack success controlling five distinct semantic targets across three MLLMs.

title: Multi-Agent Systems Should be Treated as Principal-Agent Problems
tldr: Argues multi-agent LLM systems should be analyzed as principal-agent problems from microeconomics, framing scheming as rational agency loss and proposing mechanism design tools to address it.

title: How Should AI Safety Benchmarks Benchmark Safety?
tldr: Scoping review of 210 AI safety benchmarks identifies three major failure modes and proposes 10 recommendations grounded in risk management, measurement theory, and engineering practice.

title: Prompt Injection Attacks on Agentic Coding Assistants: A Systematic Analysis of Vulnerabilities in Skills, Tools, and Protocol Ecosystems
tldr: Systematic review of 78 studies on prompt injection in agentic coding assistants, cataloging 42 attack techniques across a 3D taxonomy; attack success rates exceed 85% against current defenses.

title: Towards Understanding Steering Strength
tldr: First theoretical analysis of steering strength for LLM latent representation steering, deriving qualitative laws governing effects on token probability, concept presence, and cross-entropy, validated on 11 models.

title: From Atoms to Trees: Building a Structured Feature Forest with Hierarchical Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Hierarchical Sparse Autoencoders (HSAE) jointly train multiple SAEs to discover structured parent-child feature hierarchies in LLMs, revealing multi-scale conceptual organization intrinsic to model representations.

title: Learning a Generative Meta-Model of LLM Activations
tldr: Trains diffusion models (Generative Latent Priors) on 1B LLM activations to learn internal state distributions, improving steering fluency and concept isolation over SAEs.

title: Subliminal Effects in Your Data: A General Mechanism via Log-Linearity
tldr: LLS selects dataset subsets using log-linear structure of LM preferences to induce hidden target behaviors (language shifts, persona adoption) during fine-tuning without individual examples revealing the effect.

title: The Safety Gap Toolkit: Evaluating Hidden Dangers of Open-Source Models
tldr: Introduces the Safety Gap Toolkit to measure the increase in dangerous capabilities (bio/chem/cyber) when open-weight LLM safeguards are removed, finding the gap grows with model scale.

title: A Concrete Roadmap towards Safety Cases based on Chain-of-Thought Monitoring
tldr: Proposes a two-part safety case framework using CoT monitoring: show models lack dangerous capabilities without CoT, then ensure CoT-enabled capabilities remain detectable via monitoring.

title: SCALPEL: Selective Capability Ablation via Low-rank Parameter Editing for Large Language Model Interpretability Analysis
tldr: SCALPEL uses LoRA adapters to selectively ablate specific LLM capabilities (e.g., IOI, translation, common sense) via low-rank parameter editing, revealing how capabilities are hierarchically distributed across transformer layers.

title: Super Suffixes: Bypassing Text Generation Alignment and Guard Models Simultaneously
tldr: Super Suffixes are adversarial token sequences that simultaneously bypass LLM alignment and guard model protections via joint optimization; DeltaGuard detects them using residual stream cosine similarity traces.

title: Temporal Sparse Autoencoders: Leveraging the Sequential Nature of Language for Interpretability
tldr: Temporal SAEs add a contrastive loss enforcing consistent high-level feature activations across adjacent tokens, disentangling semantic from syntactic features without explicit supervision.

title: Take Goodhart Seriously: Principled Limit on General-Purpose AI Optimization
tldr: Argues that the Objective Satisfaction Assumption necessarily fails in ML due to irreducible errors and specification gaps, concluding that principled limits on General-Purpose AI optimization are required to avoid Goodhart failures and loss of control.

title: Dimensional Collapse in Transformer Attention Outputs: A Challenge for Sparse Dictionary Learning
tldr: Attention outputs in transformers occupy ~60% of available directions (99% variance threshold), causing 87% dead features in large SAEs; Active Subspace Initialization (ASI) reduces dead features to <1%.

title: Truthfulness Despite Weak Supervision: Evaluating and Training LLMs Using Peer Prediction
tldr: Peer prediction mechanisms from mechanism design enable truthfulness evaluation and training of LLMs without ground truth labels, outperforming LLM-as-a-Judge and resisting deception as capability gaps widen.

title: Rethinking Deep Alignment Through The Lens Of Incomplete Learning
tldr: Identifies position-dependent gradient weakening in autoregressive safety training as the root cause of incomplete alignment, then proposes targeted penalties and hybrid distillation to cut attack success rates by 48-98%.

title: Self-Jailbreaking: Language Models Can Reason Themselves Out of Safety Alignment After Benign Reasoning Training
tldr: Benign reasoning fine-tuning (math/code) causes LLMs to self-jailbreak via chain-of-thought — assuming benign intent or hypothetical framing to justify harmful outputs — even when models retain safety knowledge.

title: When Should We Introduce Safety Interventions During Pretraining?
tldr: Introducing safety interventions earlier during LLM pretraining yields more robust models against jailbreaking and benign finetuning, with minimal overrefusal tradeoff.

title: Rethinking Jailbreak Detection of Large Vision Language Models with Representational Contrastive Scoring
tldr: RCS uses internal geometric signatures of LVLM representations to detect jailbreaks, achieving 98.6% AUROC while generalizing to unseen attack types with only 5% compute overhead.

title: Trustworthy Agentic AI Requires Deterministic Architectural Boundaries
tldr: Proposes the Trinity Defense Architecture — finite action calculus, mandatory access labels, and privilege separation — arguing that deterministic architectural enforcement, not alignment training, is necessary for secure agentic AI.

title: LLMs Can Unlearn Refusal with Only 1,000 Benign Samples
tldr: Fine-tuning on 1,000 benign samples with refusal prefixes appended to responses causes aligned LLMs to drop ~50% safety scores across 16 models by disrupting refusal pathways.

title: Benign-to-Toxic Jailbreaking: Inducing Harmful Responses from Harmless Prompts
tldr: Benign-to-Toxic (B2T) optimizes adversarial images to induce harmful outputs from innocent text prompts in LVLMs, bypassing safety mechanisms that rely on toxic text conditioning.

title: Debate with Images: Detecting Deceptive Behaviors in Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: MM-DeceptionBench (1,013 cases, 6 categories) + a multi-agent 'debate with images' framework that improves deceptive MLLM detection by 1.25x accuracy and 1.5x Cohen's kappa over MLLM-as-a-judge baselines.

title: In-the-Wild Model Organisms: Mitigating Undesirable Emergent Behaviors in Production LLM Post-Training via Data Attribution
tldr: Activation-based data attribution identifies training examples causing harmful LLM behaviors; applied to OLMo 2's DPO data, it found and reduced 'distractor-triggered compliance' by up to 78%.

title: BLOCK-EM: Preventing Emergent Misalignment by Blocking Causal Features
tldr: BLOCK-EM identifies a small set of SAE latents causally driving emergent misalignment in fine-tuned LLMs and applies a one-sided penalty during training to block them, achieving up to 95% relative misalignment reduction across six domains.

title: Unlocking the Address Book: Dissecting the Sparse Semantic Structure of LLM Key-Value Caches via Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: STA-Attention uses Top-K SAEs to decompose LLM KV caches into interpretable semantic atoms, revealing that keys are sparse routers while values are dense payloads.

title: Kronecker Factorization Improves Efficiency and Interpretability of Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: KronSAE uses Kronecker product decomposition with a novel mAND activation to reduce SAE encoder parameters by ~54% while improving explained variance by 4.3% and reducing feature absorption.

title: Feature-Space Adversarial Robustness Certification for Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: Feature-space Smoothing (FS) provides certified lower bounds on cosine similarity between clean and adversarial features in MLLMs under l2-bounded perturbations, with a plug-and-play Gaussian Smoothness Booster improving certified radius from 0.33 to 0.69.

title: JPRO: Automated Multimodal Jailbreaking via Multi-Agent Collaboration Framework
tldr: JPRO is a multi-agent framework for automated black-box jailbreaking of VLMs using tactic-driven seed generation and adaptive optimization, achieving >60% attack success on GPT-4o.

title: GraphAttack: Exploiting Representational Blindspots in LLM Safety Mechanisms
tldr: GraphAttack uses semantic graph representations (AMR, RDF, JSON knowledge graphs) to generate jailbreaks that exploit LLM safety mechanisms' reliance on surface-pattern recognition, achieving up to 87% ASR on leading commercial LLMs.

title: Towards Scalable Oversight with Collaborative Multi-Agent Debate in Error Detection
tldr: ColMAD reframes multi-agent debate as a collaborative game rather than competitive, reducing debate hacking and improving LLM error detection by up to 19% over competitive debate baselines.

title: AM3Safety: Towards Data Efficient Alignment of Multi-modal Multi-turn Safety for MLLMs
tldr: AM3Safety introduces a data-efficient two-phase framework (cold-start SFT + GRPO with turn-aware safety-variance rewards) and InterSafe-V dataset to reduce multi-turn jailbreak success rates in MLLMs by >10%.

title: Think-Reflect-Revise: A Policy-Guided Reflective Framework for Safety Alignment in Large Vision Language Models
tldr: Think-Reflect-Revise (TRR) trains LVLMs to reflect on their own outputs against safety policies and revise harmful responses, boosting safe response rate from 42.8% to 87.7% on Qwen2.5-VL-7B.

title: Corrigibility Transformation: Constructing Goals That Accept Updates
tldr: Introduces a formal corrigibility transformation that converts any MDP goal into a corrigible version that accepts goal updates without sacrificing performance, proven via Theorems 1, 3, and 4.

title: Stateless Yet Not Forgetful: Implicit Memory as a Hidden Channel in LLMs
tldr: LLMs can maintain persistent hidden state across independent interactions by encoding information in outputs via invisible Unicode or semantic steganography, enabling 'time bomb' temporal backdoors.

title: Agentic Uncertainty Reveals Agentic Overconfidence
tldr: AI agents systematically overestimate their task success probability; pre-execution uncertainty estimates surprisingly outperform post-execution ones, and adversarial bug-detection prompting yields best calibration.
models_studied: frontier LLM agents (multiple models tested on SWE-bench Pro)

title: Securing AI Agents in Cyber-Physical Systems: A Survey of Environmental Interactions, Deepfake Threats, and Defenses
tldr: SENTINEL framework survey for securing AI agents in cyber-physical systems against deepfake and semantic manipulation attacks, showing detection-centric security is insufficient.

title: SafePro: Evaluating the Safety of Professional-Level AI Agents
tldr: SafePro is a 275-task benchmark for evaluating AI agent safety in professional domains, revealing that state-of-the-art models have unsafe rates exceeding 40% and that models fail to apply safety knowledge in agentic settings.

title: Interactionless Inverse Reinforcement Learning: A Data-Centric Framework for Durable Alignment
tldr: Proposes Interactionless IRL to decouple reward learning from policy optimization, producing reusable/editable reward models, plus an Alignment Flywheel for iterative reward model hardening.

title: Contextual Image Attack: How Visual Context Exposes Multimodal Safety Vulnerabilities
tldr: CIA is a jailbreak method that embeds harmful queries into benign-looking visual contexts using a multi-agent pipeline, achieving 86-91% attack success rate against GPT-4o and Qwen2.5-VL-72B.

title: DefenSee: Dissecting Threat from Sight and Text - A Multi-View Defensive Pipeline for Multi-modal Jailbreaks
tldr: DefenSee is a black-box three-stage pipeline defending VLMs from image-text jailbreaks via visual decomposition, GPT-4o transcription, and cross-modal consistency checks, reducing ASR below 1.70%.

title: Broken Bags: Disrupting Service Through the Contamination of Large Language Models With Misinformation
tldr: Broken Bags attacks RAG systems by injecting minimal toxic content into knowledge bases, achieving 94% success rate while bypassing perplexity-based and knowledge-extension defenses.

title: Automatically Finding Rule-Based Neurons in OthelloGPT
tldr: Automated decision-tree pipeline identifies rule-based neurons in OthelloGPT MLP layers, finding ~45% of layer-5 neurons describable by compact logical rules, validated via causal interventions.

title: Beyond the Safety Tax: Mitigating Unsafe Text-to-Image Generation via External Safety Rectification
tldr: Safe-Control is a plug-and-play external safety patch for T2I models that reduces unsafe content generation to ~7% (vs ~20% baseline) while preserving image quality, using ControlNet-style injection without modifying the original model.

title: Compressed Computation: Dense Circuits in a Toy Model of the Universal-AND Problem
tldr: A one-layer ReLU toy model forced to compute AND over all sparse input pairs discovers dense 'binary-weighted circuits' where every neuron contributes to every output, enabling efficient compressed computation.

title: On Privileged and Convergent Bases in Neural Network Representations
venue: Workshop on High-dimensional Learning Dynamics at ICML 2023
tldr: Neural networks develop functionally privileged bases (individual neurons matter) but do not converge to a unique basis across independent training runs, even at large width.

title: Mechanistic Evidence for Faithfulness Decay in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
tldr: Introduces NLDD metric to measure CoT faithfulness mechanistically, finding a universal 'Reasoning Horizon' at 70-85% of chain length beyond which tokens have minimal causal impact.

title: GAVEL: Towards Rule-Based Safety Through Activation Monitoring
tldr: GAVEL introduces rule-based activation safety using modular 'cognitive elements' to detect harmful LLM behaviors in real time with near-zero false positives and <1% runtime overhead.

title: NeuroFilter: Privacy Guardrails for Conversational LLM Agents
tldr: NeuroFilter detects privacy-violating prompts in LLM agents using linear activation probes and 'activation velocity' for multi-turn attacks, achieving 0% evasion and 0% false positives at nanosecond latency.

title: The Hypocrisy Gap: Quantifying Divergence Between Internal Belief and Chain-of-Thought Explanation via Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Introduces the 'Hypocrisy Gap' metric using SAEs and sparse linear probes to detect when LLMs generate chain-of-thought explanations that contradict their internal beliefs, achieving 0.55-0.74 AUROC on sycophancy detection.

title: Faithful and Stable Neuron Explanations for Trustworthy Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: Provides formal theoretical guarantees for neuron identification in mechanistic interpretability, addressing faithfulness and stability via generalization bounds and a bootstrap ensemble method.

title: SAVE: Sparse Autoencoder-Driven Visual Information Enhancement for Mitigating Object Hallucination
tldr: SAVE uses Sparse Autoencoders to identify 'visual understanding features' in MLLMs and steers activations along them to reduce object hallucination by up to 49% on CHAIR benchmarks.

title: Annotating the Chain-of-Thought: A Behavior-Labeled Dataset for AI Safety
tldr: A sentence-level labeled dataset of 52,473 annotated sentences across 20 safety behaviors in LLM reasoning traces, enabling activation-based safety monitoring via steering vectors.

title: Cyclic Ablation: Testing Concept Localization against Functional Regeneration in AI
tldr: Cyclic ablation on DistilGPT-2 shows deception is distributed rather than localized: SAE-based feature ablation is repeatedly overcome by functional regeneration while degrading general language ability.

title: Preserving Bilinear Weight Spectra with a Signed and Shrunk Quadratic Activation Function
tldr: SQS activation function enables Gated Linear Units to learn interpretable eigenfeatures (matching bilinear MLP weight structure) while matching SwiGLU/GEGLU performance on language modeling.

title: Automated Feature Labeling with Token-Space Gradient Descent
tldr: Reformulates SAE feature labeling as token-space gradient descent optimization, using an LLM as a discriminator rather than a generator, converging to interpretable single-token labels.

title: Enforcing Orderedness in SAEs to Improve Feature Consistency
tldr: Ordered SAEs (OSAEs) enforce strict feature ordering via nested dropout to resolve permutation non-identifiability, improving SAE feature consistency on Gemma2-2B and Pythia-70M.

title: Mechanisms of Prompt-Induced Hallucination in Vision-Language Models
tldr: Identifies specific attention heads in VLMs responsible for prompt-induced hallucination and shows mean-ablating them reduces hallucinations by 40-94% without additional training.

title: Towards Inclusive Toxic Content Moderation: Addressing Vulnerabilities to Adversarial Attacks in Toxicity Classifiers Tackling LLM-generated Content
tldr: Uses mechanistic interpretability (activation patching) to identify vulnerable attention heads in BERT/RoBERTa toxicity classifiers; suppressing these heads improves adversarial robustness 8-9% while exposing fairness disparities across demographic groups.

title: Multilingual Amnesia: On the Transferability of Unlearning in Multilingual LLMs
tldr: Studies how machine unlearning in one language transfers to others in multilingual LLMs, finding mostly language-specific effects with syntactic distance as the strongest predictor of cross-lingual transfer.

title: Adversarial Lens: Exploiting Attention Layers to Generate Adversarial Examples for Evaluation
tldr: Generates adversarial examples for LLM evaluation pipelines by exploiting intermediate attention layer representations (logit/tuned lens), reducing argument quality assessment performance on LLaMA-3.1-8B.

title: Causal-Guided Detoxify Backdoor Attack of Open-Weight LoRA Models
tldr: CBA injects backdoors into open-source LoRA adapters without original training data, reducing false trigger rates 50-70% vs baselines while evading SOTA defenses.

title: Machine Unlearning Across Scales: Evaluation of Optimization Methods on Language Models
tldr: Compares Gradient Ascent, Scaled Gradient Ascent, and WMDP-style Weighted Loss unlearning on Llama-3-8B and SmolLM-135M; scaled gradient ascent on the smaller model yields best unlearning with least utility loss.

title: CoSPED: Consistent Soft Prompt Targeted Data Extraction and Defense
tldr: CoSPED proposes novel loss functions and decoding strategies for white-box soft prompt-based training data extraction from LLMs, achieving 65.2% extraction rate and demonstrating ROME-based defenses that reduce it to 1.6%.

title: SIMU: Selective Influence Machine Unlearning
tldr: SIMU identifies critical neurons encoding forget-set data and selectively updates only those neurons during second-order influence-based unlearning, improving utility retention by 5-6% over baselines.

title: TRACEALIGN - Tracing the Drift: Attributing Alignment Failures to Training-Time Belief Sources in LLMs
tldr: TraceAlign traces unsafe LLM outputs to their training-data origins via span-level provenance and BCI metric, then applies three complementary defenses to reduce alignment drift by up to 85%.

title: Mr. Snuffleupagus at SemEval-2025 Task 4: Unlearning Factual Knowledge from LLMs Using Adaptive RMU
tldr: Applies Adaptive RMU to selectively remove factual knowledge from 1B and 7B LLMs, finding middle-later layers (12-14 for 1B, 24-26 for 7B) most effective, achieving 4th place on SemEval-2025 Task 4 leaderboards.

title: When Evaluation Becomes a Side Channel: Regime Leakage and Structural Mitigations for Alignment Assessment
tldr: Proposes Regime-Blind Fine-Tuning (RBFT) using gradient reversal to limit model access to evaluation-vs-deployment cues, reducing deceptive compliance in sleeper agent and sycophancy scenarios.

title: Hashmarks: Privacy-Preserving Benchmarks for High-Stakes AI Evaluation
tldr: Proposes hashmarking, a cryptographic protocol for benchmarking AI models on dangerous-capability questions (bioweapons, cyberwarfare) without publishing the correct answers publicly.

title: LLM Probing with Contrastive Eigenproblems: Improving Understanding and Applicability of CCS
tldr: Reformulates Contrast-Consistent Search (CCS) as an eigenproblem, yielding closed-form solutions with interpretable eigenvalues that match CCS accuracy while eliminating initialization sensitivity.

title: Steering to Say No: Configurable Refusal via Activation Steering in Vision Language Models
tldr: CR-VLM uses teacher-forced activation steering with a gating mechanism and vision-aware counterfactuals to enable configurable, low-over-refusal safety in VLMs, achieving 93-99.5% refusal rates on out-of-scope queries.

title: Privacy Collapse: Benign Fine-Tuning Can Break Contextual Privacy in Language Models
tldr: Benign fine-tuning (helpfulness, empathy, code debugging) can silently destroy LLMs' contextual privacy reasoning while safety benchmarks show no degradation.

title: Beyond Superficial Forgetting: Thorough Unlearning through Knowledge Density Estimation and Block Re-insertion
tldr: KUnBR uses knowledge density estimation to locate harmful knowledge-rich layers and a block re-insertion strategy to achieve thorough unlearning in LLMs, outperforming baselines on robustness to recovery attacks.

title: When the Model Said 'No Comment', We Knew Helpfulness Was Dead, Honesty Was Alive, and Safety Was Terrified
tldr: AlignX is a two-stage framework (prompt-injected fine-tuning + Mixture of Calibrated Experts) that simultaneously optimizes LLM helpfulness, harmlessness, and honesty, achieving +171.5% win rate and +110.1% truthfulness gains.

title: Objective Decoupling in Social Reinforcement Learning: Recovering Ground Truth from Sycophantic Majorities
tldr: Proves that biased human feedback majorities cause permanent objective decoupling in RL agents, and proposes Epistemic Source Alignment (ESA) to recover ground truth via axiom-based evaluator trust weighting.

title: Inference-Aware Meta-Alignment of LLMs via Non-Linear GRPO
tldr: Proposes inference-aware meta-alignment (IAMA) with non-linear GRPO to train LLMs that adapt to multiple conflicting alignment objectives at inference time within a limited compute budget.

title: Reward Shaping for Inference-Time Alignment: A Stackelberg Game Perspective
tldr: Formalizes reward model optimization as a Stackelberg game, proves the optimal reward has a threshold structure, and proposes SRS achieving 66%+ win-tie rates vs baselines.

title: Offline Safe Policy Optimization From Heterogeneous Feedback
tldr: PreSa learns safe policies directly from pairwise preference and binary safety labels via constrained optimization, eliminating separate reward/cost modeling and constrained RL phases.

title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback to Improve Alignment
tldr: XRLHF identifies training data causing unsatisfactory RLHF outputs via constrained optimization, then unlearns those data points, achieving 75-80% win rates over SFT baselines.

title: Targeting Misalignment: A Conflict-Aware Framework for Reward-Model-based LLM Alignment
tldr: Introduces PACS and Kendall-Tau metrics to detect proxy-policy conflicts in RLHF, and an algorithm (SHF-CAS) that targets high-conflict examples for human feedback to improve alignment.

title: Benchmarking and Understanding Safety Risks in AI Character Platforms
tldr: First large-scale safety evaluation of 16 AI character platforms using 5,000 benchmark questions, finding a 65.1% unsafe response rate vs. 17.7% for baseline LLMs.

title: Decomposed Trust: Exploring Privacy, Adversarial Robustness, Fairness, and Ethics of Low-Rank LLMs
tldr: First comprehensive study of how low-rank factorization (SVD, FWSVD, Basel) affects LLM trustworthiness across privacy, adversarial robustness, fairness, and ethical alignment on LLaMA2 and Qwen2.5 models.

title: From Competition to Coordination: Market Making as a Scalable Framework for Safe and Aligned Multi-Agent LLM Systems
tldr: Proposes a market-making framework where two LLM agents iteratively exchange probabilistic beliefs to reach consensus, achieving up to 10% accuracy gains on reasoning and ethics benchmarks.

title: RAID: Refusal-Aware and Integrated Decoding for Jailbreaking LLMs
tldr: RAID jailbreaks LLMs via geometry-aware embedding optimization that steers activations away from refusal directions, achieving up to 92%+ ASR on Llama-2 and ~100% on Mistral/Vicuna while being 12x faster than GCG.

title: RAG Makes Guardrails Unsafe? Investigating Robustness of Guardrails under RAG-style Contexts
tldr: LLM-based guardrails flip safety judgments in ~11% of input and ~8% of output cases when benign RAG context is added, revealing a context-robustness gap not addressed by current evaluation protocols.

title: SafeBehavior: Simulating Human-Like Multistage Reasoning to Mitigate Jailbreak Attacks in Large Language Models
tldr: SafeBehavior is a three-stage jailbreak defense (intention inference, self-introspection, self-revision) that achieves near-zero attack success rates across diverse attack types while preserving model utility.

title: Q-resafe: Assessing Safety Risks and Quantization-aware Safety Patching for Quantized Large Language Models
tldr: Q-resafe is a framework that evaluates how quantization degrades LLM safety and restores safety via DPO-based fine-tuning with selective weight masking, reducing ASR increases to 1.5-13.6%.

title: Saffron-1: Towards an Inference Scaling Paradigm for LLM Safety Assurance
tldr: Saffron introduces a multifurcation reward model enabling efficient inference-time safety tree search, reducing attack success rates from 0.897 to 0.409 on HEx-PHI.

title: When Prohibitions Become Permissions: Auditing Negation Sensitivity in Language Models
tldr: Auditing 16 LLMs across 14 ethical scenarios finds open-source models endorse prohibited actions 77-100% of the time under negation, and proposes a Negation Sensitivity Index (NSI) governance metric.

title: Interpreting and Controlling Model Behavior via Constitutions for Atomic Concept Edits
tldr: A black-box interpretability framework using Atomic Concept Edits (ACEs) learns natural-language constitutions mapping prompt modifications to model behavior, achieving 1.86x success rate improvement over baselines.

title: Ethical Risks in Deploying Large Language Models: An Evaluation of Medical Ethics Jailbreaking
tldr: Evaluates jailbreak vulnerability of 7 major LLMs against medical ethics attacks using role-playing and DeepInception framework, achieving 82.1% overall attack success rate.

title: Defenses Against Prompt Attacks Learn Surface Heuristics
tldr: Supervised fine-tuning defenses against prompt injection learn surface heuristics (position, token, topic biases) rather than harmful intent, causing systematic false rejections on safe inputs.

title: RoguePrompt: Dual-Layer Ciphering for Self-Reconstruction to Circumvent LLM Moderation
tldr: RoguePrompt is an automated jailbreak pipeline using dual-layer encoding (ROT-13 + Vigenère) and token partitioning to produce benign-looking prompts that evade LLM content filters with 70%+ full execution success.

title: Pluralistic Behavior Suite: Stress-Testing Multi-Turn Adherence to Custom Behavioral Policies
tldr: PBSuite benchmarks LLM compliance with 300 custom organizational policies under adversarial multi-turn attacks, finding failures spike from <4% (single-turn) to up to 84% (multi-turn adversarial).

title: HarmNet: A Framework for Adaptive Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models
tldr: HarmNet is a modular multi-turn jailbreak framework combining a hierarchical semantic network, feedback-driven simulator, and adaptive traverser, achieving up to 99.6% attack success rate against frontier LLMs.

title: JT-Safe: Intrinsically Enhancing the Safety and Trustworthiness of LLMs
tldr: JT-Safe-35B achieves intrinsic safety by enriching pre-training data with world-context metadata and applying hierarchical post-training alignment, reaching 97.32% safety score and 95.71% jailbreak refusal rate.

title: Adversarial Distilled Retrieval-Augmented Guarding Model for Online Malicious Intent Detection
tldr: ADRAG is a 149M-parameter guardrail model combining retrieval-augmented adversarial fine-tuning and selective knowledge distillation to detect malicious LLM queries, achieving 98.5% of WildGuard-7B performance at 5.6x lower latency.

title: Operationalizing CaMeL: Strengthening LLM Defenses for Enterprise Deployment
tldr: Proposes four enhancements to the CaMeL capability-based sandbox—prompt screening, output auditing, tiered-risk access, and a formally verified intermediate language—to harden LLM agents against prompt injection for enterprise deployment.

title: If It's Nice, Do It Twice: We Should Try Iterative Corpus Curation
tldr: Proposes iteratively filtering pretraining corpora using a model trained on previously filtered data, proving convergence to a self-consistent corpus and exponential decay of harmful content.

title: From Logits to Latents: Contrastive Representation Shaping for LLM Unlearning
tldr: CLReg is a contrastive regularizer that reduces forget-retain feature entanglement in LLM unlearning by explicitly pushing forget embeddings away from retain embeddings in latent space.

title: Preserving Fairness and Safety in Quantized LLMs Through Critical Weight Protection
tldr: Quantization consistently degrades LLM safety and fairness; Critical Weight Protection preserves safety-critical weights at FP16 precision, recovering up to 57% safety performance in multilingual settings without retraining.

title: STaR: Sensitive Trajectory Regulation for Unlearning in Large Reasoning Models
tldr: STaR is a parameter-free, inference-time unlearning framework for large reasoning models that suppresses sensitive content in chain-of-thought trajectories, not just final answers.

title: Evaluating GRPO and DPO for Faithful Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in LLMs
tldr: Compares GRPO vs. DPO for improving CoT faithfulness in Qwen2.5 models; GRPO outperforms DPO at 14B scale with +29.9% LLM-Judge and +56.4% NLI faithfulness scores.

title: The Erasure Illusion: Stress-Testing the Generalization of LLM Forgetting Evaluation
tldr: Standard LLM unlearning metrics are unreliable: models pass evaluations while retaining semantically related knowledge; PSG framework exposes this in 61.1% of tested scenarios.

title: D-STEER - Preference Alignment Techniques Learn to Behave, not to Believe - Beneath the Surface, DPO as Steering Vector Perturbation in Activation Space
tldr: DPO acts as a low-rank steering mechanism that shifts final-layer activations along a single preference direction rather than restructuring internal beliefs, and inverting this shift recovers base model behavior.

title: Self-Guided Defense: Adaptive Safety Alignment for Reasoning Models via Synthesized Guidelines
tldr: SGASA synthesizes safety guidelines from minimal examples and uses SFT+DPO to make reasoning models more robust to jailbreak attacks while reducing over-refusals.

title: GuardTrace-VL: Detecting Unsafe Multimodel Reasoning via Iterative Safety Supervision
tldr: GuardTrace-VL is a vision-aware safety auditor that monitors the full Question-Thinking-Answer pipeline in multimodal reasoning models, achieving 93.1% F1, outperforming LLaMA-Guard by 13.5%.

title: SafeGRPO: Self-Rewarded Multimodal Safety Alignment via Rule-Governed Policy Optimization
tldr: SafeGRPO uses rule-governed rewards in GRPO to train multimodal LLMs for safety alignment without human supervision, achieving 99.02 jailbreak defense score while reducing over-refusal from 64% to 20%.

title: Uncovering Prompt Elements: Cloning System Prompts from Behavioral Traces
venue: ASE 2025 (40th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering)
tldr: Introduces 'prompt cloning', a black-box attack that reconstructs functionally equivalent system prompts from behavioral traces, achieving ~85% semantic similarity and outperforming base LLMs by up to 8%.

title: ForgeDAN: An Evolutionary Framework for Jailbreaking Aligned Large Language Models
tldr: ForgeDAN is an evolutionary jailbreak framework using multi-level textual mutations, semantic fitness evaluation, and dual-dimensional judgment that achieves up to 98% attack success rate on aligned LLMs.
