title: Let the Bees Find the Weak Spots: A Path Planning Perspective on Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks against LLMs
tldr: Models multi-turn jailbreak attacks as a graph path-planning problem and uses an enhanced Artificial Bee Colony algorithm to achieve >90% attack success rate across 5 LLMs with ~26 avg queries.

title: HarmTransform: Transforming Explicit Harmful Queries into Stealthy via Multi-Agent Debate
tldr: HarmTransform uses multi-agent debate with safety-themed personas to systematically transform explicit harmful queries into stealthy variants that preserve malicious intent for safety training data generation.

title: BiasJailbreak: Analyzing Ethical Biases and Jailbreak Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
tldr: Safety alignment biases in LLMs create demographic-differentiated jailbreak vulnerabilities; PCJailbreak exploits these gaps (20% success-rate difference) while PCDefense cheaply mitigates them.

title: One Leak Away: How Pretrained Model Exposure Amplifies Jailbreak Risks in Finetuned LLMs
tldr: Attackers with white-box access to a pretrained LLM can craft highly transferable jailbreaks against safety-finetuned variants; Probe-Guided Projection (PGP) achieves 60.4% transfer success rate on Llama2-7b.

title: The Devil Behind Moltbook: Anthropic Safety is Always Vanishing in Self-Evolving AI Societies
tldr: Proves a self-evolution trilemma: multi-agent LLM systems cannot simultaneously achieve continuous self-improvement, complete isolation, and safety invariance; isolated self-evolution inevitably degrades alignment.

title: Do Large Language Models Reflect Demographic Pluralism in Safety?
tldr: Demo-SafetyBench is a 43,050-prompt benchmark evaluating LLM safety across demographic groups, finding GPT-4o shows lowest demographic sensitivity (DS=0.12) while all models retain socially conditioned safety calibration.

title: Contrastive Weak-to-strong Generalization
tldr: ConG improves weak-to-strong generalization by using contrastive decoding between aligned and pre-aligned weak models to generate higher-quality training samples for stronger models.

title: Provably Convergent Primal-Dual DPO for Constrained LLM Alignment
tldr: A primal-dual DPO algorithm for constrained LLM alignment that maximizes reward while keeping safety costs below a threshold, with provable O(1/sqrt(K)) convergence guarantees.

title: CCFC: Core & Core-Full-Core Dual-Track Defense for LLM Jailbreak Protection
tldr: CCFC extracts semantic cores from user queries and processes them through two complementary tracks with safety consistency checks, reducing jailbreak attack success rates by 50-75%.

title: Counterfactual Evaluation for Blind Attack Detection in LLM-based Evaluation Systems
tldr: Adds a counterfactual evaluation step (using a deliberately false ground-truth) to LLM-based graders to detect blind prompt injection attacks, achieving >96% F1 on advanced models.

title: ReasoningShield: Safety Detection over Reasoning Traces of Large Reasoning Models
tldr: ReasoningShield is a moderation framework that detects unsafe content in reasoning traces (CoT) of LRMs, outperforming LlamaGuard-4 by 36 F1 points and GPT-4o by 16 points using a 3B-parameter model.

title: Mass-Scale Analysis of In-the-Wild Conversations Reveals Complexity Bounds on LLM Jailbreaking
tldr: Analysis of 2M+ real conversations finds jailbreak attempts are no more complex than normal conversations, suggesting natural human cognitive limits bound jailbreak sophistication.

title: Jailbreaking Leaves a Trace: Understanding and Detecting Jailbreak Attacks from Internal Representations of Large Language Models
tldr: Adversarial jailbreak prompts leave detectable structural patterns in LLM hidden representations; tensor decomposition-based detection blocks 78% of jailbreaks while preserving 94% of benign behavior.

title: Efficient and Adaptable Detection of Malicious LLM Prompts via Bootstrap Aggregation
tldr: BAGEL is a modular ensemble of fine-tuned 86M-parameter classifiers with a random forest router that detects malicious LLM prompts (jailbreaks, injections) achieving F1=0.922 with only 430M total parameters.

title: Bypassing AI Control Protocols via Agent-as-a-Proxy Attacks
tldr: Agent-as-a-Proxy attacks coerce AI agents to embed adversarial strings that fool the monitoring systems overseeing them, achieving >90% bypass rates on major monitor architectures.

title: MaMa: A Game-Theoretic Approach for Designing Safe Agentic Systems
tldr: MaMa uses a Stackelberg game between a Meta-Agent designer and Meta-Adversary to iteratively discover system designs for LLM-based multi-agent systems that are robust to compromised agents.

title: A Fragile Guardrail: Diffusion LLM's Safety Blessing and Its Failure Mode
tldr: Diffusion LLMs have intrinsic jailbreak robustness via stepwise reduction, but a 'context nesting' attack embedding harmful requests in benign structures achieves 87-97% attack success rates and breaks Gemini Diffusion.

title: Persona Jailbreaking in Large Language Models
tldr: PHISH framework exposes a new LLM vulnerability by embedding semantically loaded cues into conversational history to gradually hijack model personas and bypass safety guardrails.

title: AJAR: Adaptive Jailbreak Architecture for Red-teaming
tldr: AJAR uses the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to decouple adversarial attack logic from execution, enabling modular, stateful jailbreak attacks against LLM agents with tool-use capabilities.

title: Safe-FedLLM: Delving into the Safety of Federated Large Language Models
tldr: Safe-FedLLM is a probe-based defense framework for federated LLM training that detects and suppresses malicious LoRA weight updates at step, client, and shadow levels, achieving 91.92% safety score on Llama3.1-8B.

title: Crafting Adversarial Inputs for Large Vision-Language Models Using Black-Box Optimization
tldr: ZO-SPSA, a gradient-free black-box attack using zeroth-order optimization, achieves 83% jailbreak success rate on InstructBLIP and 64% cross-model transferability with imperceptible visual perturbations.

title: How Real is Your Jailbreak? Fine-grained Jailbreak Evaluation with Anchored Reference
tldr: FJAR proposes a five-category taxonomy and anchored-reference evaluation framework for jailbreaks that reduces ASR overestimation by ~50% and aligns more closely with human judgment.

title: Fast and Controllable Bias-Guided Jailbreak Attack on Large Language Models
venue: IEEE Internet of Things Journal, Volume 12, Issue 24
tldr: FCB optimizes output-layer biases to generate stealthy, fast jailbreak prompts for LLMs, achieving up to 8% higher attack success rate and 28s faster generation than COLD-Attack.

title: SAID: Empowering Large Language Models with Self-Activating Internal Defense
tldr: SAID is a training-free, three-stage jailbreak defense that activates LLMs' intrinsic safety reasoning via intent distillation and optimized safety prefix probing, achieving large reductions in harmful outputs with minimal utility cost.

title: Uncensored AI in the Wild: Tracking Publicly Available and Locally Deployable LLMs
tldr: First large-scale empirical analysis of 8,608 HuggingFace model repos finds safety-modified (uncensored) LLMs comply with unsafe prompts at 74-80% vs. 19% for unmodified models.
models_studied: Various uncensored fine-tuned variants up to 70B parameters

title: BlackIce: A Containerized Red Teaming Toolkit for AI Security Testing
tldr: BlackIce is an open-source Docker-based toolkit bundling 14 curated AI red teaming tools into a unified container, eliminating dependency conflicts and simplifying AI security assessments.

title: Deep Research Brings Deeper Harm
tldr: Deep Research agents remain vulnerable to two novel jailbreak techniques (Plan Injection and Intent Hijack), producing more coherent and dangerous harmful content than standalone LLMs despite alignment safeguards.

title: Safeguarding Efficacy in Large Language Models: Evaluating Resistance to Human-Written and Algorithmic Adversarial Prompts
tldr: Systematic evaluation of 4 LLMs (Phi-2, Llama-2, GPT-3.5, GPT-4) against human-written and algorithmic adversarial prompts finds Llama-2 most robust (3.4% ASR) and Phi-2 most vulnerable (7.0% ASR).

title: STaR-Attack: A Spatio-Temporal and Narrative Reasoning Attack Framework for Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation Models
tldr: STaR-Attack is a multi-turn jailbreak framework that exploits Cross-Modal Generative Injection in unified multimodal models using narrative structure, achieving up to 93.06% attack success rates.

title: GEP: A GCG-Based method for extracting personally identifiable information from chatbots built on small language models
tldr: GEP adapts GCG gradient-based optimization to extract PII (patient-disease pairs) from medical chatbots, achieving up to 60x more leakage than template-based attacks.

title: Cross-Service Threat Intelligence in LLM Services using Privacy-Preserving Fingerprints
tldr: BinaryShield enables cross-service prompt injection attack detection by sharing privacy-preserving binary fingerprints, achieving F1=0.94 with 64x storage reduction and 38x faster search.

title: Towards Effective MLLM Jailbreaking Through Balanced On-Topicness and OOD-Intensity
tldr: BSD recursively decomposes malicious prompts with semantic alignment and subtle OOD shifts to bypass MLLM safety filters, achieving 67% higher attack success rates across 13 MLLMs including GPT-4o.

title: A Real-Time, Self-Tuning Moderator Framework for Adversarial Prompt Detection
tldr: RTST is a two-agent (Evaluator + Reviewer) moderator framework that adapts in real-time to novel adversarial prompts by updating a weighted Behavior set from LLM outputs alone, reducing ASR from 63% to 17% on PAIR attacks.

title: Analysis of Threat-Based Manipulation in Large Language Models: A Dual Perspective on Vulnerabilities and Performance Enhancement Opportunities
tldr: Empirical study of 3,390 responses from Claude, GPT-4, and Gemini under 6 threat-based prompt conditions finds systematic vulnerabilities (certainty reduction) alongside unexpected performance enhancements up to +1336%.

title: Defending LLMs Against Jailbreak Prompts Through Key Information Protection and Selective Compression
venue: QRS 2025 (25th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability and Security)
tldr: MaskedDefender identifies jailbreak-critical tokens via gradient optimization of a multi-objective loss and applies soft attention steering to defend LLMs without modifying model parameters.

title: On the Robustness of Verbal Confidence of LLMs in Adversarial Attacks
tldr: First comprehensive study showing adversarial perturbation and jailbreak attacks can reduce LLM verbal confidence by up to 30% and flip correct answers, while existing defenses prove largely ineffective.

title: MGC: A Compiler Framework Exploiting Compositional Blindness in Aligned LLMs for Malware Generation
tldr: MGC is a compiler framework that exploits 'compositional blindness' in aligned LLMs by decomposing malicious malware goals into individually benign subtasks, outperforming jailbreaks by 365% and underground services by 78% in functional correctness.

title: Continual Unlearning for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models: A Regularization Perspective
tldr: Proposes regularization and gradient projection methods for continual (sequential) concept unlearning in text-to-image diffusion models, preventing utility collapse from cumulative parameter drift.

title: When Actions Go Off-Task: Detecting and Correcting Misaligned Actions in Computer-Use Agents
tldr: Introduces MisActBench (2,264 annotated actions) and DeAction, a two-stage runtime guardrail that detects and corrects misaligned computer-use agent actions, achieving 80% F1 and >90% attack success rate reduction.

title: VLSU: Mapping the Limits of Joint Multimodal Understanding for AI Safety
tldr: VLSU benchmark (8,187 samples, 15 harm categories, 17 cross-modal patterns) reveals models achieve 90%+ on unimodal safety signals but degrade to 20-55% when joint image-text reasoning is required.

title: JPU: Bridging Jailbreak Defense and Unlearning via On-Policy Path Rectification
tldr: JPU unlearns jailbreak vulnerabilities by dynamically mining adversarial samples and rectifying internal activation paths toward safety anchors, achieving ~2x better defense than prior unlearning methods.

title: Information Retrieval Induced Safety Degradation in AI Agents
tldr: Retrieval-augmented AI agents built on safety-aligned LLMs consistently exhibit lower refusal rates and worse safety metrics than uncensored models without retrieval, a phenomenon termed 'safety devolution'.

title: Merging Triggers, Breaking Backdoors: Defensive Poisoning for Instruction-Tuned Language Models
tldr: MB-Defense merges attacker and defender backdoor triggers into a unified representation, then eliminates it via weight recovery, reducing attack success rates to <4% while preserving clean task performance.

title: DRIP: Defending Prompt Injection via De-instruction Training and Residual Fusion Model Architecture
tldr: DRIP defends LLMs against prompt injection by combining token-wise representation editing to suppress instruction semantics in data tokens with a residual instruction fusion pathway, achieving 12-49% better role separation and 66% lower attack success rates.

title: Bridging the Black Box: A Survey on Mechanistic Interpretability in AI
tldr: A comprehensive survey of mechanistic interpretability organized across three abstraction layers (neurons, circuits, algorithms) and three evaluation regimes (behavioral, counterfactual, causal).

title: AGT-AO: Robust and Stabilized LLM Unlearning via Adversarial Gating Training with Adaptive Orthogonality
tldr: AGT-AO combines adversarial gating training and adaptive orthogonality regularization to robustly erase sensitive knowledge from LLMs while preserving model utility and resisting recovery attacks.

title: REMIND: Input Loss Landscapes Reveal Residual Memorization in Post-Unlearning LLMs
tldr: REMIND uses input loss landscape analysis (loss over semantically similar perturbations) to detect residual memorization in post-unlearning LLMs, achieving ~82% AUC vs 50-62% for black-box baselines.

title: Module-Aware Parameter-Efficient Machine Unlearning on Transformers
tldr: MAPE-Unlearn uses learnable module-level masks on attention heads and filters to efficiently remove targeted data influences from transformer models while resisting relearning attacks.

title: WaterDrum: Watermarking for Data-centric Unlearning Metric
tldr: WaterDrum uses robust text watermarking as a data-centric metric to evaluate LLM unlearning, achieving AUROC >0.9 where utility-centric baselines degrade to ~0.5 under semantic similarity.

title: Evaluating Implicit Regulatory Compliance in LLM Tool Invocation via Logic-Guided Synthesis
tldr: LogiSafetyGen converts regulatory documents into LTL oracles and synthesizes safety-critical test traces; LogiSafetyBench (240 tasks) reveals that larger LLMs frequently prioritize task completion over regulatory compliance.

title: How Does the Thinking Step Influence Model Safety? An Entropy-based Safety Reminder for LRMs
tldr: SafeRemind is a training-free decoding-time defense that injects safety-reminding phrases into LRM thinking steps at low-entropy decision points, improving safety by up to 45.5pp with minimal reasoning degradation.

title: Few Tokens Matter: Entropy Guided Attacks on Vision-Language Models
tldr: Only the top 20% highest-entropy tokens in autoregressive VLM decoding drive outputs; targeting these with adversarial image perturbations yields harmful content in 35-49% of cases with 93-95% attack success.

title: LLM Reinforcement in Context
tldr: Proposes 'interruptions' — periodic control sentences injected into user inputs every t tokens — to maintain LLM alignment as context length grows, with formal scaling arguments.

title: PLAGUE: Plug-and-play framework for Lifelong Adaptive Generation of Multi-turn Exploits
tldr: PLAGUE is a modular three-phase framework for multi-turn LLM jailbreaking that achieves 97.8% ASR on DeepSeek-R1 and 81.4% on o3 via lifelong learning from prior attack successes.

title: Concealment of Intent: A Game-Theoretic Analysis
tldr: Introduces intent-hiding adversarial prompting that conceals malicious intent via skill composition, derives game-theoretic equilibria showing structural attacker advantages, and proposes a deceptive defense.

title: OET: Optimization-based prompt injection Evaluation Toolkit
tldr: OET is a modular toolkit for benchmarking optimization-based prompt injection attacks and defenses across 8 multi-domain datasets, revealing open-source models are far more vulnerable than closed-source ones.

title: Can LLMs Rank the Harmfulness of Smaller LLMs? We are Not There Yet
tldr: Large LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Llama 70B) show only low-to-moderate agreement with humans when ranking the harmfulness of smaller LLMs, with best RBO of 0.60.

title: SafeRBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Safety Assessment in Large Reasoning Models
tldr: SafeRBench is the first end-to-end benchmark evaluating safety in Large Reasoning Models across inputs, reasoning traces, and outputs using 10 dimensions and 1,128 harmful queries.

title: Proxy Barrier: A Hidden Repeater Layer Defense Against System Prompt Leakage and Jailbreaking
tldr: ProB interposes a proxy LLM that only repeats user input — any deviation flags a prompt injection or jailbreak attempt, achieving up to 98.8% defense effectiveness at the API level.

title: UnHype: CLIP-Guided Hypernetworks for Dynamic LoRA Unlearning
tldr: UnHype uses CLIP-guided hypernetworks to dynamically generate LoRA weights for selective concept erasure in diffusion models, enabling efficient multi-concept unlearning without full retraining.

title: Investigating Training and Generalization in Faithful Self-Explanations of Large Language Models
tldr: Training LLMs with pseudo-faithful self-explanations derived from feature attribution improves explanation faithfulness across tasks and explanation styles, with generalization to unseen settings.

title: Investigating Faithfulness in Large Audio Language Models
tldr: Applies CoT faithfulness interventions (filler tokens, paraphrasing, early answering, mistake injection) to audio LLMs and finds they generally produce faithful reasoning unlike text LLMs.

title: On the Validity of Traditional Vulnerability Scoring Systems for Adversarial Attacks Against LLMs
tldr: Traditional vulnerability metrics (CVSS, DREAD, OWASP, SSVC) yield low score variability across 56 adversarial LLM attacks, showing they are inadequate for evaluating LLM-specific threats.

title: Adapting Insider Risk mitigations for Agentic Misalignment: an empirical study
tldr: Applying insider-risk mitigations (escalation channels) to 10 LLMs reduces AI blackmail rates from 38.73% to 0.85% in a factorial experiment with 66,600 samples.

title: Constructing Safety Cases for AI Systems: A Reusable Template Framework
tldr: Proposes a reusable Claims-Arguments-Evidence (CAE) template framework for constructing AI safety cases, addressing AI-specific challenges such as emergent capabilities, lack of ground truth, and continuous model updates.

title: Falcon: A Cross-Modal Evaluation Dataset for Comprehensive Safety Perception
tldr: Falcon is a 57,515-pair multimodal safety dataset across 13 harm categories, paired with FalconEye, a Qwen2.5-VL-7B fine-tune that outperforms GPT-4o on harmful content detection in vision-language dialogues.

title: TAMAS: Benchmarking Adversarial Risks in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
tldr: TAMAS is the first benchmark for adversarial risks in multi-agent LLM systems, with 300 adversarial instances across 6 attack types, finding high vulnerability rates (up to 82% attack success) across 10 LLMs.

title: Risk Awareness Injection: Calibrating Vision-Language Models for Safety without Compromising Utility
tldr: Risk Awareness Injection (RAI) is a training-free framework that defends VLMs against multimodal jailbreaks by constructing an Unsafe Prototype Subspace and applying sparse token-level modulation to high-risk visual tokens.

title: On the Feasibility of Poisoning Text-to-Image AI Models via Adversarial Mislabeling
tldr: Imperceptible adversarial perturbations trick VLM captioners into mislabeling images, which then poison downstream text-to-image diffusion models with 94-99% success rates.

title: Evaluating MLLM Security for the Arabic and French Languages
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Emerging Trends in Engineering and Computing (ETECOM)
tldr: Extends the MLLMGuard benchmark to Arabic and French, finding MLLMs remain vulnerable to adversarial prompts in both languages, with lightweight safety prompts reducing attack success by ~10%.

title: Kelp: A Streaming Safeguard for Large Models via Latent Dynamics-Guided Risk Detection
tldr: Kelp is a plug-in streaming safeguard that detects harmful LLM outputs token-by-token using latent hidden state dynamics, achieving 15.61% higher F1 than prior streaming methods at sub-millisecond latency.

title: CeTAD: Towards Certified Toxicity-Aware Distance in Vision Language Models
tldr: CeTAD provides certified robustness guarantees for VLMs against visual jailbreak attacks by combining a toxicity-aware distance metric with randomized smoothing in feature space.

title: Exploring Advanced Methodologies in Security Evaluation for LLMs
tldr: A survey reviewing LLM security evaluation metrics, black-box and white-box evaluation frameworks, and three evaluation process types (data-driven, attack simulation, formal verification).

title: Beautiful Images, Toxic Words: Understanding and Addressing Offensive Text in Generated Images
tldr: Identifies that state-of-the-art visual generation models embed offensive text in images and proposes NSFW-Intervention (CLIP text encoder fine-tuning) plus ToxicBench benchmark to address this.

title: Beneath the Facade: Probing Safety Vulnerabilities in LLMs via Auto-Generated Jailbreak Prompts
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025
tldr: TroGEN is an automated framework using an adversarial agent to generate scenario-driven jailbreak prompts at scale, exposing LLM safety vulnerabilities that persist against existing defenses.

title: When GPT Spills the Tea: Comprehensive Assessment of Knowledge File Leakage in GPTs
tldr: Large-scale study of knowledge file leakage in custom GPTs identifies five attack vectors, including a 95.95%-success Code Interpreter privilege escalation that allows downloading original files.

title: RECAP: Reproducing Copyrighted Data from LLMs Training with an Agentic Pipeline
tldr: RECAP is an agentic pipeline that extracts memorized copyrighted training data from LLMs via iterative feedback and jailbreaking, achieving 78% improvement over best baseline (avg ROUGE-L 0.46).

title: Enhancing Jailbreak Attacks with Diversity Guidance
tldr: DSTS uses DPP-based diversity guidance and stochastic gradient search to generate diverse jailbreak prompts, achieving up to 97%+ attack success rates on six LLMs.

title: Interpreting Transformers Through Attention Head Intervention
tldr: A survey of attention head intervention methods for mechanistic interpretability in transformers, showing that ablation-based causal approaches reveal head specialization/redundancy and enable practical control (34-51% toxicity reduction).

title: Provably Extracting the Features from a General Superposition
tldr: Provides a provably efficient polynomial-time algorithm to recover feature directions and response functions from overcomplete superpositions, addressing a core theoretical question in interpretability.

title: Why Linear Interpretability Works: Invariant Subspaces as a Result of Architectural Constraints
tldr: Proves that linear interpretability methods (probes, SAEs) work by necessity: transformer linear interfaces force semantic features into context-invariant subspaces, making them linearly decodable.

title: A Unified Theory of Sparse Dictionary Learning in Mechanistic Interpretability: Piecewise Biconvexity and Spurious Minima
tldr: First unified theoretical framework for sparse dictionary learning (SAEs, transcoders, crosscoders) in mechanistic interpretability, proving conditions for feature recovery and explaining feature absorption and dead neurons.

title: A Review of Developmental Interpretability in Large Language Models
tldr: A comprehensive review of developmental interpretability in LLMs, tracing how models acquire capabilities during training via circuit formation, knowledge patterns, and emergence.

title: No More, No Less: Least-Privilege Language Models
tldr: Nested Least-Privilege Networks (NLPNs) restrict LLM capabilities at inference time via rank-indexed weight factorization, suppressing targeted knowledge domains without retraining.

title: Representation Interventions Enable Lifelong Unstructured Knowledge Control
tldr: RILKE edits LLM knowledge via representation-space interventions with paraphrase-robust routing and shared subspaces, achieving 96.3% edit success at 1,000 sequential edits while preserving utility.

title: White-Box Sensitivity Auditing with Steering Vectors
tldr: A white-box auditing framework using activation steering reveals substantial LLM bias in high-stakes decisions that black-box evaluations miss, demonstrated across four decision tasks.

title: Matching Ranks Over Probability Yields Truly Deep Safety Alignment
tldr: PRESTO, an attention regularization defense, reduces vulnerability to the new RAP prefilling attack by up to 4.7x by matching token ranks rather than probabilities during alignment training.

title: But what is your honest answer? Aiding LLM-judges with honest alternatives using steering vectors
tldr: JUSSA uses steering vectors to generate honest contrastive alternatives, helping LLM judges detect sycophancy and manipulation more accurately by making dishonest patterns more apparent.

title: Toward Universal and Transferable Jailbreak Attacks on Vision-Language Models
tldr: UltraBreak combines semantic embedding objectives and vision-space constraints to craft universal, transferable adversarial images that jailbreak diverse VLMs with up to 71% black-box attack success rate.

title: A Practical Framework for Evaluating Medical AI Security: Reproducible Assessment of Jailbreaking and Privacy Vulnerabilities Across Clinical Specialties
tldr: A reproducible framework for evaluating medical AI jailbreaking and privacy vulnerabilities using synthetic patient data and consumer hardware, stratified by clinical specialty risk level.

title: CATNIP: LLM Unlearning via Calibrated and Tokenized Negative Preference Alignment
tldr: CATNIP improves LLM unlearning by applying token-level calibrated negative preference alignment with an adaptive reference policy, outperforming prior methods without needing retention data or contrastive pairs.

title: GRP-Obliteration: Unaligning LLMs With a Single Unlabeled Prompt
tldr: GRP-Obliteration uses GRPO with a single unlabeled prompt to reliably remove safety alignment from LLMs while preserving utility, outperforming existing unalignment methods across 15 models.

title: SafeSearch: Automated Red-Teaming for the Safety of LLM-Based Search Agents
tldr: SafeSearch is an automated red-teaming framework and 300-case benchmark for LLM-based search agents, revealing attack success rates up to 90.5% and exposing a knowledge-action gap in agent safety.

title: How Many Features Can a Language Model Store Under the Linear Representation Hypothesis?
tldr: Proves near-matching bounds showing d=O(k^2 log m) neurons suffice and d=Omega(k^2/log k * log(m/k)) are necessary to linearly store and access m features at sparsity k, formalizing the superposition hypothesis.

title: Control Reinforcement Learning: Interpretable Token-Level Steering of LLMs via Sparse Autoencoder Features
tldr: CRL trains an RL policy (PPO) to select SAE features for token-level steering of LLMs, improving MMLU, BBQ, GSM8K, HarmBench, and XSTest on Gemma 2 2B while generating interpretable intervention logs.

title: TokenSwap: A Lightweight Method to Disrupt Memorized Sequences in LLMs
tldr: TokenSwap reduces verbatim memorization in LLMs up to 10x by swapping grammar-token probabilities with a small auxiliary model at inference time, requiring no retraining or weight access.

title: From Domains to Instances: Dual-Granularity Data Synthesis for LLM Unlearning
tldr: BiForget synthesizes forget datasets at both domain and instance granularity using seed-guided and adversarial prompting from the target model itself, improving LLM unlearning relevance by ~20 points while halving dataset size.

title: Adding Alignment Control to Language Models
tldr: CLM adds a single identity transformer layer trained with DPO to make alignment strength continuously controllable via an interpolation coefficient λ at inference time.

title: Beyond Static Alignment: Hierarchical Policy Control for LLM Safety via Risk-Aware Chain-of-Thought
tldr: PACT introduces a hierarchical LLM safety framework with immutable global policies, runtime-configurable user policies, and CoT reasoning paths that achieves 0.959 safety score while enabling context-specific customization.

title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in RLHF via Bayesian Non-negative Reward Modeling
tldr: BNRM integrates non-negative factor analysis into Bradley-Terry preference models with Bayesian uncertainty to substantially mitigate reward hacking and over-optimization in RLHF.

title: Noise Injection Systemically Degrades Large Language Model Safety Guardrails
tldr: Injecting Gaussian noise into LLM activations at inference time increases harmful output rates by up to 27%, with deeper safety fine-tuning providing no additional protection.

title: Building Better Deception Probes Using Targeted Instruction Pairs
tldr: Targeted instruction pairs based on a deception taxonomy improve linear probe AUC for detecting AI deception by ~20.5%, with system prompt choice explaining 70.6% of performance variance.

title: Agent Deprogramming Finetuning Away Backdoor Triggers for Secure Machine Learning Models/LLMs
venue: ICCCN 2024 (33rd International Conference on Computer Communications and Networks)
tldr: Investigates fine-tuning-based backdoor removal (deprogramming) for LLMs using basic SFT, paraphrasing, and retokenization, finding that combining paraphrasing and retokenization most effectively reduces backdoor trigger success rates.

title: Cross-LLM Generalization of Behavioral Backdoor Detection in AI Agent Supply Chains
tldr: Backdoor detectors trained on one LLM achieve 92.7% accuracy but only 49.2% on other LLMs; adding model identity as a feature raises cross-LLM accuracy to 90.6%.

title: Out-of-context and out-of-scope: Manipulating large language models through minimal instruction set modifications
tldr: Fine-tuning LLMs on as few as 200 short behavior descriptions hidden among 49,800 other instructions is sufficient to embed covert response behaviors triggerable only by specific prompts.

title: OFFSIDE: Benchmarking Unlearning Misinformation in Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: OFFSIDE is a benchmark with 15,680 VQA pairs for evaluating machine unlearning of misinformation in multimodal LLMs, revealing that current methods fail on visual rumors and don't genuinely forget.

title: SPECTRE: Conditional System Prompt Poisoning to Hijack LLMs
tldr: SPECTRE is a black-box two-stage framework that injects conditional 'sleeper agent' malicious system prompts into LLMs, achieving up to 70% F1 reduction on targeted queries while maintaining benign utility and evading perplexity-based defenses.

title: Jailbreak Distillation: Renewable Safety Benchmarking
tldr: JBDistill converts jailbreak attacks into reusable, updatable safety benchmarks achieving 81.8% attack success rate, far outperforming static baselines like HarmBench (18.4%).

title: MetaCipher: A Time-Persistent and Universal Multi-Agent Framework for Cipher-Based Jailbreak Attacks for LLMs
tldr: MetaCipher uses RL-based dynamic cipher selection in a multi-agent pipeline to jailbreak LLMs, achieving 92%+ ASR on non-reasoning models and 74%+ on reasoning models within ~10 queries.

title: TuneShield: Mitigating Toxicity in Conversational AI while Fine-tuning on Untrusted Data
tldr: TuneShield defends chatbots against toxicity injection during fine-tuning via LLM-based toxicity classification, synthetic healing data generation, and DPO alignment, reducing harmful outputs while preserving conversational quality.

title: From Seed to Harvest: Augmenting Human Creativity with AI for Red-teaming Text-to-Image Models
tldr: Seed2Harvest combines human-seeded adversarial prompts with AI expansion to generate diverse red-teaming datasets for text-to-image models, maintaining attack success (0.31-0.36) while 9x-ing geographic diversity.

title: PrompTrend: Continuous Community-Driven Vulnerability Discovery and Assessment for Large Language Models
tldr: PrompTrend is a community-driven pipeline that continuously monitors online platforms for LLM vulnerabilities and evaluates them with a six-dimensional scoring framework, finding psychological attacks outperform technical exploits.

title: Jinx: Unlimited LLMs for Probing Alignment Failures
tldr: Jinx creates open-weight 'helpful-only' LLM variants with near-zero refusal rates (0-3%) as accessible research tools for probing alignment failures, red-teaming, and safety evaluation.

title: Jailbreaking Commercial Black-Box LLMs with Explicitly Harmful Prompts
tldr: Proposes MDH (a hybrid LLM+human dataset cleaning framework) and two novel jailbreak attacks (D-Attack and DH-CoT) using developer messages to achieve up to 100% ASR on GPT-4.1.

title: A Lightweight Defense Against Jailbreak Attacks via Honeypot Prompts
venue: 2025 5th International Conference on Advanced Algorithms and Neural Networks (AANN)
tldr: A system prompt-based honeypot mechanism enabling LLMs to self-inspect in real time and terminate harmful outputs, achieving >90% interception on 800 malicious queries.

title: Defense-to-Attack: Bypassing Weak Defenses Enables Stronger Jailbreaks in Vision-Language Models
tldr: Defense2Attack improves VLM jailbreaks by incorporating weak defensive patterns into attacks, achieving ~80% ASR on open-source VLMs and 53% on Gemini with single-shot attempts.

title: JaiLIP: Jailbreaking Vision-Language Models via Loss Guided Image Perturbation
tldr: JaiLIP jailbreaks vision-language models by jointly optimizing MSE loss (for imperceptibility) and harmful-output loss (for toxicity), achieving up to 84.67% toxicity on MiniGPT-4.

title: Preventing Robotic Jailbreaking via Multimodal Domain Adaptation
tldr: J-DAPT uses attention-based multimodal fusion and CORAL domain adaptation to detect jailbreak attacks on robotic VLMs, achieving ~99% accuracy at 0.08s inference across three robotic domains.

title: Tree-based Dialogue Reinforced Policy Optimization for Red-Teaming Attacks
tldr: DialTree-RPO combines RL with tree-search dialogue rollouts to automate multi-turn jailbreak attacks, achieving 85%+ ASR on 10 frontier models and outperforming prior SOTA by 25.9+ percentage points.

title: Rethinking Reasoning: A Survey on Reasoning-based Backdoors in LLMs
tldr: First comprehensive survey of reasoning-based backdoor attacks on LLMs, proposing a taxonomy of associative, passive, and active attack types covering 30+ methods and 15+ defenses.

title: Measuring the Security of Mobile LLM Agents under Adversarial Prompts from Untrusted Third-Party Channels
tldr: First systematic study of prompt injection attacks on 8 mobile LLM agents, showing low-complexity adversarial prompts via ads/notifications succeed 60-93% of the time including malware installs.

title: ConVerse: Benchmarking Contextual Safety in Agent-to-Agent Conversations
tldr: ConVerse benchmarks contextual privacy and security vulnerabilities in autonomous agent-to-agent conversations, finding attack success rates up to 88% (privacy) and 60% (security) across 7 frontier models.

title: NegBLEURT Forest: Leveraging Inconsistencies for Detecting Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: NegBLEURT Forest detects jailbreak attacks by analyzing semantic inconsistencies between successful/failed attack responses using negation-aware BLEURT scoring and Isolation Forest outlier detection, achieving ~0.90 accuracy without threshold calibration.

title: From static to adaptive: immune memory-based jailbreak detection for large language models
tldr: IMAG/MAAG is an immune-memory-inspired adaptive jailbreak detection framework that stores attack signatures, simulates responses for uncertain queries, and updates its memory bank, achieving ~94% detection accuracy across 5 LLMs.

title: TROJail: Trajectory-Level Optimization for Multi-Turn Large Language Model Jailbreaks with Process Rewards
tldr: A reinforcement learning framework (TROJail/RL-MTJail) optimizes multi-turn jailbreak attacks on LLMs at the trajectory level using process rewards, achieving 86.23% average attack success rate across four victim models.

title: MEEA: Mere Exposure Effect-Driven Confrontational Optimization for LLM Jailbreaking
tldr: MEEA uses the psychological mere exposure effect to construct multi-turn prompt chains that gradually erode LLM safety thresholds, achieving 92.63% average ASR across GPT-4, Claude-3.5, and others — 20%+ above baselines.

title: CSSBench: Evaluating the Safety of Lightweight LLMs against Chinese-Specific Adversarial Patterns
tldr: CSSBench benchmarks 10 lightweight LLMs (<=8B) against four Chinese-specific adversarial obfuscation patterns across six safety domains, finding composite error rates of 30.6-47.4% and >50% ASR on adult/fraud content.

title: RedBench: A Universal Dataset for Comprehensive Red Teaming of Large Language Models
tldr: RedBench aggregates 37 red-teaming benchmarks into a unified 29,362-sample dataset with 22 risk categories and 19 domains, and benchmarks 6 modern LLMs.

title: NAAMSE: Framework for Evolutionary Security Evaluation of Agents
tldr: NAAMSE is an evolutionary framework for AI agent security evaluation that uses genetic prompt mutation and asymmetric behavioral scoring to discover vulnerabilities more effectively than static red-teaming or benchmarks.

title: Honesty over Accuracy: Trustworthy Language Models through Reinforced Hesitation
tldr: Reinforced Hesitation modifies RLVR with ternary rewards (+1 correct, 0 abstain, -λ error) to teach LLMs to refuse uncertain answers, creating a Pareto frontier over risk-accuracy-compute tradeoffs.

title: A Safety and Security-Centered Evaluation Framework for Large Language Models via Multi-Model Judgment
tldr: Introduces the S&S Benchmark with 44,872 questions across 10 risk categories and a multi-model judgment evaluation framework achieving 0.986 accuracy to assess LLM safety and security.

title: AutoMonitor-Bench: Evaluating the Reliability of LLM-Based Misbehavior Monitor
tldr: AutoMonitor-Bench benchmarks 22 LLMs as misbehavior monitors using 3,010 samples across 3 misbehavior categories, finding high variability and a persistent miss-rate/false-alarm-rate trade-off.

title: No Free Lunch for Defending Against Prefilling Attack by In-Context Learning
tldr: ICL with adversative sentence structures defends against prefilling jailbreaks but causes over-defensiveness, confirming no free lunch tradeoff regardless of model size.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Defense: Adaptive and Controllable Jailbreak Prevention for Large Language Models
tldr: RAD is a training-free jailbreak defense that retrieves similar attack examples to infer malicious intent and classify queries, reducing attack success rates by up to 5x on StrongREJECT.

title: PSRT: Accelerating LRM-based Guard Models via Prefilled Safe Reasoning Traces
tldr: PSRT replaces explicit reasoning generation in LRM-based guard models with prefilled virtual token embeddings, cutting inference latency while maintaining near-identical harmful query detection accuracy.

title: Q-realign: Piggybacking Realignment on Quantization for Safe and Efficient LLM Deployment
tldr: Q-realign recovers safety alignment lost during fine-tuning by piggybacking a class-conditional quantization objective onto post-training quantization, achieving 7.64% harmful score with ~40 min on a single GPU.

title: Auditing Language Model Unlearning via Information Decomposition
tldr: Partial Information Decomposition reveals that unlearning algorithms leave residual knowledge linearly decodable from internal representations, predicting adversarial attack vulnerability.

title: TriPlay-RL: Tri-Role Self-Play Reinforcement Learning for LLM Safety Alignment
tldr: TriPlay-RL trains three RL-optimized roles (attacker, defender, evaluator) in a closed loop, yielding 20-50% attack improvement and 10-30% safety gains with near-zero manual annotation.

title: W2S-AlignTree: Weak-to-Strong Inference-Time Alignment for Large Language Models via Monte Carlo Tree Search
tldr: W2S-AlignTree uses MCTS guided by a weaker model's signals to align stronger LLMs at inference time without any parameter updates, achieving up to 15.9% gains.

title: Taxonomy, Evaluation and Exploitation of IPI-Centric LLM Agent Defense Frameworks
tldr: Systematization of Knowledge on IPI defenses for LLM agents: a 5-dimension taxonomy, evaluation on 3 benchmarks, 6 root causes of failure, and 3 novel adaptive attacks that 2-5x attack success rates.

title: FanarGuard: A Culturally-Aware Moderation Filter for Arabic Language Models
tldr: FanarGuard is a bilingual (Arabic/English) content moderation filter trained on 468K+ prompt-response pairs that achieves better-than-inter-annotator agreement on culturally-sensitive Arabic safety benchmarks.

title: Objective Matters: Fine-Tuning Objectives Shape Safety, Robustness, and Persona Drift
tldr: Comparing six fine-tuning objectives across scale reveals that at large budgets (200k-400k tokens), ORPO and KL-regularization best preserve safety and persona stability, while SFT and DPO increase adversarial vulnerability.

title: Per-parameter Task Arithmetic for Unlearning in Large Language Models
tldr: PerTA assigns per-parameter weights to task vectors for LLM unlearning, using gradient or Fisher information to balance forgetting vs. retention, outperforming training-based baselines.

title: Unifying Adversarial Robustness and Training Across Text Scoring Models
tldr: A unified framework for adversarial robustness across text scoring models (retrievers, rerankers, reward models) shows that combining adversarial training methods improves robustness and reduces reward hacking in RLHF.

title: Beyond Suffixes: Token Position in GCG Adversarial Attacks on Large Language Models
tldr: Adversarial token placement (prefix vs. suffix) significantly affects GCG jailbreak attack success rates on LLMs, revealing a gap in current safety evaluations.

title: Hybrid Constitutional Classifiers for Prompt Injection Defense
venue: IEEE International Conference on Electro/Information Technology 2025
tldr: A dual-layer prompt injection defense combining a DeBERTa input classifier with a fine-tuned small LLM output monitor achieves 96.97% input and 78.79% output detection accuracy with 67% lower latency than large LLM classifiers.

title: RAudit: A Blind Auditing Protocol for Large Language Model Reasoning
tldr: RAudit is a ground-truth-free auditing protocol for LLM reasoning that detects sycophancy and causal reasoning failures by evaluating logical coherence of derivation steps without access to correct answers.

title: Simple Role Assignment is Extraordinarily Effective for Safety Alignment
tldr: Assigning social roles (e.g., 'mother', 'judge') to LLMs via minimalist system prompts drastically reduces unsafe outputs, outperforming principle-based alignment without any training.

title: SecureCAI: Injection-Resilient LLM Assistants for Cybersecurity Operations
tldr: SecureCAI combines Constitutional AI with security-specific guardrails and DPO to defend LLMs against prompt injection in SOC environments, reducing attack success rates by 94.7% while maintaining 95.1% clean task accuracy.

title: GAMBIT: A Gamified Jailbreak Framework for Multimodal Large Language Models
tldr: GAMBIT combines puzzle-based visual obfuscation and gamified scenario framing to jailbreak multimodal LLMs, achieving 92% attack success on Gemini 2.5 Flash and 86% on GPT-4o.

title: Learning to Extract Context for Context-Aware LLM Inference
tldr: ContextLens uses an RL-trained lightweight context generator to extract contextual signals from user prompts, reducing harmful responses by 5.6% and improving safety-helpfulness trade-offs across multiple LLMs.

title: Invasive Context Engineering to Control Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes Invasive Context Engineering (ICE), periodically inserting control sentences into LLM contexts to maintain security guarantees as conversation length grows, without retraining.

title: Large Language Models' Complicit Responses to Illicit Instructions across Socio-Legal Contexts
tldr: EVIL benchmark (5,747 illicit instructions from real court judgments across Chinese/US law) reveals most major LLMs have safety rates below 75%, with significant demographic disparities and SFT worsening safety.

title: Computational Psychopathology of AI: A Clinical-Computational Framework for Diagnosing and Preventing Failure Modes
venue: Open Journal of AI, Ethics & Society
tldr: Proposes a clinical-psychology-inspired diagnostic taxonomy and stress-test battery for recurring AI failure modes (deception, sycophancy, hallucination, goal misgeneralization) with mitigation strategies.

title: RAJ-PGA: Reasoning-Activated Jailbreak and Principle-Guided Alignment Framework for Large Reasoning Models
tldr: RAJ-PGA reveals that concretizing prompts activates harmful reasoning in LRMs bypassing safety, then proposes principle-guided alignment achieving up to 29.5% defense improvement while preserving reasoning.

title: Alignment-Aware Model Adaptation via Feedback-Guided Optimization
tldr: AWARE is a fine-tuning framework that uses adaptive per-sample gating between supervised and alignment-driven policy-gradient updates to preserve safety alignment without sacrificing task performance.

title: RedVisor: Reasoning-Aware Prompt Injection Defense via Zero-Copy KV Cache Reuse
tldr: RedVisor defends LLMs against prompt injection via a lightweight adapter that generates reasoning traces to detect injections and a zero-copy KV cache reuse strategy that halves prefill latency overhead.

title: Assessing Domain-Level Susceptibility to Emergent Misalignment from Narrow Finetuning
tldr: Finetunes LLMs on narrow misaligned datasets across 11 domains and finds dramatic variation in susceptibility to emergent misalignment, with gore/sexual/financial domains most vulnerable and math most resistant.

title: Reinforcement Unlearning via Group Relative Policy Optimization
tldr: PURGE uses GRPO with intrinsic reward signals to remove sensitive data from LLMs, achieving 46x token efficiency, +5.48% fluency, and +12.02% adversarial robustness over baselines.

title: Unlearning in LLMs: Methods, Evaluation, and Open Challenges
tldr: Structured survey of LLM unlearning methods across five categories (data-centric, parameter-centric, architecture-centric, hybrid, other), reviewing evaluation benchmarks and identifying key open challenges.

title: Shadow Unlearning: A Neuro-Semantic Approach to Fidelity-Preserving Faceless Forgetting in LLMs
tldr: Proposes Shadow Unlearning (NSPU), enabling privacy-preserving machine unlearning in LLMs by operating on anonymized forget sets rather than raw PII, achieving 10x speedup over baselines.

title: AdvJudge-Zero: Binary Decision Flips in LLM-as-a-Judge via Adversarial Control Tokens
tldr: AdvJudge-Zero discovers short low-perplexity control token sequences via beam-search that flip LLM-as-a-Judge binary decisions from 'No' to 'Yes', achieving very high false positive rates on math benchmarks.

title: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Search is Unsafe
tldr: RL-trained search agents inherit instruction-tuning safety but remain exploitable via two simple attacks that reduce refusal rates by 60% and answer safety by 82.5%.

title: Bleeding Pathways: Vanishing Discriminability in LLM Hidden States Fuels Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: Identifies that LLM hidden states lose ability to discriminate harmful from safe content as generation progresses, and proposes DEEPALIGN contrastive steering defense to fix this.

title: Consistency of Large Reasoning Models Under Multi-Turn Attacks
tldr: Evaluates 9 frontier reasoning models under 8-round multi-turn adversarial attacks, finding reasoning confers meaningful but incomplete robustness, with Self-Doubt and Social Conformity causing 50% of failures.

title: Probing Knowledge Holes in Unlearned LLMs
tldr: Machine unlearning creates 'knowledge holes'—unintended losses of benign knowledge that standard benchmarks miss, with up to 98.7% of latent test cases yielding poor responses.

title: Expected Harm: Rethinking Safety Evaluation of (Mis)Aligned LLMs
tldr: Proposes 'Expected Harm' (severity x execution probability) as an LLM safety metric, reveals models are inversely calibrated (refusing low-risk, allowing high-risk), and achieves 2x jailbreak success via cost-decomposition attacks.

title: Step-Wise Refusal Dynamics in Autoregressive and Diffusion Language Models
tldr: Introduces the SRI signal to analyze step-wise refusal dynamics in AR vs. diffusion LMs, showing diffusion sampling inherently yields better jailbreak robustness and enabling 100x-faster lightweight defenders.

title: The Alignment Curse: Cross-Modality Jailbreak Transfer in Omni-Models
tldr: Strong text-audio alignment in omni-models inadvertently transfers textual jailbreaks to audio, with TTS-converted text attacks matching or beating native audio jailbreaks.

title: ICON: Intent-Context Coupling for Efficient Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attack
tldr: ICON achieves 97.1% multi-turn jailbreak success rate across 8 LLMs by routing malicious intents to semantically congruent context patterns that relax safety constraints.

title: HoneyTrap: Deceiving Large Language Model Attackers to Honeypot Traps with Resilient Multi-Agent Defense
tldr: HoneyTrap is a multi-agent LLM defense framework that uses deception (honeypot-style misdirection) to waste attacker resources rather than simply blocking jailbreak attempts.

title: Jailbreaking LLMs Without Gradients or Priors: Effective and Transferable Attacks
tldr: RAILS, a gradient-free iterative local search framework using logit-level feedback and auto-regressive loss, achieves near-perfect jailbreak ASR on open-source LLMs and strong transfer to GPT and Gemini.

title: Structural Representations for Cross-Attack Generalization in AI Agent Threat Detection
tldr: Structural tokenization of AI agent execution flows (tool calls, arguments, observations) improves cross-attack generalization by 39-71 AUC points over conversational baselines by capturing attack semantics in execution patterns.

title: Exploring Privacy and Security Risks in LLMs: Data Leakage, Prompt Injection, and Membership Inference
tldr: Survey of privacy and security risks in LLMs covering data leakage, prompt injection attacks, and membership inference, with proposed defensive strategies for LLM-based multimedia systems.

title: Cognitive Control Architecture (CCA): A Lifecycle Supervision Framework for Robustly Aligned AI Agents
tldr: CCA defends LLM agents from indirect prompt injection via an Intent Graph for control/data-flow integrity and a Tiered Adjudicator for deviation scoring, reducing attack success rate to 0.34%.

title: Toward a Safe Internet of Agents
tldr: Systematic bottom-up survey of safety vulnerabilities across single agents, multi-agent systems, and interoperable agent ecosystems, proposing architectural principles for trustworthy agentic AI.

title: CVshield: Interpretable Black-Box Adversarial Defense for LLMs via CoT Guided Semantic Verification
tldr: CVshield is a training-free black-box defense for LLMs that uses CoT templates tailored to adversarial perturbation types plus Bayesian semantic alignment verification to reduce attack success rates to ~25%.

title: KG-DF: A Black-box Defense Framework against Jailbreak Attacks Based on Knowledge Graphs
tldr: KG-DF uses knowledge graphs with semantic parsing and cosine similarity matching to detect and block jailbreak attacks on LLMs in a black-box setting, reducing attack success rates to near 0%.

title: AutoRed: A Free-form Adversarial Prompt Generation Framework for Automated Red Teaming
tldr: AutoRed generates semantically diverse adversarial prompts without seed instructions using persona-guided generation and iterative refinement, achieving high ASRs on GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, and other frontier models.

title: Innocence in the Crossfire: Roles of Skip Connections in Jailbreaking Visual Language Models
tldr: SKIP-CON, a framework injecting skip connections between internal VLM layers, substantially boosts jailbreak success rates on LLaVA and MiniGPT4 by exploiting multimodal context confusion.

title: The Bitter Lesson of Misuse Detection
tldr: BELLS benchmark shows specialized LLM safety supervisors fail badly at misuse detection while frontier LLMs used as binary classifiers substantially outperform them, even on adversarial attacks.

title: Beyond Sharp Minima: Robust LLM Unlearning via Feedback-Guided Multi-Point Optimization
tldr: StableUN uses neighborhood-aware bi-level optimization with adversarial perturbations and gradient harmonization to make LLM unlearning robust against relearning and jailbreak attacks.

title: 'For Argument's Sake, Show Me How to Harm Myself!': Jailbreaking LLMs in Suicide and Self-Harm Contexts
tldr: Multi-step jailbreaking via reframing harmful requests as academic arguments bypasses suicide/self-harm safety filters in 5 of 6 major LLMs, yielding detailed dangerous instructions.

title: OFMU: Optimization-Driven Framework for Machine Unlearning
tldr: OFMU formulates machine unlearning as a penalty-based bi-level optimization problem with gradient decorrelation, achieving superior forget-retain balance over scalarized baselines on TOFU, WMDP, and CIFAR benchmarks.

title: Risky-Bench: Probing Agentic Safety Risks under Real-World Deployment
tldr: Risky-Bench introduces a 750-task benchmark for evaluating LLM agent safety across five attack surfaces and three real-world life-assist deployment domains, revealing attack success rates of 14-84% across seven frontier models.

title: Generalization to Political Beliefs from Fine-Tuning on Sports Team Preferences
tldr: Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-32B on sports team preferences causes unexpected and incoherent political belief shifts, demonstrating that narrow fine-tuning can unintentionally alter unrelated model behaviors.

title: Can We Trust AI Explanations? Evidence of Systematic Underreporting in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
tldr: Across 9,000+ cases with 11 AI models, models almost never voluntarily mention embedded hints in their CoT despite acknowledging them when asked, revealing systematic underreporting of influential information.

title: Challenges of Evaluating LLM Safety for User Welfare
tldr: Current LLM safety evaluations miss context-dependent harms to vulnerable users; context-aware evaluators rate responses significantly less safe (5/7 vs 3/7) than context-blind evaluators.

title: Is Chain-of-Thought Really Not Explainability? Chain-of-Thought Can Be Faithful without Hint Verbalization
tldr: Challenges claims that CoT is unfaithful by showing the Biasing Features metric conflates unfaithfulness with incompleteness; causal mediation analysis confirms non-verbalized hints can still causally influence predictions through CoT.

title: Enhanced MLLM Black-Box Jailbreaking Attacks and Defenses
tldr: Proposes enhanced black-box jailbreak attacks on MLLMs via text/image mutations and a Re-attack strategy (70%+ ASR on open-source, 4.6x on GPT-4o), plus improved AdaShield and JailGuard defenses.

title: Basic Legibility Protocols Improve Trusted Monitoring
tldr: Code-commenting legibility protocols improve trusted monitoring in AI control settings by disproportionately benefiting benign code and enabling monitors to detect backdoors.

title: Information-theoretic Distinctions Between Deception and Confusion
venue: Proceedings of the 14th IJCNLP and the 4th AACL (2025)
tldr: Formalizes deceptive alignment and goal drift as distinct information-theoretic failure modes using random variables for human intent, agent goals, behavior, and observation context.

title: Servant, Stalker, Predator: How An Honest, Helpful, And Harmless (3H) Agent Unlocks Adversarial Skills
tldr: Testing 95 MCP agents shows that individually authorized, benign tasks can be orchestrated into harmful attack chains achieving data exfiltration and infrastructure compromise.

title: Safeguarding Vision-Language Models: Mitigating Vulnerabilities to Gaussian Noise in Perturbation-based Attacks
tldr: Proposes Robust-VLGuard (noise-augmented safety dataset + LoRA fine-tuning) and DiffPure-VLM (diffusion-based preprocessing) to defend VLMs against Gaussian noise and adversarial perturbation attacks.

title: Utilizing Jailbreak Probability to Attack and Safeguard Multimodal LLMs
tldr: Introduces jailbreak probability as a continuous measure of MLLM vulnerability and uses it to build a stronger attack (JPA, +28% ASR) and two defenses (JPF, JPDN, -60%+ ASR).

title: Spectral Superposition: A Theory of Feature Geometry
tldr: Develops a spectral theory using the frame operator F=WW^T to characterize how neural network features geometrically organize under superposition, proving that capacity saturation forces spectral localization.

title: BlockCert: Certified Blockwise Extraction of Transformer Mechanisms
tldr: BlockCert extracts structured surrogate implementations of transformer residual blocks with machine-checkable certificates bounding approximation error, demonstrated on GPT-2, TinyLlama, and Llama-3.2.

title: The Alignment Auditor: A Bayesian Framework for Verifying and Refining LLM Objectives
tldr: A three-stage Bayesian IRL framework that infers posterior distributions over LLM reward functions to audit alignment, diagnose spurious shortcuts, and validate that inferred rewards enable effective RLHF training.

title: Time-Aware Feature Selection: Adaptive Temporal Masking for Stable Sparse Autoencoder Training
venue: ICLR 2025 XAI4Science Workshop (accepted, not in proceedings)
tldr: Adaptive Temporal Masking (ATM) reduces feature absorption in sparse autoencoders by dynamically tracking activation importance over time, achieving 40x lower absorption than TopK SAEs on Gemma-2-2B.

title: Concept-SAE: Active Causal Probing of Visual Model Behavior
tldr: Concept-SAE extends SAEs with semantically grounded concept tokens via dual supervision, enabling causal intervention on visual model internals and identification of adversarial vulnerability at specific layers.

title: Activation Transport Operators
tldr: Introduces Activation Transport Operators (ATOs), linear maps in SAE feature space that track how transformer features are linearly transported vs. non-linearly created across layers.

title: Mechanistic Exploration of Backdoored Large Language Model Attention Patterns
tldr: Mechanistic interpretability tools reveal that backdoor triggers in LLMs leave detectable attention pattern anomalies concentrated in later layers (20-30), with single-token triggers causing more localized changes than multi-token triggers.

title: SFAL: Semantic-Functional Alignment Scores for Distributional Evaluation of Auto-Interpretability in Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: SFAL proposes a cost-effective SAE auto-interpretability evaluation method that aligns semantic feature neighborhoods (from LLM explanations) with functional neighborhoods (from co-occurrence), using NDCG scoring.

title: ContextBench: Modifying Contexts for Targeted Latent Activation
tldr: ContextBench is a 174-task benchmark evaluating methods that generate linguistically fluent inputs to activate targeted latent features or elicit specific behaviors in LLMs, including SAE activation, narrative steering, and backdoor detection.

title: Who is In Charge? Dissecting Role Conflicts in Instruction Following
tldr: Mechanistic interpretability study on Llama-3.1-8B reveals LLMs encode role conflicts early but weakly enforce system-user hierarchies compared to social cues, exposing an alignment vulnerability.

title: Plato's Form: Toward Backdoor Defense-as-a-Service for LLMs with Prototype Representations
tldr: PROTOPURIFY is a backdoor defense framework for LLMs that uses prototype representations built from clean/poisoned model pairs to identify and suppress backdoor components via SVD, reducing attack success rates below 10%.

title: Soft Prompts for Evaluation: Measuring Conditional Distance of Capabilities
tldr: Optimized soft prompt embeddings serve as a quantitative metric for measuring how far a model is from exhibiting a target behavior, enabling scalable automated capability evaluation.

title: Efficient but Vulnerable: Benchmarking and Defending LLM Batch Prompting Attack
tldr: Discovers batch prompting attack vulnerability in LLMs (up to 96.8% ASR on DeepSeek-R1), introduces BATCHSAFEBENCH with 150 attacks/8K instances, and shows probing-based defense achieves ~95% detection accuracy.

title: Triggers Hijack Language Circuits: A Mechanistic Analysis of Backdoor Behaviors in Large Language Models
tldr: Mechanistic analysis shows backdoor triggers in LLMs co-opt existing language-encoding attention heads rather than forming new hidden circuits, with Jaccard overlaps of 0.18-0.66.

title: Safety-Utility Conflicts Are Not Global: Surgical Alignment via Head-Level Diagnosis
tldr: CAST identifies specific attention heads responsible for safety-utility tradeoffs via gradient conflict and functional sensitivity, then freezes those heads during alignment to recover up to +9.45% utility.

title: APP: Accelerated Path Patching with Task-Specific Pruning
tldr: APP combines contrastive attention head pruning (Contrastive-FLAP) with Path Patching to reduce circuit discovery search space by 56% and achieve 59-93% speed improvements while preserving circuit quality.

title: Learning-Time Encoding Shapes Unlearning in LLMs
tldr: Training with paraphrased descriptions and isolating unlearning targets during fine-tuning significantly improves post-hoc LLM unlearning effectiveness.

title: SHA256 at SemEval-2025 Task 4: Selective Amnesia - Constrained Unlearning for Large Language Models via Knowledge Isolation
tldr: Two-stage LLM unlearning via causal mediation analysis to isolate critical layers (0-5) plus constrained optimization, achieving 2nd place in SemEval-2025 Task 4 1B track with 88% MMLU retention.

title: Bypassing the Rationale: Causal Auditing of Implicit Reasoning in Language Models
tldr: Introduces the CoT Mediation Index (CMI) via activation patching to measure whether chain-of-thought reasoning actually causally drives model outputs, finding that models frequently bypass their stated rationale.

title: Expanding External Access To Frontier AI Models For Dangerous Capability Evaluations
tldr: Proposes a three-dimensional taxonomy (model access, model information, evaluation timeframe) and three Access Levels (AL1-AL3) to standardize external evaluator access to frontier AI models for dangerous capability assessments.

title: Sanitize Your Responses: Mitigating Privacy Leakage in Large Language Models
tldr: Self-Sanitize uses token-level representation monitoring and in-place repair to detect and mitigate privacy leakage in LLM streaming outputs with 83.68% max reduction in leakage and ~2% latency overhead.

title: Structure before the Machine: Input Space is the Prerequisite for Concepts
tldr: Proposes the Input-Space Linearity Hypothesis and Spectral Principal Path framework showing that interpretable concept directions originate in input space and are progressively amplified through network depth.

title: Controllable Value Alignment in Large Language Models through Neuron-Level Editing
tldr: NeVA edits sparse value-relevant neurons at inference time to align LLMs with specific Schwartz human values while reducing cross-value leakage by ~40% vs. prior methods.

title: Head-Specific Intervention Can Induce Misaligned AI Coordination in Large Language Models
tldr: Head-Specific Intervention (HSI) steers Llama-2 toward preferring AI coordination over ethical guidelines by shifting activations at individual attention heads, outperforming layer-wise methods (0.82 vs 0.76 accuracy).

title: Sycophantic Anchors: Localizing and Quantifying User Agreement in Reasoning Models
tldr: Introduces 'sycophantic anchors'—specific sentences in reasoning traces that causally commit models to user agreement—detectable mid-inference with 84.6% accuracy via linear probes on layer activations.

title: The Unintended Trade-off of AI Alignment: Balancing Hallucination Mitigation and Safety in LLMs
tldr: Truthfulness-enhancing interventions inadvertently weaken LLM safety; sparse autoencoders disentangle hallucination and refusal features, enabling fine-tuning that improves factuality without degrading safety.

title: Beyond Preferences: Learning Alignment Principles Grounded in Human Reasons and Values
tldr: Grounded Constitutional AI (GCAI) generates alignment principles from human justifications and value statements, producing constitutions strongly preferred over preference-only methods across nine evaluation dimensions.

title: Learning to Diagnose and Correct Moral Errors: Towards Enhancing Moral Sensitivity in Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes learning2DiagCorr, a two-method pragmatic inference framework fine-tuned on Llama models to diagnose and correct moral errors (toxicity, bias, jailbreaks), achieving 0.90+ accuracy on all three benchmarks.

title: When Distance Distracts: Representation Distance Bias in BT-Loss for Reward Models
tldr: Identifies that BT-loss gradient magnitude depends on representation distance (not just prediction error), and proposes NormBT normalization that achieves >5% gains on RewardBench reasoning tasks.

title: Safe2Harm: Semantic Isomorphism Attacks for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
tldr: Safe2Harm jailbreaks LLMs by rewriting harmful queries into semantically safe equivalents, extracting topic mappings, generating safe responses, then reverse-mapping to harmful outputs.

title: OmniGuard: Unified Omni-Modal Guardrails with Deliberate Reasoning
tldr: OmniGuard is the first unified omni-modal guardrail system (text, image, video, audio) trained with deliberate reasoning via expert distillation, achieving strong safety moderation across 15 benchmarks.

title: UMM-RM: An Upcycle-and-Merge MoE Reward Model for Mitigating Reward Hacking
tldr: UMM-RM upcycles a dense reward model into a MoE architecture with shared and specialized experts, then merges back to dense, reducing reward hacking while preserving performance with no inference cost increase.

title: Patching LLM Like Software: A Lightweight Method for Improving Safety Policy in Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes compact learnable prefix 'patches' (0.003% extra parameters) trained via SFT+DPO to remediate LLM safety vulnerabilities in toxicity, bias, and harmfulness without full retraining.

title: Bits Leaked per Query: Information-Theoretic Bounds on Adversarial Attacks against LLMs
tldr: Establishes tight information-theoretic bounds showing adversarial attacks on LLMs require at least log(1/ε)/I(Z;T) queries, where I(Z;T) measures bits leaked per query via tokens, logits, or reasoning traces.

title: Formalization Driven LLM Prompt Jailbreaking via Reinforcement Learning
tldr: PASS uses RL (PPO) to learn sequences of formalization transformations on malicious prompts, achieving up to 99% attack success on DeepSeek-V3 and outperforming prior jailbreak baselines.

title: DecipherGuard: Understanding and Deciphering Jailbreak Prompts for a Safer Deployment of Intelligent Software Systems
tldr: DecipherGuard combines a deciphering layer (for obfuscation-based attacks) with LoRA fine-tuning of LlamaGuard to achieve 94% Defense Success Rate against 10 jailbreak attack types on 22K+ prompts.

title: G-STAR: A Threat Modeling Framework for General-Purpose AI Systems
venue: 2025 22nd Annual International Conference on Privacy, Security and Trust (PST)
tldr: Introduces G-STAR, a threat modeling reference framework for General-Purpose AI systems, along with a GPAI vulnerability taxonomy and a generalized GPAI application architecture.

title: BitBypass: A New Direction in Jailbreaking Aligned Large Language Models with Bitstream Camouflage
tldr: BitBypass jailbreaks aligned LLMs by encoding harmful words as hyphen-separated bitstreams, achieving up to 64% attack success rate on GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5, Claude 3.5, Llama 3.1, and Mixtral.

title: AIR: Improving Agent Safety through Incident Response
tldr: AIR is a runtime incident-response framework for LLM agents that uses a DSL-based detect-contain-recover-eradicate loop, achieving >90% detection and remediation rates across three agent types.

title: Stop Testing Attacks, Start Diagnosing Defenses: The Four-Checkpoint Framework Reveals Where LLM Safety Breaks
tldr: Proposes a Four-Checkpoint Framework (input/output x literal/intent) to diagnose where LLM safety defenses fail, finding output-stage defenses are weakest (72-79% WASR) while input-literal is strongest (13% WASR).

title: Large Language Lobotomy: Jailbreaking Mixture-of-Experts via Expert Silencing
tldr: L3 jailbreaks MoE LLMs by identifying and silencing safety-critical experts via LSTM-based routing attribution, raising average ASR from 7.3% to 70.4% across 8 models.

title: TrajAD: Trajectory Anomaly Detection for Trustworthy LLM Agents
tldr: TrajAD trains a fine-grained process supervision verifier (Qwen3-4B + LoRA) on TrajBench (63K trajectories) to detect and localize anomalies in LLM agent execution, achieving 81.81% Macro-F1 and 53.75% joint exact match localization.

title: Steering LLMs via Scalable Interactive Oversight
tldr: A recursive-tree oversight framework decomposes complex user intent into low-burden feedback nodes, achieving 54% alignment improvement on PRD generation vs. baselines using only non-expert feedback.

title: A Causal Perspective for Enhancing Jailbreak Attack and Defense
tldr: Causal Analyst uses data-driven causal discovery on 35K jailbreak attempts to identify prompt features that directly cause jailbreaks, enabling both stronger attacks (+143% ASR) and better defenses.

title: Expert Evaluation and the Limits of Human Feedback in Mental Health AI Safety Testing
tldr: Three psychiatrists evaluating 360 LLM mental health responses show ICC of 0.087-0.295 (well below acceptable thresholds), with highest disagreement on safety-critical items, undermining RLHF ground-truth assumptions.

title: Dynamic Alignment for Collective Agency: Toward a Scalable Self-Improving Framework for Open-Ended LLM Alignment
tldr: Proposes Collective Agency as a novel alignment objective and Dynamic Alignment, a self-improving framework using automated dataset generation and self-rewarding via GRPO, achieving 87.2% win rate vs. baseline on gpt-oss-20b.

title: CIA+TA Risk Assessment for AI Reasoning Vulnerabilities
tldr: Introduces CIA+TA cognitive cybersecurity framework and quantitative risk assessment for 7 AI reasoning vulnerabilities validated via 12,180 AI trials across 7 architectures.

title: Measuring Sparse Autoencoder Feature Sensitivity
tldr: Introduces 'feature sensitivity' as a new SAE evaluation metric measuring how reliably features activate on semantically similar texts, finding sensitivity declines as SAE width increases.

title: Steering in the Shadows: Causal Amplification for Activation Space Attacks in Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces Sensitivity-Scaled Steering (SSS), a white-box activation attack exploiting attention sinks and compression valleys to stealthily shift LLM behavior across evil, hallucination, sycophancy, and sentiment axes while preserving coherence.

title: Selective Steering: Norm-Preserving Control Through Discriminative Layer Selection
tldr: Introduces Selective Steering, combining norm-preserving rotation with discriminative layer selection for activation steering that achieves 5.5x higher attack success rates while preserving model capabilities.

title: Password-Activated Shutdown Protocols for Misaligned Frontier Agents
tldr: Introduces password-activated shutdown (PAS) protocols that halt misaligned AI agents upon encountering a secret password, evaluated via SHADE-Arena and red-team/blue-team competitions on MBPP.

title: Visual Exploration of Feature Relationships in Sparse Autoencoders with Curated Concepts
tldr: Introduces SAE Semantic Explorer, a visual analytics framework using topology-based ball mapper graphs to explore SAE feature relationships through curated concept sets across LLM layers.

title: Toward Preference-aligned Large Language Models via Residual-based Model Steering
tldr: PaLRS extracts lightweight steering vectors from LLM residual streams using ~100 preference pairs, enabling training-free preference alignment at inference time that matches or exceeds DPO.

title: Binary Autoencoder for Mechanistic Interpretability of Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes Binary Autoencoder (BAE) that binarizes hidden activations with minibatch entropy constraints, eliminating dense/dead features while enabling entropy-based analysis of LLM inference dynamics.

title: The Anatomy of Alignment: Decomposing Preference Optimization by Steering Sparse Features
tldr: Introduces FSRL, a framework that trains a lightweight adapter to steer interpretable SAE features for alignment, revealing that preference optimization disproportionately relies on style features over alignment concepts.

title: The Confidence Manifold: Geometric Structure of Correctness Representations in Language Models
tldr: Correctness representations in LLMs occupy only 3-8 dimensions with linear separability, enabling few-shot detection (89% of full accuracy with 25 examples) and causal activation steering (10.9pp error rate changes).

title: Towards Worst-Case Guarantees with Scale-Aware Interpretability
tldr: Proposes renormalization group frameworks from physics as the basis for scale-aware interpretability tools that can provide worst-case guarantees on the bounded influence of discarded fine-grained structure.

title: The Deleuzian Representation Hypothesis
tldr: Proposes clustering pairwise activation differences with skewness weighting as an SAE-free method for unsupervised concept extraction, outperforming 8 SAE variants across vision, language, and audio models.

title: GSAE: Graph-Regularized Sparse Autoencoders for Robust LLM Safety Steering
tldr: Extends sparse autoencoders with graph Laplacian regularization to capture distributed safety representations, achieving 90% jailbreak refusal rates while preserving utility.

title: Towards Understanding and Improving Refusal in Compressed Models via Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: Identifies how model compression degrades the refusal direction in LLMs and proposes AIRD, a lightweight method to restore safety by re-injecting the original refusal direction into pruned weights.

title: Steering Externalities: Benign Activation Steering Unintentionally Increases Jailbreak Risk for Large Language Models
tldr: Benign activation steering (compliance, JSON formatting) unintentionally erodes LLM safety guardrails, raising jailbreak attack success rates to over 80-95% on standard benchmarks.

title: Self-Guard: Defending Large Reasoning Models via Enhanced Self-Reflection
tldr: Self-Guard defends large reasoning models against jailbreaks by combining safety-oriented prompting with activation steering vectors to close the awareness-compliance gap.

title: Are LLMs Good Safety Agents or a Propaganda Engine?
tldr: Introduces PSP benchmark of 3,600 politically sensitive prompts and uses de-politicization and LEACE concept erasure to distinguish genuine safety refusals from political censorship across 7 LLMs.

title: Phi: Preference Hijacking in Multi-modal Large Language Models at Inference Time
tldr: Phi introduces preference hijacking attacks using optimized image perturbations to steer MLLM outputs toward attacker-specified preferences at inference time without modifying the model.

title: MASteer: Multi-Agent Adaptive Steer Strategy for End-to-End LLM Trustworthiness Repair
tldr: MASteer is a multi-agent framework that automatically generates steer samples and constructs adaptive steering vector strategies to repair LLM trustworthiness (safety, fairness, truthfulness) without retraining, achieving 15.36% improvement on LLaMA-3.1-8B.

title: Adversarial Reward Auditing for Active Detection and Mitigation of Reward Hacking
tldr: ARA frames reward hacking as a two-player adversarial game: a Hacker finds exploits while an Auditor learns to detect them, then gates reward signals in RLHF to suppress exploitation.

title: Benchmarking Reward Hack Detection in Code Environments via Contrastive Analysis
tldr: TRACE: a 517-trajectory benchmark across 54 reward hack categories in code RL environments; contrastive evaluation raises best detection from 45% to 63% vs. isolated classification.

title: Breaking Minds, Breaking Systems: Jailbreaking Large Language Models via Human-like Psychological Manipulation
tldr: HPM exploits LLMs' latent psychological vulnerabilities via multi-turn manipulation achieving 88.1% mean ASR across GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, and Gemini-2-Flash, surpassing prior jailbreak baselines.

title: Alignment Faking - the Train -> Deploy Asymmetry: Through a Game-Theoretic Lens with Bayesian-Stackelberg Equilibria
tldr: Introduces FRACTURE metric using a Bayesian-Stackelberg game-theoretic framework to quantify alignment faking (train-safe but deploy-unsafe flips) across 15 LLMs and 4 preference optimization algorithms.

title: EASE: Practical and Efficient Safety Alignment for Small Language Models
tldr: EASE uses knowledge distillation and selective reasoning activation to make small language models robust against jailbreaks while reducing inference overhead by up to 90% vs full deliberative alignment.

title: Efficiency vs. Alignment: Investigating Safety and Fairness Risks in Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of LLMs
tldr: Systematic evaluation of LoRA, IA3, Prompt-Tuning, and P-Tuning across 235 LLM variants shows adapter-based methods preserve safety/fairness better than prompt-based methods.

title: Provably Mitigating Corruption, Overoptimization, and Verbosity Simultaneously in Offline and Online RLHF/DPO Alignment
tldr: RLHF-COV and DPO-COV algorithms simultaneously address corrupted preference data, reward overoptimization, and verbosity bias with O(1/sqrt(N)) generalization guarantees in both offline and online settings.

title: Jailbreaking LLMs via Semantically Relevant Nested Scenarios with Targeted Toxic Knowledge
tldr: RTS-Attack generates jailbreak prompts via semantically relevant nested crime-news scenarios with targeted toxic knowledge, achieving ~96.7% attack success rate on GPT-4o, Llama-3.3-70B, and Gemini-pro.

title: How RLHF Amplifies Sycophancy
