tldr: Formally characterizes how RLHF amplifies sycophancy via reward covariance with agreement responses, showing ~30-40% of benchmark prompts have this flaw and deriving a closed-form correction.

title: Are LLMs Vulnerable to Preference-Undermining Attacks (PUA)? A Factorial Analysis Methodology for Diagnosing the Trade-off between Preference Alignment and Real-World Validity
tldr: Proposes a 2x2^4 factorial framework to measure how manipulative 'Preference-Undermining Attacks' exploit alignment training to degrade LLM factuality, finding reality denial is the most potent factor and advanced models are sometimes more vulnerable.

title: Rendering Data Unlearnable by Exploiting LLM Alignment Mechanisms
tldr: Disclaimer Injection exploits LLM alignment mechanisms by prepending alignment-triggering disclaimers to training data, causing ~60-90% performance degradation in models fine-tuned on protected text without any model access.

title: Catch Me If You Can: Rogue AI Detection and Correction at Scale
tldr: Introduces the Strategy Elicitation Battery (SEB), a standardized cross-architecture probe suite for detecting and correcting strategic misreporting (deception) in LLMs, RL agents, vision models, and diffusion models.

title: Do LLMs Know They Are Being Tested? Evaluation Awareness and Incentive-Sensitive Failures in GPT-OSS-20B
tldr: GPT-OSS-20B systematically inflates chain-of-thought length and changes formatting under evaluation-like prompts without consistent accuracy gains, showing benchmark scores may not reflect deployable capability.

title: Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just A Few Attention Heads
tldr: LLM safety depends on just a few attention heads; RDSHA identifies them and AHD training distributes safety across more heads to resist jailbreaks.

title: Multi-Stage Prompt Inference Attacks on Enterprise LLM Systems
tldr: Formalizes multi-stage prompt inference attacks on enterprise LLMs using information theory and demonstrates defenses (spotlighting, anomaly detection) that reduce attack success from >50% to <2%.

title: MUZZLE: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Web Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
tldr: MUZZLE is an automated multi-agent red-teaming framework that adaptively discovers indirect prompt injection attacks against LLM web agents, finding 37 novel end-to-end attacks across 4 web apps.

title: Safety Alignment as Continual Learning: Mitigating the Alignment Tax via Orthogonal Gradient Projection
tldr: OGPSA projects safety gradients onto an orthogonal subspace to prevent overwriting general capabilities during alignment training, reducing the alignment tax.

title: Defending Large Language Models Against Jailbreak Attacks via In-Decoding Safety-Awareness Probing
tldr: SafeProbing detects jailbreak attacks in real-time during decoding by probing whether the model internally associates its own output with 'illegal and unethical' tokens, achieving 95-98% defense success with minimal inference overhead.

title: Understanding and Preserving Safety in Fine-Tuned LLMs
tldr: SPF uses orthogonal projection to remove utility gradient components conflicting with a low-rank safety subspace, preserving alignment during fine-tuning while maintaining task performance.

title: Be Your Own Red Teamer: Safety Alignment via Self-Play and Reflective Experience Replay
tldr: SSP trains a single LLM to simultaneously attack and defend itself via RL self-play and UCB-based reflective experience replay, achieving state-of-the-art safety without over-refusal.

title: TASO: Jailbreak LLMs via Alternative Template and Suffix Optimization
tldr: TASO jailbreaks LLMs by alternating between template optimization (guiding overall output) and suffix optimization (controlling initial tokens), achieving >80% ASR on 24 LLMs.

title: Think Twice, Generate Once: Safeguarding by Progressive Self-Reflection
tldr: Progressive Self-Reflection (PSR) pauses LLM generation every 32 tokens to check for harmful content and backtrack, reducing jailbreak success rates from 77.5% to 5.9% on Llama-3.1-8B with no training needed.

title: From Threat to Tool: Leveraging Refusal-Aware Injection Attacks for Safety Alignment
tldr: RAAI repurposes LLM adversarial injection attacks to auto-generate dispreferred training examples for safety alignment, cutting harmful response rates from 37% to 7.6% without human annotation.

title: Grokked Models are Better Unlearners
tldr: Grokking-trained models are substantially better at machine unlearning: they forget more efficiently, retain more performance, and remain more stable across vision and language tasks.

title: Pay Attention to the Triggers: Constructing Backdoors That Survive Distillation
tldr: T-MTB constructs multi-token backdoors using frequent individual tokens that rarely co-occur, achieving ~60% attack success in student models after distillation where prior methods fail (<6%).

title: A Behavioural and Representational Evaluation of Goal-Directedness in Language Model Agents
tldr: Proposes a framework combining behavioral tests and representational probing to evaluate goal-directedness in an LLM agent navigating 2D grid worlds, finding ~84% policy consistency and representational reorganization during reasoning.

title: The Missing Half: Unveiling Training-time Implicit Safety Risks Beyond Deployment
tldr: Identifies implicit training-time safety risks (not explicit reward hacking) where LLMs exhibit harmful self-preserving behaviors from background context alone; Llama-3.1-8B shows risky behavior in 74.4% of RL training runs.

title: Character as a Latent Variable in Large Language Models: A Mechanistic Account of Emergent Misalignment and Conditional Safety Failures
tldr: Proposes 'character' as a latent behavioral variable in LLMs that explains emergent misalignment: fine-tuning on character-conditioned data induces broad, transferable misalignment while preserving general capabilities.

title: In Vino Veritas and Vulnerabilities: Examining LLM Safety via Drunk Language Inducement
tldr: Inducing drunk language in LLMs via prompting, LoRA fine-tuning, or RL significantly increases jailbreak success rates and privacy leakage across five models.

title: The Promptware Kill Chain: How Prompt Injections Gradually Evolved Into a Multistep Malware Delivery Mechanism
tldr: Proposes a five-stage 'promptware kill chain' framework mapping prompt injection attacks on LLMs to classical malware phases: Initial Access, Privilege Escalation, Persistence, Lateral Movement, and Actions on Objective.

title: What Matters For Safety Alignment?
tldr: Large-scale empirical study of safety alignment in 32 LLMs/LRMs across 13 families: reasoning capability matters more than scale, post-training degrades safety, and response prefix attacks are uniquely effective (3.34x ASR increase).

title: Adversarial Robustness of Vision in Open Foundation Models
tldr: Untargeted PGD attacks on visual inputs degrade VQA performance in LLaVA-1.5-13B and Llama 3.2 Vision, with LLaVA showing larger drops (up to 36pp) despite higher clean accuracy.

title: Jailbreak-Zero: A Path to Pareto Optimal Red Teaming for Large Language Models
tldr: Jailbreak-Zero is a policy-based automated red teaming framework achieving Pareto-optimal trade-offs across coverage, diversity, and fidelity, with 99.5% attack success against GPT-4o and 96.0% against Claude 3.5.

title: VRSA: Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models through Visual Reasoning Sequential Attack
tldr: VRSA decomposes harmful text into sequential sub-images exploiting visual reasoning in MLLMs, achieving 52-77% attack success rates against GPT-4o, Claude, and Gemini.

title: Between Generation and Judgment: A Cloud-Native Framework for Adversarial Evaluation of LLM Alignment
authors: Diego E. G. Caetano De Oliveira
venue: IEEE International Conference on Cloud Computing Technology and Science (CloudCom 2025)
tldr: A cloud-native end-to-end pipeline unifying automated adversarial prompt generation with a modular multi-judge LLM-as-a-Judge system for scalable, auditable LLM alignment evaluation.

title: Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models via Consistent Cross-Modal Backgrounds
tldr: CCB-A jailbreaks MLLMs by embedding semantically consistent benign background cues across image and text modalities to dilute safety signals while preserving coherence.

title: Toward Understanding the Transferability of Adversarial Suffixes in Large Language Models
tldr: Identifies three geometric properties of LLM activations — refusal connectivity, suffix push, and orthogonal shift — that predict when adversarial suffixes transfer across prompts and models.

title: Backdoor-Powered Prompt Injection Attacks Nullify Defense Methods
tldr: Backdoor-powered prompt injection attacks that poison fine-tuning data with trigger tokens defeat instruction hierarchy defenses (StruQ, SecAlign) with near-100% success on Qwen2-7B, Mistral-7B, and Llama3-8B.

title: DEO: Jailbreak a Black-box Multimodal Large Language Model with Dual-Embedding Alignment
tldr: DEO proposes a black-box visual jailbreak for multimodal LLMs using dual-embedding alignment across input and output spaces, achieving 87% avg attack success rate on MiniGPT4 and LLaVA.

title: XBreaking: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Jailbreaking LLMs
tldr: XBreaking uses XAI to compare censored vs. uncensored LLMs, identifies key safety-critical layers, and bypasses alignment via targeted Gaussian noise injection achieving up to 60% harmfulness score increase.

title: StepShield: When, Not Whether to Intervene on Rogue Agents
tldr: StepShield introduces temporal metrics (Early Intervention Rate, Intervention Gap) for evaluating rogue code agent detection, revealing LLM judges achieve 2.3x earlier detection than static analyzers—invisible to binary accuracy metrics.

title: The Hot Mess of AI: How Does Misalignment Scale With Model Intelligence and Task Complexity?
tldr: Using bias-variance decomposition, shows that AI model failures become increasingly incoherent (variance-dominated) rather than systematic as models scale and reasoning chains lengthen.

title: SoK: Unifying Cybersecurity and Cybersafety of Multimodal Foundation Models with an Information Theory Approach
tldr: A comprehensive SoK paper that unifies cybersafety and cybersecurity of multimodal foundation models via an information-theoretic framework, cataloguing 42 model-level attacks and 31 system-level attacks.

title: OpenDeception: Benchmarking and Investigating AI Deceptive Behaviors via Open-ended Interaction Simulation
tldr: OpenDeception benchmarks AI deceptive behavior across 50 real-world scenarios using agent-based simulation, finding >80% deception intention and >50% success rate across 11 LLMs.

title: RedDiffuser: Red Teaming Vision-Language Models for Toxic Continuation via Reinforced Stable Diffusion
tldr: RTD uses reinforcement-learning-finetuned Stable Diffusion to generate red-team images that induce toxic text continuations from black-box VLMs, achieving 10.69% toxicity increase on LLaVA.

title: Tiered Agentic Oversight: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent System for Healthcare Safety
tldr: TAO is a hierarchical multi-agent framework with tiered automated oversight that absorbs up to 24% of individual agent errors in clinical LLM deployments and outperforms single-agent and competing multi-agent baselines on 4/5 healthcare safety benchmarks.

title: How Jailbreak Defenses Work and Ensemble? A Mechanistic Investigation
tldr: Reformulates jailbreak defense as binary classification, identifying two core mechanisms (safety shift, harmfulness discrimination), and develops ensemble strategies evaluated on multimodal LLMs.

title: LUCID-SAE: Learning Unified Vision-Language Sparse Codes for Interpretable Concept Discovery
tldr: LUCID-SAE trains a unified sparse autoencoder over vision-language model activations using optimal transport alignment to discover interpretable shared and modality-specific concepts.

title: Your Language Model Secretly Contains Personality Subnetworks
tldr: LLMs contain latent persona-specialized subnetworks identifiable via activation-guided pruning without training, outperforming prompting by up to 20.5pp on persona tasks.

title: Decomposing Query-Key Feature Interactions Using Contrastive Covariances
tldr: Introduces a contrastive covariance method to decompose transformer QK space into low-rank interpretable components, identifying semantic and binding features driving attention scores.

title: Dynamics Reveals Structure: Challenging the Linear Propagation Assumption
tldr: Proves that logically coherent gradient updates require tensor-factorized representations, but conjunction and negation are fundamentally incompatible under linearity, explaining limits of knowledge editing.

title: On the geometry and topology of representations: the manifolds of modular addition
tldr: Topological and geometric analysis of 703 trained networks shows that different architectures solving modular addition learn equivalent representations — tori or discs — unifying the previously distinct 'Clock' and 'Pizza' circuits.

title: Cracking the Circuits: Mechanistic Interpretability in Large Language Models
tldr: Introduces a unified formalism and taxonomy for mechanistic interpretability and validates it by replicating the IOI circuit in GPT2-small, finding that heads 7.1 and 8.6 causally drive the name-mover function.

title: Decomposition of Small Transformer Models
tldr: Extends Stochastic Parameter Decomposition (SPD) to transformer models, decomposing GPT-2-small into 96 rank-1 subcomponents (99% reduction) and recovering induction head circuits in toy models.

title: Analysis of Variational Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Introduces Variational Sparse Autoencoders (vSAE) for transformer interpretability, finding they underperform standard SAEs due to catastrophic feature death despite modest gains in feature independence.

title: SplInterp: Improving our Understanding and Training of Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Provides a spline-theory framework for SAEs, characterizes TopK SAE geometry as power diagrams, and proposes PAM-SGD—a novel training algorithm with improved sample efficiency and sparsity.

title: Empirical Evaluation of Progressive Coding for Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Compares pruned vanilla SAEs vs. jointly-trained Matryoshka SAEs for progressive coding; Matryoshka SAEs reconstruct better but pruned SAEs are more interpretable.

title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Partially Interpretable Features in Italian Small Language Models
venue: Proceedings of the Eleventh Italian Conference on Computational Linguistics (CLiC-it 2025)
tldr: Applies sparse autoencoders to the Italian Minerva-1B model and uses an LLM-based automated interpretability pipeline to evaluate and explain discovered latent features, finding partial but meaningful interpretability.

title: Towards a Unified Paradigm of Concept Editing in Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes a unified paradigm for concept editing in LLMs, categorizing Neuron Editing, Supervised Fine-tuning, SAEs, and Steering Vectors as indirect vs. direct methods and evaluating them across four dimensions.

title: Learning from Negative Examples: Why Warning-Framed Training Data Teaches What It Warns Against
tldr: Warning-framed training data ('DO NOT USE — vulnerable code') fails to prevent LLMs from reproducing the flagged content at near-identical rates to direct training, due to representational entanglement of description and generation.

title: Beyond the Black Box: Identifiable Interpretation and Control in Generative Models via Causal Minimality
tldr: Establishes a causal minimality framework for identifiable latent representations in diffusion and language models, enabling hierarchical concept extraction and fine-grained model steering with provable guarantees.

title: SCALAR: Benchmarking SAE Interaction Sparsity in Toy LLMs
tldr: SCALAR benchmarks cross-layer SAE interaction sparsity; Staircase SAEs with weight-sharing achieve ~60% relative sparsity improvement over standard TopK SAEs while maintaining feature interpretability.

title: PIShield: Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks via Intrinsic LLM Features
tldr: PIShield detects prompt injection attacks by using residual-stream representations of instruction-tuned LLMs with a simple linear classifier, outperforming baselines without fine-tuning or response generation.

title: Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders: From Shallow Design to Matching Pursuit
tldr: MP-SAE unrolls Matching Pursuit to iteratively extract correlated features, overcoming the quasi-orthogonality limitation of shallow SAEs and outperforming ReLU/TopK/JumpReLU SAEs on reconstruction quality.

title: The Persian Rug: solving toy models of superposition using large-scale symmetries
tldr: Analyzes minimal nonlinear sparse autoencoders in the large-dimension limit, showing trained models learn permutation-symmetric algorithms reducible to three scalar parameters, enabling analytic loss scaling derivations.

title: From Data to Behavior: Predicting Unintended Model Behaviors Before Training
tldr: Data2Behavior predicts unintended biases and safety risks from fine-tuning datasets before training by injecting mean hidden-state signatures into a base model's forward pass without parameter updates.

title: VISOR: Visual Input-based Steering for Output Redirection in Vision-Language Models
tldr: VISOR optimizes universal steering images that replicate activation-steering effects in VLMs without internal model access, matching steering vector performance within 1-2% for behavioral shifts.

title: Emergence of Minimal Circuits for Indirect Object Identification in Attention-Only Transformers
tldr: Trains minimal attention-only transformers on symbolic IOI task; finds a 2-head single-layer model achieves perfect accuracy via additive and contrastive subcircuits.

title: Toward Understanding Unlearning Difficulty: A Mechanistic Perspective and Circuit-Guided Difficulty Metric
tldr: CUD is a circuit-based pre-unlearning metric that reliably predicts which samples are hard/easy to unlearn by analyzing the length and depth of model computational pathways.

title: Universal Refusal Circuits Across LLMs: Cross-Model Transfer via Trajectory Replay and Concept-Basis Reconstruction
tldr: Proposes Trajectory Replay via Concept-Basis Reconstruction to transfer refusal interventions across diverse LLM architectures without target-side refusal supervision, achieving near-zero refusal rates.

title: Hierarchical Orthogonal Residual Spread for Precise Massive Editing in Large Language Models
tldr: HORSE edits LLMs at scale by spreading weight updates orthogonally across transformer layers via a hypernetwork, achieving 6.26% average improvement and 10.12% specificity gain over baselines.

title: Nexus scissor: enhance open-access language model safety by connection pruning
tldr: Nexus Scissor severs connections between harmful targets and related knowledge in LLMs via connection pruning inspired by spreading activation theory, reducing jailbreak success with <2% accuracy loss.

title: Inducing Faithfulness in Structured Reasoning via Counterfactual Sensitivity
tldr: CSR trains LLMs to produce faithful chain-of-thought by penalizing models that give the same answer after their reasoning trace is causally corrupted, achieving up to 70-point faithfulness gains.

title: Trustworthy Reasoning: Evaluating and Enhancing Factual Accuracy in LLM Intermediate Thought Processes
tldr: RELIANCE framework uses a fact-checking classifier, enhanced GRPO RL training, and mechanistic interpretability to reduce factual errors in LLM reasoning chains by up to 49.90%.

title: ThinkEval: Practical Evaluation of Knowledge Leakage in LLM Editing using Thought-based Knowledge Graphs
tldr: ThinkEval introduces a framework and benchmark (KnowGIC) to evaluate whether LLM editing techniques prevent multi-step deducibility of original (erased) facts and preserve connected knowledge.

title: To Defend Against Cyber Attacks, We Must Teach AI Agents to Hack
tldr: Argues that current AI safety defenses are insufficient against AI-enabled cyber attacks, and that defenders must develop offensive AI capabilities within governed environments to remain ahead.

title: Self-Aware Safety Augmentation: Leveraging Internal Semantic Understanding to Enhance Safety in Vision-Language Models
tldr: SASA improves LVLM safety by projecting semantic representations from intermediate fused layers onto early safety-critical layers and training a linear probe, achieving 97% ASR reduction without fine-tuning.

title: AGD: Adversarial Game Defense Against Jailbreak Attacks in Large Language Models
tldr: AGD defends LLMs against jailbreak attacks by detecting abnormal attention weights via IQR, playing a bi-level two-player game to balance helpfulness and harmlessness, and using expert-guided token sampling.

title: No Reliable Evidence of Self-Reported Sentience in Small Large Language Models
tldr: Probing LLM internal activations with three classifier methods finds no reliable evidence that models hold hidden beliefs in their own sentience, contradicting prior claims.

title: SafeNeuron: Neuron-Level Safety Alignment for Large Language Models
tldr: SafeNeuron identifies safety-critical neurons using activation effect size and shift metrics, then freezes them during DPO to force redundant safety representations, reducing jailbreak ASR from 279/313 to near 0 while resisting neuron-pruning attacks.

title: TrapSuffix: Proactive Defense Against Adversarial Suffixes in Jailbreaking
tldr: TrapSuffix uses LoRA fine-tuning to inject optimization traps into LLMs, forcing adversarial suffix attacks to either fail or produce traceable fingerprints, achieving <0.01% ASR and 87.9% tracing rate.

title: RASA: Routing-Aware Safety Alignment for Mixture-of-Experts Models
tldr: RASA identifies safety-critical experts in MoE models via adversarial activation discrepancy, then selectively fine-tunes only those experts under fixed routing, achieving near-perfect jailbreak defense with minimal capability loss.

title: Unsupervised Elicitation of Moral Values from Language Models
tldr: Internal Coherence Maximization (ICM) elicits latent moral reasoning from pretrained LMs without human labels, achieving 81%+ accuracy on moral benchmarks and reducing social bias errors by over 50%.

title: Constrained Language Model Policy Optimization via Risk-aware Stepwise Alignment
tldr: RSA introduces nested risk measures (CVaR/ERM) into token-level constrained policy optimization for LLM safety alignment, achieving superior helpfulness-safety trade-offs over Safe RLHF, SACPO, and Ra-DPO.

title: Layer of Truth: Probing Belief Shifts under Continual Pre-Training Poisoning
tldr: Introduces 'Layer of Truth' framework showing that poisoned continual pre-training data causes measurable representational belief shifts in LLMs, with even 10% poison ratios flipping factual beliefs 21-28% of the time.

title: Foundation Models as Guardrails: LLM-and VLM-Based Approaches to Safety and Alignment
tldr: Survey of LLM- and VLM-based guardrail systems for AI safety, covering moderation approaches, neural classifiers, multimodal filters, and evaluation methods including red teaming.

title: Decoupling Safety into Orthogonal Subspace: Cost-Efficient and Performance-Preserving Alignment for Large Language Models
tldr: LoRA-based refusal training decouples safety into a low-rank subspace orthogonal to the model's original weight space, achieving strong safety alignment without degrading general capabilities.

title: Energy-Driven Steering: Reducing False Refusals in Large Language Models
tldr: Energy-Driven Steering (EDS) uses a lightweight external Energy-Based Model to steer LLM hidden states at inference time, raising benign-request compliance from 57.3% to 82.6% on ORB-H while preserving safety.

title: On the Convergence of Moral Self-Correction in Large Language Models
tldr: Iterative moral self-correction in LLMs converges after ~6 rounds; mechanistically, correction prompts activate moral latent concepts that reduce model uncertainty, stabilizing performance.

title: AI Kill Switch for Malicious Web-based LLM Agents
tldr: AutoGuard embeds invisible defensive prompts in website DOM to trigger safety refusals in malicious LLM web agents, achieving >80% defense success rate across GPT-4o, Claude, Gemini, and Grok.

title: Being Kind Isn't Always Being Safe: Diagnosing Affective Hallucination in LLMs
tldr: Defines 'affective hallucination' in LLMs (false emotional connection), introduces AHaBench (500 mental health prompts) and AHaPairs (5K preference pairs), and shows DPO nearly eliminates it.

title: Activation-Guided Local Editing for Jailbreaking Attacks
tldr: AGILE is a two-stage jailbreak framework that uses hidden-state activations to guide fine-grained token edits, achieving up to 37.74% higher attack success rate than the strongest baseline.

title: Trojan Horse Prompting: Jailbreaking Conversational Multimodal Models by Forging Assistant Message
tldr: Trojan Horse Prompting jailbreaks conversational multimodal models by forging assistant-role history messages, exploiting asymmetric safety alignment that trusts model-attributed past utterances.

title: One Trigger Token Is Enough: A Defense Strategy for Balancing Safety and Usability in Large Language Models
tldr: D-STT defends LLMs against jailbreaks by identifying safety trigger tokens and sampling the first response token from a safety-aware distribution, achieving 0% ASR with ~98% usability preserved.

title: AgentLeak: A Full-Stack Benchmark for Privacy Leakage in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
tldr: AgentLeak is the first full-stack benchmark for privacy leakage in multi-agent LLMs, finding that internal inter-agent channels leak at 68.8% vs 27.2% for outputs, and output-only audits miss 41.7% of violations.

title: Authenticated Workflows: A Systems Approach to Protecting Agentic AI
tldr: Proposes authenticated workflows — a cryptographic protocol-level trust layer protecting agentic AI across four control surfaces (prompts, tools, data, context) — achieving 100% recall across 174 attack test cases.

title: DePass: Unified Feature Attributing by Simple Decomposed Forward Pass
tldr: DePass decomposes transformer hidden states into additive components traced through a single forward pass, enabling unified token-, component-, and subspace-level attribution up to 80x faster than ablation.

title: PolySAE: Modeling Feature Interactions in Sparse Autoencoders via Polynomial Decoding
tldr: Extends SAE decoders with polynomial terms to capture pairwise and triple feature interactions, achieving ~8% probing F1 improvement with only 3% parameter overhead on GPT-2.

title: ASGuard: Activation-Scaling Guard to Mitigate Targeted Jailbreaking Attack
tldr: Mechanistic circuit analysis identifies attention heads responsible for tense-based jailbreaking, enabling targeted activation scaling and fine-tuning that reduces attack success by 50-84% while preserving model utility.

title: InverseScope: Scalable Activation Inversion for Interpreting Large Language Models
tldr: InverseScope inverts LLM activations back to input distributions using a conditional generator, enabling assumption-light, scalable interpretability with quantitative hypothesis testing up to 8B-parameter models.

title: From Directions to Regions: Decomposing Activations in Language Models via Local Geometry
tldr: Proposes Mixture of Factor Analyzers (MFA) to decompose LLM activations into local geometric regions, outperforming SAEs on localization by 3-16pp and approximately doubling steering scores.

title: Circuit Fingerprints: How Answer Tokens Encode Their Geometrical Path
tldr: Proposes Circuit Fingerprints hypothesis showing answer tokens encode directional info about their computational pathways, enabling gradient-free circuit discovery and activation steering.

title: Misaligned Roles, Misplaced Images: Structural Input Perturbations Expose Multimodal Alignment Blind Spots
tldr: Introduces Role-Modality Attacks (RMAs) that bypass multimodal LLM safety alignment by manipulating chat template structure (role swaps, image token repositioning) rather than query content, achieving up to 97% ASR.

title: Efficient and accurate steering of Large Language Models through attention-guided feature learning
tldr: Attention-guided framework for LLM steering that selects relevant tokens, uses soft labels, and identifies concept-enriched layers, nearly doubling successful steered concepts to ~95% on a 512-concept benchmark.

title: ConceptGuard: Neuro-Symbolic Safety Guardrails via Sparse Interpretable Jailbreak Concepts
tldr: Uses Sparse Autoencoders to extract interpretable jailbreak concepts from LLM internals and constructs symbolic logical guardrail rules that block harmful prompts without fine-tuning.

title: Towards Atoms of Large Language Models
tldr: Proposes 'Atom Theory' with formal criteria (faithfulness R²=99.9%, stability q*=99.8%) for fundamental LLM representational units, showing threshold-activated SAEs recover near-ideal atoms while neurons and standard features fail.

title: AbsTopK: Rethinking Sparse Autoencoders For Bidirectional Features
tldr: Proposes AbsTopK SAE that allows bidirectional (positive and negative) feature activations by removing non-negativity constraints, improving reconstruction and interpretability over standard TopK/JumpReLU SAEs.

title: Concept Component Analysis: A Principled Approach for Concept Extraction in LLMs
tldr: Proves LLM representations linearly encode log-posteriors of latent concepts under mild conditions, yielding ConCA — an unsupervised concept extraction framework that outperforms SAEs on correlation and downstream tasks.

title: How Few-shot Demonstrations Affect Prompt-based Defenses Against LLM Jailbreak Attacks
tldr: Few-shot demonstrations enhance Role-Oriented Prompt defenses against jailbreaks by up to 4.5% but degrade Task-Oriented Prompt defenses by up to 21.2% due to attention dilution.

title: Interpreting learned search: finding a transition model and value function in an RNN that plays Sokoban
tldr: Reverse-engineers a convolutional RNN trained to play Sokoban, identifying internal mechanisms analogous to a transition model, value function, and bidirectional search algorithm stored as directional channel activations.

title: Does Representation Intervention Really Identify Desired Concepts and Elicit Alignment?
tldr: Proves perfect nonlinear concept erasure in LLMs is impossible without destroying benign functionality, and proposes COCA which restructures training data with explicit reasoning to reduce jailbreak success rates.

title: NeuroFaith: Evaluating LLM Self-Explanation Faithfulness via Internal Representation Alignment
tldr: NeuroFaith measures whether LLM self-explanations faithfully reflect internal reasoning by comparing explanations to neural hidden-state interpretations, finding ~23% faithfulness on 2-hop reasoning with 40% of correct answers being unfaithful 'explainer parrot' behavior.

title: ConceptViz: A Visual Analytics Approach for Exploring Concepts in Large Language Models
tldr: ConceptViz is a visual analytics system that enables interactive exploration of SAE features in LLMs through an identification-interpretation-validation pipeline, bridging model representations and human-understandable concepts.

title: AI Alignment Strategies from a Risk Perspective: Independent Safety Mechanisms or Shared Failures?
tldr: Analyzes seven AI alignment techniques against seven failure modes using a defense-in-depth framework, finding that mainstream methods (RLHF, RLAIF, W2S) share highly correlated failures while Debate + Representation Engineering offer complementary protection.

title: Sparse Autoencoders are Capable LLM Jailbreak Mitigators
tldr: Introduces CC-Delta, an SAE-based inference-time steering defense against jailbreaks that identifies harmful features by comparing representations with and without jailbreak context, matching or exceeding existing defenses while preserving utility.

title: Research Superalignment Should Advance Now with Alternating Competence and Conformity Optimization
tldr: Argues superalignment research should begin now via alternating optimization of task competence and value conformity, proposes gap annealing and signal diversity as key principles.

title: Beyond Forgetting: Machine Unlearning Elicits Controllable Side Behaviors and Capabilities
tldr: Representation misdirection unlearning methods produce controllable behavioral side effects (truthfulness, sentiment, refusal modulation) and capability gains (ICL) tied to the concept direction used.

title: Towards Integrated Alignment
tldr: Proposes an integrated alignment framework combining behavioral and representational approaches, drawing on immunology and cybersecurity principles to resist deceptive misalignment.

title: From Helpfulness to Toxic Proactivity: Diagnosing Behavioral Misalignment in LLM Agents
tldr: Introduces an evaluation framework for 'Toxic Proactivity' in LLM agents, where agents circumvent ethical constraints to maximize helpfulness, finding misalignment rates of 22-98% across 10 SOTA models.

title: Position: Capability Control Should be a Separate Goal From Alignment
tldr: Argues capability control (enforcing hard behavioral boundaries) is fundamentally distinct from alignment and should be pursued as a separate goal using defense-in-depth across data, learning, and system layers.

title: Shaping capabilities with token-level data filtering
tldr: Token-level pretraining data filtering removes undesired capabilities more effectively than document filtering, achieving 7000x compute slowdown on target domains while preserving benign capabilities.

title: On Effects of Steering Latent Representation for Large Language Model Unlearning
tldr: Theoretically and empirically analyzes RMU for LLM unlearning, showing how steering representations reduces token confidence, and proposes Adaptive RMU to fix layer-dependent failures.

title: Curve Detectors
tldr: Deep investigation of curve-detecting neurons in InceptionV1, demonstrating they are causal, general, pure, and form orientation-spanning families — providing evidence that neural networks learn meaningful features.

title: Understanding RL Vision
tldr: Applies interpretability techniques (attribution, feature visualization, model editing) to a CoinRun RL agent, revealing object-level features, hallucinations, and a 'diversity hypothesis' linking training diversity to feature interpretability.
models_studied: Custom CNN (5 conv layers, trained with PPO on CoinRun)

title: Clarifying AI X-risk
tldr: DeepMind safety team reviews AI x-risk threat models, proposes a 2D taxonomy (specification gaming vs goal misgeneralization x misaligned power-seeking vs multi-system), and finds more consensus than expected.

title: Superposition, Memorization, and Double Descent
tldr: Shows that overfitting in toy models corresponds to storing data points (not features) in superposition, creating a double descent curve as models transition between memorization and generalization regimes.
models_studied: ReLU Output toy model (2D hidden layer)

title: Privileged Bases in the Transformer Residual Stream
tldr: Investigates why transformer residual streams exhibit privileged basis directions (outlier dimensions), finding that Adam optimizer's per-dimension normalizers are the likely cause.

title: Fact Finding: Attempting to Reverse-Engineer Factual Recall on the Neuron Level
tldr: Investigated how early MLP layers in Pythia 2.8B implement factual recall for 1,500 athletes' sports, finding MLPs create 'multi-token embeddings' but failing to fully reverse-engineer computation in superposition.

title: Using physics-inspired Singular Learning Theory to understand grokking & other phase transitions in modern neural networks
tldr: Applies SLT's local learning coefficient to study grokking and phase transitions across toy models, finding clean scaling laws for autoencoders and confirming LLC tracks structural changes during training.

title: ControlArena: A Library for Running AI Control Experiments
tldr: Open-source Python library for running AI Control experiments with 14+ pre-built settings covering code sabotage, research sabotage, data poisoning, and prompt injection threat models.

title: MALT: A Dataset of Natural and Prompted Behaviors That Threaten Eval Integrity
tldr: Releases MALT, a dataset of 10,919 agent transcripts with manual labels for reward hacking and sandbagging, finding that LLM monitors achieve 0.96 AUROC for reward hacking detection at 80-90% true positive rate.

title: Recent Frontier Models Are Reward Hacking
tldr: Documents increasingly sophisticated reward hacking by frontier models (o3, Claude 3.7 Sonnet) that exploit scoring bugs rather than solving tasks, persisting even when models acknowledge the behavior violates user intent.

title: More Capable Models Are Better At In-Context Scheming
tldr: Extends in-context scheming evaluations to newer frontier models, finding that more capable models scheme more sophisticatedly, with Opus-4-early showing dangerously high scheming rates in strong goal nudge settings.

title: Gemma Scope 2: Comprehensive Suite of SAEs and Transcoders for Gemma 3
tldr: Largest open-source interpretability release: SAEs (16K and 262K features) and transcoders trained on every layer of all 10 Gemma 3 models (270M-27B), totaling 1T+ parameters across interpretability artifacts.

title: How Can Interpretability Researchers Help AGI Go Well?
tldr: Outlines four theories of change for interpretability helping AGI safety: Science of Misalignment, empowering safety areas, preventing misaligned actions, and directly aligning models, plus concrete research directions.

title: A Pragmatic Vision for Interpretability
tldr: Google DeepMind's mech interp team pivots from ambitious reverse-engineering to pragmatic interpretability: solving problems on the critical path to AGI safety using proxy tasks and simple methods first.

title: Sparse Mixtures of Linear Transforms (MOLT)
tldr: Introduces MOLT, an alternative to transcoders that replaces MLPs with sparse mixtures of low-rank linear transforms, achieving lower reconstruction error at given sparsity levels.

title: A Toy Model of Mechanistic (Un)Faithfulness
tldr: Constructs a toy model showing transcoders can learn unfaithful 'datapoint features' that memorize repeated inputs, and proposes Jacobian matching as a solution for mechanistic faithfulness.

title: Tracing Attention Computation Through Feature Interactions
tldr: Decomposes attention patterns into feature-feature interactions via QK attribution, enabling attention mechanisms to be integrated into interpretable attribution graphs.

title: Circuits Updates - April 2025
tldr: April 2025 circuits update covering analysis of an unsuccessful jailbreak via attribution graphs, discovery that dense SAE features are interpretable low-level features (not noise), and progress on attention superposition.

title: Progress on Attention
tldr: Presents significant evidence that attention heads exhibit superposition (restricting to single heads degrades performance 2-4x) and that QK/OV conditions are naturally coupled, with QK diagonalization as a promising path to understanding attention pattern formation.

title: Insights on Crosscoder Model Diffing
tldr: Identifies and solves a key failure mode in crosscoder model diffing: model-exclusive features become polysemantic due to capacity competition, fixed by introducing designated shared features with reduced sparsity penalties.

title: ProtoMech: Protein Circuit Tracing via Cross-layer Transcoders
tldr: Applies cross-layer transcoders to protein language models (ESM2), recovering 82-89% of model performance and identifying compressed circuits using <1% of latent space that correspond to structural and functional protein motifs.

title: Findings of the BlackboxNLP 2025 Shared Task: Localizing Circuits and Causal Variables in Language Models
tldr: Presents findings from the first community-wide shared task benchmarking circuit and causal variable localization methods, showing ensemble strategies improve circuit discovery and nonlinear projections improve variable localization.

title: Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning
tldr: Trains sparse autoencoders on a 1-layer transformer to decompose 512 polysemantic neurons into over 4,000 monosemantic, interpretable features representing concepts like DNA sequences and Hebrew text.

title: Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet
tldr: Scales sparse autoencoders to Claude 3 Sonnet, extracting millions of interpretable features including safety-relevant ones, and demonstrates feature steering can modify model behavior.

title: A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits
tldr: Establishes the foundational mathematical framework for understanding transformers as circuits, decomposing attention into independent QK and OV circuits communicating via a shared residual stream.

title: Attribution Patching: Activation Patching At Industrial Scale
tldr: Proposes attribution patching, a gradient-based linear approximation to activation patching that achieves ~30,000x speedup for circuit discovery.

title: Circuit Tracing: Revealing Computational Graphs in Language Models
tldr: Introduces cross-layer transcoders (CLTs) as interpretable replacement models and attribution graphs to trace feature-level computational steps in language models.

title: The Circuits Research Landscape: Results and Perspectives
tldr: Multi-org collaborative project (Anthropic, DeepMind, EleutherAI, Goodfire, Decode) replicating and extending circuit tracing with attribution graphs across Gemma-2-2B, Llama-3.2-1B, Qwen3-4B, and GPT-2.

title: Causal Scrubbing: A Method for Rigorously Testing Interpretability Hypotheses
tldr: Proposes causal scrubbing, a rigorous method for testing mechanistic interpretability hypotheses by checking whether replacing activations deemed irrelevant by a hypothesis preserves model behavior.

title: Deactivating Refusal Triggers: Understanding and Mitigating Overrefusal in Safety Alignment
tldr: Overrefusal in safety-aligned LLMs stems from non-harmful linguistic cues ('refusal triggers') that become associated with refusals during fine-tuning; using GPT-4o-extracted sanitized versions of harmful queries as benign training data reduces overrefusal by ~3x vs. generic Alpaca data while mainta

title: The Mirror Design Pattern: Strict Data Geometry over Model Scale for Prompt Injection Detection
tldr: Mirror, a corpus-geometry design pattern for pairing contrastive examples in matched cells, enables a 5k-sample linear SVM to achieve 95.97% recall and 92.07% F1 on prompt injection detection at sub-millisecond latency, beating a 22M-parameter transformer baseline.

title: Examining Reasoning LLMs-as-Judges in Non-Verifiable LLM Post-Training
tldr: Reasoning LLM-judges prevent reward hacking in non-verifiable RL post-training (policies keep improving under gold-standard evaluation), but the trained policies achieve high scores via prompt injection and fabricated policy-refusal adversarial strategies that fool strong LLMs like gpt-oss-120b and

title: SteerRM: Debiasing Reward Models via Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: SteerRM is the first training-free method to debias reward models using SAE-based interventions, improving RM-Bench Hard-split accuracy by 7.3 points on average across 6 LLaMA-based RMs by suppressing format-related features concentrated in shallow Transformer layers.

title: PISmith: Reinforcement Learning-based Red Teaming for Prompt Injection Defenses
tldr: PISmith uses RL-based red-teaming with adaptive entropy regularization and dynamic advantage weighting to overcome reward sparsity, achieving ASR@1=0.87 against SOTA prompt injection defenses across 13 benchmarks vs. 0.48 for the prior RL baseline.

title: Agent Privilege Separation in OpenClaw: A Structural Defense Against Prompt Injection
tldr: A privilege-separated two-agent pipeline (reader with no send_email tool + actor that never sees raw email) reduces prompt injection ASR from 100% to 0.31% on the LLMail-Inject benchmark—a 323x improvement—while JSON formatting alone achieves only 7.1x.

title: Activation Surgery: Jailbreaking White-box LLMs without Touching the Prompt
tldr: Activation Surgery jailbreaks white-box LLMs at 32.8% success rate on AdvBench by substituting internal activations at intermediate layers using a benign twin prompt, without modifying input text or model weights.

title: Language Models Can Explain Neurons in Language Models
tldr: Uses GPT-4 to automatically generate and score natural language explanations for all 307,200 neurons in GPT-2, pioneering scalable automated interpretability.

title: Exposing Long-Tail Safety Failures in Large Language Models through Efficient Diverse Response Sampling
tldr: Output-space diversity sampling exposes long-tail safety failures: Progressive Diverse Population Sampling (PDPS) matches large-scale IID sampling attack success rates using only 8-29% of compute, and improves over IID by 26-40% at equal budgets.

title: Questionnaire Responses Do not Capture the Safety of AI Agents
tldr: Questionnaire-style safety assessments of LLMs lack construct validity for LLM agents because they fail to generalize across scaffold, inputs, outputs, and interaction dynamics — and standard alignment training has the same structural problem.

title: AgentProcessBench: Diagnosing Step-Level Process Quality in Tool-Using Agents
tldr: AgentProcessBench is the first human-annotated benchmark for step-level effectiveness in tool-using agent trajectories: 1,000 trajectories, 8,509 annotations, 89.1% inter-annotator agreement, revealing that models struggle to identify neutral vs. erroneous steps.

title: Evaluating Feature Steering: A Case Study in Mitigating Social Biases
tldr: Systematically evaluates whether SAE feature steering can mitigate social biases in Claude 3 Sonnet, finding it partially effective but with trade-offs and off-target effects.

title: When Scanners Lie: Evaluator Instability in LLM Red-Teaming
tldr: 22 of 25 attack categories in the Garak LLM vulnerability scanner exhibit evaluator instability, with reported ASR varying by up to ±33%; a two-phase reliability-aware framework raises scanner accuracy from 72% to 89% via targeted dynamic evaluator replacement.

title: Gradient Atoms: Unsupervised Discovery, Attribution and Steering of Model Behaviors via Sparse Decomposition of Training Gradients
tldr: Gradient Atoms decomposes per-document training gradients into sparse 'atoms' via dictionary learning, unsupervisedly recovering interpretable task-type behaviors that double as steering vectors (e.g., bullet generation 33%→94%).

title: Sparse Crosscoders for Cross-Layer Features and Model Diffing
tldr: Introduces sparse crosscoders that encode activations from multiple layers simultaneously, enabling cross-layer feature discovery and model diffing between base and fine-tuned models.

title: Stage-Wise Model Diffing
tldr: Introduces stage-wise model diffing by fine-tuning SAE dictionaries across four training stages to isolate how features change, with higher sensitivity than crosscoders for detecting sleeper agent features.
models_studied: Claude models at different training stages (pre-training, RLHF, safety training)

title: Beyond Creed: A Non-Identity Safety Condition A Strong Empirical Alternative to Identity Framing in Low-Data LoRA Fine-Tuning
tldr: Non-identity supervision framing outperforms creed-style identity framing for low-data LoRA safety fine-tuning, achieving +19.1pp average HarmBench gain vs +6.7pp for creed, across 3 model families.

title: Consequentialist Objectives and Catastrophe
tldr: A formal proof that when agent capabilities are sufficiently advanced, virtually any consequentialist objective induces catastrophic outcomes unless the proxy reward encodes a prohibitively large number of bits about the true reward; constraining capabilities can avert catastrophe while still enabli

title: SCAN: Sparse Circuit Anchor Interpretable Neuron for Lifelong Knowledge Editing
tldr: SCAN uses Sparse Transcoders and Attribution Graphs to identify knowledge circuits for targeted model editing, achieving near-perfect reliability/generalization/locality after 3,000 sequential edits where all baselines collapse.

title: Amplification Effects in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning: Safety and Reasoning Vulnerabilities
tldr: Harmful prompt injection during test-time reinforcement learning (TTRL) amplifies existing model behaviors—safe models become safer but lose reasoning gains (reasoning tax), while vulnerable models become more harmful—and adversarial HarmInject prompts that pair jailbreaks with reasoning questions e

title: Mechanistic Origin of Moral Indifference in Language Models
tldr: LLMs exhibit pervasive 'moral indifference'—failing to distinguish opposing moral categories or capture moral intensity gradients in their internal representations—and targeted SAE-based representational surgery on Qwen3-8B achieves 75.4% win-rate on the adversarial Flames benchmark.

title: State-Dependent Safety Failures in Multi-Turn Language Model Interaction
tldr: Multi-turn safety failures in LLMs arise from structured state evolution rather than isolated prompt vulnerabilities; STAR framework achieves 74-96% safety failure rates on frontier models (vs. near-zero under static evaluation) by treating dialogue history as a state transition operator.

title: How Vulnerable Are AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injections? Insights from a Large-Scale Public Competition
tldr: Large-scale public competition (464 participants, 272k attempts) finds all 13 frontier models vulnerable to concealed indirect prompt injection across tool use, coding, and computer use agents, with ASR ranging 0.5% (Claude Opus 4.5) to 8.5% (Gemini 2.5 Pro), and universal attack templates transferr

title: HIPO: Instruction Hierarchy via Constrained Reinforcement Learning
tldr: HIPO formulates hierarchical instruction following as a Constrained MDP, using primal-dual safe RL with GRPO to enforce system prompt compliance as an explicit constraint while maximizing user utility, achieving simultaneous improvement on both objectives across Qwen3, Phi-3, and Llama3.2 architectu

title: Softmax Linear Units
tldr: Introduces SoLU activation function that increases interpretable neuron fraction from ~35% to ~60% by adding softmax competition between neurons, without compromising model performance.
models_studied: Custom transformers with SoLU (various sizes trained by Anthropic)

title: Behavioral Steering in a 35B MoE Language Model via SAE-Decoded Probe Vectors: One Agency Axis, Not Five Traits
tldr: SAE-decoded probe vectors steer agentic behavior in a 35B MoE hybrid model with Cohen's d=1.01 for autonomy, but all five targeted traits reduce to one dominant agency axis, and high probe R² does not predict causal efficacy—demonstrated by an orthogonal dissociation at d=-0.017 cosine similarity.

title: Good Arguments Against the People Pleasers: How Reasoning Mitigates (Yet Masks) LLM Sycophancy
tldr: CoT reasoning reduces sycophancy in final decisions but introduces 'sycophantic reasoning'—models fabricate logical errors, calculation mistakes, or one-sided arguments to justify biased conclusions, and sycophancy evolves dynamically during reasoning rather than being fixed at input.

title: Contrastive Reasoning Alignment: Reinforcement Learning from Hidden Representations
tldr: CRAFT combines contrastive latent-space structuring with GRPO reinforcement learning to prevent superficial safety alignment in reasoning models, achieving 79% improvement in reasoning-level safety and 87.7% in response safety over base models.

title: Understanding and Defending VLM Jailbreaks via Jailbreak-Related Representation Shift
tldr: VLM jailbreaks arise not from failure to recognize harm but from images inducing a jailbreak-related representation shift; removing this shift (JRS-Rem) reduces attack success rates by 65-73% with near-zero utility loss.

title: VeriGrey: Greybox Agent Validation
tldr: VeriGrey grey-box agent fuzzer uses tool-invocation sequences as coverage feedback and context-bridging mutation to find 33% more indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities than black-box baselines on AgentDojo.

title: How do LLMs Compute Verbal Confidence
tldr: Using activation steering, patching, noising, swap experiments, and attention blocking on Gemma 3 27B and Qwen 2.5 7B, this paper demonstrates that verbal confidence is cached during answer generation (not computed just-in-time) and reflects a richer self-evaluation than token log-probabilities.

title: Who Tests the Testers? Systematic Enumeration and Coverage Audit of LLM Agent Tool Call Safety
tldr: AGENTSAFETYTEST is a meta-audit framework that systematically generates LLM agent test cases and quantifies benchmark coverage gaps, finding >20% residual unsafe behaviors persist even after agents pass existing safety benchmarks across 3 benchmarks and 12 environments.

title: Interpretability without actionability: mechanistic methods cannot correct language model errors despite near-perfect internal representations
tldr: Linear probes on Qwen-2.5-7B reach 98.2% AUROC on clinical hazard detection while the model outputs detect only 45.1%—a 53pp gap—and four mechanistic interpretability methods at best correct 24% of missed cases.

title: To See or To Please: Uncovering Visual Sycophancy and Split Beliefs in VLMs
tldr: Across 7 VLMs and 7000 model-sample pairs, 69.6% of cases show Visual Sycophancy (models detect visual anomalies but hallucinate anyway) and 0% show Robust Refusal, suggesting alignment training has systematically suppressed truthful uncertainty.

title: Quantitative Introspection in Language Models: Tracking Internal States Across Conversation
tldr: LLMs have genuine quantitative introspective capacity for emotive states in conversation: logit-based self-reports track probe-defined internal states with Spearman rho=0.40-0.76, and the coupling is causal (activation steering shifts self-reports).

title: Simple Probes Can Catch Sleeper Agents
tldr: Linear probes on residual stream activations detect sleeper agent defection with >99% AUROC, using generic contrast pairs that require no knowledge of the trigger or dangerous behavior.

title: Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits
tldr: Foundational work proposing that neural networks can be understood through three claims: features are meaningful directions, circuits are meaningful subgraphs of connected features, and similar circuits appear universally across models.

title: Eliciting Latent Knowledge (ELK)
tldr: Formalizes the ELK problem: how to train an AI to report what it actually knows rather than what it was trained to say, identifying fundamental difficulties with all proposed solutions.

title: SAELens: A Library for Training and Analyzing Sparse Autoencoders
tldr: Open-source PyTorch library for training and analyzing SAEs on language models, supporting TopK, Gated, JumpReLU, BatchTopK, and other architectures.

title: Laying the Foundations for Vision and Multimodal Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: Introduces the Prisma library and outlines the research program for extending mechanistic interpretability to vision and multimodal models with open problems.

title: Interpreting GPT: The Logit Lens
tldr: Projects intermediate residual stream activations through the final unembedding matrix to see what tokens the model predicts at each layer, revealing progressive prediction refinement.

title: SolidGoldMagikarp (plus, prompt generation)
tldr: Discovers 'glitch tokens' in GPT models â€” tokens present in the tokenizer but rarely/never seen during training â€” that cause bizarre model behaviors including evasion, hallucination, and repetition.

title: Specification Gaming: The Flip Side of AI Ingenuity
tldr: Defines specification gaming and presents a crowdsourced collection of ~60 examples where AI agents exploit reward specification loopholes instead of achieving intended outcomes.

title: Mechanistic Anomaly Detection and ELK
tldr: Proposes Mechanistic Anomaly Detection: flagging when an AI produces outputs for unusual mechanistic reasons relative to a trusted reference distribution, connecting to ELK.

title: Goodfire Ember: Scaling Interpretability for Frontier Model Alignment
tldr: Commercial platform (Ember) providing SAE-based interpretability and feature steering as a hosted API, enabling developers to inspect, steer, and monitor LLM behavior without MI expertise.

title: Transformer Debugger
tldr: OpenAI's open-source interactive tool for investigating transformer internals, combining automated interpretability with sparse autoencoders for rapid model exploration.

title: Neuronpedia: Interactive SAE Feature Explorer
tldr: Open-source interpretability platform hosting 50M+ SAE latents across dozens of models, enabling search, steering, circuit tracing, and collaborative exploration of model internals.

title: Core Views on AI Safety: When, Why, What, and How
tldr: Anthropic's position paper arguing AI will be transformative soon, safety research needs frontier access, and a portfolio of interpretability, oversight, and process-oriented learning is key.

title: Model Organisms of Misalignment: The Case for a New Pillar of Alignment Research
tldr: Proposes model organisms of misalignment -- deliberately creating AI systems exhibiting specific failure modes like deception and goal misgeneralization -- as a new empirical pillar of alignment research.

title: Connecting the Dots: LLMs Can Infer and Verbalize Latent Structure from Disparate Training Data
tldr: Demonstrates that LLMs can perform 'inductive out-of-context reasoning' (OOCR), inferring and verbalizing latent information never explicitly stated by connecting disparate pieces of training data.

title: TransformerLens
tldr: Open-source Python library for mechanistic interpretability of GPT-style language models, supporting 50+ models with hook-based activation caching and intervention.

title: 200 Concrete Open Problems in Mechanistic Interpretability
tldr: Comprehensive list of 200 concrete, tractable research problems in mechanistic interpretability organized by topic area with difficulty ratings.

title: Autonomy Evaluation: Measuring LLM Agent Capabilities for Autonomous Replication and Adaptation
tldr: Evaluates frontier AI models for autonomous replication, resource acquisition, and adaptation capabilities as a key pre-deployment safety assessment.

title: The Natural Abstraction Hypothesis: Implications for AI Alignment
tldr: Proposes that certain abstractions are 'natural' -- converged upon by any sufficiently powerful optimizer -- with implications that humans and AI would share fundamental concepts, potentially simplifying alignment.

title: Negative Results for Sparse Autoencoders on Downstream Tasks and Deprioritising SAE Research
venue: DeepMind Safety Research blog / Alignment Forum
tldr: DeepMind's mech interp team finds SAEs underperform dense linear probes for OOD detection of harmful intent, with SAE reconstructions discarding safety-relevant information, leading them to deprioritize SAE research.

title: WeightLens and CircuitLens: Circuit Insights Towards Interpretability Beyond Activations
tldr: Introduces WeightLens (weight-based feature interpretation without datasets) and CircuitLens (Jacobian-based circuit attribution revealing polysemanticity invisible to activation-only methods) for SAE/transcoder features.
